If anyone offers a victim because of a vow or voluntarily, it shall likewise be eaten on the same day. If anything remains until the next day, it may be eaten; but whatever is found on the third day, fire shall consume. [Col. 0307B]

[C. VIII]

If anyone eats the flesh of the peace-offering victim on the third day, the offering shall be rejected and shall not benefit the one who offered it. Rather, whoever defiles himself by such food shall be guilty of sacrilege.

Flesh that has touched anything unclean shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. Whoever is clean may eat it.

A person who is unclean and eats from the flesh of the peace offering offered to the Lord shall be cut off from his people. Whoever touches human uncleanness, or that of an animal, or anything else that can defile, and eats from such flesh, shall be cut off from his people.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel: You shall not eat the fat of sheep, oxen, or goats. The fat of a carcass that has died, and the fat of an animal captured by a beast, you may use for various purposes. [Col. 0307C]

If anyone eats the fat that ought to be offered as incense to the Lord [Hebrew: “the fat of animals that ought to be offered as a sacrifice”], that person shall be cut off from his people.

You shall not consume the blood of any animal as food, whether of birds or of livestock [Hebrew: “you shall not consume it as food in all your dwellings”]. Whoever eats blood shall be cut off from his people.

[C. IX]

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel [Vulgate adds: “saying”]: Whoever offers a peace offering to the Lord shall offer with it a sacrifice—that is, its libations.

He shall hold in his hands the fat of the victim and the breast. When he has consecrated both by offering them to the Lord, he shall hand them to the priest. The priest shall burn the fat upon the altar, but the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons. [Col. 0307D]

The right shoulder of the peace offerings shall also fall to the priest as firstfruits. The son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat shall have the right shoulder as his portion.

For I have taken from the sons of Israel, from their peace offerings, the breast of elevation and the shoulder of separation, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as a perpetual ordinance, from the entire people of Israel.

[T, V, B. IV]

This is the anointing of Aaron and his sons in the rites of the Lord, on the day when Moses offered them so that they might exercise the priesthood. It is also what the Lord commanded to be given them by the sons of Israel as a perpetual religious observance throughout their generations.

This is the law of the burnt offering, the sin offering, the offense offering, the consecration offering, and the peace offerings, which the Lord established for Moses on Mount Sinai, when he commanded the children of Israel to offer their offerings to the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai. [Col. 0308A]

[C. X, Chapter VIII]

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Take Aaron and his sons, their garments, the oil of anointing, the bull for the sin offering, two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread, and gather the whole assembly at the entrance of the Tent.

[C. XI]

Moses did as the Lord had commanded. When the whole congregation had assembled before the doors of the Tent, he said: “This is the word that the Lord commanded to be done.”

Immediately he presented Aaron and his sons. When he had washed them, he clothed the high priest in the linen tunic, girded him with the sash, put the violet-colored robe upon him [Vulgate adds: “upon him”], and placed the ephod over it. Fastening it with its belt, he fitted it with the breastpiece, in which were Doctrine and Truth. [Col. 0308B]

He covered his head with the turban and, upon it, over his forehead, placed the consecrated golden plate of sanctification, as the Lord had commanded him.

He also took the oil of anointing, with which he anointed the Tent and all its furnishings. After sprinkling the altar seven times while sanctifying it, he anointed it and all its vessels, and sanctified the basin and its base [Hebrew: “its pipe”] with oil.

Pouring the oil upon Aaron’s head, he anointed him and consecrated him. He clothed Aaron’s sons, who had been presented, in linen tunics, girded them with a sash [Vulgate: “sashes”], and placed turbans upon them, as the Lord had commanded.

He offered the bull for the sin offering. When Aaron had placed his hand upon its head, and his sons had placed their hands upon it, he slaughtered it, took its blood, and, dipping his finger in it, touched the horns of the altar all around. Having made atonement for and sanctified it, he poured the remaining blood at its base. [Col. 0308C]

He burned upon the altar the fat that was over the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fatty portions. He burned the bull, together with its hide, flesh, and dung, outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded.

He also offered a ram as a burnt offering. After Aaron and his sons had placed their hands upon its head, he slaughtered it and poured its blood around the altar [Vulgate: “around the altar”].

Cutting the ram into pieces, he burned its head, limbs, and fat in the fire. After washing the entrails and legs, he burned the entire ram together upon the altar, because it was a burnt offering of most pleasing fragrance to the Lord, as he had commanded. [Col. 0308D]

He also offered the second ram for the consecration of the priests. Aaron and his sons placed their hands upon its head. When Moses had slaughtered it, he took some of its blood and touched the tip of Aaron’s right ear, the thumb of his right hand, and likewise the great toe of his right foot.

He also presented Aaron’s sons. Having touched the tip of each man’s right ear, and the thumbs of their right hands and right feet, with some of the blood of the slaughtered ram, he poured the rest around the altar.

He separated the fat, the tail, all the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right shoulder. Taking from the basket of unleavened bread that was before the Lord a loaf without leaven, a cake mixed with oil, and a thin cake, he placed them upon the fat and the right shoulder and handed everything together to Aaron and his sons. [Col. 0309A]

> **Note:** The canon here, as well as the manuscript of Saint-Germain, no. 3, not inappropriately reads: *postquam libaverunt ea coram Domino* (“after they had tasted them before the Lord”). Some manuscripts cited by Martianus read *libaverunt* (“they tasted”) instead of *levaverunt* (“they lifted”), quite absurdly, whatever he himself may think; for the Hebrews were not permitted to taste what they offered. This is a customary error of Latin scribes, who, following popular pronunciation, substitute the letters I for E and B for V.

After they had lifted these up before the Lord, he took them back from their hands and burned them upon the altar of burnt offering, because it was an offering of consecration, a sacrifice of pleasing fragrance to the Lord.

He also took the breast and, lifting it before the Lord, took it as his portion from the ram of consecration [Hebrew: “Moses took it as his portion”], as the Lord had commanded him.

Taking the ointment and the blood that was upon the altar [Vulgate: “upon the altar”], he sprinkled it upon Aaron and his garments, and upon his sons and their garments. When he had sanctified them in their vestments [Hebrew: “when he had sanctified them and their garments”], he commanded them, saying:

“Cook the flesh before the doors of the Tent [Hebrew: ‘the Tent of Witness’], and eat it there. Eat also the loaves of consecration that are placed in the basket, as the Lord commanded me, saying: ‘Aaron and his sons shall eat them.’ Whatever remains of the flesh and the loaves, fire shall consume.

“You shall not leave the entrance of the Tent for seven days, until the day on which the period of your consecration is completed. For your consecration is completed over seven days, as has now been done, so that the rite of the sacrifice may be completed [Vulgate: ‘might be completed’].

“You shall remain in the Tent day and night, observing the watches of the Lord, lest you die; for so I have been commanded.”

Aaron and his sons did everything that the Lord had spoken through Moses. [Col. 0309B]

[Chapter IX]

When the eighth day had come, Moses summoned Aaron, his sons, and the elders of Israel. He said to Aaron:

“Take from the herd a bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both unblemished, and offer them before the Lord. Speak also to the children of Israel:

“Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a bull and a year-old lamb, unblemished, for a burnt offering; an ox and a ram for peace offerings. Slaughter them before the Lord, offering for each sacrifice fine flour mixed with oil. For today the Lord will appear to you.”

They therefore brought everything that Moses had commanded to the entrance of the Tent. When the whole multitude was standing there, Moses said:

“This is the word that the Lord has commanded: Do it, and his glory will appear to you.”

He said to Aaron: “Approach the altar and slaughter your sin offering. Offer the burnt offering and intercede for yourself and for the people. When you have slaughtered the people’s victim, pray for them, as the Lord commanded.” [Col. 0309C]

Immediately Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the bull for his sin. His sons presented its blood to him; dipping his finger in it, he touched the horns of the altar and poured the remainder at its base.

He burned the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver, which are for the sin offering, upon the altar, as the Lord had commanded Moses. But he burned its flesh and hide outside the camp. [Col. 0310A]

He slaughtered the victim of the burnt offering. His sons presented its blood to him, and he poured it around the altar. They also presented the victim, cut into pieces, with its head and each of its limbs. He burned all these upon the altar [Hebrew lacks: “with fire”], after first washing the entrails and legs with water.

For the sin of the people he offered and slaughtered a male goat. After making atonement for the altar [Hebrew: “after washing and offering it”], he made the burnt offering, adding the libations that are offered with it, and burning them upon the altar, apart from the rites of the morning burnt offering.

He also slaughtered the ox and the ram as the people’s peace offerings. His sons presented their blood to him, and he poured it around the altar. [Col. 0310B]

They placed the fat of the ox, the tail of the ram [Hebrew: “the fat of the ox and the ram, and the tail of the ram”], the kidneys with their fat, and the lobe of the liver upon the breasts.

When the fat had been burned upon the altar, Aaron separated their breasts and right shoulders, lifting them before the Lord, as Moses had commanded.

> **Note:** Various small readings occur here in the Hebrew and Samaritan texts. The Hebrew reads *el ha-am*, “to the people”; the Samaritan reads *al ha-am*, “upon” or “against the people.” MART. The Urbinas and Palatine manuscripts read *extendens* (“stretching out”); this follows the Hebrew more closely, “to the people,” and “he blessed him,” rather than “them.” [Col. 0310D]

Stretching out his hand toward the people, he blessed them. When he had completed the sin offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings, he came down.

Then Moses and Aaron entered the Tent of Witness; afterward they came out and blessed the people.

[B. V.]

The glory of the Lord appeared to the whole multitude. Behold, fire came out from the Lord and consumed the burnt offering and the fat that was upon the altar. When the crowds saw this, they praised the Lord and fell upon their faces. [Col. 0310C]

[C. XII, Chapter X]

Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took censers, placed fire and incense upon them, and offered before the Lord strange fire, which he had not commanded them to offer.

Fire went out from the Lord and consumed them, and they died before the Lord. Moses said to Aaron: “This is what the Lord has spoken: ‘I shall be sanctified in those who draw near to me, and in the sight of all the people I shall be glorified.’”

When Aaron heard this, he was silent.

Moses summoned Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, Aaron’s uncle, and said to them: “Go and carry your brothers away from the presence of the sanctuary, and take them outside the camp.”

They immediately went and carried them away as they lay, clothed in linen tunics, and cast them outside [Hebrew: “they immediately went and carried them out in their tunics, and cast them outside”], as they had been commanded. [Col. 0310D]

Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons: “Do not uncover your heads and do not tear your garments, lest you die and indignation arise against the whole assembly. Let your brothers, the whole house of Israel [our manuscripts: ‘and all’], mourn the burning that the Lord has kindled.

“But you shall not leave the doors of the Tent, lest you perish; for the oil of the holy anointing is upon you.”

They did everything according to Moses’ command. [Col. 0311A]

[T. VI, C. XIII]

The Lord also said to Aaron: “You and your sons shall not drink wine or anything that can intoxicate when you enter the Tent of Witness, lest you die; for [Hebrew lacks this phrase] it is a perpetual commandment throughout your generations.

“You are to have the knowledge to distinguish between holy and profane, between unclean and clean, and you are to teach the children of Israel all my statutes that the Lord has spoken to them through Moses.”

[C. XIV]

Moses spoke to Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar, his sons who remained:

“Take the sacrifice that remains from the Lord’s offering and eat it without leaven beside the altar, because it is most holy. You shall eat it in a holy place, for it has been given to you and your sons from the Lord’s offerings, as I was commanded. [Col. 0311B]

“You and your sons and your daughters with you shall eat the breast that was offered and the shoulder that was separated, in a completely clean place. For these have been set aside for you and your children from the peace offerings of the children of Israel, because they lifted up before the Lord the shoulder and the breast and the fat that is burned upon the altar. They shall belong to you and to your sons as a perpetual ordinance, as the Lord commanded.”

Meanwhile, when Moses looked for the male goat that had been offered for sin, he found that it had been burned. He became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons, and said:

“Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place, since it is most holy and has been given to you so that you may bear the iniquity of the multitude and intercede for them before the Lord—especially since its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary, and you ought to have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I was commanded?” [Col. 0311C]

Aaron replied: “Today the victim for sin and the burnt offering were offered before the Lord; yet what you see has happened to me. How could I have eaten it, or pleased the Lord through the rites, with a sorrowful heart?”

When Moses heard this, he accepted the explanation.

[B. VI, C. XV, Cap. XI.] The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: Say to the children of Israel: These [Col. 0311D] are the animals that you may eat from all the living creatures [h. quadrupeds] of the earth: Everything that has a divided hoof and chews the cud among the animals, you may eat. But whatever does indeed chew the cud and has a hoof, yet does not divide it, such as the camel and the rest, you shall not eat; you shall regard it as unclean. The *choerogryllus*, which chews the cud but does not divide the hoof, is unclean; the hare likewise, for it too chews the cud but does not divide the hoof. And the pig, although it divides the hoof, does not chew the cud. You shall not eat their flesh, nor touch their carcasses, because they are unclean for you.

[C. XVI.] These likewise are the creatures born in the waters, and which it is lawful to eat. Everything that has fins and scales, both in the sea and in rivers and pools [h. does not have, and in pools], you may eat. But whatever among those that move and live in the waters does not have fins and scales shall be abominable and detestable to you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall avoid their carcasses. Everything in the waters that does not have fins and scales shall be polluted.

[C. XVII.] These are the birds that you must not eat and that must be avoided by you: the eagle, the griffin, and the osprey; the kite and the vulture according to their kind; every creature of the raven kind according to its likeness; the ostrich, the owl, the gull, and the hawk according to its kind; the horned owl, the cormorant, the ibis, the swan, the pelican, the [Col. 0312B] purple bird, the heron, and the plover according to its kind; also the hoopoe and the bat.

[C. XVIII.] Every winged creature that walks on four feet shall be abominable to you. But whatever walks on four feet and has longer hind legs, by which it leaps over the ground, you may eat, such as the *bruchus* according to its kind, the *attacus*, the *ophiomachus*, and the locust, each according to its kind. Whatever among the winged creatures has only four feet shall be detestable to you; and whoever touches their carcasses shall be defiled and shall be unclean until evening. If it is necessary for anyone to carry any of these dead creatures [h. and whoever carries any of these dead creatures], he shall wash his garments and be unclean until sunset.

Every animal that has a hoof but does not divide it and does not chew the cud shall be unclean, and whoever touches it shall be defiled. Whatever walks on its hands, among all the living creatures that go on four feet, shall be unclean. Whoever touches their carcasses shall be polluted until evening. Whoever carries such carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening, because all these are unclean for you.

These too shall be counted among the polluted creatures that move upon the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the crocodile, each according to its kind; the shrew, the chameleon, the gecko, the lizard, and the mole. All these are unclean. Whoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening. Whatever any of their carcasses falls upon shall be polluted, whether a wooden vessel, a garment, skins, or sackcloth; and every article used for any work shall be immersed in water, and they shall be unclean until evening, after which they shall become clean.

But an earthen vessel into which any of these things falls shall be polluted, and therefore it must be broken. Every food that you eat, if water has been poured over it, shall be unclean; and every liquid that is drunk from any vessel shall be unclean. Whatever from such carcasses falls upon it shall be unclean, whether ovens or cooking pots; they shall be destroyed and shall be unclean.

But springs [Col. 0313A] and cisterns, and every collection of water, shall be clean. Whoever touches their carcasses shall be polluted. If they fall upon seed, they shall not pollute it. But if someone pours water upon the seed, and afterward it is touched by their carcasses, it shall immediately become polluted.

If an animal dies that you are permitted to eat, whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening. Whoever eats anything from it, or carries it, shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.

[C. XIX.] Everything that creeps upon the earth shall be abominable and shall not be taken as food. Whatever walks upon its breast on four feet and has many feet, or drags itself along the ground, you shall not eat, because it is abominable. Do not defile your souls, and do not touch any of them, lest you become unclean. [Col. 0313B] For I am the Lord your God. Be holy, because I am holy. Do not pollute your souls with any creeping creature that moves upon the earth. For I am the Lord who brought you out of the land of Egypt, so that I might be your God. You shall be holy, because I am holy.

This is the law concerning animals and birds, every living creature that moves in the water and creeps upon the earth, so that you may know the distinctions between clean and unclean and may know what you ought to eat and what you ought to reject.

[B. VII, C. XX, Cap. XII.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: If a woman, having received seed [h. seed having been emitted], gives birth to a male, she shall be unclean for seven days, as during the days of the separation caused by her menstruation. On the eighth day [Col. 0313C] the infant shall be circumcised. She herself shall remain thirty-three days in the blood of her purification. She shall touch nothing holy and shall not enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification have been completed.

[C. XXI.] But if she gives birth to a female, she shall be unclean for two weeks, according to the manner of menstrual discharge, and shall remain sixty-six days in the blood of her purification. When the days of her purification have been completed, for a son or for a daughter she shall bring a yearling lamb as a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove as a sin offering, to the door of the tabernacle of testimony. She shall deliver them to the priest, who shall offer them before the Lord and pray for her; thus she shall be cleansed from her flow of blood. This is the law for a woman giving birth to a male or a female.

But if her hand cannot find the means, and she is unable to offer a lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a burnt offering and the other as a sin offering. The priest shall pray for her, and thus she shall be cleansed.

[B. VII, C. XXII, Cap. XIII.] And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: If a person’s skin and flesh develop a different-colored swelling, or a pustule, or something resembling a shining spot—that is, a lesion of leprosy—he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons. When he sees the leprosy on the skin, and the hairs have been turned white, and the appearance of the leprosy is lower than the surrounding skin and flesh, it is a lesion of leprosy, and he shall be separated according to the priest’s decision.

But if there is a shining whiteness on the skin, and it is not lower than the surrounding flesh, and the hairs retain their former color, the priest shall shut him up for seven days. On the seventh day he shall examine him, and if the leprosy has not spread farther and has not crossed its former boundaries on the skin, he shall shut him up again [Vulg. shall shut him up] for another seven days. On the seventh day he shall examine him. If the leprosy is darker and has not spread on the skin, he shall pronounce him clean, because it is a scab. The man shall wash his garments and shall be clean.

But if, after he has been examined by the priest and restored to cleanness, the leprosy spreads again, he shall be brought to the priest and condemned as unclean. If a lesion of leprosy is on a person, he shall be brought to the priest, who shall examine him. When there is a white color on the skin, the appearance of the hair has changed, and living flesh has appeared, it shall be judged a very old leprosy that has become established in the skin. The priest shall therefore declare him unclean and shall not shut him up, [Note: [Col. 0313D] Here it can also be read, as in the canon and in several manuscript books, “because it is clearly uncleanness.” MART. —One Palatine manuscript has *condemnabit*, “he shall condemn,” and shortly afterward, together with the Urbinate and others in Martianay, “because it is clearly uncleanness.”] because it is manifestly uncleanness.

But if the leprosy breaks out and spreads over the skin and covers the entire skin from head to feet, whatever comes under the priest’s eyes, the priest shall examine him [h. under the priest’s eyes], and shall judge him wholly clean of leprosy, because the whole has turned white; the man shall therefore be clean. But whenever living flesh appears in him, he shall be polluted by the priest’s judgment and counted among the unclean. For if living flesh is covered with leprosy, it is unclean. But if it turns white again [Col. 0314C] and covers the entire person, the priest shall examine him and declare him clean.

The flesh and skin in which a sore has arisen and healed, and in the place of the sore a white or reddish scar has appeared, shall be brought to the priest. When he sees that the place of the leprosy is lower than the surrounding flesh and that the hairs have turned white, he shall declare him unclean, for a lesion of leprosy has arisen in the sore. But if the hair retains its former color, the scar is somewhat dark, and it is not lower than the neighboring flesh, he shall shut him up for seven days. If it has spread, he shall judge him to have leprosy. But if it remains in its place, it is the scar of a sore, and the man shall be clean.

The flesh and skin that fire has burned, and that, after healing, has a white or reddish scar, the priest shall examine. If it has turned white [Col. 0314D] [h. And behold, the hair has turned white], and its place is lower than the surrounding skin, he shall declare him unclean, because a lesion of leprosy has arisen in the scar. But if the color of the hairs has not changed, the lesion is not lower than the surrounding flesh, and the appearance of the leprosy is somewhat dark, he shall shut him up for seven days. On the seventh day he shall examine him. If the leprosy has spread on the skin, he shall declare him unclean. But if the whiteness remains in its place without being sufficiently distinct, it is the lesion of a burn, and therefore he shall be cleansed, because it is the scar of a burn.

Whether a man or a woman has leprosy growing on the head or in the beard, the priest shall examine them. If the place is lower than the surrounding flesh, and the hair is yellow and thinner than usual, he shall declare them unclean, because it is leprosy of the head or beard. But if he sees that the place of the spot is level with the neighboring flesh and the hair is black, he shall shut him up for seven days and examine him on the seventh day. If the spot has not spread, the hair is of its own color, and the place of the lesion is level with the surrounding flesh, the man shall be shaved, except for the place of the spot, and shall be shut up for another seven days. If on the seventh day the lesion appears to have remained in its place and is not lower than the surrounding flesh, he shall declare him clean. After washing his garments, he shall be clean.

But if, after his cleansing, the spot spreads again on the skin, he shall no longer inquire whether the hair has changed to yellow, because he is plainly unclean. But if the spot remains and the hairs are black [Col. 0315B], he should know that the man has been healed and should confidently pronounce him clean.

Whether a man or a woman has a whiteness appearing on the skin, the priest shall examine them. If he finds that a somewhat dark whiteness shines on the skin, he shall know that it is not leprosy but a white-colored spot, and that the person is clean.

A man from whose head the hair falls is bald and clean; and if the hair falls from his forehead, he is front-bald and clean. But if a white or reddish color appears on the baldness or front-baldness, and the priest sees this, he shall unquestionably condemn him as having leprosy that has arisen on the baldness.

Therefore whoever is marked by leprosy and separated according to the priest’s decision shall wear torn garments [h. rent], keep his head uncovered, cover his mouth with his clothing, and cry out that he is contaminated and unclean [Col. 0315C] [h. he shall proclaim him contaminated and unclean]. For all the time that he is a leper and unclean, he shall live alone outside the camp.

A woolen or linen garment that has leprosy in its warp or woof, or a skin or anything made from skin, if it is infected with a white or reddish spot, shall be regarded as leprosy and shall be shown to the priest. After examining it, he shall shut it up for seven days. On the seventh day, looking again, if he finds that it has spread, it is persistent leprosy. He shall declare the garment and everything in which it is found polluted, and therefore it shall be burned in the flames.

But if he sees that it has not spread, he shall command that the thing in which the leprosy is found be washed, and he shall shut it up for another seven days. When he sees that its former appearance has not returned, although the leprosy has not spread, he shall declare it unclean [Col. 0315D] and burn it in the fire, because the leprosy has penetrated the surface or the whole of the garment.

But if the place of the leprosy is darker after the garment has been washed, he shall tear it away and separate it from the whole. If it appears again in those places that were previously unblemished, it is a flying and spreading leprosy; it must be burned in the fire. If it ceases, he shall wash [Note: [Col. 0315] It seems that, from the words written by one person as *aqua*, “with water,” the printed books have resulted in preferring both readings together.] the clean portions a second time, and they shall be clean.

This is the law concerning the leprosy of a woolen or linen garment, of its warp and woof, and of every leather article: how it is to be cleansed or declared unclean.

[C. XXIII, Cap. XIV.] And the Lord spoke [Col. 0316A] to Moses, saying: This is the ritual for the leper when he is to be cleansed. He shall be brought to the priest, who, going outside the camp, shall find that the leprosy has been cleansed. He shall command the person being purified to offer on his behalf two living sparrows of a kind permitted as food, cedar wood, scarlet material, and hyssop. He shall order one of the sparrows to be slaughtered in an earthen vessel over living water. But the other living sparrow, together with the cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop, he shall dip in the blood of the slaughtered sparrow. With it he shall sprinkle the one who is to be cleansed seven times, so that he may be properly purified, and he shall release the living sparrow to fly into the open country.

When the man has washed his garments, he shall shave all the hair of his body and wash himself with water. After he has been purified, he shall enter the camp, but only on condition that he remain outside his tent [Col. 0316B] for seven days. On the seventh day he shall shave the hair of his head, his beard, his eyebrows, and all the hair of his body. After washing his garments and his body again, on the eighth day he shall take two unblemished lambs, a yearling ewe without blemish, three-tenths of a measure of fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice, and separately one sextary of oil.

When the priest who purifies the man has placed him, and all these things, before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony, he shall take one lamb and offer it as a guilt offering, together with the sextary of oil. After all have been offered before the Lord, he shall slaughter the lamb where the sin offering and the burnt offering are accustomed to be slaughtered—that is, in the holy place. For just as the sin offering belongs to the priest, so does the guilt offering; it is most holy.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sacrifice that was offered as a guilt offering and place it on the tip of the right ear of the one being cleansed, and on the thumbs of his right hand and right foot. From the sextary of oil he shall pour into his own left hand, dip his right finger into it, and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord [Vulg. in the presence of the Lord]. Whatever remains of the oil in his left hand he shall put on the tip of the right ear of the one being cleansed, on the thumbs of his right hand and right foot, over the blood poured out for the guilt offering, and upon his head. He shall pray for him before the Lord and offer the sin offering.

Then he shall slaughter the burnt offering and place it on the altar with its libations, and the man shall be properly cleansed.

But if he is poor and cannot afford the things mentioned, he shall take one lamb as a guilt offering, so that the priest may pray [Col. 0316D] for him, one-tenth of a measure of fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice, one sextary of oil, and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. On the eighth day of his purification he shall offer these to the priest at the door of the tabernacle of testimony before the Lord.

The priest, receiving the lamb as a guilt offering and the sextary of oil, shall raise them together. After slaughtering the lamb, he shall place some of its blood on the tip of the right ear of the one being cleansed and on the thumbs of his right hand and right foot. He shall put some of the oil into his left hand, dip the finger of his right hand into it, [Col. 0317A] and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord. He shall touch the tip of the right ear of the one being cleansed and the thumbs of his right hand and right foot with it, in the place of the blood poured out for the guilt offering. The remaining oil in his left hand he shall place upon the head of the purified person, so that the Lord may be favorably disposed toward him. He shall offer the turtledove or young pigeon, one as a guilt offering and the other as a burnt offering with its libations.

This is the sacrifice of the leper who cannot obtain everything required for his cleansing.

[C. XXIV.] And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: When you enter the land of Canaan, which I shall give you as a possession, if there is a leprous lesion in a house, the owner of the house shall go and report it to the priest, saying: “It seems to me that there is a leprous lesion in my house.” He shall then command that everything be removed from the house before he enters it and sees whether it is leprous [Vulg. whether it is affected by leprosy], lest everything that is in the house become unclean.

Afterward he shall enter to inspect the leprosy of the house. When he sees on its walls something like hollows disfigured by pale or reddish color and lower than the rest of the surface, he shall go out through the door of the house and immediately shut it for seven days. Returning on the seventh day, he shall inspect it. If he finds that the leprosy has spread, he shall order the stones in which the leprosy is found to be removed and thrown outside the city into an unclean place. He shall have the house scraped inside all around, and the scrapings shall be scattered outside the city in an unclean place. Other stones shall be put in place of those removed, and the house shall be plastered with other mortar.

But if, after the stones have been removed, the plaster scraped away, and the house plastered with other earth, the priest enters and sees that the leprosy has returned and that the walls are covered with spots [Vulg. sprinkled with spots], it is persistent leprosy, and the house is unclean. It shall immediately be demolished, and its stones, timbers, and all its plaster shall be thrown outside the town into an unclean place.

Whoever enters the house while it is closed shall be unclean until evening. Whoever sleeps in it or eats anything in it shall wash his garments.

But if the priest enters and sees that the leprosy has not spread in the house after it has been plastered again, he shall purify it, since its condition has been restored. For its purification he shall take two sparrows, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop. After slaughtering one sparrow in an earthen vessel over living water, he shall take the cedar wood, hyssop, [Col. 0317D] scarlet, and the living sparrow, dip everything in the blood of the slaughtered sparrow and in the living water, and sprinkle the house seven times. Thus he shall purify it with the blood of the sparrow, the living water, the living sparrow, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet. When he has released the sparrow to fly freely into the open country, he shall pray for the house, and it shall properly be cleansed.

This is the law concerning every kind of leprosy and lesion: the leprosy of garments and houses, scars and erupting pustules, shining spots, and changes of color into various forms, so that it may be known at what time something is clean or unclean.

[T. VIII, B. VIII, C. XXV, Cap. XV.] And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: A man who suffers from a discharge of semen shall be unclean. He shall be judged subject to this condition when, moment by moment, the foul humor adheres to his flesh and gathers.

Every bed on which he sleeps shall be unclean, and everything on which he sits. If anyone touches his bed, he shall wash his garments, and after washing himself with water shall be unclean until evening. If he sits where that man sat, he too shall wash his garments, and after washing himself with water shall be unclean until evening. Whoever touches his flesh shall wash his garments, and after washing himself with water shall be unclean until evening. If such a man spits upon someone who is clean, that person shall wash his garments, and after washing himself with water shall be unclean until evening.

The saddlecloth on which he sits shall be unclean, and whatever is beneath the one who suffers from the discharge of semen shall be polluted until evening. Whoever carries any of these things shall wash his garments, and after washing himself with water shall be unclean until evening. Everyone whom such a person touches without first washing his hands shall wash his garments, and after washing himself with water shall be unclean until evening.

An earthen vessel that he touches shall be broken [h. the person suffering from the discharge of semen shall break it]; but a wooden vessel shall be washed with water.

If the person suffering from such an affliction is healed, he shall count seven days after his cleansing. After washing his garments and his whole body in living water, he shall be clean. On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and come before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony. [Col. 0318C] He shall give them to the priest, who shall make one a sin offering and the other a burnt offering. He shall pray for him before the Lord, so that he may be cleansed from his discharge of semen.

A man from whom the seed of intercourse goes out shall wash his whole body with water and shall be unclean until evening. He shall wash with water the garment and skin that he has, and they shall be unclean until evening. The woman with whom he has intercourse shall wash herself with water and be unclean until evening.

[C. XXVI.] A woman who suffers from a flow of blood when her month returns [h. a woman who suffers from a flow of blood] shall be separated for seven days. Everyone who touches her shall be unclean until evening. Everything on which she sleeps or sits during the days of her separation shall be polluted. Whoever touches her bed shall wash his garments, and after washing himself [Col. 0318D] with water shall be unclean until evening. Whoever touches any vessel on which she has sat shall wash his garments and [Vulg. adds: he himself], after washing himself with water, shall be polluted until evening.

If a man has intercourse with her during the time of her menstrual blood, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he sleeps shall be polluted.

A woman who suffers for many days from a flow of blood outside the time of menstruation, or whose flow continues after the menstrual blood, shall be unclean for as long as she is subject to this condition, as though she were in the time of menstruation. Every bed on which she sleeps and every vessel on which she sits shall be polluted. Whoever touches them shall wash his garments, and after washing himself with water shall be unclean until evening.

If the blood stops and the flow ceases, she shall count seven days for her purification. On the eighth day she shall offer on her behalf to the priest, at the door of the tabernacle of testimony, two turtledoves or two young pigeons. He shall make one a sin offering and the other a burnt offering, and shall pray for her before the Lord and for the discharge of her uncleanness.

Therefore you shall teach the children of Israel to beware of uncleanness, so that they do not die in their defilements when they pollute my tabernacle, which is among them.

This is the law for the one who suffers a discharge of semen, the one polluted by intercourse, the woman separated during her menstrual periods, the woman who continually flows with blood, and the man who has slept with her.

[T. IX, B. IX, C. XXXVII, Cap. XVI.] The Lord spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron’s two sons, when they were killed while offering unauthorized fire, and he commanded him, saying: Speak to Aaron your brother, that he may not enter the sanctuary at all times, within the veil before the mercy seat that covers the ark, lest he die—for I shall appear in a cloud over the oracle—unless he has first done these things.

He shall offer a young bull as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering. He shall put on a linen tunic and cover his nakedness with linen undergarments. He shall gird himself with a linen sash and place a linen turban on his head. These are holy garments; after he has washed himself, he shall put them on.

From the entire assembly of the children of Israel he shall receive two he-goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering. When he has offered the bull and prayed for himself and his household, he shall make the two he-goats stand before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony, [Note: [Col. 0319C] Certain very ancient membranes surviving from the lost Veronese manuscript, with which we have compared this chapter, the following chapter, and several other passages below, here read *in ostia*, “at the doors.”] casting lots over the two: one lot for the Lord and the other [h. and the other for the cruel god] [Note: [Col. 0319D] The name is explained here by the Scholiast, although in Hebrew it is *laazazel*, that is, “for Azazel.” Below, in verse 26, our Scholiast again interprets Azazel as “the cruel god,” because he thinks that *azazel* is a compound of *azaz* and *el*, so that *azazel* is read in place of *azazel*, which properly means “harsh,” “savage,” or “cruel of God.” The Syriac interpreter seems to have held the same view, for here he has *lazozojel*, that is, “to the strongest God,” or “to the cruel god,” according to the marginal annotation. Rabbi Saadias Gaon likewise approves this etymology of the word *azazel*. But other Hebrew scholars reject it; preserving the order of the letters, they say that the word *azazel* is formed from *ez*, “goat,” and *azal*, “he went away.” In this sense the Greeks and Latins understand the word, all those who wish *Azazel* to have been the name of the goat sent into the wilderness. Concerning the scapegoat, see more in the learned Bochart, *On the Animals of Scripture*, book II, chapter 54. MART. —The Palatine and Urbinate manuscripts have “casting one lot over each of the two,” etc. In place of “for the scapegoat,” the Scholiast translates “for the cruel god.” This is an explanation of the Hebrew word *laazazel*. Consult the interpreters of this passage.]

The goat upon which the lot for the Lord has fallen he shall offer as a sin offering. But the goat upon which the lot for the scapegoat has fallen he shall set alive before the Lord, to pour out prayers over it and send it into the wilderness [h. to Lazazel in the wilderness].

After duly performing these rites, he shall offer the bull and, praying for himself and his household, slaughter it. Taking a censer that he has filled with coals from the altar, and gathering a handful of prepared incense, he shall enter beyond the veil into the holy place, [Note: [Col. 0320D] The Veronese membranes read “and having placed.” Shortly afterward, in the Urbinate manuscript, the words “before the Lord” are absent.] so that, when the aromatics have been placed upon the fire [Col. 0320A] before the Lord, their cloud and vapor may cover the oracle that is above the testimony [Ms. “will cover”], and he may not die.

He shall also take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger seven times [Note: [Col. 0320D] The Palatine manuscript here also inserts “before the Lord.”] [h. He shall also take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it upon the mercy seat toward the east, and before the mercy seat he shall sprinkle seven times] toward the mercy seat on the eastern side.

When he has slaughtered the goat as a sin offering for the people, he shall bring its blood inside the veil, as he was commanded concerning the bull’s blood, so that he may sprinkle it opposite the oracle [h. so that he may sprinkle it upon the mercy seat and before the mercy seat], and may make atonement for the sanctuary from the uncleannesses of the children of Israel, their transgressions, and all their sins.

According to this rite he shall act for the tabernacle of testimony, which is fixed among them in the midst of the uncleanness of their dwelling [Col. 0320B]. No human being shall be in the tabernacle [Note: [Col. 0320D] Our manuscripts and printed books omit the word “of testimony” here, although it is present in Hebrew.] of testimony when the high priest enters the sanctuary to pray for himself, his household, and the entire assembly of Israel, until he comes out.

When he has gone out to the altar that is before the Lord, he shall pray for himself [Note: [Col. 0320D] The Palatine manuscript also adds “and for his household,” contrary to the Hebrew text. Then the Veronese membranes have: “and taking the blood of the bull, etc., he shall sprinkle seven times with his finger, and shall make atonement and sanctify.” The Palatine manuscript has “sprinkling … he shall make atonement and shall be sanctified”; finally, the Urbinate differs by this one word, “he shall sanctify.”], take the blood of the bull and the goat, and pour it around upon the horns of the altar. He shall sprinkle it seven times with his finger and cleanse and sanctify it from the uncleannesses of the children of Israel.

After he has cleansed the sanctuary, the tabernacle, and the altar, he shall then offer the living goat. Placing both hands upon its head, he shall confess all the iniquities of the children of Israel and all their offenses and sins. Having invoked them upon its head, he shall send it away by the hand of a man prepared for this purpose into the wilderness.

When the goat has carried all their iniquities into a solitary land and has been released in the wilderness, Aaron shall return to the tabernacle of testimony. He shall remove the garments that he had previously worn when he entered the sanctuary and leave them there. He shall wash his flesh in the holy place and put on his own garments.

After he has gone out and offered his own burnt offering and that of the people, he shall pray both for himself and for the people, and shall burn upon the altar the fat that was offered for sins.

The one who released the scapegoat [in Latin it has *emissarius*, “sent away”; in Hebrew it has “to Azazel,” which is interpreted as “cruel”] shall wash his garments and his body with water, and then enter the camp [Col. 0321A].

But the bull and the goat that were slaughtered as sin offerings, whose blood [Note: [Col. 0321D] The Palatine manuscript incorrectly has “whose blood was offered.” The Vulgate translator has “was brought into the sanctuary, so that atonement might be completed,” etc.] was brought in so that atonement might be completed in the sanctuary, shall be carried outside the camp. Their skins, flesh, and dung shall be burned in the fire. Whoever burns them shall wash his garments and his flesh with water, and then enter the camp.

This shall be for you a perpetual ordinance.

[C. XXVIII.] On the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls and perform no work, whether native-born or a foreigner who dwells among you. On that day atonement shall be made for you, and you shall be cleansed from all your sins [Note: [Col. 0321D] The Urbinate manuscript omits the words “before the Lord.”] before the Lord. For it is a sabbath of rest, and you shall afflict your souls as a perpetual religious observance.

The priest who has been anointed and whose hands have been consecrated to exercise the priesthood in place of his father shall make atonement. He shall put on a linen robe and holy garments, and shall make atonement for the sanctuary, the tabernacle of testimony, and the altar, as well as for the priests and the entire people.

This shall be for you a perpetual ordinance: you shall pray for the children of Israel and for all their sins once a year.

And he did as the Lord had commanded Moses.

[T. X, C. XXIV, Chapter XVII.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the children of Israel, and say to them: This is the word which the Lord has commanded, saying: Any man of the house of Israel who kills an ox, sheep, or goat in the camp or outside the camp, and does not bring it as an offering to the Lord at the entrance of the tabernacle, shall be guilty of bloodshed; he has shed blood, and that man shall be cut off from among his people. Therefore the children of Israel must bring to the priest the sacrifices that they kill in the open country,

[Note: [Col. 0321D] The manuscript of Saint-Germain, no. 3, reads: “that they may sacrifice to the Lord,” etc. In Hebrew we read *vehevîʾû*, “and let them bring them.” The sense is that the children of Israel should bring their victims to the entrance of the tabernacle, so that there they may be consecrated to the Lord or offered by the hands of the priests. [Col. 0322D] MART.]

so that they may be consecrated to the Lord before the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony, and may sacrifice them as sacrifices of peace to the Lord. The priest shall pour the blood upon the altar of the Lord at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony, and shall burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. They shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to demons, with whom they have played the harlot. This shall be an everlasting statute for them and for their descendants.

And you shall say to them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of the resident foreigners who dwell among you, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice but does not bring it to the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony to offer it to the Lord, shall perish from his people.

[C. XXX.] Any man of the house of Israel and of the resident foreigners who dwell among you, if he eats blood, I will set my face against that person and cut him off from his people, because the life of the flesh is in the blood. I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives, and the blood shall serve as atonement for the life.

Therefore I said to the children of Israel: No person among you shall eat blood, nor shall any of the resident foreigners who dwell among you eat blood. Any man, whether one of the children of Israel or one of the resident foreigners who dwell among you, who catches a wild animal or a bird by hunting or fowling—animals that may be eaten—shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth [Hebrew: dust]. For the life of every creature is in its blood. Therefore I said to the children of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any creature, because the life of every creature is in its blood; whoever eats it shall perish.

[C. XXXI.] Any person who eats an animal that has died of itself or has been torn by a beast, whether native-born or resident foreigner, shall wash his clothes and bathe himself in water, and shall be unclean until evening; then he shall be clean. But if he does not wash his clothes and bathe his body, he shall bear his guilt.

[B. X, C. XXXII, Chapter XVIII.] The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: I am the Lord your God. You shall not act according to the customs [Hebrew: works] of the land of Egypt, in which you lived, nor shall you act according to the practices [Hebrew: works] of the land of Canaan, to which I am bringing you; you shall not follow their ordinances. You shall carry out my judgments, keep my commandments, and walk in them [Hebrew: so that you may walk in them]. I am the Lord your God. Keep my statutes and judgments; the person who does them shall live by them. I am the Lord.

No man shall approach a close relative [Hebrew: flesh of his flesh] to uncover that person’s nakedness. I am the Lord. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother; she is your mother. You shall not uncover her nakedness. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife; for it is your father’s nakedness. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, whether she is your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether born at home or elsewhere. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s granddaughter, for it is your own nakedness. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, whom she bore to your father; she is your sister [Hebrew: whom she bore to your father; do not uncover her, for she is your sister]. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister, for she is your father’s flesh [Hebrew: relative]. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister, for she is your mother’s flesh [Hebrew: relative]. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your paternal uncle [the Vulgate omits “your”], nor approach his wife, who is related to you by marriage [Hebrew: she is your paternal uncle’s wife].

[Col. 0322D] You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law, for she is your son’s wife; you shall not uncover her shame. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife, for it is your brother’s nakedness. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your wife and her daughter [Hebrew: the woman and her daughter]. You shall not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter in order to uncover her shame, for they are her flesh [Hebrew: her close relatives], and such intercourse is incestuous. You shall not take your wife’s sister as a rival wife while she is still living, nor uncover her nakedness.

You shall not approach a woman during her menstrual period, nor uncover her uncleanness. You shall not lie with your neighbor’s wife, nor defile yourself by an emission of semen. You shall not give any of your offspring to be consecrated to the idol Molech, nor profane the name of your God. I am the Lord.

[C. XXXIII.] You shall not lie with a male as with a woman, for it is an abomination. You shall not lie with any animal, nor defile yourself with it. A woman shall not submit herself to an animal or mate with it, for it is a disgrace.

Do not defile yourselves by any of these things, by which all the nations have been defiled [Hebrew omits this word], whom I am casting out before you, and by which the land has been polluted. I will visit its crimes, so that it vomits out its inhabitants. Keep my statutes and judgments, and do not commit any of these abominations, whether native-born or resident foreigner dwelling among you. For the inhabitants of the land who were here before you committed all these abominations, and they polluted it. Take care lest the land vomit you out as well, when you commit the same things, just as it vomited out the nation that was here before you. Every person who commits any of these abominations shall be cut off from among his people. Keep my commandments. Do not do what those who were here before you did, and do not defile yourselves by them. I am the Lord your God.

[T. XI, C. XXXIV, Chapter XIX.] The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to all the assembly of the children of Israel, and say to them: You shall be holy, because I, the Lord your God, am holy. Let each person fear his mother [the Vulgate adds “his”] and his father. Keep my Sabbaths. I am the Lord your God.

Do not turn to idols, and do not make cast gods for yourselves. I am the Lord your God.

If you sacrifice a sacrifice of peace offerings to the Lord, so that it may be acceptable, you shall eat it on the day it is sacrificed and on the following day [Hebrew: If you sacrifice a peace offering, sacrifice it voluntarily; it shall be eaten on the day it is sacrificed and on the following day]. Whatever remains until the third day you shall burn with fire. If anyone eats from it after the second day, he shall be profane and guilty of impiety. He shall bear his guilt, because he has profaned what is holy to the Lord; that person shall perish from his people.

[C. XXXV.] When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not cut your field down to its very edge, nor gather the ears that remain [Hebrew: When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap the whole field, but leave part of it]. You shall not gather the fallen grapes and berries from your vineyard, but leave them for the poor and for resident foreigners to glean. I am the Lord your God.

[C. XXXVI.] You shall not steal. You shall not lie, and no one shall deceive his neighbor.

[Note: [Col. 0323D] The canon, together with several manuscripts, reads: “You shall not swear falsely,” which has the same meaning. MART. —The Urbinas manuscript reads: “nor shall he deceive.” Immediately afterward, Hesychius serves as a witness for the Hieronymian translation in this passage of Leviticus: “You shall not profane the name of the Lord your God,” whereas Jerome’s translation reads: “You shall not pollute the name of your God.” [Col. 0324D]]

You shall not swear falsely by my name, nor profane [Hebrew: violate] the name of your God. I am the Lord.

[C. XXXVII.] You shall not defraud your neighbor, nor oppress him by force [Hebrew: by fraud].

[C. XXXVIII.] The wages of a hired laborer [the Vulgate adds “your”] shall not remain with you until morning.

[C. XXXIX.] You shall not curse the deaf.

[C. XL.] You shall not place a stumbling block before the blind.

[C. XLI.] But you shall fear your God, for [Hebrew omits this] I am [Hebrew omits this] the Lord.

[C. XLII.] You shall not do what is unjust, nor judge unjustly [Hebrew: what is unjust in judgment].

[C. XLIII.] You shall not show partiality to the poor, nor honor the face of the powerful. Judge your neighbor justly.

[C. XLIV.] You shall not be a slanderer, nor a whisperer among the people.

[C. XLV.] You shall not stand against the blood of your neighbor. I am the Lord.

[C. XLVI.] You shall not hate your brother in your heart; instead, rebuke him openly, lest you incur sin because of him. You shall not seek vengeance, nor remember the injury done by your fellow citizens.

[C. XLVII.] You shall love your friend [Hebrew: neighbor] as yourself. I am the Lord. Keep my laws [Hebrew: my statutes].

[C. XLVIII.] You shall not mate your animals with animals of another kind. You shall not sow your field with mixed seed. You shall not wear a garment woven from two kinds of material.

[C. XLIX, L.] If a man lies with a woman in an emission of semen, and she is both a slave and marriageable [Hebrew: a slave and bound to a husband], but has neither been redeemed for a price nor granted her freedom, both shall be flogged, but they shall not be put to death, because she was not free. For his offense he shall bring a ram to the Lord at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony. The priest shall pray for him and for his offense before the Lord, and atonement shall be made for him, and his sin shall be forgiven.

When you enter the land and plant fruit trees in it, you shall remove their foreskins: their first fruits shall be unclean to you [Hebrew: for three years], and you shall not eat them. In the fourth year all their fruit shall be consecrated as an offering of praise to the Lord. In the fifth year you shall eat their fruit, gathering the produce they yield. I am the Lord your God.

You shall not eat with blood [Hebrew: over blood].

[C. LI.] You shall not practice divination, nor observe dreams. You shall not cut the hair of your head in a circle, nor shave your beard. You shall not make cuts in your flesh for the dead, nor make any figures or marks upon yourselves. I am the Lord.

[C. LII.] Do not prostitute your daughter, lest the land become polluted and filled with guilt. Keep my Sabbaths, and fear my sanctuary. I am the Lord.

[C. LIII.] Do not turn to magicians [Hebrew: *Pithones*], nor inquire of diviners, lest you be defiled by them. I am the Lord your God.

[C. LIV.] Rise before a gray head, and honor the person of an old man; and fear the Lord your God. I am the Lord.

[C. LV.] If a resident foreigner dwells in your land and stays among you [Hebrew omits this], do not reproach him [Hebrew: do not defraud him]. Let him be among you as a native-born person, and you shall love him as yourselves, for you too were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

[C. LVI.] You shall not commit injustice in judgment, in a measuring rod, in weight, or in measure. Let the balance and the weights be just and equal [Hebrew omits this]; let the measure be just and the sextarius equal [Hebrew: let them be yours]. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. Keep all my commandments and all my judgments, and carry them out. I am the Lord.

[T. XII, C. LVII, Chapter XX.] The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Say this to the children of Israel: Any man among the children of Israel or among the resident foreigners dwelling in Israel who gives any of his offspring to the idol Molech shall surely be put to death; the people of the land shall stone him. I will set my face against him, cut him off from among his people, because he has given some of his offspring to Molech and has polluted my sanctuary and profaned [Hebrew: violated] my holy name.

But if the people of the land are negligent and, as though regarding my command as insignificant, let the man who gave some of his offspring to Molech go and refuse to kill him, I will set my face against that man and his family. I will cut him off, together with all who agreed with him to prostitute themselves with Molech, from among his people.

[B. XI, C. LXIII.] Any person who turns to magicians [Hebrew: *Pythones*] and diviners and prostitutes himself with them, I will set my face against that person and destroy him from among his people.

Consecrate yourselves and be holy, [Note: [Col. 0325D] The Septuagint, followed by the Samaritan and Arabic versions, reads as follows: “And you shall be holy, because I, the Lord your God, am holy,” or, “because I am the holy Lord your God.” The Hebrew lacks the words which the scholion says are absent, and in the best Latin Vulgate manuscripts we correctly read: “Be holy, because I am the Lord your God.” [Col. 0326D] Yet, so that we may not offend in any respect and our faith may not waver under the pretext of better readings, we present the text as it stands in its respective places. MART. —The words enclosed in brackets, “and I am holy,” are more correctly absent from the Urbinas manuscript, as well as from the Hebrew and the Vulgate.]

because I [Hebrew omits this] am holy, the Lord your God. Keep my commandments and carry them out. I am the Lord who sanctifies you.

[C. LIX.] Whoever curses his father or mother shall surely be put to death. He has cursed his father and mother; his blood shall be upon him.

[C. LX.] If a man commits adultery with another man’s wife and commits adultery with his neighbor’s spouse, both the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.

[C. LXI.] Whoever lies with his stepmother and uncovers his father’s shame, both shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.

[C. LXII.] If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both shall be put to death, because they have committed a disgraceful act; their blood shall be upon them.

[C. LXIII.] Whoever lies with a male as with a woman, both have committed an abomination; they shall surely be put to death. Their blood shall be upon them.

[C. LXIV.] Whoever takes a woman together with her daughter and marries her mother has committed a disgraceful act; he shall be burned alive with them [Hebrew: both he and the other shall be burned with fire], so that such an enormity may not remain among you.

[C. LXV.] Whoever lies with an animal or beast shall surely be put to death; you shall also kill the animal.

[C. LXVI.] A woman who submits herself to any animal shall be killed together with it; their blood shall be upon them.

[C. LXVII.] Whoever takes his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and sees her nakedness, and she sees her brother’s shame, they have committed an abominable act. They shall be killed in the sight of their people, because they have mutually uncovered their nakedness; they shall bear their guilt.

[C. LXVIII.] Whoever lies with a woman during her menstrual flow and uncovers her nakedness, and she exposes the source of her blood, both shall be cut off from among their people.

You shall not uncover the nakedness of your maternal aunt or paternal aunt. Whoever does this has exposed the shame of his flesh [Hebrew: his close relative]; they shall bear their guilt. Whoever lies with the wife of his paternal uncle or maternal uncle and uncovers the shame of his relative, both shall bear their sin; they shall die childless [Hebrew: Whoever lies with the wife of his paternal uncle and uncovers her nakedness, both shall bear their sin; they shall die childless]. Whoever takes his brother’s wife has done an unlawful thing; he has uncovered his brother’s nakedness. They shall be childless.

Keep my statutes [Hebrew: my ordinances] and judgments, and carry them out, lest the land to which you are entering and in which you will dwell vomit you out. Do not walk according to the ordinances of the nations whom I am casting out before you. For they did all these things, and I abhorred them. But I say to you: Possess their land, which I will give you as an inheritance, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God, who separated you from the other peoples.

Therefore you too shall distinguish between clean and unclean animals, and between clean and unclean birds. Do not defile yourselves with animals, birds, or anything that moves upon the earth, which I have shown you to be unclean. And [the Vulgate omits “and”] you shall be holy to me, because I, the Lord, am holy, and I have separated you from the other peoples so that you may be mine.

[C. LXIX.] A man or woman in whom there is a spirit of a *python* or of divination shall surely be put to death. They shall stone them; their blood shall be upon them.

[T. XIII, C. LXX, Chapter XXI.] The Lord also said to Moses: Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: A priest shall not defile himself by the deaths of his fellow citizens, except for his blood relatives and close kin—that is, for his mother, father, son, daughter, brother, or virgin sister who is not married to a man. He shall not defile himself even for the ruler of his people.

They shall not shave their heads or their beards [Hebrew: They shall not make baldness upon their heads, nor trim their beards], nor make cuts in their flesh. They shall be holy to their God and shall not pollute [Hebrew: violate] his name, for they offer the Lord’s fire offerings and [Hebrew omits this] the bread of their God; therefore they shall be holy.

He shall not take a prostitute or a degraded harlot as a wife.

[Note: [Col. 0327D] The Hebrew, Samaritan, and Septuagint versions read in the plural: “They shall take,” “they shall receive”; and what immediately follows—“because he is consecrated to his God”—in the singular, although all these expressions refer to the same priest. It is therefore better to read in the Hebrew canon of truth and in all the Latin manuscripts: “he shall take,” “he offers,” “he is consecrated,” “let him be holy,” and so forth. MART.]

He shall not marry a woman repudiated by her husband, because he is consecrated to his God and offers the bread of presentation [Hebrew: therefore sanctify him, because he offers the bread of presentation of your God]. He shall be holy, because I, the Lord who sanctify you, am holy [the Vulgate: who sanctify them].

[C. LXXI.] If a priest’s daughter is discovered in fornication and has profaned her father’s name, she shall be burned with fire.

The high priest—that is, the chief priest among his brothers—upon whose head the oil of anointing has been poured, whose hands have been consecrated for the priesthood, and who is clothed in holy garments, shall not uncover his head or tear his garments, nor enter at all where there is any dead person. He shall not defile himself even for his father or mother. He shall not leave the sanctuary, lest he pollute [Hebrew: violate] the sanctuary of his God, because the oil of the holy anointing of his God [Hebrew: because the crown of the anointing oil of his God is upon him] is upon him [the Vulgate: “of the Lord,” omitting “his”]. I am the Lord.

He shall take a virgin as wife. He shall not take a widow, a repudiated woman, a defiled woman, or a prostitute, but a virgin from his own people. He shall not mingle the stock of his lineage with the common people of his nation [Hebrew: he shall not mingle his seed with the common people of his nation], because I am the Lord who sanctifies him.

[B. XII, C, LXXII.] The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron: No man of your descendants, throughout their families, who has a blemish shall offer the bread of his God or approach his service. If he is blind, lame, has a small, large, or crooked nose, has a broken foot or hand, is hunchbacked, bleary-eyed, has a white spot in his eye, a persistent skin disease, an eruption on his body, or is herniated, he shall not approach.

No man among the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall approach to offer sacrifices to the Lord or the bread of his God. Nevertheless, he may eat the bread that is offered in the sanctuary, provided only that he does not enter within the veil or approach the altar, because he has a blemish and must not profane my sanctuary. I am the Lord who sanctifies them.

Moses therefore spoke to Aaron, to his sons, and to all Israel everything that had been commanded him.

[C. LXXIII, Chapter XXII.] The Lord also spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and his sons, so that they may beware of the things consecrated by the children of Israel and not profane the name of the holy things consecrated to me, which they offer. I am the Lord [Hebrew: so that they may not profane my holy name through the things consecrated to me. I am the Lord].

Say to them and to their descendants: Any man of your offspring who approaches the holy things which the children of Israel offer to the Lord while he has an uncleanness shall perish before the Lord. I am the Lord.

Any man descended from Aaron who is leprous or suffers from an emission of semen shall not eat of the holy things consecrated to me until he is healed. Whoever touches an unclean thing associated with a dead body [Hebrew: until he is healed; a person who touches an unclean thing associated with a dead body], or a man from whom semen has issued as in intercourse, or one who touches a creeping creature, or any unclean thing whose touch is defiling, shall be unclean until evening. He shall not eat of the holy things, but when he has washed his body with water and the sun has set, then, having been cleansed, he may eat of the holy things, because they are his food.

They shall not eat an animal that has died of itself or has been torn by a beast, nor shall they be defiled by them. I am the Lord. They shall keep my commandments [Hebrew: observe my charges], so that they do not incur sin and die in the sanctuary when they have polluted [Hebrew: violated] it. I am the Lord who sanctifies them [the Vulgate: you].

No outsider shall eat of the holy things. A tenant or hired worker of a priest shall not eat of them. But one whom the priest has bought, and anyone born in his household, may eat of them. If a priest’s daughter is married to anyone from the people, she shall not eat of the holy things or of the first fruits. But if she becomes a widow, is repudiated, and returns childless to her father’s house, she may be nourished by her father’s food, as she was when she was a girl. No outsider has the right to eat of them.

If anyone eats of the holy things unknowingly, he shall add a fifth part to what he has eaten and give it to the priest for the sanctuary. They shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, which they offer to the Lord, lest they incur the guilt of their offense by eating what has been consecrated. I am the Lord who sanctifies them.

[T. XIV, C. LXXIV.] The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the children of Israel, and say to them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of the resident foreigners dwelling among you, who brings his offering—whether to fulfill a vow or as a voluntary offering—whatever he brings as a burnt offering to the Lord, so that it may be offered through you, shall offer an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats. If it has a blemish, you shall not offer it, and it shall not be acceptable.

A man who offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to the Lord, whether to fulfill a vow or as a voluntary offering, shall offer an unblemished animal, whether from cattle or sheep, so that it may be acceptable; there shall be no blemish in it. If it is blind, broken, scarred, covered with sores, or afflicted with scabies or an eruption, you shall not offer it to the Lord, nor burn any of it upon the altar of the Lord.

You may voluntarily offer an ox or sheep whose ear or tail has been cut off [Hebrew: an ox or sheep that is generally larger or smaller], but it may not be used to fulfill a vow. You shall not offer to the Lord any animal that has crushed, bruised, cut, or removed testicles; you shall not do this at all in your land.

You shall not offer the bread of your God from the hand of a foreigner, nor anything else that he wishes to give, because all such things are corrupt and blemished; you shall not accept them [Hebrew: You shall not offer the bread of your God from the hand of a foreigner from any of these things, because all are corrupt and blemished; you shall not accept them].

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: An ox, sheep, or goat, once born, shall remain under its mother for seven days; from the eighth day onward it may be offered to the Lord. Whether it is an ox or a sheep, it shall not be slaughtered on the same day as its young.

[C. LXXV.] If you sacrifice a thanksgiving offering to the Lord so that it may be acceptable, you shall eat it on the same day [Hebrew: it shall be eaten on the same day]; nothing shall remain of it until the morning of the next day [Hebrew: nothing shall remain of it until morning]. I am the Lord. Keep my commandments and carry them out. I am the Lord.

You shall not profane my holy name, so that I may be sanctified in the midst of the children of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctifies you and brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord.

[B. XIII, C. LXXVI, Chapter XXIII.] The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: These are the festivals of the Lord, which you shall call holy assemblies. For six days you shall work; the seventh day, because it is the Sabbath rest, shall be called holy. You shall do no work on it; it is the Sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.

[C. LXXVII.] These, then, are the holy festivals of the Lord, which you must celebrate at their appointed times. In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month toward evening, it is the Passover of the Lord. On the fifteenth day of this month is the solemnity of the unleavened bread of the Lord. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. The first day shall be especially solemn and holy for you; you shall do no servile work on it [Hebrew omits this], but for seven days you shall offer a sacrifice by fire to the Lord.

[C. LXXVIII.] The seventh day shall be more solemn and holier, and you shall do no servile work [the Vulgate adds “on it”].

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: When you enter the land that I will give you and reap its harvest, you shall bring a sheaf of the first fruits of your harvest to the priest. He shall lift up the sheaf before the Lord, so that it may be acceptable for you, on the day after the Sabbath, and he shall consecrate it. On the same day on which the sheaf is consecrated, an unblemished year-old lamb shall be slaughtered as a burnt offering to the Lord. With it shall be offered a grain offering: two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, as an offering by fire to the Lord, with a most pleasing aroma, and a wine offering of one-fourth of a hin.

You shall not eat bread, parched grain, or porridge [Hebrew: tender grain] from the harvest until the day on which you offer it to your God. This is an everlasting command throughout your generations and in all your dwellings.

You shall count from the day after the Sabbath, on which you offered the sheaf of the first fruits, seven full weeks, until the day after the completion of the seventh week—that is, fifty days. Then you shall offer a new sacrifice to the Lord from all your dwellings: two loaves of first fruits [Hebrew: From your dwellings you shall offer two loaves of first fruits], made from two-tenths of fermented fine flour, which you shall bake as first fruits for the Lord.

You shall offer with the loaves seven unblemished year-old lambs, one young bull from the herd, and two rams. They shall be a burnt offering with their grain offerings, a most pleasing aroma to the Lord. You shall also offer one male goat [Hebrew: of goats] as a sin offering, and two year-old lambs as peace offerings.

When the priest has lifted them up with the loaves of the first fruits before the Lord, they shall become his due [Hebrew: they shall be holy to the Lord, for the priest]. You shall call that day especially solemn and holy; you shall do no servile work on it. This shall be an everlasting statute throughout your dwellings and generations.

When you reap the harvest of your land [Hebrew: And when you reap the harvest], you shall not cut it down to the ground, nor gather the remaining ears, but leave them for the poor and for resident foreigners. I am the Lord your God.

[T. XV, C. LXXIV.] The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a Sabbath of remembrance, with the sound of trumpets, and it shall be called holy. You shall do no servile work on it [Hebrew omits this], and you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: On the tenth day of this seventh month shall be the most solemn Day of Atonement, and it shall be called holy.
