You shall afflict your souls on that day, and offer a burnt offering to the Lord. You shall do no work [the Vulgate adds “servile”] during this day, because it is the Day of Atonement, so that the Lord your God may make atonement for you. Any person who is not afflicted on that day shall perish from among his people, and whoever performs any work I will destroy from among his people. Therefore you shall do no work on it [Hebrew omits this]. It shall be an everlasting statute for you throughout your generations and in all your dwellings.

It is a Sabbath of rest, and you shall afflict your souls on the ninth day of the month, from evening until [Hebrew: You shall afflict your souls on the ninth day of the month until evening; from evening until] evening you shall celebrate your Sabbaths.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel: From the fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the festival of tabernacles for seven days to the Lord. The first day shall be called especially solemn and holy; you shall do no servile work on it [Hebrew omits this]. For seven days you shall offer burnt offerings to the Lord. The eighth day shall also be especially solemn and holy, and you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord; for it is an assembly and a gathering. You shall do no servile work on it [Hebrew omits this].

These are the festivals of the Lord, which you shall call especially solemn and holy, and at which you shall offer offerings to the Lord—burnt offerings and libations—according to the rite appointed for each day, in addition to the Sabbaths of the Lord, your gifts, and whatever you offer in fulfillment of a vow or give voluntarily to the Lord.

Therefore, from the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered all the produce of your land, you shall celebrate the festival of the Lord for seven days. On the first day and on the eighth day there shall be a Sabbath, that is, rest. On the first day you shall take for yourselves the fruit of a beautiful tree, palm branches, branches of leafy trees, and willows from the stream, and you shall rejoice before the Lord [Col. 0331A] your God. You shall celebrate his solemnity for seven days each year. It shall be an everlasting statute throughout your generations.

In the seventh month you shall celebrate the festival and dwell in shelters [Hebrew: tabernacles] for seven days. Everyone of Israelite descent shall dwell in tabernacles, so that your descendants may learn that I made the children of Israel dwell in tabernacles when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

Moses spoke to the children of Israel concerning the solemnities of the Lord.

[C. LXXX, Chapter XXIV.] The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command the children of Israel to bring you pure oil of olives, clear, for the continual preparation of the lamps, outside the veil of testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant [Hebrew: testimony]. Aaron shall arrange them from evening until morning before the Lord. They shall always be placed upon the purest lampstand before the Lord, as a perpetual observance throughout your generations.

You shall also take fine flour and bake twelve loaves from it [Hebrew: cakes], each of which shall contain two-tenths. You shall arrange six of them on each side upon the pure table before the Lord, and place pure frankincense upon them, so that it may serve [Hebrew: for the bread as] a memorial portion of the Lord’s offering. On every Sabbath they shall be changed [Hebrew: prepared] before the Lord, received from the children of Israel as an everlasting covenant. They shall belong to Aaron and his sons, so that they may eat them in a holy place, because they are most holy among the Lord’s sacrifices, by perpetual right.

[T. XVI, B. XIV, C. LXXXI.] Now the son of an Israelite woman, whom she had borne to an Egyptian man among the children of Israel, went out and quarreled in the camp with an Israelite man. When he had blasphemed the name of God and cursed him [Hebrew omits “of God” and “him”], he was brought to Moses. His mother was named Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan. They placed him in custody until they might know what the Lord would command.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Bring the blasphemer outside the camp, and let all who heard him place their hands upon his head; then let the entire assembly stone him. And speak to the children of Israel: Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin, and whoever blasphemes the name of the Lord shall surely be put to death. The entire assembly shall stone him, whether he is a citizen or a resident foreigner. Whoever blasphemes the name of the Lord [Hebrew omits “of the Lord”] shall surely be put to death.

[C. LXXXII.] Whoever strikes and kills a man shall surely be put to death. Whoever strikes an animal shall make restitution—life for life. Whoever causes a blemish in any of his fellow citizens: as he has done, so shall it be done to him; fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. Whatever blemish he inflicted, such shall be inflicted upon him. Whoever strikes an animal shall make restitution for it. Whoever strikes a man shall be punished. Let there be one judgment among you, whether the resident foreigner or the citizen is at fault [Hebrew: whether he is].

I am the Lord your God.

Moses spoke to the children of Israel, and they brought the one who had blasphemed outside the camp and stoned him. The children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses.

## [Chapter XXV]

The Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying: “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: When you have entered the land that I shall give you, let the land keep a sabbath for the Lord.

[Note: The printed editions have *sabbatizes*. The better manuscripts read *sabbatizet sabbatum Domino* (“let it keep a sabbath for the Lord”). A later manuscript of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, no. 164, reads exactly as in the Hebrew: *sabbatizet terra sabbatum Domino* (“let the land keep a sabbath for the Lord”). This appears to have been taken from a marginal annotation of the canon, as in six hundred other places where readings found in the body of the Bible are those which the canon notes in the margin as being in the Hebrew. MART.]

For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather its produce. But in the seventh year the land shall have a sabbath, a rest for the Lord: you shall not sow your field, nor prune your vineyard. Whatever the soil produces of its own accord you shall not harvest, and you shall not gather the grapes of your first produce as though for a vintage.

[Col. 0332B] [Hebrew: And you shall not gather the grapes that the vineyard has produced of its own accord as though for a vintage.]

For it is a year of rest for the land. Rather, they shall be food for you, for you, your male and female slaves, your hired servant, and the resident alien who dwells with you. For your cattle and livestock they shall provide food—all that grows.

You shall also count seven weeks of years for yourself, that is, seven times seven, making forty-nine years. Then you shall sound the trumpet in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, at the time of atonement, throughout all your land. You shall sanctify the fiftieth year and proclaim release to all the inhabitants of your land. It shall be a Jubilee. Each person shall return to his possession, and each shall return to his former family, because it is a Jubilee and the fiftieth year.

You shall not sow, nor reap what grows spontaneously in the field, nor gather the first produce of the vintage, because of the sanctification of the Jubilee; rather, you shall eat what is offered immediately.

[Hebrew: And you shall not harvest the vineyard, but shall eat immediately in the field.]

In the year of the Jubilee everyone shall return to his possessions. When you sell anything to your fellow citizen, or buy from him, do not distress your brother; rather, you shall buy from him according to the number of years since the Jubilee, and he shall sell to you according to the calculation of the crops. The more years remain after the Jubilee, the greater the price shall be; and the fewer years you count, the lower the purchase price shall be. For he is selling you the time of the crops.

Do not oppress your countrymen, but let each fear his God, because I am the Lord your God. Perform my commandments, observe my judgments, and fulfill them, so that you may dwell in the land without fear, and so that the soil may yield its fruits for you to eat to satiety, fearing no hostile attack.

But if you say: “What shall we eat in the seventh year, if we do not sow and do not gather our crops?”—I shall give you my blessing in the sixth year, and it shall produce the harvest of three years. You shall sow in the eighth year and eat the old crops until the ninth year; until the new crops have grown, you shall eat the old.

The land shall not be sold permanently, because it is mine, and you are resident aliens and tenants with me.

[Hebrew: And tenants in my presence.]

Therefore, throughout all the land of your possession, you shall sell subject to a right of redemption.

### [C. LXXXIII]

If your brother becomes poor and sells his small holding, and his near relative wishes to redeem what he sold, he may redeem it. But if he has no near relative, and he himself is able to find the price of redemption, the value of the crops shall be calculated from the time when he sold it, and he shall return what remains to the buyer; thus he shall recover his possession.

But if his hand does not find enough to repay the price, the buyer shall retain what he bought until the year of the Jubilee. For in that year every sale returns to the owner and to the former possessor.

Whoever sells a house within the walls of a city shall have the right to redeem it until one year has been completed. If he does not redeem it, and the full year has passed, the buyer and his descendants shall possess it forever, and it cannot be redeemed even in the Jubilee.

But if the house is in a village without walls, it shall be sold according to the law of fields. If it has not previously been redeemed, it shall return to its owner in the Jubilee.

The houses of the Levites that are in their cities may always be redeemed. If they have not been redeemed, they shall return to their owners in the Jubilee, because the houses of the Levite cities are their possessions among the children of Israel. But their surrounding pasturelands shall not be sold, because they are an everlasting possession.

If your brother becomes poor and weak in hand, and you receive him as a resident alien and sojourner, and he lives with you, do not take interest from him, nor more than you gave. Fear your God, so that your brother may live beside you. You shall not lend him your money at interest, nor demand an increase of grain. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.

### [C. LXXXIV]

If your brother, compelled by poverty, sells himself to you, you shall not oppress him with the service of slaves. Rather, he shall be like a hired servant and tenant [Hebrew: “with you”]; he shall work for you until the year of the Jubilee. Then he shall go out with his children and return to his kindred and to the possession of his ancestors, for they are my servants, and I brought them out of the land of Egypt.

They shall not be sold as slaves. Do not oppress him by force, but fear your God.

Your male and female slaves shall come from the nations around you. Likewise, from the resident aliens who dwell among you, and from those born of them in your land, you may take them as servants. You shall pass them on by hereditary right to your descendants and possess them forever.

But you shall not oppress your Israelite brothers by force. If the hand of a resident alien or sojourner among you grows strong, and your brother becomes poor and sells himself to him or to someone from his family, he may be redeemed after his sale. One of his brothers may redeem him, or his uncle, or his uncle’s son, or a blood relative, or a kinsman.

[Hebrew: One of his brothers shall redeem him, or his uncle, or his uncle’s son, or any blood relative of his family.]

But if he is able, he may redeem himself, calculating only the years from the time of his sale until the year of the Jubilee, and the price for which he was sold according to the number of years and the calculation of a hired servant. If many years remain until the Jubilee, he shall repay according to them. If few remain, he shall calculate with him according to the number of years and repay the buyer the value of the remaining years, deducting the wages for which he had previously served. He shall not oppress him violently before your eyes.

But if he cannot be redeemed by these means, he shall go out in the year of the Jubilee with his children. For the children of Israel are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt.

## [C. LXXXV, Chapter XXVI]

I am the Lord your God. You shall not make for yourselves [Hebrew: lacuna] an idol or carved image; you shall not erect pillars, nor set up a marked stone in your land to worship it.

### [C. LXXXVI]

For I am the Lord your God. Observe my sabbaths and stand in awe of my sanctuary. I am the Lord.

### [C. LXXXIX, B. XV]

If you walk in my commandments, observe my orders, and perform them, I shall give you rains in their seasons, and the land shall produce its growth, and the trees shall be filled with fruit. Threshing shall overtake the vintage, and the vintage shall overtake the sowing; you shall eat your bread to satiety and dwell in your land without fear.

I shall give peace within your borders. You shall sleep, and there will be no one to terrify you. I shall remove harmful beasts, and the sword shall not pass through your borders. You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you. Five of you shall pursue a hundred strangers, and a hundred of you ten thousand. Your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.

I shall look favorably upon you and make you fruitful. You shall multiply, and I shall establish my covenant with you. You shall eat the oldest of the old, and you shall cast out the old when the new arrives. I shall set my tabernacle in your midst, and my soul shall not reject you.

### [C. LXXXVIII]

I shall walk among you and be your God, and you shall be my people. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would not serve them; I broke the chains of your necks so that you might walk upright.

But if you do not listen to me and do not perform all my commandments; if you despise my laws

[Hebrew: my statutes]

and reject my judgments, so that you do not do what I have established, and annul my covenant, then I too shall do this to you: I shall swiftly visit you with poverty and burning fever, which shall consume your eyes and waste away your lives. You shall sow seed in vain, for your enemies shall devour it.

I shall set my face against you, and you shall fall before your enemies. You shall be subjected to those who hate you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.

But if even then you do not obey me, I shall increase your chastisements sevenfold because of your sins, and I shall break the pride of your stubbornness. I shall make your sky above you like iron and your earth like bronze. Your labor shall be consumed in vain; the land shall not produce its growth, nor shall the trees yield fruit.

If you walk contrary to me and refuse to listen to me, I shall increase your plagues sevenfold because of your sins. I shall send wild beasts among you, which shall consume you and your cattle and reduce everything to a small number; your roads shall become deserted.

But if even then you refuse to accept discipline and walk contrary to me, I too shall proceed against you in opposition, and I shall strike you seven times because of your sins. I shall bring upon you the avenging sword of my covenant.

When you flee into your cities, I shall send pestilence among you, and you shall be delivered into the hands of your enemies after I have broken your staff of bread. Ten women shall bake their bread in one oven and return it by weight.

[Hebrew: And your bread shall be returned by weight.]

You shall eat and not be satisfied.

But if even by these things you do not listen to me and walk against me, I too shall proceed against you in contrary fury and chastise you with seven plagues

[Hebrew: seven times]

because of your sins, so that you will eat the flesh of your sons and daughters. I shall destroy your high places and break your images.

[The Vulgate omits “your.”]

You shall fall among the ruins of your idols, and my soul shall abhor you, so that I shall reduce your cities to solitude and make your sanctuaries desolate; nor shall I accept any longer the fragrance of a pleasing offering.

I shall destroy your land, and your enemies who dwell in it shall be astonished over it. I shall scatter you among the nations and draw the sword after you. Your land shall become desolate and your cities ruins.

Then the land shall enjoy its sabbaths throughout all the days of its desolation. When you are in the land of your enemies, it shall keep sabbath and rest during the sabbaths of its desolation, because it did not rest during your sabbaths when you dwelt in it.

As for those of you who remain, I shall bring fear into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a flying leaf shall terrify them, and they shall flee as though from a sword; they shall fall when no one pursues them, and each shall stumble over his brother as though fleeing from battle. None of you shall dare to resist your enemies.

You shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall consume you. If any of them remain, they shall waste away in their iniquities, in the land of their enemies, and because of the sins of their fathers and their own sins they shall be afflicted, until they confess their iniquities and those of their ancestors, by which they transgressed against me and walked contrary to me.

I too shall walk against them and bring them into the land of their enemies, until their uncircumcised mind is humbled. Then they shall pray concerning their impieties.

I shall remember my covenant, which I made with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham. I shall also remember the land, which, when it has been abandoned by them, shall take pleasure in its sabbaths, enduring desolation because of them. They themselves shall pray concerning their sins, because they rejected my judgments and despised my laws.

[Hebrew: my statutes.]

Yet even while they are in the land of their enemies, I shall not utterly reject them, nor despise them so as to destroy them and annul my covenant with them. For I am the Lord their God, and I shall remember my former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, so that I might be their God. I am the Lord.

These are the commandments, judgments, and laws that the Lord gave between himself and the children of Israel on Mount Sinai through the hand of Moses.

## [B. XVI, C. LXXXVIII, Chapter XXVII]

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: When a person makes a vow and promises his life under an assessment, he shall give the assessed price.

If he is a male from twenty years of age to sixty, he shall give fifty shekels of silver according to the sanctuary’s measure; if a female, thirty. From the fifth year to the twentieth, a male shall give twenty shekels, and a female ten. From one month to the fifth year, five shekels shall be given for a male and three for a female. From sixty years onward, a male shall give fifteen shekels and a female ten.

If he is poor and cannot pay the assessment, he shall stand before the priest, and he shall give whatever the priest assesses and sees that he is able to pay.

An animal that can be offered in sacrifice to the Lord, if anyone vows it to the Lord [the Vulgate omits “to the Lord”], shall be holy and may not be exchanged—that is, neither a better one for a worse nor a worse one for a better. If he exchanges it, both the animal that was exchanged and the one for which it was exchanged shall be consecrated to the Lord.

If it is an unclean animal that cannot be offered to the Lord, and someone vows it, it shall be brought before the priest. He shall determine whether it is good or bad and establish its price. If the person who offers it wishes to redeem it,

[Hebrew: give its redemption price]

he shall add one-fifth to the assessment.

If someone vows his house and consecrates it to the Lord, the priest shall examine whether it is good or bad, and it shall be sold according to the price established by him. But if the one who vowed it wishes to redeem it, he shall add one-fifth to the assessment and retain the house.

If someone vows and consecrates to the Lord a field from his possession, its price shall be assessed according to the amount of seed required: if land is sown with thirty measures of barley, it shall be sold for fifty shekels of silver. If he vows the field immediately from the beginning of the Jubilee year, it shall be assessed at whatever its full value may be. But if he vows it after some time has passed, the priest shall calculate the money according to the number of years remaining until the Jubilee, and the price shall be reduced accordingly.

If the one who vowed the field wishes to redeem it, he shall add one-fifth of the assessed price and possess it. But if he does not wish to redeem it, and it is sold to anyone else, he may no longer redeem it after the one who vowed it, because when the day of the Jubilee arrives it shall be holy to the Lord, and the consecrated possession belongs by right to the priests.

If a field has been purchased, and not consecrated from the ancestral possession, the priest shall calculate its price according to the number of years remaining until the Jubilee, and the one who vowed it shall give it to the Lord. In the Jubilee it shall return to its former owner, who sold it and had it as part of his allotted possession.

Every assessment shall be weighed according to the sanctuary shekel. The shekel contains twenty obols.

No one may consecrate or vow the firstborn, which belongs to the Lord; whether it is an ox or a sheep, it belongs to the Lord. If it is an unclean animal, the one who offered it shall redeem it according to your assessment and add one-fifth of the price. If he does not wish to redeem it, it shall be sold to another for whatever price you assess it.

Whatever is consecrated to the Lord—whether a person, an animal, or a field—shall not be sold and cannot be redeemed. Whatever has once been consecrated shall be most holy to the Lord.

Every person consecrated by a human being shall not be redeemed, but shall surely die.

All the tithes of the land, whether of grain or fruit from the trees, belong to the Lord and are consecrated to him. If anyone wishes to redeem his tithes, he shall add one-fifth to them.

As for all the tithes of oxen, sheep, and goats

[Hebrew: the Hebrew does not have “and goats”]

—that is, whatever passes under the shepherd’s rod—every tenth animal shall be consecrated to the Lord. No selection shall be made of good or bad, and it shall not be exchanged for another. If anyone exchanges it, both the animal exchanged

[the Vulgate has “that was exchanged”]

and the one for which it was exchanged shall be consecrated to the Lord, and it shall not be redeemed.

These are the commandments that the Lord commanded Moses for the children of Israel on Mount Sinai.

[Col. 0337] The book of Vayiqra, that is, Leviticus, ends.

# The Book of Numbers

## Chapter Summaries of the Book of Numbers

### Titles of the Book of Numbers, Called in Hebrew *Vayedabber*

[Col. 0337B]

I. The Lord commanded Moses to record the number of the entire people from twenty years of age upward, all the men and heads of families, excluding the tribe of Levi, and to prescribe how the camps should advance or be stationed.

II. The description of the Levitical tribe, and who should be assigned to the service of the Lord.

III. Where he commanded that the unclean be outside the camp; concerning the vows of the guilty; and concerning the waters of jealousy between wife and husband.

IV. Concerning the consecration of the Nazirites and their offerings, and how the priests should bless the people.

V. Concerning the dedication of the tabernacle and altar, and what each tribal prince offered during the twelve days. Concerning the consecration of the Levites, and the lamps to be placed toward the north so that they face the table of the bread of the Presence.

VI. Concerning the first Passover in the wilderness and the second Passover for those who could not celebrate the first, and concerning the making of silver trumpets for gathering the people.

VII. When the camps moved, Moses urged his kinsman to go with him to the promised land. Concerning the murmuring of the people and the fire of God’s anger that avenged it. Concerning the people’s desire for meat, onions, cucumbers, and other things, and those who rejected the sweetest manna. Concerning the seventy elders who prophesied, and the quail brought for eating, at which God grew angry, and concerning the graves of desire.

VIII. Concerning Aaron’s and Miriam’s murmuring and her leprosy. Concerning the spies sent to examine the promised land. Concerning the signs of the fruits they brought back. Concerning the people’s testing and fear. Concerning the faith of Joshua and Caleb. Concerning God’s anger, when he swore by himself that none of them would enter the promised land.

IX. Concerning spontaneous vows. Concerning firstfruits to be set apart. Concerning the person who sins through ignorance or pride. Concerning the man gathering wood, and the sentence by which, at God’s command, he was to be stoned. Concerning tassels on the corners of garments.

X. Concerning the conflict of Dathan, Korah, and Abiram, and their destruction. The people murmured against Moses and Aaron on their account. When anger went out from the Lord and began to strike the people, Aaron offered a censer with incense and restrained the destroyer. Concerning the twelve staffs and Aaron’s staff that blossomed.

XI. Concerning the guardianship of the tabernacle, which belongs to the priest. Concerning the redemption of the firstborn and the tithing of tithes.

XII. Concerning the red heifer, which is slaughtered outside the camp. Concerning purification. Concerning the water of contradiction and Miriam’s death.

XIII. Moses sends messengers to Edom requesting passage, but is refused. Concerning Aaron’s death on Mount Hor and his son Eleazar as his successor. Concerning the bronze serpent and the messengers sent to Sihon, king of the Amorites.

XIV. Concerning Balak the king and Balaam the diviner, when the donkey spoke and he blessed the people of Israel contrary to his intention.

[Col. 0338C]

XV. The people initiated into the worship of Baal-peor. The Lord commands the leaders of the people to be hanged on gallows. Concerning the Midianite prostitute and Phinehas’s vengeance. Concerning the war brought against the Midianites and the people counted again. Concerning the daughters of Zelophehad seeking an inheritance. Concerning Moses’s predicted death and Joshua appointed as his successor.

XVI. Concerning the rite of the morning sacrifice and the burnt offering made each month in succession throughout the year. Concerning the offering at Pentecost. Concerning the offerings of the month of trumpets and women’s vows.

XVII. Concerning the slaughter of the Midianites and their booty. Concerning the request of the Reubenites and Gadites that they receive their allotted share in that land on account of their animals, and Moses’s grant.

XVIII. Here he recalls the places of their journeys and the places where they fixed their tents.

XIX. The Lord commands how they are to divide the promised land by lot and within what boundaries each tribe’s territory is to be enclosed.

XX. Where they are commanded to set apart cities as refuges for fugitives and who are to receive refuge there. The descendants of Joseph’s sons appeal to Moses concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, so that, if they receive an inheritance, they may not marry into another tribe, lest the allotments be confused and one group’s possession pass to another; they are commanded to marry within their own tribe whomever they wish.

## Brief Summaries of the Book of Numbers

[Col. 0339]

[Col. 0339A]

I. A census of the twelve tribes conducted by Moses and Aaron and twelve leaders, from twenty years of age upward, excluding the Levites: 603,550.

[Note: One Palatine manuscript reads “and the twelve tribal leaders from thirty years of age upward,” apart from the Levites, 604,550.]

II. The Lord commands that the tribe of Levi not be counted, so that they may serve the tabernacle and minister.

III. The Lord commands them to advance in orderly arrangement by ancestral houses and their companies.

IV. Concerning the lineage of Moses and Aaron and his sons, who were anointed to the priesthood.

V. The Lord says that the Levites are to be attached to Aaron, because he has taken them for all the firstborn of Israel.

VI. The Levites are counted from one month of age upward: 2,274.

VII. The Lord commands every firstborn male of the children of Israel from one month of age upward to be counted.

[Col. 0339B]

VIII. The Lord commands the sons of Kohath to carry the ark, the table, and the altar, and not to touch the holy things, lest they die.

IX. The Lord commands the sons of Gershon to carry the tabernacle and its cords.

X. The sons of Merari carry the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, pillars, and bases; all those carrying out the work of the tabernacle number 8,580.

XI. The Lord commands every unclean person to be expelled from the camps.

XII. Concerning the woman who has secretly committed adultery.

XIII. Concerning those who have made a vow of chastity.

XIV. How the priests should bless the people.

XV. Moses anoints the tabernacle, and the leaders offer gifts.

XVI. Each of the twelve leaders offers his gifts to Moses on his appointed day.

XVII. Concerning the lampstand and its lamps.

XVIII. Concerning the Levites purified for the service of the tabernacle.

XIX. The Levites are to begin ministering at twenty-five years of age and withdraw at fifty.

XX. In the second year after the exodus from Egypt, in the first month, the Lord commands the Passover to be celebrated.

XXI. The tabernacle is completed, and the cloud covers it by day and fire by night.

XXII. With the cloud going before them, they advanced and halted at the command of the Lord.

XXIII. Concerning the silver trumpets for moving the camps.

XXIV. In the second year, in the second month, all the children of Israel move their camps.

XXV. Moses urges Hobab, his kinsman

[Note: The same manuscript reads “his son-in-law” instead of “his kinsman.”]

to come with him.

XXVI. They move from the mountain of the Lord, and the ark of the covenant goes before them.

XXVII. The people murmur, and fire consumes some of them.

[Col. 0340A]

XXVIII. The people weep, asking for meat, and Moses says to the Lord: “I cannot bear this people alone.”

XXIX. The Lord says to Moses: “Gather seventy elders for me, and I shall give them to you as assistance.”

XXX. The Lord takes from Moses’s spirit and places it upon the elders, and they prophesy.

XXXI. The Lord sends a flock of quail into the camp and strikes 23,000 men from the people.

XXXII. Aaron and Miriam speak against Moses, and Miriam is struck with leprosy and remains outside the camp for seven days.

[Note: The Palatine manuscript reads “was covered” instead of “was struck.”]

XXXIII. Moses sends twelve spies, one from each tribe. When they return, they spread terror among the people. Caleb, however, exhorts the people to go up against them.

XXXIV. The people murmur, saying: “Let us appoint a leader for ourselves, and let us return to Egypt.”

[Note: The Palatine manuscript repeats the words: “Let us appoint leaders for ourselves; let us appoint leaders for ourselves.”]

XXXV. The Lord becomes angry and says that he will strike the people. Moses intercedes with the Lord, and he is merciful to them.

XXXVI. The Lord swears not to bring them into the promised land because they murmured.

XXXVII. Concerning the burnt offering and sacrifice.

XXXVIII. The Lord commands that the firstfruits of the bread of the land into which they will enter be offered to him.

XXXIX. The Lord commands that the one who gathers wood on the sabbath be stoned.

XL. Concerning the making of tassels.

[Col. 0340C]

XLI. Concerning Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and the 250 leaders.

XLII. The Lord says that he will destroy the entire assembly. Moses and Aaron intercede for the people, the earth swallows Dathan and Abiram, and fire consumes the 250 men carrying incense.

[Note: The Palatine manuscript inserts the name “Korah” here.]

XLIII. Anger goes out from the presence of the Lord, a crash occurs, and 14,700 people die because they murmured against Moses and Aaron.

XLIV. Concerning Aaron’s staff, which blossomed, and the command that the people cease murmuring, lest they die.

XLV. The Lord commands the tribe of Levi to serve the tabernacle and guard it, and not to approach the holy vessels.

XLVI. The Lord commands the Levites to receive tithes and offer tithes from them.

XLVII. The cow is burned to ashes for the water of sprinkling.

XLVIII. Miriam dies in the wilderness. The people murmur because of the water, and Moses strikes the rock with his staff, saying: “Can we bring water for you from this rock?” Much water comes out. The Lord says to Moses and Aaron: “You shall not bring this people into the land that I have given them.”

[Note: The Palatine manuscript omits the words that follow in this chapter.]

XLIX. Moses sends to the king of Edom, asking that they pass through his territory, but he refuses.

L. The Lord commands Moses to clothe Eleazar with the robe of his father Aaron on Mount Hor and that Aaron die there.

[Note: The Palatine manuscript also lacks the words “on Mount Hor, etc.”]

LI. King Arad wages war against Israel, but, with the Lord’s prohibition, they are subjected to him.

LII. The people murmur, and the Lord sends deadly serpents among them.

LIII. They set out and travel through the wilderness. Moses sends to Sihon asking to pass through his borders, but Sihon refuses and comes to battle; Israel kills him.

[Note: The Palatine manuscript again lacks these words, “and Israel killed him,” as well as, later in this chapter, the final words “and he wished to kill him.”]

LIV. Og the king comes out to meet Israel in battle, and Israel does to him what it did to Sihon, king of the Amorites.

LV. Balak, king of Moab, sends for Balaam to come and curse Israel. An angel with a drawn sword confronts him and wishes to kill him.

LVI. Some of the people fornicate with the Midianites. Phinehas kills Zimri with the Midianite woman, and 24,000 of the people die.

LVII. The Lord tells Moses to strike the Midianites.

LVIII. The Lord commands Moses to count the people from twenty years of age upward.

[Note: The Palatine manuscript reads “from thirty years of age.”]

They are counted: 601,730.

LIX. The sons of Levi, among whom were Amram and his wife Jochebed (who bore Aaron, Moses, and Miriam), are counted from one month of age upward: 23,000.

LX. Moses takes Joshua son of Nun and lays his hands upon him before all the people, as the Lord appointed him.

LXI. The Lord tells Moses to command the people concerning the sacrifices and offerings to be made.

LXII. He shows what offerings are to be made on the day of Passover.

LXIII. What is to be offered at Pentecost.

LXIV. What is to be offered in the seventh month for seven days.

LXV. A vow that anyone makes must not be neglected.

LXVI. The Lord tells Moses to take vengeance on the Midianites. They wage war against Midian and kill every male.

LXVII. The sons of Reuben and Gad ask Moses for land on this side of the Jordan, saying: “We shall leave our wives and cattle here, and we shall go ahead of the people armed and arranged for battle.”

[Note: The same manuscript reads “beyond the Jordan.”]

LXVIII. The stopping places of the children of Israel from the time they departed from Egypt.

LXIX. The Lord commands them to destroy all the inhabitants of Canaan; if any remain, they will be thorns in their eyes.

[Note: Instead of “Canaan,” the Palatine manuscript prefers “Moab.”]

LXX. The Lord commands that the land of Canaan be divided by lot among nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

LXXI. The names of the men who divide the land of Canaan among the children of Israel.

LXXII. He identifies the cities given to the Levites and those that are refuges.

LXXIII. In the cities of refuge he explains for what reasons those who have committed homicide must flee there.

LXXIV. Concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, who are commanded to remain within the tribe of their father’s people.

## THE BOOK OF VA-YEDABBER BEGINS

Which among us is called **NUMBERS**.

[Col. 0343]

[T. I, B. I, Cap. I.] And the Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tabernacle of the covenant, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after their departure from Egypt, saying:

“Take the census of the entire congregation of the children of Israel, by their clans and households, and the names of each individual, every male from twenty years of age and upward, all the able-bodied men of Israel [h.: all the warriors of Israel], and count them by their companies, you and Aaron.

“And with you shall be the leaders of the tribes and of the households in their clans, whose names are these:

Of Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur.

Of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

Of Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab.

Of Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar.

Of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon.

Of the sons of Joseph: of Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; of Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

Of Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni.

Of Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

Of Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran.

Of Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel.

Of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.

“These were the most distinguished leaders of the multitude, by their tribes and clans, and the heads of Israel’s army.” Moses and Aaron took these men, together with the entire assembly of the people, and gathered them on the first day of the second month, listing them by their clans, households, families, heads, and individual names [h.: their households and family groups, and the names of each individual], from twenty years of age and upward, as the Lord had commanded.

And they were counted in the wilderness of Sinai.

Of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, by their generations, families, households, and the names of their individual heads, every male from twenty years of age and upward who was fit for war: forty-six thousand five hundred.

Of the sons of Simeon, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, they were counted by the names and heads of each individual, every male from twenty years of age and upward who was fit for war: fifty-nine thousand three hundred.

Of the sons of Gad, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, they were counted by the names of each individual from twenty years of age and upward, all who were to go out to war: forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.

Of the sons of Judah, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, by the names of each individual from twenty years of age and upward, all who were able to go out to war, they were counted: seventy-four thousand six hundred.

Of the sons of Issachar, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, by the names of each individual from twenty years of age and upward, all who were to go out to war, they were counted: fifty-four thousand four hundred.

Of the sons of Zebulun, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, they were counted by the names of each individual from twenty years of age and upward, all who were able to go out to war: fifty-seven thousand four hundred.

Of the sons of Joseph, the sons of Ephraim, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, they were counted by the names of each individual from twenty years of age and upward, all who were able to go out to war: forty thousand five hundred.

Of the sons of Manasseh, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, they were counted by the names of each individual from twenty years of age and upward, all who were able to go out to war: thirty-two thousand two hundred.

Of the sons of Benjamin, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, they were counted by the names of each individual from twenty years of age and upward, all who were able to go out to war: thirty-five thousand four hundred.

Of the sons of Dan, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, they were counted by the names of each individual from twenty years of age and upward, all who were able to go out to war: sixty-two thousand seven hundred.

Of the sons of Asher, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, they were counted by the names of each individual from twenty years of age and upward, all who were able to go out to war: forty-one thousand five hundred.

Of the sons of Naphtali, by their generations, families, and the households of their clans, they were counted by the names of each individual from twenty years of age and upward, all who were able to go out to war: fifty-three thousand four hundred.

These are those whom Moses and Aaron, together with the twelve leaders of Israel, counted individually by the households of their clans.

[Note: [Col. 0345D] In the manuscripts we read, “And all the sons of Israel were,” and elsewhere, “And all the sons of Israel together were.” But in the manuscript codex of the Church of Anicium, now in the Colbert Library, no. 157, it seems to have originally been written by the first hand, “And all the sons of Israel were counted,” and so forth. This would be the best reading; but two words [Col. 0346D] have been erased with a knife, and *together* has been written above them, so that it reads: “And all the sons of Israel together were,” and so forth. MART. —The Urbinas manuscript has: “And all the sons of Israel were.” Martianay reports other variant readings.]

And the entire number of the children of Israel, by their households and families [h.: it always has “the households of their families” instead of “the households of their clans”], from twenty years of age and upward, who were able to go out to war, was six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty men [h. omits “men”].

But the Levites were not counted among them by the tribe of their families.

[B. II, C. I.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“You shall not count the tribe of Levi, nor shall you include their total among the children of Israel. Instead, appoint them over the tabernacle of the testimony and all its vessels, and everything pertaining to its ceremonies [h.: and all its equipment]. They shall carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, they shall serve in it, and around the tabernacle they shall encamp.

“When it is time to set out, the Levites shall take down the tabernacle; when it is time to encamp, they shall erect it. Whoever else approaches shall be put to death.

“The children of Israel shall encamp, each by his companies, divisions, and army.”

[C. II.] But the Levites shall pitch their tents around the tabernacle, so that indignation may not fall upon the congregation of the children of Israel; and they shall keep watch over the tabernacle of the testimony [h.: the guard of the tabernacle]. And the children of Israel did everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.

[B. III, Cap. II.] And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

“The children of Israel shall encamp, each by his companies, standards, and banners [h. omits “and banners”], and by the households of his clan, around the tabernacle of the covenant.

“On the eastern side Judah shall pitch its tents by the companies of its army. Its leader shall be Nahshon son of Amminadab, and the total of his army’s fighting men shall be seventy-four thousand six hundred.

“Beside him shall encamp the tribe of Issachar, whose leader shall be Nethanel son of Zuar. The total of its fighting men shall be fifty-four thousand four hundred.

“In the tribe of Zebulun the leader shall be Eliab son of Helon. The total of his army’s fighting men shall be fifty-seven thousand four hundred.

“All those counted in the camp of Judah numbered one hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred; they shall set out first by their companies.

“In the camp of the sons of Reuben, on the southern side, the leader shall be Elizur son of Shedeur, and his entire army of fighting men who were counted shall number forty-six thousand five hundred.

“Beside him shall encamp the tribe of Simeon, whose leader shall be Shelumiel [Vulg.: Salamiel] son of Zurishaddai. Its entire army of fighting men who were counted shall number fifty-nine thousand three hundred.

“In the tribe of Gad the leader shall be Eliasaph son of Deuel [Note: [Col. 0347D] The Samaritans and Arabs read this name with *daleth*, *Dauel* and *Dauail*, which our Vulgate likewise reads. Modern Hebrew, the Septuagint, the Chaldean, and the Syriac, however, have *resh* at the beginning: *Rahuel* or *Raguel*. Yet Saint Jerome, following Samaritan manuscripts, read it again with *daleth* in his book of Hebrew Names; and, citing the name from Numbers, he interprets it as “let them acknowledge God”: “Deuel,” he says, “let them acknowledge God,” namely from the root *jada*, which means “he acknowledged.” This does not mean, however, that any suspicion should immediately arise from the marginal annotation that it is not Jerome’s, since in his own Hebrew exemplar he read *deuel*. For he frequently teaches us that the same names were customarily written in different ways and with different letters. Thus, concerning the name Dibon, he wished the following to be noted in Book VI of his Commentary on Isaiah, chapter 15: “Let no one,” he says, “think it a scribal fault, and, while wishing to correct an error, create one: one city is written both with the letters *m* and *b*. Of these, Dimon means ‘silence,’ while Dibon means ‘flowing’; both names were assigned on account of the waters that flow silently. To this day the town is indifferently called both Dimon and Dibon.” But why was it necessary to use Dibon as an example, when the very name about which we are now speaking is written below, in chapter 7, verses 42 and 47, both in Hebrew and in Chaldean, *Deuel* and not *Rauel?* MART. —The Hebrew scholiast very correctly notes that the Hebrew has *Rahuel*. But this is the same name which, in the preceding chapter, verse 14, is written in the Hebrew itself as *Dahuel*, and likewise twice below, in chapter 7, verses 42 and 47. The entire cause of the difference is clearly to be attributed to the haste of scribes and the excessive similarity of the letters.]

Deuel [h.: Rahuel], and the entire army of his fighting men who were counted shall number forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.

“All those counted in the camp of Reuben numbered one hundred and fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty by their companies; they shall set out second.

“The tabernacle of the testimony shall be carried according to the duties of the Levites and their companies. As it is erected, so shall it be taken down. Each shall set out according to his places and ranks [h.: the tabernacle of the testimony shall be carried according to the duties of the Levites in the middle of the camp; as they encamp, so shall they set out, each according to his places and ranks].

“On the western side shall be the camp of the sons of Ephraim, whose leader shall be Elishama son of Ammihud. The entire army of his fighting men who were counted shall number forty thousand five hundred.

“With them shall be the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, whose leader shall be Gamaliel son of Pedahzur. The entire army of its fighting men who were counted shall number thirty-two thousand two hundred.

“In the tribe of the sons of Benjamin the leader shall be Abidan son of Gideoni. The entire army of its fighting men who were counted shall number thirty-five thousand four hundred.

“All those counted in the camp of Ephraim numbered one hundred and eight thousand one hundred by their companies; they shall set out third.

“On the northern side the sons of Dan shall encamp [h.: shall encamp], whose leader shall be Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. The entire army of his fighting men who were counted shall number sixty-two thousand seven hundred.

“Beside him shall pitch their tents [h.: shall encamp] those of the tribe of Asher, whose leader shall be Pagiel son of Ocran [Vulg.: Ochran]. The entire army of its fighting men who were counted shall number forty-one thousand five hundred.

“Of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali the leader shall be Ahira son of Enan. The entire army of its fighting men shall number fifty-three thousand four hundred.

“All those counted in the camp of Dan numbered one hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred; they shall set out last.

“This was the number of the children of Israel, divided by the households of their clans and by the companies of their armies: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.

“But the Levites were not counted among the children of Israel, for so the Lord had commanded Moses.

“And the children of Israel did everything that the Lord had commanded Moses. They encamped by their companies and set out by their families and the households of their fathers [Vulg. omits “their”].”

[T. II, B. IV, C. III, Cap. III.] These are the generations of Aaron and Moses, on the day when the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.

And these are the names of the sons of Aaron: his firstborn Nadab, then [h. omits “then”] Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the priests who were anointed and whose hands were filled and consecrated so that they might perform the priesthood.

But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai, without children; and Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests before Aaron their father.

[B. V, C. IV.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Bring the tribe of Levi and have them stand before Aaron the priest, [Col. 0348C] so that they may serve him, keep watch, and guard everything pertaining to the service of the congregation before the tabernacle of the testimony; and let them guard the vessels of the tabernacle, serving in its ministry.

“You shall give the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons, to whom they have been handed over by the children of Israel.

“You shall appoint Aaron and his sons over the priestly service. Any outsider who approaches to minister [h. omits “to minister”] shall die.”

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the children of Israel, and the Levites shall be mine.

“For every firstborn is mine, from the day when I struck down the firstborn in the land of Egypt. I consecrated to myself everything that is firstborn in Israel, from human being to livestock: they are mine. I am the Lord.”

[B. VI, C. VI.] And the Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying:

“Count the sons of Levi by the households of their fathers and by their families, every male from one month old and upward.”

Moses counted them as the Lord had commanded, and the sons of Levi were found by their names: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei.

The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi.

Of Gershon there were two families, the Libnite and the Shimeite; their male population, counted from one month old and upward, was seven thousand five hundred.

They shall encamp behind the tabernacle, on the western side, under the leadership of Eliasaph son of Lael.

They shall be responsible for the tabernacle of the covenant: the tabernacle itself and its covering, the curtain that is drawn before the entrance of the covering of the covenant, the curtains of the court, the curtain that hangs at the entrance of the court of the tabernacle, and everything pertaining to the rite of the altar, the cords of the tabernacle, and all its furnishings.

The clan of Kohath shall consist of the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites.

These are the families of the Kohathites, counted by their names: every male from one month old and upward, eight thousand six hundred. They shall be responsible for the sanctuary and shall encamp on the southern side.

Their leader shall be Elizaphan son of Uzziel. They shall guard the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary with which service is performed, the veil, and all equipment of this kind.

The chief leader of the Levites shall be Eleazar son of Aaron the priest; he shall oversee those responsible for guarding the sanctuary.

But of Merari there shall be the Mahlites and the Mushites, counted by their names: every male from one month old and upward, six thousand two hundred.

Their leader shall be Zuriel son of Abihail; they shall encamp on the northern side.

Their responsibility shall include the boards of the tabernacle, its bars, its columns and their bases, and everything pertaining to this kind of service; also the columns of the court all around, with their bases, and the tent-pegs with their cords.

Before the tabernacle of the covenant—that is, on the eastern side—Moses and Aaron shall encamp with his sons [h.: Moses, Aaron, and his sons, that is, Aaron], having responsibility for the sanctuary in the midst of the children of Israel.

Whoever else approaches shall die.

All the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the Lord’s command, by their families, every male from one month old and upward, numbered twenty-two thousand.

[B. VII, C. VII.] And the Lord said to Moses:

“Count the male firstborn among the children of Israel from one month old and upward, and determine their total.

“Take the Levites for me in place of every firstborn among the children of Israel. I am [h. omits “I am”] the Lord. And take their livestock in place of all the firstborn livestock of the children of Israel [Vulg.: of the livestock].”

Moses counted the firstborn of the children of Israel as the Lord had commanded. The males, by their names, from one month old and upward, numbered twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three.

[C. VIII.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Take the Levites in place of the firstborn of the children of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock; and the Levites shall be mine. I am [h. omits “I am”] the Lord.

“For the redemption of the two hundred and seventy-three who exceed the number of the Levites among the firstborn of the children of Israel, you shall take five shekels for each head, according to the sanctuary’s standard. The shekel contains twenty obols.

“You shall give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption-price of those who are in excess.”

So Moses took the money for those who were in excess, those whom they redeemed from the Levites in place of the firstborn of the children of Israel—one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels according to the sanctuary’s weight—and gave it to Aaron and his sons, according to the word that the Lord had commanded him.

[C. IX, Cap. IV.] And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

“Take the total of the sons of Kohath from among the Levites, by their households and families [h.: by the households of their families], from thirty years of age and upward to fifty years, all who enter upon service, to serve in the tabernacle of the covenant.

“This is the service of the sons of Kohath: when the camp is to move, Aaron and his sons shall enter the tabernacle of the covenant and the holy of holies [h.: this is the service of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the testimony, the holy of holies]. They shall take down the veil that hangs before the entrance, wrap the ark of the testimony in it, cover it again with a covering of violet-colored skins, spread over it a wholly hyacinth-colored cloth, and insert its poles.

“They shall also wrap the table of the Presence in a hyacinth-colored cloth, place upon it the censers, bowls, cups, and basins for pouring libations—the bread shall always be on it—and spread over it a scarlet cloth, which they shall again cover with a covering of violet-colored skins, and insert its poles.

“They shall also take a hyacinth-colored cloth [Vulg.: ‘and’], with which they shall cover the lampstand with its lamps, tongs, snuffers, and all its oil vessels required for preparing the lamps. Over everything they shall place a covering of violet-colored skins and insert its poles.

“They shall also wrap the golden altar in a hyacinth-colored covering, spread over it a covering of violet-colored skins, and insert its poles.

“They shall wrap all the vessels used in the sanctuary in a hyacinth-colored cloth, spread over them a covering of violet-colored skins, and insert their poles.

“They shall also cleanse the altar of ashes, wrap it in a purple covering, and place with it all the vessels used in its service: fire pans, forks, three-pronged instruments, hooks, and shovels.

“They shall cover all the vessels of the altar together with a covering of violet-colored skins and insert its poles.

[B. VIII.] “When Aaron and his sons have wrapped the sanctuary and all its vessels during the breaking up of the camp, then the sons of Kohath shall enter to carry the wrapped objects; but they shall not touch the vessels of the sanctuary, lest they die.

“These are the burdens of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the covenant. Eleazar son of Aaron the priest shall be over them; he shall be responsible for the oil used to prepare the lamps [h.: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest shall be over the oil used to prepare the lamps], the incense mixture, the continual offering, the anointing oil, and everything pertaining to the service of the tabernacle and all its vessels that are in the sanctuary.”

And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

“Do not destroy the people of Kohath from among the Levites. Rather, do this for them, so that they may live and not die when they touch the holy of holies [h.: when they approach to carry the holy of holies]. Aaron and his sons shall enter, assign each person his task, and determine what each one is to carry.

“Let no others look with curiosity upon the things that are in the sanctuary before they have been wrapped; otherwise they shall die.”

[B. IX, C. X.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Take the total of the sons of Gershon by their households, families, and clans [h.: by the households of their families], from thirty years of age and upward to fifty years.

“Count all who enter upon service and minister in the tabernacle of the covenant [h.: of the testimony].

“This is the duty of the family of the Gershonites: they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the covering of the covenant, the other covering, and above all the violet-colored covering and the curtain that hangs at the entrance of the tabernacle of the covenant; the curtains of the court and the curtain at the entrance before the tabernacle.

“The sons of Gershon shall carry everything pertaining to the altar—the cords and the vessels of the service—at the command of Aaron and his sons; and they shall know to whom each burden is to be assigned.

“This is the service of the family of the Gershonites in the tabernacle of the covenant; and they shall be under the authority of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

[B. X.] “You shall also count the sons of Merari by the families and households of their fathers, from thirty years of age and upward to fifty years, all who enter upon the duty of their service and the service of the tabernacle of the testimony.

“These are their burdens: they shall carry the boards of the tabernacle and its bars, its columns and their bases, and also the columns of the court all around, with their bases, tent-pegs, and cords.

“They shall receive all the vessels and equipment according to an inventory, and so shall carry them.

“This is the duty of the family of the Merarites and their service in the tabernacle of the covenant; and they shall be under the authority of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.”

So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the congregation counted the sons of Kohath by their clans and the households of their fathers, from thirty years of age and upward to fifty years, all who entered upon the service of the tabernacle of the covenant; and they were found to number two thousand seven hundred and fifty.

This is the number of the people of Kohath who enter the tabernacle of the covenant; Moses and Aaron counted them according to the word of the Lord through Moses.

[C. XI.] The sons of Gershon were also counted by their clans and the households of their fathers, from thirty years of age and upward to fifty years, all who entered to serve in the tabernacle of the covenant; and they were found to number two thousand six hundred and thirty.

This is the number of the Gershonites whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the word of the Lord.

[C. XII.] The sons of Merari were also counted by their clans and the households of their fathers, from thirty years of age and upward to fifty years, all who entered to perform the rites of the tabernacle of the covenant; and they were found to number three thousand two hundred.

This is the number of the sons of Merari whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the command of the Lord through Moses.

All those counted among the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron caused to be counted by name [Note: [Col. 0351D] The word “counted” is absent from all our manuscripts—and, what is more surprising, it is absent from the text of the Hebrew canonical truth, although a scholion has been placed alongside it, sufficiently instructing the reader that this passage has no sense unless the aforementioned word is present in the text. Accordingly, following the evidence of the Vulgate edition, we supplied what had been omitted through the carelessness of ancient copyists. MART. —Martianay states that the word “counted,” absent from all his manuscripts, is supplied by our Urbinas codex. The Palatine manuscript omits not only that word but also the words “by name.”]

—and Aaron [h.: whom Moses and Aaron counted]—together with the leaders of Israel, by their clans and the households of their fathers, from thirty years of age and upward to fifty years, entering upon the service of the tabernacle and the carrying of burdens, numbered altogether eight thousand five hundred and eighty.

According to the word of the Lord, Moses counted them, each according to his duty and burdens, as the Lord had commanded him.

[T. III, B. XI, C. XIII, Cap. V.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Command the children of Israel to expel from the camp every leper, everyone who suffers a discharge, and anyone who is polluted by the dead [h.: polluted by a person], both male and female. Expel them from the camp, so that they may not defile it while they dwell with you [Note: [Col. 0352D] All the manuscripts unanimously have this reading; but the reading in our Vulgate is better, namely, “I shall dwell,” in the first person singular, as may be learned from the marginal scholion of the Hebrew canonical text. MART. —The Palatine manuscript has, in the first hand, “because I dwell with you.” Certainly the Hebrew also reads in the first person, in nearly the same words: [Hebrew term not legible in the supplied text].]

[h.: in whose midst I dwell].”

And the children of Israel did so and expelled them outside the camp, as the Lord had spoken to Moses.

[C. XIV.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Speak to the children of Israel: When a man or woman commits any of the sins that people ordinarily commit, and through negligence transgresses the Lord’s command and incurs guilt, they shall confess their sin and restore the principal itself, adding a fifth of it, to the person against whom they sinned.

“But if there is no one to receive it, they shall give it to the Lord, and it shall belong to the priest, apart from the ram that is offered for atonement, so that it may be an acceptable sacrifice.

[C. XV.] “All the firstfruits that the children of Israel offer belong to the priest; and whatever is offered by individuals in the sanctuary and placed in the hands of the priest shall be his.

[B. XII, C. XVI.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: If a man’s wife goes astray and, despising her husband, sleeps with another man, while the husband does not discover it, because the adultery remains hidden and cannot be proved by witnesses, since she was not caught in the act; if a spirit of jealousy [h.: and a spirit] stirs the man against his wife, whether she has truly been defiled or is accused under a false suspicion, he shall bring her to the priest and offer on her behalf a tenth of an ephah [h.: an ephah] of barley flour.

“He shall not pour oil over it or place frankincense on it, because it is a jealousy-offering, an offering that investigates adultery [h.: an offering of remembrance that investigates iniquity].

“The priest shall offer it and set her before the Lord. He shall take holy water in an earthen vessel and put a little dust from the floor of the tabernacle into it.

“When the woman has been placed before the Lord, he shall uncover her head and place the offering of remembrance, the jealousy-offering, in her hands. The priest himself shall hold the bitter waters that bring a curse.

“He shall adjure her and say: ‘If no foreign man has slept with you, and if you have not been defiled by leaving your husband’s bed, these bitter waters into which I have put the curse shall not harm you.

“But if you have turned away from your husband, have been defiled, and have slept with another man, you shall be subject to these curses:

“‘May the Lord make you a curse and an example among all his people; may he cause your thigh to rot and your swollen womb to burst.

“‘May these waters of the curse enter your belly, and, as your womb swells, may your thigh waste away’ [h.: ‘May he cause your thigh to fall away and your womb to swell. May the waters of the curse enter your inward parts, so that your womb may burst’].”

And the woman shall answer, “Amen, amen.”

The priest shall write these curses in a book and wash them away with the bitter waters into which he has put the curse, and he shall give them to the woman to drink.

When she has drunk them, the priest shall take the jealousy-offering from her hand, lift it before the Lord, and place it upon the altar—except that he shall first take a handful from the offering and burn it upon the altar—and then give the bitter waters to the woman to drink.

When she has drunk them, if she has been defiled, has despised her husband, and is guilty of adultery, the waters of the curse shall pass through her; her belly shall swell and her thigh shall rot [h.: and when her womb has burst, her thigh shall fall away]. The woman shall become a curse and an example to all the people [h.: a curse in the midst of her people].

But if she has not been defiled, she shall be innocent and shall bear children.

“This is the law of jealousy.

“If a woman turns away from her husband and has been defiled, and her husband, stirred by a spirit of jealousy, brings her before the Lord, and the priest does to her everything that is written here, the husband shall be free from guilt, and she shall bear her iniquity [h.: the woman shall bear her iniquity].”

[T. IV, B. XIII, C. XVII, Cap. VI.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When a man or woman makes a vow in order to be consecrated and wishes to dedicate himself or herself to the Lord, they shall abstain from wine and everything that can intoxicate.

“They shall not drink vinegar made from wine or from any other drink, nor anything pressed from grapes. Throughout all the days during which they are consecrated to the Lord by their vow, they shall not eat fresh or dried grapes. They shall eat nothing that comes from the vine, from the raisin to the grape seed.

“Throughout all the time of their separation, no razor shall pass over their head until the day is complete for which they are consecrated to the Lord. They shall be holy, letting the hair of their head grow.

“Throughout the time of their consecration they shall not approach a dead person, nor shall they defile themselves over the corpse of even their father, mother, brother, or sister, because the consecration of their God is upon their head.

[Note: [Col. 0353D] The manuscripts read this verse in two or three ways. Most have: “All the days of his separation he shall be holy to the Lord.” Others have: “Every day of his separation,” and so forth. Finally, the Regal manuscript, mentioned above, reads with the Latin Vulgate: “Throughout all the days of his separation,” and so forth. The Hebrew canonical text contains variants of this kind and teaches what should be read according to the Hebrew. MART. —Martianay needlessly restored *omnis*, as though it meant something different from *omnes*, although the meaning is the same and they differ only because of the older pronunciation, which freely alternates the letters I and E. The Urbinas codex more clearly has: “on all the days,” and so forth.]

“All the days of his separation [h.: on all the days of his separation] he shall be holy to the Lord.

“But if someone suddenly dies in his presence [h.: over him], the head of his consecration shall be defiled. He shall shave it immediately, on the day of his purification, and again on the seventh day.

“On the eighth day he shall offer two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tabernacle of the covenant.

“The priest shall make one for sin and the other as a burnt offering, and shall make atonement for him, because he sinned through the dead [h.: over a person]. He shall consecrate his head on that day and consecrate the days of his separation to the Lord [h.: he shall consecrate his head on that day and consecrate the days of his separation to the Lord], offering a year-old lamb for sin. In this way the earlier days shall be void, because his consecration has been defiled.

[Col. 0354C] “This is the law of consecration.

“When the days that he had appointed by his vow have been completed, he shall bring his offering to the door of the tabernacle of the covenant and offer his gift to the Lord: a flawless year-old male lamb as a burnt offering, a flawless year-old ewe for sin, and a flawless ram as a peace-offering, together with a basket of unleavened bread made with oil, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and the libations belonging to each.

“The priest shall offer these before the Lord and make both the sin-offering and the burnt offering.

“He shall slaughter the ram as a peace-offering to the Lord, offering at the same time the basket of unleavened bread and the libations that are customarily due.

“Then the Nazirite [Vulg.: ‘the Nazirite shall be shaved’] shall shave the hair of his consecration before the door of the tabernacle of the covenant. He shall take his hair and place it upon the fire that is beneath the peace-offering.

“He shall take the cooked shoulder of the ram, one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and place them in the hand of the Nazirite after his head has been shaved.

“After receiving them back from him, he shall lift them before the Lord. They shall belong to the priest, like the breast that was commanded to be set apart and the thigh.

“After this the Nazirite may drink wine.

“This is the law of the Nazirite, when he vows his offering to the Lord at the time of his consecration, apart from what his hand may find. According to what he had vowed in his mind, so shall he act to complete his consecration.

[B. XIV, C. XVIII.] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Speak to Aaron and his sons:

“Thus shall you bless the children of Israel, and say to them:

‘May the Lord bless you and keep you.

‘May the Lord show his face to you and have mercy on you’ [h.: ‘May the Lord illuminate his face over you and have mercy on you’].

‘May the Lord turn his countenance toward you and give you peace.’

“And they shall invoke my name over the children of Israel, and I shall bless them.”

[T. V, B. XV, Cap. VII.] Now it came to pass on the day when Moses finished the tabernacle and erected it, that he anointed and sanctified it with all its vessels, and likewise the altar and all its vessels. The princes of Israel and the heads of their families, who were leaders of the individual tribes and overseers of those who had been counted, presented gifts before the Lord: six covered wagons with twelve oxen. Two leaders presented one wagon, and each presented one ox; and they offered them before the tabernacle. The Lord then said to Moses: “Receive these from them, so that they may serve in the ministry of the tabernacle of the testimony” [Vulgate omits “of the testimony”], “and give them to the Levites according to the arrangement of their ministry.” Accordingly, when Moses had received the wagons and oxen, he gave them to the Levites. He gave two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, according to what they needed. He gave four other wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, according to their duties and service, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest. But to the sons of Kohath he gave neither wagons nor oxen [Hebrew omits this], because they serve in the sanctuary and carry the burdens on their own shoulders.

[B. XVII.] Therefore the leaders offered their offering at the dedication of the altar, on the day when it was anointed, before the altar.

[C. XIX.] And the Lord said to Moses: “Let each leader offer gifts for the dedication of the altar on his appointed day.” On the first day Naasson son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah, presented his offering. It consisted of a silver basin weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl containing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a small golden mortar weighing ten shekels [Hebrew omits this], filled with incense; a bull [Vulgate adds: “from the herd”], a ram, and a yearling lamb for a burnt offering; a goat for sin; and, for a sacrifice of well-being, two oxen, five rams, five goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Naasson son of Amminadab.

On the second day Nathanael son of Zuar, leader of the tribe [Hebrew omits this] of Issachar, presented a silver basin weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl containing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar containing ten shekels [Hebrew: “of gold”], filled with incense; a bull from the herd, a ram, and a yearling lamb for a burnt offering; a goat for sin; and, for a sacrifice of well-being, two oxen, five rams, five goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Nathanael son of Zuar.

On the third day the leader of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon, presented a silver basin weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl containing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar weighing ten shekels [Hebrew: “of gold”], filled with incense; a bull from the herd, a ram, and a yearling lamb for a burnt offering; a goat for sin; and, for a sacrifice of well-being, two oxen, five rams, five goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.

On the fourth day the leader of the sons of Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur, presented a silver basin weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl containing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar weighing ten shekels [Hebrew: “of gold”], filled with incense; a bull from the herd, a ram, and a yearling lamb for a burnt offering; a goat for sin; and, for sacrifices of well-being [Hebrew: “a sacrifice”], two oxen, five rams, five goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.

On the fifth day the leader of the sons of Simeon, Shelumiel [Vulgate: Salamiel] son of Zurishaddai, presented a silver basin weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl containing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar weighing ten shekels [Hebrew: “of gold”], filled with incense; a bull from the herd, a ram, and a yearling lamb for a burnt offering; a goat for sin; and, for sacrifices of well-being [Hebrew: “a sacrifice”], two oxen, five rams, five goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Shelumiel [Vulgate: Salamiel] son of Zurishaddai.

On the sixth day the leader of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel, presented a silver basin weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl containing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar weighing ten shekels [Hebrew always has: “ten gold shekels”], filled with incense; a bull from the herd, a ram, and a yearling lamb for a burnt offering; a goat for sin; and, as a sacrifice [Hebrew always has: “for a sacrifice”] of well-being, two oxen, five rams, five goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.

On the seventh day the leader of the sons of Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, presented a silver basin weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl containing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar weighing ten shekels, filled with incense; a bull from the herd, a ram, and a yearling lamb for a burnt offering; a goat for sin; and, as sacrifices of well-being, two oxen, five rams, five goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.

On the eighth day the leader of the sons of Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, presented a silver basin weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl containing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar weighing ten shekels, filled with incense; a bull from the herd, a ram, and a yearling lamb for a burnt offering; a goat for sin; and, as sacrifices of well-being, two oxen, five rams, five goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
