**Note.** The Hebrew scholiast interprets this most aptly: “in Pethor, beside the river of the land of the children of his people,” rather than “of the children of Ammon.” For no river that watered the land of the Ammonites is known at all. Saint Jerome may have taken the word [Hebrew term not reproduced in the supplied text] according to its etymology, since it signifies “diviner,” as the name of a place, namely Pethor, in Greek *Phathoura*. He may also have read [Hebrew term not reproduced in the supplied text], “Ammon,” in place of [Hebrew term not reproduced in the supplied text], “his people.” —MART.

to call him and say:

“Behold, a people has come out of Egypt and covered the surface of the earth, sitting opposite me. Come, therefore, and curse this people for me, because it is stronger than I. Perhaps I may be able to strike them and drive them out of my land [h. does not have ‘my’]. For I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed.”

The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed, carrying the payment for divination in their hands. When they came to Balaam, they told him all the words of Balak. He answered them: “Stay here tonight, and I will answer you whatever the Lord tells me.”

While they remained with Balaam, God came and said to him: “What do these men want from you? [h. Who are all these men who are with you?]”

He answered: “Balak, son of Zippor, king of the Moabites, sent them to me, saying: ‘Behold, a people that came out of Egypt has covered the surface of the earth. Come and curse it for me, if perhaps I may be able to fight against it and drive it away.’”

God said to Balaam: “Do not go with them, and do not curse the people, because it is blessed.”

Balaam rose in the morning and said to the leaders: “Go back to your land, because the Lord has forbidden me to come with you.”

The leaders returned and said to Balak: “Balaam refused to come with us.”

Again he sent many more messengers, more distinguished than the former ones. When they came to Balaam, they said: “Thus says Balak son of Zippor: Do not hesitate to come to me. I am ready to honor you, and whatever you wish I will give [h. I will do; the Vulgate adds ‘to you’]. Come and curse this people.”

Balaam answered: “Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not alter the word of the Lord my God, to speak either more or less. Please remain here tonight also, so that I may learn what the Lord will answer me again.”

God came to Balaam at night and said to him: “If these men have come to call you, rise and go with them, but only do what I command you.”

Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his she-ass, and departed with them. God was angry [h. God was angry because he was going].

The angel of the Lord stood in the road against Balaam, who was riding on the she-ass and had two servants with him. When the she-ass saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road with a drawn sword, she turned aside from the road and went through the field.

When Balaam beat her and tried to bring her back to the path, the angel of the Lord stood in a narrow place between two walls enclosing vineyards. When the she-ass saw him, she pressed herself against the wall and crushed the rider’s foot. He beat her again.

The angel of the Lord went ahead to another narrow place, where there was no room to turn either right or left, and stood in the way. When the she-ass saw the angel of the Lord standing there, she fell beneath the feet of her rider. In anger he beat her sides more violently with a staff [h. a rod].

[C. LXIV.] The Lord opened the mouth of the she-ass, and she said: “What have I done to you? Why do you strike me? Behold, this is already the third time.”

Balaam answered: “Because you have deserved it and mocked me [h. Because you mocked me]. If only I had a sword, I would strike you [h. If I had a sword in my hand, I would certainly kill you].”

The she-ass said: “Am I not your animal, upon which you have always been accustomed to ride until this day? Tell me whether I have ever done anything like this to you.”

He said: “Never.”

Immediately the Lord opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road with a drawn sword. He bowed down and worshiped him, prostrate on the ground [h. does not have “on the ground”].

The angel of the Lord said to him: “Why have you beaten your she-ass three times? I came to oppose you, because your way is perverse and contrary to me. If the she-ass had not turned aside from the road, giving way before the one resisting you, I would have killed you, and she would have lived.”

Balaam said: “I have sinned, not knowing that you were standing against me. Now, if it displeases you that I go, I will return.”

The angel of the Lord said: “Go with these men, but take care to speak nothing other than what I command you.”

So he went with the leaders.

When Balak heard this, he came out to meet him in the town of the Moabites, which lies at the edge of the Arnon. He said to Balaam: “I sent messengers to call you. Why did you not come to me immediately? Was it because I am unable to reward your arrival?”

He answered: “Behold, I have come. Can I say anything other than what God places in my mouth?”

They went on together and came to a city that was at the farthest [*Husoth*, translated into Latin as “extremes”] limits of his kingdom.

**Note.** The Samaritans read [Hebrew term not reproduced in the supplied text], *ḥizzot*, that is, “of visions,” as found in the Latin version of the Hebrew-Samaritan text. —MART.

**Note.** Instead of “which was at the farthest limits of his kingdom,” there is a single expression in Hebrew, *Chuzoth*. Unless one wishes to take it as a proper name, it may rightly be translated “of streets,” so that the meaning is that they came to “the city of streets,” that is, a very populous city. The Septuagint agrees, translating it by *epaulēōn*, meaning “of tents,” “lodgings,” or similar places. Our translator, with Onkelos, may have read [Hebrew term not reproduced in the supplied text], “at the limits of his dominion.” There are also those who think that the Hebrew text is corrupt and has [Hebrew term not reproduced in the supplied text] instead of [Hebrew term not reproduced in the supplied text], which they take to be the city Areopolis; but I will never agree with them.

[h. Does not have: “which was at the farthest limits of his kingdom”; it reads: “And they came to the city.”]

When Balak had slaughtered cattle and sheep, he sent gifts to Balaam and the leaders who were with him. When morning came, he led Balaam up to the high places of Baal, and from there he surveyed the farthest part of the people.

[Chap. XXIII.] Balaam said to Balak: “Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and an equal number of rams.”

When he had done as Balaam said, they placed a bull and a ram together upon each altar.

Balaam said to Balak: “Stand for a while [h. does not have ‘for a while’] beside your burnt offering until I go, in case the Lord should meet me; and whatever he commands, I will tell you.”

When he had gone quickly, God met him. Balaam said to him: “I have erected seven altars and placed a bull and a ram upon each.”

The Lord placed a word in his mouth and said: “Return to Balak, and speak as follows.”

He returned and found Balak standing beside his burnt offering, with all the leaders of the Moabites. Balaam took up his parable and said:

“Balak, king of the Moabites, brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the East. ‘Come,’ he said, ‘curse Jacob; hasten and denounce Israel.’ How shall I curse one whom God has not cursed? How shall I denounce one whom the Lord does not denounce? From the summits of the rocks I shall see him, and from the hills I shall look upon him. The people shall dwell alone and shall not be counted among the nations. Who can count the dust of Jacob or number the stock of Israel? May my soul die the death of the just, and may my end be like theirs.”

Balak said to Balaam: “What are you doing? I called you to curse my enemies [h. I brought you], and instead you bless them.”

He answered: “Can I say anything except what the Lord commands?”

Balak said: “Come with me to another place, from which you may see part of Israel but not all of it; curse it for me from there.”

He led him to a high place, to the summit of Mount Pisgah [h. does not have “of the mountain”]. Balaam built seven altars and placed bulls and rams upon them. He said to Balak: “Stand here beside your burnt offering while I go to meet him.”

When the Lord met him and placed a word in his mouth, he said: “Return to Balak and speak as follows [the Vulgate adds ‘to him’].”

He returned and found Balak standing beside his burnt offering, with the leaders of Moab. Balak said to him: “What did the Lord say?”

Balaam took up his parable and said:

“Stand, Balak, and listen; hear me, son of Zippor [h. Balak, listen and hear; son of Zippor, my words]: God is not like a man, that he should lie, nor like a son of man, that he should change. Has he said something and will he not do it? Has he spoken and will he not fulfill it?”

**Note.** The Hebrew and Samaritan texts differ at this point. The Hebrew reads [Hebrew term not reproduced in the supplied text], *hinneh barekh laqaḥti uvereikh*, that is, “Behold, I have received a blessing, and he has blessed.” The Samaritan has [Hebrew term not reproduced in the supplied text], *hen levarekh laqaḥti; avarekh*, which they translate into Latin: “Behold, I have been taken up to bless; I will bless.” —MART.

The Urbinate manuscript has “I have been brought,” a slight difference in reading but one of considerable importance here, where the original texts differ and it is not sufficiently clear in what sense Balaam now says that he has come to bless, since he had come to curse.

“I have been brought to bless; I cannot prevent the blessing [h. Behold, I have received blessings, and I cannot be prevented from them]. There is no idol in Jacob, nor is any image seen in Israel. The Lord their God is with them, and the shout of a king’s victory is among them. God brought them out of Egypt; his strength is like that of a rhinoceros. There is no augury in Jacob, nor divination in Israel. In due time it shall be told to Jacob and Israel what God has done [h. what God is doing]. Behold, the people shall rise like a lioness and lift themselves up like a lion; they shall not lie down until they devour prey and drink the blood of the slain.”

Balak said to Balaam: “Neither curse it nor bless it.”

He answered: “Did I not tell you that whatever the Lord [the Vulgate: God] commanded me, I would do?”

Balak said to him: “Come, and I will lead you to another place, in case it should please God that you curse it from there.”

He led him to the summit of Mount Peor, which looks toward the wilderness. Balaam said to him: “Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and an equal number of rams.”

Balak did as Balaam had said, and placed a bull and a ram upon each altar.

[Chap. XXIV.] When Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord that he should bless Israel, he did not go away as he had previously done to seek an omen. Instead, turning his face toward the wilderness and raising his eyes, he saw Israel dwelling in its tents according to its tribes. The Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he took up his parable and said:

“Balaam son of Beor speaks; the man whose eye is closed speaks; the hearer of the words of God speaks, who sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls and whose eyes are opened.

“How beautiful are your tents, Jacob, and your dwellings, Israel! They are like wooded valleys, like gardens beside irrigated streams, like tents that the Lord has pitched, like cedars beside the waters. Water shall flow from his buckets, and his seed shall be among many waters. His king shall be raised up because of Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.

“God brought him out of Egypt; his strength is like that of a rhinoceros. They shall devour the nations that are his enemies, crush their bones, and pierce them with arrows. He lies down and sleeps like a lion, and like a lioness; who will dare awaken him? [h. Who will awaken him?]

“Whoever blesses you shall himself be blessed, and whoever curses you shall be counted accursed [the Vulgate omits ‘you’].”

Balak became angry with Balaam, clapped his hands, and said: “I called you to curse my enemies, but instead you have blessed them three times. Return [h. flee] to your place. I had intended to honor you magnificently, but the Lord has deprived you of the honor I had planned.”

Balaam answered Balak: “Did I not tell your messengers, whom you sent to me: ‘If Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not transgress the word of the Lord my God [h. does not have ‘my God’], to utter anything good or evil from my own heart; whatever the Lord says, that I will speak’?

“Nevertheless, as I go to my people, I will give counsel concerning what your people shall do to this people in the final time.”

He took up his parable again and said:

“Balaam son of Beor speaks; the man whose eye is closed speaks; the hearer of the words of God speaks, who knows the knowledge of the Most High and sees the visions of the Almighty, who falls yet has his eyes opened.

“I shall see him, but not now; I shall behold him, but not near [h. I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near]. A star shall rise out of Jacob, and a scepter shall arise from Israel. It shall strike the leaders of Moab and destroy all the sons of Seth.

“Edom shall be his possession; Seir shall become the inheritance of his enemies, while Israel shall act valiantly. From Jacob shall come one who rules and destroys the survivors of the city.

“When he saw Amalek, he took up his parable and said: ‘Amalek is the first of the nations, but its end shall be destruction.’

“He also saw the Kenite and took up his parable and said: ‘Your dwelling is indeed strong; but if you set your nest in the rock, and if you are chosen from the stock of the Kenite [the scribal error has become established here, so that *Cain* is written instead of *Kenite*], how long can you remain? For Asshur will take you captive.’

“He took up his parable again and said: ‘Alas, who will live when God does this? Ships will come from Italy; they will conquer the Assyrians, devastate the Hebrews, and in the end they too will perish.’”

Balaam rose and returned to his place, and Balak also returned by the road along which he had come.

### [T. XV, B. LVI, C. LXV, Chapter XXV]

At that time Israel was dwelling at Shittim, and the people committed fornication with the daughters of Moab, who invited them to their sacrifices [h. “to the sacrifices of their gods”]. They ate and worshiped their gods. Israel was initiated into the worship of Baal-Peor, and the Lord became angry with Israel [h. “Israel was joined to them”; Vulg. omits “Israel”] and said to Moses: “Take all the leaders of the people and hang them up before the sun on gallows, so that my fury may be turned away from Israel.”

Moses said to the judges of Israel: “Let each one kill those of his neighbors who have been initiated [h. “joined”] to Baal-Peor.” And behold, one of the children of Israel entered before his brothers to a Midianite prostitute [Col. 0384D], while Moses and the whole assembly of the children of Israel looked on; they were weeping before the entrance of the tent of meeting [C. LXVI].

When Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose from the midst of the assembly, seized a dagger, entered after the Israelite man into the brothel, and pierced them both at once—the man, that is, and the woman—through their genitals. And the plague among the children of Israel ceased; twenty-four thousand men were killed.

[Col. 0385A] And the Lord said to Moses: “Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned away my anger from the children of Israel, because he was moved by zeal for me against them, so that I myself would not destroy the children of Israel in my zeal. Therefore say to him [h. does not have “to him”]: ‘Behold, I give him the covenant of my peace, and it shall be for him and for his offspring a perpetual covenant of priesthood, because he was zealous on behalf of his God and made atonement for the crime of the children of Israel.’”

The name of the Israelite man who was killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri, son of Salu, a leader of a clan and tribe of Simeon. The Midianite woman who was killed with him was called Cozbi, daughter of Zur, a most distinguished prince of the Midianites.

### [B. LVII]

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “Let the Midianites feel that you are their enemies, and strike them, because they too acted hostilely against you and deceived you by their treachery through the idol of Peor, and through Cozbi, the daughter of the prince of Midian, their sister, who was struck down on the day of the plague because of the sacrilege of Peor.”

### [B. LVIII, C. LXVII, Chapter XXVI]

After the blood of the guilty had been shed, the Lord said to Moses and Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest: “Count the entire number of the children of Israel from twenty years old and upward, by households [h. “by the households of their fathers”] and by their clans—all who are able to go forth to war.”

Accordingly Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke [h. “Moses and Eleazar the priest counted”] in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho, to those who were twenty years old and upward, as the Lord had commanded; and this is their number:

Reuben, the firstborn of Israel [Col. 0385C]. His sons were Enoch, from whom came the clan of the Enochites; Phallu, from whom came the clan of the Phalluites; Hezron, from whom came the clan of the Hezronites; and Carmi, from whom came the clan of the Carmites. These were the clans from the stock of Reuben, whose number was forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.

The son of Phallu was Eliab. His sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These were Dathan and Abiram, leaders of the people, who rose up against Moses and Aaron in the rebellion of Korah, when they rebelled against the Lord. The earth opened its mouth and swallowed Korah [h. “swallowed them and Korah”]. When many had died, and fire had consumed two hundred and fifty men, a great miracle occurred: although Korah perished, his sons did not perish [h. “the sons of Korah also did not perish”].

The sons of Simeon, by their clans: Nemuel, from whom came the clan of the Nemuelites; Jamin, from whom came the clan of the Jaminites; Jachin, from whom came the clan of the Jachinites; Zerah, from whom came the clan of the Zerahites; and Saul, from whom came the clan of the Saulites. These were the clans from the stock of Simeon, whose entire number was twenty-two thousand two hundred.

The sons of Gad, by their clans: Zephon, from whom came the clan of the Zephonites; Haggi, from whom came the clan of the Haggites; Shuni, from whom came the clan of the Shunites; Ozni [Col. 0386A], from whom came the clan of the Oznites; Eri, from whom came the clan of the Erites; Arod, from whom came the clan of the Arodites; and Areli, from whom came the clan of the Arelites. These were the clans of Gad, whose entire number was forty thousand five hundred.

The sons of Judah, Er and Onan, both of whom died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Judah, by their clans, were Shelah, from whom came the clan of the Shelanites; Perez, from whom came the clan of the Perezites; and Zerah, from whom came the clan of the Zerahites. The sons of Perez were Hezron, from whom came the clan of the Hezronites, and Hamul, from whom came the clan of the Hamulites. These were the clans of Judah, whose entire number was seventy-six thousand five hundred.

The sons of Issachar, by their clans: Tola, from whom came the clan of the Tolaites; Pua, from whom came the clan of the Puites [Col. 0386B]; Jashub, from whom came the clan of the Jashubites; and Shimron, from whom came the clan of the Shimronites. These were the clans of Issachar, whose number was sixty-four thousand three hundred.

The sons of Zebulun, by their clans: Sered, from whom came the clan of the Seredites; Elon, from whom came the clan of the Elonites; and Jahleel, from whom came the clan of the Jahleelites. These were the clans of Zebulun, whose number was sixty thousand five hundred.

The sons of Joseph, by their clans, Manasseh and Ephraim.

From Manasseh came Machir, from whom came the clan of the Machirites. Machir fathered Gilead, from whom came the clan of the Gileadites. Gilead had sons: Iezer, from whom came the clan of the Iezerites; Helek, from whom came the clan of the Helekites; Asriel, from whom came the clan of the Asrielites; Shechem, from whom came the clan of the Shechemites; Shemida, from whom came the clan of the Shemidaites; and Hepher [Col. 0386C], from whom came the clan of the Hepherites.

Hepher was the father of Zelophehad, who had no sons, but only daughters, whose names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. These were the clans of Manasseh, and their number was fifty-two thousand seven hundred.

The sons of Ephraim, by their clans, were: Shuthelah, from whom came the clan of the Shuthelahites; Becher, from whom came the clan of the Becherites; and Tahan, from whom came the clan of the Tahanites. The son of Shuthelah was Eran, from whom came the clan of the Eranites. These were the clans of the sons of Ephraim, whose number was thirty-two thousand five hundred. These were the sons of Joseph by their clans.

The sons of Benjamin, by their clans: Bela, from whom came the clan of the Belaites; Ashbel, from whom came the clan of the Ashbelites; Ahiram, from whom came the clan of the Ahiramites; Shupham, from whom came the clan of the Shuphamites; and Hupham, from whom came the clan of the Huphamites.

The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman. From Ard came the clan of the Ardites; from Naaman, the clan of the Naamites. These were the sons of Benjamin by their clans, whose number was forty-five thousand six hundred.

[Note: [Col. 0385D] At this point one *phe* has dropped out in the Hebrew, which is why we read “of the Shuphamites” (*Suphamitarum*) instead of “of the Sephuphamites,” in accordance with the Canon of the Hebrew truth. MART. —Together with the standard printed books, the Urbinas manuscript has *Supham* and *Suphamitarum*. The Hebrew does indeed have *sephupham*, but not *Sephuphamitarum*; rather, it has only *Suphamitarum*. Hence Martianay declares that the second *phe* has dropped out of the Hebrew archetype.]

The sons of Dan, by their clans: Shuham, from whom came the clan of the Shuhamites. These were the clans of Dan by their families. All were Shuhamites, whose number was sixty-four thousand four hundred [Col. 0387A].

The sons of Asher, by their clans: Imnah, from whom came the clan of the Imnites; Ishvi, from whom came the clan of the Ishvites; and Beriah, from whom came the clan of the Beriites. The sons of Beriah were Heber, from whom came the clan of the Heberites, and Malchiel, from whom came the clan of the Malchielites. The name of Asher’s daughter was Serah. These were the clans of the sons of Asher, and their number was fifty-three thousand four hundred.

The sons of Naphtali, by their clans: Jahzeel, from whom came the clan of the Jahzeelites; Guni, from whom came the clan of the Gunites; Jezer, from whom came the clan of the Jezerites; and Shillem, from whom came the clan of the Shillemites. These were the clans of the sons of Naphtali by their families, whose number was forty-five thousand four hundred.

This is the total of the children of Israel who were counted: six hundred and one thousand seven hundred and thirty [Col. 0387B].

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “The land shall be divided among these according to the number of names, as their possessions. To the larger number you shall give a larger portion, and to the smaller number a smaller one; possession shall be assigned to each according to those who have now been counted. Only let the lot divide the land among the tribes and clans. Whatever falls by lot, whether received by the larger or the smaller group, shall belong to them.”

### [B. LIX, C. LXIX]

This also is the number of the sons of Levi [h. does not have “of the sons”], by their clans: Gershon, from whom came the clan of the Gershonites; Kohath, from whom came the clan of the Kohathites; and Merari, from whom came the clan of the Merarites. These were the clans of Levi: the clan of Libni, the clan of Hebron, the clan of Mahli, the clan of Mushi, and the clan of Korah.

Kohath fathered Amram, who had as his wife Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, who was born to him in Egypt. She bore to her husband Amram Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam.

The sons born to Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord. All those counted [h. does not have “all”] were twenty-three thousand males from one month old and upward, because they were not counted among the children of Israel, nor was an inheritance given to them with the others.

This is the number of the children of Israel who were registered by Moses and Eleazar the priest in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho. Among them there was no one of those who had previously been counted by Moses and Aaron in the wilderness of Sinai. For the Lord had foretold that all would die in the wilderness. None of them remained except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun [Col. 0387D].

### [C. LXX, Chapter XXVII]

The daughters of Zelophehad, son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, who was the son of Joseph, approached. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They stood before Moses and Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the people, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and said: “Our father died in the wilderness. He was not involved in the rebellion that was stirred up against the Lord under Korah, but he died in his own sin. He had no male children. Why should his name be removed from his clan because he had no son? Give us a possession among the relatives [h. “brothers”] of our father.”

Moses brought their case before the judgment of the Lord [h. “Moses brought their case before the Lord”]. He said to him: “The daughters of Zelophehad are asking for a just thing. Give them a possession among the relatives [h. “brothers”] of their father, and let their father’s inheritance pass to them.”

### [C. LXXI]

And you shall speak to the children of Israel as follows [h. does not have “as follows”]: “When a man dies without a son, his inheritance shall pass to his daughter. If he has no daughter, you shall give his brothers as his successors. But if he has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to his father’s brothers. If he has no paternal uncles, you shall give the inheritance to the one nearest to him among his kin. This shall be a sacred statute for the children of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses [h. “This shall be a lawful judgment for the children of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses”].”

### [C. LXXII]

The Lord also said to Moses: “Go up into this mountain of Abarim and look from there upon the land that I shall give to the children of Israel. When you have seen it, you too shall go to your people [h. “you shall be gathered”], as your brother Aaron went [h. “was gathered”], because you offended me in the wilderness of Zin, in the dispute of the assembly, and you were unwilling to sanctify me before them over the waters.

### [B. LX]

These are the waters of Contradiction at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.”

Moses answered him [h. “And Moses spoke before the Lord, saying”]: “May the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, provide a man who will be over this multitude, able to go out before them and come in before them, to lead them out and bring them in, so that the people of the Lord may not be like sheep without a shepherd.”

### [C. LXXIII]

The Lord said to him: “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand upon him [Col. 0388C]. He shall stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole assembly, and you shall give him commands in the sight of all and a share of your glory, so that the whole congregation of the children of Israel may hear him.

For matters requiring action, Eleazar the priest shall consult the Lord on his behalf [h. “He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, so that he may consult him in a judgment of instruction before the Lord”]. At his word he shall go out and at his word he shall come in, he and all the children of Israel with him, and the entire assembly.”

Moses did as the Lord had commanded. When he had taken Joshua, he set him before Eleazar the priest and the whole assembly of the people. Having laid his hands upon his head, he repeated everything that the Lord had commanded.

### [T. XVI, B. LXI, C. LXXIV, Chapter XXVIII]

The Lord also said to Moses: “Command the children of Israel, and say to them [Col. 0388D]: ‘Present my offering and my bread [h. “the offering of my bread”], and the incense of most pleasing fragrance, at their appointed times.’

“These are the sacrifices that you shall offer: two unblemished yearling lambs each day as a perpetual burnt offering. You shall offer one in the morning and the other in the evening; together with a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the purest oil, and a quarter of a hin. This is the continual burnt offering that you offered on Mount Sinai as a pleasing fragrance, an offering made by fire to the Lord. You shall offer a quarter of a hin of wine as a libation with each lamb in the sanctuary of the Lord.

“You shall likewise offer the second lamb in the evening, according to all the rite of the morning sacrifice and its libations, as an offering of most pleasing fragrance to the Lord.”

### [C. LXXV]

“On the sabbath day you shall offer two unblemished yearling lambs, and two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice, together with the libations that are properly poured on each sabbath, as a perpetual burnt offering.

### [C. LXXVI]

“On the first days of the months [that is, at the beginnings of the months], you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord: two bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven unblemished yearling lambs; together with three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice for each bull, and two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each ram [Col. 0389A], and one-tenth of a tenth of fine flour with oil as a sacrifice for each lamb [Note: [Col. 0389] The scholion teaches that this passage should be read, as above at verse 13, “and individual tenths,” etc. MART.] [h. “and one-tenth for each lamb”]. It shall be a burnt offering of most pleasing fragrance and an offering made by fire to the Lord.

“Their wine libations, which are to be poured out with each victim, shall be as follows: half a hin for each bull, a third for a ram, and a quarter for a lamb. This shall be the burnt offering for all the months that follow one another in the course of the year. A goat shall also be offered to the Lord for sins as a perpetual burnt offering, with its libations.”

### [B. LXII, C. LXXVII]

“In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, the Passover of the Lord shall be [h. does not have “shall be”], and on the fifteenth day shall be a solemn feast. For seven days they shall eat unleavened bread. The first day shall be venerable and holy; you shall do no servile work on it [h. does not have “on it”].

“You shall offer a burnt offering made by fire to the Lord: two bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven unblemished yearling lambs; together with their sacrifices of fine flour mixed with oil, three-tenths for each bull [Col. 0389C], two-tenths for the ram, and one-tenth of a tenth for each lamb [h. “likewise here”], that is, for the seven lambs. And one goat for sin, to make atonement for you, besides the morning burnt offering, which you shall always offer.

“You shall do this on each of the seven days, as food for the fire and as a pleasing fragrance to the Lord, arising from the burnt offering and the libations of each. The seventh day shall also be most solemn and holy for you; you shall do no servile work on it [h. does not have “on it”].”

### [B. LXIII, C. LXXVIII]

“The day of the firstfruits also, when you offer new produce to the Lord after the weeks have been completed, shall be venerable and holy; you shall do no servile work on it [h. does not have “on it”].

“You shall offer a burnt offering as a pleasing fragrance to the Lord: two bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven unblemished yearling lambs. With their sacrifices, you shall offer three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, two-tenths for each ram, and one-tenth of a tenth for each lamb [h. “here as above”], of which there are seven lambs altogether. You shall also offer one goat [Vulg. omits “one”], which is slaughtered [h. does not have “which is slaughtered”] for atonement, besides the perpetual burnt offering and its libations. You shall offer everything unblemished, with its libations.”

### [B. LXIV, C. LXXIX, Chapter XXIX]

“The first day of the seventh month shall also be venerable and holy for you. You shall do no servile work on it, because [h. does not have “on it, because”] it is a day of trumpet blast [h. “It shall be a day of trumpet blast for you”] and tumult.

“You shall offer a burnt offering as a pleasing fragrance to the Lord: one bull from the herd, one ram, and seven unblemished yearling lambs; with their sacrifices, three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, two-tenths for the ram, and one-tenth for each lamb, seven lambs altogether; and one goat for sin, offered for the atonement of the people, besides the burnt offering of the beginnings of the months with its sacrifices, and the perpetual burnt offering with its customary libations. You shall offer these with the same rites as an incense of pleasing fragrance to the Lord.

### [C. LXXX]

“The tenth day of this seventh month shall also be holy and venerable for you, and you shall afflict your souls. You shall do no servile work on it [h. does not have “on it”].

“You shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord as a pleasing fragrance: one bull from the herd, one ram, and seven unblemished yearling lambs; with their sacrifices, three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, two-tenths for the ram, and one-tenth of a tenth for each lamb [h. “one-tenth for each lamb”], seven lambs altogether; and one goat for sin, besides those normally offered for guilt as an atonement, and the perpetual burnt offering, with its sacrifice and libations.

“On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, which shall be holy and venerable for you, you shall do no servile work on it [h. does not have “on it”], but you shall celebrate a solemn feast to the Lord for seven days.”

### [C. LXXXI]

“You shall offer a burnt offering as a pleasing fragrance to the Lord: thirteen bulls from the herd, two rams, and fourteen unblemished yearling lambs; and with their libations, three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull—the thirteen bulls altogether—and two-tenths for one ram, that is, for the two rams together, and one-tenth of a tenth for each lamb [h. “as above”], fourteen lambs altogether; and one goat for sin, besides the perpetual burnt offering, its sacrifice, and its libation.

“On the second day you shall offer twelve bulls from the herd, two rams, and fourteen unblemished yearling lambs. You shall duly offer the sacrifices and libations of each bull, ram, and lamb, and a goat for sin, besides the perpetual burnt offering, its sacrifice, and its libation.

“On the third day you shall offer eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished yearling lambs. You shall duly offer their sacrifices and libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs, and a goat for sin, besides the perpetual burnt offering, its sacrifice, and its libation.

“On the fourth day you shall offer ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished yearling lambs. You shall duly offer their sacrifices [Vulg. omits “their”] and the libations of each bull, ram, and lamb, and a goat for sin, besides the perpetual burnt offering, its sacrifice, and its libation.

“On the fifth day you shall offer nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished yearling lambs [Col. 0391A]. You shall duly offer their sacrifices and libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs, and a goat for sin, besides the perpetual burnt offering, its sacrifice, and its libation.

“On the sixth day you shall offer eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished yearling lambs. You shall duly offer their sacrifices and libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs, and a goat for sin, besides the perpetual burnt offering, its sacrifice, and its libation.

“On the seventh day you shall offer seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished yearling lambs. You shall duly offer their sacrifices and libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs, and a goat for sin, besides the perpetual burnt offering, its sacrifice, and its libation.

“On the eighth day, which is most solemn, you shall do no servile work. You shall offer a burnt offering as a pleasing fragrance to the Lord: one bull, one ram, and seven unblemished yearling lambs; you shall duly offer their sacrifices and libations for the bull, ram, and lambs, and a goat for sin, besides the perpetual burnt offering, its sacrifice, and its libation.

“These you shall offer to the Lord at your solemn feasts, besides vows and voluntary offerings, in burnt offerings, sacrifices, libations, and peace offerings.”

### [B. LXV, C. LXXXII, Chapter XXX]

Moses recounted to the children of Israel everything that the Lord had commanded him. He spoke to the leaders of the tribes of the children of Israel: “This is the word that the Lord has commanded: If a man makes a vow to the Lord or binds himself by an oath, he shall not invalidate his word, but shall fulfill everything that he promised.”

### [C. LXXXIII]

“If a woman makes a vow and binds herself by an oath while she is in her father’s house and still of girlhood age—if her father learns of the vow that she has made and the oath by which she has bound her soul, and remains silent, she shall be liable for her vow [Note: [Col. 0391D] Martianay prints *quidquid* and adds at the bottom of the page: ‘Because she has sworn, she shall fulfill it in deed. Thus it is read in the Canon and in another old manuscript codex of Saint-Germain-des-Prés.’]. Whatever she has promised and sworn, she shall fulfill in deed.

“But if her father contradicts her as soon as he hears, her vows and oaths shall be null, and she shall not be bound by her promise, because her father contradicted her [h. “The Lord also will be merciful to her, because her father contradicted her”].

“If she has a husband and vows something, and a word once proceeding from her mouth binds her soul by an oath—if the husband hears on the day he learns of it and does not contradict her, she shall be liable for her vow and shall fulfill whatever she promised. But if, upon hearing it, he immediately contradicts her and invalidates her promises and the words by which she had bound her soul [Col. 0391D], the Lord will be merciful to her.

“A widow or a divorced woman shall fulfill whatever they vow.

“If a wife in her husband’s house binds herself by a vow and an oath, and her husband hears and remains silent, and does not contradict the promise, she shall fulfill whatever she promised. But if he immediately contradicts her [Col. 0392A], she shall not be bound by the liability of her promise, because her husband contradicted her, and the Lord will be merciful to her.

“If she has vowed and bound herself by an oath to afflict her soul through fasting or abstinence from other things, it shall be within the husband’s discretion whether she does it or does not do it. But if the husband hears and remains silent, postponing his decision until the following day, she shall fulfill whatever she vowed and promised, because when he heard it, he remained silent. But if he contradicts her after learning of it, he himself shall bear her iniquity.

“These are the statutes [h. “the lawful ordinances”] that the Lord established for Moses between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter who is still of girlhood age or remains in her parent’s house [h. “in her father’s house].”

### [T. XVII, B. LXVI, C. LXXXIV, Chapter XXXI]

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “First take vengeance [h. does not have “first”] for the children of Israel against the Midianites [Col. 0392B], and afterward you shall be gathered to your people.”

Immediately Moses said: “Arm from among yourselves men for battle who can exact the Lord’s vengeance from the Midianites. Let one thousand men from each tribe of Israel be selected and sent to war.”

They supplied one thousand from every tribe—that is, twelve thousand equipped for battle—which Moses sent with Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest. He also entrusted to him the holy vessels and the trumpets [h. “flutes”] for sounding.

When they had fought against the Midianites and [Note: [Col. 0391D] The Urbinas manuscript inserts the pronoun *ei* (“to him”).] conquered them [Note: [Col. 0391D] The same manuscript reads *venissent* (“had come”), which I do not deny is corrupt; yet the wording is farther from the Hebrew than is the context of this Latin translation [Col. 0392D], a fact not even noticed by the scholiast. For example, instead of the words “and had conquered,” the Hebrew has “as the Lord had commanded Moses.”], they killed all the males, together with their kings Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, five leaders of the nation [h. “five kings of Midian”]. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.

They captured their women and children, all their cattle, and all their possessions. They plundered everything they were able to possess; both cities, villages, and fortresses were consumed by flame.

[Note: [Col. 0392D] The sense is clear in the scholion, but somewhat obscure in the text, although the Latin translator follows the order of the words rather closely. MART.]

They took the spoil and everything they had captured, both human beings and animals, and brought them to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the whole assembly of the children of Israel. They carried the remaining equipment to the camp in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho [“They took the spoil and everything they had captured, both human beings and animals, and the remaining equipment, and brought it to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the whole assembly of the children of Israel, to the camp in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho”].

Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the assembly went out to meet them outside the camp.

### [C. LXXXV]

Moses became angry with the leaders of the army, the tribunes, and the centurions who had come from the battle, and said: “Why did you spare the women? Are these not the ones who deceived the children of Israel at the suggestion of Balaam and caused you to transgress against the Lord in the matter of the sin of Peor, for which the people was struck?

“Therefore kill every male among the little ones as well, and slaughter every woman who has known a man in intercourse. But preserve for yourselves the girls and all the female virgins, and remain outside the camp for seven days. Whoever has killed a person or touched someone killed shall be purified on the third and seventh days.

[h. “But whoever has killed a person or touched someone killed shall remain outside the camp for seven days, and shall be purified on the third and seventh days.”]

“Everything taken as spoil, whether clothing, a vessel, or anything prepared for use, whether made of goatskins, hair, or wood, shall be purified [h. “washed”].”

Eleazar the priest also spoke as follows to the men of the army who had fought: “This is the ordinance of the law that the Lord commanded Moses: gold, silver, bronze, iron [Col. 0393B], tin, lead, and everything that can pass through the flames shall be purified by fire [h. “shall be purified by fire and cleansed with the water of purification”]. But whatever cannot withstand fire shall be sanctified with the water of purification. You shall wash your clothes on the seventh day, and afterward, when you have been purified, you shall enter the camp.”

### [C. LXXXVI]

And the Lord said to Moses: “Take the total of what has been captured, from human beings to cattle—you, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the assembly—and divide the spoil equally between those who fought and went out to war and the rest of the whole assembly. You shall set apart for the Lord a portion from those who fought and were in the battle: one head out of every five hundred, from human beings, oxen, donkeys, or sheep [Col. 0393C], and you shall give it to Eleazar the priest, because they are the firstfruits of the Lord.

“From the half belonging to the children of Israel you shall take one out of every fifty human beings, oxen, donkeys, sheep, and all animals, and give them to the Levites who keep watch over the duties of the tabernacle of the Lord.”

Moses and Eleazar [h. “the priest”] did as the Lord had commanded.

The spoil that the army had captured consisted of six hundred seventy-five thousand sheep, seventy-two thousand oxen, sixty-one thousand donkeys, and thirty-two thousand human beings of the female sex who had not known men.

Half was given to those who had taken part in the battle: three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep, of which six hundred seventy-five sheep were reckoned as the Lord’s portion; thirty-six thousand oxen, of which seventy-two were the Lord’s portion; thirty thousand five hundred donkeys, of which sixty-one were the Lord’s portion; and sixteen thousand human beings, of whom thirty-two persons were assigned to the Lord’s portion.

Moses gave the number of the Lord’s firstfruits to Eleazar the priest, as had been commanded, from the half belonging to the children of Israel, which he had separated from those who had taken part in the battle.

From the half that had fallen to the rest of the assembly—that is, from three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep, thirty-six thousand oxen, thirty thousand five hundred donkeys, and sixteen thousand human beings—Moses took one out of every fifty and gave them to the Levites who keep watch in the tabernacle of the Lord [Vulg. “who kept watch”], as the Lord had commanded.

When the leaders of the army, the tribunes, and the centurions approached Moses, they said: “We, your servants, have counted the number of the fighters whom we had under our command, and not one of them was missing. For this reason we offer as gifts to the Lord, each of us, whatever gold we were able to find in the spoil: anklets, bracelets, rings, armlets, and necklaces, so that you may entreat the Lord for us.”

Moses and Eleazar the priest accepted all the gold in its various forms [Note: [Col. 0393D] Our manuscripts and others in Martianay’s possession read *pondere sanctuarii* (“by the weight of the sanctuary”). Yet not only these words are absent from the Hebrew; the immediately preceding words are absent as well: “in its various forms.”], weighing [h. does not have “weighing”] sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels, from the tribunes and centurions. For each man had taken what he had seized in the spoil as his own.

They brought what had been received into the tent of testimony, as a memorial for the children of Israel before the Lord.

[B. LXVII, C. LXXXVII, Chapter XXXII.] Now the sons of Reuben and Gad possessed very many flocks, and they had an exceedingly great abundance of livestock. When they saw that Jazer and Gilead were lands suitable for raising animals, they came to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the leaders of the assembly, and said:

“Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Shebam, Nebo, and Beon—the land which the Lord struck down before the sons of Israel [Hebrew: the assembly]—is an exceedingly fertile region for pasturing animals, and we, your servants, possess very numerous herds [Col. 0394C] [Hebrew does not have ‘very numerous’]. We ask that, if we have found favor before you, you grant it to us, your servants, as a possession, and do not make us cross the Jordan.”

Moses answered them: “Will your brothers go to war while you sit here? Why are you turning the minds of the sons of Israel away, so that they dare not cross into the land which the Lord is going to give them? Did not your fathers act in the same way when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to inspect the land? When they had come as far as the Valley of Eshcol and surveyed the whole region, they turned the heart of the sons of Israel away, so that they would not enter the territory [Hebrew: the land] which the Lord had given them.

“And the Lord, being angry, swore, saying: ‘If these men who came up from Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, will see the land which I promised under oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob’ [Hebrew: ‘because’] [Col. 0394D] ‘—for they would not follow me—except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun: these have fulfilled my will.’ And the Lord, being angry against Israel, led them around through the wilderness for forty years, until the entire generation that had done evil in his sight was consumed.

“And behold,” he said, “you have risen up in place of your fathers, offspring and fosterlings of sinful men, to increase the Lord’s anger against Israel. [Note: [Col. 0393D] All the manuscripts of the Bible, together with the Hebrew Canon of the truth, read as follows: ‘But if you will not follow him.’ It makes little difference whether one reads ‘who’ or ‘that,’ since there is no loss of meaning. MART. —Our editions and all Martianus’s manuscripts read ‘who.’]

“But if you will not follow him, [Col. 0395A] he will abandon the people in the wilderness, and you will be the cause of everyone’s death.”

They drew near and said: “We shall build sheepfolds for the sheep, and stalls for the livestock, and fortified cities for our little ones. But we ourselves, armed and equipped, shall go forth to battle before the sons of Israel, until we bring them to their places. Our little ones and everything else we are able to possess shall remain in fortified cities, because of the inhabitants’ attacks. We shall not return [Note: [Col. 0395D] The scholiast read in his Hebrew copy *el banenu*, that is, ‘to our sons,’ or ‘to our little ones,’ unless perhaps he was attending to the meaning rather than the words. Today we read everywhere *el battenu*, ‘to our houses.’ MART.] to our houses [Hebrew: to our little ones] until the sons of Israel possess their inheritance. We shall seek nothing across the Jordan, because we already have our possession on its eastern side.”

Moses said to them: “If you do what you promise, proceed equipped before the Lord to battle; and every armed man shall cross the Jordan before the Lord until the Lord has overthrown his enemies and the whole land has been subjected to him [Hebrew: ‘and afterward you shall return’]. Then you will be blameless before the Lord and before Israel, and you will obtain the regions which you desire before the Lord. But if you do not do what you say, there is no doubt that you will sin against the Lord; and know that your sin will overtake you.

“Build, therefore, cities for your little ones, and sheepfolds and stalls for your sheep and livestock, and fulfill what you have promised.”

The sons of Gad and Reuben said to Moses: “We are your servants; we shall do what our lord commands [Hebrew: ‘Your servants shall do what our Lord commands’]. We shall leave our little ones, our wives, our flocks, and our livestock in the cities of Gilead; but we, your servants, shall all proceed equipped to war, just as you, lord, command.”

Therefore Moses commanded Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families of the tribes of Israel, and said to them:

“If the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben cross the Jordan with you, all armed for battle before the Lord, and the land is subjected to you, [Note: [Col. 0395D] Manuscript Bible codex no. 1 in our library of Saint-Germain reads, as in the Hebrew: ‘Give them the land of Gilead.’ This, unless I am mistaken, arose from a gloss in the Canon of the Hebrew truth. MART.] give them Gilead [Hebrew: give them the land of Gilead] as a possession. But if they do not wish to cross armed [Note: [Col. 0396D] The Urbinas manuscript omits the word ‘armed’] with you into the land of Canaan, let them receive places for dwelling among you.”

The sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben answered: “As our lord has spoken to his servants, so shall we do. We ourselves, armed, shall proceed before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and we acknowledge that we have already received our possession [Note: [Col. 0396D] Thus read the Royal Bible manuscript no. 3563, another Corbiensis manuscript no. 10, and one of Saint-Germain no. 7. Others, with the printed editions, read ‘across the Jordan,’ but with an unsuitable meaning. MART. —That same manuscript reads *confitebimur*, ‘we shall acknowledge,’ and, together with the Palatine manuscript and the printed books, ‘across the Jordan’; the Hebrew has ‘on this side.’] on this side of the Jordan.”

Therefore Moses gave to the sons of Gad, the sons of Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph [Col. 0395D] the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, with their land and the cities surrounding it.

The sons of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer, Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah, Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran, fortified cities and sheepfolds for their flocks [Hebrew does not have ‘for their flocks’]. The sons of Reuben built Heshbon, [Col. 0396A] Elealeh, Kiriathaim, Nebo, and Baal-meon, changing their names, and also Shebam, giving names to the cities which they had built [Hebrew: “And Baal-meon, and Musaboth-shem, and Sibmah; giving names to the cities which they had built”].

But the sons of Machir, son of Manasseh, went to Gilead and devastated it, killing the Amorite who inhabited it. So Moses gave the land of Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he lived in it. Jair, son of Manasseh, went and occupied its villages, which he called Havvoth-jair, that is, “the villages of Jair” [Hebrew does not have this]. Nobah also went and seized Kenath with its dependent settlements, and called it Nobah after his own name.

[B. LXVIII, Chapter XXXIII.] These are the journeys of the sons of Israel who went out from Egypt by their companies [Col. 0396B] under the leadership of Moses and Aaron. Moses recorded them according to the places of the camps, which they changed at the Lord’s command.

[T. XVIII, C. LXXXVIII.] Thus they departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month, on the second day of Passover. The sons of Israel went out with an exalted hand, while all the Egyptians watched and buried their firstborn, whom the Lord had struck down—for he had also executed vengeance upon their gods—on the day after Passover; and they camped at Succoth.

From Succoth they came to Etham, which is at the extremity of the wilderness [Hebrew does not have this]. From there they departed and came opposite Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and they camped before Migdol. Departing from Pi-hahiroth, they passed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness; and, traveling for three days through the wilderness of Etham, they camped at Marah.

Departing from Marah, they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; and there they camped. From there also they departed and pitched their tents beside the Red Sea. Departing from the Red Sea, they camped in the wilderness of Sin. From there they departed and came to Dophkah. Departing from Dophkah, they camped at Alush. Departing from Alush, they pitched their tents at Rephidim [it should be noted that the Hebrew does not say “they pitched their tents,” but “they camped”], where the people had no water to drink.

Departing from Rephidim, they camped in the wilderness of Sinai. From the wilderness of Sinai also they departed and came to the Graves of Lust. Departing from the Graves of Lust, they camped at Hazeroth. From Hazeroth they came to Rithmah. Departing [Col. 0396D] from Rithmah, they camped at Rimmon-perez. From there they departed and came to Libnah. From Libnah they camped at Rissah. Departing from Rissah, they came to Kehelathah. From there they departed and camped at Mount Shepher.

Departing from Mount Shepher, they came to Haradah. From there they proceeded and camped at Makheloth. Departing from Makheloth, they came to Tahath. [Col. 0397A] From Tahath they camped at Terah. From there they departed and pitched their tents at Mithkah. From Mithkah they camped at Hashmonah. Departing from Hashmonah, they came to Moseroth. From Moseroth they camped at Bene-jaakan. Departing from Bene-jaakan, they came to Mount Hor-haggidgad. From there they departed and camped at Jotbathah. From Jotbathah they came to Abronah. Departing from Abronah, they camped at Ezion-geber.

From there they departed and came to the wilderness of Zin, which is Kadesh. Departing from Kadesh, they camped at Mount Hor, at the extremity of the land of Edom [Hebrew does not have “at the extremity”]. Aaron the priest ascended Mount Hor at the Lord’s command, and died there in the fortieth year after the sons of Israel had gone out from Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month, when he was 123 years old.

The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negeb in the land of Canaan, heard that the sons of Israel had come. Departing from Mount Hor, they camped at Zalmonah. From there they departed and came to Punon. Departing from Punon, they camped at Oboth. From Oboth they came to Iye-abarim, which is [Hebrew does not have “which is”] at the borders of the Moabites.

Departing from [Note: [Col. 0397D] We read the same annotation in Jerome, in the already-mentioned letter concerning the forty-two encampments of the Israelites in the wilderness. There Jerome observes the following: “And they departed,” he says, “from Iye-abarim, or, as it is found in the second place among the Hebrews, from Iim, and camped at Dibon-gad, etc.” The Urbinas manuscript has “Iye-abarim, which is,” perhaps “Iim.” The holy translator himself, in Letter 78 to Fabiola, concerning the thirty-ninth encampment, says: “They departed from Iye-abarim, or, as it is found in the second place among the Hebrews, from Iim, etc.” I am persuaded that the same name is written in Hebrew in both places, namely [Hebrew characters omitted in the supplied text]; for the fact that it is first written without the final [letter], is due to the construct relation, which grammarians call the regimen, with the following word, Habarim. The land itself appears to be the one called Gai, or Hai, in Jeremiah XLIX.] Iye-abarim [Hebrew: from Iim; here it has “Iim,” whereas above it has “Iye-abarim”], they pitched their tents at Dibon-gad. From there they departed and camped at Almon-diblathaim. Departing from Almon-diblathaim, they came to the mountains of Abarim opposite Nebo.

[B. LXIX.] Departing from the mountains of Abarim, they crossed to the plains of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho. There they camped from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim, in the level places of the Moabites [Hebrew: on the plain of the Moabites], where the Lord spoke to Moses.

[C. LXXXIX.] “Command the sons of Israel, and say to them: When you have crossed the Jordan, entering the land of Canaan, destroy all the inhabitants of that region. Break their carved images and smash their statues, and lay waste all their high places, cleansing the land and dwelling in it. For I have given it to you as a possession, which you shall divide among yourselves by lot. To the larger group you shall give a larger portion, and to the smaller a smaller one. Each person shall receive an inheritance according to where the lot falls. You shall divide the possession by tribes and families [Hebrew: ‘By the tribes of your families you shall receive the inheritance’].

“But if you do not kill the inhabitants of the land [Hebrew: ‘from before you’], those who remain [Col. 0398A] will be like nails in your eyes and spears in your sides. They will oppose you in the land where you dwell, and whatever I had planned to do to them, I shall do to you.”

[T. XIX, B. LXX, Chapter XXXIV.] The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Command the sons of Israel, and say to them: When you enter the land of Canaan and it falls to you as a possession by lot, its boundaries shall be as follows. The southern region shall begin at the wilderness of Zin, beside Edom, and its boundary on the east shall be the Salt Sea. The boundary shall turn around the southern side by the ascent of Akrabbim, and pass into Zin, and reach [Note: [Col. 0397D] The present Hebrew text reads in this way: [Hebrew text omitted in the supplied text]. But all the manuscripts, following the Septuagint, read: ‘and reach into the south as far as Kadesh-barnea.’ MART. —The Palatine manuscript has: ‘into Senna, and reach into the south as far as…’ The Urbinas has: ‘into Semnah, and reach toward the south, as far as…’] from the south as far as Kadesh-barnea.

“From there the boundary will go out to the village called Adar [Hebrew does not have this], and extend as far as Azmon. [Col. 0398B] The boundary will turn from Azmon toward the Wadi of Egypt and end at the shore of the Great Sea. The western region shall begin at the Great Sea, and its boundary shall end there.

“On the northern side the boundaries shall begin at the Great Sea, reaching as far as Mount Hor [Hebrew: the mountain], from which they shall come to Hamath, as far as the boundary of Zedad. The boundary shall go on to Ziphron and the village of Hazar-enan. These were the boundaries on the northern side.

“From there the boundaries shall be measured toward the eastern side, from Hazar-enan to Shepham; and from Shepham the boundary shall descend to Riblah, opposite Ain [Note: [Col. 0398D] The Hebrew does not contain the word Daphim, and I found that word added in an old manuscript of the Latin codex. We also searched for it in vain in the books of Hebrew names and places. MART. —I would prefer, following the authority of the Urbinas codex, that the name Daphim, or Daphnin, which the printed books offer, be deleted. For it is neither in the Hebrew, nor can it be determined what place this was. Those who, following the Targums, interpret it as the spring of Daphne not far from Antioch will scarcely persuade anyone.] Daphim [Hebrew: toward the east]. From there they shall extend eastward from the Sea of Chinnereth, and proceed as far as the Jordan, and finally end at the most saline sea. This shall be your land, according to its boundaries on every side.”

[C. XC.] Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying:

“This is the land which you shall possess by lot, and which the Lord commanded to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe. For the tribe of the sons of Reuben according to their families, the tribe of the sons of Gad according to the number of their clans, and the half-tribe of Manasseh—that is, two and a half tribes—received their portion across the Jordan, opposite Jericho, on the eastern side.”

And the Lord said to Moses:

[B. LXXI, C. XCI.] “These are the names of the men who shall divide the land for you: Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and one leader from each tribe. Their names are as follows:

“From the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh. From the tribe of Simeon, Samuel son of Ammihud. From the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon. From the tribe of the sons of Dan, Bukki son of Jogli [Hebrew: ‘The leader Bukki’; so from this point onward for each tribe]. From the sons of Joseph, from the tribe of Manasseh, Hanniel son of Ephod. From the tribe of Ephraim, Kemuel son of Shiphtan. From the tribe of Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach. From the tribe of Issachar, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan. From the tribe of Asher, Ahihud son of Shelomi. From the tribe of Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud.

“These are the men whom the Lord commanded to divide the land of Canaan among the sons of Israel.”

[C. XCII, Chapter XXXV.] The Lord also spoke these words to Moses [Hebrew: “And the Lord spoke to Moses”] in the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho:

“Command the sons of Israel to give the Levites cities for dwelling from their possessions, together with their surrounding suburbs, so that they may live in the towns and the suburbs may be for their flocks and livestock. These suburbs shall extend outside the walls of the cities, all around, for a distance of one thousand paces. On the eastern side there shall be two thousand cubits, and likewise on the southern side two thousand. Toward the sea, which faces west, the same measure shall apply, and the northern side shall be bounded by an equal limit. The cities shall be in the middle, and the suburbs outside.

[B. LXXIII.] “Of the towns which you shall give to the Levites, six shall be set apart as places of refuge, so that one who has shed blood may flee there. Besides these, there shall be forty-two other towns—that is, forty-eight towns in all, with their suburbs.

“The cities which shall be given from the possessions of the sons of Israel shall be taken in greater number from those who possess more, and in smaller number from those who possess less. Each person shall give towns to the Levites according to the measure of his inheritance.”

[T. XX, C. XCIII.] The Lord said to Moses:

“Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you have crossed the Jordan into the land of Canaan, designate which cities shall serve as places of refuge for fugitives who have shed blood unintentionally. When someone has fled to one of them, the relative of the slain person shall not be able to kill him until he stands before the assembly and his case has been judged [Hebrew: ‘for judgment’].

“Of those cities which are set apart as places of refuge, three shall be beyond the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan. They shall be available equally to the sons of Israel, to resident foreigners, and to sojourners, so that anyone who has unintentionally shed blood may flee there.

“If someone strikes another with an iron weapon [Hebrew: ‘with an iron instrument’], and the person struck dies, he shall be guilty of murder, and he himself shall die. If he throws a stone [Col. 0399D] and the person struck dies, he shall likewise be punished [Hebrew: ‘If he strikes him with a stone and the person struck dies, and the stone… of the size… of him… dies, the striker shall die… because he struck with something of such… that by estimation… its size… the striker shall die…’]. If the person struck with a piece of wood dies, the striker’s blood shall be avenged.

[C. XCIV.] “The relative of the slain shall kill the murderer; as soon as he seizes him, he shall kill him. If someone, out of hatred, pushes a man or throws something at him in ambush, or, being his enemy, strikes him with his hand and he dies, the striker shall be guilty of murder. The relative of the slain shall slaughter him as soon as he finds him.

[C. XCV.] “But if by chance, without hatred or hostility, he has done any of these things [Col. 0400A], and this has been established before the people, and the matter has been contested between the striker and the blood-relative, the innocent man shall be freed from the avenger’s hand and, by judgment, restored to the city to which he had fled. He shall remain there until the great priest who has been anointed with holy oil dies.

“If the killer is found outside the boundaries of the cities assigned to exiles, and is struck by the one who is the avenger of blood, the one who killed him shall be without guilt. For the fugitive ought to have remained in the city until the death of the high priest. After the high priest has died, the murderer shall return to his own land.

“These things shall be everlasting statutes in all your dwellings [Hebrew: ‘in all your generations and dwellings’]. A murderer shall be punished on the testimony of witnesses; no one shall be condemned on the testimony of a single witness.

“You shall not accept a price from one who is guilty of blood, for he must certainly die. Exiles and fugitives shall in no way be able to return to their cities before the death of the high priest: lest [Hebrew: ‘because he will die. You shall not accept a price from exiles and fugitives, so that they may return to their cities before the death of the high priest. Lest…’] you pollute the land where you dwell, which is stained by the blood of the innocent. It cannot otherwise be purified except by the blood of the one who shed another’s blood. Thus your possession shall be cleansed while I dwell among you. For I am the Lord, who dwell among the sons of Israel.”

[B. LXXIV, C. XCVI, Chapter XXXVI.] The leaders of the families of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clan of the sons of [Hebrew: “the leaders of the families, of the clan of the sons of”] Joseph, approached. They spoke before the leaders of Israel and said:

“The Lord commanded you, our lord, to divide the land by lot among the sons of Israel, and to give the daughters of Zelophehad, our brother, the possession due to their father. But if men of another tribe take them as wives, their possession will follow them; and, transferred to another tribe, it will be diminished from our inheritance. Thus it will happen that when the jubilee arrives—that is, the fiftieth year of remission—the distribution by lots will be confused, and one group’s possession will pass to another.”

Moses answered the sons of Israel and, at the Lord’s command, said:

“The tribe of the sons of Joseph has spoken rightly. This is also the law which the Lord has enacted concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: Let them marry whom they wish, provided that they marry men of their own tribe, so that the possession of the sons of Israel may not pass from tribe to tribe. For all men shall take wives from their own tribe and clan, and all women shall take husbands from the same tribe, so that the inheritance may remain within the families. The tribes shall not be mixed with one another, but shall remain as the Lord has separated them.”

The daughters of Zelophehad did as they had been commanded. Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah married the sons of their paternal uncle, from the family of Manasseh, who was a son of Joseph. The possession assigned to them remained in the tribe and family of their father.

These are the commands and judgments which the Lord gave through Moses to the sons of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho.

The book of Numbers, which in Hebrew is called *Vajedabber*, ends here.

[Col. 0401]

# THE BOOK OF DEUTERONOMY

## TABLE OF CONTENTS OF THE BOOK OF DEUTERONOMY

## TITLES OF THE BOOK OF DEUTERONOMY

[Col. 0401A]

I. Beyond the Jordan he explains the law to the people and recalls how he urged them to choose prudent men whom they should appoint as judges; how he sent inspectors to the promised land; how the whole multitude of the people proved rebellious; and how, on account of their transgression, Moses himself was also deprived of entry into the promised land. He also relates how the Lord commanded that nothing be taken from the possession of the sons of Esau and Lot.

II. He recalls the passage through the city of Har, which the Cappadocians possessed, and how he sent messengers to Sihon and Og, kings of the Amorites. When they rejected the Lord’s commands, battle was begun against them, and their land was handed over for possession to the two and a half tribes.

[Col. 0401B]

III. He exhorts the people to observe and perform the commands and judgments, and not to offend the Lord by devoting themselves to the rites of the nations. He appeals to them with paternal affection, declaring that there is no nation so renowned as to be near to God. He recalls how they approached the mountain and heard the voice of God from the midst of the fire, and how the Decalogue was written on tablets of stone by the finger of God. He says that he is going to die. He warns them not to make idols, since there is no other God but one. He recalls which cities were separated as places of refuge for fugitives who had killed a man unintentionally.

IV. Having summoned the whole people, he said that he himself had been an intermediary, or mediator, between Israel and God, and he sets out in order the ten words. He urges them to keep them, lest they perish as transgressors.

[Col. 0401C]

V. Hear, Israel: the Lord your God is one God, and you shall love the Lord your God. This must always be meditated upon and commended to sons and grandsons. One must not go after foreign gods. It must not be forgotten that they served Pharaoh, and that seven nations were to be destroyed by the Lord. They were not permitted to mingle in marriage even with the daughters of those nations. They must not fear the most powerful enemies, because the Lord would deliver them into their hands. They must not desire any gold or silver from idols, because it is accursed. He recalls the forty years’ journeys through the wilderness, the manna provided, and the fact that their clothing and all their other possessions were not worn out by age; for these things they ought always to remember the Lord their God.

VI. He says that the people will enter the land which the Lord God promised, and warns them not to presume that the land was subjected or given to them on account of their righteousness, especially since they had continually provoked the Lord to anger when they made the calf, and for this reason he had broken the tablets and had approached as an intercessor on account of that crime. He then recalls the Graves of Lust; the inspectors who were sent; the making of the second tablets; the construction of the ark; and the death of Aaron on Mount Hor.

VII. He warns that the Lord commands a person nothing else except his worship and the keeping of his commandments, and that he must not follow the crime of transgressors. Blessings if you obey; curses if you neglect them.

[Col. 0402A]

VIII. He gives the judgments that must be carried out in the promised land: idols must be broken; tithes and firstborn must be given; burnt offerings must be offered; and the priests must not be abandoned.

IX. Concerning the false prophet and dreamer. He warns that a brother, son, friend, or wife who urges someone to go after idols must be stoned. Concerning the distinction between clean and unclean animals, birds, and fish; what may and may not be eaten; and the year of remission, in which nothing is to be demanded from the needy and poor and nothing refused them. Concerning a Hebrew sold into slavery; the redemption of firstborn animals; and the prohibition against eating blood.

X. The Passover must be celebrated, together with the rite of its solemnity. In judgment no one’s person is to be favored. Those who worship the sun and moon are to be stoned. A man of another nation must not be appointed king; and the Levites and priests must be content with tithes and offerings.

XI. A Levite coming from his own city to another must exercise the ministry of the Lord by right among his brothers. Magicians are to be removed. A great prophet is to arise from the same people, while a false prophet must be destroyed. He also treats of the laws which they must observe.

XII. Concerning the advance of warriors: how they should proceed, and how, after the enemies have been destroyed, the spoils should be divided among the army. Concerning a man’s corpse found beside a city; a beautiful woman taken captive; two wives and their sons; a disobedient son; a grave sin; an object found and to be returned; men’s and women’s clothing; and various laws.

XIII. Concerning things that ordinarily occur in dreams, and other laws promulgated for acts of righteousness.

XIV. Concerning entry into the promised land, and how they are to profess before the priests that they have obtained it.

XV. The commandments must be kept; curses belong to the negligent, blessings to those who keep them; and the people respond by saying “Amen.”

XVI. He repeats the words of the covenant and exhorts them not to abandon the Lord and follow idols, or the rites of the nations whose land they are to receive and possess.

XVII. He says that he is 120 years old. He summons Joshua and strengthens him with his words, and foretells that Joshua himself will divide the land by lot. He writes the law, hands it over to the priests, and reads it to the assembled people.

[Col. 0402D]

XVIII. The Lord says to Moses: “The days of your death are near; call Joshua to the entrance of the tabernacle, and I shall command him.” The Lord appears to them in a pillar of cloud and declares that the people will follow idols. Moses writes a song and teaches it to the sons of Israel. He commands the Levites to place the law beside the ark as a testimony. He calls heaven and earth as witnesses against them, that they may perish when they commit evil, and he sings a prophetic song concerning future events, in which, speaking in the person of the Lord, he reproaches them, saying: “Where are your gods, Israel, in whom you trusted?”—and other things wonderfully and terribly to be feared.

XIX. After Moses has completed all the words of the song, the Lord speaks to him on that same day: “Ascend Mount Nebo, die, and be joined to your people.” Before he ascends, he blesses all Israel according to their tribes. After ascending the summit of the mountain, he sees the whole promised land, into which he could not enter because of the contradiction and provocation at the waters of contradiction. There he is described as having died; his burial place is unknown; and no prophet like him arose afterward in Israel.

# Contents of the Book *Elle Addabarim*, which in Greek is called *Deuteronomy*

[Col. 0405]

[Col. 0405C] I. The words that Moses spoke to all Israel in the fortieth year in the wilderness, after the killing of Sihon and Og, kings, concerning all that God had commanded him at Horeb.

[Col. 0405D] II. Moses said to the people at that time: “I cannot bear you alone,” and he appointed wise men over them.

III. They set out from Horeb and traveled through the whole wilderness.

IV. You approached me and said: “Let us send men ahead of us,” and I acted according to this word.

V. And you were unwilling to go up, nor did you believe the word of the Lord.

VI. And I said to you: “The Lord your God will go before you,” and you did not believe.

VII. You murmured, and the Lord was angered; and he swore that you would not enter that good land, except Caleb and his sons.

[Col. 0406C] VIII. The Lord was also angry with me because of you, saying: “Neither shall you enter there, but Jesus son of Nun shall enter there, and their sons, whom they had said would be taken captive.”

IX. And contrary to the command you went up the mountain, and the Amorite came out and pursued you.

X. He proceeds similarly through each matter, enumerating all the great deeds of God and the powers by which God went before them, and how he fed them in the wilderness for forty years, and what God did to the two kings, Sihon and Og.
