XI. And at that time I pleaded with the Lord, but he rejected me because of you.

XII. Here again he urges them not to depart from the commandments.

XIII. Beware lest you make for yourselves a carved image, the likeness of any human being, or of cattle, or of anything that is on the earth, or in heaven, or in the sea.

XIV. The Lord was angry with me because of you, and I shall not enter with you, but shall die in this land. Take heed [Col. 0407A] lest you forget the covenant of the Lord your God; for if you provoke God, I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that you shall perish from that land.

XV. Ask whether anything like this has ever been heard, from the day God created humanity: whether there is any people under heaven to whom the Lord has spoken from the midst of fire.

XVI. Then Moses designated cities of refuge for homicides.

XVII. This is the law that Moses spoke when he summoned all Israel to himself.

XVIII. These are the words that the Lord spoke to the whole assembly of Israel, and you said to me that I should hear from God and speak to you. Now do whatever the Lord has commanded you, turning neither to the right nor to the left.

[Col. 0407B] XIX. Hear, Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord, and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your strength.

XX. You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve him alone.

XXI. You shall not follow foreign gods, lest you be uprooted.

XXII. You shall not put the Lord your God to the test, but you shall do what he has commanded you; and you shall tell your son how the Lord brought you out of Egypt.

XXIII. But when the Lord brings you into the land that you are to possess, you shall destroy all those nations, their altars and pillars, and burn their carved images with fire.

XXIV. If you observe these commandments and ordinances, the Lord will keep for you the covenant that he swore to your fathers; he will bless you and remove every sickness from you.

[Col. 0407C] XXV. You shall not spare the nations whom the Lord will subject to you, nor say: “This is a great nation; how shall I be able to oppose it?” You shall not covet the gold or silver of their carved images, but shall devote them to destruction.

XXVI. You shall observe all the commandments that I give you today, so that you may live; and remember all that you experienced in the wilderness: you were hungry, and the Lord gave you manna, so that you might know that a human being lives not by bread alone, but by every word of God.

XXVII. Take heed to yourself, lest you forget the benefits of the Lord your God.

XXVIII. Do not say in your heart: “My strength has accomplished all these things.”

XXIX. Hear, Israel: today you are crossing the Jordan and will take possession of great nations and fortified cities; and you shall know that the Lord your God goes before you.

XXX. Do not say in your heart: “Because of my righteousness the Lord has brought me into this land.”

XXXI. Remember how often you provoked the Lord in the wilderness.

XXXII. At Horeb you provoked the Lord when you made the molten image.

XXXIII. And the Lord said to me: “Leave me, and I shall destroy them.”

XXXIV. I came down from the mountain and saw that you had sinned; I threw the tablets from my hands and broke them.

[Col. 0408A] XXXV. And I again pleaded with the Lord as before, for forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water.

XXXVI. The Lord was exceedingly angry with Aaron because of what you had done in making the calf.

XXXVII. I seized it and burned it.

XXXVIII. And at the incident of the testing you provoked the Lord.

XXXIX. And when the Lord sent you from Kadesh-Barnea.

XL. I pleaded before the Lord for forty days and forty nights.

XLI. At that time the Lord said to me: “Cut for yourself two stone tablets like the former ones, and come up to me on the mountain.”

XLII. I made the ark and went up the mountain.

[Col. 0408B] XLIII. I came down and placed the tablets in the ark.

XLIV. At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark.

XLV. And now, Israel, what else does the Lord require of you except that you fear the Lord your God, love him, and serve him?

XLVI. You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve him alone.

XLVII. When your fathers went down to Egypt with seventy souls [Note: [Col. 0407D] In the Palatine manuscript, “with 75 souls.”], God made you as numerous as the stars of heaven.

XLVIII. And you shall love the Lord, and you shall know how the Lord brought you out of Egypt, and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab.

XLIX. If you obey his commandments, he will give rain to your land [Col. 0408C] and abundance to your fields.

L. But if you obey this whole commandment, the Lord will drive out all the nations from before you.

LI. Behold, I set before you today a blessing and a curse.

LII. These are the commandments and ordinances that you shall observe.

LIII. You shall not do whatever you please.

LIV. In the place that the Lord chooses, you shall offer everything that I command you.

LV. You shall eat all your firstfruits in the presence of the Lord your God.

LVI. Take heed lest you eat blood.

LVII. Keep and do all the words that I command you.

LVIII. Every word that I command you, keep and do; and if a prophet says to you, “Let us go and serve gods,” you shall not listen.

[Col. 0408D] LIX. You shall follow the Lord your God and fear him.

LX. But if your brother, or son, or wife, or friend says to you, “Let us go and serve gods,” you shall not spare him, but shall denounce him, and he shall be stoned.

LXI. But if you hear that in one of your cities there are sinful men who have caused all its inhabitants to apostatize, and if the deed is truly established, you shall kill them all.

LXII. You shall not make baldness upon the dead.

[Col. 0409A] LXIII. These are the animals that you shall eat.

LXIV. These you shall eat among the creatures that are in the waters.

LXV. You shall eat every clean bird.

LXVI. You shall offer the tithes of your field in the place that the Lord chooses.

LXVII. But when it is far from you, you shall sell them and redeem them there.

LXVIII. Every seven years you shall grant remission.

LXIX. If you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, you shall be ruler of many nations.

LXX. If one of your brothers becomes needy among you.

LXXI. If you purchase a Hebrew boy, he shall serve you for six years.

LXXII. You shall consecrate every firstborn to the Lord.

LXXIII. Observe the month of new produce, and celebrate the Passover [Col. 0409B] to the Lord your God.

LXXIV. You shall appoint judges and scribes to judge justly.

LXXV. You shall not plant for yourself a sacred grove.

LXXVI. If someone among you is found serving gods, he shall die on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

LXXVII. If a matter is hidden from you, go to the priest.

LXXVIII. Whoever does not listen to the priest shall die.

LXXIX. You shall not appoint a foreigner as ruler over you.

LXXX. This is the judgment concerning priests.

LXXXI. No one among you shall be found purifying his son or daughter.

LXXXII. “I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brothers.”

LXXXIII. If a prophet speaks a word and it does not come to pass, he shall be killed.

[Col. 0409C] LXXXIV. This is the command concerning a homicide.

LXXXV. You shall not move the boundaries that your fathers established.

LXXXVI. You shall not accept the testimony of one person against another.

LXXXVII. Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth.

LXXXVIII. If you go out to war, do not be afraid.

LXXXIX. If you approach to attack a city.

XC. If you besiege a city.

XCI. If a wounded man is found in the land.

XCII. If God delivers your enemies into your hand.

XCIII. If a man has two wives, one beloved and one hated.

XCIV. [Note: [Col. 0409D] The whole of this chapter is absent from the Palatine manuscript.] If someone has a disobedient son.

[Col. 0409D] XCV. If there is in anyone a sin deserving death.

XCVI. If you see your brother’s animal straying or fallen.

XCVII. A woman shall not put on a man’s garment.

XCVIII. If you find a bird’s nest.

XCIX. If you build a new house.

C. You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey.

CI. If someone takes a wife and hates her.

CII. If an adulterer is found with an adulteress.

CIII. If someone sleeps with a betrothed girl.

CIV. If someone finds a betrothed girl in the field and uses force against her.

[Col. 0410A] CV. If someone finds a virgin girl and sleeps with her.

CVI. A man shall not take his father’s wife.

CVII. A castrated man shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.

CVIII. A prostitute shall not enter, nor an Ammonite or Moabite, into the assembly of the Lord.

CIX. You shall not abominate an Edomite or an Egyptian.

CX. If a man is unclean, he shall go outside the camp.

CXI. You shall not hand over a slave to his master.

CXII. There shall not be a prostitute among the Israelites.

CXIII. You shall not bring the earnings of a prostitute.

CXIV. [Note: [Col. 0410D] This chapter too is missing from the same manuscript.] You shall not exact interest from your brother.

CXV. If you make a vow to the Lord, do not delay fulfilling it.

CXVI. If you enter your neighbor’s vineyard.

[Col. 0410B] CXVII. If you enter your neighbor’s standing grain.

CXVIII. If someone takes a wife and finds in her an indecent matter.

CXIX. If someone has recently taken a wife, he shall not go out to war.

CXX. You shall not take the millstone as a pledge.

CXXI. If a thief is caught.

CXXII. Remember what the Lord did to Miriam.

CXXIII. You shall not take a debtor’s pledge by force.

CXXIV. You shall not sleep with a poor man’s pledge, and do not delay returning the wages of a laborer.

CXXV. Fathers shall not die for their sons.

CXXVI. You shall not pervert the judgment of the resident alien, the orphan, or the widow.

CXXVII. You shall not take a widow’s garment as a pledge.

[Col. 0410C] CXXVIII. If you reap your standing grain.

CXXIX. If you gather olives.

CXXX. If you harvest your vineyard.

CXXXI. If you judge a wicked person, you shall give him forty lashes.

CXXXII. You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

CXXXIII. If someone dies who has a wife but no children, his brother shall take her.

CXXXIV. If a man refuses to take his brother’s wife.

CXXXV. If two men quarrel with each other.

CXXXVI. You shall not have an unjust weight or double measures.

CXXXVII. Remember how much Amalek did to you.

CXXXVIII. When you enter the land that the Lord [Col. 0410D] your God will give you.

CXXXIX. And Moses said to the people: “Be silent and listen.”

CXL. These shall stand to bless the people, and these to curse.

CXLI. Cursed is everyone who does these things.

CXLII. If you keep the commandments of the Lord, these blessings shall come upon you.

CXLIII. If you do not listen, these curses shall come upon you.

CXLIV. Moses summoned all the sons of Israel and said to them: “You know what the Lord did to Pharaoh for your sake.”

[Col. 0411A] CXLV. The things hidden belong to God, but the things that are manifest belong to us.

CXLVI. The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart.

CXLVII. Behold, I have set before your eyes life and death.

CXLVIII. And Moses completed all these words.

CXLIX. Moses summoned Jesus and said to him: “Act manfully and be strong.”

CL. The Lord said to Moses: “You shall sleep with your fathers, and this people shall prostitute itself after foreign gods.”

CLI. Moses wrote this song.

CLII. The Lord said to Moses: “Go up into Mount Abarim and die there.”

CLIII. Moses, the man of God, blessed the sons of Israel.

CLIV. Moses died in the land of Moab.

CLV. And no prophet arose in Israel like Moses.

# The Book *Elle Addabarim* Begins, Which in Greek Is Called *Deuteronomy*

[Col. 0411]

[Col. 0411B] [T. I, C. I, Chap. I.] These are the words that Moses spoke [Note: [Col. 0411C] At this point the Jewish apostate Aben-Ezra, as well as the dregs of the Christians—Hobbes, Spinoza, and other writers of the same audacity—abuse the passage by stubbornly denying that Moses was the author of the whole Pentateuch. Le Clerc and Richard Simon likewise adopted this position; although they disagree most vehemently on many matters, they ultimately agree in this: that they should overthrow the most ancient tradition in the Church of God and the conviction received into everyone’s mind. But our most learned scholiast refutes such innovators, aptly observing that the Hebrew should be read: “These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel at the crossing of the Jordan.” He also noted this with admirable diligence in what follows, in order to remove the ambiguity of the word *trans* (“across”), so that one would say that Moses wrote these things with no other intention than that we should be taught that Moses himself was the author of every word of Deuteronomy. Let the interested reader compare this first chapter, verses 1 and 5, [Col. 0411D] with what is read below, in the third chapter, verses 8 and 25: he will immediately perceive the particle *trans*, which is explained by scholia where it could not refer to Moses speaking, but remains untouched and without scholia where it agrees with Moses speaking. For example, Moses beseeches the Lord in chapter III, verse 25, in these words: “Let me cross over, then, and see this excellent land beyond the Jordan”—that is, the land of Canaan, which, with respect to Moses speaking, was beyond the Jordan. Therefore no scholion is added there, as is seen in verse 8 of the same chapter, because the Amorite kings of whom Moses was speaking were not beyond but on this side of the Jordan with respect to him. Who would ever have believed that the audacious writers of our time would be routed by the Canon of Hebrew Truth, and that the principal argument which they thought they possessed would be completely dissolved by the opinions of the ancient teachers? It should not be omitted that the author of the spurious work *On the Ten Temptations in the Wilderness*, which was published among the writings of Jerome, borrowed much from the scholia of the Canon of Hebrew Truth. MART. —The Hebrew indeed has it literally, just as it is noted by the Scholiast: “at the crossing of the Jordan.” Jerome seems to have retained “beyond the Jordan” from the old Latin translation, although this hardly suits Moses, who never crossed that river. Accordingly, others, following the character of the Hebrew language, understand it as “on this side,” others as “beside” or “opposite.” Nor were there lacking those who, conversely, argued from this particle that the text had been substituted by another person after Moses; among them Richard Simon, whom Martianay does not entirely justly include and censure. The Hebrew exemplar, however, leaves no room for such quibbling.]

to all Israel beyond the Jordan [h. at the crossing of the Jordan], in the wilderness of the plain [h. in the plain], opposite the Red Sea, between Paran and Tophel and Laban and Hazeroth, where there is a great abundance of gold [h. and an abundance of gold]. It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir as far as Kadesh-Barnea [h. an eleven-days’ journey from Horeb to Mount Seir as far as Kadesh-Barnea]. In the fortieth year [and it came to pass in the fortieth year], in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke to the sons everything that the Lord had commanded him to say to them, after he had struck down Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, who remained in Ashtaroth and Edrei, beyond the Jordan [h. at the crossing of the Jordan], in the land of Moab. And Moses began to explain the law [h. this law] and to say: “The Lord our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying: ‘You have stayed long enough on this mountain. Turn back and come [h. look back and come] to the mountain of the Amorites and to all the neighboring plain and mountain country, and to the lower regions opposite the south, and beside the sea, the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates. Behold,’ he said, ‘I have delivered it to you. Enter and possess it, concerning which the Lord swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, that he would give it to them and to their descendants after them.’”

[B. I, C. II.] And I said to you at that time: “I cannot bear you alone, because the Lord your God has multiplied you, and today you are as numerous as the stars of heaven.” (May the Lord, the God of your fathers, add many thousands to this number and bless you as he has spoken.) “I cannot alone bear your affairs [Col. 0412C] and your burden and quarrels. Provide from among yourselves wise and experienced men, whose conduct has been tested in your tribes, that I may appoint them over you [Col. 0413A] as leaders.” Then you answered me: “The matter you wish to undertake is good.” So I took from your tribes wise and noble men and appointed them as leaders, tribunes, centurions, commanders of fifty, and decans, to teach you each matter. And I commanded them, saying: “Hear them, and judge what is just, whether the person is a citizen or a resident alien. There shall be no distinction of persons; you shall hear the small as well as the great, and you shall not accept anyone’s person, because judgment belongs to God. But if anything appears difficult to you, refer it to me, and I shall hear it.” And I commanded you everything that you ought to do.

[C. III.] Setting out from Horeb, we traveled through that terrible and vast wilderness which you saw, by the way of the mountain of the Amorites, as the Lord our God had commanded us. And when we had come [Col. 0413B] to Kadesh-Barnea, I said to you: “You have come to the mountain of the Amorites, which the Lord our God is about to give us. See the land that the Lord your God is giving you; go up and possess it, [Note: [Col. 0413D] In the printed editions we read, “as the Lord our God spoke to your fathers,” which several manuscript codices also follow, with a few omissions or alterations. For some have “to our fathers”; others omit “our” and read, “the Lord God spoke to your fathers.” The Canon reads purely according to the Hebrew. MART. —Together with the Vulgate and the Urbinas manuscript: “as the Lord our God spoke to your fathers.” The Palatine differs from it only in omitting the pronoun “our.”] as the Lord, the God of your fathers, spoke to you. Do not fear or be afraid of anything.”

[C. IV.] And you all approached me and said: “Let us send men to inspect the land [h. before us] and report by which route we should go up and to which cities we should proceed.”

[B. II.] When the proposal had pleased me, I sent twelve men from among you, one from each tribe. When they had gone and ascended into the hill country, they came as far as the Valley of Botri [h. as far as the torrent of Botri], and after inspecting the land, they took some of its fruit to display its fertility and brought it [Col. 0413C] to us; and they said: “The land that the Lord our God is about to give us is good.”

[C. V.] You were unwilling to go up, however, but, unbelieving toward the word of the Lord our God, you murmured in your tents and said: “The Lord hates us, and therefore he brought us out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorite and destroy us. Where [h. Brothers, where] shall we go up? Our messengers terrified our hearts, saying: ‘The multitude is enormous and taller in stature than we; the cities are great and fortified up to heaven; there we saw the sons of the Anakim.’” And I said to you: “Do not fear or be afraid of them.”

[C. VI.] “The Lord God, who is your guide, himself will fight for you, as he did in Egypt, before the eyes of all.”

[Note: [Col. 0413D] In the Canon and many other very ancient manuscripts this parenthesis is expressed in the plural, namely, “you yourselves saw”; but there is no dispute over readings of this kind. Thus Saint Jerome, explaining a similar variant reading of Psalm 83 in his letter to Sunnia and Fretela, says: “And I ask you,” he says, “to avoid such foolish and superfluous disputes, where there is no change in meaning.” It seemed worthwhile to warn the reader of this once, so that he may know that we have passed over many similar matters. MART.]

And in the wilderness (you yourselves saw) the Lord your God carried you, as a man is accustomed to carry his little [h. does not have “little”] son, along the whole way by which you traveled, until you came to this place. Yet even then you did not believe the Lord your God, who went before you on the way and marked out the place where you were to pitch your tents [h. camps], showing you the way by night through fire and by day through a column of cloud.

[C. VII.] When the Lord heard the sound of your words, he was angry and swore, saying: “No one among the men of this most wicked generation shall see the good land that I promised under oath to your fathers, except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and to him I shall give the land on which he trod, and to his son, because he followed the Lord.”

Nor was his anger against the people surprising, since the Lord was also angry with me because of you and said:

[C. VIII.] “Neither shall you enter there; but Joshua son of Nun, your minister, shall enter in your place. Encourage and strengthen him, and he shall divide the land by lot among Israel. Your little ones, of whom you said that they would be taken captive, and the children who today do not know the difference between good and evil, they shall enter, and to them I shall give the land, and they shall possess it. But you, turn back and depart into the wilderness by way of the Red Sea.”

And you answered me: “We have sinned against the Lord.”

[C. IX.] “We shall go up and fight, as the Lord our God commanded.”

When you had armed yourselves and were going toward the mountain, the Lord said to me: “Say to them: ‘Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not with you, lest you fall before your enemies.’” I spoke, but you did not listen. Instead, resisting the command of the Lord and swelling with pride, you went up the mountain. Then the Amorite who lived in the mountains came out [h. in the mountain and to meet you] and pursued you as bees are accustomed to pursue, and he struck you down from Seir as far as Hormah. When you returned and wept before the Lord, he did not hear you and was unwilling to heed your voice. So you remained at Kadesh-Barnea for a long time.

[C. X, Chap. II.] Setting out from there, we came into the wilderness that leads to the Red Sea, as the Lord had said to me, and we went around Mount Seir for a long time.

[B. III.] And the Lord said to me: “You have gone around this mountain long enough. Turn northward, and command the people, saying: ‘You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, and they will fear you. Take great care, therefore, not to move against them. For I shall not give you any of their land—not even enough for the sole of a foot to tread upon—because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession. You shall purchase food from them for money and eat; you shall draw purchased water and drink.’ The Lord your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He knows your journey, how you crossed this great wilderness, while the Lord your God was with you for forty years, and you lacked nothing.”

When we had passed by our brothers, the sons of Esau, who lived in Seir, by the plain road from Elath and from Ezion-Geber, we came to the road that leads into the wilderness of Moab. And the Lord said to me: “Do not fight against the Moabites or engage them in battle, for I shall not give you any of their land, because I have given Ar to the sons of Lot as a possession. The Emim were its first inhabitants, a great and powerful people, so tall that they were believed to be of the race of the Anakim, and they were like the sons of the Anakim. Indeed, the Moabites call them Emim. In Seir the Horites formerly lived; after they were expelled and destroyed, the sons of Esau lived there, as Israel did in the land of its possession, which the Lord gave it.”

So we arose to cross the torrent [Col. 0415B] Zered and came to it. The time during which we traveled from Kadesh-Barnea to the crossing of the torrent Zered was thirty-eight years, until the whole generation of fighting men was consumed from the camp, as the Lord had sworn. His hand was against them, so that they perished from the midst of the camp.

[B. IV.] After all the warriors had fallen:

[T. II.] The Lord spoke to me, saying: “Today you shall cross the territory of Moab, the city called Ar, and, approaching the vicinity of the sons of Ammon, beware lest you fight against them or move to battle, for I shall not give you any of the land of the sons of Ammon, because I have given it to the sons of Lot as a possession. It was reckoned as the land of giants; giants once lived there, whom the Ammonites call Zamzummim, a great and numerous people of tall stature like the Anakim. The Lord destroyed them from before them and caused them to live in their place, as he had done for the sons of Esau who live in Seir, destroying the Horites and giving them their land, which they possess to the present day. The Avvim, who lived in Hazerim as far as Gaza, were expelled by the Cappadocians, who came out from Cappadocia, destroyed them, and lived in their place. [h. The Avvim also, who lived in Hazerim as far as Gaza, were destroyed by the Cappadocians who lived in Cappadocia, and they lived in their place.]”

[B. V.] “Rise up and cross the torrent Arnon. Behold, I have delivered Sihon, king of Heshbon, the Amorite, into your hand; begin to possess his land and engage him in battle. Today I shall begin to send your terror and dread among the peoples who live under the whole heaven, so that when they hear your name [h. when they hear your fame], they may fear, tremble like women in labor, and be overcome with pain [h. tremble before you].”

So I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon, king of Heshbon, with words of peace, saying: [h.] “I shall pass through your land; I shall travel on the public road. I shall turn neither to the right nor to the left. Sell me food for money, so that I may eat; give me water for money, so that I may drink. Only grant me passage, as the sons of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who dwell in Ar have done, until I come to the Jordan and cross into the land that the Lord our God is about to give [Col. 0416A] us.”

But Sihon, king of Heshbon, was unwilling to grant us passage, because the Lord your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart stubborn, so that he might be delivered into your hands, as you now see.

And the Lord said to me: “Behold, I have begun to deliver Sihon to you and his land; begin to possess it.”

Then Sihon came out to meet us with all his people for battle at Jahaz. And the Lord our God delivered him to us; we struck him, his sons, and all his people. At that time we captured all his cities, killing their inhabitants—men, women, and little ones. We left nothing in them, except the animals, which became the share of the plunderers, and the spoils of the cities that we captured from Aroer, which is on the bank of the torrent Arnon, and from the town situated in the valley, as far as Gilead. No village or city escaped our hands; the Lord our God delivered them all to us, except the land of the sons of Ammon, to which we did not approach, and all the places adjoining the torrent Jabbok, the cities of the hill country, and all the places from which the Lord our God forbade us to go.

[Chap. III.] Then we turned and went up by the road to Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, came out to meet us with his people [h. with all his people] to fight at Edrei. And the Lord said to me: “Do not fear him, for he has been delivered into your hand, together with all his people and his land. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”

So the Lord our God delivered Og, king of Bashan, also into our hands, together with all his people. We struck them down to complete destruction, devastating all his cities at one time [h. at that time]. There was no town that escaped us: sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan. All the cities were fortified with very high walls, gates, and bars, apart from innumerable towns that had no walls. We destroyed them as we had done Sihon, king of Heshbon, destroying every city and its men, women, and little ones; but we seized the animals and the spoils of the cities.

At that time we took the land from the hands of the two Amorite kings who were beyond the Jordan [h. who were at the crossing of the Jordan], from the torrent Arnon to Mount Hermon, which the Sidonians call Sirion [Col. 0416D] and the Amorites call Senir; all the cities situated in the plain, and the whole of Gilead and Bashan as far as Salcah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan. For only Og, king of Bashan, remained of the race of giants.

[B. VI.] His iron bedstead is displayed in Rabbah [h. Behold, his bedstead is iron in Rabbah] of the sons of Ammon; it is nine cubits long and four cubits wide, according to the measure of a man’s cubit [h. according to a man’s cubit].

At that time we possessed the land [h. This land also, which we possessed] from Aroer, which is on the bank of the torrent Arnon, to the middle of Mount Gilead; and I gave its cities to Reuben and Gad. The remaining [Col. 0417A] part of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to half the tribe of Manasseh, the whole region of Argob; all Bashan is called the land of giants. Jair son of Manasseh possessed the whole region of Argob as far as the borders of the Geshurites and Maacathites. He called Bashan by his own name, Havvoth-Jair—that is, the Villages of Jair [h. does not have “that is, the villages of Jair”]—to the present day. To Machir I also gave Gilead.

To the tribes of Reuben and Gad I gave part of Gilead [h. does not have “land”], from the torrent Arnon—the middle of the torrent [Note: [Col. 0417D] The Canon and other more ancient manuscripts have not “boundary” but “boundaries,” reading as follows: “the middle of the torrent and of the boundaries”; this amounts to the same meaning. MART. [Col. 0418D] —The Urbinas manuscript reads, “I gave the land of Gilead.” Shortly afterward the Palatine and other manuscripts in Martianay’s possession have “boundaries” instead of “boundary.”]—and the boundary as far as the torrent Jabbok, which is the boundary of the sons of Ammon, and the plain of the wilderness, together with the Jordan and the borders of Chinnereth [h. and the wilderness and the Jordan, and the border of Chinnereth], as far as the sea of the wilderness, which is most salty, at the foot of Mount Pisgah [Col. 0417B] toward the east.

And at that time I commanded you, saying: “The Lord your God is giving you this land as an inheritance. Equipped for battle, go before all your brothers, the sons of Israel, every strong man, without wives, children, or animals. For I know that you have many herds, and they must remain in the cities that I have given you, until the Lord grants rest to your brothers as he has granted it to you, and they too possess the land that he will give them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you shall return to his possession, which I have given you.”

[B. VII.] At that time I also commanded Joshua, saying: “Your eyes have seen what the Lord your God did to these two kings; so will he do to all the kingdoms through which you are about to pass. Do not fear [h. Do not fear, plural] them. For the Lord [Col. 0417C] your God will fight for you.”

And at that time I pleaded with the Lord, saying: “Lord God [h. Lord, Lord], you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your very strong hand. For there is no other god, either in heaven or on earth, who can perform your works or be compared with your strength. Let me cross over [h. Please let me cross over], then, and see this excellent land beyond the Jordan, this splendid mountain, and Lebanon.”

But the Lord was angry with me because of you and did not hear me; rather, he said to me: “It is enough for you; never speak to me again about this matter. Go up to the summit of Pisgah, lift your eyes toward the west, the north, the south, and the east, and look; for you shall not cross this Jordan. Command Joshua, strengthen him, and encourage him, [Col. 0417D] for he shall go before this people and divide among them the land that you will see.”

And we remained in the valley opposite the shrine of Peor.

## [T. III, B. IX, C. XII, Chapter IV]

“And now, Israel, hear the ordinances and judgments that I teach you, so that, by doing them, you may live and enter in and possess the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, is going to give you. You shall not add to the word that I speak to you [h. that I command you], nor shall you take anything away from it. Keep the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you.

Your eyes have seen everything that the Lord did [Col. 0418A] against Baal-peor, how he destroyed all its worshipers from among you. But you who cling to the Lord your God are all alive to the present day. You know that I taught you ordinances and judgments, just as the Lord my God commanded me; so shall you do them in the land that you are going to possess, and you shall observe and fulfill them in practice [h. and the judgments, just as the Lord my God commanded me, so that you should do them in the land that you are going to possess, and observe and fulfill them in practice].

For this is your wisdom and understanding before the peoples: when they hear all these ordinances, they shall say, ‘Behold, this is a wise and understanding people, a great nation’ [h. this great nation]. For what other nation is so great that it has gods drawing near to it, as the Lord [Vulgate omits: the Lord] [Col. 0418B] our God is to all our petitions? What other nation is so renowned that it has rites, just judgments, and a whole law [h. in accordance with the whole law] that I shall set before your eyes today [h. before your presence]?

### [B. X.]

“Therefore, watch over yourself and your soul carefully. Do not forget the words that your eyes have seen, and do not let them depart from your heart all the days of your life. You shall teach them to your sons and grandsons: the day [Vulgate: from the day] on which I stood before the Lord your God at Horeb, when the Lord spoke to me, saying: ‘Gather the people to me, so that they may hear my words and learn to fear me all the time that they live upon the earth, and may teach their sons.’

And you approached [h. And you approached and stood] the foot of the mountain, which was burning [Col. 0418C] up to heaven; and there were darkness, cloud, and gloom upon it. The Lord spoke to you from the midst of the fire. You heard the sound of his words, but you saw no form at all. And he showed [h. And he proclaimed] you his covenant, which he commanded you to perform, and [h. this is absent: and] the ten words that he wrote on two stone tablets. At that time the Lord commanded me to teach you the rites and judgments that you would have to perform in the land that you are going to possess. Therefore, guard your souls carefully.

### [B. XI, C. XIII]

“You did not see any likeness on the day when the Lord spoke to you at Horeb from the midst of the fire, lest, being deceived, you should make for yourselves a carved likeness or an image of male or female [h. a carved likeness of an idol, an image of male or female], a likeness [Col. 0418D] of any beast that is upon the earth, or of any bird flying beneath heaven, or of any reptile moving upon the earth, or of any fish that dwells beneath the earth in the waters.

### [B. XII.]

“Beware lest, lifting your eyes to heaven, you see the sun and moon and all the stars of heaven, and, deceived by error, worship and serve them, which the Lord your God created for the service of all the nations that are beneath heaven [h. which the Lord your God allotted to all the nations that are beneath heaven].

But the Lord took you and brought you out of the iron furnace of Egypt, so that you might be his hereditary people [Col. 0419A], as you are at the present day.

### [B. XIII, C. XIV.]

“And the Lord was angry with me because of your words, and swore that I would not cross the Jordan or enter the good land that he is going to give you [h. to give you as an inheritance]. Behold, I am dying in this soil; I shall not cross the Jordan. You will cross over and possess the excellent land.

“Take care lest you ever forget the covenant of the Lord your God that he made with you, and make for yourself a carved likeness of those things that the Lord forbade to be made; for the Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

### [B. XIV.]

“If you beget sons and grandsons [h. When you beget sons and grandsons], and remain for a long time in the land, and, being deceived, make for yourselves some likeness, committing evil before the Lord your God so as to provoke him to anger [Col. 0419B], I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that you will quickly perish from the land that you are going to possess after crossing the Jordan. You shall not remain in it for a long time, but the Lord will destroy you and scatter you among all the nations, and you shall remain few in number [Vulgate omits: in number] among the peoples to which the Lord will lead you.

“There you shall serve gods made by human hands, of wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell.

### [B. XV.]

“And when you seek the Lord your God there, you shall find him—if, at least, you seek him with all your heart and with all the affliction [h. if, at least, you seek him with all your heart and soul … affliction, h. …] of your soul. After all the things foretold have befallen you, in the latter time you shall return to the Lord your God and hear his voice. [Col. 0419C] For the Lord your God is a merciful God: he will not abandon you or utterly destroy you, nor will he forget the covenant that he swore [h. that he swore] to your fathers.

### [B. XVI, C. XV.]

“Ask about the ancient days that were before you, from the day when God created humankind upon the earth, from one end of heaven to the other, whether anything like this has ever happened or whether it has ever been known that a people heard the voice of God speaking from the midst of the fire, as you heard it and lived [h. and he lived]; whether God ever acted so as to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of another nation, by trials, signs, and wonders, by war, by a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and terrifying visions, according to all that the Lord your God did for you in Egypt, before your eyes; so that you might know [Col. 0419D] that the Lord himself is God, [Note: [Col. 0419D] Some manuscript copies have *except one*; in others it is read according to the marginal scholion of the Canon. MART.] and there is no other besides one [h. besides him].

“From heaven he made you hear his voice, to instruct you; and on earth he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words from the midst of the fire, because he loved your fathers and chose their offspring after them. And he brought you out of Egypt, going before you by his great power, to destroy nations greater and stronger than you at your approach, and to bring you in and give you their land as a possession, as you see at the present day.

“Know therefore today, [Col. 0420A] and consider in your heart, that the Lord himself is God in heaven above and on earth below, and there is no other. Keep his ordinances and commandments that I command you, so that it may be well with you [h. that I command you today] and with your sons after you, and so that you may remain for a long time upon the land that the Lord your God is going to give you.”

### [B. XVII, C. XVI.]

Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan [h. at the crossing of the Jordan], toward the east, so that anyone who killed his neighbor unintentionally, without having been his enemy one or two days earlier [h. without having been his enemy yesterday or the day before], might flee to them and escape to one of those cities: Bosor in the wilderness, situated in the plainland belonging to the tribe of Reuben; and Ramoth [Col. 0420B] in Gilead, belonging to the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to the tribe of Manasseh.

### [C. XVII.]

This is the law that Moses set before the children of Israel, and these are the testimonies, rites, and judgments that he spoke to the children of Israel when they came out of Egypt, beyond the Jordan [h. at the crossing of the Jordan], in the valley opposite the shrine of Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses struck, [Note: [Col. 0419D] The sense and punctuation in the printed editions and [Col. 0420D] manuscript codices are different. Only the Canon of Hebrew truth faithfully renders the sense of its source at this place, as at six hundred others. MART. —Our manuscripts also read, “The children of Israel, moreover, came out,” in agreement with the Vulgate.]

and the children of Israel came out of Egypt. They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond [h. at the crossing of] the Jordan toward the rising of the sun: from Aroer, which is situated on the bank of the torrent Arnon, to Mount Sion, which is also Hermon; the whole plain beyond the Jordan toward the eastern region, as far as the Sea of the Wilderness, and [Col. 0420C] as far as the foothills of Mount Phasga.

Moses called all Israel and said to them [h. to them, plural]: “Hear, Israel, the rites and judgments that I speak in your ears today. Learn them and fulfill them in practice. The Lord our God made a covenant with us at Horeb. He did not make this covenant with our fathers [h. this covenant], but with us, who are alive and present today. Face to face he spoke with us on the mountain from the midst of the fire. I stood as mediator between the Lord and you at that time, to announce his words to you; for you feared the fire and did not go up the mountain. And he said:

### [B. XVIII.]

“I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.

**[1st commandment.]** You shall have no foreign gods before me.

**[2nd commandment.]** [Col. 0420D] You shall not make for yourself a graven image, nor [h. does not have *nor*] any likeness of all that is in heaven above, or on earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth. You shall not worship them or serve them. For I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, repaying the iniquity of the fathers upon the sons to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, and showing mercy for many [h. does not have *many*] thousands to those who love me and keep my commandments.

**[3rd commandment.]** You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain [h. You shall not take the name of the Lord your God for vanity], for whoever takes his name for an empty thing shall not go unpunished.

**[4th commandment.]** Observe the Sabbath day, to sanctify it, as the Lord your God commanded you. Six days you shall labor and do all your work. The seventh day is the Sabbath, that is, the rest of the Lord your God [b. The seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord your God]. You shall do no work on it—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your ox, your donkey, all your cattle, or the sojourner who is within your gates—so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as you do.

“Remember that you also served in Egypt, and that the Lord your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore he commanded you [h. Therefore the Lord your God commanded you] to observe [Col. 0421B] the Sabbath day.

**[5th commandment.]** Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God commanded you, so that you may live long and that it may be well with you in the land that the Lord your God is going to give you.

**[6th commandment.]** You shall not kill.

**[7th commandment.]** Nor shall you commit adultery.

**[8th commandment.]** You shall not steal.

**[9th commandment.]** You shall not speak false testimony against your neighbor.

**[10th commandment.]** You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his house, nor his field, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that belongs to him.

### [C. XVIII.]

“These words the Lord spoke to all your assembly on the mountain from the midst of the fire, cloud, and gloom, with a loud voice, adding nothing further; and he wrote them on two stone tablets, which he gave to me.

“But after you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness and saw the mountain burning, all the leaders of your tribes, the elders, approached me and said: ‘Behold, the Lord our God has shown us his majesty and greatness. We heard his voice from the midst of the fire, and today we have proved that, when God speaks with a human being, that person lives. Why then should we die, and why should this great fire consume us? For if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any longer, we shall die. What is all flesh, that it should hear the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire as we have heard it, and be able to live?’

“‘You rather approach and hear everything that the Lord our God will say to you. Then you shall speak to us, and we, hearing, will do it.’

### [C. XIX.]

“When the Lord heard this, he said to me: ‘I have heard the words of this people that they spoke to you; everything they have said is good. Who will grant them such a mind that they may fear me and keep all my commandments at all times [h. on all days], so that it may be well with them and with their sons forever?

“‘Go and say to them: “Return to your tents.” But you, stand here [Col. 0422A] with me, and I shall speak to you all the commandments, rites, and judgments that you shall teach them to perform in the land that I shall give them as a possession.’

“Therefore, keep and do what the Lord your God has commanded you. You shall not turn aside either to the right or to the left, but you shall walk by the way that the Lord your God has commanded you, so that you may live, that it may be well with you, and that your days may be prolonged in the land of your possession.

### [B. XX, Chapter VI.]

“These are the commandments, rites, and judgments that the Lord your God commanded me to teach you, so that you may do them in the land into which you are crossing to possess it, so that you may fear the Lord your God and keep all his commandments and ordinances that I command you, you and your sons and grandsons, all the days of your life, so that your days may be prolonged [Col. 0422B].

“Hear, Israel, [Note: [Col. 0421D] The printed editions and some more recent manuscripts add these words: ‘which the Lord commanded you’; they also express the sense of the same verse differently. But the reading in the Canon and in other manuscripts of excellent quality is plainer and clearer. The Arabic translator favors our reading, for he has ‘in the land flowing with milk and honey.’ MART. —Again, our manuscripts have more in agreement with the Vulgate reading: ‘observe what the Lord commanded you, and it shall be well,’ etc.]

and be careful to do this, so that it may be well with you and you may multiply greatly (as the Lord, the God of your fathers, promised you [Note: [Col. 0421D] The Urbinas manuscript reads: ‘the God of your fathers, to give you a land flowing with milk and honey.’ Then the Palatine manuscript has ‘the Lord [Col. 0422D] is one,’ instead of ‘God,’ etc., according to the commentator’s annotation.]) in the land flowing with milk and honey.

### [T. V, C. XIX.]

“Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, [Note: [Col. 0422D] All manuscript codices of the Bible read in this way, except Corbeiensis no. 1, which reads ‘the Lord is one,’ according to the marginal annotation of the Canon, from which much has evidently flowed into that same codex. MART.] one God [h. Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one] is. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength.

“These words that I command you today shall be in your heart. You shall repeat them to your sons and meditate on them [Note: [Col. 0422D] The Vulgate books add: ‘on them.’] while sitting in your house, walking on the road, lying down, and rising. You shall bind them as a sign upon your hand; they shall be, and shall move, between your eyes [h. as a sign upon your hand, and they shall be phylacteries between your eyes]. You shall write them on the threshold and doors of your house [h. upon the doorposts of your house and upon your gates].

“When the Lord your God brings you into the land concerning which he swore to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give it to you, and gives you great and excellent cities that you did not build, houses full of every kind of wealth that you did not construct [h. that you did not fill], cisterns that you did not dig, vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant, and when you have eaten and are satisfied, take great care lest you forget the Lord, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.

### [C. XX.]

“You shall fear the Lord your God and [Note: [Col. 0422D] Thus the Canon and the more ancient manuscript codices. Others have ‘you shall serve him alone,’ in accordance with what is written at Matthew 4:10. MART.] serve him, and swear by his name.

### [C. XXI.]

“You shall not follow foreign gods, the gods of all the nations around you, because the Lord your God, who is in your midst, is a jealous God; lest at some time the anger of the Lord your God be kindled against you and remove you from the face of the earth.

### [B. XXI, C. XXII.]

“You shall not test the Lord your God, as you tested him at the place of testing [h. You shall not test the Lord your God, as you tested him in the tests]. Keep the commandments of the Lord your God, his testimonies and rites [Col. 0423A] that he commanded you, and do what is pleasing and good in the sight of the Lord, so that it may be well with you; and, when you enter, you may possess the excellent land concerning which the Lord swore to your fathers that he would destroy all your enemies before you, as he said.

### [B. XXII.]

“When your son asks you tomorrow, saying, ‘What do these testimonies, rites, and judgments mean that the Lord our God commanded you?’ you shall say to him: ‘We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand. He performed [h. He gave] great and terrible signs and wonders in Egypt against Pharaoh and all his household, before our eyes [h. before our eyes], and he brought us out from there in order to bring us in and give us the land concerning which he swore to our fathers.’

“The Lord commanded us [Col. 0423B] to perform all these statutes and to fear the Lord our God, so that it might be well with us all the days of our life, as it is today. And he will be merciful to us if we keep and perform all his commandments [h. these] before the Lord our God, as he commanded us.

### [B. XXIII, C. XXIII, Chapter VII.]

“When the Lord your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess, and destroys many nations before you—the Hittite, Girgashite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite—seven nations much more numerous than you and stronger than you; and when the Lord your God delivers them to you, you shall strike them down to complete destruction. You shall not make a covenant with them, nor shall you show them mercy, nor shall you form marriages [Col. 0423C] with them.

### [B. XXIV.]

“You shall not give your daughter to his son, nor take his daughter for your son, because he will seduce your son so that he does not follow me and instead serves foreign gods. Then the anger of the Lord will be kindled, and he will quickly destroy you.

### [B. XXV.]

“Rather, this is what you shall do to them: overthrow their altars, break their pillars, cut down their sacred groves, and burn their carved images. For you are a holy people to the Lord your God. The Lord your God chose you to be his special people from all the peoples who are upon the earth.

### [B. XXVI.]

“It was not because you outnumbered all the nations that the Lord joined himself to you and chose you, since you are fewer than all the peoples. Rather, it was because the Lord loved you and kept the oath that he swore to your fathers. He brought you out with a strong hand and redeemed [Col. 0423D] you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

“And you shall know that the Lord your God is himself the mighty and faithful God, keeping covenant and mercy with those who love him and with those who keep his commandments, for a thousand generations, and repaying those who hate him immediately, so that he destroys them and does not delay any longer, promptly rendering to them what they deserve.

### [B. XXVII, C. XXIV.]

“Therefore keep the commandments, rites, and judgments that I command you today to perform. If, after hearing these judgments, you keep and perform them, the Lord your God will keep for you the covenant and the mercy that he swore to your fathers. He will love you, multiply you, and bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land, your grain, your vintage, and your oil, and the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep, upon the land concerning which he swore to your fathers that he would give it to you. You shall be blessed among all peoples. Among you there shall be no one barren of either sex, whether among human beings or among your herds.

“The Lord will remove every sickness from you; and the terrible diseases of Egypt that you have known he will not inflict upon you, but upon all your enemies.

### [C. XXV.]

“You shall consume all the peoples that the Lord your God is going to give you. Your eye shall not spare them, and you shall not serve their gods, lest they become a ruin for you.

“If you say in your heart, ‘These nations are more numerous than I am; how will I be able to destroy [h. drive out] them?’ do not be afraid, [Col. 0424B] but remember what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and to all the Egyptians: the great plagues [h. trials] that your eyes saw, and the signs and wonders, the strong hand and the outstretched arm, by which the Lord your God brought you out. So will he do to all the peoples whom you fear.

### [B. XXVIII.]

“Moreover, the Lord your God will send hornets against them, until he destroys and scatters all those who flee from you and are able to hide. You shall not fear them, because the Lord your God is in your midst.

### [B. XXIX.]

“The great and terrible God—he himself will consume these nations before you little by little and in stages. You will not be able to destroy them all at once, lest the beasts of the earth [h. of the field] multiply against you. The Lord your God will deliver them before you and kill them until they are completely destroyed. [Col. 0424C] He will deliver their kings into your hands, and you shall obliterate their names from beneath heaven. No one will be able to stand against you [h. before you] until you crush them. You shall burn their carved images with fire [h. the carved images of their gods].

### [B. XXX.]

“You shall not covet the silver and gold from which they are made, nor take anything from them for yourself, lest you offend, because it is an abomination to the Lord your God. You shall not bring anything from the idol into your house, lest you become accursed, like it. You shall detest it as filth and regard it as defilement and dirt, as an abomination, because it is accursed.

### [B. XXXI, C. XXVI, Chapter VIII.]

“Every commandment that I command you today, take great care to perform, so that you may live and multiply, and, entering in, may possess the land concerning which the Lord swore to your fathers.

“And you shall remember the whole journey by which the Lord your God led you for forty years [h. behold, forty years] through the wilderness, to afflict you and test you, and to make known what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not.

### [B. XXXII.]

“He afflicted you with want [h. He afflicted you and made you hunger], and gave you manna for food, which neither you nor your fathers knew, to show you that a human being does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth [Note: [Col. 0423D] Here too the printed editions and some manuscript books read [Col. 0424D] ‘according to what is written’ in the fourth chapter of Matthew. [Col. 0425D] Moreover, in Hebrew and Samaritan it has , *Adonai*, or *YHWH*, which is interpreted as ‘of the Lord,’ not ‘of God.’ MART. —The Urbinas manuscript has ‘from the mouth of God,’ in agreement with the Vulgate.] of the Lord.

### [B. XXXIII.]

“Your garment, with which you were clothed, did not wear out through age, and your foot did not become swollen; behold, it is the fortieth year. So you may recognize in your heart that, just as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God disciplined you, so that you might keep the commandments of the Lord your God, walk in his ways, and fear him.

“For the Lord your God will bring you into a good land, a land of streams [h. torrents] and waters and springs, in whose plains and mountains the depths of rivers burst forth; a land of grain, barley, vineyards, figs, pomegranates, and olive groves; a land of oil and honey. There you shall eat your bread without any want [h. poverty] and enjoy abundance in everything. Its stones are iron, and from its mountains copper ore is mined. When you have eaten and are satisfied, bless the Lord [Col. 0425B] your God for the excellent land that he has given you.

### [B. XXXIV, C. XXVII.]

“Observe and beware lest you ever forget the Lord your God and neglect his commandments, judgments, and rites that I command you today, lest, after you have eaten and are satisfied, built beautiful houses and lived in them, and acquired herds of cattle, flocks of sheep, silver and gold, and abundance of everything, your heart be lifted up and you forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery, and was your guide through the great and terrible wilderness, in which there was a serpent burning with its breath, a scorpion, and a dipsas, with absolutely no water; who brought streams [h. water] out of the hardest rock and fed you manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know. And after he had afflicted and tested you, at last he had mercy on you.

### [C. XXVIII.]

“Do not say in your heart, ‘My strength and the power of my hand have produced all this for me,’ but remember the Lord your God, that he himself gave you strength so as to fulfill his covenant, concerning which he swore to your fathers, as the present day shows.

“But if you forget the Lord your God and follow foreign gods, serving and worshiping them, behold, I now declare to you that you will utterly perish. Just as the nations that the Lord destroyed at your approach perished, so you too shall perish if you are disobedient to the voice of the Lord your God.

## [T. VI, C. XXIX, Chapter IX.]

“Hear, Israel: today you are crossing the Jordan in order to possess nations greater and stronger than you, cities immense and fortified up to heaven, a great and lofty people, the sons of the Anakim, whom you yourself have seen and heard, against whom no one can stand [h. whom you know and have heard. Who can stand before the sons of Anak?]

### [B. XXXV.]

“Know therefore today that the Lord your God himself will cross before you, a devouring and consuming fire [h. does not have ‘and consuming’], to crush them and destroy and annihilate them [Col. 0426A] before your face swiftly, as he has told you.

### [B. XXXVI, C. XXX.]

“Do not say in your heart, when the Lord your God has destroyed them before your sight [h. when the Lord your God has driven them out before your presence]: ‘Because of my righteousness the Lord brought me in to possess this land,’ when it was because of their wickedness that these nations were destroyed.

“For it is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are entering to possess their lands; rather, because they acted wickedly, they were destroyed as you entered, and so that the Lord might fulfill his word that he promised under oath to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

“Know therefore that the Lord your God has not given you this excellent land as a possession because of your righteousness, since you are a people of exceedingly stubborn neck.

### [C. XXXI.]

“Remember, and do not forget, how you provoked the Lord your God to anger in the wilderness. From the day when you came out of Egypt until this place, you have continually contended against the Lord.

### [C. XXXII.]

“For at Horeb also you provoked him, and he was angry and wished to destroy you, when I went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the Lord made with you; and I remained [h. sat] on the mountain for forty days and nights, eating no bread and drinking no water. The Lord gave me two stone tablets written with the finger of God, containing all the words that he spoke to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire, when the assembly of the people had gathered.

### [B. XXXVII.]

“When forty days and an equal number of nights had passed, the Lord gave me two [Col. 0426C] stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

### [C. XXXIII.]

“And he said to me: ‘Rise and go down quickly from here, because your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have quickly abandoned the way that I [Note: [Col. 0425D] The present Hebrew has a first-person verb, if we trust the vowel-points of the Masoretes, , *Isiuvithim*, that is, ‘I commanded them.’ But the translators of the Septuagint, the Chaldean, the Syriac, and our Jerome read , *siuvitham*, meaning ‘you commanded them.’ MART. —The Hebrew word, furnished with different vowel-points, can mean both ‘I commanded them’ and ‘you commanded them,’ as Martianus also observes. Jerome, following the Septuagint, preferred this latter reading, or retained the reading that was current at that time.] showed [h. that you commanded] them, and they made for themselves a molten image.’

“Again the Lord said to me: ‘I see that this people is stiff-necked. Leave me, so that I may crush them and blot out their name from beneath heaven, and make you into a nation [h. and make you into a nation] greater and stronger than this one.’

### [C. XXXIV.]

“When I had come down from the burning mountain, holding the two tablets of the covenant in both hands, and had seen that you had sinned against the Lord your God and had made for yourselves a molten calf, and had quickly abandoned his way that he had shown you [h. commanded you], I threw the tablets from my hands [Col. 0426D] and broke them before your eyes [h. before your face].

### [B. XXXVIII, C. XXXV.]

“And I fell prostrate before the Lord as before, for forty days and nights, eating no bread and drinking no water, because of all your sins that you had committed against the Lord and had provoked him to anger. For I feared his indignation and anger, with which he was enraged against you and wanted to destroy you. And [Col. 0427A] the Lord heard me this time also.

### [C. XXXVI.]

“He was also exceedingly angry with Aaron and wanted to crush him, and I prayed for him in the same way [h. I prayed at that time].

### [C. XXXVII.]

“But I took your sin, namely the calf that you had made, burned it in the fire, crushed it into pieces, and reduced it completely to powder; then I threw it into the torrent that descended from the mountain.

### [C. XXXVIII.]

“At Taberah, at Massah, and at the Graves of Lust you provoked the Lord.

### [C. XXXIX.]

“And when he sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, ‘Go up and possess the land that I have given you,’ and you despised the command of the Lord your God, and did not believe him, nor were willing to hear his voice, but were always rebellious from the day when I began to know you [Col. 0427B].

### [C. XL.]

“And I lay prostrate before the Lord for forty days and nights, during which I implored him not to destroy you, as he had threatened. And while praying I said: ‘Lord God [h. And while praying to the Lord I said: Lord, Lord], do not destroy your people and your inheritance, whom you redeemed in your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a strong hand. Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not regard the stubbornness, wickedness, and sin of this people, lest the inhabitants of the land from which you brought us should say: “The Lord was unable to bring them into the land that he promised them, and he hated them; therefore he brought them out in order to kill them in the wilderness.”

“They are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great strength [Col. 0427C] and your outstretched arm.’”

[B. XXXIX, C. XLI, Cap. X.] At that time the Lord said to me: “Hew for yourself two stone tablets like the former ones, and come up to me on the mountain; and make a wooden ark, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on those which you broke before, and you shall place them in the ark.” Accordingly I made an ark of acacia wood.

[C. XLII.] When I had hewn two stone tablets resembling the former ones, I went up the mountain, carrying them in my hands. And he wrote on the tablets, according to what he had written before, the ten words that the Lord spoke to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire, when the people were assembled; and he gave them to me [Hebrew: “on the day of the assembly, and the Lord gave them to me”].

[C. XLIII.] Returning from the mountain, I came down and placed the tablets in the ark that I had made; and they are there to this day, as the Lord commanded me. The Israelites then set out from Beeroth of the sons of Jaakan toward Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried; and his son Eleazar succeeded him in the priesthood. From there they came to Gudgodah [Hebrew: “Gud-god”]; and departing from that place, they camped at Jotbathah, in a land of waters [Hebrew: “in a land of streams of water”] and torrents.

[C. XLIV.] At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, to stand before him in service, and to bless in his name, even to the present day. For this reason Levi had no share or inheritance with his brothers [Vulgate: “fruits”], because the Lord himself is his possession, as the Lord your God promised him [Hebrew: “as the Lord your God spoke to him”].

But I remained on the mountain, as before, forty days and nights. And the Lord heard me on this occasion also, and did not wish to destroy you. He said to me: “Go and lead the people, so that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their fathers I would give them.”

[T. VII, B. XL, C. XLV.] And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you, except that you fear the Lord your God, walk in his ways, love him, and serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul; that you keep the commandments of the Lord and his statutes, which I command you today, so that it may go well with you?

[B. XLI.] Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth and everything that is in it, belong to the Lord your God; yet the Lord was attached to your fathers and loved them, and chose their descendants after them—that is, you—out of all the nations, as is evident today.

[B. XLII.] Circumcise, therefore, the foreskin of your heart, and do not harden your neck any longer; for the Lord your God himself is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribes. He executes justice for the orphan and the widow; he loves the foreigner and gives him food and clothing. You, too, must love the foreigners, because you yourselves were foreigners [Hebrew: “sojourners”] in the land of Egypt.

[B. XLIII, C. XLVI.] You shall fear the Lord your God and serve him [Vulgate adds: “alone”]; you shall cling to him and swear by his name. He is your praise and your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things that your eyes have seen.

[C. XLVII.] Your fathers went down to Egypt as seventy persons; and now, behold, the Lord your God has multiplied you like the stars of heaven.

[C. XLVIII, Cap. XI.] Therefore love the Lord your God, and observe his precepts, statutes, judgments, and commandments at all times.

[B. XLIV.] Recognize today what your children do not know, because they did not see the discipline of the Lord your God, his greatness, his strong hand [Hebrew omits this], and his outstretched arm, the signs and deeds that he performed in the midst of Egypt against Pharaoh the king and all his land, and against the entire army of the Egyptians, their horses and chariots: how the waters of the Red Sea covered them when they pursued you, and the Lord destroyed them to the present day; and what he did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place; and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, who was the son of Reuben [Hebrew: “the sons of Eliab, son of Reuben”], whom the earth swallowed openly with its mouth [Hebrew: “swallowed up”], together with their houses and tents and all their possessions, which they had in the midst of Israel. [Hebrew: “Know today—for I do not speak these things to your children, who have not known and seen—the discipline of the Lord your God, his greatness, and his outstretched arm”; it omits “and his strong hand.”]

Your eyes [Hebrew: “But your eyes”] have seen all the great works of the Lord that he performed, so that you may keep [Hebrew: “therefore keep”] all his commandments, which I command you today, in order that you may enter and possess the land into which you are entering and live in it for a long time—a land that the Lord swore he would give to your fathers and their descendants, flowing with milk and honey.

[B. XLV.] For the land into which you are entering to possess it is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came, where, after sowing the seed, water is brought in by irrigation like that used in gardens. Rather, it is mountainous and level country, awaiting rain from heaven. The Lord your God continually watches over it, and his eyes are upon it from the beginning of the year to its end.

[B. XLVI, C. XLIX.] Therefore, if you obey my commandments, which I command you today, loving the Lord your God and serving him with all your heart and with all your soul, he will give rain to your land, the early and the late rain, so that you may gather your grain, wine, and oil, and hay from the fields for feeding your cattle, and so that you yourselves may eat and be satisfied.

Beware lest your heart be deceived and you depart from the Lord, serving foreign gods and worshiping them; then the Lord, becoming angry, may shut up the heavens, so that rain does not fall [Hebrew: “so that there is no rain”] and the earth does not yield its produce, and you perish quickly from the good land that the Lord is going to give you.

[B. XLVII.] Place these words of mine in your hearts and minds, and hang them as a sign on your hands and place them between your eyes [Hebrew: “bind them as a sign upon your hand, and they shall be as phylacteries between your eyes.” *Phylacteria* is Greek; in Hebrew, *totaphoth*].

[B. XLVIII.] Teach your children to meditate on them when you sit in your house, when you walk on the road, when you lie down, and when you rise. Write them on the doorposts and gates of your house [Hebrew: “on the doorposts of your house and on your gates”], so that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied in the land that the Lord swore to your fathers he would give them, for as long as the heavens extend over the earth.

[B. XLIX, C. L.] For if you carefully keep the commandments that I command you and do them—loving the Lord your God, walking in all his ways, and clinging to him—the Lord will destroy all these nations before your face, and you will possess nations greater and stronger than you. Every place on which the sole of your foot treads shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the great river Euphrates [Hebrew: “from the river, the river Euphrates”] as far as the western sea shall be your boundaries. No one will stand against you; the Lord your God will spread your terror and dread over the whole land that you are about to tread, as he has told you.

[C. LI.] Behold [Hebrew: “See, I set”], I place before you today a blessing and a curse: a blessing, if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today; a curse, if you do not listen to the commandments [Vulgate: “obey the commandments”] of the Lord your God, but depart from the way that I now show you and follow foreign gods whom you do not know.

[B. L.] When the Lord your God brings you into the land to which you are going to live, setting the blessing upon Mount Gerizim and the curse upon Mount Ebal—these mountains are beyond the Jordan, beyond the road that runs toward the setting of the sun, in the land of the Canaanite who dwells in the plain opposite Gilgal, near [Hebrew: “which is near the conspicuous oak”] [Note: The Septuagint has *plēsion tēs dryos tēs hypsēlēs*, “near the lofty oak.” In Hebrew we read *etsel elene More*. The Samaritans read the same, but add these two words, *mul Sichem*, that is, “toward Shechem.” *More*, or *Mora*, has various interpretations: some understand *elon More* to mean the plain or meadows of More; the Syriac has “the oak of Mamre,” and so forth. MART. —The Hebrew has literally only “near the oaks of More.” This is the same place that is called “the notable valley” in Genesis 12:6.]—you will cross the Jordan to possess the land that the Lord your God is going to give you, and you will have and possess it. See, therefore, that you fulfill the statutes and judgments that I set before you today.

[Col. 0430B] [T. VIII, B. LI, C. LII, Cap. XII.] These are the precepts and judgments that you must carry out in the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, is going to give you to possess, all the days that you walk upon the earth. Destroy all the places where the nations whom you are going to possess served their gods, upon high mountains and hills and beneath every leafy tree. Demolish their altars, break their pillars, burn their sacred groves with fire, and shatter their idols; blot out their names from those places.

[B. LII, C. LIII.] You shall not act in this way toward the Lord your God.

[C. LIV.] Rather, you shall come to the place that the Lord your God chooses from all your tribes, to establish his name there and to dwell there, and in that place you shall offer your burnt offerings and sacrifices.

[C. LV.] You shall bring the tithes and firstfruits of your hands, your vows and offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and sheep. You shall eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice in everything to which you put your hand—you and your households—in which the Lord your God has blessed you.

You shall not do there what we are doing here today, each person doing whatever seems right to him. For you have not yet come to the rest and inheritance that the Lord your God is going to give you. You will cross the Jordan and dwell in the land that the Lord your God is going to give you, so that you may rest from all your enemies round about and dwell without any fear.

[Note: You will find a somewhat different sense of this passage in the published editions. Whoever wishes may compare them. MART. —Our manuscripts, too, in agreement with the printed books, prefer: “you shall dwell in the place that the Lord chooses,” and so forth.]

And to the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be there, you shall bring everything that I command you: burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, the firstfruits of your hands, and whatever is most choice among the gifts that you vow to the Lord. There you shall feast before the Lord your God—you and your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite who dwells in your cities [Hebrew: “who is within your gates”].

[B. LIII.] For he has no other share or inheritance among you. Take care that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see; rather, in the place that the Lord chooses, in one of your tribes, you shall offer sacrifices and do everything that I command you.

[C. LVI.] But if you wish to eat, and eating meat pleases you, kill and eat according to the blessing of the Lord your God, which he has given you in your cities, whether the animal is unclean—that is, blemished and defective—or clean—that is, whole and without blemish—which may be offered. You may eat it as you would a gazelle or deer [Hebrew: “the blessing of the Lord that he has given you in all your gates. Both the clean and the unclean may eat of it, as of the gazelle and deer,” and so forth], except only that you must not eat the blood, which you shall pour out upon the ground like water.

You may not eat in your towns the tithe of your grain, wine, and oil, the firstborn of your herds and flocks, or anything that you have vowed or freely wished to offer, or the firstfruits of your hands [Hebrew: “sacrifice is understood in this passage”]. Rather, you shall eat these things before the Lord your God, in the place that the Lord your God chooses—you, your son and daughter, your male and female servant, and the Levite who dwells in your cities. You shall rejoice and be refreshed before the Lord your God in everything to which you stretch out your hand.

[B. LIV.] Take care not to abandon the Levite throughout the time that you live in the land. When the Lord your God enlarges your boundaries, as he has told you, and you wish to eat meat, because your soul desires it, but the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell there is far away, you may kill from the herds and flocks that you possess, as I have commanded you, and eat in your towns as you please.

As the gazelle and deer are eaten, so you shall eat these animals; both the clean and the unclean shall eat them together. Take care only not to eat blood. For their blood is their life, and therefore you must not eat the life with the meat; rather, pour it out upon the ground like water, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, when you do what is pleasing in the sight of the Lord.

But whatever you have consecrated and vowed to the Lord, you shall take and bring to the place that the Lord chooses, and you shall offer your sacrifices, flesh and blood, upon the altar of the Lord your God. You shall pour the blood of your sacrifices upon the altar [Vulgate omits “of your sacrifices”], but you shall eat the meat yourself.

[C. LVII.] Observe and hear all the words [Vulgate omits “the words and I”] that I command you, so that it may go well with you and your children after you forever, when you do what is good and pleasing in the sight of the Lord your God.
