When the Lord your God has destroyed before your face the nations into whose land you are entering [Vulgate: “into whose land you will enter”] to possess it, and you have possessed them and dwelt in their land, take care not to imitate them after they have been overthrown as you enter, and do not seek out their statutes, saying [Hebrew: “their gods, saying”]: “As these nations served their gods, so I too will serve them.” You shall not act in this way toward the Lord your God. For they have done to their gods all the abominations that the Lord detests, offering their sons and daughters and burning them in fire.

[C. LVIII.] Do only what I command you for the Lord; you shall neither add anything nor take anything away.

[T. IX, B. LV, Cap. XIII.] If a prophet arises among you, or someone who claims to have seen a dream, and announces a sign or portent, and what he has spoken comes to pass, and he says to you, “Let us go and follow foreign gods whom you do not know, and let us serve them,” you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer; for the Lord your God is testing you, to make it clear whether you love him or not, with all your heart and with all your soul.

[C. LIX.] You shall follow the Lord your God and fear him; you shall keep his commandments and listen to his voice. You shall serve him and cling to him. But that prophet or maker of dreams [Hebrew: “dreamer”] shall be put to death, because he spoke in order to turn you away from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, and to make you stray from the way that the Lord your God commanded you. Thus you shall remove the evil from your midst.

[C. LX.] If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or daughter, or your wife who lies in your bosom, or your friend whom you love as your own soul, secretly tries to persuade you, saying, “Let us go and serve foreign gods whom neither you nor your fathers know, gods of all the surrounding nations, whether near or far, from one end of the earth to the other,” do not consent to him or listen to him. Do not let your eye spare him in pity or conceal him; rather, you shall kill him immediately. Your hand shall be the first against him, and afterward the hand of all the people shall be raised.

[Note: The Palatine manuscript and others among Martianay’s manuscripts have *post te*, “after you.”]

He shall be stoned to death, because he sought to draw you away from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery, so that all Israel, hearing of it, may fear and never again do anything like this [Hebrew: “anything like this in your midst”].

[C. LXI.] If you hear in one of your cities, which the Lord your God will give you to dwell in, that certain people are saying [Hebrew omits “certain people are saying,” having only “saying”]: “The sons of Belial have gone out from among you and have led the inhabitants of their city astray [Hebrew: “its inhabitants”], and they have said, ‘Let us go and serve foreign gods whom you do not know,’” you shall inquire, investigate, and examine the matter diligently. If, after establishing the truth, you find that what is said is certain and that this abomination has actually been committed [Hebrew: “committed in your midst”], you shall immediately strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, and you shall destroy it and everything in it, even the cattle.

Whatever furnishings or property it contains, you shall gather in the middle of its streets and burn them, together with the city, so that you may consume everything for the Lord your God, and it may become an everlasting mound. It shall never again be built, and nothing from that accursed thing shall cling to your hand, so that the Lord may turn away from the anger of his wrath, have mercy on you, and multiply you as he swore to your fathers—when you listen to the voice of the Lord your God and keep all his commandments that I command you today, doing what is pleasing in the sight of the Lord your God.

[B. LVI, C. LXII, Cap. XIV.] You are children of the Lord [Hebrew: “You are children of the Lord your God”] your God. You shall not cut yourselves or make baldness upon yourselves for the dead. For you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and he chose you to be his treasured people out of all the nations upon the earth.

[B. LVII, C. LXIII.] You shall not eat anything unclean [Hebrew: “You shall not eat anything abominable”]. These are the animals that you may eat: cattle, sheep, goats, deer, gazelle, buffalo, wild goat, pygarg, wild ox, and giraffe. Every animal that divides the hoof into two parts and chews the cud you may eat.

But among those that chew the cud and do not divide the hoof, you shall not eat these [Vulgate omits “these”]: the camel, hare, and rock badger; because they chew the cud but do not divide the hoof, they shall be unclean for you. The pig also, because it divides the hoof but does not chew the cud, shall be unclean. You shall not eat their meat, nor touch their carcasses.

[C. LXIV.] These you may eat from all that live in the waters: whatever has fins and scales, you may eat; whatever lacks fins and scales, you shall not eat, because they are unclean.

[C. LXV.] Eat every clean bird. You shall not eat the unclean: namely, the eagle, griffin, osprey, *ixion*, vulture, and kite according to its kind; every kind of raven; the ostrich, owl, gull, and hawk according to its kind; the heron, swan, ibis, cormorant, purple bird, night heron, pelican, and plover, each according to its kind; and also the hoopoe and bat.

Everything that creeps and has wings shall be unclean and shall not be eaten. Whatever is clean, you may eat. But you shall not eat anything that has died of itself. Give it to the foreigner who is within your gates, so that he may eat it, or sell it to a foreigner [Hebrew: “or sell it to an outsider”], because you are a holy people to the Lord your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.

[B. LVIII, C. LXVI.] You shall set apart a tenth of all the produce that grows in your fields each year, and you shall eat it before the Lord your God, in the place that he chooses so that his name may be invoked there: the tenth of your grain, wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and sheep, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God at all times.

[C. LXVII.] But when the journey is too long and the place that the Lord your God chooses is far away, and he has blessed you so that you cannot carry all these things there, you shall sell everything, convert it into money, carry the money in your hand, and go to the place that the Lord your God chooses. With that money you shall buy whatever pleases you—whether cattle or sheep, wine or strong drink, or anything that your soul desires—and you shall eat before the Lord your God and feast, you and your household, together with the Levite who is within your gates. Take care not to abandon him, because [Vulgate: “who”] he has no other share in your possession.

[B. LIX.] In the third year you shall set apart another tithe from everything that is produced for you [Hebrew: “At the end of the third year you shall set apart the whole tithe of your produce, from everything produced for you that year”], and you shall store it within your gates. Then the Levite, who has no other share or inheritance with you, and the foreigner, orphan, and widow who are within your gates shall come, eat, and be satisfied, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works of your hands that you do.

[B. LX, C. LXVIII, Cap. XV.] In the seventh year you shall make a remission, which shall be observed in this manner: Whoever is owed anything by a friend, neighbor, or brother shall not be able to demand it, because it is the Lord’s year of remission. From a foreigner and sojourner you may demand it [Hebrew: “From an outsider you may demand it”]; but you shall have no authority to demand it from a citizen or relative [Hebrew: “citizen or brother”]. And there shall be no needy or beggar among you, so that the Lord may bless you in the land that he is going to give you as a possession.

[B. LXI, C. LXIX.] If, however, you listen to the voice of the Lord your God and carefully observe everything that he commanded, and everything that I command you today, he will bless you as he promised. You will lend to many nations, but you yourself will borrow from none. You will rule over many nations, but none will rule over you.

[B. LXII, C. LXX.] If one of your brothers who dwell within the gates of your city becomes poor in the land that the Lord your God is going to give you, you shall not harden your heart or close your hand. Rather, open it to the poor person and lend him whatever you see that he needs.

Beware lest an ungodly thought secretly arise in you and you say in your heart: “The seventh year, the year of remission, is approaching,” and you turn your eyes away from your poor brother, unwilling to lend him what he requests, lest he cry out against you to the Lord and it become a sin for you. Instead, you shall give to him and act without guile in relieving his needs, so that the Lord your God may bless you at all times and in everything to which you put your hand.

There will never be a lack of poor people in the land where you dwell. Therefore I command you to open your hand to your needy and poor brother who lives with you in the land.

[B. LXIII, C. LXXI.] When your Hebrew brother, male or female, has been sold to you and has served you for six years, in the seventh year you shall set him free. And when you grant him freedom, you shall not let him go away empty-handed; rather, you shall provide him with provisions from your flocks, threshing floor, and winepress, with which the Lord your God has blessed you.

Remember that you yourself were a slave in the land of Egypt and that the Lord your God freed you; therefore I now command you this. But if he says, “I do not wish to leave,” because he loves you and your household and finds that he is well treated by you, you shall take an awl and pierce his ear at the door of your house, and he shall serve you forever. You shall do the same for your female slave.

You shall not turn your eyes away from them when you set them free, because for six years they have served you for the wage of a hired worker. Thus the Lord your God will bless you in all the works that you do.

[B. LXIV, C. LXXII.] Of the firstborn that are born among your cattle and sheep, whatever is male you shall consecrate to the Lord your God. You shall not work with the firstborn of an ox, nor shear the firstborn of your sheep [Hebrew: “of your flocks”]. You shall eat them year by year before the Lord your God, in the place that the Lord chooses—you and your household.

But if it has a blemish, or is lame, blind, disfigured in any part, or defective, it shall not be sacrificed to the Lord your God. Rather, you shall eat it within the gates of your city; both the clean and the unclean may eat it alike, as they may eat a gazelle or deer. Take care only not to eat its blood; you shall pour it out upon the ground like water.

[T. X, B. LXV, C. LXXIII, Cap. XVI.] Observe the month of new grain and the first month of spring [Hebrew omits this], so that you may celebrate the Passover to the Lord your God, because in this month the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt by night. You shall sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God from sheep and cattle, in the place that the Lord your God chooses so that his name may dwell there.

You shall not eat leavened bread with it. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, the bread of affliction, because you came out of Egypt in fear, so that you may remember the day of your departure from Egypt all the days of your life. No leaven shall be seen throughout all your territory for seven days, and none of the meat of what was sacrificed in the evening shall remain [Note: The Hebrew has *labboeer*, that is, “until morning,” which the printed editions follow; but all our Latin manuscripts read, with the Hebrew canon of truth, “on the first day in the morning.” MART.] until the first day in the morning.

[Note: The Urbinas manuscripts read *fermentatum*, “leavened,” instead of *fermentum*, “leaven.” A little later they read, together with the printed editions and the Hebrew itself, “from the first day until morning.”]

You may not sacrifice the Passover in any of your cities that the Lord your God is going to give you. Rather, in the place that the Lord your God chooses so that his name may dwell there, you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening, at sunset, at the time when you came out of Egypt. You shall cook and eat it in the place that the Lord your God chooses, and in the morning you shall rise and go to your tents. For six days you shall eat unleavened bread; and on the seventh day, because it is the solemn assembly of the Lord your God, you shall do no work.

[B. LXVI.] You shall count seven weeks for yourself from the day when you first put the sickle to the standing grain. And you shall celebrate the feast [Hebrew omits “the day”] of Weeks to the Lord your God, with a freewill offering from your hand, which you shall give according to the blessing of the Lord your God. You shall feast before the Lord your God—you, your son and daughter, your male and female servant, the Levite who is within your gates, and the foreigner, orphan, and widow who dwell among you—in the place that the Lord your God chooses so that his name may dwell there. You shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and you shall carefully observe and carry out these commands.

[B. LXVII.] You shall also celebrate the feast of Booths for seven days, when you have gathered your produce from your threshing floor and winepress. You shall feast at your festival—you, your son and daughter, your male and female servant, the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who are within your gates. For seven days you shall keep the festival to the Lord your God, in the place that the Lord chooses. The Lord your God will bless you in all your produce and in every work of your hands, and you shall be joyful.

Three times each year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God, in the place that he chooses: at the feast of Unleavened Bread, at the feast of Weeks, and at the feast of Booths.

[B. LXVIII.] No one shall appear before the Lord empty-handed. Rather, each person shall give according to what he possesses, according to the blessing of the Lord his God that he has given him.

[B. LXIX, C. LXXIV.] You shall appoint judges and magistrates in all your gates that the Lord your God gives you, throughout your tribes, so that they may judge the people with righteous judgment and not turn aside toward either side [Hebrew: “you shall not turn aside”]. You shall not show partiality or accept gifts, because gifts blind the eyes of the wise and distort the words of the righteous. You shall pursue justice, justice alone, so that you may live and possess the land that the Lord your God gives you.

[C. LXXV.] You shall not plant a sacred grove or any tree beside the altar of the Lord your God [Hebrew omits “or”]. You shall not make for yourself or set up a pillar [Hebrew: “You shall not plant a sacred grove, any tree, beside the altar of the Lord your God that you are going to make; and you shall not set up for yourself a pillar”], which the Lord your God hates.

[B. LXX, Cap. XVII.] You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God an ox or sheep in which there is a blemish or any defect, because it is an abomination to the Lord your God.

[B. LXXI, C. LXXVI.] If a man or woman is found among you, within one of the gates that the Lord your God gives you, who does evil in the sight of the Lord your God and transgresses his covenant, going and serving foreign gods and worshiping them—the sun, moon, or any army of heaven [Hebrew: “the sun and moon, or any army of heaven”]—which I have not commanded; and if this is reported to you, and you investigate carefully, and the truth is found to be established, and this abomination has been committed in Israel, you shall lead the man or woman who committed this most wicked deed to the gates of your city, and they shall be stoned to death.

[B. LXXII.] At the word of two or three witnesses, the one who is to be killed shall die. No one shall be put to death on the testimony of a single person speaking against him. The hands of the witnesses shall be the first to kill him, and afterward the hand of the rest of the people shall be raised, so that you may remove the evil from your midst.

[B. LXXII, C. LXXVII.] If you perceive that a judgment among you is difficult and ambiguous, between blood and blood, case and case, leprosy and [Note: The same sense, though not the same words, is found in the manuscripts, where they consistently read “leprosy and non-leprosy.” MART. —Then, in the manuscripts examined by Martianay, our books read “leprosy and non-leprosy,” that is, whether it is leprosy or not. The original texts, however, do not recognize the negative particle.] leprosy, and if words of judgment appear to vary within your gates, rise and go up to the place that the Lord your God chooses. You shall come to the priests of the Levitical order and to the judge who is in office at that time, and you shall ask them; they will declare the truth of the judgment to you.

You shall do whatever they say who preside over the place that the Lord chooses, and whatever they teach you. You shall follow their decision according to his law. You shall not turn aside to the right or to the left.

[B. LXXIV, C. LXXVIII.] But the person who acts arrogantly and refuses to obey the command of the priest who ministers at that time before the Lord your God, or the decision of the judge [Hebrew: “to the judge”], shall die. Thus you shall remove the evil from Israel, and all the people, hearing of it, shall fear, so that no one thereafter may swell with pride.

[B. LXXV, C. LXXIX.] When you enter the land that the Lord your God will give you, possess it, and dwell in it, and say, “I will set a king over me, as all the surrounding nations have,” you shall appoint as king over you the one whom the Lord your God chooses from among [Hebrew: “from the midst of”] your brothers. You may not make a man of another nation king over you who is not your brother.

When he has been appointed, he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor lead the people back to Egypt, increasing his cavalry, especially since the Lord has commanded you never again to return by that same road. He shall not have many wives, lest they seduce his heart, nor shall he accumulate immense quantities of silver and gold.

When he has taken his seat upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write for himself a copy of this law in a book, receiving a copy from the Levitical priests, and he shall keep it with him and read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord his God and observe his words and statutes prescribed by the law.

His heart shall not be lifted up in pride above his brothers, nor shall he turn aside from the law [Hebrew: “from the commandment”] to the right or to the left.

[Note: The word “law” is not in the Hebrew text; it may be believed to have been added by the Latin scholiast for purposes of explanation, as we see done by the interpreter of the Chaldean paraphrase, who added the name “the Lord” to the word “commandment,” or “from the commandment.” MART. —The Hebrew text in fact adds “from the commandment”; but it does not add “of the law,” as the scholiast notes.]

Thus he and his sons may reign for a long time over Israel.

### [B. LXXVI, Chapter XVIII]

The priests and Levites [Hebrew omits “and”], and all who belong to the same tribe, shall have no portion or inheritance with the rest of Israel, because they shall eat the sacrifices of the Lord and his offerings, and they shall receive nothing else from the property of their brothers; for the Lord himself is their inheritance, as he said to them.

### [C. LXXX]

This shall be the due of the priests from the people and from those who offer sacrifices: whether they sacrifice an ox or a sheep, they shall give the priest the shoulder and the stomach [Hebrew: the shoulder, the jaw, and the stomach].

> **Note:** The Scholiast has very correctly observed that the part assigned to the priest is the jawbone, which the Septuagint calls καὶ σιαγόνα (“and the jaw”) and which Onkelos likewise names. Jerome himself, in his writings, both recognizes this portion and draws allegories from it.

They shall also give the firstfruits of their grain, wine, and oil, and a portion of the wool from the shearing of the sheep; for the Lord your God chose him from all your tribes, that he might stand and minister in the name of the Lord, he and his sons, forever.

### [T. XI, B. LXXVII]

If a Levite goes out from one of your cities, from anywhere in Israel where he lives, and wishes to come, desiring the place that the Lord has chosen, he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, like all his brother Levites who stand at that time before the Lord. He shall receive the same share of food as the others, except for what is owed to him by hereditary succession in his own city.

### [B. LXXVIII, C. LXXXI]

When you enter the land that the Lord your God will give you, take care that you do not wish to imitate the abominations of those nations. Let there not be found among you anyone who makes his son or daughter pass through fire; or one who consults soothsayers, observes dreams or omens; nor a sorcerer, enchanter, consulter of pythonic spirits, or diviner [Vulgate: a diviner, or one who], or one who seeks the truth from the dead.

For the Lord detests all these things, and because of such crimes he will destroy them at your entrance. You shall be perfect and without blemish with the Lord your God [Hebrew: You shall be without blemish with the Lord your God]. These nations, whose land you will possess, listen to augurs and diviners; but you have been instructed differently by the Lord your God.

### [C. LXXXII]

The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from your nation and from your brothers, like me [Hebrew: from among you, from your brothers, one like me]; you shall listen to him, just as you asked of the Lord your God at Horeb, when the assembly was gathered, and you said: “Let me not hear again the voice of the Lord my God, nor see again this great fire, lest I die.” And the Lord said to me: “They have spoken well in all that they said.”

### [B. LXXIX]

“I will raise up for them a prophet from the midst of their brothers, like you, and I will put my words in his mouth; he shall speak to them everything that I command him. Whoever will not listen to my words that he speaks in my name, I myself will be his avenger.”

### [C. LXXXIII]

But the prophet who, corrupted by arrogance, wishes to speak in my name what I did not command him to say, or who speaks in the name of foreign gods, shall be killed [Hebrew: But the prophet who speaks presumptuously in my name what I did not command him to say, or who speaks in the name of foreign gods, shall die].

### [B. LXXX]

But if you say in silent thought: “How can I understand the word that the Lord did not speak?”—you shall have this sign: whatever that prophet foretells in the name of the Lord does not happen; the Lord did not speak it, but the prophet fabricated it through the pride of his spirit. Therefore you shall not fear him [Hebrew: you shall not be afraid because of him].

---

### [B. LXXXI, Chapter XIX]

When the Lord your God has destroyed the nations whose land he is going to give you, and you possess it and dwell in their cities and houses [Vulgate: his], you shall set apart three cities for yourself in the middle of the land that the Lord your God will give you as a possession. Carefully prepare the road, and divide the whole territory of your land into three equal parts, so that the fugitive who has fled because of homicide may have a nearby place to escape.

### [C. LXXXIV]

This shall be the law for the homicide who flees, whose life must be preserved: whoever strikes his neighbor unknowingly, and against whom it is shown that he had no hatred yesterday or the day before; rather, that he went simply with him into the forest to cut wood, and while cutting the wood the axe flew from his hand, and the iron slipped from the handle and struck his companion and killed him—he shall flee to one of the cities mentioned above and live. Otherwise, the avenger of the blood of the one whose blood was shed might pursue him, driven by grief, and overtake him if the road were longer, and strike the life of one who is not guilty of death, since it is shown that he had previously held no hatred against the one who was killed.

Therefore I command you to divide the three cities among yourselves at equal distances. But when the Lord your God enlarges your borders, as he swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land that he promised them—provided that you keep his commandments and do what I command you today, loving the Lord your God and walking in his ways at all times—you shall add three more cities for yourself and double the number of the three cities mentioned above, so that innocent blood may not be shed in the midst of the land that the Lord your God will give you to possess, and you may not become guilty of bloodshed.

But if someone hates his neighbor, lies in wait for his life, rises up, strikes him, and he dies, and the killer flees to one of the cities mentioned above, the elders of that city shall send for him and seize him from the place of refuge. They shall deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, and he shall die. You shall not pity him; thus you shall remove innocent blood from Israel, and it shall go well with you.

### [B. LXXXII, C. LXXXIII]

You shall not move or transfer your neighbor’s boundary markers, which earlier people established in your possession, in the land that the Lord your God gives you to possess.

### [B. LXXXVI, C. LXXXVI]

One witness shall not stand against anyone concerning any iniquity or crime, whatever it may be; every matter shall stand on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

If a false witness stands against a man, accusing him of transgression, both parties shall stand before the Lord, in the presence of the priests and judges who are in those days. When, after the most careful investigation, they discover that the false witness has spoken a lie against his brother, they shall do to him [Hebrew: they shall do to him] what he intended to do to his brother. Thus you shall remove the evil from among you, so that the others, hearing of it, may fear and never again dare to do such a thing.

### [B. LXXXIV, C. LXXXVII]

You shall not pity him, but shall exact life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

---

### [T. XII, C. LXXXVIII, Chapter XX]

If you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots, and a greater number of the opposing army than you possess, you shall not fear them, because the Lord your God is with you, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.

When the battle is near, the priest shall stand before the battle line and speak to the people: “Hear, Israel: today you are entering battle against your enemies. Let not your heart be afraid; do not fear, do not retreat, and do not be terrified of them, because the Lord your God is in your midst and will fight for you against your adversaries, to rescue you from danger.”

The commanders of the individual units shall also proclaim before the army: “Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in battle and another dedicate it. Who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not yet made it common, so that everyone may eat from it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in battle and another man perform his duty. Who is the man who has betrothed a wife but has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in battle and another man take her.”

After these words they shall add the rest and speak to the people: “Who is the man who is fearful and fainthearted? Let him go and return to his house, lest he make the hearts of his brothers faint, just as he himself has been terrified by fear.”

When the commanders of the army have become silent and finished speaking, each man shall prepare his own divisions for battle [Hebrew: When they have finished speaking, the commanders of the armies shall appoint officers at the head of the people].

### [C. LXXXIX]

Whenever you approach a city to fight against it, you shall first offer it peace. If it accepts and opens its gates to you, all the people who are in it shall be saved and shall serve you under tribute.

But if they refuse to make a treaty with you and instead wage war against you [Hebrew: act] against you, you shall besiege it. When the Lord your God delivers it into your hand, you shall strike every male in it with the edge of the sword, except for the women and children, the livestock, and everything else that is in the city. You shall divide all the spoil among the army and eat from the plunder of your enemies, which the Lord your God has given you.

Thus you shall do to all the cities that are very far from you and are not among the cities that you are to receive as a possession. But in the cities that are given to you, you shall permit no one at all to live; you shall kill them with the edge of the sword: the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, as the Lord your God commanded you. Otherwise they may teach you to commit all the abominations that they themselves have committed for their gods, and you will sin against the Lord your God.

### [B. LXXXVI, C. XC]

When you besiege a city for a long time and surround it with fortifications in order to capture it, you shall not cut down trees from which food can be eaten, nor shall you use axes to lay waste the countryside around it; for it is a tree, not a man, and it cannot increase the number of those fighting against you.

But if there are trees that are not fruit trees, but wild and suitable for other uses, cut them down [Hebrew: it cannot present itself before you. But the trees that are not fruit trees, cut down], and construct siege works until you capture the city that is waging war against you.

---

### [B. LXXXVIII, C. XCI, Chapter XXI]

When, in the land that the Lord your God is giving you, the corpse of a slain man is found and the killer is unknown, your elders and judges shall go out and measure the distances from the corpse to the surrounding cities. The elders of the city that they determine to be nearest shall take a heifer from the herd that has never been under a yoke and has never plowed the earth [Hebrew: on which no work has ever been done], and they shall lead it to a rough and rocky valley [Hebrew: the words “and rocky” are absent] that has never been plowed or received seed.

> **Note:** In the Hebrew text we read וְעָרְפוּ (*ve-ʿārfū*), which means “and they shall break the neck” or “and they shall decapitate.” Here and below, in verse 6, the Scholiast takes the verb עָרַף (*ʿāraph*) in the same sense in which Jerome uses בָּלַע (*bālaʿ*), which Jerome often renders in Latin by *praecipitare* (“to hurl down”) and *destruere* (“to destroy”). Thus, in 2 Samuel 20:19: “Why do you hurl down the inheritance of the Lord?” And in Isaiah 25:7–8: “He will hurl down the face of the covering. He will hurl down death forever,” and so forth. Among Jerome’s usages, therefore, to slaughter, destroy, and hurl down are treated as equivalent. —Martianay.
>
> The Urbinas manuscript, in the singular, reads *cervicem* (“the neck”). The Hebrew, like Aquila, has one verb: “they shall decapitate.”

They shall break the necks of the heifer there [Hebrew: and they shall hurl it down in the ravine]. Then the priests, the sons of Levi, shall approach—those whom the Lord your God chose to minister to him, to bless in his name, and according to whose word every matter, and everything clean or unclean, is to be judged.

> **Note:** The Vulgate books read “and the elders shall come,” differing from the Hebrew text, which has “and all the elders,” without “shall come.”

All the elders of that city shall come to the slain man, wash their hands over the heifer that was struck in the valley [Hebrew: that was hurled down], and say: “Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it. Be merciful to your people Israel, whom you redeemed, Lord, and do not charge innocent blood against your people Israel.” Thus the guilt of blood shall be removed from them. But you shall be free of the innocent blood that was shed when you do what the Lord commanded [Hebrew: what is right in the eyes of the Lord].

### [B. LXXXVIII, C. XCII]

If you go out to battle against your enemies, and the Lord your God delivers them into your hand, and you take them captive, and among the captives you see a beautiful woman, love her, and wish to take her as your wife, you shall bring her into your house. She shall shave her hair, cut her nails, and remove the garment in which she was captured. She shall sit in your house and mourn her father and mother for one month. Afterward you shall go in to her, sleep with her, and she shall be your wife.

But if afterward she does not remain pleasing to your mind, you shall release her free. You may not sell her for money or oppress her by force, because you humbled her [Hebrew: because you afflicted her].

### [B. LXXXIX, C. XCIII]

If a man has two wives, one loved and the other hated, and they bear him children, and the son of the hated wife is the firstborn, and he wishes to divide his property among his sons, he may not make the son of the loved wife the firstborn and give him precedence over the son of the hated wife. Rather, he shall acknowledge the son of the hated wife as the firstborn and give him a double portion of everything he possesses, for he is the beginning of his children, and the rights of the firstborn belong to him.

### [B. XC, C. XCIV]

If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not obey the command of his father and mother, and, after being disciplined, refuses to obey, they shall seize him and bring him to the elders of that city and to the gate of judgment [Hebrew: to the gate of the place]. They shall say to them: “This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he refuses to listen to our admonitions; he gives himself to revelry, dissipation, and feasting.”

The men of the city shall stone him, and he shall die, so that you may remove the evil from among you, and all Israel, hearing of it, may fear.

### [B. XCI, C. XCV]

When a man commits an offense punishable by death, is sentenced to death, and is hanged on a gallows, his corpse shall not remain on the wood; rather, he shall be buried on the same day, because the one who hangs on a tree is accursed by God. You shall not defile the land that the Lord your God gives you as a possession.

> **Note:** To elucidate this statement, the most learned Jerome gathered much material in Book II of his *Commentary on the Epistle to the Galatians*, chapter 3. It is not appropriate to reproduce all of it here; it is enough to observe that the Hebrew text formerly read, as it still does, כִּי קִלְלַת אֱלֹהִים תָּלוּי, which Jerome himself reads as *chi calalath Eloim thalui*. But Ebion, the arch-heretic and semi-Christian, interprets it as ὅτι ὕβρις Θεοῦ ὁ κρεμάμενος, that is, “because the one who hangs is an insult to God.” The Hebrew who instructed Jerome to some extent in the Scriptures told him that it could also be read: “Because God has been suspended insultingly.” Finally, if Jerome is to be trusted, it should rather be thought that, after Christ’s passion, the name of God was inserted by someone both in Hebrew and in our manuscripts in order to brand us with infamy, since we believe that Christ was accursed by God. For the rest, see the cited passage. —Martianay.
>
> Recall also what Martianay notes: namely, the holy Doctor’s *Commentary on the Epistle to the Galatians*, chapter 3. But do not suppose, with that editor, that the name, that is, “of God,” was inserted after Christ’s passion into the Hebrew and our manuscripts by someone wishing to brand us with infamy.

---

### [B. XCII, C. XCVI, Chapter XXIII]

You shall not see your brother’s ox or sheep straying and pass by; rather, you shall lead it back to your brother, even if he is not your close relative and you do not know him. You shall bring it into your house, and it shall remain with you until your brother seeks it and receives it. You shall do the same with his donkey, his garment, and every possession of your brother that has been lost: if you find it, do not neglect it as though it belonged to someone else.

### [B. XCIII, C. XCVII]

If you see your brother’s donkey or ox fallen on the road, you shall not disregard it, but shall help him raise it.

A woman shall not wear a man’s clothing, nor shall a man use a woman’s garment, for whoever does these things is an abomination before God.

### [B. XCIV, C. XCVIII]

If, while walking along the road, you find a bird’s nest in a tree or on the ground, with the mother sitting over the chicks or eggs, you shall not take her together with her young. Rather, you shall let the mother go, keeping the young for yourself, so that it may go well with you and you may live a long time.

### [B. XCV, C. XCIX]

When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet around the roof, lest blood be shed in your house and you become liable when someone falls from it and plunges downward.

### [B. XCVI]

You shall not sow your vineyard with a second kind of seed, lest both the seed you sowed and what grows from the vineyard be consecrated together.

### [B. XCVII, C. C]

You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.

### [B. XCVIII]

You shall not wear a garment woven from wool and linen.

### [B. XCIX, C. CI]

You shall make cords on the fringes [Hebrew: you shall make fringes] at the four corners of your cloak with which you cover yourself.

If a man takes a wife and afterward hates her, seeks grounds on which to dismiss her, makes a serious accusation against her, and says: “I took this woman as my wife, and when I approached her I did not find her a virgin,” her father and mother shall take her and bring with them the signs of her virginity [Vulgate: to the gate] before the elders of the city who are within the gates.

The father shall say: “I gave my daughter to this man as a wife. Because he hates her, he has brought a serious accusation against her, saying: ‘I did not find your daughter a virgin.’ But here are the signs of my daughter’s virginity.” They shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.

The elders of that city shall seize the man and beat him. They shall also condemn him to a fine of one hundred shekels of silver [Hebrew: one hundred silver pieces], which he shall give to the girl’s father, because he brought a serious accusation against an Israelite virgin. She shall remain his wife, and he shall not be able to dismiss her for all the days of his life.

But if what he alleges is true, and virginity is not found in the girl, they shall cast her outside the door of her father’s house. The men of her city shall stone her, and she shall die, because she has committed a disgraceful act in Israel by committing fornication in her father’s house. Thus you shall remove the evil from among you.

### [B. C, C. CII]

If a man sleeps with another man’s wife, both shall die—that is, the adulterer and the adulteress—and you shall remove the evil from Israel.

### [C. CIII]

If a man betroths a virgin, and someone encounters her in the city and sleeps with her, you shall bring both of them out to the gate of that city, and they shall be stoned: the girl, because she did not cry out, although she was in the city; and the man, because he humbled [Hebrew: afflicted] his neighbor’s wife. Thus you shall remove the evil from among you.

### [C. CIV]

But if a man finds a betrothed girl in the countryside, seizes her, and sleeps with her, he alone shall die. The girl shall suffer nothing, nor is she guilty of death, because just as a thief rises against his brother and kills him, so also did the girl suffer. She was alone in the countryside; she cried out, and there was no one to rescue her.

### [B. CI, C. CV]

If a man finds a virgin girl who has no fiancé, seizes her, and sleeps with her, and the matter comes to court, the man who slept with her shall give the girl’s father fifty shekels of silver [Hebrew: silver pieces], and she shall be his wife, because he humbled [Hebrew: afflicted] her. He shall not be able to dismiss her for all the days of his life.

### [B. CII, C. CVI]

No man shall take his father’s wife, nor uncover his father’s covering [Hebrew: his, that is, his father’s].

---

### [B. CIII, C. CVII, Chapter XXIII]

A eunuch, with crushed or amputated testicles or with his penis cut off, shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.

### [C. CVIII]

A *mamzer*—that is, one born of a prostitute [Hebrew: the words “born of a prostitute” are absent]—shall not enter the assembly of the Lord, even to the tenth generation.

Ammonites and Moabites shall not enter the assembly of the Lord even after the tenth generation, forever, because they refused to meet you with bread and water on the road when you came out of Egypt. They hired Balaam son of Beor from Mesopotamia of Syria [Hebrew: son of Beor from Pethor, which is in Mesopotamia of Syria] to curse you. But the Lord your God was unwilling to listen to Balaam; he turned his curse into your blessing, because he loved you.

You shall not make peace with them or seek their welfare all the days of your life, forever.

### [C. CIX]

You shall not abhor an Edomite, because he is your brother; nor an Egyptian, because you were a resident alien in his land. Those born from them shall enter the assembly of the Lord in the third generation.

When you go out against your enemies for battle, you shall guard yourself from every evil thing.

---

### [T. XIII, B. CIV, C. CX]

If there is among you a man who has been defiled by a nocturnal emission, he shall go outside the camp and shall not return until he has washed with water toward evening; after sunset he may return to the camp.

You shall have a place outside the camp to which you may go for the necessities of nature, carrying a stake on your belt. When you sit down, you shall dig around yourself and cover with the excavated earth what has been exposed, for the Lord your God walks in the midst of your camps [Vulgate omits “your”], to rescue you and deliver your enemies to you, so that your camp may be holy and nothing indecent may appear in it, and he may not abandon you [Vulgate: lest he abandon you].

### [B. CV, C. XI]

You shall not hand over to his master a slave who has fled to you. He shall dwell with you in the place that he chooses, and he shall rest in one of your cities wherever he prefers. You shall not oppress him [Vulgate: lest you oppress him].

### [B. CVI, C. CXII]

There shall be no prostitute among the daughters of Israel, nor a fornicator among the sons of Israel.

### [B. CVII, C. CXIII]

You shall not bring the wages of a prostitute or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God, for any vow that you may make; both are an abomination before the Lord your God.

### [B. CVIII, C. CXIV]

You shall not lend money to your brother at interest, nor grain, nor anything else; but you may lend at interest to a foreigner. To your brother, however, you shall lend without interest whatever he needs, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your work in the land that you are entering [Vulgate: to which you are entering] to possess.

### [B. CIX, C. CXV]

When you make a vow to the Lord your God, you shall not delay fulfilling it, because the Lord your God will require it of you [Hebrew: the Lord your God will require it from you]. If you delay, it will be counted as sin against you. If you do not wish to promise, you will be free of sin. But what has once gone out from your lips, you shall observe and do, just as you promised the Lord your God and spoke with your own will and mouth.

### [C. CXVI]

When you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, eat grapes as much as you please, but do not carry any away with you.

### [B. CX, C. CXVII]

If you enter your friend’s standing grain, you may break off ears and rub them in your hand, but you shall not reap it with a sickle.

---

### [B. CXI, C. CXVIII, Chapter XIV]

If a man takes a wife, possesses her, and does not find favor in her because of some indecency, he shall write a bill of divorce, place it in her hand, and send her away from his house.

When she has left and married another husband, and he too hates her, gives her a bill of divorce, and sends her away from his house—or if the second husband dies—the first husband may not take her again as his wife, because she has been defiled and made abominable before the Lord. You shall not cause the land that the Lord your God has given you as a possession to sin.

### [B. CXII, C. XIX]

When a man has recently taken a wife, he shall not go out to war, nor shall any public duty be imposed upon him; rather, he shall be free from public duty at home, so that he may rejoice with his wife for one year.

> **Note:** All manuscript codices, together with the Canon, read as follows: “but he shall remain free from obligation to his own house.” The Arabic translator expressed the same meaning. In Hebrew there is לְבֵיתוֹ (*le-vethō*), which corresponds very well to *suae*. In any case, it is not especially important which reading we adopt, since the sense of the words comes to the same thing. —Martianay.
>
> The Urbinas manuscript, along with others in Martianay’s possession, has *domui suae* (“for his own house”), which also adheres more closely to the Hebrew; the Palatine manuscript has *domus suae* (“of his own house”).

### [B. CXIII, C. CXX]

You shall not take as a pledge either the lower or the upper millstone, because he has placed his life in your hands [Vulgate: placed his life].

### [B. CXIV, C. CXXI]

If a man is caught kidnapping one of his brothers, the sons of Israel, and selling him and receiving payment, he shall be killed, and you shall remove the evil from among you.

### [B. CXV]

Take careful heed not to incur the disease of leprosy, but do everything that the priests of Levitical descent teach you, according to what I commanded them, and diligently fulfill it.

### [B. CXVI, C. CXXII]

Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out of Egypt.

### [B. CXVII, C. CXXIII]

When you demand from your neighbor some object that he owes you, you shall not enter his house to take the pledge; rather, you shall stand outside, and he shall bring out to you whatever he has.

### [C. CXXIV]

But if he is poor, the pledge shall not spend the night with you [Hebrew: his pledge]; instead, you shall certainly return it to him before sunset, so that he may sleep in his garment and bless you, and you may have righteousness before the Lord your God.

### [B. CXVIII]

You shall not withhold [Hebrew: defraud] the wages of a needy and poor brother of yours, or of the resident alien who lives with you in your land and within your gates. You shall give him the payment for his labor on the same day, before sunset, because he is poor and sustains his life from it; otherwise he may cry out against you to the Lord and it will be counted as sin against you.

### [B. CXIX, C. CXXV]

Fathers shall not be put to death for their sons, nor sons for their fathers; each one shall die for his own sin.

### [B. CXX, C. CXXVI]

You shall not pervert the judgment of the resident alien or the orphan. You shall not take a widow’s garment as a pledge.

### [C. CXXVII]

Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and that the Lord your God rescued you from there.

### [C. CXXVIII]

Therefore I command you to do this thing.

### [B. CXXI]

When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf there, you shall not return to take it; rather, you shall leave it for the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

### [B. CXXII, C. CXXIX]

When you gather the fruit of your olive trees, whatever remains on the trees you shall not return to collect; rather, you shall leave it for the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow.

### [C. CXXX]

When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not gather the remaining grapes; they shall go for the use of the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow. Remember that you too were a slave in Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.

---

### [B. CXXIII, C. CXXXI, Chapter XXV]

If there is a dispute between people and they appeal to the judges, then the one whom they determine to be righteous shall receive the palm of justice, while the one whom they determine to be wicked shall be condemned for wickedness.

But if they judge the one who sinned worthy of blows, they shall throw him down and have him beaten in their presence. The measure of the blows shall correspond to the measure of the offense, but only so far that they do not exceed forty, lest your brother, being disgracefully torn, depart before your eyes [Hebrew: lest your brother be disgraced before your eyes].

### [B. CXXIV, C. CXXXII]

You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing your grain on the threshing floor.

### [B. CXXV, C. CXXXIII]

When brothers dwell together and one of them dies without children, the wife of the deceased shall not marry an outsider. Rather, his brother shall take her and raise up offspring for his brother. He shall call the firstborn son whom she bears by the name of the deceased, so that his name may not be erased from Israel.

### [C. CXXXIV]

But if he refuses to take his brother’s wife, who is owed to him by law, the woman shall go to the gate of the city and appeal to the elders. She shall say: “My husband’s brother refuses to raise up his brother’s name in Israel; he will not take me as his wife.”

They shall immediately summon him and question him. If he answers: “I do not wish to take her as my wife,” the woman [Hebrew: his kinswoman], shall approach him before the elders, remove his sandal from his foot, spit in his face, and say: “This is what shall be done to the man who does not build up his brother’s house.” His name shall be called in Israel: “House of the Barefoot One.”

### [B. CXXVI, C. CXXXV]

If men have a quarrel with one another [Vulgate adds: two men], and one begins to fight against the other, and the wife of one wishes to rescue her husband from the hand of the stronger man [Hebrew: the man striking him], and she reaches out her hand and seizes his genitals, you shall cut off her hand; you shall not show her any pity.

### [B. CXXVII, C. CXXXVI]

You shall not have in your bag different weights, a larger and a smaller; nor shall there be in your house a larger and a smaller measure. You shall have a just and true weight, and a measure that is equal and true, so that you may live for a long time upon the land that the Lord your God will give you.

For the Lord detests the one who does these things [Hebrew: the Lord your God detests him who does these things] and abhors every injustice.

### [B. CXXVIII, C. CXLVII]

Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you were coming out of Egypt: how he met you and struck the rear of your army, those who were exhausted and lingering behind, when you were weakened by hunger and toil, and he did not fear God.

### [T. XIV]

Therefore, when the Lord your God gives you rest and subdues all the surrounding nations in the land that he promised you, you shall blot out his name [Hebrew: his memory] from under heaven. Take care not to forget.

---

### [B. CXXIX, C. CXXXVIII, Chapter XXVI]

When you enter the land that the Lord your God is going to give you as a possession, obtain it, and dwell in it, you shall take some of the firstfruits of all your produce, place them in a basket, and go to the place that the Lord your God will choose, so that his name may be invoked there.

You shall approach the priest who is serving in those days and say to him: “Today I profess before the Lord your God that I have entered the land concerning which he swore to our fathers that he would give it to us.”

The priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it before the altar of the Lord your God. Then you shall speak in the presence of the Lord your God:

“An Aramean pursued my father, who went down into Egypt and lived there as a resident alien, few in number; but he grew into a great, strong nation of immense population. The Egyptians afflicted us and persecuted us, imposing extremely heavy burdens upon us. We cried out to the Lord, the God of our fathers, and he heard us, looked upon our humiliation, our labor, and our distress, and brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, signs, and wonders. He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

“Therefore, now I offer the firstfruits of the produce of the land that the Lord has given me.”

You shall leave them in the presence of the Lord your God, worship the Lord your God, and rejoice in all the good things that the Lord your God has given you and your household—you, the Levite, and the resident alien who is with you.

When you have completed the tithe of all your produce, in the third year, the year of tithing, you shall give it to the Levite, the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow, so that they may eat within your gates and be filled. Then you shall speak in the presence of the Lord your God:

“I have removed from my house what was consecrated, and I have given it to the Levite, the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow, just as you commanded me. I have not transgressed your commandments, nor have I forgotten your instruction [Vulgate adds: your].

“I have not eaten of it in my mourning, nor separated any of it for any impurity, nor spent anything from it for a funeral. I have obeyed the voice of the Lord my God and have done everything as you commanded me.

“Look down from your sanctuary, from your lofty dwelling in the heavens, and bless your people Israel and the land that you have given us, as you swore to our fathers—a land flowing with milk and honey.”

Today the Lord your God has commanded you to do these commandments and judgments, and to keep and fulfill them with all your heart and with all your soul.

### [B. CXXX]

Today you have chosen the Lord to be your God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, commandments, and judgments, and to obey his command.

And today the Lord has chosen you to be his special people, as he told you, and to keep all his commandments. He will make you higher than all the nations that he created, for praise, renown, and his glory [Hebrew omits “his”]; and you shall be a holy people to the Lord your God, as he said.

Then Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying: “Keep every commandment that I command you today.”

### [T. XV, B. CXXXI, Chapter XXVII]

When you have crossed the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God will give you, you shall erect large stones and smooth them with lime, so that you can write upon them all the words of this law [Heb. “And you shall write upon them all the words of this law”], after crossing the Jordan. Thus you shall enter the land that the Lord your God will give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as he swore to your fathers.

When, therefore, you have crossed the Jordan, erect the stones that I command you today on Mount Ebal; smooth them with lime; and build there an altar to the Lord your God, from stones untouched by iron, from rough and unhewn stones. Offer upon it burnt offerings to the Lord your God; sacrifice peace offerings; eat there and rejoice before the Lord your God. Write upon the stones all the words of this law plainly and clearly.

### [C. CXXXIX]

Moses and the Levitical priests said to all Israel: “Pay attention and listen, Israel. Today you have become the people of the Lord your God. You shall listen to his voice and do the commandments and ordinances that I command you today” [Vulgate omits “today”].

### [C. CXL]

Moses commanded the people on that day, saying: “These shall stand to bless the people on Mount Gerizim, after the Jordan has been crossed: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin. Opposite them, these shall stand for the cursing on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.

### [C. CXLI]

“The Levites shall proclaim and say to all the men of Israel in a loud voice:

### [B. CXXXII]

‘Cursed is the man who makes a carved or molten image, an abomination to the Lord, the work of craftsmen’s hands, and places it in secret.’”

And all the people shall answer and say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who does not honor his father and mother.”

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who moves his neighbor’s boundary marker.”

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who leads a blind man astray on the road.”

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who perverts justice for the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow.”

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who lies with his father’s wife and uncovers the covering of his bed.”

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who lies with any animal.”

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother.”

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who lies with his mother-in-law” [Heb. “with his mother-in-law,” that is, his female relative].

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who strikes his neighbor secretly.”

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who accepts a bribe to strike down an innocent person.”

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

“Cursed is he who does not abide by the words of this law and carry them out in practice.”

And all the people shall say: “Amen.”

[Note: Saint Jerome discusses at length the variant readings of this verse among the Hebrews, Samaritans, and Greeks in Book II of his Commentary on the Epistle to the Galatians, chapter III; the curious reader may be referred there. MART. — Saint Jerome’s Commentary on the Epistle to the Galatians, chapter III, should again be consulted, as Martianus also directs.]

### [B. CXXXIII, C. CXLII, Chapter XXVIII]

But if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and perform all his commandments that I command you today, the Lord your God will make you higher than all the nations that inhabit the earth. All these blessings will come upon you and overtake you, if you listen to his commandments.

Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed in the field. Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your land, and the fruit of your livestock—the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep. Blessed shall be your granaries, and blessed your stores. Blessed shall you be when you enter, and blessed when you depart.

The Lord will cause your enemies who rise against you to fall defeated before you. They will come against you by one road, and flee before you by seven. The Lord will send blessing upon your storehouses and upon all the works of your hands [Heb. “and upon everything to which you put your hand”], and he will bless you in the land that you receive.

The Lord will raise you up for himself as a holy people, as he swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the Lord your God and walk in his ways. All the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord has been invoked over you, and they shall fear you.

The Lord will make you abound in every good thing: in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your land, which the Lord swore to your fathers that he would give you. The Lord will open for you his excellent treasury, heaven, to give rain to your land in its season, and he will bless all the works of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but you yourself will borrow from none.

The Lord will set you as the head and not the tail; you will always be above and not below, if you listen to the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today, and keep and perform them, and do not turn away from them either to the right or to the left, and do not follow foreign gods or worship them [Heb. “and do not turn away from the commandments that I command you today, either to the right or to the left; do not go after foreign gods or worship them”].

### [C. CXLIII]

But if you do not wish to listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and perform all his commandments and ordinances that I command you today, all these curses will come upon you and overtake you.

Cursed shall you be in the city, and cursed in the field. Cursed shall be your granary, and cursed your stores. Cursed shall be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep. Cursed shall you be when you enter, and cursed when you depart.

The Lord will send upon you famine and hunger, and rebuke in all the works that you undertake, until he crushes and quickly destroys you because of your very evil inventions by which you have abandoned me. The Lord will bring pestilence upon you until he consumes you from the land that you are entering to possess. The Lord will strike you with wasting disease, fever and cold, burning heat and feverishness, corrupt air and mildew, and will pursue you until you perish.

The sky above you shall be bronze, and the earth that you tread shall be iron. The Lord will give the rain of your land as dust, and ash shall descend upon you from heaven until you are crushed [Heb. “Dust and ashes shall descend upon you from heaven until you are crushed”].

The Lord will hand you over, falling before your enemies. You will go out against them by one road and flee by seven, and you will be scattered throughout all the kingdoms of the earth. Your corpse shall become food for all the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, and there will be no one to drive them away.

The Lord will strike you with the Egyptian ulcer, and with the part of the body through which excrement is discharged, as well as with scabies and itching, so that you cannot be healed. The Lord will strike you with madness, blindness, and derangement of mind. At midday you will grope about as a blind man usually gropes in darkness, and you will not make your ways straight. At all times you shall suffer oppression and be crushed by violence, and you shall have no one to rescue you.

You shall take a wife, and another man shall sleep with her. You shall build a house, but shall not live in it. You shall plant a vineyard, but shall not harvest it. Your ox shall be slaughtered before your eyes, but you shall not eat from it. Your donkey shall be taken away in your sight, and shall not be returned to you. Your sheep shall be given to your enemies, and there shall be no one to help you.

Your sons and daughters shall be handed over to another people. You shall see it with your own eyes, and your eyes shall fail from watching them all day, while your hand has no strength. The fruit of your land and all your labors shall be eaten by a people whom you do not know. You shall continually suffer oppression and be crushed all your days, astonished at the terror of what your eyes will see.

The Lord will strike you with a terrible ulcer on your knees and thighs, so that you cannot be healed from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head. The Lord will lead you and the king whom you set over yourself to a nation that neither you nor your fathers know, and there you shall serve foreign gods, wood and stone. You shall become a byword and a tale among all the peoples to whom the Lord leads you.

You will sow much seed in the ground but gather little, because locusts will devour everything. You will plant and cultivate a vineyard, but you will not drink wine or gather anything from it, because worms will ravage it. You will have olive trees throughout all your borders, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, because the olives will fall and perish. You will beget sons and daughters, but you will not enjoy them, because they will be taken captive. Rust will consume all your trees and the produce of your land.

The resident alien who lives with you in your land will rise above you and become higher, while you will descend and become lower. He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.

All these curses will come upon you [Vulgate omits “these”], pursuing and overtaking you until you perish, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God and did not keep his commandments and ordinances that he commanded you. They shall be signs and portents upon you and upon your offspring forever, because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and gladness of heart, despite the abundance of everything.

You shall serve your enemy whom the Lord will send against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and utter want. He will place an iron yoke upon your neck until he crushes you.

The Lord will bring against you a nation from far away, from the ends of the earth [Heb. omits “and from the ends of the earth”], like a flying eagle rushing upon you—a nation whose language you cannot understand, a shameless nation that does not respect the old or pity the young. It will devour the fruit of your livestock and the produce of your land until you perish. It will leave you neither grain, wine, and oil, nor herds of cattle and flocks of sheep, until it destroys and crushes you in all your cities.

It will besiege you in all your gates until your strong and lofty walls, in which you trusted throughout all your land, are destroyed [Heb. “You shall be besieged in all your gates until your walls are destroyed”]. You will be besieged within your gates throughout the land that the Lord your God will give you [Vulgate adds “your”], and you will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons [Vulgate adds “your”] and daughters, whom the Lord your God has given you, in the distress and devastation with which your enemy will oppress you.

The delicate and luxurious man among you [Heb. “and tender”] will begrudge his brother, and the wife who lies in his embrace, lest he give them any of the flesh of his sons [Vulgate omits “his”] that he will eat, because he has nothing else during the siege and deprivation with which your enemies will devastate you within all your gates.

The tender and delicate woman, who could not set her foot upon the ground because of her extreme softness and delicacy, will begrudge the husband who lies in her embrace the flesh of her son and daughter, and the afterbirth that comes out from between her thighs, and the children who are born at that very hour. For in the scarcity of everything, during the siege and devastation with which your enemy will oppress you within your gates, she will secretly eat them.

Unless you keep and perform all the words of this law written in this book, and fear its glorious and terrible name—that is, the Lord your God—the Lord will increase your plagues and the plagues of your offspring: great and enduring plagues [Heb. “faithful”], terrible and perpetual diseases [Heb. “faithful”].

He will turn against you all the afflictions of Egypt that you feared, and they will cling to you. Moreover, the Lord will bring upon you every sickness and every plague not written in the book of this law, until he crushes you. You will be left few in number, though previously you were as numerous as the stars of heaven, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God.

And just as the Lord formerly rejoiced over you, doing you good and multiplying you, so he will rejoice over you by destroying and overthrowing you, until you are removed from the land that you are entering to possess [Vulgate: “that you are entering to possess”]. The Lord will scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you will serve foreign gods whom neither you nor your fathers have known, gods of wood and stone.

Among those nations you will have no rest, nor will there be repose for the sole of your foot. There the Lord will give you a fearful heart, failing eyes, and a soul consumed by sorrow.

### [B. CXXXIV]

Your life shall hang before your eyes like something suspended [Heb. “before you”]. [Note: The Latins first borrowed “before your eyes” from the Septuagint; this reading is found in the Canon and in a few other ancient manuscript codices. In the course of time, “before you” appears to have passed into many Latin codices from a marginal scholium in the Canon; for, along with the printed editions, the greater part of the manuscripts read thus. MART.] You will fear night and day, and you will not trust your life. In the morning you will say, “If only it were evening!” and in the evening, “If only it were morning!” because of the fear in your heart with which you will be terrified, and because of what your eyes will see.

The Lord will bring you back in ships to Egypt, by the route of which he said to you, “You shall never see it again.” There you will be sold to your enemies as male and female slaves, and there will be no one to buy you.

### [T. XVI, Chapter XXIX]

These are the words of the covenant that the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant that he made with them at Horeb.

### [C. CXLIV]

Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: “You have seen all that the Lord did before your eyes in the land of Egypt—to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to his entire land—the great trials that your eyes saw, those great signs and wonders.

### [B. CXXXV]

“But the Lord has not given you an understanding heart, seeing eyes, or ears capable of hearing, even to the present day. He led you through the wilderness for forty years. Your garments were not worn out, nor were the sandals on your feet consumed by age” [Note: One manuscript, the Canon of Hebrew truth, preserves here the true reading from its source: “the sandal of your foot”; all other printed copies and manuscripts read “the sandals of your feet.” MART. — Here too our manuscripts and most others cited by Martianus, along with the Vulgate, read “your feet” instead of “your foot.” In Hebrew literally: “your sandal was on your foot,” and so forth.]

“You did not eat bread, nor did you drink wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the Lord your God. You came to this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us in battle. We struck them, took their land, and gave it as a possession to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

“Therefore keep the words of this covenant and perform them, so that you may understand all that you do. You are all standing today before the Lord your God: your leaders, your tribes, your elders, your teachers, all the people of Israel, your children, your wives, and the resident alien who is living in your camp, excepting the woodcutters and those who carry water [Heb. “the woodcutters and those who carry water”], in order that you may enter into the covenant of the Lord your God and into the oath that the Lord your God is making with you today, so that he may establish you as his people and that he may be your God, as he told you and as he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

“I am not making this covenant and confirming these oaths with you alone, but with all who are here today and with those who are absent. You yourselves know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the midst of the nations. As you passed through them, you saw their abominations and impurities—that is, their idols of wood and stone, silver and gold, which they worshiped.

“Let there not be among you any man or woman, family or tribe, whose heart turns away today from the Lord our God, to go and serve the gods of those nations, lest there be among you a root producing gall and bitterness.

“When he hears the words of this oath, let him bless himself in his heart, saying, ‘Peace will be mine, and I will walk in the stubbornness of my heart,’ and ‘Let the drunken sweep away the thirsty’ [Note: Thus the Canon of Hebrew truth reads, as do all the manuscripts, supported by the Syriac, Chaldean, Arabic, and Samaritan versions. The sense is more obscure in the printed editions because one small letter has been changed—from s to b: “let him consume.” MART. — The Urbinas manuscript reads: “let the drunkard take away the thirsty.” I do not know whether the Vulgate reading, “let him consume,” which Sixtus V ordered restored in the Latin Bibles, is more correct; it can conveniently be derived from the Hebrew. Certainly the passage, obscure by its own nature, does not become more obscure through this reading, as Martianus thinks; rather, it has seemed clearer to learned interpreters.]

“The Lord will not forgive him. Rather, then the Lord’s anger and jealousy will burn most fiercely against that man. All the curses written in this book will settle upon him, and the Lord will blot out his name from under heaven. The Lord will separate him for destruction from all the tribes of Israel, according to the curses contained in the book of this law and covenant.

“The following generation, the children who will be born afterward, and the foreigners who come from a distant land, will see the plagues of that land and the diseases with which the Lord has afflicted it, burning it with sulfur and the heat of salt, so that it is no longer sown and nothing growing sprouts from it. It will be like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboim, which the Lord overthrew in his anger and fury.

“All the nations will say: ‘Why has the Lord done this to this land? What is the meaning of this immense and furious anger?’ And they will answer: ‘Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord, which he made with their fathers when he brought them out of the land of Egypt; they served foreign gods and worshiped them—gods whom they did not know and who had not been assigned to them. Therefore the Lord’s anger burned against this land, bringing upon it all the curses written in this book, and he expelled them from their land in anger, fury, and great indignation.’”

### [B. CXXXVI, C. CXLV]

“He cast them into a foreign land, as is witnessed today.

“The hidden things belong to the Lord our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, so that we may perform all the words of this law.”

### [Chapter XXX]

“When all these words come upon you—the blessing or the curse that I have set before you—and you take them to heart among all the nations to which the Lord your God has scattered you, and you return to him and obey his commands, as I command you today, you and your children, with all your heart and all your soul, the Lord your God will restore your captivity, have compassion on you, and gather you again from all the peoples among whom the Lord your God previously scattered you.

“If you have been scattered to the ends of heaven, from there the Lord your God will gather you and take you, and he will bring you into the land that your fathers possessed. You will take possession of it, and he will bless you and make you more numerous than your fathers.

“The Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, so that you may love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul, and may live. The Lord will turn all these curses upon your enemies and upon those who hate and persecute you.

“You will return and listen to the voice of the Lord your God. You will perform all the commandments that I command you today, and the Lord your God will make you abound in all the works of your hands, in the offspring of your womb [Heb. “in the fruit of your womb”], in the fruit of your livestock, in the abundance of your land, and in the plenty of all things.

“For the Lord will again rejoice over you, doing you good, as he rejoiced over your fathers, if only you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, keep his commandments and ordinances written in this book of the law, and return to the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul.”

### [C. CXLVI]

“This commandment that I command you today is not above you, nor is it far away, nor is it situated in heaven, so that you might say: ‘Who among us can ascend to heaven to bring it to us, so that we may hear it and perform it?’

“It is not beyond the sea, so that you might make excuses and say: ‘Who among us can cross the sea and bring it to us, so that we may hear and perform what has been commanded?’ Rather, the word is very near you—in your mouth and in your heart—so that you may perform it.”

### [B. CXXXVII, C. CXLVII]

“Consider that today I have set before you life and good, and, conversely, death and evil, so that you may love the Lord your God, walk in his ways, keep his commandments, ordinances, and judgments, and live, and so that he may multiply you and bless you in the land that you are entering to possess.

“But if your heart turns away, and you are unwilling to listen, and, deceived by error, you worship foreign gods and serve them, I declare to you today that you shall perish and soon die in the land that you are entering, after crossing the Jordan, to possess.”

### [B. CXXXVIII]

“I call heaven and earth as witnesses today: I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. Therefore choose life, so that you and your offspring may live, love the Lord your God, obey his voice, and cling to him—for he is your life and the length of your days—so that you may dwell in the land that the Lord swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give them.”

### [T. XVII, C. CXLVIII, Chapter XXXI]

Moses went and spoke all these words to all Israel. He said to them: “I am today one hundred and twenty years old. I can no longer go out and come in, especially since the Lord has said to me, ‘You shall not cross this Jordan.’ The Lord your God himself will cross before you. He will destroy all these nations before you, and you will possess them. Joshua himself will cross before you, as the Lord has spoken.

“The Lord will do to them as he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land; he will destroy them. When the Lord has handed these over to you, you shall deal with them in the same way as I have commanded you.

“Act manfully and be strong. Do not fear or be terrified before them, because the Lord your God himself is your leader. He will not abandon or forsake you.”

### [C. CXLIX]

Moses summoned Joshua and said to him before all Israel: “Be strong and courageous, for you will bring this people into the land that the Lord swore to their fathers he would give them, and you will divide it by lot. The Lord, who is your guide, will himself be with you. He will not abandon or forsake you. Do not fear or be terrified.”

Moses wrote this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and to all the elders of Israel. He commanded them, saying:
