They struck the city with the edge of the sword, along with all its inhabitants, and left no remnant in it. They did to the king of Libnah as they had done to the king of Jericho.

[C. XLVI.] From Libnah he passed with all Israel to Lachish and attacked it, deploying the army all around. The Lord delivered Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the following day. He struck it with the edge of the sword [Col. 0483C] and every living being that had been in it, just as he had done to Libnah.

[C. XLVII.] At that time Horam, king of Gezer, went up to assist Lachish. Joshua struck him and all his people until they were destroyed.

[C. XLVIII.] He passed from Lachish to Eglon, surrounded it, and attacked it on that same day. He struck with the edge of the sword every living being that was in it, according to all that he had done to Lachish.

[C. XLIX.] He also went up with all Israel from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it. He captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword, as well as its king and all the towns of that region, and every living being that had dwelt there. He left no remnant in it. As he had done to Eglon, so he did to Hebron, consuming by the sword everything he found in it.

[Col. 0483D] [C. L.] From there he returned to Debir, captured it, and devastated it. He also struck its king and all the surrounding towns with the edge of the sword. He left no remnant in it. As he had done to Hebron and Libnah and their kings, so he did to Debir and its king.

[C. LI.] Thus Joshua struck the whole hill country, the Negeb, the lowland, and the slopes, together with their kings. He left no remnant among them [h. “in them”], but killed everything that breathed, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded him, from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza [h. “Azzah”]. He captured and devastated the whole land of Goshen as far as Gibeon, together with all their kings and regions, in a single assault. For the Lord [Col. 0484A] God of Israel was fighting for him. Then he returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.

[C. LII, Chapter XI.] When Jabin, king of Hazor, heard this, he sent to Jobab, king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph. He also sent to the kings of the north who lived in the hill country and in the plain south of Chinneroth, in the lowlands and in the regions of Dor by the sea, and to the Canaanite in the east and west, and to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite in the hill country. He also sent to the Hivite who lived at the foot of Hermon in the land of Mizpeh.

All these went out with their troops, a very large population, like the sand on the shore of the sea, together with horses and chariots in an immense multitude. All these kings gathered together [Col. 0484B] at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.

The Lord said to Joshua:

“Do not fear them, for tomorrow at this same hour I shall deliver all these to be wounded [h. “wounded”] before Israel. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”

[C. LIII.] Joshua came, and the whole army with him, against them at the waters of Merom suddenly. They fell upon them, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of Israel. They struck them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon, the waters of Misrephoth [h. “Misrephoth, in Latin, ‘hot waters’”], and the plain of Mizpeh, which lies to its east. He struck them all so that he left no remnant of them. He did as the Lord had commanded him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.

He immediately returned and captured Hazor and struck its king with the sword. For Hazor had formerly held supremacy among all these kingdoms. He struck every living being that dwelt there and left no remnant in it. He devastated everything to destruction and burned the city itself with fire [h. “burned it”].

[C. LIV.] He captured, struck, and destroyed all the surrounding cities and their kings, as Moses, the servant of the Lord, had commanded. Israel burned all the cities except those situated on hills and mounds; only Hazor, the most strongly fortified, did the flames consume [h. “Yet Israel did not burn the cities situated on mounds. Only Joshua consumed the very strongly fortified Hazor with fire”].

The Israelites divided among themselves all the spoils of these cities and their livestock, after killing all the people. Just as the Lord had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and he fulfilled everything. He did not omit a single word from all the commands that the Lord had given Moses.

Joshua thus captured the whole hill country, the Negeb, the land of Goshen, the lowland, the western region, Mount Israel and its lowlands, and the section of the mountain that rises toward Seir as far as Baal-gad, in the valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. He captured, struck, and killed all their kings.

Joshua waged war against these kings for a long time. There was no city that surrendered itself to the Israelites, except the Hivite who lived in Gibeon; he captured them all in battle.

[C. LV.] For it had been the Lord’s decision that their hearts should be hardened, so that they would fight against Israel, fall, receive no mercy, and perish, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

[T. VI, C. LVI.] At that time Joshua came and killed the Anakim from the hill country, from [Vulg. omits “from”] Hebron, Debir, and Anab, and from all the mountain of Judah and Israel. He destroyed their cities and left no one of the stock of the Anakim in the land of the Israelites, except in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod, where alone some were left [h. does not have “in the cities”].

Thus Joshua captured the whole land, as the Lord had spoken to Moses, and gave it as a possession to the Israelites according to their divisions and tribes. And the land rested from war.

[Col. 0485B] [Chapter XII.] These are the kings whom the Israelites struck and whose land they possessed beyond the Jordan [Note: [Col. 0485D] The canon reads, “from the rising of the sun.” This came from the Seventy Interpreters, who read *mizzerach* without the locative ending at the end. In Hebrew today it is *mizrehhah*, that is, “toward the rising.” MART.] toward the sunrise, from the torrent of Arnon to Mount Hermon, and the whole eastern region facing the wilderness.

[C. LVII.] Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, ruled from Aroer, which is situated on the bank of the torrent of Arnon, and from the middle of the valley and half of Gilead, as far as the torrent of Jabbok, which is the boundary of the Ammonites. He ruled also from the wilderness to the Sea of Chinneroth toward the east, and to the Sea of the Wilderness, which is the Salt Sea, on the eastern side along the road leading to Beth-jeshimoth, and on the southern side below the slopes of Pisgah.

[B. XIX.] The territory of Og, king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived in Ashtaroth [Col. 0485C] and Edrei, extended over Mount Hermon, Salecah, and all Bashan, as far as the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half of Gilead, to the territory of Sihon, king of Heshbon.

Moses, the servant of the Lord, and the Israelites struck them, and Moses gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

[B. XX, C. LVIII.] These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the Israelites struck beyond the Jordan on the western side, from Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon to the mountain whose section rises toward Seir. Joshua gave it as a possession to the tribes of Israel, each receiving its portion, in the hill country, the plains, and the lowlands.

In the slopes, the wilderness, and the Negeb there were the Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, [Col. 0485D] Hivite, and Jebusite.

The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one; the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one; the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one; the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one; the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one; the king of Hormah, one; the king of Harad, one; the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one; the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one; the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Epher, one; the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lassaron, one; the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one; the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one; the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one; the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam of Carmel, one; the king of Dor and of the province [h. “of the province”] of Dor, one; the king of the nations of Gilgal, one; the king of Tirzah, one: all the kings, thirty-one.

[T. VII, C. LIX, Chapter XIII.] Joshua was old and advanced in years, and the Lord said to him:

“You have grown old and are advanced in years, but a very large amount of land remains, which has not yet been divided by lot. This is the whole of Galilee, Philistia, and all the Geshurites, from the turbid river that waters Egypt to the borders of Ekron toward the north: the land of Canaan, which is divided among the five rulers of the Philistines—the Gazites, Ashdodites, Ashkelonites, Gittites, and Ekronites.

“To the south are [h. ‘To the Negeb are’] the Hivites; the whole land of Canaan; Maara of the Sidonians, as far as Aphek and the borders of the Amorites, [Col. 0486B] and its boundaries [h. . . .]. Also the region of Lebanon toward the east [h. . . .], from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon until one enters Hamath. All who live in the hill country, from Lebanon to the waters of Misrephoth, and all the Sidonians—I am the one who will drive them out [h. ‘expel them’] from before the Israelites. Let it therefore fall as an inheritance to Israel, as I commanded you.”

[C. LX.] “And now divide the land as a possession among the nine tribes and half the tribe of Manasseh, with which Reuben and Gad possessed the land that Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave them beyond the streams of the Jordan on the eastern side.

“From Aroer, which is situated on the bank of the torrent of Arnon, and from the middle of the valley, together with all the plain of Medeba, as far as Dibon, and all the cities of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the borders of the Ammonites; and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah; the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei—he was one of the remnant of the Rephaim. Moses struck and destroyed them.

“But the Israelites did not destroy the Geshurites and Maacathites, and they have lived among Israel to the present day.

“To the tribe of Levi he did not give a possession, but the sacrifices and offerings of the Lord God of Israel are themselves its inheritance, as he said to him.”

[C. LXI.] Moses therefore gave a possession to the tribe of the sons of Reuben according to their clans. Their boundary was from Aroer, which is situated on the bank of the torrent of Arnon, and from the middle of the valley of the same torrent; the whole plain [h. “and the city that is in the middle of the same torrent, and the whole plain”] that leads to Medeba; Heshbon and all its villages [Vulg. “their villages”] that are in the lowlands; Dibon, Bamoth-baal, the town of Baal-meon, Jazer, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, and Zereth-shahar on the mountain of the valley; Beth-peor and the slopes of Pisgah, Beth-jeshimoth; all the cities of the plain and the entire kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck together with the princes of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the leaders [Vulg. omits “leaders”] of Sihon, inhabitants of the land.

The Israelites also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword, together with the other slain. The Jordan River became the boundary of the Reubenites. This is the possession of the Reubenites according to their clans, consisting of cities and villages.

[C. LXII.] Moses also gave to the tribe of Gad and its sons, according to their clans, a possession, whose division is as follows [h. “whose boundary is as follows”]: the territory of Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites, as far as Aroer, which is opposite Rabbah. From Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim; from Mahanaim to the boundary of Debir [h.].

In the valley were Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the remaining part of the kingdom of Sihon [Col. 0487B] king of Heshbon. The Jordan is also its boundary, extending to the far end of the Sea of Chinneroth beyond the Jordan on the eastern side. This is the possession of the sons of Gad according to their families, with their cities and villages.

[C. LXIII.] He also gave to half the tribe of Manasseh and its sons, according to their clans, a possession, whose beginning is as follows: from Mahanaim, all Bashan and all the kingdoms of Og, king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair that are in Bashan, sixty towns. Also half of Gilead, Ashtaroth, and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, for the sons of Machir, son of Manasseh, for half the sons of Machir according to their clans.

Moses divided this possession in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan, opposite Jericho, on the eastern side. But to the tribe of Levi he did not give a possession [Col. 0487C], because the Lord God of Israel himself is its possession, as he had said to it.

[C. LXIV, Chapter XIV.] This is what the Israelites possessed in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel gave them, dividing everything by lot, as the Lord had commanded through Moses, among the nine tribes and half the tribe.

For Moses had given a possession beyond the Jordan to two and a half tribes. Apart from the Levites, who received no land among their brothers, the sons of Joseph took their place [h. does not have “their place,” but reads as follows: “Since the sons of Joseph were divided into two tribes”], divided into two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites received no other portion in the land except cities in which to dwell [Col. 0487D] and their suburbs for feeding their animals and cattle. As the Lord had commanded Moses, so the Israelites did, and they divided the land.

[B. XXII, C. LXV.] Then the sons of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite spoke to him:

“You know what the Lord spoke to Moses, the man of God, concerning me and you at Kadesh-barnea. I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of the Lord, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to inspect the land, and I reported to him what seemed true to me. But my brothers who had gone up with me discouraged the heart of the people; nevertheless I followed the Lord my God.

“Moses swore on that day, saying: ‘The land upon which your foot has trodden shall be your possession and that of your sons forever, because you have followed the Lord my God.’

“Therefore the Lord granted me life, as he promised, down to the present day. It is forty-five years since the Lord spoke this word to Moses, when Israel was traveling through the wilderness. Today I am eighty-five years old. I am as strong today as I was at the time when I was sent to explore the land; the strength I then possessed remains in me to this day, both for warfare and for walking.

“Therefore give me this mountain, which the Lord promised—when you yourself were listening—in which there are Anakim and great, fortified cities. Perhaps the Lord will be with me, and I shall be able to destroy them, as he promised me.”

[C. LXVI.] Joshua blessed him and gave Hebron to him as a possession [Vulg. adds “to him”]. Therefore Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite down to the present day, because he followed the Lord, the God of Israel.

The name of Hebron formerly was Kiriath-arba. Adam, the greatest among the Anakim, lies there. And the land rested from war.

### [B. XXIII, C. LXVII, Chapter XV]

Accordingly, this was the lot of the descendants of Judah by their clans: from the boundary of Edom, the wilderness of Zin toward the south, and extending to the farthest part of the southern region. Its beginning was at the summit of the Salt Sea and at its tongue that faces south. It goes out toward the ascent of Scorpion Pass and passes through Zin; it ascends to Kadesh-barnea and reaches Hezron, ascending toward Addar and turning around Karkaah. From there it passes through Azmon and reaches the Wadi of Egypt. Its boundaries shall be the Great Sea [Hebrew: “the great” is absent]. This shall be the boundary of the southern region.

On the east, the beginning shall be from the Salt Sea to the end of the Jordan, and the territory facing north, from the tongue of the sea to that same Jordan River. The boundary ascends to Beth-hoglah and passes northward to Beth-arabah, ascending to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben. It extends as far as the boundary of Debir, from the Valley of Achor, facing north toward Gilgal, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, south of the wadi. It passes over the waters called the Spring of the Sun, and its termination shall be at the Spring of Rogel.

It ascends through the ravine of the son of Hinnom, on the southern side of the Jebusite—this is Jerusalem—and from there rises to the summit of the mountain that is opposite Ge-hinnom, westward, at the summit of the Valley of Rephaim, toward the north. It passes from the summit of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah and reaches as far as the villages of Mount Ephron. It bends toward Baalah, which is Kiriath-jearim, that is, “city of forests” [Hebrew: absent].

It circles from Baalah westward as far as Mount Seir. It passes along the side of Mount Jearim northward to Cheslon and descends to Beth-shemesh; it passes through Timnah. It reaches opposite the northern side of Ekron, bends toward Shicron, and passes over Mount Baalah. It reaches Jebneel and ends at the Great Sea toward the west [Col. 0489A].

These are the boundaries of the descendants of Judah all around, according to their clans.

### [C. LXVIII]

To Caleb son of Jephunneh he gave a portion among the descendants of Judah, as the Lord had commanded him: Kiriath-arba, father of Anak—that is, Hebron. Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, descendants of Anak. From there he went up against the inhabitants of Debir, which had formerly been called Kiriath-sepher, that is, “city of letters” [Hebrew: absent].

### [C. LXIX]

Caleb said: “Whoever attacks Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I shall give him my daughter Achsah as wife.” Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, captured it, and he gave him his daughter Achsah as wife.

As they were going together, [Note: [Col. 0489B] The sense of this passage in Hebrew is contrary to the Latin, and there it does not say that Achsah was persuaded by her husband Othniel to ask her father Caleb for a field; rather, Achsah herself urged her husband to ask for such a field. *vattesithehu lischol*, that is, “and she stirred him up”—namely, her husband—“to ask.” [Col. 0489C] This is also consistently read below, Judges 1:14, where the same events concerning Achsah are recounted. The truth of the Hebrew is supported by one Corbie manuscript of the Bible in our library of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, no. 1. In its first hand it reads thus at Joshua 15:18: “As they were going together, she persuaded her husband to ask her father for a field.” We would almost have adopted this reading, had not the unanimous agreement of the other manuscripts, both here and in the first chapter of Judges, suggested otherwise; nor would different and conflicting interpretations of the same context in one Scriptural narrative be readily acceptable to the reader.

Moreover, in this passage Jerome conformed to the custom of the Seventy Elders, as he often did elsewhere, and in the *Epitaphium Paulae* he says that Othniel son of Jephunneh received the upper and lower waters to possess in exchange for the southern and arid land. Hence a conjecture arises that is by no means implausible: in saying that Achsah was persuaded by Othniel, Jerome understood the same thing as the Seventy translators. Nevertheless, let the reader’s judgment remain free concerning these matters. MART.

—The learned have disputed the sense of the Hebrew text in both directions. It seems, on the contrary, to state that Achsah herself urged her husband to ask for a field, as do the parallel text of the first chapter, the ancient Syriac and Arabic versions, and finally many interpreters, including some who adhere more closely to the Hebrew; these approve the sense of the Vulgate and the reading of the Latin manuscripts. Martianus reports that he found in one Corbie manuscript, in the first hand, “she persuaded her husband,” though this was later altered. Yet, apart from the fact that the manuscript has suffered tampering and its testimony is therefore unreliable in this very place, all the others present the contrary sense, although they differ from one another only in their wording [Col. 0490B].

Among our manuscripts, the Urbinas has: “As they were going together, etc.” The Palatinus has: “And as they were going together, she persuaded him to ask, etc.” This reading, however, seems to have been substituted by a later hand for an earlier reading, which is no longer visible.] she was persuaded by her husband to ask her father for a field. [Col. 0489B]

### [C. LXX]

As she was sitting on the donkey, she sighed. Caleb said to her: “What do you want?” She answered: “Give me a blessing. You have given me southern and dry land [Hebrew: absent]; add also land with water.” Caleb therefore gave her the upper and lower springs.

This is the possession of the tribe of the descendants of Judah, according to their clans. Their cities, from the farthest parts of the descendants of Judah [Hebrew], at the boundary of Edom toward the south, were: Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur, Kina, Dimonah, Adadah, Kedesh, and Hazor [Note: [Col. 0490B] Saint Jerome mentions both Hazors in his book *On Hebrew Places*. In accordance with the present annotation of the Canon, he says that this Hazor was called “new” in Scripture, to distinguish it from the old Hazor, which was a city of Jabin’s kingdom. MART.

—The Urbinas manuscript has *Capsel*, and shortly afterward *Addada*, *Aziph*, and *Celem*, and finally *Asor* and *Naba nova*; the name *Naba* has been rashly repeated in place of *Nova*. Saint Jerome, in his book *On Names*, lists several cities called Hazor.] and Hazor, Jethnam, Ziph, Telem, Baaloth, and Hazor the New [Hebrew: “Hazor the New,” because another Hazor, the old one, existed], and Kiriath, Hezron—that is, Hazor; Amam, Shema, Moladah, Hazar-gaddah, Heshmon, Beth-pelet, Hazar-shual, Beer-sheba, and Biziothiah; Baalah, Iim, Ezem, El-tolad, Chesil, Hormah, Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah, Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon.

All the cities were twenty-nine, with their villages [Note: [Col. 0490C] The same manuscript has “thirty-nine cities,” etc. Indeed, if you count the cities listed, you find not merely twenty-nine, as the printed reading has it, but thirty-five; if Hebron, Debir, and Kiriath-sepher are added, there are thirty-eight.]

### [C. LXXII]

In the lowland: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim—fourteen cities, with their villages.

Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal-gad, Dilean, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmam, Kithlish, Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah—sixteen cities, with their villages.

Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Jiphtah, Esnah, Nezib, Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah—nine cities, with their villages.

Ekron, with its villages and hamlets. From Ekron to the sea, everything that slopes toward Ashdod and its villages. Ashdod, with its villages and hamlets. Gaza, with its villages [Vulgate: “villages”] and hamlets, as far as the Wadi of Egypt, the Great Sea, and its boundary.

In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, Dannah, Kiriath-sannah—that is, Debir—Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon, and Giloh—eleven cities, with their villages.

Arab, Ruma [Note: [Col. 0490C] In place of *Ruma*, the Hebrew and Chaldean read *Dumah*, because of the similarity between *resh* and *daleth*, which are distinguished by a small stroke. Conversely, at Isaiah 21 some Hebrews read *Roma* in place of *Dumah*, wishing to direct the prophecy against the Roman kingdom, through the frivolous persuasion by which they always suppose that Romans are signified by the name Idumea. See Saint Jerome’s fifth book of commentaries on Isaiah. MART.

—Our manuscript reads *Roma* by common agreement; the Hebrew has *Duma*. Compare the commentary on Isaiah 21.] and Eshean, Janum, Beth-tappuah, Aphekah, Amata [Note: [Col. 0490D] The printed editions, with some manuscripts, read *Athmatha*; others, *Atmatha* or *Admatha*. The Canon, however, now has *Umata*, for *Humata*, or *Hhumta* in the modern Masoretes. Yet *Umata* could have been derived from the *Euma* (Εὐμὰ) of the Septuagint translators. The Canon originally read *Amata*, which Jerome read in the books on Hebrew places and names; nowhere, however, did he read *Humata* or *Umata*. Moreover, in correcting names which Jerome found—apart from a few—to be almost wholly corrupt in Greek and Latin codices, we too labored so hard that we were a thousand times weary of the undertaking and of this restoration. MART. [Col. 0492D]

—The Palatine manuscripts read *Atma*; the Urbinas, *Amatha*. In Hebrew the reading is absent or illegible in the supplied text.] and Kiriath-arba—that is, Hebron—and Zior—nine cities, with their villages.

Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah, Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah—ten cities, with their villages.

Halhul, Beth-zur, Gedor, Mareshah, Beth-anoth, and Eltekon—six cities, with their villages.

Kiriath-baal—that is, Kiriath-jearim, “city of forests” [Hebrew: absent]—and Rabbah: two cities, with their villages.

In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En-gedi—six cities, with their villages.

### [C. LXXIII]

The Jebusite, the inhabitant of Jerusalem, the descendants of Judah were unable to destroy. The Jebusite has lived with the descendants of Judah in Jerusalem to the present day.

## [B. XXIV, Chapter XVI]

The lot of the descendants of Joseph also fell from the Jordan opposite Jericho and its waters, eastward: the wilderness that rises from Jericho toward the highlands of Bethel. It goes out from Bethel to Luz; it passes along the boundary of Archi-Ataroth. It descends westward beside the boundary of Japhleti as far as the boundary of Lower Beth-horon and Gazer. Its regions end at the Great Sea.

### [C. LXXIV]

The descendants of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took possession. The boundary of the descendants of Ephraim by their clans was this: their possession toward the east extended from Atroth-addar to Upper Beth-horon. The borders go out to the sea. Michmethath faces north; the boundary turns eastward toward Taanath-shiloh [Hebrew: “the boundary” is absent] and passes eastward by Janohah. It descends from Janohah to Ataroth and Naarath; it reaches Jericho and goes out to the Jordan.

From Tappuah it passes westward into the Valley of Reeds, and its termination is at the Salt Sea [Hebrew: “Salt” is absent].

### [C. LXXV]

This is the possession of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim, according to their families. Cities were assigned to the descendants of Ephraim within the possession of the descendants of Manasseh, together with their villages [the source has an apparent OCR error: *earum* for “their”].

### [C. LXXVI]

The descendants of Ephraim did not kill the Canaanite who lived in Gazer. The Canaanite lived among Ephraim to this day, subject to tribute.

### [C. LXXVII, Chapter XVII]

The lot of the tribe of Manasseh also fell—for he was Joseph’s firstborn—to Machir, Manasseh’s firstborn and the father of Gilead, who was a warrior [Vulgate: “warrior” is absent]. He possessed Gilead and Bashan.

For the remaining descendants of Manasseh, according to their families: for the descendants of Abiezer, the descendants of Helek, the descendants of Asriel, the descendants of Shechem, the descendants of Hepher, and the descendants of Shemida. These are the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, males, according to their clans.

### [C. LXXVIII]

Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, but only daughters. Their names were: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They came before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders, saying: “The Lord commanded through Moses that an inheritance be given to us among our brothers.”

He gave them, according to the Lord’s command, an inheritance among their father’s brothers. Ten allotments therefore fell to Manasseh, apart from the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan. For the daughters of Manasseh possessed an inheritance among his sons.

### [C. LXXIX]

The land of Gilead fell to the lot of the remaining descendants of Manasseh.

The boundary of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethath, which faces Shechem, and goes out on the right beside the inhabitants of the spring of Tappuah. For the land of Tappuah, which lies beside the boundaries of the descendants of Ephraim, had fallen to Manasseh by lot.

The boundary descends to the Valley of Reeds, south of the wadi of the cities of Ephraim that lie among the cities of Manasseh. The boundary of Manasseh is north of the wadi, and its termination proceeds to the sea, so that Ephraim’s possession is to the south and Manasseh’s to the north; the sea encloses both, and they join one another at the tribe of Asher toward the north and at the tribe of Issachar toward the east.

Manasseh’s inheritance in Issachar and Asher consisted of Beth-shean and its villages, Ibleam with its villages, the inhabitants of Dor with its towns, the inhabitants of En-dor with its villages, likewise the inhabitants of Taanach with its villages [Vulgate: “villages”], the inhabitants of Megiddo with its villages, and the third part of the city of Naphath.

### [C. LXXX]

The descendants of Manasseh could not destroy these cities, but the Canaanite began to live in this land [Vulgate: “their land”]. When the descendants of Israel grew stronger, they subjected the Canaanites and made them tributaries, but they did not kill them.

### [B. XXV]

The descendants of Joseph spoke to Joshua and said: “Why have you given me the possession of one allotment, when I am such a numerous people and the Lord has blessed me?” [Col. 0492C]

Joshua answered them: “If you are a numerous people, go up into the forest and clear spaces for yourself in the land of the Perizzites and Rephaim, because the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you.”

The descendants of Joseph replied: “We cannot go up into the hill country, since the Canaanites who live in the lowland use iron chariots; Beth-shean with its villages is there, and Jezreel possesses the middle of the valley.”

Joshua said to the house of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh: “You are a numerous people and possess great strength; you shall not have one allotment only. Rather, you shall go up into the mountain country, clear it, and prepare spaces for yourselves to inhabit. You will be able to advance farther when you have overthrown the Canaanite whom you say has iron chariots and is very strong.”

## [T. VIII, B. XXVI, C. LXXXI, Chapter XVIII]

All the descendants of Israel gathered at Shiloh, and there they set up the Tabernacle of Testimony; the land was subject to them.

### [C. LXXXII]

Seven tribes of the descendants of Israel remained, which had not yet received their possessions. Joshua said to them: “How long will you remain weakened by laziness and not enter to possess the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you?

“Choose three men from each tribe, so that I may send them. Let them go through the land and survey it, describing it according to the number of each tribe’s population; then let them bring me what they have described.

“Divide the land among yourselves into seven parts. Let Judah remain within its boundaries toward the south, and the house of Joseph toward the north. Describe the land lying between them in seven parts [Hebrew: “You, however, shall describe the land in seven parts”], and come here to me, so that here, before the Lord your God, I may cast lots for you; for there is no portion among you for the Levites, but the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance.

“Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh have already received their possessions beyond the Jordan, toward the east, which Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave them.”

### [B. XXVII]

When the men had risen to go and survey the land, Joshua commanded them, saying: “Go through the land and describe it, then return to me, so that here, before the Lord [Note: [Col. 0493D] The manuscripts have “before the Lord God,” but the Hebrew does not have the word “God.” The names “God” and “Lord” are very often added in Greek and Latin copies; Saint Jerome warns that, as superfluous, they should be removed. MART.

—Those manuscripts likewise add “God,” but the Urbinas additionally has “your.”], at Shiloh, I may cast lots for you.”

They went out, surveyed it, and divided it into seven parts [Col. 0493B], writing them in a book. They returned to Joshua in the camp at Shiloh.

### [C. LXXXIII]

He cast lots for them before the Lord at Shiloh and divided the land among the descendants of Israel into seven parts [Hebrew: “according to their divisions”].

The first lot fell to the descendants of Benjamin by their clans, so that they might possess the land between the descendants of Judah and the descendants of Joseph. Their boundary toward the north was from the Jordan, running beside the northern side of Jericho; from there it went westward, ascending into the hill country and reaching the wilderness of Beth-aven. It passed beside Luz toward the south—this is Bethel—and descended to Atroth-addar, to the mountain south of Lower Beth-horon.

It bends and circles toward the sea, south of the mountain that faces Beth-horon toward the southwest. Its terminations are at Kiriath-baal, also called Kiriath-jearim, the city of the descendants of Judah. This is the region toward the sea and the west [Vulgate: “toward”].

From the south, near Kiriath-jearim, the boundary goes out toward the sea and reaches the spring of the waters of Nephtoah. It descends to the part of the mountain that faces the Valley of the Sons of Hinnom, toward the northern side at the farthest part of the Valley of Rephaim.

It descends to Ge-hinnom, that is, the Valley of Hinnom [Hebrew: absent], beside the Jebusite toward the south. It reaches the Spring of Rogel, passes northward, and goes out to En-shemesh, that is, the Spring of Sothis [Hebrew: absent]. It passes as far as the mounds opposite the ascent of Adummim. It descends to the Stone of Bohan, that is, the Stone of Bohan [Col. 0493D] son of Reuben [Hebrew: absent], and passes along the northern side toward the lowlands. It descends into the plain and goes past Beth-hoglah toward the north. Its termination is opposite the tongue of the Salt Sea, northward at the end of the Jordan, toward the south, which is its eastern boundary.

This is the possession of the descendants of Benjamin, according to their boundaries all around and their clans [Note: [Col. 0494D] The Palatinus, as do our other manuscripts, has “each of their clans” in place of “their clans,” with the same sense.]

### [C. LXXXIV]

Their cities were: Jericho, Beth-hoglah, the Valley of Keziz, Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Pharah, Ophrah, the village of Emek, Ophni, and Geba—twelve cities, with their villages.

Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zela, Eleph, Jebus—that is, Jerusalem—Gibeah, and Kiriath—fourteen cities, with their villages.

This is the possession of the descendants of Benjamin according to their clans.

### [C. LXXXV, Chapter XIX]

The second lot came out for the descendants of Simeon by their clans. Their inheritance was within the possession of the descendants of Judah: Beer-sheba, Sheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual, Baalah, Ezem, El-tolad, Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susah, Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen—thirteen cities, with their villages.

Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan—four cities, with their villages—and all the villages surrounding these cities as far as Baalath-beer, Ramah toward the south.

This is the inheritance of the descendants of Simeon according to their clans, within the allotment and possession of the descendants of Judah, which was larger. Therefore the descendants of Simeon possessed land within their inheritance.

### [C. LXXXVI]

The third lot came out for the descendants of Zebulun by their clans, and the boundary of their possession extended to Sarid. It ascended from the sea and Maralah, reached Dabbasheth, and extended to the wadi opposite Jokneam.

It turned from Sarid eastward toward the boundary of Chislot-tabor and went out to Daberath; it ascended toward Japhia. From there it passed toward the eastern side of Gath-hepher, Ittah-kazin, and went out at Rimmon. It turned toward Amthohar and Neah.

It circled northward to Hannathon, and its termination was the Valley of Iphtahel, with Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem—twelve cities, with their villages.

This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun according to their clans, its cities and villages.

### [C. LXXXVII]

The fourth lot came out for Issachar according to his clans. His inheritance was [Hebrew: “his boundary”]: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah, and Beth-pazzez.

The boundary reached Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh; its termination was at the Jordan—sixteen cities, with their villages.

This is the possession of the descendants of Issachar according to their clans, its cities and villages.

### [C. LXXXVIII]

The fifth lot fell to the tribe of the descendants of Asher according to their clans. Their boundary was Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph, Alammelech, Amad, and Mishal; it reached Carmel by the sea and Shihor-libnath.

It turned eastward toward Beth-dagon and passed as far as Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtahel, toward the north, to Beth-emek and Neiel. It went out to the left of Cabul and [Note: [Col. 0495D] All the manuscripts have this; the printed editions read *Abran*. MART.] Achran [Hebrew: Hebron], Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon.

It turned toward Hormah as far as the fortified city of Tyre and as far as Hosah. Its termination was at the sea, from the territory of Achzib, and also at Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob—twenty-two cities, with their villages.

This is the possession of the descendants of Asher according to their clans, their cities and villages.

### [C. LXXXIX]

The sixth lot fell to the descendants of Naphtali according to their families. Their boundary began at Heleph and Elon in Zaanannim, and at Adami, which is Nekeb, and Jebneel, as far as Lakkum; its termination was at the Jordan.

The boundary turned westward toward Aznoth-tabor and from there went out to Hukkok. It passed through Zebulun toward the south, through Asher toward the west, and through Judah to the Jordan toward the rising of the sun.

The fortified cities were: Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth, Adamah, Ramah, Hazor, Kedesh, Edrei, En-hazor, Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh—nineteen cities, with their villages.

This is the possession of the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali according to their clans, its cities and villages.

### [C. XC]

The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the descendants of Dan according to their families. The boundary of its possession was Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-shemesh—that is, “city of the sun” [Hebrew: absent]—Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Jethlah, Elon, Timnah, Ekron, Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath, Jehud, Bene-berak, Gath-rimmon, the waters of the Yarkon, and Rakkon, with the boundary opposite Joppa; and its boundary ended there.

### [C. XCI]

The descendants of Dan went up and fought against Leshem. They captured it, struck it with the edge of the sword, took possession of it, and lived in it, calling its name Leshem-dan [Hebrew: “calling it Leshem-dan”], after the name of Dan their father.

This is the possession of the tribe of the descendants of Dan according to their clans, its cities and villages.

### [C. XCII]

When he had finished dividing the land by lots among the tribes, the descendants of Israel gave Joshua son of Nun a possession among themselves, according to the Lord’s command: the city he requested, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He rebuilt the city and lived in it.

These are the possessions that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the clans and tribes of Israel divided by lot at Shiloh before the Lord, at the entrance of the Tabernacle of Testimony [Col. 0495D]; and they divided the land.

## [T. IX, B. XXVIII, C. XCIII, Chapter XX]

The Lord spoke to Joshua, saying: “Speak to the descendants of Israel and say to them: Set apart cities of refuge, about which I spoke to you through Moses, so that whoever has struck a person unintentionally may flee there and escape the anger of the nearest relative, who is the avenger of blood.

“When he has fled to one of these cities, he shall stand at the gate of the city and speak to the elders of that city, presenting the matters by which he may prove his innocence. They shall receive him and give him a place in which to live.

“When the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not hand him over to his power, because he struck his neighbor unintentionally and is not proved to have been his enemy previously, whether two or three days before.

“He shall live in that city until he stands before the tribunal and gives an account of his deed, and until the high priest who is in office at that time dies. Then the killer shall return and enter his city and his house from which he had fled.”

They set apart [Hebrew: “sanctified”] Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali; Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim; and Kiriath-arba, that is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

### [C. XCIV]

Beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho, they designated Bezer [Hebrew: Beser], situated in the plain wilderness, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

These cities were established for all the descendants of Israel and for the resident foreigners living among them, so that anyone who had unintentionally struck a person might flee there and not die at the hand of the nearest relative wishing to avenge the blood that had been shed, until he stood before the people to present his case.

[C. XCV, Chapter XXI.] The heads of the Levitical families approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the clans of each tribe of the Israelites. They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying: [B. XXIX.] “The Lord commanded through Moses that towns should be given to us for dwelling, together with their pasturelands for feeding our livestock.” The Israelites gave [Hebrew: to the Levites] from their own inheritances, according to the Lord’s command, towns and their pasturelands.

[C. XCVI.] The lot came out for the clan of Kohath, the priest Aaron’s descendants, from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin: thirteen towns. For the remaining descendants of Kohath—that is, for the Levites left from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and half the tribe of Manasseh—ten towns.

[C. XCVII.] For the descendants of Gershon the lot came out so that they were to receive from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali, and from half the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen towns.

[C. XCVIII.] For the descendants of Merari, according to their clans, from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun, twelve towns. The Israelites gave the Levites towns and their pasturelands, as the Lord had commanded through Moses, assigning them by lot to each group.

From the tribes of the descendants of Judah and Simeon Joshua gave towns, whose names are as follows, to the descendants of Aaron, by the clans of the Kohathite Levitical line—for the first lot came out for them: Kiriath-arba, the father of Anak, which is called Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, together with its pasturelands all around. But Caleb son of Jephunneh had given its fields and villages as a possession [Hebrew: they gave].

[C. XCIX.] Thus he gave [Hebrew: they gave] to the descendants of Aaron the priest Hebron, the city of refuge, with its pasturelands; Libnah with its pasturelands; Jattir; Eshtemoa; Holon; Debir; Ain; Juttah; and Beth-shemesh, with their pasturelands: nine towns from the two tribes, as stated.

[Col. 0497A] From the tribe of the descendants of Benjamin: Gibeon, Geba, Anathoth, and Almon, with their pasturelands: four towns. All the towns of the descendants of Aaron the priest, together with their pasturelands, were thirteen.

For the remaining clans of the descendants of Kohath of the Levitical line, this was the possession given. From the tribe of Ephraim: the cities of refuge, Shechem with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, Gezer, Kibzaim, and Beth-horon, with their pasturelands: four towns.

From the tribe of Dan: Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Aijalon, and Gath-rimmon, with their pasturelands: four towns.

From half the tribe of Manasseh: Taanach and Gath-rimmon, with their pasturelands: two towns. All ten towns, together with their pasturelands, were given to the lower-ranking descendants of Kohath.

[C. C.] To the descendants of Gershon [Col. 0497B] of the Levitical line he gave from half the tribe of Manasseh [Col. 0498A] the city [Vulgate: cities] of refuge, Golan in Bashan and Bosrah [Hebrew: Bosthram], with their pasturelands: two towns.

From the tribe of Issachar: Kedesh, Daberath, Jarmuth, and En-gannim, with their pasturelands: four towns.

From the tribe of Asher: Mishal, Abdon, Helkath, and Rehob, with their pasturelands: four towns.

[C. CI.] From the tribe of Naphtali, the city [Vulgate: cities] of refuge: Kedesh in Galilee, Hammoth-dor, and Kartan, with their pasturelands: three towns. All the towns of the families of Gershon were thirteen, together with their pasturelands.

For the descendants of Merari, the lower-ranking Levites, according to their families, from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam, Kartah, Dimnah, and Nahalal, four towns with their pasturelands.

[Note: [Col. 0497B] After the Zebulunite towns, printed editions and several manuscripts add: “From the tribe of Reuben, beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho, cities of refuge: Bezer in the wilderness, Jahzah, Kedemoth, and Mephaath, four towns with their pasturelands.” There can scarcely be any doubt that this came from the translators of the Septuagint, for what is read in the Hebrew volumes is expressed in other words, as we shall presently say. Yet, so that no diligence or fidelity may be thought lacking on our part where the matters seem most important for understanding the Scriptures, we shall not hesitate to state everything concerning the absence of this verse and the variant readings of the Hebrew, Greek, and Latin witnesses.

“First, it must be known that the Greek copies of the Seventy Interpreters agree in all respects, apart from a few matters of lesser importance and one variant reading reported by Nobilius, who says that in one book there is ‘Bosor in the wilderness, Misor,’ instead of the words read in the text, ‘Bosor in the desert; Miso and its pasturelands,’ and so forth.

“Among the Latins, however, there are very many disagreements. The entire verse 36 is absent from older and better manuscripts—for example, the Royal manuscript no. 3563, the Colbertine manuscript of Anjou no. 157, the Corbie manuscripts 1 and 10, and one of Saint-Germain, no. 157. Finally, the copyist of the Canon of the Hebrew Truth, correcting his own text against another more carefully revised exemplar, erased all these words with a stroke, as he did certain similar additions.

“We possess only three more recent manuscript copies of the Bible that read the aforesaid clause as it stands in our Latin Vulgate—not counting the disorderly editions of the Bible by Robert Estienne and the Louvain theologians, in which the towns granted to the Gileadites of Merari are mentioned before those of the Reubenites. The Syriac translator also erred in listing the towns from the tribe of Reuben before those belonging to the tribe of Zebulun.

“With these observations made, it is plainly evident that Jerome’s Hebrew exemplars were mutilated in some portion and did not contain all the verses of the Bible. For if verse 36 of this twenty-first chapter of Joshua had been present in them, Jerome would have rendered it into Latin, and it would be found in the older manuscripts of the Latin edition of the holy Doctor, in which, as we stated above, it is absent.

“True, therefore, is the note concerning the Hebrew books, by which we are informed that in the Hebrew copies of Joshua belonging to Hillel and other ancient exemplars two verses are absent (we say one), in which the four Reubenite towns are mentioned. Since these verses were lacking in some books in Jerome’s time, no one can deny that they were omitted in certain others as well.

“But concerning the Hebrew volumes, these further points remain to be noted: in some ancient and excellent manuscript copies the passage is found in this form, which we read as follows:

“*Umimmatte reuben, eth-hir miclat harotseahh: eth-betser bammidbar, veeth-migrascheha; eth-jahatsa, veeth-migrascehha. Eth-cedemoth, veeth-migrascheha; veeth-mephahat, veeth-migrascheha, arim arba.*

“It is translated: ‘And from the tribe of Reuben, the city of refuge for the manslayer: Bezer in the desert, and its pasturelands; Jahzah and its pasturelands; Kedemoth and its pasturelands; and Mephaath and its pasturelands—four towns.’

“These words are found written in the Hebrew manuscript of the Royal Library, no. 7, and in another excellent manuscript exemplar marked BB. 32 in the library of the Oratory in Paris, on the Rue Saint-Honoré. In this latter manuscript, however, a second hand erased—not two entire verses, as Richard Simon wrongly asserts in book I, chapter 22 of his *Critical History of the Old Testament*—but only four or five words that are not read in the other Hebrew exemplars or in the printed editions.

“The erased words are these: *eth hirmiclat harotseahh . . . bammidhar*, that is, ‘the city of refuge for the manslayer . . . in the desert.’ Except for these four or five words, everything else is written in the manuscript exemplars of the Royal Library, nos. 5 and 6; also in a manuscript of the very distinguished Paul Pellisson, recently donated by him to our library of Saint-Germain-des-Prés; and in many others, which we do not list for the sake of brevity.

“There are also some, though more recent, in which the two aforesaid verses are absent, just as in the ancient Latin books. Hence we know for certain that both ancient and more recent Hebrew volumes—or, rather, volumes of the later age—have been mutilated through scribal error. Consequently, in this place we have an incomplete Latin version of Joshua by Jerome, lacking one or two verses, although he repeatedly declares that he changed nothing of the Hebrew truth but produced a new edition for the people of his language in pure and faithful speech.

“We have called certain Hebrew exemplars mutilated and Jerome’s version incomplete here because, unless the four towns from the inheritance of the Reubenites were supplied in these two verses, the total of twelve towns said to have been assigned to the Merarites could in no way be made complete. Yet in verse 38 of the Scripture we explicitly read this total.

“The passage in Jerome’s version must therefore be supplied from the Greek translation of the Seventy, or rather from verses 78 and 79 of chapter 6 of the First Book of Chronicles, where the same words that are missing here are expressly found both in the Hebrew and in the Latin copies. MART.”

—The Palatine manuscript supplies in the margin of the book the passage that the Vulgate books add: “From the tribe of Reuben, beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho, cities of refuge: Bezer in the wilderness, Jahzah, Kedemoth, and Mephaath, four towns with their pasturelands.” It is well known that this verse has long been absent from the Hebrew manuscripts, as both the Masorah and Rabbi David Kimchi note. Indeed, learned men generally believe that it was absent in Jerome’s age as well; for the way in which we observe it in the Vulgate books is a word-for-word translation from the Greek of the Seventy (*τῶν LXX*, “of the Seventy”).

“Martianay discusses this matter at length in his annotation, together with the sacred critics and interpreters. As for the action of the holy Father, I am almost persuaded that he could not have taken it from the Seventy unless he had first noticed that this verse was absent from the Hebrew. If he observed this, I can scarcely believe that he would have failed to inform the reader of the lacuna in the Hebrew archetype in the preface or elsewhere when the opportunity arose. Yet it is even less credible that he would have preferred to supply the passage from the Seventy when he could have supplied it much more properly from Aquila and Symmachus.”]

And from the tribe of Gad, cities of refuge: Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim, Heshbon, and Jazer, four towns with their pasturelands.

[Col. 0499A] All the towns of the descendants of Merari, by their families and clans, were twelve. Thus all the towns of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the Israelites were forty-eight, together with their pasturelands, each distributed according to its families.

[C. CII.] The Lord [Vulgate adds: God] gave Israel all the land that he had sworn to their fathers that he would give them. They possessed it and lived in it.

[B. XXX.] The Lord gave them peace on every side with all the surrounding nations. None of their enemies dared resist them; instead, they were all brought under their authority. Not one word of all that he had promised to grant them fell void; everything was fulfilled in reality.

[Col. 0499B] [T. X, C. CIII, Chapter XXII.] At that time Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, and said to them:

“You have done everything that Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded you. You have also obeyed me in everything, and you have not abandoned your brothers for a long time, up to this present day, guarding the commandment of the Lord your God. Since, therefore, the Lord your God has given your brothers rest and peace, as he promised, return and go to your tents and to the land of your possession which Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave you beyond the Jordan.

“Only take great care to observe and fulfill in action the commandment and law that Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded you: to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to observe his commandments, to cling to him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul.”

Joshua blessed them and dismissed them, and they returned to their tents.

Moses had given the half-tribe of Manasseh its possession in Bashan; therefore, to the remaining half Joshua gave a share among their other brothers beyond the Jordan, on its western side.

When he dismissed them to their tents and blessed them, he said to them:

“Return to your dwellings [Hebrew: houses] with great wealth and riches, with silver and gold, bronze and iron, and abundant clothing. Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brothers.”

The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh returned and departed from the Israelites [Col. 0499D] at Shiloh, which is situated in Canaan, to enter Gilead, the land of their possession, which they had obtained according to the command of the Lord through Moses.

[B. XXXI, C. CIV.] When they came to the mounds of the Jordan in the land of Canaan, they built beside the Jordan an altar of immense size.

When the Israelites heard this, and reliable messengers reported to them that the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh had built an altar in the land of Canaan, on the mounds of the Jordan, opposite the Israelites [Hebrew: at the crossing of the Israelites], they all assembled at Shiloh to go up and fight against them.

Meanwhile they sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, together with ten leaders, one from each tribe, to the land of Gilead. They came to the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead and said to them:

“This is what the entire people of the Lord say: What is this transgression? Why have you abandoned the Lord, the God of Israel, building a sacrilegious altar and withdrawing from his worship? Was the sin at Baal-peor [Hebrew: Peor] not enough for you, when the stain of that crime remains upon us to this day and many of the people perished?

“And today you have abandoned the Lord; tomorrow his wrath will rage against all Israel. But if you think that the land of your possession is unclean, cross over to the land in which the Lord’s tabernacle is, and live among us. Only do not withdraw from the Lord or from our fellowship by building an altar apart from the altar of the Lord our God.

“Did not Achan son of Zerah violate the commandment of the Lord, and did not his wrath fall upon all the people of Israel? He was one man; and would that he alone had perished in his crime!”

[Col. 0500B] The descendants of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of the Israelite delegation:

“The most mighty God, the Lord; the most mighty God, the Lord: he knows, and Israel too shall understand: if we built this altar with intent to rebel, may he not preserve us but punish us now. And if we did this with the intention of offering burnt offerings, sacrifices, and peace offerings upon it, let him himself investigate and judge.

“But we did it rather with this thought and purpose: that tomorrow your sons might say to our sons, ‘What have you to do with the Lord, the God of Israel? The Lord has set the Jordan as a boundary between us and you, sons of Reuben and sons of Gad; therefore you have no share in the Lord.’ By this means your sons might turn our sons away from fearing the Lord.

“Therefore we thought it better and said: Let us build an altar for ourselves, not for burnt offerings or for the offering of sacrifices, but as a testimony between us and you, and between our descendants and your descendants, so that we may serve the Lord and have the right to offer burnt offerings, sacrifices, and peace offerings, and so that your sons may never say tomorrow to our sons, ‘You have no share in the Lord.’

“If they wish to say this, our sons will answer them: ‘Behold the altar of the Lord which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings or sacrifice, but as a testimony between us and you.’

“Far be it from us to commit this crime—to withdraw from the Lord and abandon his ways by building an altar for burnt offerings, sacrifices, and offerings apart from the altar of the Lord our God, which has been built before his tabernacle.”

When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the Israelite delegation who were with him heard this, they were appeased and gladly accepted the words of the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to them:

“Now we know that the Lord is with us, because you are free from this transgression and have delivered the Israelites from the Lord’s hand.”

Then he and the leaders returned from the descendants of Reuben and Gad, from the land of Gilead, at the borders of Canaan, to the Israelites and reported to them. The report pleased all who heard it.

The Israelites praised [Hebrew: blessed] God and no longer spoke of going up against them to fight and destroy the land of their possession.

The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad called the altar they had built “Our Testimony,” because, they said, “the Lord himself is God.”

[T. XI, B. XXXII, C. CV, Chapter XXIII.] After a long time had passed, when the Lord had given Israel peace and subdued all the surrounding nations, and Joshua had grown old and was of very advanced age, Joshua summoned all Israel, the elders, leaders, commanders, and officials, and said to them:

“I am old and advanced in years. You yourselves see everything that the Lord your God has done to all the surrounding nations, and how he himself fought for you. Now, because he divided all this land among you by lot, from the eastern side of the Jordan to the Great Sea, many nations still remain.

“The Lord your God will destroy them and drive them away from before you, and you will possess their land, as he promised you. Only be very courageous and take care to observe everything written in the book of the law of Moses. Do not turn away from it either to the right or to the left, lest, after you have entered among the nations that remain among you, you swear by the name of their gods, serve them, and worship them.

“Instead, cling to the Lord your God, as you have done to this day. Then the Lord your God will remove from your presence great and very powerful nations, and no one will be able to resist you. One of you will pursue a thousand enemies, because the Lord your God himself will fight for you, as he promised.

“Take this very careful precaution: love the Lord your God. But if you wish to cling to the errors of these nations that dwell among you, to intermarry with them and form alliances of friendship, know even now that the Lord your God will not drive them out before you. They will instead become for you a pit and a snare, a stumbling block at your side, and thorns in your eyes, until he removes and destroys you from this excellent land which he has given you.”

[C. CVI.] “Behold, today I am entering upon the way of all the earth, and with all your heart and all your soul you shall know that, of all the words which the Lord your God promised to grant you, not one has failed.

“Just as he fulfilled in action what he promised and all good things came to you, so he will bring upon you every evil thing with which he threatened you, until he removes and destroys you from this excellent land which he has given you, because you have violated the covenant of the Lord your God which he made with you, served foreign gods, and worshiped them. The anger of the Lord will rise against you quickly and swiftly, and you will be removed from this excellent land which he has given you.”

[Note: [Col. 0501] Through the carelessness of the copyists, the following words were omitted from the Vulgate books: “and with all your heart.” Yet the Hebrew text and the Greek text both contain them.]

[B. XXXIII, Chapter XXIV.] Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem and summoned the elders, leaders, judges, and officials. They stood in the presence of God [Vulgate: the Lord], and he spoke to the people as follows:

“Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Beyond the River your fathers lived from the beginning—Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor—and they served foreign gods. Therefore I took your father Abraham from the region of Mesopotamia and brought him into the land of Canaan. I multiplied his descendants and gave him Isaac; and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau.

“To Esau I gave Mount Seir as a possession; but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt. I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with many signs and wonders. I brought you and your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and cavalry as far as the Red Sea.

“But the Israelites cried out to the Lord [Hebrew lacks this]. He placed darkness between you and the Egyptians, brought the sea over them, and covered them. Your eyes saw everything that I did in Egypt. You lived in the wilderness for a long time.

“I brought you into the land of the Amorite who lived beyond the Jordan. When they fought against you, I delivered them into your hands, and you possessed their land and killed them.

“Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you; but I was unwilling to listen to him. On the contrary, through him I blessed you and delivered you from his hand.

“You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The men of Jericho fought against you, as did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites; and I delivered them into your hands.

[C. CVII.] “I sent hornets before you, and I drove them [Hebrew: they drove them] from their places—the two kings of the Amorites—not by your sword or your bow. I gave you a land for which you had not labored, and towns which you had not built, so that you might live in them; vineyards and olive groves which you had not planted [Hebrew: from which you eat].

“Now therefore fear the Lord and serve him with a perfect and most sincere heart. Remove the gods whom your fathers served in Mesopotamia and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.

“But if it seems evil to you to serve the Lord, you are given a choice: choose today what seems good to you and whom you ought chiefly to serve—whether the gods whom your fathers served in Mesopotamia, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But I and my household will serve the Lord.”

The people answered:

“Far be it from us to abandon the Lord and serve foreign gods. The Lord [Hebrew: For the Lord] our God himself brought us and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. He performed great signs before our eyes and guarded us throughout the whole way by which we traveled and among all the peoples through whom we passed. He drove out all the nations, including the Amorite who inhabited the land into which we entered. Therefore we too will serve the Lord, because he is our God.”

[C. CIX.] Joshua said to the people:

“You will not be able to serve the Lord, for he is a holy God and a strong, jealous God; he will not forgive your crimes and sins. If you abandon the Lord and serve foreign gods, he will turn against you and afflict and overthrow you, after having done you good.”

The people said to Joshua:

“No, it will not be as you say; we will serve the Lord.”

Joshua said to the people:

“You are witnesses that you yourselves have chosen the Lord, to serve him.”

They answered:

“We are witnesses.”

“Now therefore,” he said, “remove the foreign gods from among you and incline your hearts to the Lord God of Israel.”

The people said to Joshua:

“We will serve the Lord our God and obey his commands.”

Therefore on that day Joshua made a covenant and set before the people commands and judgments at Shechem.

[C. CX.] He wrote all these words in the book of the law of the Lord. He took a very large stone and placed it beneath the oak that was in the sanctuary of the Lord. He said to all the people:

“Behold, this stone will be a witness for you, for it has heard all the words of the Lord which he spoke to you, lest you later wish to deny them and lie to the Lord your God.”

Then he dismissed the people, each one to his possession.

After this Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at the age of one hundred and ten years. They buried him within the boundaries of his possession at Timnath-serah, which is situated in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

Israel served the Lord throughout all the days of Joshua and of the elders who lived for a long time after Joshua and who knew all the works that the Lord had done for Israel.

The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, they also buried at Shechem, in the portion of the field that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for one hundred young sheep; and it became the possession of the descendants of Joseph.

Eleazar son of Aaron also died, and they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.

[Col. 0503] Here ends the Book of Joshua son of Nun.

[Col. 0503]

[BOOK OF JUDGES]

[CAPITULATIONS OF THE BOOK OF JUDGES]

TITLES OF THE BOOK OF JUDGES

[Col. 0503C] I. After the death of Joshua, the Israelites consulted the Lord about who should be their military leader, and the Lord answered: Judah. Adonibezek is captured by Israel; then Kiriath-arba and the other towns. Concerning Caleb and Achsah his daughter: concerning the field she requested, and Gaza; concerning the destruction of the sons of Anak; concerning Bethel, Luz, and its treacherous informant. Because the inhabitants of these towns were not destroyed, they later returned and oppressed Israel; then the angel of the Lord came and reproached them while they wept.

II. Here Joshua is mentioned as having just died, and after the death of the devout elders a new and dissolute generation arose which did not worship God at all. By serving the Baals they provoked the Lord to anger, and he delivered them into the hands of their enemies. Concerning the five satraps of the Philistines who remained; concerning the associated descendants of Canaan; concerning Chushan-rishathaim of Mesopotamia; and concerning Othniel, king of Israel.

III. The Israelites sinned, and the Lord delivered them to Eglon king of Moab. They cried out to the Lord, and he raised up Ehud son of Gera, who killed the fat Eglon and ten thousand Moabites. Concerning Shamgar son of Anath, who killed six hundred men with an ox-goad. They sinned again and were delivered to King Jabin; Deborah and Barak, leading an army, killed Jabin. Concerning Jael, the wife of Heber, who killed Sisera with a tent peg. And the song of Deborah and Barak.

VI. Having sinned again, they were delivered into the hand of Midian. They were humbled and cried out to the Lord; and he sent them a prophet. He sent them a prophet to rebuke them. The angel of the Lord came to Gideon while he was threshing grain; Gideon recounted the evils that had befallen him, and heard that the Lord would deliver Israel through him. Concerning the sacrifice offered; and the Lord said to him by night that, after destroying his father’s altar of Baal and cutting down the sacred grove, he should offer the sacrifice of his father’s seven-year-old bull. Concerning the assembly and the Midianites. Gideon placed a fleece on the threshing floor and sought a sign. The Lord said to him: “The people with you are too numerous.” They were tested at the waters, and three hundred worthy men were found. At the Lord’s command he went down into the camp and heard a man recounting a dream about the outcome of the battle. Concerning Salmana and Zebah. Concerning Oreb. Concerning the men of Succoth, the tower of Penuel, and the one hundred and twenty thousand slain. Concerning the golden earrings Gideon requested from the spoil; and Gideon’s peaceful death.

V. The Israelites sinned again, and Abimelech, Gideon’s natural son, conspired with the men of Shechem. Hiring vagrants, he killed Gideon’s seventy sons; of these, Jonatha, the youngest, was hidden, later came forward, and spoke a parable against them. Concerning Gaal son of Ebed, who came with his brothers to Shechem; and Zebul, the city’s ruler, secretly sent word to Abimelech. They joined battle. Concerning the tower of the Shechemites, where a thousand people perished by smoke and fire. Concerning the people of Thebez and the very strong tower in its midst; when Abimelech approached it, a woman threw a fragment of a millstone and killed him.

[Col. 0505A] VI. After Abimelech, Tola arose; after him, Jair. The Israelites sinned against God again and were delivered to the Philistines. Greatly afflicted, they cried out to the Lord, saying: “We have sinned against you.” They did so a second time, and he had mercy on them. Concerning Jephthah the Gileadite, appointed leader over Israel. He sends messengers to the Philistines. Concerning his rash vow. Concerning the victory in battle and the death of his daughter. Concerning the revolt in Ephraim. After Jephthah, Ibzan arose, then Elon and Abdon. Again concerning Israel’s sin.

VII. Concerning Manoah, to whom an angel appeared. Concerning the birth of Samson, who, when grown, took a wife from the daughters of the Philistines. Concerning the lion he killed and the honeycomb. He proposed a riddle, which his wife disclosed; after he had dismissed her, she was given to another. In anger Samson caught foxes, tied them together, [Col. 0505B] and set fire beneath them, burning the crops. With an ass’s jawbone he killed a thousand men, and water came forth for him when he was thirsty. Concerning the woman and the gates at Gaza. Concerning Delilah, who took him. He was brought out of prison to provide amusement and pulled down the temple upon them and himself.

[Col. 0506A] VIII. Concerning Micah and the eleven hundred silver pieces. Concerning the carved and cast image. Concerning another young man from Bethlehem who became priest in Micah’s house. Concerning the descendants of Dan going to Laish and taking away the priest and the idols. Concerning Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Moses, priest of the idol.

IX. Concerning the Levite who took a wife from Bethlehem in Judah. When she returned to her father’s house, her husband followed her and was warmly received. Concerning their joy and journey. Concerning the wicked men of Gibeah of Benjamin, who desired the man and the woman. Concerning the woman who was abused, exhausted, and died. Concerning her corpse, divided into twelve parts and sent throughout the twelve tribes. Because of this act the whole people assembled and declared war against the tribe of Benjamin. They were defeated once and again; the third time they emerged victorious. Moved to repentance, they wept and grieved that one tribe had perished, and, since six hundred men remained, they deliberated how the fallen tribe might be restored.

[Note: [Col. 0505C] The Palatine manuscript customarily calls these “chapters”; it combines the first and second under a single numeral and in continuous sequence, where it also reads: “The angel of the Lord reproves them for their transgression,” and so forth.]

BRIEF OUTLINE OF THE BOOK OF JUDGES

[Col. 0505]

[Col. 0505B] I. Judah is chosen as military leader.

II. The Lord reproves the people for their transgression concerning idols.

III. After the death of Joshua, the Israelites did evil in the sight of the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0505C] The Palatine manuscript omits the rest of the wording: “whom he delivered to their enemies as spoil.”] He delivered them to their enemies as spoil.

IV. Judges are raised up by the Lord for Israel’s deliverance. They themselves also rejected them; the Lord left the nations in place so that Israel might be tested through them.

[Col. 0505C] V. These are the nations whom the Lord left behind. [Note: [Col. 0506C] Conversely, the same Palatine manuscript adds: “to instruct them through Israel.”]

VI. Because of their transgression concerning idols, they were taken captive by Chushan, king of Mesopotamia.

VII. Again, because of their evil deeds, they were delivered to Eglon king of Moab. Ehud killed him in his upper room by a stratagem; he also killed ten thousand Moabites, and the land rested [Note: [Col. 0506C] In the Palatine manuscript, only “thirty years” are stated.] eighty years.

VIII. Shamgar, who killed six hundred men with an ox-goad.

[Col. 0506B] IX. The steadfastness of Jael, who drove a tent peg into Sisera’s temple. The song of Barak and Deborah follows.

X. After the people’s customary transgressions, the angel of the Lord appeared to Gideon and encouraged him to fight. He also overthrew Baal and offered a sacrifice to the Lord. His three hundred men lapped the water like dogs. Later he too transgressed with Israel.

XI. Concerning the weak reign of Abimelech, who died from a fragment of a millstone. [Note: [Col. 0506C] The Palatine manuscript adds: “He killed his daughter and established an evil custom,” which they immediately refer to Jephthah, to whom those matters belong.]

[Col. 0506C] XII. The reign of Jair.

XIII. The reign of Jephthah. He killed his daughter and established an evil custom.

XIV. Ibzan the judge.

XV. Manoah the judge, whose famous son was Samson.

XVI. Micah’s transgression.

XVII. Concerning the Levite youth recognized at Micah’s house and recalled by the tribe of Dan to serve as priest of the idol.

XVIII. The Levite whose wife suffered the outrage.

CAPITULATIONS OF THE BOOK OF JUDGES

[Col. 0505]

[Col. 0505D] I. Adonibezek, fleeing, was captured after the tips of his hands and feet had been cut off.

II. The inhabitants of Debir, whose former name was Kiriath-sepher, that is, “city of letters.”

III. The descendants of the Kenite, relatives of Moses, went up from the City of Palms with the descendants of Judah.

IV. The Benjaminites did not destroy the Jebusite inhabitants of Jerusalem.

V. He called the city Luz, which is so called to the present day.

[Col. 0506D] VI. Asher did not destroy the inhabitants of Acco.

VII. When the angel of the Lord spoke to the Israelites, they raised their voices and wept.

VIII. Joshua dismissed the people, and the Israelites went each to his own possession.

IX. The Lord was angry with Israel and delivered them into the hands of plunderers.

X. The Lord’s anger burned against Israel, and he said: “Because this nation has broken my covenant, I will not destroy the nations.”

[Col. 0507A] XI. The Lord left these nations and did not quickly overthrow them.

XII. These are the nations whom the Lord left behind, to instruct Israel through them.

XIII. Therefore the Israelites lived among the Canaanites.

XIV. Othniel son of Kenaz, the people’s deliverer.

XV. Ehud son of Gera, son of Gemini, the people’s deliverer; he used both hands as though they were his right hand.

XVI. Shamgar son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistine men.

XVII. Deborah the prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, was judging the people.

XVIII. Therefore Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.

[Col. 0507B] XIX. It was reported to Sisera that Barak had gone up Mount Tabor.

XX. Jael went out to meet Sisera and said: “Come in to me, my lord.”

XXI. The song of Deborah, which she sang with Barak.

XXII. The Israelites were delivered into the hand of Midian for seven years.

XXIII. Israel cries out to the Lord, seeking help against the Midianites.

XXIV. The angel of the Lord sat beneath the oak that was in Ophrah.

XXV. Gideon asks for a sign in the fleece.

XXVI. Concerning the three hundred men tested at the waters.

XXVII. Gideon prayed to the Lord, while a Midianite recounted to his companion a dream about a loaf baked under the ashes.

[Col. 0507C] XXVIII. The three hundred men, breaking their jars and sounding their trumpets, cried out: “The sword of the Lord and of Gideon!”

XXIX. The Lord sent a sword throughout the entire camp, and they slaughtered one another in mutual carnage.

XXX. Ephraim pursued Midian, carrying the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon.

XXXI. “Is not the cluster of grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?”

XXXII. Gideon asked Zebah and Zalmunna about their brothers, whom they had killed at Tabor.
