They do not judge the orphan,

and the widow’s case does not come before them.

Therefore the Lord of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, says:

Ah! I will take comfort over my enemies,

and I will avenge myself on my foes.

[Col. 0775C] And I will turn my hand against you,

and I will smelt away your dross to purity,

and remove all your tin.

And I will restore your judges as they were at first,

and your counselors as in the beginning.

After this you will be called the city of the just,

the faithful city.

Zion will be redeemed through judgment,

and they will restore her through righteousness;

and he will crush the wicked and sinners together,

and those who abandoned the Lord will be consumed.

For they will be ashamed because of the idols to which they sacrificed,

and you will be disgraced because of the gardens that you chose,

when you become like an oak [Alternative: “for they will be like a terebinth”] with falling leaves,

and like a garden without water.

And your strength will be like a spark of tow,

and your work like a flame,

and both will burn together,

and there will be no one to extinguish them.

## Chapter II

The word [Note: [Col. 0775D] Note that, according to Jerome in his Commentary, this is called the second vision and that Isaiah’s vision begins here. MART.] that Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw

concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

And it will come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the house

of the Lord will be prepared at the summit of the mountains,

and it will be raised above the hills,

and all nations will flow to it.

[Col. 0776A] And many peoples will go and say:

“Come, let us ascend to the mountain of the Lord,

and to the house of the God of Jacob,

and he will teach us his ways,

and we have walked in his paths;

for from Zion the law will go forth,

and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.”

And he will judge the nations,

and rebuke many peoples,

and they will beat their swords into ploughshares,

and their spears into pruning-hooks.

Nation will not lift up sword against nation,

nor will they train for war any longer.

House of Jacob, come,

let us walk in the light of the Lord.

For you have rejected your people, the house of Jacob,

because they have been filled as [Vulgate omits “as”] formerly,

and they have had diviners like the Philistines,

and they have clung to foreign children.

[Note: [Col. 0775D] Augustine’s Speculum marks three verses, from the word “they have clung” up to “Its land is filled with idols.” But after carefully examining the manuscript codices of Jerome’s version and the Commentary of the same holy Doctor, we judged that four should be set out: for the division of the sentence and clarity of meaning seem to require that many. If anyone is troubled that we sometimes omit the verse numbers [Col. 0776D] assigned in the Speculum, let him remember that they were corrupted by the error of copyists, as the different numbers assigned in different copies of the Speculum prove. MART.] Its land is filled with silver and gold,

[Col. 0776B] and there is no end to its treasures;

and its land is filled with horses,

and its chariots are innumerable.

And its land is filled with idols:

they worship the work of their hands,

what their fingers have made.

And the human being is bowed down, and the man is humbled:

therefore do not forgive them.

Enter into the rock;

hide in a pit in the ground from the face of the fear of the Lord

and from the glory of his majesty.

[Note: [Col. 0776D] This is how the copies of the Canon read, and likewise the Commentaries in the older manuscript books. Others, both printed and manuscript, read: “the eyes of the exalted man.” The Hebrew letter has: “the eyes of the elevation of man.” MART.] The eyes of the exalted man are humbled,

and the height of men will be bowed down,

but the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.

For the day of the Lord of hosts will be against every proud and lofty person,

and against every arrogant person, and he will be humbled.

And against all the lofty and upright cedars of Lebanon,

[Col. 0776C] and against all the oaks of Bashan.

And against all the lofty mountains,

and against all the raised hills.

And against every high tower,

and against every fortified wall.

And against all the ships of Tarshish,

and against everything beautiful to behold.

And the loftiness of human beings will be bowed down,

and the height of men will be humbled,

and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day;

and the idols will be utterly crushed.

And they will enter into the caves of the rocks and the hollows

of the earth,

from the face of the Lord’s terror and from the glory of his majesty,

when he rises to strike the earth.

On that day a man will cast away his silver idols

and his golden images, which he had made for himself to worship moles and bats.

And he will enter into the fissures of rocks and the caverns

of stones,

[Col. 0776D] from the face of the Lord’s terror and from the glory of his majesty,

when he rises to strike the earth.

Therefore cease from the human being, whose breath is in his nostrils,

[Col. 0777A] for he is regarded as exalted.

## Chapter III

For behold, the sovereign Lord of hosts

will remove from Jerusalem and from Judah the strong and the mighty,

all the strength of bread and all the strength of water;

the mighty man and the warrior,

the judge and the prophet,

the diviner and the elder;

the commander of fifty,

and the honorable man in appearance;

the wise counselor among architects [Alternative: architect],

and the skilled interpreter of mystical speech.

And I will give children as their princes,

and effeminate men will rule over them.

And the people will rush together, man against man,

each one against his neighbor;

the child will become insolent against the elder,

and the lowly against the noble.

For a man will seize his brother, a member of his father’s household,

[Col. 0777B] saying: “You have clothing; be our prince,

and let this ruin be under your hand.”

He will answer on that day, saying:

“I am not a physician,

and there is neither bread nor clothing in my house.

Do not appoint me as prince of the people.”

For Jerusalem has collapsed, and Judah has fallen,

because their tongue and their inventions are against

the Lord,

to provoke the eyes of his majesty.

The recognition of their faces has answered them,

and they have proclaimed their sin like Sodom,

and have not concealed it.

Woe to their soul,

for evils have been repaid to them.

Tell the just man that it is well,

for he will eat the fruit of his inventions.

Woe to the wicked man, for evil;

for the recompense of his hands will be done to him.

[Col. 0777C] My people have been stripped by their exactors,

and women have ruled over them [Alternative: ruled them].

My people, those who call you blessed deceive you,

and destroy the way of your steps.

The Lord stands to judge,

and stands to judge the peoples.

The Lord will come to judgment with the elders of his people

and its princes.

For you have devoured the vineyard [Alternative: add “my vineyard”];

the plunder of the poor is in your houses.

Why do you crush my people,

and grind the faces of the poor? says the Lord God

of hosts.

And the Lord said:

Because the daughters of Zion have become exalted,

and have walked with outstretched necks,

and gone about with glances of their eyes,

and with gestures;

they walked along, and with measured steps

advanced on their feet:

the Lord will make the crown of the daughters of Zion bald,

[Col. 0777D] and the Lord [Alternative: omits “the Lord”] will uncover their hair.

On that day the Lord will remove the ornament of their footwear,

the little crescents, the necklaces, the pendants, the bracelets,

and the headdresses;

the hair ornaments, the anklets, the serpent-shaped ornaments,

the perfume containers, and the earrings;

the rings and the jewels hanging on the forehead;

the changes of clothing, the cloaks, the linen garments, and the needles;

[Col. 0778A] the mirrors, the fine linen, the headbands, and the summer garments.

And instead of a pleasant fragrance there will be stench;

instead of a belt, a cord;

instead of curled hair, baldness;

instead of a breast-band, sackcloth.

Your handsomest men will also fall by the sword,

and your strong men in battle.

And her gates will mourn and lament,

and she, desolate [Alternative: add “the city itself”], will sit on the ground.

## Chapter IV

And seven women will seize one man on that day, saying:

“We will eat our own bread,

and wear our own clothing;

only let your name be invoked over us;

take away our disgrace.”

On that day the branch of the Lord will be in magnificence and glory,

and the fruit of the earth will be exalted,

and a cause of rejoicing for those who have been saved from Israel.

[Col. 0778B] And it will come to pass: Everyone who is left in Zion

and remains in Jerusalem

will be called holy,

everyone who has been written among the living

in Jerusalem.

If the Lord washes away the filth of the daughters of Zion,

and cleanses the blood of Jerusalem from her midst,

by the spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning [Alternative: combustion].

And the Lord will create over every place of Mount Zion

and where he has been invoked,

a cloud by day,

and smoke and the brightness of a flaming fire by night;

for over all glory there will be protection.

And there will be a tent as a shade by day from the heat,

and as a refuge and hiding place from storm and

rain.

## Chapter V

I will sing [Alternative: add “now”] for my beloved

the song of my cousin concerning his vineyard.

A vineyard belonged to my beloved,

on a fertile hill.

And he fenced it,

and removed stones from it,

and planted it as a choice vine.

[Note: [Col. 0777D] Saint Jerome reports in his Commentary that Symmachus translated “choice,” and there he himself also appears to prefer “the vineyard of Sorek.”] And he built a tower in its midst,

and constructed a winepress in it.

And he expected it to produce grapes,

but it produced wild grapes.

Now therefore, inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah,

judge between me and my vineyard.

What more ought I to have done for my vineyard

that I have not done for it [Alternative: “that I did not do for it”]?

Or was it that I expected it to produce grapes,

but it produced wild grapes?

And now I will show you what I will do to my vineyard:

I will remove its hedge,

and it will be for plundering;

I will tear down its wall,

and it will be for trampling.

And I will make it desolate:

it will not be pruned,

and it will not be dug;

thorns and briars will rise up;

and I will command the clouds not to rain upon it.

For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel,

and the man of Judah is his delightful shoot.

And I expected him to execute judgment,

but behold, iniquity;

and righteousness,

but behold, a cry.

Woe to you who join house to house,

and connect field to field, up to the boundary of the place.

Will you alone dwell in the midst of the earth [Alternative:

over the earth]?

In my ears are the words of [Note: [Col. 0777D] Thus read all the older and better manuscripts, in accordance with what is read in the Hebrew. In the Canon of Saint-Germain: “In my ears are these things, says the Lord of hosts.” Jerome himself teaches us that this reading is corrupt in his explanation of this passage of Isaiah: “For what we translated according to the Hebrew, ‘In my ears are [the words] of the Lord of hosts’—that is, the words which the Lord spoke still resound in my ears—the Septuagint translated …” Whatever, therefore, conflicts with the printed reading of ours undoubtedly conflicts also with the mind and words of Saint Jerome. MART.] the Lord of hosts:

Unless many houses become desolate,

great and beautiful,

without an inhabitant.

[Col. 0779A] For ten acres of vineyard will produce one little jar,

and thirty measures of seed will produce three measures.

Woe to you who rise early to watch for drunkenness,

and drink until evening, so that you burn with wine.

Lyre, harp, tambourine, flute, and wine are in your feasts;

but you do not regard the work of the Lord,

nor consider the works of his hands.

Therefore my people have been led captive,

because they had no knowledge.

And its nobles have perished from hunger,

and its multitude has dried up from thirst.

Therefore the underworld has enlarged its soul,

and opened its mouth without any limit.

And its strong men and its people,

and its lofty and glorious ones, will descend to it.

And the human being will be bowed down,

and the man will be humbled,

and the eyes of the lofty will be brought low.

And the Lord of hosts will be exalted in judgment,

and the holy God will be sanctified in righteousness.

And lambs will feed according to their order,

and strangers will eat the desolate places turned into abundance.

Woe to you who drag iniquity with cords of vanity,

and sin as though with a cart rope.

You who say: “Let him hasten,

and let his work come quickly, so that we may see it;

[Col. 0779B] let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel approach and come,

so that we may know it.”

Woe to you who call evil good and good evil,

who make darkness light and light darkness,

who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter.

Woe to you who are wise in your own eyes,

and prudent in your own sight.

Woe to you who are powerful at drinking wine,

and mighty men at mixing drunkenness.

You who justify the wicked for gifts,

and take away the righteousness of the just from him.

Therefore, just as the tongue of fire devours stubble,

and the heat of flame consumes,

so their root will be like ashes,

and their shoot will rise like dust.

For they rejected the law of the Lord of hosts,

and blasphemed the utterance of the Holy One of Israel.

Therefore the anger of the Lord was kindled against his people,

and he stretched out his hand over them and struck them;

and the mountains were shaken,

and their corpses became like dung

in the midst of the streets.

In all this his anger has not turned away,

but his hand is still extended.

And he will raise a sign among nations from far away,

[Col. 0779C] and whistle for it from the ends of the earth;

and behold, it will come swiftly, speedily.

There is none failing or weary among them;

he will not sleep, nor slumber;

the belt of his loins will not be loosened,

nor will the strap of his sandal be broken.

His arrows are sharp,

and all his bows are drawn.

The hooves of his horses are like flint,

and his wheels like the force of a storm.

His roar is like that of a lion;

he will roar like young lions.

He will growl and seize the prey;

he will carry it away,

and there will be no one to rescue it.

And he will roar over it on that day like the roar of the sea.

We will look toward the land,

and behold, darkness of tribulation;

the light has been darkened in its gloom.

## Chapter VI

In the year in which King Uzziah died,

I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and exalted,

[Col. 0780A] and the things beneath him filled the temple.

Seraphim stood above it:

six wings for one and six wings for the other.

With two they covered his face,

with two they covered his feet,

and with two they flew.

And one cried out to the other and said:

“Holy, holy, holy, Lord of hosts;

the whole earth is full of his glory.”

And the lintels of the pivots were shaken by the voice

of the one crying out,

and the house was filled with smoke. And I said:

“Woe is me, for I have been silent,

because I am a man of unclean lips,

and I dwell [Alternative: “will dwell”] in the midst of a people

with unclean lips,

and I have seen the King, the Lord of hosts, with my eyes.”

And one of the Seraphim flew to me,

and in his hand was a coal which he had taken with tongs from

the altar.

And he touched my mouth and said:

“Behold, this has touched [Alternative: “I have touched”] your lips,

and your iniquity will be removed,

and your sin will be cleansed.”

And I heard the voice of the Lord saying:

“Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said:

[Col. 0780B] “Here am I; send me.” And he said:

“Go, and say to this people:

‘Hear by hearing [Alternative: ‘Hear with your ears’], and do not understand;

and see the vision [Alternative: ‘with sight’], and do not know.

Make the heart of this people blind,

and make their ears heavy,

and close their eyes,

lest perhaps [Note: [Col. 0779C] In the Canon of Saint-Germain the plural number is found according to the Septuagint: “let them see, let them hear,” and so forth. But that this is a copyist’s error is clearly proved not only by the Canon of the Church of Carcassonne, together with many [Col. 0780C] manuscript codices of the sacred books, but also by the third book of Saint Jerome’s Commentaries, where these matters are discussed at length. MART.] they see with their eyes,

and hear with their ears,

and understand with their heart [Alternative: omits “their”],

and are converted,

and I heal them.’”

And I said:

“How long, Lord?”

And he said:

“Until the cities are desolated without an inhabitant,

and the houses without a human being,

and the land is left desolate.

And the Lord will remove the people far away,

and what had been abandoned in the midst of the land will be multiplied.

And there will still be a tenth in it,

and it will turn again,

and will be for display like [Alternative: “again be for plundering like, etc.”] a terebinth,

and like an oak that spreads its branches [Alternative: “casts down its fruit”].

[Col. 0780C] The holy seed will be what remains standing in it.”

## Chapter VII

And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah,

that Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to fight against it;

and they could not conquer it.

And they reported to the house of David, saying:

“Syria has rested upon [Alternative: “has agreed … with”] Ephraim.”

And his heart was shaken,

and the heart of his people,

as the trees of the forests are shaken before the wind.

And the Lord said to Isaiah:

“Go out to meet Ahaz,

you and your son Jasub, who has been left,

at the end of the conduit of the upper pool,

on the road to the Fullers’ Field.

And you shall say to him:

‘See that you remain silent.

Do not fear,

[Col. 0781A] and do not let your heart be afraid because of the two tails of these smoking firebrands,

because of the anger of the fury of Rezin [Note: [Col. 0781D] The Hebrew does not add “king,” nor does Jerome read that word in the Commentary.] king of Syria and of the son of Remaliah,

because Syria has taken counsel against you for evil [Alternative: “the worst”],

Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, saying:

“Let us go up against Judah;

let us stir it up and tear it away [Alternative: “pull it away”] to ourselves,

and set the son of Tabeel as king in its midst.”

Thus says the Lord God:

“This shall not stand, and it shall not be.

But the head of Syria is Damascus,

and the head of Damascus is Rezin.

And for another sixty-five years

Ephraim will cease to be a people.

And the head of Ephraim is Samaria,

and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah.

If you do not believe,

[Col. 0781B] you will not remain.”’”

And the Lord continued to speak to Ahaz, saying:

“Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God,

either in the depth of the underworld

or in the height above.”

And Ahaz said:

“I will not ask,

and I will not tempt the Lord.”

And he said:

“Hear, then, house of David.

Is it not enough for you to be troublesome to human beings,

that you are also troublesome to my God?

Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign.

Behold, a virgin will conceive and bear a son [Alternative: omits “a son”],

and [Note: [Col. 0781D] Many manuscripts give a corrupt reading here. Some read “and you will call”; others, “and he will be called.” But in fewer, though more accurate, copies we read “and you will call.” This passage is too important in Jerome for us to omit it. Thus you should read him explaining it in Book III of the Commentaries on Isaiah: “What follows,” he says, “‘and you will call his name Emmanuel,’ the Septuagint and the other three likewise translated; in Matthew it is written ‘they will call,’ although that name is not found in the Hebrew … The word CARATHI [Col. 0782D] () which all have interpreted ‘and you will call,’ may be understood as ‘and he will call,’ namely, that the virgin who will conceive and bear will give Christ this name. In many testimonies which the Evangelists or Apostles took from the ancient books, one must carefully observe that they did not follow the order of the words but the meaning. Thus in the present passage, instead of ‘she will conceive in the womb,’ Matthew wrote ‘she will have in the womb,’ and instead of ‘you will call,’ ‘they will call.’ Much remains to be said about [unprinted Hebrew], Carathi, which Jerome read in place of the current [unprinted Hebrew], Carath, or Vecarath; but we will discuss these matters in the notes to the Commentary. MART.] you will call his name Emmanuel.

He will eat butter and honey,

so that he may know how to reject evil and choose good.

For before the child knows how to reject evil and choose good,

[Col. 0781C] the land that you detest will be abandoned before

its two kings.

The Lord will bring upon you, and upon your people,

and upon your father’s house,

days such as have not come since the days of the separation

of Ephraim from Judah,

through the king of the Assyrians.

And it will come to pass on that day:

The Lord will whistle for the fly that is at the farthest reaches of the rivers of Egypt,

and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria;

and they will come and rest

in all the ravines of the valleys,

and in the clefts of the rocks,

and in all the thickets,

and in every opening.

On that day the Lord will shave with a hired razor,

with those who are beyond the river,

with the king of the Assyrians,

the head and the hair of the feet,

and he will remove the entire beard.

And it will come to pass on that day:

[Col. 0781D] A man will nourish a cow and two sheep,

and because of the abundance of milk he will eat butter.

For everyone who is left in the midst of the land

will eat butter and honey.

And it will come to pass on that day:

[Col. 0782A] Every place where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand pieces of silver

will become thorns and briars.

They will enter there with arrows and bow.

For briars and thorns will be throughout the whole land,

and all the mountains that are hoed with a hoe—

fear of briars and thorns will not come there.

And it will become pasture for cattle,

and a place for the trampling of sheep.

## Chapter VIII

And the Lord said to me:

“Take for yourself a large book,

and write in it with a human stylus:

‘Quickly strip the spoils;

hasten to plunder.’”

And I took for myself faithful witnesses,

Uriah the priest and Zechariah, son of Barachiah.

And I approached the prophetess,

and she conceived and bore a son.

And the Lord said to me:

“Call his name ‘Hasten to strip the spoils’

[Alternative: “Strip the spoils”];

[Col. 0782B] ‘Hasten to plunder.’

For before the child knows how to call his father and

his mother,

the strength of Damascus will be taken away,

and the spoils of Samaria, before the king of the Assyrians.”

And the Lord continued to speak to me, saying:

“Because this people rejected the waters of Shiloah,

which flow quietly,

and chose Rezin and the son of Remaliah instead,

therefore, behold, the Lord will bring upon them

the strong and abundant waters of the river:

the king of the Assyrians and all his glory.

And he will rise over all its channels,

and flow over all its banks,

and he will go through Judah,

flooding and passing through,

and he will reach up to the neck.

And the extension of his wings will be,

filling the breadth of your land,

O Emmanuel.

Gather together, peoples, and be conquered;

[Col. 0782C] and hear, all you distant lands.

Be strengthened, and be conquered;

gird yourselves, and be conquered.

Take counsel, and it will be scattered.

Speak a word, and it will not come to pass,

because God is with us.

For thus the Lord said to me:

As he instructed me with a strong hand,

so that I would not walk in the way of this people, saying:

‘Do not call it conspiracy.’

For everything that this people says is conspiracy,

and you shall not fear its fear,

nor be afraid.

Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself.

He is your fear,

and he is your terror.

And he will be for you as a sanctuary,

but as a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense

for the two houses of Israel,

as a snare and a ruin

for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

[Col. 0782D] And many of them will stumble,

and fall,

and be crushed;

and they will be entangled,

and captured.

Bind up the testimony [Alternative: testimonies];

seal the law among my disciples.

[Col. 0783A] And I will wait for the Lord,

who hides his face from the house of Jacob,

and I will await him.

Behold, I and the children whom the Lord has given me

for a sign and portent [Alternative: “signs and portents”] in Israel,

from the Lord of hosts,

who dwells on Mount Zion.

And when they say to you:

‘Seek the mediums and diviners,

who chirp in their incantations,’

should not a people seek its God,

on behalf of the living and the dead?

Rather, seek the law and the testimony.

But if they do not speak according to this word,

there will be no morning light for them.

And he will pass through it,

and will fall,

and will hunger.

And when he is hungry, he will become angry,

and curse his king and his God,

and he will look upward;

and he will gaze upon the earth.

[Col. 0783B] And behold, tribulation and darkness,

dissolution and distress,

and pursuing gloom;

and he will not be able to flee from his distress.

## Chapter IX

At the first time the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali were lightened,

but at the last the way of the sea was made heavy,

beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.

The people who walked in darkness saw a great light.

For those dwelling in the region and shadow of death,

a light has risen.

You have multiplied the nation,

but you have not magnified its joy.

They will rejoice before you

as those who rejoice at harvest,

as conquerors exult

[Alternative: add “when the captured spoil is divided”]

when they divide the spoils.

For you have broken the yoke of its burden,

the rod of its shoulder,

and the scepter of its exactor,

as on the day of Midian.

[Col. 0783C] For every violent plunder with tumult,

and garment mixed with blood,

will be for burning and fuel for fire.

For a child has been born to us,

and a son has been given to us.

And the government has been made upon his shoulder,

and his name will be called:

Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God,

Father of the age to come,

Prince of Peace.

His government will be multiplied,

and there will be no end of peace.

He will sit upon the throne of David

and over his kingdom,

to establish it and strengthen it

in judgment and righteousness,

from now and forever.

The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this.

The Lord sent a word into Jacob,

and it fell upon Israel.

And all the people of Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria will know,

[Col. 0783D] saying in pride and greatness of heart:

“The bricks have fallen,

but we will build with squared stones.

They cut down the sycamores,

but we will replace them with cedars.”

And the Lord will raise up the enemies of Rezin against him,

and will turn his enemies into tumult:

Syria from the east,

and the Philistines from the west;

and they will devour Israel with their whole mouth.

In all this his anger has not turned away,

but his hand is still extended.

And the people have not returned to the one who struck them,

and they have not sought the Lord of hosts.

And the Lord will destroy from Israel head and tail,

the one bending down and the one restraining [Alternative: “corrupting”],

in one day.

[Col. 0784A] The long-lived and honorable man is the head,

and the prophet who teaches falsehood is the tail.

And those who bless this people will be deceivers,

and those who are blessed [Alternative: “called blessed”] will be overthrown.

Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over its young men,

and he will not have mercy on its orphans and widows.

For everyone is hypocritical and wicked,

and every mouth has spoken folly.

In all this his anger has not turned away,

but his hand is still extended.

For wickedness has been kindled like fire;

it will devour the briar and the thorn,

and it will burn in the density of the forest,

and pride will roll up in smoke.

The earth was shaken by the anger of the Lord of hosts,

and the people became like fuel for fire.

A man will not spare his brother.

He will turn to the right and hunger,

and he will eat on the left and not be satisfied.

[Col. 0784B] Each one will devour the flesh of his own arm:

Manasseh, Ephraim,

and Ephraim, Manasseh;

together they are against Judah.

In all this his anger has not turned away,

but his hand is still extended.

## Chapter X

Woe to those who make unjust laws,

and who, when writing, have written injustice

to oppress the poor in judgment

and to do violence to the case of the humble of my people,

so that widows might become their prey

and they might plunder orphans.

What will you do on the day of visitation,

and of calamity coming from far away?

To whom will you flee for help?

And where will you leave your glory,

lest you bend beneath the bond

and fall among the slain?

Above all this his anger has not turned away,

[Col. 0784C] but his hand is still extended.

Woe to Assyria,

the rod of my anger,

and the staff itself;

in their hand is my indignation.

I will send him against a deceitful nation,

and I will command him against the people of my fury

to take away spoils and plunder prey,

and to set him down for trampling

like the mud of the streets.

But he will not judge in this way,

and his heart will not think thus.

Rather, his heart will be set on destroying

and exterminating nations, not a few.

For he will say:

“Are not my princes altogether kings?

Is not Calno like Carchemish?

And Arpad like Hamath?

Is not Damascus like Samaria?

Just as my hand found the kingdoms of an idol,

so also their images from Jerusalem and Samaria.

[Col. 0784D] Is it not that, as I did to Samaria and its idols,

so I will do to Jerusalem and its images?”

And it will come to pass, when the Lord has completed all his works

on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem,

that I will visit the fruit of the magnificent heart

of the king of Assyria,

and the glory of the loftiness of his eyes.

For he said:

“By the strength of my hand I have acted,

and by my wisdom I have understood.

I have removed the boundaries of peoples,

and I have plundered their princes.

I have brought down, as a powerful man,

those who dwell on high.

And my hand found the strength of peoples

as though it were a nest.

And as eggs that have been abandoned are gathered,

so I gathered the whole earth,

and there was no one who moved a wing,

opened his mouth,

or chirped.”

[Col. 0785A] Will the ax boast against the one who cuts with it?

Or will the saw exalt itself against the one who draws it?

As though a rod should rise against the one lifting it,

and a staff should exalt itself,

though it is only wood.

Therefore the sovereign Lord of hosts will send leanness among his fat ones,

and beneath his glory a burning fire will blaze

like the burning of fire.

And the light of Israel will be in the fire,

and his Holy One in the flame.

And it will burn and devour his thorn,

and the briars in one day.

And the glory of his forest and his Carmel

will be consumed from soul to flesh,

and he will flee in terror.

And the remaining wood of his forest

will be so few that they can be counted,

[Col. 0785B] and a child will write them down.

And it shall be on that day:

The remnant of Israel and those who have escaped

[Alternative: have been saved] from the house of Jacob

will no longer rely upon him who strikes them,

but will rely upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.

In truth the remnant will return,

the remnant, I say, of Jacob, to the mighty God

[Alternative: the Lord].

For even if your people, Israel, should be like the sand of the sea,

a remnant of them will return:

A consummation, shortened,

will overflow with righteousness.

For the Lord God of hosts will carry out a consummation

and a shortening

in the midst of the whole earth.

Therefore thus says the Lord God of hosts:

Do not fear, my people, inhabitant of Zion, because of Assyria:

[Col. 0785C] he will strike you with a rod,

and will raise his staff against you on the road to Egypt.

For yet a very little while,

and indignation

[Alternative: my indignation] will be brought to an end,

and my anger against their crime.

And the Lord of hosts will raise a scourge against him,

as at the plague of Midian at the rock of Horeb,

and his rod over the sea,

and he will lift it up on the road to Egypt.

And it shall be on that day: his burden will be removed from your shoulder,

and his yoke from your neck,

and the yoke will rot away because of the anointing oil.

He will come to Aiath,

pass through Magron;

at Michmash he will entrust his vessels.

They have crossed over in haste:

Geba is our dwelling;

Ramah was astonished,

Gibeah of Saul has fled.

Cry aloud with your voice, daughter of Gallim;

[Col. 0785D] pay attention, Laish,

poor little Anathoth.

Madmenah has migrated;

inhabitants of Gebim, strengthen yourselves.

There is still a day for him to stand at Nob:

he will shake his hand over the mountain of the daughter of Zion,

the hill of Jerusalem.

Behold, the sovereign Lord of hosts will shatter the flask in terror,

and those of lofty stature will be cut down,

and the exalted will be humbled.

The dense growth of the forest will be overturned by iron,

and Lebanon with its tall trees will fall.

[Chapter XI.]

And a rod will go forth from the root of Jesse,

and a flower will rise from his root.

And the spirit of the Lord will rest upon him:

the spirit of wisdom and understanding,

the spirit of counsel and strength,

[Col. 0786A] the spirit of knowledge and piety,

and the spirit of the fear of the Lord will fill him.

He will not judge according to the sight of his eyes,

nor reprove according to the hearing of his ears,

but he will judge the poor with justice,

and reprove with equity on behalf of the meek of the earth.

And he will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth,

and with the breath of his lips he will slay the wicked.

And justice will be the belt of his loins,

and faith the girdle of his kidneys.

The wolf will dwell with the lamb,

and the leopard will lie down with the young goat.

The calf and the lion and the sheep will remain together,

and a little child will lead them.

The calf and the bear will feed together;

their young will rest together,

and the lion will eat straw like an ox.

And the infant at the breast will delight over the hole of the asp,

and the weaned child will put his hand

[Col. 0786B] into the den of the basilisk.

They will not harm, and they will not kill,

throughout all my holy mountain,

for the earth has been filled with the knowledge of the Lord,

as waters cover the sea.

On that day the root of Jesse,

who stands as a sign for the peoples,

the nations will entreat him,

and his tomb will be glorious.

And it shall be on that day:

The Lord will again extend his hand to possess the remnant of his people,

which will be left by the Assyrians,

and by Egypt,

and by Pathros,

and by Ethiopia,

and by Elam,

and by Shinar,

and by Hamath,

[Col. 0786C] and by the islands of the sea.

And he will raise a sign for the nations,

and gather the fugitives of Israel,

and collect the dispersed of Judah from the four quarters of the earth.

And the jealousy of Ephraim will be removed,

and the enemies of Judah will perish.

Ephraim will not rival Judah,

and Judah will not fight against Ephraim.

And they will fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines by the sea;

together they will plunder the sons of the East.

Edom and Moab will be under the command of their hand,

and the sons of Ammon will be obedient.

And the Lord will lay waste the tongue of the sea of Egypt,

and will raise his hand

[Alternative: omits “his hand”]

over the river in the strength of his spirit,

and will strike it into seven channels,

so that they may cross it wearing sandals.

And there will be a road for the remnant of my people,

which will be left by the Assyrians,

[Col. 0786D] as there was for Israel on the day when he came up from the land of Egypt.

And you will say on that day:

[Chapter XII.]

I will give thanks to you, Lord,

for although you were angry with me,

your anger has turned away,

and you have consoled me.

Behold, God is my savior:

I will act confidently,

and I will not fear.

For the Lord God is my strength and my praise,

and he has become my salvation.

You will draw water with joy from the springs of the Savior,

and you will say on that day:

Give thanks to the Lord,

and call upon his name.

Make his deeds known among the peoples;

remember that his name is exalted.

Sing to the Lord,

for he has acted magnificently.

Announce this throughout the whole earth.

Rejoice and praise, inhabitant of Zion,

[Col. 0787A] for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.

THE BURDEN OF BABYLON,

which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.

[Chapter XIII.]

Upon the mountain of darkness raise a sign;

exalt your voice,

raise your hand,

and let the commanders enter the gates.

I have commanded my consecrated ones,

and I have summoned my warriors in my anger,

those rejoicing in my glory.

A voice of a multitude in the mountains,

like that of

[Note: The copyist of the Canon of Saint-Germain, following his own judgment, wrote “like that of peoples at play” instead of “of populous peoples.” Thus scribes are often mocked, when they write not what they find but what they understand, as we have noted elsewhere. MART.]

populous peoples:

the sound of the noise of kings,

of nations gathered together.

The Lord of hosts has commanded the army of war,

those coming from a distant land.

The Lord comes from the summit of heaven,

with the instruments of his wrath,

to destroy the whole earth.

Howl,

for the day of the Lord is near;

it will come like devastation from the Lord.

Therefore all hands will be loosened,

[Col. 0787B] and every human heart will waste away and be broken.

Pangs and pains will seize them;

they will writhe like a woman in labor.

Each one will be astounded at his neighbor;

their faces will be faces scorched by fire.

Behold, the day of the Lord comes,

cruel,

full of indignation,

anger,

and fury,

to make the earth a desolation,

and to destroy its sinners from it.

For the stars of heaven and their brightness

will not shine with their light.

The sun will be darkened at its rising,

and the moon will not shine with its light.

And I will punish the world for its evil,

and the ungodly for their iniquity.

I will make the pride of the faithless cease,

and humble the arrogance of the strong.

A man will be more precious than gold,

and a human being than pure gold.

[Col. 0787C] Because of this I will disturb heaven,

and the earth will be shaken from its place,

because of the indignation of the Lord of hosts,

and because of the day of the anger of his fury.

And it will be like a fleeing doe,

and like a sheep;

and there will be no one to gather them.

Each one will turn back to his own people,

and each will flee to his own land.

Everyone who is found will be killed,

and everyone who comes upon them will fall by the sword.

Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes;

their houses will be plundered,

and their wives will be violated.

Behold, I will raise up the Medes against them,

who will not seek silver

nor desire gold.

But with arrows they will kill the children,

they will not pity nursing infants,

and their eye will not spare the sons.

And that Babylon, glorious among kingdoms,

renowned in the pride of the Chaldeans,

will be like Sodom and Gomorrah when the Lord overthrew them.

It will not be inhabited forever,

and it will not be founded from generation to generation.

The Arab will not pitch his tent there,

nor will shepherds rest there.

But beasts will rest there

[Alternative: will be there],

and their houses will be filled with dragons,

and ostriches will dwell there,

and satyrs will dance there.

And owls will answer there in its houses

[Alternative: omits “there”],

[Col. 0788A] and sirens in its pleasure-shrines.

[Chapter XIV.]

Its time is near to come,

and its days will not be prolonged.

For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob,

and will still choose Israel,

and make them rest upon their own soil.

The foreigner will be joined to them,

and will cling to the house of Jacob.

And peoples will take possession of them,

and bring them to their place.

And the house of Israel will possess them upon the land of the Lord

as male and female slaves.

And those who had taken them captive will become their captives,

[Alternative: “taking and having taken them”],

and they will subject those who had exacted tribute from them.

And it shall be on that day:

when God gives you rest from your labor,

from your trembling,

and from the harsh servitude in which you formerly served,

you will take up this parable against the king of Babylon,

and say:

[Col. 0788B] How has the exactor ceased?

How has the tribute come to rest?

The Lord has broken the staff of the wicked,

the rod of rulers,

which struck peoples in indignation with an incurable blow,

subjected nations in fury,

and pursued them cruelly.

The whole earth has come to rest and is quiet;

it has rejoiced and exulted.

Even the fir trees have rejoiced over you,

and the cedars of Lebanon:

“Since you have fallen asleep,

no one has come up to cut us down.”

The underworld below was troubled to meet your arrival;

it stirred up the giants for you.

All the rulers of the earth rose from their thrones,

all the rulers of the nations.

And all will answer you and say:

[Col. 0788C] “You too have been wounded as we were;

you have become like us.

Your pride has been brought down to the underworld;

your corpse has fallen.

Beneath you the moth will be spread

[Alternative: decay],

and worms will be your covering.

How have you fallen from heaven,

morning star,

you who rose at dawn?

You have fallen to the earth,

you who wounded nations.

You who said in your heart:

‘I will ascend into heaven;

above the stars of God I will exalt my throne.

I will sit on the mountain of the covenant,

on the sides of the north.

I will ascend above the heights of the clouds,

and I will be like the Most High.’

Yet you will be brought down to the underworld,

to the depth of the pit.

Those who see you

will bend toward you

and gaze upon you:

[Col. 0788D] ‘Is this the man who disturbed the earth,

who shook kingdoms,

who made the world a desert,

and destroyed its cities,

who did not open the prison for his captives?’

All the kings of the nations,

all of them,

sleep in glory,

each man in his own house.

But you have been cast out of your tomb,

like a useless shoot,

defiled and wrapped together with those

who were killed by the sword,

and who descended to the foundations of the pit,

like a rotting corpse.

You will not share their burial,

[Col. 0789A] for you destroyed the earth

[Alternative: your earth],

you killed the people.

The offspring of evildoers will never again be called.

Prepare his sons for slaughter because of the iniquity of their fathers.

They will not rise,

nor inherit the earth,

nor fill the face of the world with cities.”

And I will rise up against them, says the Lord of hosts,

and destroy Babylon’s name,

its remnant,

its shoot,

and its offspring,

says the Lord.

And I will make it the possession of the hedgehog,

and marshes of waters,

and I will sweep it with a sweeping broom,

says the Lord of hosts.

The Lord of hosts has sworn, saying:

“Surely, as I have thought,

so it will be;

and as I have considered in my mind,

so it will happen,

that I may crush the Assyrian in my land,

[Col. 0789B] and trample him upon my mountains.

His yoke will be removed from them,

and his burden will be lifted from their shoulder.

This is the plan that I have planned for the whole earth,

and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.

For the Lord of hosts has decreed,

and who will be able to weaken it?

His hand is stretched out,

and who will turn it back?”

In the year in which King Ahaz died,

this burden came to pass:

Do not rejoice, all Philistia,

because the rod of your striker has been broken.

For from the root of the serpent a basilisk will come forth,

and its offspring will devour the flying creature.

And the firstborn of the poor will feed,

and the poor will rest confidently.

I will cause your root to perish through famine,

and I will kill your remnant.

[Col. 0789C] Howl, gate;

cry out, city.

All Philistia has been laid low,

for smoke will come from the north,

and there is no one who can escape its ranks.

And what will be answered to the messengers of the nation?

That the Lord founded Zion,

and in him

[Alternative: in her, following the Hebrew]

the poor of his people will hope.

THE BURDEN OF MOAB.

[Chapter XV.]

Because Ar was devastated by night,

Moab fell silent.

Because the wall of Moab was devastated by night,

Moab fell silent.

The house has gone up,

and Dibon to the high places,

to lament over Nebo and over Medeba.

Moab has howled

[Alternative: will howl, following the Hebrew].

All its heads are bald.

Every beard is shaved.

In its crossroads they gird themselves with sackcloth.

Upon its roofs and in its streets everyone howls

[Note: In the commentary he reads: “Every howl will descend,” and so forth. The Hebrew likewise has … .]

[Col. 0789D] and descends into weeping.

Heshbon and Elealeh will cry out;

their voice has been heard as far as Jahaz.

Therefore the armed men of Moab will howl;

its soul will howl for itself.

My heart will cry out over Moab;

its bars reach as far as Zoar,

the three-year-old heifer

[Note: This is an exceedingly obscure passage, but Jerome’s commentaries make it clear and intelligible in many places. For in the Book of Hebrew Questions on Genesis, speaking of Zoar, he says: “The Hebrews therefore relate that this same place is called Salissa in another book of Scripture, and is again said to be μόσχον τριετίζουσαν, that is, ‘a heifer in its third year,’ because it was swallowed up by the third movement of the earth.” He reports the same in Book V of his Commentary on Isaiah, but adds there: “We may take ‘the heifer in its third year’ as denoting the age of maturity. For just as the thirtieth year is the strongest among human beings, so among cattle and beasts the third year is the most robust. Understand ‘bars’ as boundaries and strength, since Zoar lies on the borders of the Moabites, separating from them the land of the Philistines.” MART. —Concerning the meaning of this word, compare the commentaries of the holy interpreter, Book V; also the Hebrew Questions, cols. 326 and 334; the Book of Hebrew Names; and finally the Epitaph of Saint Paula, where it is likewise noted that other manuscripts incorrectly read “consternantem.” See what we observe in those places.]

in its third year.

For along the ascent of Luhith,

weeping will ascend,

and on the road to Horonaim

they will raise a cry of destruction.

For the waters of Nimrim will be desolate,

because the grass has dried up,

the vegetation has failed,

and all greenery has perished.

According to the greatness of the work,

so also will be their visitation.

They will lead them to the torrent of the willows.

For a cry has encircled the territory of Moab.

Its howl reaches as far as Gallim,

and its cry as far as the well of Elim,

because the waters of Dibon are filled with blood.

For I will bring further things upon Dibon:

a lion upon those who flee from Moab,

and upon the remnant of the land.

[Chapter XVI.]

Send the lamb to the ruler of the land,

from the rock of the desert

to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.

And it shall be:

As a fleeing bird,

and as young birds flying from the nest,

so will the daughters of Moab be

at the crossing of the Arnon.

Take counsel,

call an assembly.

Make your shadow like night at midday.

Hide the fugitives,

and do not betray the wanderers.

My fugitives will dwell with you.

Moab, be their hiding place

from the face of the destroyer.

For the dust has ended,

the wretched man has been consumed,

and the one who trampled the earth has failed.

And a throne will be prepared in mercy,

and one will sit upon it in truth

in the tabernacle of David,

judging and seeking judgment,

and swiftly rendering what is just.

We have heard of the pride of Moab:

he is exceedingly proud.

His pride,

his arrogance,

and his indignation

are greater than his strength.

Therefore Moab will howl over Moab;

everyone will howl,

for those who rejoice over the walls of baked brick:

“Speak of his wounds.”

For the suburbs of Heshbon are desolate,

and the lords of the nations have cut down the vine of Sibmah

[Alternative: the vine Sibmah].

Its branches have reached as far as Jazer;

they have wandered in the desert,

its shoots have been abandoned,

and they have crossed the sea.

Because of this I will weep in the weeping of Jazer

over the vine of Sibmah

[Alternative: the vine Sibmah].

I will drench you with my tears,

Heshbon and Elealeh,

because over your vintage

and over your harvest

the voice of those who tread has broken out.

And joy and exultation will be removed from Carmel,

and no one will rejoice or shout for joy in the vineyards.

The one accustomed to treading will not tread wine in the winepress.

I have taken away the voice of those who tread.

Because of this my belly will sound like a lyre for Moab,

and my inward parts for the wall of baked brick.

[Col. 0791A] And it shall be:

when it appears that Moab has labored on his high places,

he will enter his sanctuaries to pray,

but he will not prevail.

This is the word that the Lord spoke to Moab from that time,

and now the Lord has spoken, saying:

[Note: The manuscripts of the Canon do not read this correctly: “from this time, and now,” instead of “from that time, and now.” MART.]

“In three years,

like the years of a hired laborer,

the glory of Moab will be removed

from the whole great multitude,

and a small and insignificant remnant will be left,

by no means a great one.”

THE BURDEN OF DAMASCUS.

[Chapter XVII.]

Behold, Damascus will cease to be a city,

and it will become like a heap of stones in a ruin.

The abandoned cities of Aroer will belong to flocks,

and they will rest there,

and there will be no one to frighten them.

And help will cease from Ephraim,

and the kingdom from Damascus.

[Col. 0791B] And the remnant of Syria will be like the glory of the sons of Israel,

says the Lord of hosts.

And it shall be on that day:

the glory of Jacob will be diminished,

and the fatness of his flesh will waste away

[Alternative: his fat flesh will waste away].

And it will be like one gathering what remains in the harvest,

and his arm will gather ears of grain.

And it will be like one seeking ears of grain in the valley of Rephaim.

And something will be left in it like a cluster,

and like the shaking of an olive tree,

two or three olives at the top of a branch,

or four or five on its highest shoots,

its fruits,

says the Lord God of Israel.

On that day a man will bow toward his Maker,

and his eyes will look toward the Holy One of Israel.

And he will not bow toward the altars

that his hands have made.

He will not look upon what his fingers have fashioned,

the sacred groves and shrines.

[Col. 0791C] On that day the cities of his stronghold will be abandoned,

like plowed fields and crops

that were abandoned before the sons of Israel.

And it will be desolate.

For you have forgotten God your Savior,

and you have not remembered the strong one who helped you.

Therefore you will plant a faithful plantation,

and sow a foreign shoot.

On the day of your planting you will make it grow luxuriantly,

and in the morning your seed will flower.

The harvest has been removed on the day of inheritance,

and it will grieve severely.

Woe to the multitude

[Alternative: to the multitude of]

many peoples,

like the multitude of the roaring sea,

and the tumult of crowds,

like the sound of many waters.

The peoples will roar like the sound of overflowing waters,

[Col. 0791D] and he will rebuke him,

and he will flee far away.

He will be carried off like the dust of the mountains before the wind,

and like a whirlwind before a storm.

At evening time—behold, trouble;

in the morning—and it will not remain.

This is the portion of those who laid us waste,

and the lot of those who plundered us.

[Chapter XVIII.]

Woe to the land of the winged cymbal,

which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,

which sends messengers by sea

and in vessels of papyrus upon the waters.

Go, swift messengers,

to a nation shaken and torn apart,

to a terrible people,

after whom there is no other,

[Col. 0792A] to a nation waiting and trampled,

whose rivers have plundered its land.

All you inhabitants of the world,

you who dwell upon the earth,

when the sign is raised on the mountains,

you will see it,

and when the trumpet sounds,

you will hear it.

For thus the Lord said to me:

“I will rest,

and I will consider in my place,

like a clear midday light,

and like a cloud of dew on the day of harvest.

For before the harvest it has all blossomed,

and the immature fruit has produced its perfection.

And its little branches will be pruned with sickles;

what remains will be cut off and shaken down.

They will be left together to the birds of the mountains

and to the beasts of the earth.

The birds will remain upon it throughout the perpetual summer,

and all the beasts of the earth will winter upon it.”

At that time a gift will be brought to the Lord of hosts

[Col. 0792B] from a people torn apart and ravaged,

from a terrible people,

after whom there has been no other,

from a nation waiting,

waiting and trampled,

whose rivers have plundered its land,

to the place of the name of the Lord of hosts,

Mount Zion.

THE BURDEN OF EGYPT.

[Chapter XIX.]

Behold, the Lord will ascend upon a light cloud

and enter Egypt.

The idols of Egypt will be shaken before him,

and the heart of Egypt will waste away within it.

And I will incite Egyptians against Egyptians.

A man will fight against his brother,

and a man against his neighbor,

city against city,

and kingdom against kingdom.

And the spirit of Egypt will be broken within it,

and I will overthrow its counsel.

[Col. 0792C] And they will consult their idols,

their diviners,

their mediums,

and their seers.

And I will deliver Egypt into the hand of cruel masters,

and a strong king will rule over them,

says the Lord God of hosts.

And the water of the sea will dry up,

and the river will be desolated and dried.

And the rivers will fail;

they will become shallow and dry up in the channels of the embankments.

The reed and the rush will wither.

The riverbed will be stripped bare from its source,

and every irrigated seedbed will dry up,

wither,

and cease to exist.

And the fishermen will mourn,

and all who cast a hook into the river will lament,

and those who spread nets over the surface of the waters

[Alternative: water]

will wither.

Those who work flax,

combing it

[Alternative: plaiting it],

and weaving fine cloth,

will be confounded.

And its irrigated places will become slack,

all who made pools for catching fish.

The princes of Tanis are fools.

The wise counselors of Pharaoh have given foolish counsel.

How will you say to Pharaoh:

“I am a son of the wise,

a son of ancient kings”?

Where are your wise men now?

Let them announce to you

and declare

what the Lord of hosts has planned concerning Egypt.

The princes of Tanis have become fools.

The princes of Memphis have withered.

They have deceived Egypt,

the cornerstone of its peoples.

The Lord has mingled within it a spirit of dizziness.

[Col. 0793A] They have caused Egypt to wander in all its work,

as a drunkard wanders while vomiting.

And Egypt will have no work

that can make head and tail,

[Note: Here the holy Father himself should be heard, since in his Commentary he reviews and corrects his rendering of this passage. Martianay also praises the passage. “In that too,” he says, “which we translated ‘bending and restraining,’ we may say ‘bent and wanton,’ so that we understand an old man and a child. But when we translated the Hebrew word AGMON (), while quickly rendering what was written, we were deceived by its ambiguity and said ‘restraining.’” And shortly afterward: “I think it better to criticize one’s own error than, while ashamed to confess ignorance, to persist in error. In what I translated, ‘And the land of Judah will be a festival for Egypt,’ the Hebrew reads AGGA (), which can mean ‘festival’; hence Aggaeus is rendered ‘festive.’ It can also mean ‘fear,’ which Aquila translated more significantly as γύρωσιν [gyrōsin, “turning about”], when someone fearful and trembling casts his eyes around and dreads an approaching enemy. Therefore, if we wish to take the recollection of Judah in a favorable sense—as a source of joy—it is rightly called a festival; but if, as I think, “festival” is to be rendered “fear,” we should understand dread or terror.]

bending and restraining.

On that day Egypt will be like women.

They will be astounded and afraid

at the face of the shaking of the hand of the Lord of hosts,

which he himself will shake over it.

And the land of Judah will be a festival for Egypt.

[Note: Saint Jerome provides an outstanding example of modesty and humility for all learned people in Book V of his Commentary on the Prophet Isaiah. There, criticizing himself because, being too hasty and rash, he had not translated certain words of this chapter correctly into Latin, he frankly confessed the following: “In that too which we translated ‘bending and restraining,’ we may say ‘bent and wanton,’ so that we understand an old man and a child. But when we translated the Hebrew word AGMON (), while quickly rendering what was written, we were deceived by its ambiguity and said ‘restraining.’” And shortly afterward: “I think it better to criticize one’s own error than, while ashamed to confess ignorance, to persist in error. In what I translated, ‘And the land of Judah will be a festival for Egypt,’ the Hebrew reads AGGA (), which can mean ‘festival’; hence Aggaeus is rendered ‘festive.’ It can also mean ‘fear,’ which Aquila translated more significantly as γύρωσιν [gyrōsin], when someone fearful and trembling casts his eyes around if he fears an approaching enemy. Therefore, if we wish to take the recollection of Judah in a favorable sense—as a source of joy for Egypt—it is rightly called a festival; but if, as I think, “festival” is to be rendered “fear,” we should understand dread or terror. MART.]

Everyone who remembers it

will tremble before the face of the plan of the Lord of hosts,

which he himself has planned concerning it.

On that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt

speaking the language of Canaan

and swearing by the Lord of hosts.

One will be called the City of the Sun.

On that day there will be an altar of the Lord

in the midst of the land of Egypt,

and a pillar of the Lord beside its boundary.

[Col. 0793B] And it will be for a sign and a testimony

to the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt.

For they will cry out to the Lord

because of the face of the oppressor,

and he will send them a savior and defender

who will free them.

And the Lord will be known to Egypt,

and the Egyptians will know the Lord on that day.

They will worship him with sacrifices and offerings;

they will make vows to the Lord,

and fulfill them.

And the Lord will strike Egypt with a plague,

and heal it.

They will return to the Lord,

and he will be appeased toward them,

and will heal them.

On that day there will be a road from Egypt to the Assyrians.

The Assyrian will enter Egypt,

and the Egyptian

[Alternative: the Egyptian man]

into Assyria,

and the Egyptians will serve Assur.

On that day Israel will be third with Egypt

[Alternative: with the Egyptian]

and Assyria,

a blessing in the midst of the land,

which the Lord of hosts has blessed, saying:

“Blessed is my people, Egypt,

and the work of my hands, Assyria,

but Israel is my inheritance.”

[Chapter XX.]

In the year when Tartan entered Ashdod,

when Sargon, king of the Assyrians, had sent him,

and he had fought against Ashdod

and captured it,

at that time the Lord spoke by the hand of Isaiah son of Amoz, saying:

Go,

loosen the sackcloth from your loins,

and remove your sandals from your feet.

[Col. 0794A] And he did so,

walking naked and barefoot.

And the Lord said:

As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot,

he will be a sign and portent for three years

concerning Egypt and Ethiopia.

So the king of the Assyrians will lead away the captivity of Egypt

and the deportation of Ethiopia,

young and old

[Alternative: the young and the old],

naked and barefoot,

with their buttocks uncovered,

to the shame of Egypt.

And they will fear and be confounded because of Ethiopia,

their hope,

and because of Egypt,

their glory.

And the inhabitant of this island will say on that day:

“Behold, this was our hope,

to whom we fled for help,

that they might free us from the face of the king of the Assyrians.

And how will we be able to escape?”

THE BURDEN OF THE DESERT OF THE SEA.

[Col. 0794B]

As whirlwinds come from the south,

it will come from the desert,

from a terrible land.

A harsh vision has been announced to me.

The unbeliever acts faithlessly,

and the despoiler lays waste.

Go up, Elam;

besiege, Media.

I have made all its groaning cease.

Therefore my loins are filled with pain;

anguish has possessed me

like the anguish of a woman in labor.

I collapsed when I heard;

I was troubled when I saw.

My heart has withered away;

darkness has astounded me.

Babylon, my beloved,

has been made a wonder to me.

Set the table;

watch from the lookout

those eating and drinking.

Rise, commanders;

seize the shield.

For thus the Lord said to me:

Go,

set a watchman,

and whatever he sees,

let him announce.

And he saw a chariot of two horsemen,

a rider on a donkey,

and a rider on a camel.

And he watched attentively,

with much concentration.

And the lion cried out:

“Upon the Lord’s watchtower I stand,

standing continually by day,

[Col. 0795A] and upon my guard I stand,

standing through all the nights.

Behold, this one comes,

the rider,

the man of the two-horse chariot.”

And he answered and said:

“Babylon has fallen,

and all the carved images of her gods

have been broken to the ground.

My threshing floor,

and the son of my threshing floor,

[Note: The manuscripts do not read this correctly as “and the daughter of my threshing floor,” since the Hebrew has ben, that is, “son.” The phrase “my threshing floor and son of my threshing floor” addresses Jerusalem and the temple situated in Ornan’s threshing floor, and says to it: “O Jerusalem, and people, son of my temple, do not think it incredible that I have spoken; for these are not my words but the Lord’s,” and so forth. MART.]

what I have heard from the Lord of hosts,

the God of Israel,

I have announced to you.”

THE BURDEN OF DUMA.

He cries out to me from Seir:

“Watchman, what of the night?

Watchman, what of the night?”

The watchman said:

“Morning comes,

and also night.

If you seek,

seek.

Return;

come.”

THE BURDEN IN ARABIA.

[Col. 0795B]

You will sleep in the forest at evening,

on the paths of Dodanim.

Meet the thirsty with water,

you who inhabit the land of the South.

Meet the fugitive with bread.

For they fled from the face of swords,

from the face of the sword that threatens,

from the face of the drawn bow,

from the face of a fierce battle.

For thus the Lord said to me:

“Within one more year,

like a hired laborer’s year,

all the glory of Kedar will be removed.

And the remnant of the number of the mighty archers

of the sons of Kedar will be diminished,

for the Lord God of Israel has spoken.”

THE BURDEN OF THE VALLEY OF VISION.

[Col. 0795C] [Chapter XXII.]

What is the matter with you too,

that you have all gone up to the rooftops?

You are full of shouting,

a bustling city,

an exultant city.

Your slain are not slain by the sword,

nor dead in battle.

All your rulers have fled together,

and have been bound harshly.

All who were found were bound together;

they fled far away.

Therefore I said:

“Withdraw from me;

I will weep bitterly.

Do not press upon me to console me

over the destruction of the daughter of my people.”

For there is a day of slaughter,

of trampling,

and of weeping,

for the Lord God of hosts

in the valley of vision,

searching the wall

and magnificent upon the mountain.

And Elam took up the quiver,

the chariot of a mounted man,

and the shield stripped the wall.

And your chosen valleys will be full of chariots,

and horsemen will set their seats at the gate.

[Col. 0796A] And the covering of Judah will be revealed,

and on that day you will see the armory

of the house of the forest.

And you will see the breaches of the city of David,

for they have been multiplied.

And you gathered the waters of the lower pool,

and counted the houses of Jerusalem,

and demolished houses to fortify the wall.

And you made a pool between the two walls

[Note: All the manuscripts read “and water” instead of “for water,” but in Hebrew we read “for waters,” so that the sense is: “And you made a pool between the two walls to preserve the waters”; or, “You restored the old pool for preserving water.” MART.]

for the water of the old pool.

But you did not look toward the one who made it,

nor see from afar the one who fashioned it.

And on that day the Lord God of hosts will call

to weeping,

to mourning,

to baldness,

and to the wearing of sackcloth.

And behold, joy and gladness:

slaughtering calves,

killing rams,

eating meat,

and drinking wine.

“Let us eat and drink,

for tomorrow we shall die.”

[Col. 0796B] And it was revealed in my ears,

[Note: In both Canons the genuine reading of Scripture is altered in this way: “And it was revealed in my ears, says the Lord of hosts.” Moreover, the Carcassonian copy adds the word “voice” after “it was revealed.” Some manuscripts, with the Vulgate, read “the voice of the Lord of hosts.” See the same phrase above in the notes to verse thirty of chapter V, or verse nine according to the numbering of verses now used in Bibles. MART.]

by the Lord of hosts

[Vulgate: the voice of the Lord of hosts]:

“If this iniquity will be forgiven you until you die,”

says the Lord God of hosts.

Thus says the Lord God of hosts:

Go,

enter in to the one who dwells in the tabernacle,

to Shebna, the overseer of the temple,

and say to him:

“What are you doing here?

Or who are you here?

For you have cut out a tomb for yourself here;

you have carefully cut out a memorial for yourself on high,

a tabernacle for yourself in the rock.

Behold, the Lord will cause you to be carried away,

as a rooster is carried away,

and he will lift you up like a garment.

He will crown you with tribulation;

like a ball he will throw you into a broad and spacious land.

There you will die,

and there will be the chariot of your glory,

[Col. 0796C] the disgrace of your lord’s house.

And I will drive you from your station,

and remove you from your office.

And it shall be on that day:

I will call my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah,

and clothe him in your robe,

and strengthen him with your belt,

and place your authority in his hand.

And he will be like a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem

and to the house of Judah.

And I will place the key of the house of David upon his shoulder.

He will open,

and there will be no one who closes;

he will close,

and there will be no one who opens.

And I will fix him as a peg in a secure place,

and he will be upon the throne of glory of his father’s house

[Alternative: upon the throne of the house of his father].

And they will hang upon him all the glory of his father’s house,

vessels of various kinds,

[Col. 0796D] every small vessel,

from the vessels of bowls to every kind of musical vessel.

On that day, says the Lord of hosts,

the peg that was fixed in a secure place will be removed.

It will be broken and fall,

and what hung upon it will perish,

for the Lord has spoken.”

THE BURDEN OF TYRE.

[Col. 0797A] [Chapter XXIII.]

Howl, ships of the sea,

for the house from which they were accustomed to come

has been laid waste.

It has been revealed to them from the land of Kittim

[Alternative: “it has been revealed,” feminine].

Be silent, you inhabitants of the island:

the commerce of Sidon.

Those crossing the sea have filled you with many waters.

The seed of the Nile, the harvest of the river, was its produce,

and it became the commerce of the nations.

Be ashamed, Sidon,

for the sea has spoken, the strength of the sea, saying:

“I have not travailed, and I have not given birth;

I have not nourished young men,

nor brought virgins to maturity.”

When this is heard in Egypt,

they will grieve when they hear of Tyre:

“Cross over the seas;

wail, you inhabitants of the island!

Is this not your city,

[Col. 0797B] which gloried from former days in its antiquity?

Its own feet will carry it far away to dwell as an exile.”

Who devised this against Tyre, once crowned,

whose merchants were princes,

whose traders were renowned throughout the earth?

The Lord of hosts devised this,

to bring down the pride of all glory

and to lead all the renowned of the earth to disgrace.

Cross through your land like a river, daughter of the sea;

you have no girdle any longer.

He stretched out his hand over the sea;

he disturbed kingdoms.

The Lord commanded concerning Canaan,

to crush its strongholds, and said:

“You shall no longer continue to boast,

you disgraced virgin daughter of Sidon.”

Arise and cross over to Cethim;

there too you will have no rest.

[Col. 0797C] Behold, the land of the Chaldeans—

such a people did not exist.

Assyria founded it;

they led its strong men away into captivity;

they dug up its houses;

they reduced it to ruin.

Wail, ships of the sea,

for your stronghold has been devastated.

And it shall come to pass on that day:

You shall be forgotten, O Tyre, for seventy years,

like the days of one king.

But after seventy years

Tyre shall be like the song of a prostitute.

Take up the lyre, go around the city,

prostitute delivered over to oblivion;

sing well,

repeat the song, so that you may be remembered.

And it shall come to pass after seventy years:

[Col. 0797D] The Lord will visit Tyre,

and restore her to her wages [Note: Here and below, Saint Jerome reads *merces* (“wages”) instead of *mercede* (“payment”) in his Commentary, although that passage is believed by Victorius to be corrupt.]

And she will again fornicate with all the kingdoms of the earth,

upon the face of the earth.

And her commerce and her wages shall be consecrated to the Lord;

[Col. 0798A] they shall not be stored up or hoarded.

For her commerce shall be for those who dwell before the Lord,

so that they may eat to fullness

and dress themselves even to old age.

[Chapter XXIV.] Behold, the Lord will lay waste the earth,

and strip it bare,

and afflict its surface,

and scatter its inhabitants.

And it shall be: as with the people, so with the priest;

as with the servant, so with his master;

as with the maidservant, so with her mistress;

as with the buyer, so with the seller;

as with the lender, so with the borrower;

as with the creditor, so with the debtor.

The earth shall be utterly laid waste,

and shall be utterly plundered.

For the Lord has spoken this word.

It mourned, and the earth melted away, and grew weak;

the world melted away;

the height of the people of the earth grew weak.

[Col. 0798B] And the earth was slain by its inhabitants [Note: Thus read the manuscripts of Saint Jerome and the printed editions, including those in the Commentaries. The holy Doctor himself sufficiently indicates this reading when he says: “And they made the blood of the slain cry out to God, after the manner of Abel’s.” See more in Book VIII of the Commentaries on Isaiah. MART. — The Vulgate editions read *infecta est* (“was defiled”). Martianay, however, thinks that the printed reading is better supported in the commentary by Saint Jerome himself. The Hebrew has a verb meaning “to conceal,” “to cover,” or “to be inwardly infected by some fault.” It is often used elsewhere of the earth, where the sense is that it covers spilled blood and receives sin into itself, infected by a kind of hypocrisy because it conceals the crime and nevertheless bears fruit for the sinner. See Genesis 4:11; Numbers 35:33; Job 16:18 and 20:27; Jeremiah 3:1–2, and elsewhere. By these testimonies the Vulgate reading, *infecta* (“defiled”), is rather supported and is more pleasing to us.]

because they transgressed the laws [Alternative: law],

changed the right,

and violated the everlasting covenant.

Therefore a curse shall devour the earth,

and its inhabitants shall sin.

Therefore the inhabitants of the earth shall rage,

and few human beings shall remain.

The vintage mourned;

the vine grew weak;

all who were joyful in heart groaned.

The joy of tambourines ceased;

the sound of revelers fell silent;

the sweetness of the lyre was hushed.

They shall not drink wine with singing;

the drink shall be bitter to those who drink it.

The city of vanity has been crushed;

every house has been shut, with no one entering.

There shall be a cry over wine in the streets;

[Col. 0798C] all joy has been deserted;

the joy of the earth has been removed.

Solitude remains in the city,

and calamity will oppress the gates.

For these things shall be in the midst of the earth,

in the midst of the peoples,

as when a few olives remaining after the olive harvest are shaken down,

and clusters of grapes when the vintage has ended.

These shall raise their voice and give praise.

When the Lord has been glorified,

they shall neigh from the sea.

Therefore glorify the Lord in the teachings,

the name of the Lord, the God of Israel, in the islands of the sea.

From the ends of the earth we have heard praises,

the glory of the righteous one.

And I said:

“My secret is for me,

my secret is for me!

Woe is me! The transgressors have transgressed,

and they have transgressed with the transgression of transgressors.”

[Col. 0798D] Terror, pit, and snare are upon you,

inhabitant of the earth.

And it shall be:

Whoever flees from the sound of terror will fall into the pit;

and whoever extricates himself from the pit

will be caught in the snare.

[Col. 0799A] For the floodgates from on high have been opened,

and the foundations of the earth will be shaken.

The earth shall be utterly broken;

the earth shall be utterly shattered;

the earth shall be utterly shaken.

The earth shall reel and stagger like a drunken man,

and shall be removed

like a tent for one night.

Its iniquity shall weigh upon it, and it shall fall,

and shall not rise again.

And it shall come to pass:

On that day the Lord will visit the host

of heaven on high,

and the kings of the earth who are upon the earth.

And they shall be gathered in the gathering of one bundle

into the pit,

and shall be shut up there in prison;

and after many days they shall be visited.

And the moon shall blush and the sun be ashamed,

when the Lord of hosts reigns on Mount

Sion and in Jerusalem,

and is glorified in the presence of his elders.

[Col. 0799B] [Chapter XXV.] O Lord, you are my God;

I will exalt you,

I will confess your name,

for you have done wonders—

ancient plans, faithful and sure.

For you have made a city into a mound,

a fortified city into ruin;

a house of strangers, so that it is no city

and shall never be rebuilt.

For this a strong people will praise you;

the city of mighty nations will fear you.

For you have become a stronghold for the poor,

a stronghold for the needy in his distress;

a refuge from the storm,

a shade from the heat.

For the breath of the mighty is like a storm driving against a wall.

As heat in thirst, you will humble

the tumult of strangers,

and like heat beneath a torrential cloud,

you will make the offshoot of the mighty wither.

[Col. 0799C] And the Lord of hosts will make for all peoples

on this mountain

a feast of rich foods,

a feast of wine,

of rich foods full of marrow,

of wine purified of its dregs.

And on this mountain he will cast down the face of the bond

bound over all peoples,

and the web that he wove over all nations.

He will cast down death forever;

and the Lord God will wipe away the tear from every face,

and remove the reproach of his people from all

the earth;

for the Lord has spoken.

And he will say on that day:

“Behold, this is our God;

we waited for him, and he will save us.

This is the Lord;

we endured for him.

We shall exult and rejoice in his salvation.”

[Col. 0799D] For the hand of the Lord will rest on this mountain,

and Moab shall be threshed beneath him,

as straw is threshed on a wagon.

And he will stretch out his hands beneath him,

as a swimmer stretches them out for swimming.

And he will humble his glory with the striking of his hands.

And the fortifications of your lofty walls shall fall,

and they shall be humbled

and dragged down to the earth,

even to the dust.

On that day this song shall be sung in the land of Judah:

[Chapter XXVI.] “The city of our strength is Sion; the Savior will be placed in it as wall and rampart.

Open the gates,

and let the righteous nation enter,

the one that guards the truth.

The ancient error has passed away.

You will preserve peace, peace,

because we have hoped in you.

[Col. 0800A] You have hoped in the Lord for eternal ages,

in the Lord God, the strong one, forever.

For he will bend down those who dwell on high;

he will humble the lofty city.

He will humble it to the earth;

he will drag it down to the dust.

The foot shall trample it—

the feet of the poor,

the steps of the needy.

The path of the righteous is straight;

the way of the righteous is direct for walking.

And on the path of your judgments, O Lord,

we have waited for you.

Your name and your memorial

are the desire of the soul.

My soul desired you in the night;

and with my spirit within me,

from morning I will keep watch for you.

When you perform your judgments on the earth,

the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.

Let us show mercy to the wicked,

and he will not learn righteousness.

He acted wickedly in the land of the saints,

and he will not see the glory of the Lord.

O Lord, let your hand be exalted,

and let them not see.

Let them see and be confounded,

those who are jealous for the people [Alternative: let the zeal of the people be confounded].
