Let the fire devour your enemies.

O Lord, you will give us peace,

for you have accomplished all our works for us.

O Lord our God, other masters have possessed us besides you;

only in you shall we remember your name.

Let the dead not live;

let the giants not rise again.

Therefore you visited and crushed them,

and destroyed every memory of them.

You have been gracious to the nation, O Lord;

you have been gracious to the nation.

Have you truly been glorified?

You have extended all the boundaries of the earth.

[Col. 0800C] O Lord, in distress they sought you;

in the tribulation of murmuring,

your instruction was given to them.

As a woman conceiving [Alternative: who has conceived],

when she draws near to childbirth,

cries out in her pains,

so we have become before your face, O Lord.

We conceived,

and as though in labor we gave birth;

we brought forth spirit.

We did not bring salvation upon the earth;

therefore the inhabitants of the earth did not fall [Alternative: of the world].

Your dead shall live;

my slain shall rise again [Alternative: let them rise].

Awake and praise,

you who dwell in the dust,

for your dew is a dew of light,

and you will drag the land of giants to ruin.

Go, my people;

enter your chambers;

close your doors behind you.

Hide yourself for a little while,

for a moment,

until the indignation passes.

[Col. 0800D] For behold, the Lord will go out from his place

to visit the iniquity of the inhabitant of the earth against him.

And the earth will reveal its blood,

and will no longer cover its slain.

[Chapter XXVII.] On that day the Lord will visit

with his hard,

great,

and strong sword

Leviathan the bar-shaped serpent,

and Leviathan the twisting serpent;

and he will kill the sea monster that is in the sea.

On that day the vineyard of pure wine will sing to him.

I am the Lord who guards it;

I will suddenly give it drink,

lest it be visited against it.

By night and by day I guard it.

There is no indignation in me.

Who will give me a thorn and a brier in battle?

I will advance against it;

[Col. 0801A] I will burn it up altogether.

Or rather, will it hold fast to my strength?

Will it make peace with me?

Will it make peace with me?

Those who come forth [Note: The Carcassonne Canon and several manuscript biblical codices read, as does our Latin Vulgate, “Those who enter violently against Jacob.” But the Saint-Germain-des-Prés Canon, the Colbertinus Aniciensis manuscript in its first hand, and the very old manuscript of Saint-Victor in Paris, no. 379, read: “Those who come forth,” and so on. Through scribal error, unless we are mistaken, all the books we examined—except our Saint-Germain manuscript no. 164—have “against Jacob” instead of “from Jacob.” Moreover, the sacred text in Saint Jerome’s Commentary on Isaiah agrees sufficiently with our reading, for there we read as follows: “Those who come forth from the root of Jacob.” Its meaning is this: After the apostles, preaching the Gospel throughout the whole world, have said, “We will make peace with Christ; we will make peace with him,” those who are exalted from the seed of Jacob and have attained apostolic dignity will be called sons of Jacob, and so forth. Hence the Septuagint: “Those who come, sons of Jacob.” Nor should we omit ten manuscript codices, among the variant readings of Lucas Brugensis, which present this reading with the Royal Bibles: “Those who come forth violently from Jacob.” Consult the notes on this passage among the critics. MART.] violently from Jacob,

Israel will blossom and bud,

and they will fill the face of the world with seed.

Has he struck him as he struck the one who strikes?

Or has he been killed as his slain were killed?

With measure against measure,

when it has been cast away,

you will judge it.

He has pondered it with his harsh spirit

during the day of heat.

Therefore, because of this, the iniquity of the house of Jacob shall be forgiven [Alternative: because of these things];

and this shall be all its fruit:

that its sin may be removed,

when it has made all the stones of the altar like crushed ash-stones.

The sacred groves and shrines shall not stand.

[Col. 0801B] For the fortified city shall be desolate;

the beautiful city shall be abandoned and left like a wilderness [Alternative: desolate].

There the calf shall graze and lie down,

and consume its branches.

Its harvest shall be crushed in drought [Alternative: its harvest],

women coming and teaching it.

For it is not a wise people;

therefore the one who made it will not have mercy on it,

and the one who formed it will not spare it.

And it shall come to pass on that day:

The Lord will strike from the channel of the river

to the torrent of Egypt,

and you shall be gathered one by one,

sons of Israel.

And it shall come to pass on that day:

A great trumpet shall sound,

and those who had been lost in the land of Assyria shall come,

and those who had been cast out into the land of Egypt,

and they shall worship the Lord on the holy mountain

in Jerusalem.

[Col. 0801C] [Chapter XXVIII.] Woe to the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim,

and to the fading flower,

the glory of their exultation,

who were on the summit of the richest valley,

wandering from wine.

Behold, the Lord is mighty and strong [Alternative: of the Lord, with the Hebrew],

like a hailstorm,

a tempest breaking,

like a flood of mighty waters overflowing

and released upon a spacious land.

The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim

shall be trampled underfoot.

And the fading flower of the glory of their exultation,

which is upon the summit of the fertile valley,

shall be like an early fruit before the ripeness of autumn:

when the one who sees it looks upon it,

as soon as he holds it in his hand,

he will swallow it.

On that day the Lord of hosts shall be

a crown of glory

and a wreath of exultation

for the remnant of his people;

a spirit of judgment for the one seated in judgment,

and strength for those returning from battle to the gate.

[Col. 0802A] But these too have not known because of wine,

and have wandered because of drunkenness.

Priest and prophet have not known because of drunkenness;

they have been swallowed up by wine;

they have wandered in drunkenness;

they have not known the seer;

they have ignored judgment.

For all the tables are full of vomit and filth,

so that there is no longer any place.

Whom will he teach knowledge,

and whom will he make understand what has been heard?

Those weaned from milk [Note: All the manuscripts, apparently through scribal mispronunciation, corruptly read *apulsos* (“driven away”) instead of *avulsos* (“torn away”). Jerome himself notes this verse in his Commentaries, although copyists divide it into two in the manuscript codices. MART.],

those torn away from the breasts.

For: “Command, command again;

command, command again;

wait, wait again;

wait, wait again;

a little here, a little there.”

For with the speech of the lip

and with another tongue

he will speak to this people.

[Col. 0802B] To whom he said:

“This is my rest; refresh the weary,

and this is my refreshment.”

But they were unwilling to hear.

And the word of the Lord shall be to them:

“Command, command again;

command, command again;

wait, wait again;

wait, wait again;

a little here, a little there,”

so that they may go

and fall backward,

and be crushed [Note: In Martianay’s text it incorrectly read “be converted.” In the Hebrew, to omit the other books, the reading is: [blank in the supplied text]],

and be ensnared,

and be captured.

Therefore hear the word of the Lord,

mocking men,

you who rule over my people,

which is in Jerusalem.

For you said:

“We have made a covenant with death,

and with the underworld we have made an agreement.

When the overflowing scourge passes through,

it shall not come upon us,

[Col. 0802C] because we have made falsehood our hope,

and we have been protected by falsehood.”

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

“Behold, I will place in the foundations of Sion a stone,

a tested stone,

a precious cornerstone,

firmly founded [Alternative: a foundation stone firmly founded].

Whoever believes

shall not hasten [Note: In place of *non festinet* (“shall not hasten”), which Jerome translated according to the Hebrew, the Saint-Germain Canon reads *non turbetur* (“shall not be disturbed”). But our oldest biblical manuscript, no. 3, retains both readings: namely, “shall not hasten” and “shall not be disturbed.” The Septuagint reads, “shall not be confounded.” MART.].

And I will set judgment as a weight

and righteousness as a measure.

And hail will overturn the hope of falsehood,

and waters will flood the protection.

And your covenant with death shall be erased,

and your agreement with the underworld shall not stand.

When the overflowing scourge passes through,

you shall become a trampling.

Whenever it passes through,

it will carry you away,

for morning by morning it will pass through,

by day and by night;

and only vexation will give understanding to what is heard.”

[Col. 0803A] For the bed is too narrow,

so that one of the two falls off,

and the short covering cannot cover both.

For just as on the mountain of divisions the Lord will stand,

so in the valley that is in Gabaon he will be angry,

to perform his work,

his strange work;

to accomplish his work,

his work is foreign to him.

And now do not mock,

lest your bonds be tightened.

For I have heard from the Lord God of hosts

a decree of destruction and abbreviation

over the whole earth.

Give ear and hear my voice;

attend and hear my speech.

Does the plowman plow all day to sow,

does he continually break up and harrow his ground?

Is it not so that, when he has leveled its surface,

he sows black cumin and scatters cumin,

and places wheat in rows,

[Col. 0803B] and barley and millet and vetch at their boundaries?

And he instructs him in judgment;

his God teaches him.

For black cumin is not threshed with a sharp instrument,

nor does the wheel of a wagon revolve over cumin,

but black cumin is beaten out with a rod,

and cumin with a staff.

But bread grain is crushed.

Yet the one threshing does not thresh it forever,

nor does he torment it with the wheel of a wagon,

nor crush it with his hooves.

And this has gone forth from the Lord God of hosts [Note: When Saint Jerome quotes this passage in his Commentary, he does not insert “Lord”; he has only, “And this has gone forth from the God of hosts.” This is altogether closer to the Hebrew exemplar.],

to make his counsel wonderful

and magnify righteousness.

[Chapter XXIX.] Woe to Ariel, the city

which David captured.

Year has been added to year;

the festivals have run their course.

And I will surround Ariel,

[Col. 0803C] and it shall be sad and mournful,

and shall be to me like Ariel.

And I will encircle you like a sphere,

and cast up a mound against you,

and set up fortifications for your siege.

You shall be humbled;

from the earth you shall speak,

and from the ground your speech shall be heard.

And your voice shall be like that of a python from the earth;

from the ground your speech shall mutter.

And the multitude of those who scatter you shall be like fine dust,

and the multitude of those who prevailed against you

shall be like passing chaff.

And it shall happen suddenly,

in an instant.

You shall be visited by the Lord of hosts

with thunder,

and with the shaking of the earth,

and with the loud voice of a whirlwind and storm,

and with the flame of devouring fire.

And the multitude of all the nations

that fought against Ariel,

and all who fought,

besieged,

and prevailed against it,

shall be like a dream of a nighttime vision.

[Col. 0803D] And as a hungry man dreams that he is eating,

but when he awakens,

his soul is empty;

and as a thirsty man dreams that he is drinking,

but after he awakens [Alternative: has become fully awake],

he is still weary and thirsty,

and his soul is empty;

so shall be the multitude of all the nations

that fought against Mount Sion.

Be stunned and wonder;

waver and stagger.

[Col. 0804A] Become drunk, but not from wine;

be shaken, but not from drunkenness.

For the Lord has mixed for you a spirit of stupor;

he will close your eyes—your prophets—

and cover your princes, who see visions [Note: The Saint-Germain Canon reads, with no difference in sense but in wording, “and your princes who see visions shall perish.” MART.].

And the vision of all of you shall be like the words of a sealed book.

When they give it to one who knows letters,

saying, “Read this,”

he will answer,

“I cannot, for it is sealed.”

And the book shall be given to one who does not know letters,

and they will say to him,

“Read.”

And he will answer,

“I do not know letters.”

And the Lord said:

“Because this people draws near with its mouth,

and glorifies me with its lips,

but its heart is far from me,

and they feared me according to the commandment of men

and according to teachings,

[Col. 0804B] therefore behold, I will add that I may astonish this people

with a great and wondrous marvel.

For the wisdom of its wise men shall perish,

and the understanding of its prudent men shall be hidden.

Woe to those who are deep in heart,

to hide their counsel from the Lord,

whose works are in darkness,

and who say:

‘Who sees us,

and who knows us?’

This thought of yours is perverse,

as if clay were to think against the potter

and say to its maker,

‘You did not make me’;

and the thing formed were to say to its former,

‘You do not understand.’

Will not Lebanon shortly and in a little while

be turned into Carmel,

and Carmel be counted as a forest?

And on that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book,

and from darkness and gloom

the eyes of the blind shall see.

And the meek shall increase their joy in the Lord,

and the poor among men shall exult in the Holy One of Israel.

[Col. 0804C] For the one who prevailed has failed;

the mocker has been brought to an end;

and all who watched for iniquity have been cut down—

those who made people sin by their word,

who tripped up the one reproving them at the gate,

and turned aside from the righteous without cause.

Therefore thus says the Lord to the house of Jacob,

who redeemed Abraham:

‘Jacob shall not now be confounded,

nor shall his face now blush.

For when he sees his children,

the work of my hands,

sanctifying my name in his midst,

they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob,

and proclaim the God of Israel.

And those who err in spirit shall know understanding,

and murmurers shall learn the law.’”

[Chapter XXX.] Woe, rebellious children, says the Lord,

who make a plan, but not from me,

and weave a web, but not by my spirit,

to add [Alternative: that you may add] sin upon sin;

who walk in order to descend into Egypt,

and have not asked my mouth,

hoping in the strength of Pharaoh

and trusting in the shadow of Egypt.

And the strength of Pharaoh shall be for you a disgrace,

and trust in the shadow of Egypt an embarrassment.

For your princes were in Tanis,

and your messengers reached as far as Anes.

All were confounded because of the people

who could not help them [Alternative: will not be able to help them],

who were not for assistance

or any benefit,

but for disgrace and reproach.

[Col. 0805A] THE BURDEN OF THE BEASTS OF THE SOUTH.

In a land of tribulation and distress:

lioness and lion,

adder and flying basilisk from them,

carrying their riches on the shoulders of beasts,

and their treasures on the humps of camels,

to a people who cannot profit them.

For Egypt will help in vain and to no purpose.

Therefore I cried out concerning this:

“Pride alone—

be still.”

Now go in;

write this for them on a tablet,

and carefully engrave it in a book.

And it shall be on the last day as a testimony,

even forever.

For it is a people provoking to anger,

lying children,

children unwilling to hear the law of God.

They say to the seers,

“Do not see,”

and to those who look,

“Do not look upon for us the things that are right.

[Col. 0805B] Speak pleasant things to us;

see errors for us.

Take the way away from me;

turn aside from me the path.

Let the Holy One of Israel cease from before us.”

Therefore thus says the Holy One of Israel:

“Because you rejected this word,

and hoped in slander and tumult,

and relied upon it,

therefore this iniquity shall be for you

like a breach falling down,

like a crack sought out in a high wall.

For suddenly,

when it is not expected,

its collapse will come.

And it shall be shattered

like a potter’s vessel crushed with a mighty crushing,

so that no shard will be found among its fragments

with which to carry a coal from the fire,

or draw a little water from a pit.”

[Col. 0805C] For thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel:

“If you return and remain quiet,

you shall be saved.

In silence and hope

shall be your strength.”

But you were unwilling,

and you said:

“No, rather we shall flee to the horses.”

Therefore you shall flee.

“And we shall mount swift animals.”

Therefore those who pursue you shall be swifter [Alternative: swift].

A thousand shall flee at the threat of one;

and at the threat of five you shall flee,

until you are left like a mast on the top of a mountain,

and like a signal on a hill.

Therefore the Lord waits

to have mercy on you;

and therefore he will be exalted

in sparing you.

For the Lord is a God of judgment.

Blessed are all who wait for him.

[Col. 0805D] For the people of Sion shall dwell in Jerusalem.

Weeping, you shall not weep.

Showing mercy, he will have mercy on you.

At the sound of your cry,

as soon as he hears it,

he will answer you.

And the Lord will give you scant bread

and little water.

And he will no longer cause your teacher to fly away [Alternative: “from you” is added],

and your eyes shall see your instructor.

And your ears shall hear a word behind you

admonishing:

“This is the way;

walk in it.”

And do not turn aside [Alternative: “and do not turn aside” is omitted],

neither to the right nor to the left.

And you shall defile the plates of your silver idols,

and the garment of your golden image,

and scatter them like the impurity of a menstruating woman.

You shall say to it:

“Go out.”

[Col. 0806A] And rain shall be given to your seed

wherever you sow in the land.

And the bread of the produce of the land

shall be exceedingly abundant and rich.

On that day the lamb shall be fed in your possession

in spacious pasture;

and your bulls and the young asses that till the ground

shall eat mixed fodder,

as it is winnowed on the threshing floor.

And upon every high mountain

and every raised hill

there shall be streams of running waters,

on the day of the slaughter of many,

when the towers fall.

And the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun,

and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold,

like the light of seven days,

on the day when the Lord binds up the wound of his people

and heals the stroke of its wound.

Behold, the name of the Lord comes from afar,

his anger burning,

and grievous to bear.

[Col. 0806B] His lips are filled with indignation,

and his tongue is like a devouring fire.

His breath is like an overflowing torrent

reaching to the middle of the neck,

to destroy nations utterly [Alternative: for nothing],

and the bridle of error that was in the jaws of the peoples.

There shall be a song for you

like the night of a sanctified festival,

and joy of heart

like that of one who walks with a flute,

to enter the mountain of the Lord,

to the Strong One of Israel.

And the Lord will make the glory of his voice heard,

and display the terror of his arm

in the threatening of his wrath

and the flame of devouring fire.

He will strike with whirlwind

and hailstone.

For at the voice of the Lord Assyria will tremble,

struck by the rod.

And there shall be a passage for the rod that is founded,

which the Lord will cause to rest upon him.

[Col. 0806C] With tambourines and lyres,

and with great battles,

he will fight against them.

For Topheth has been prepared from yesterday;

it has been prepared by the king,

deep and wide.

Its fuel is fire

and much wood.

The breath of the Lord,

like a torrent of sulfur,

burns it.

[Chapter XXXI.] Woe to those who descend into Egypt for help,

hoping in horses

and trusting in chariots because they are many,

and in horsemen because they are exceedingly strong.

But they have not trusted in the Holy One of Israel,

and they have not sought the Lord.

Yet he is wise;

he has brought evil,

and has not withdrawn his words.

He will rise against the house of the wicked,

and against the help of those who work iniquity.

Egypt is human, and not God;

their horses are flesh, and not spirit.

[Col. 0806D] And the Lord will incline his hand,

and the one who gives help will fall,

and the one receiving help will fall,

and all of them together will be consumed.

For thus says the Lord to me:

“As when a lion roars,

or a young lion over its prey,

when a multitude of shepherds comes against it,

it will not fear their voice,

nor be frightened by their multitude,

so the Lord of hosts will descend

to fight upon Mount Sion

and upon its hill.

As flying birds,

so the Lord of hosts will protect Jerusalem,

protecting and delivering,

passing over and saving.

Return, as you had deeply withdrawn,

sons of Israel.

[Col. 0807A] For on that day each man will cast away

the idols of his silver

and the idols of his gold,

which your hands made for you as a sin.

And Assyria shall fall by a sword not belonging to a man,

and a sword not belonging to a human being shall devour it;

and it shall flee,

not from the face of the sword.

Its young men shall become tributaries,

and its strength shall pass away because of terror;

its princes shall tremble as they flee.

Thus says the Lord,

whose fire is in Sion

and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.”

[Chapter XXXII.] Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness,

and princes shall rule in judgment.

And a man shall be like one hiding from the wind

and concealing himself from the storm,

like streams of water in thirst,

and like the shade of a projecting rock in a desert land.

The eyes of those who see shall not grow dim,

and the ears of those who hear shall listen attentively.

And the heart of fools shall understand knowledge,

[Col. 0807B] and the tongue of stammerers shall speak swiftly and clearly.

The one who is foolish shall no longer be called a prince,

nor shall the fraudulent be called great [Alternative: greater].

For the fool will speak foolishness,

and his heart will practice iniquity,

to complete hypocrisy,

to speak deceitfully against the Lord,

to empty the soul of the hungry,

and to take drink away from the thirsty.

The vessels of the fraudulent are exceedingly wicked;

for he has devised schemes

to destroy the meek with lying speech,

when he speaks judgment against the poor.

But the prince will devise things worthy of a prince,

and he himself will stand over rulers.

Rich women, rise up

and hear my voice.

Confident daughters,

give ear to my speech.

[Col. 0807C] After days and a year,

you confident women shall be troubled.

For the vintage is finished;

the gathering will not come again.

Be stunned, wealthy women;

be troubled, confident women.

Strip yourselves and be ashamed;

gird your loins.

Beat your breasts

over the desirable land,

over the fruitful vine.

Upon the soil of my people

thorns and briers shall rise,

and how much more upon all the houses of joy

of the exultant city!

For the house has been abandoned;

the multitude of the city has been left.

Darkness and groping have come upon the caves forever.

The pasture of wild asses is the grazing ground of flocks,

[Col. 0807D] until the spirit from on high is poured out upon us.

And the wilderness shall become Carmel,

and Carmel shall be counted as a forest.

And judgment shall dwell in the wilderness,

and righteousness shall sit in Carmel.

And the work of righteousness shall be peace,

and the service of righteousness shall be quietness

and security forever.

And my people shall sit in the beauty of peace,

in tents of confidence,

and in abundant rest.

But hail shall fall in the descent of the forest,

[Col. 0808A] and the city shall be utterly humbled.

Blessed are you who sow beside all waters,

letting the foot of the ox and the ass go forth.

[Chapter XXXIII.] Woe to you who plunder!

Will you not yourself be plundered?

And you who despise—

will you not yourself be despised?

When you have finished plundering,

you shall be plundered.

When, exhausted, you cease to despise,

you shall be despised.

O Lord, have mercy on us;

for we have waited for you.

Be our arm [Alternative: their arm] in the morning,

and our salvation in the time of tribulation.

At the voice of the angel

the peoples fled;

at your exaltation

the nations were scattered.

And your spoils shall be gathered

as the locust is gathered,

as when the ditches are filled with it.

The Lord has been magnified,

[Col. 0808B] for he has dwelt on high.

He has filled Sion with judgment and righteousness.

And there shall be faithfulness in your times:

the riches of salvation,

wisdom and knowledge.

The fear of the Lord himself is his treasure.

Behold, those who see shall cry out outside;

the angels of peace shall weep bitterly.

The roads have been destroyed;

the one passing along the path has ceased.

The covenant has been annulled.

He has rejected the cities;

he has not regarded human beings.

The earth mourned and languished.

Lebanon was confounded and withered;

and Sharon became like a wilderness.

Bashan and Carmel were shaken.

Now I will rise, says the Lord.

Now I will be exalted;

now I will be lifted up.

You shall conceive burning heat;

you shall give birth to stubble.

Your breath, like fire,

shall devour you.

And the peoples shall be like ash from a fire;

thorns gathered together shall be burned in the fire.

Hear, you who are far away,

what I have done,

and know, you who are near,

my strength.

The sinners in Sion were terrified;

trembling possessed the hypocrites.

Who among you can dwell with devouring fire?

Who among you will dwell with everlasting burnings?

The one who walks in righteousness

and speaks the truth,

who rejects dishonest gain from oppression

and shakes his hands free from every bribe,

who stops his ears so as not to hear of bloodshed,

and closes his eyes so as not to see evil.

This one shall dwell on high.

The heights of rocky fortifications shall be his refuge.

His bread shall be given to him;

[Col. 0808D] his waters shall be sure.

His eyes shall see the king in his beauty;

they shall behold a distant land.

Your heart shall meditate on terror:

“Where is the learned man?” [Alternative: “the scribe?”]

Where is the one who weighs the words of the law?

Where is the teacher of little ones?

You shall not see the shameless people [Note: Several manuscript codices, together with the Saint-Germain Canon, read *populum imprudentem*, “an imprudent people”; but from Jerome’s Commentaries it is certain that the reading should be *impudentem*, “shameless,” by which he means the Jewish people, or the philosophers and orators of the world, who [Col. 0808D] applaud themselves for their secular learning and eloquence. MART. — The Palatine manuscript and others, examined both by us and by Martianay, read *imprudentem*. We discussed this reading earlier in the commentary.],

a people of deep speech,

so that you cannot understand the eloquence of its language,

in which there is no wisdom.

[Col. 0809A] Look upon Zion, the city of our solemn assembly:

your eyes shall see Jerusalem, a wealthy dwelling,

a tent that shall never be moved;

its stakes shall never be removed forever,

and none of its cords shall be broken.

For only there is our magnificent Lord:

a place of rivers,

of very broad and open streams.

No galley of oars shall pass through it,

nor shall a large trireme cross it.

For the Lord is our judge,

the Lord is our lawgiver,

the Lord is our king:

he himself will save us.

Your cords have been loosened,

but they shall not prevail.

So shall your mast be [Note: [Col. 0809D] The Hebrew nevertheless has “their mast,” but perhaps the holy Father preferred “your” according to the Septuagint, ὁ ἱστός σου, “your mast.”]

so that you cannot spread the standard.

Then the spoil of abundant plunder shall be divided;

[Col. 0809B] the lame shall seize the prey.

Nor shall the inhabitant say, “I am languishing”:

the iniquity of the people who dwell in it shall be taken away.

### Chapter XXXIV

Draw near, nations, and hear;

and peoples, pay attention.

Let the earth and its fullness hear,

the world and all its offspring.

For the indignation of the Lord is against all nations,

and fury against all their armies:

he killed them and gave them over to slaughter [Al. omits *eos*, “them”].

Their slain shall be cast out,

and stench shall rise from their corpses.

The mountains shall melt with their blood.

And all the army of heaven shall waste away,

and they shall be folded up like a book of heaven;

and all their army shall fall away,

as a leaf falls from the vine and from the fig tree.

[Col. 0809C] For my sword is drunk in heaven.

Behold, it shall descend upon Idumea,

and upon the people destined for my slaughter, for judgment.

The sword of the Lord is filled with blood; it is fattened

with fat,

with the blood of lambs and goats,

with the blood of the marrow-filled rams.

For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bosra,

and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.

And unicorns shall descend with them,

and bulls with the mighty.

Their land shall be drunk with blood,

and their soil with the fat of the fattened animals.

For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance,

the year of recompense for the judgment of Zion.

And its streams shall be turned into pitch,

and its soil into sulfur.

And its land shall become burning pitch night and day;

it shall not be extinguished forever.

Its smoke shall rise from generation to generation;

it shall be desolate forever and ever,

[Col. 0809D] and no one shall pass through it.

And the pelican and the hedgehog shall possess it;

the ibis and the raven shall dwell there.

And a measuring line shall be stretched over it, to reduce it to

nothing,

and a plumb line, for desolation.

Its nobles shall not be there;

[Col. 0810A] rather, they shall call for a king,

and all its princes shall come to nothing.

And thorns and nettles shall spring up in its houses,

and the thorn-bush in its fortifications.

And it shall become a lair of dragons,

and a pasture for ostriches.

And demons shall meet the onocentaurs [Note: [Col. 0809D] The ancient copyists do not divide this verse correctly; for in manuscript codices it is read in this way: “And demons shall meet; the onocentaur and the hairy one shall call to one another.” Our Vulgate therefore retains the true reading, as Jerome’s words in his Commentary on this passage of Isaiah make very clear: “And they shall meet one another there, according to the Septuagint, various phantoms of demons; or, as all the others translated according to the Hebrew, *siim* and *iim*, onocentaurs and hairy creatures, and the lamia, which are described in the fables of the Gentiles and the inventions of poets.” MART.],

and the hairy creature shall call to the other.

There the lamia shall lie [Al. shall lie down],

and shall find rest for itself.

There the hedgehog shall make its lair,

and shall nourish its young,

and shall burrow around it and shelter in its shade.

There the kites shall gather,

one to another.

Seek diligently in the book of the Lord and read:

not one of them shall be missing;

one shall not seek another,

for what has proceeded from my mouth, he himself commanded,

[Col. 0810B] and his spirit itself gathered them.

And he himself cast lots for them,

and his hand divided it among them by measure.

They shall possess it forever;

from generation to generation they shall dwell in it.

### Chapter XXXV

The desert and the trackless land shall rejoice,

and the wilderness shall exult and blossom like a lily.

It shall blossom abundantly,

and shall exult, exulting and praising.

The glory of Lebanon has been given to it,

the beauty of Carmel and Sharon.

They shall see the glory of the Lord,

and the beauty of our God.

Strengthen the slack hands,

and make firm the weak knees.

Say to the fainthearted:

“Take courage; do not fear.

Behold, your God will bring vengeance and recompense.

God himself will come and save you.”

[Col. 0810C] Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened,

and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.

Then the lame shall leap like a deer,

and the tongue of the mute shall be opened.

For waters have burst forth in the desert,

and torrents in the wilderness.

And what was dry shall become a pool,

and the thirsty land, springs of water.

In the lairs where dragons formerly dwelt,

there shall arise the greenness of reeds and rushes.

And there shall be a path and a road,

and it shall be called the holy way.

The unclean shall not pass through it,

and this shall be the straight road for us [Vulg. “for you”] [Note: [Col. 0810D] Thus the manuscripts read, a reading supported by Saint Jerome’s exposition in Book X of his Commentaries. In Hebrew it is *lamo*, that is, “for them.” Perhaps, instead of “for us,” the Vulgate has “for you.” MART.],

so that fools shall not go astray on it.

There shall be no lion there,

and no savage beast shall ascend it,

nor shall it be found there.

And those who have been liberated shall walk [Al. adds “on it”],

those redeemed by the Lord.

They shall return and come to Zion with praise,

and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads.

They shall obtain joy and gladness,

and sorrow and groaning shall flee away.

### Chapter XXXVI

And it came to pass in the fourteenth year

of King Hezekiah

that Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

[Col. 0811A] And the king of the Assyrians sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a large force,

and he stood by the conduit of the upper pool on the road

to the fuller’s field.

And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the palace, went out to him,

and Shebna the scribe,

and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder.

And Rabshakeh said to them:

“Say to Hezekiah:

‘Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians:

What is this confidence in which you trust?

Or by what counsel or strength do you intend to rebel?

In whom do you place your trust, since you have revolted from me?

Behold, you trust in that broken reed-staff, Egypt,

on which, if a man leans, it will enter his hand

and pierce it.

So is Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to all who trust in him.

But if you answer me, “We trust in the Lord

[Col. 0811B] our God,”

is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed,

and who said to Judah and Jerusalem,

“You shall worship before this altar”?

And now surrender yourself to my lord, the king of the Assyrians,

and I will give you two thousand horses,

if you are able, of yourself, to provide riders for them.

And how will you withstand the face of one governor from

the least of my lord’s servants?

But if you trust in Egypt, in chariots and horsemen,

then now, was it without the Lord that I came up against this land

to destroy it?

The Lord said to me:

“Go up against this land and destroy it.”’”

And Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh:

“Speak to your servants in the Syrian language,

for we understand it.

[Col. 0811C] Do not speak to us in Judean in the hearing of the people

who are on the wall.”

And Rabshakeh said to them:

“Was it to your master and to you that my master sent me to speak all these words,

and not rather to the men who sit on the wall,

so that they may eat their own excrement

and drink the urine of their feet with you?”

And Rabshakeh stood and cried out in a loud voice in Judean,

and said:

“Hear the words of the great king,

the king of the Assyrians.

Thus says the king:

‘Let not Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver

you.

And let not Hezekiah give you confidence in the Lord, saying:

“The Lord will certainly deliver us;

this city shall not be given into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.”

Do not listen to Hezekiah.

[Col. 0811D] For thus says the king of the Assyrians:

Make peace with me and come out to me,

and let each man eat from his own vine,

and each man from his own fig tree,

and let each man drink the water of his own cistern,

until I come and take you to a land like your land

[Al. “similar to your land”],

a land of grain and wine,

a land of bread and vineyards.

And let not Hezekiah trouble you, saying:

“The Lord will deliver us.”

Have the gods of the nations each delivered his own land

from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?

[Col. 0812A] Where is the god of Hamath and of Arpad?

Where is the god of Sepharvaim?

Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?

Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his land

from my hand?’”

And they were silent, so that the Lord might deliver Jerusalem from my hand,

and they did not answer him a word.

For the king had commanded, saying:

“Do not answer him.”

And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the palace,

and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, entered

to Hezekiah with torn garments,

and reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.

### Chapter XXXVII

And it came to pass, when King Hezekiah heard this,

that he tore his garments, covered himself with sackcloth,

and entered the house of the Lord [Al. “of God”].

And he sent Eliakim, who was over the palace, and Shebna

[Col. 0812B] the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered

with sackcloth, to Isaiah son of Amos the prophet [Al.

“of the prophet”],

and they said to him:

“Thus says Hezekiah:

‘This is a day of tribulation [Note: [Col. 0811D] The Saint-Germain Canon has: “A day of tribulation and distress, and corruption, and blasphemy”; but the word “distress” is redundant and is not read in the Commentaries. MART.],

and correction,

and blasphemy.

For the children have come to the point of birth,

but there is no strength for the woman in labor [Al. “for giving birth”].

Perhaps the Lord your God will hear the words of Rabshakeh,

whom the king of the Assyrians, his lord, sent to blaspheme the living God

and to reproach him with the words that the Lord your God has heard.

Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant

that has been found.’”

And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

[Col. 0812C] And Isaiah said to them:

“Thus shall you say to your lord:

‘Thus says the Lord:

Do not fear because of the words that you heard,

with which the young men of the king of the Assyrians blasphemed me.

Behold, I will put a spirit in him,

and he shall hear a report and return to his own land,

and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.’”

Rabshakeh returned,

and found the king of the Assyrians fighting against

Libnah.

For he had heard that he had departed from Lachish,

and he heard people saying concerning [Note: [Col. 0812D] The Carcassonne Canon reads *Tharsa* in the sacred text, but in the margin it has this annotation: that is, “Tirhakah.” MART.]

Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia:

“He has gone out to fight against you.”

When he heard this, he sent messengers to Hezekiah,

saying:

“Thus shall you say to Hezekiah, king of Judah:

‘Let not your God deceive you,

in whom you trust, saying:

“Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.”

[Col. 0812D] Behold, you have heard all that the kings of the Assyrians did

to all the lands that they overthrew;

and can you be delivered?

Have the gods of the nations delivered those whom my fathers overthrew?

Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the sons of Eden who were

in Telassar?

Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad,

and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Ana, and of Ava?’”

And Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers,

and read them,

and went up to the house of the Lord,

and Hezekiah spread them out before the Lord [Al. omits “Hezekiah”].

[Col. 0813A] And Hezekiah prayed to the Lord, saying:

“Lord of hosts, God of Israel, who sit upon

the cherubim,

you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth;

you made heaven and earth.

Incline your ear, O Lord, and hear.

Open your eyes, O Lord, and see,

and hear all the words of Sennacherib that he sent

to blaspheme the living God.

Truly, O Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have laid waste lands and their regions,

and have given their gods to the fire.

For they were not gods,

but the works of human hands,

wood and stone;

and they destroyed them.

And now, O Lord our God, save us from his hand,

[Col. 0813B] so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know

that you alone are the Lord [Al. “God”].”

And Isaiah son of Amos sent to Hezekiah, saying:

“Thus says the Lord God of Israel:

‘Because you prayed to me concerning Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians,

this is the word that the Lord has spoken concerning him:

He has despised you

and mocked you, virgin daughter of Zion;

behind you he has shaken his head, daughter of Jerusalem.

Whom have you reproached, and whom have you blasphemed?

Against whom have you raised your voice [Al. adds “your”],

and lifted up the height of your eyes?

Against the Holy One of Israel.

By the hand of your servants you have reproached the Lord,

and you have said:

“With the multitude of my chariots I have gone up to the height of the mountains, the ridges of Lebanon.

And I shall cut down its lofty cedars,

[Col. 0813C] and its choice fir trees.

I shall enter the height of its summit,

its forest of Carmel.

I dug, and I drank water,

and with the sole of my foot I dried up all the streams of the embankments.”

Have you not heard what I did to it long ago?

From ancient days I formed it,

and now I have brought it [Al. adds “them”; perhaps “it,” from the Hebrew].

And it came to be for the uprooting of contending hills

and fortified cities.

Their inhabitants, with weakened hands, trembled,

and were confounded.

They became like the grass of the field,

and the green grass of the pasture,

and the grass of the rooftops, which withered before it matured.

I know your dwelling,

your going out and your coming in,

[Col. 0813D] and your madness against me.

Because you raged against me,

your arrogance has risen into my ears.

Therefore I will put a ring in your nostrils

and a bridle on your lips,

and I will bring you back by the way by which you came.

And this shall be a sign for you:

This year eat what grows of its own accord;

in the second year feed on the fruit.

But in the third year sow and reap,

plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.

And what has been saved from the house of Judah,

and what remains, shall send down roots,

and shall produce fruit above.

For from Jerusalem a remnant shall go forth,

and salvation from Mount Zion.

The zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this.

Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians:

[Col. 0814A] “He shall not enter this city,

and he shall not shoot an arrow there,

and he shall not seize it with a shield,

and he shall not cast up a rampart around it.

By the way by which he came [Al. “shall come”],

by that same way he shall return,

and he shall not enter this city,” says the Lord.

“And I will protect this city, so that I may save it [Al. “and I will save it”]

for my own sake

and for the sake of David my servant.”

And the angel of the Lord [Al. “of God”] went out

and struck one hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians.

And they rose in the morning,

and behold, all were corpses of the dead.

And he went out and departed,

and Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, returned and dwelt in Nineveh.

And it came to pass, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nefrach,

[Col. 0814B] that Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, struck him with the sword.

And they fled into the land of Ararat,

and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

### Chapter XXXVIII

In those days Hezekiah became sick unto death.

And Isaiah son of Amos the prophet entered to him,

and said:

“Thus says the Lord:

Set your house in order,

for you shall die and not live.”

And Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall,

and prayed to the Lord, and said:

“I beseech you, O Lord,

remember, I ask,

how I have walked before you in truth,

and with a perfect heart,

and have done what is good in your eyes.”

And Hezekiah wept with great weeping.

And the word of the Lord came to Isaiah, saying:

[Col. 0814C] “Go and say to Hezekiah:

‘Thus says the Lord God of David your father:

I have heard your prayer;

I have seen your tears.

Behold, I will add fifteen years to your days,

and I will deliver you and this city

from the hand of the king of the Assyrians,

and I will protect it.

And this shall be a sign to you from the Lord,

that the Lord will do this word which he has spoken:

Behold, I will cause the shadow of the lines,

by which it descends on the sundial of Ahaz in the sun,

to turn backward ten lines.’”

And it turned back ten lines,

and the sun returned ten lines,

along the steps by which it had descended.

## The Writing of Hezekiah, King of Judah

When he had been sick and recovered from his illness.

[Col. 0814D] I said: “In the middle of my days I shall go to the gates of the underworld.

I sought the remainder of my years.

I said: I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living.

I shall no longer look upon a human being

or an inhabitant of rest.

My generation has been taken away

and rolled up from me like a shepherd’s tent.

My life has been cut off like a weaver’s thread.

While I was still weaving, he cut me off.

From morning until evening you will finish me.

I hoped until morning;

like a lion, so he crushed all my bones.

From morning until evening you will finish me.

Like a swallow’s fledgling, so I shall cry out;

I shall meditate like a dove.

My eyes have grown weak,

[Col. 0815A] looking upward.

Lord, I am oppressed;

answer for me.

What shall I say, or what shall he answer me, since he himself has done it?

I shall review [Al. “reckon”] all my years

in the bitterness of my soul.

O Lord, if one lives in this way,

and in such things is the life of my spirit,

you will correct me and give me life.

Behold, my bitterness is most bitter in peace.

But you have delivered my soul so that it would not perish;

you have cast all my sins behind your back.

For the underworld shall not confess to you,

nor shall death praise you.

Those who descend into the pit shall not hope for your truth.

The living, the living—he himself shall confess to you,

as I do today.

The father shall make your truth known to his children.

Lord, save me,

[Col. 0815B] and we shall sing our psalms all the days of our life

in the house of the Lord.”

And Isaiah commanded that they take a mass of figs

and apply it as a poultice to the wound,

and he was healed.

And Hezekiah said:

“What shall be the sign that I shall go up to the house of the Lord?”

### Chapter XXXIX

At that time

Merodach-baladan, son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent books and gifts to Hezekiah;

for he had heard that he had been sick and recovered.

Hezekiah rejoiced over them,

and showed them the chamber of spices,

and of silver and gold,

and perfumes,

and the finest ointment,

and all the storerooms of his furnishings,

and everything that was found in his treasuries.

There was nothing that Hezekiah did not show them

in his house,

[Col. 0815C] and in all his power.

Then Isaiah the prophet entered to King Hezekiah,

and said to him:

“What did these men say,

and from where did they come to you?”

And Hezekiah said:

“They came to me from a distant land,

from Babylon.”

And he said:

“What did they see in your house?”

And Hezekiah said:

“They saw everything that is in my house.

There was nothing that I did not show them in my treasuries.”

And Isaiah said to Hezekiah:

“Hear the word of the Lord of hosts:

Behold, days shall come,

and everything that is in your house shall be taken away,

and what your fathers have stored up until this day,

to Babylon.

Nothing shall be left,” says the Lord.

“And from your sons who shall come from you, whom you shall beget,

they shall take them,

and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”

And Hezekiah said to Isaiah:

“Good is the word of the Lord which he has spoken.”

And he said:

“Let there be only peace and truth in my days.”

### Chapter XL

“Comfort, comfort my people,”

says your God.

“Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and call to her,

for her wickedness has been completed,

her iniquity has been forgiven.

She has received from the hand of the Lord double

for all her sins.”

A voice of one crying in the desert:

“Prepare the way of the Lord;

make straight in the wilderness the paths of our God.

[Col. 0816A] Every valley shall be exalted,

and every mountain and hill shall be humbled.

And crooked things shall become straight,

and rough ways, level roads.

And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed,

and all flesh together shall see that the mouth of the Lord has spoken.”

A voice saying: “Cry out.”

And I said:

“What shall I cry?”

“All flesh is grass,

and all its glory is like the flower of the field.

The grass has withered, and the flower has fallen,

because the spirit of the Lord blew upon it.

Truly, the people are grass.

The grass has withered, and the flower has fallen;

but the word of our Lord shall stand forever.”

Go up upon a high mountain,

you who proclaim good news to Zion.

Lift up your voice with strength,

[Col. 0816B] you who proclaim good news to Jerusalem.

Lift it up; do not fear.

Say to the cities of Judah:

“Behold your God.

Behold, the Lord God will come with strength,

and his arm shall rule.

Behold, his reward is with him,

and his work is before him.

As a shepherd he shall feed his flock.

With his arm he shall gather the lambs,

and he shall lift them in his bosom.

He himself shall carry the pregnant ewes.”

Who measured the waters in his hollow hand,

and weighed the heavens with a span?

Who enclosed the mass of the earth with three fingers,

and weighed the mountains in a balance,

and the hills on scales?

Who has helped the spirit of the Lord?

Or who was his counselor,

[Col. 0816C] and showed him?

With whom did he take counsel and instruct him,

and teach him the path of justice,

and educate him in knowledge,

and show him the way of understanding?

Behold, the nations are like a drop from a bucket,

and are counted as a speck on the scales.

Behold, the islands are like a tiny grain of dust.

Lebanon would not suffice for burning,

nor would its animals suffice for a burnt offering.

All nations are as though they did not exist before him,

and are counted by him as nothing and emptiness.

To whom, then, have you likened God?

Or what image will you set up for him?

Has a craftsman cast an idol?

Or has a goldsmith shaped it in gold,

and a silversmith in sheets of silver?

Perhaps the skillful artisan has chosen wood that does not rot;

he seeks [Al. “and will seek”] how to establish an image that will not move.

[Col. 0816D] Do you not know [Al. “will you not know”]?

Have you not heard [Al. “will you not hear”]?

Has it not been announced to you from the beginning?

Have you not understood the foundations of the earth?

He who sits above the circle of the earth,

whose inhabitants are like grasshoppers,

who stretches out the heavens as though they were nothing,

and spreads them like a tent for dwelling,

who brings those who search out secret things to nothing,

and makes the judges of the earth as emptiness.

Indeed, they have neither been planted nor sown,

nor has their trunk taken root in the earth.

Suddenly he blew upon them, and they withered,

and a whirlwind shall carry them away like stubble.

And to whom have you likened me,

and equated me? says the Holy One.

[Col. 0817A] Lift up your eyes on high,

and see who created these things.

He brings out their army by number,

and calls them all by name.

Because of the greatness of his strength and might,

and of his power,

not one was missing.

Why do you say, Jacob,

and speak, Israel:

“My way is hidden from the Lord,

and my judgment has passed [Al. “shall pass”] from my God”?

Do you not know, or have you not heard?

The eternal God, the Lord,

who created the boundaries of the earth,

shall not fail or grow weary,

and there is no searching out his wisdom.

He gives strength to the weary,

and multiplies strength and might for those who have none [Al. “who have no strength and might,” etc.].

[Col. 0817B] Boys shall fail and grow weary,

and young men shall fall in weakness.

But those who hope in the Lord shall renew their strength.

They shall take wings like eagles;

they shall run and not grow weary;

they shall walk and not fail.

### Chapter XLI

“Let the islands keep silence before me,

and let the nations renew their strength.

Let them draw near,

and then let them speak.

Together let us approach for judgment.

Who raised up the righteous one from the east,

called him to follow him?

He shall give nations into his presence,

and he shall rule over kings.

He shall give them like dust to his sword,

like stubble carried by the wind to his bow.

He shall pursue them;

he shall pass in peace.

No path shall appear beneath his feet.

[Col. 0817C] Who has done and made these things,

calling generations from the beginning?

I, the Lord,

I am first and last.

The islands saw and were afraid;

the ends of the earth were astonished.

They drew near and came.

Each one shall help his neighbor,

and shall say to his brother: ‘Take courage.’

The bronze-worker strengthened him, striking him with the hammer,

the man who was forging at that time,

saying: ‘The soldering is good.’

And he strengthened him with nails,

so that it would not move [Al. “be moved”].

And you, Israel, my servant;

Jacob, whom I have chosen;

the offspring of Abraham, my friend.

In you I took hold from the ends of the earth,

and from its distant places I called you,

[Col. 0817D] and I said to you:

‘You are my servant.

I have chosen you and have not rejected you.

Do not fear, for I am with you.

Do not turn aside, for I am your God.

I have strengthened you and helped you,

and the right hand of my righteous one has upheld you.’

Behold, all who fight against you shall be confounded

and put to shame.

They shall be as though they did not exist,

and the men who oppose you shall perish.

You shall seek them and shall not find them,

your rebellious men [Al. “your men”];

[Col. 0818A] they shall be as though they did not exist,

and like the destruction of men fighting against you [Note: [Col. 0817D] Copies of the Canon of the Hebrew truth, together with other older manuscripts of the Bible, read this way: “and like the destruction of a man fighting against you”; but this is a copyists’ error, as is plainly evident from the Hebrew text and from Jerome’s Commentaries. MART.].

For I am the Lord your God,

holding your hand

and saying to you:

‘Do not fear;

I have helped you.

Do not fear, worm of Jacob,

you who are dead from Israel.

I have helped you,’ says the Lord,

and your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.

I have made you like a new threshing wagon,

with serrated teeth.

You shall thresh mountains and crush them,

and you shall make the hills like dust.

You shall winnow them, and the wind shall carry them away,

and the whirlwind shall scatter them.

And you shall exult in the Lord,

and rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.’”

[Col. 0818B] The needy and poor seek water, and there is none.

Their tongue has dried up with thirst.

I, the Lord, will hear them;

I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.

I will open rivers on the bare hills,

and springs in the midst of the fields.

I will make the desert into pools of water,

and the trackless land into streams of water.

I will place in the wilderness cedar,

and thorn, and myrtle, and olive wood.

I will place in the desert fir,

elm, and boxwood together,

so that they may see and know,

and reflect and understand together,

that the hand of the Lord has done this,

and the Holy One of Israel has created it.

“Bring your judgment near,” says the Lord.

“Bring forward whatever you may perhaps have,”

said the King of Jacob.

Let them draw near and announce to us whatever is to come.

[Col. 0818C] Announce the former things that happened,

and we shall set our hearts upon them

and know their final outcome.

Declare to us the things that are to come.

Announce what will happen in the future,

and we shall know that you are gods.

Do good or evil, if you can;

let us speak and see together.

Behold, you are from nothing [Al. “for nothing”],

and your work is from what does not exist.

The one who chose you is an abomination.

He raised up from the north,

and came [Al. “shall come”] from the rising of the sun.

He shall call upon my name,

and he shall bring rulers as though they were clay,

like a potter treading the earth.

Who announced it from the beginning, so that we might know,

and from the outset, so that we might say: “You are righteous”?

There is no one announcing,

nor proclaiming,

nor hearing your words.

The first shall say to Zion: “Behold, they are here,”

and I shall give an evangelist to Jerusalem.

And I looked, and there was no one,

nor was there among these anyone who entered into counsel

or who, when questioned, answered a word.

Behold, they are all unjust,

and their works are empty.

Their idols are wind and emptiness.

### Chapter XLII

[Note: [Col. 0818D] Saint Jerome himself confirms in his Letter to Algasius, Question 2, that he translated the first five verses of this chapter from the Hebrew in the form in which they appear here, except that there he reads “boy” instead of “servant.”]

Behold my servant; I will uphold him.

My chosen one, in whom my soul is well pleased.

I have given my spirit upon him;

[Col. 0819A] he shall bring forth judgment to the nations.

He shall not cry out, nor accept a person’s status,

nor shall his voice be heard outside.

He shall not break a crushed reed,

and he shall not extinguish a smoking wick.

In truth he shall bring forth judgment.

He shall not be sad or troubled

until he establishes judgment on the earth,

and the islands shall await his law.

Thus says the Lord God,

who creates the heavens and stretches them out,

who establishes the earth and what springs from it,

who gives breath to the people upon it,

and spirit to those who walk upon it.

I, the Lord, have called you in righteousness,

and I have taken your hand and preserved you.

And I have given you as a covenant for the people,

as a light for the nations,

to open the eyes of the blind,

to bring out the bound from confinement,

from the prison house those sitting in darkness.

[Col. 0819B] I am the Lord; this is my name.

I shall not give my glory to another,

nor my praise to idols.

The former things—behold, they have come.

And I announce new things.

Before they arise,

I will make them heard by you.

Sing a new song to the Lord,

his praise from the ends of the earth.

You who descend upon the sea and its fullness,

the islands and their inhabitants.

Let the desert and its cities lift up their voice [Al. “let it lift up”].

In the houses Cedar shall dwell.

Praise, inhabitants of the Rock;

from the summit of the mountains they shall cry out.

They shall give glory to the Lord,

and announce his praise in the islands.

The Lord shall go out like a strong man;

like a warrior he shall stir up zeal.

He shall shout and cry out;

he shall prevail against his enemies.

[Col. 0819C] I have been silent;

I have always kept still;

I have been patient.

Like a woman in labor, I shall speak.

I shall scatter and consume together.

I shall lay waste mountains and hills,

and dry up all their grass.

And I shall turn rivers into islands,

and dry up pools.

And I shall lead the blind by a way they do not know,

and I shall make them walk on paths they have not known [Al. “do not know”].

I shall set darkness before them as light,

and crooked things as straight.

I have done these things for them,

and I have not abandoned them.

They have turned backward.

Let those who trust in idols be utterly confounded,

those who say to a cast image, “You are our gods.”

Deaf ones, hear;

blind ones, look and see.

[Col. 0819D] Who is blind except my servant?

And who is deaf except the one to whom I sent my messengers?

Who is blind except the one who has been sold?

And who is blind except the servant of the Lord?

You who see many things,

will you not observe?

You who have open ears,

will you not hear?

And the Lord willed to sanctify him,

and to magnify and exalt the law.

But he himself is a plundered and ravaged people;

a snare for all the young men,

and they have been hidden in prison houses.

They have become a prey,

and there is no one to deliver;

a spoil,

and there is no one who says, “Restore.”

Who among you will hear this,

[Col. 0820A] attend and listen to what is to come?

Who gave Jacob over to plunder,

and Israel to those who ravaged him?

Was it not the Lord,

the one against whom we sinned?

And they were unwilling to walk in his ways,

and they did not hear his law.

And he poured out upon him the indignation of his anger,

and a strong war.

And he burned him all around, and he did not know;

and he set him on fire, and he did not understand.

### Chapter XLIII

And now thus says the Lord,

who created you, Jacob,

and formed you, Israel:

Do not fear, for I have redeemed you,

and I have called you by your name [Al. adds “you”].

You are mine.

When you pass through the waters, I shall be with you,

and the rivers shall not overwhelm you.

When you walk through fire, you shall not be burned,

and the flame shall not consume you.

[Col. 0820B] For I am the Lord your God,

the Holy One of Israel, your savior.

I have given Egypt as your ransom,

Ethiopia and Seba in your place.

Since you became honorable in my eyes

and glorious,

I have loved you.

And I shall give men for you,

and peoples for your life.

Do not fear, for I am with you.

From the east I shall bring your offspring,

and from the west I shall gather you.

I shall say to the north: “Give,”

and to the south: “Do not hinder.”

Bring my sons from far away,

and my daughters from the ends of the earth,

and everyone who calls upon my name.

I created him for my glory,

I formed him and made him.

[Col. 0820C] Bring out the blind people who have eyes,

and the deaf who have ears.

All the nations have gathered together,

and the tribes have assembled.

Who among you will announce this,

and make us hear the former things?

Let them produce their witnesses and be justified;

let them hear and say: “Truly.”

“You are my witnesses,” says the Lord,

“and my servant whom I have chosen,

so that you may know and believe me,

and understand that I am he.

Before me no god was formed,

and after me there shall be none.

I am, I am the Lord,

and there is no savior besides me.

I announced and saved;

I made it heard,

and there was no stranger among you.

You are my witnesses,” says the Lord,

[Col. 0820D] “and I am God.

And from the beginning I am he,

and there is no one who can deliver from my hand.

I shall work,

and who will turn it aside?”

Thus says the Lord, your redeemer,

the Holy One of Israel:

“For your sake I sent to Babylon,

and I brought down the bars”
all,

and the Chaldeans, glorying in their ships.

I, the Lord, your Holy One,

creating Israel, your king.

Thus says the Lord,

who made a way in the sea

and a path in the mighty waters;

who brought forth chariot and horse,

army and warrior:

they lay down together and did not rise again;

they were crushed like flax and extinguished.

[Col. 0821A] Do not remember former things,

and do not consider ancient events.

Behold, I am doing something new,

and now it shall spring forth;

surely you will recognize it.

I shall make a way in the wilderness,

and rivers in the wasteland.

The wild beast of the field will glorify me,

the dragons and the ostriches,

because I have given waters in the wilderness,

rivers in the wasteland,

to give drink to my people,

my chosen one.

I formed this people for myself;

it shall proclaim my praise.

You did not call upon me, Jacob,

nor did you labor for me, Israel.

You did not offer me the ram of your burnt offering,

and you did not glorify me with your sacrifices.

I did not make you serve in an offering,

nor did I burden you with incense.

You did not buy me calamus with silver,

[Col. 0821B] and you did not make me drunk with the fat of your victims.

Yet you made me serve in your sins;

you gave me labor in your iniquities.

I, I am he

who blots out your iniquities for my own sake,

and I will not remember your sins.

Remind me, and let us be judged together;

tell me if you have anything by which you may be justified.

Your first father sinned,

and your interpreters transgressed against me.

And I profaned the holy princes;

I gave Jacob to destruction,

and Israel to blasphemy.

[Cap. XLIV.] And now hear, Jacob, my servant,

and Israel, whom I have chosen.

Thus says the Lord,

who made and formed you,

your helper from the womb:

Do not fear, my servant Jacob,

and you, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.

[Col. 0821C] For I will pour out waters upon the thirsty,

and streams upon the dry ground.

I will pour out my spirit upon your offspring,

and my blessing upon your descendants.

And they shall spring up among the grass,

like willows beside flowing waters.

One will say, “I belong to the Lord”;

another will call himself by the name of Jacob;

another will write with his hand, “For the Lord”;

and in the name of Israel he will be designated.

Thus says the Lord,

the King of Israel,

and its redeemer, the Lord of hosts:

I am the first, and I am the last,

and besides me there is no God.

Who is like me?

Let him call and declare it,

and set forth the order before me,

from the time when I established the ancient people.

Let them announce the things that are coming

and those that will happen to them.

[Col. 0821D] Do not fear, nor be troubled.

From that time I made you hear and announced it:

You are my witnesses.

Is there a God besides me,

or a maker whom I have not known?

All the makers of idols are nothing,

and their most beloved works will not profit them.

They are their own witnesses,

because they neither see nor understand,

so that they may be put to shame.

Who has formed a god,

or cast a sculpted image for no useful purpose?

Behold, all its associates will be ashamed,

for they are craftsmen from among men.

[Col. 0822A] They will all gather, stand,

and tremble,

and be ashamed together.

The smith has worked with the file;

he formed it in the coals

and with hammers,

and worked it with his strong arm.

He will hunger and grow weak;

he will not drink water,

and he will grow weary.

The woodworker stretches out the measuring line;

he shaped it with the plane.

He made it with angular tools

and rounded it with the compass.

He made the image of a man,

like a handsome human being

dwelling in a house.

He cut down cedars,

took holm oak and oak,

which had stood among the trees of the forest.

He planted a pine,

which the rain nourished,

and it became fuel for people.

He took some of it and warmed himself;

he kindled it and baked bread.

[Col. 0822B] But from the remainder he made a god and worshiped it;

he made a sculpted image

and bowed down before it.

He burned half of it in the fire,

and from half of it he ate meat.

He cooked a stew, was satisfied,

and warmed himself;

then he said:

“Ah! I am warm;

I have seen the fire.”

But from the remainder he made a god

and his sculpted image.

He bows before it,

worships it,

and entreats it, saying:

“Deliver me,

for you are my god.”

They neither knew nor understood,

for they have forgotten, so that their eyes do not see

and their heart does not understand.

They do not reflect in their mind,

nor do they know or perceive,

so as to say:

[Col. 0822C] “I burned half of it in the fire,

and I baked bread over its coals.

I roasted meat and ate it,

and from the remainder shall I make an idol?

Shall I fall down before a block of wood?”

Its portion is ashes;

an foolish heart has worshiped it,

and it will not deliver its soul,

nor will it say:

“Perhaps there is a lie in my right hand.”

Remember these things, Jacob and Israel,

for you are my servant.

I formed you;

you are my servant, Israel.

You shall not be forgotten by me [Alt.: do not forget me].

I have wiped away your iniquities like a cloud,

and your sins like a mist.

Return to me,

for I have redeemed you.

[Col. 0822D] Praise, O heavens,

[Note: Thus read both copies of the Canon of Hebrew Truth, as well as the sacred text in Jerome’s Commentaries. Other manuscript codices retain from the Septuagint the word “mercy”: “because he showed mercy,” or “because he had compassion.” MART.—The Palatine manuscript and the Vulgate books have more, according to the Septuagint: “because he showed mercy,” etc.] because the Lord has acted.

Shout for joy, ends of the earth;

resound, O mountains, with praise,

O forest and every tree in it,

for the Lord has redeemed Jacob,

and Israel will glory.

Thus says the Lord, your redeemer,

and your former from the womb:

I am the Lord, making all things,

stretching out the heavens alone,

establishing the earth,

and there is no one with me.

I frustrate the signs of diviners,

[Col. 0823A] and turn soothsayers into madness.

I turn wise men backward

and make their knowledge foolish.

I confirm the word of my servant

and fulfill the counsel of my messengers,

who say to Jerusalem,

“You shall be inhabited,”

and to the cities of Judah,

“You shall be rebuilt.”

I shall raise up its desolate places.

I say to the deep,

“Be desolate,”

and to your rivers,

“I will dry you up.”

I say to Cyrus,

“You are my shepherd,

and you will fulfill all my will.”

I say to Jerusalem,

“You shall be rebuilt,”

and to the Temple,

“You shall be founded.”

[Cap. XLV.] Thus says the Lord to his anointed,

to Cyrus,

whose right hand I have grasped,

to subject nations before him

and turn the backs of kings.

And I will open doors before him,

and gates shall not be shut.

[Col. 0823B] I will go before you,

and humble the glorious ones of the earth.

I will shatter bronze doors

and break iron bars.

And I will give you hidden treasures

and secret stores,

so that you may know

that I am the Lord who calls you by name,

the God of Israel.

For the sake of my servant Jacob

and Israel, my chosen one,

I have called you by your name.

I have given you a title,

though you did not know me.

I am the Lord,

and there is no other [Note: All the ancient manuscripts read, “I am the Lord, and there is no other,” instead of “and there is no longer.” The Canon has “no longer” in the first hand. MART.—The same manuscript and others in Martianay’s possession have “other” instead of “longer,” which agrees with the Hebrew. Compare, if desired, the commentaries on this passage.] ;

besides me there is no God.

I girded you,

though you did not know me,

so that those from the rising of the sun

and those from the west may know

that there is none besides me.

I am the Lord,

[Col. 0823C] and there is no other,

forming light

and creating darkness,

making peace

and creating evil.

I am the Lord,

doing all these things.

Drip down, O heavens, from above,

and let the clouds rain the righteous one.

Let the earth be opened

and bring forth the Savior,

and let righteousness spring up together.

I, the Lord, have created him.

Woe to him who contends with his maker,

a potsherd among the potsherds of the earth.

Will the clay say to its potter,

“What are you doing?”

or, “Your work is without hands”?

Woe to him who says to his father,

“What are you begetting?”

and to a woman,

“What are you giving birth to?”

Thus says the Lord,

the Holy One of Israel,

its maker:

Ask me about the things to come;

concerning my sons

and concerning the work of my hands,

[Col. 0823D] command me.

[Note: “Command me” is read by the Canons and manuscripts as “you have commanded me”; but “command me” must be retained, as the copies of Jerome’s Commentaries prove. MART.]

I made the earth,

and I myself created the human being upon it.

My hands stretched out the heavens,

and I commanded all their host.

I raised him up for righteousness,

and I will direct all his ways.

He himself will build my city,

and he will release my captives,

[Col. 0824A] not for a price,

nor for gifts,

says the Lord God of hosts.

Thus says the Lord:

The labor of Egypt,

the trade of Ethiopia,

and the Sabeans,

tall men,

will cross over to you

and will be yours.

They will walk behind you;

bound with handcuffs,

they will proceed.

They will worship you

and entreat you:

“Surely God is in you,

and there is no other God besides you.”

Truly, you are a hidden God,

the God of Israel, the Savior.

They have all been put to shame

and disgraced;

together they have gone into confusion,

the makers of errors.

Israel has been saved by the Lord

with everlasting salvation.

You shall not be put to shame,

and you shall not be disgraced

for ever and ever.

For thus says the Lord,

who created the heavens;

he is God himself,

forming the earth and making it;

he himself is its maker.

He did not create it in vain;

he formed it to be inhabited [Alt.: so that it might be inhabited].

I am the Lord,

and there is no other.

I have not spoken in secret,

in a dark place of the earth.

I did not say to the offspring of Jacob,

“Seek me in vain.”

I am the Lord,

speaking righteousness

and announcing upright things.

Gather together, come,

and draw near together,

you who have been saved from the nations.

They knew nothing,

those who carry the wood of their sculpture

and entreat a god who cannot save.

Announce and come,

and deliberate together.

Who made this known from the beginning?

Who declared it beforehand from that time?

[Col. 0824C] Is it not I, the Lord,

and there is no God besides me,
a just God and a savior;
there is none except me.

Turn to me,

and you shall be saved,

all the ends of the earth,

for I am God,

and there is no other.

I have sworn by myself.

A word of righteousness shall go forth from my mouth,

and it shall not return.

For every knee shall bow to me,

and every tongue shall swear.

Therefore he will say in the Lord:

“Righteousness and dominion are mine.”

To him they will come,

and all who oppose him will be ashamed.

In the Lord all the offspring of Israel

shall be justified

and shall be praised.

[Cap. XLVI.] Bel is broken,

[Note: Through the scribes’ error, all manuscript books read “Bel has been cast,” instead of “Bel has been broken.” MART.]

[Col. 0824D] Nabo is crushed.

Their images have become burdens

for beasts and cattle;

your burdens are carried

as a heavy load,

even to weariness.

They have withered

and have been crushed together;

they could not save the one carrying them,

and their own soul shall go into captivity.

Hear me, house of Jacob,

and all the remnant of the house of Israel,

you who have been carried from my womb,

who have been borne from my uterus.

Even to old age I am the same,

and even to gray hairs I will carry you.

I made you,

and I will bear you;

I will carry you

and save you.

To whom have you likened me,

made me equal,

compared me,

and made me similar?

You who bring gold from a purse

and weigh silver on a scale,

hiring a goldsmith

to make a god.

Then they fall down

and worship.

They carry it on their shoulders,

bearing it

and setting it in its place.

It will stand,

and it will not move from its place.

Even when they cry out to it,

it will not hear;

it will not save them from distress.

Remember this,

and be ashamed [Note: I would prefer “be established,” as the holy Father himself reads it in his Commentary according to the Hebrew, “and be strong.” MART.];

return to your heart,

you transgressors.

Remember the former age,

for I am God,

and there is no other God,

nor is there one like me.

I announce the end from the beginning,

[Col. 0825B] and from the outset the things that have not yet been done,

saying:

“My counsel shall stand,

and all my will shall be done.”

I call the bird from the east,

and from a distant land

the man of my will.

I have spoken,

and I will bring it about;

I have created it,

and I will do it.

Hear me, hard of heart,

you who are far from righteousness.

I have brought my righteousness near;

it will not be far away,

and my salvation will not delay.

I will give salvation in Zion

and my glory in Israel.

[Cap. XLVII.] Descend,

sit in the dust,

virgin daughter of Babylon;

sit on the ground.

There is no throne for the daughter of the Chaldeans,

for you shall no longer be called tender and delicate.

Take the millstone

and grind flour.

Uncover your shame;

strip your shoulder;

reveal your legs;

cross the rivers.

Your disgrace shall be uncovered,

and your shame shall be seen.

I will take vengeance,

and no one will resist me.

Our Redeemer,

the Lord of hosts is his name,

the Holy One of Israel.

[Note: Saint Jerome indicates the present verse in Book XIII of his Commentaries on Isaiah. MART.]

Sit silently

and enter darkness,

daughter of the Chaldeans,

for you shall no longer be called

mistress of kingdoms.

I was angry with my people;

I profaned my inheritance,

and gave them into your hand.

You showed them no mercies.

You laid an exceedingly heavy yoke upon the old man,

and said:

“I shall be mistress forever.”

You did not set these things upon your heart,

nor did you remember your end.

And now hear this,

you delicate one,

who dwells confidently,

who says in your heart:

“I am,

and there is no one besides me.”

I shall not sit as a widow,

and I shall not know childlessness.

These two things shall come upon you suddenly

in one day:

childlessness and widowhood.

All these things have come upon you

because of the multitude of your sorceries

and because of the exceedingly great power

of your enchantments [Alt.: exceedingly].

And you trusted in your wickedness,

and said:

[Col. 0826A] “There is no one who sees me.”

Your wisdom and your knowledge

have deceived you [Alt.: have deceived them].

And you said in your heart:

“I am,

and there is no other.”

Evil shall come upon you,

and you will not know its rising.

Calamity shall fall upon you,

which you will not be able to expiate.

Misery shall come upon you suddenly,

which you will not know.

Stand with your enchanters

and with the multitude of your sorceries,

in which you have labored from your youth,

if perhaps they may profit you,

or if you may be made stronger.

You have failed through the multitude of your counsels.

Let the astrologers of the heavens stand

and save you,

those who contemplated the stars

and reckoned the months,

so that from them they might announce

what is to come upon you.

[Col. 0826B] Behold, they have become like stubble;

fire has burned them.

They will not deliver their soul

from the hand of the flame.
