They are not coals

with which they may warm themselves,

nor a fire

beside which they may sit.

So have those with whom you labored become to you:

your merchants from your youth.

Each has wandered in his own way;

there is no one who can save you.

[Cap. XLVIII.] Hear this, house of Jacob,

who are called by the name of Israel

and have come forth from the waters of Judah,

you who swear by the name of the Lord

and remember the God of Israel,

not in truth nor in righteousness.

For they are called from the holy city

and have been established upon the God of Israel.

The Lord of hosts is his name.

I announced the former things from that time;

they went out from my mouth,

and I made them heard.

Suddenly I acted,

and they came to pass.

For I knew that you are hard,

that your neck is an iron sinew,

and your forehead bronze.

I announced it to you beforehand.

Before they came to pass,

I made them known to you,

lest you should say:

“My idols did these things;

my carved and cast images commanded them.”

You have heard it;

see everything.

But have you not announced it? [Alt.: did you not announce it?]

I made new things known to you beforehand,

things that had been preserved,

which you did not know.

Now they are created,

and not from that time;

even before the day,

and you did not hear them,

lest you should say:

“Behold, I knew them.”

You neither heard nor knew,

nor from that time was your ear opened.

[Col. 0826D] For I know that you will transgress

and transgress again,

and from the womb I called you a transgressor.

For the sake of my name

I will keep my wrath far away,

and for the sake of my praise

I will restrain you,

so that you may not perish.

Behold, I have refined you,

but not as silver.

I have chosen you in the furnace of poverty.

For my own sake,

for my own sake I will act,

so that I may not be blasphemed.

I will not give my glory to another.

Hear me, Jacob,

and Israel, whom I call.

I am he,

[Col. 0827A] I am the first,

and I am the last.

My hand also founded the earth,

and my right hand measured out the heavens.

I will call them [Alt.: I called them],

and they will stand together.

Gather together, all of you,

and hear.

Who among them announced these things?

The Lord loved him;

he will do his will in Babylon

and his arm among the Chaldeans.

I, I have spoken,

and I have called him.

I brought him,

and his way was made straight.

Draw near to me,

and hear this [Alt.: these things].

I have not spoken from the beginning in secret.

From the time before it came to be,

I was there.

And now the Lord God has sent me,

and his Spirit.

Thus says the Lord,

your redeemer,

the Holy One of Israel.

I am the Lord your God,

teaching you what is useful,

guiding you on the way in which you walk.

If only you had attended to my commandments!

Your peace would have become like a river,

and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.

Your offspring would have been like sand,

and the descendants of your womb like its pebbles.

Its name would not have perished,

nor would it have been destroyed from before me.

[Col. 0827B] Go forth from Babylon,

flee from the Chaldeans.

Announce with a voice of exultation;

proclaim this,

make it heard,

and carry it to the ends of the earth.

Say:

“The Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob.”

They did not thirst in the wilderness

when he led them out.

He brought water for them from the rock;

he split the rock,

and the waters flowed.

There is no peace for the wicked,

says the Lord.

[Cap. XLIX.] Hear, islands,

and pay attention, peoples from afar.

[Col. 0827C] The Lord called me from the womb;

from my mother’s belly

he remembered my name.

And he made my mouth like a sharp sword.

In the shadow of his hand

he protected me,

and he made me like a chosen arrow;

in his quiver

he hid me.

And he said to me:

“You are my servant, Israel,

for I will glory in you.”

And I said:

“I have labored in vain;

for no purpose

and in vain I have spent my strength.

Therefore my judgment is with the Lord,

and my labor with my God.”

And now the Lord says,

who formed me from the womb

as a servant for himself,

to bring Jacob back to him.

And Israel will not be gathered.

[Col. 0827D] Yet I have been glorified in the eyes of the Lord,

and my God has become my strength.

And he said:

“It is too little for you to be my servant

to raise up the tribes of Jacob

and to restore the remnants of Israel.

[Col. 0828A] I have given you [Note: Thus read the copies of the Canon of Hebrew Truth and Jerome’s Commentaries. Other manuscript books add, “Behold.” MART.] as a light to the nations,

that you may be my salvation

to the end of the earth.”

Thus says the Lord,

the redeemer of Israel,

his Holy One,

to the despised soul,

to the abhorred nation,

to the servant of rulers:

Kings will see

and rise;

princes will worship

because of the Lord,

for he is faithful,

and because of the Holy One of Israel,

who has chosen you.

Thus says the Lord:

“In an acceptable time I have heard you,

and on the day of salvation

I have helped you.

I have guarded you

and given you as a covenant to the people,

to raise up the earth

and possess the scattered inheritances,

to say to those who are bound,

‘Come out!’

and to those who are in darkness,

‘Show yourselves!’”

They shall feed along the roads,

and their pastures shall be in all the level places.

[Col. 0828B] They shall neither hunger nor thirst,

and heat and sun shall not strike them,

for their merciful one will guide them

and give them drink at springs of waters [Note: “He will carry them” must certainly be restored, as Saint Jerome wrote it. I have almost no doubt that this is how the Hebrew text and the Greek text, ἄξει, read it; many Latin manuscript copies of the Bible cited by Victorius in his Commentary also prefer “he will carry them.” The similarity of this verb to the printed “he will give them drink,” and especially the analogy of the context—“to springs of waters”—misled critics, so that they rashly dared to change the text according to their own judgment. MART.] .

And I will make all my mountains into a road,

and my paths shall be raised up.

Behold, these will come from afar,

and behold, those from the north and the sea,

and these from the land of the south.

Praise, O heavens,

and exult, O earth;

mountains, shout for joy with praise,

for the Lord has consoled his people,

and he will have mercy on his poor.

And Zion said:

“The Lord has abandoned me,

and the Lord has forgotten me.”

Can a woman forget her infant,

so as not to have compassion on the child of her womb?

And even if she should forget,

I nevertheless will not forget you.

[Col. 0828C] Behold, I have engraved you on my hands;

your walls are always before my eyes.

Your builders have come.

Those who destroy and devastate you

will go out from you [Alt.: and those who destroyed and devastated you].

Lift up your eyes all around

and see:

all these have gathered;

they have come to you.

As I live, says the Lord,

you will clothe yourself with all these

as with an ornament,

and you will put them around you like a bride.

For your desolate places,

your solitudes,

and the land of your ruins

will now be too narrow

because of their inhabitants,

and those who swallowed you

will be driven far away.

The children of your barrenness

will still say in your ears [Note: Here again we command that “sons” be read in the nominative, as Jerome himself prefers in his Commentary and as the Hebrew exemplar has it. The Greek version likewise has οἱ υἱοί, “sons.” Nevertheless, we do not deny that many Latin codices retain the corrupt reading “to the sons.” MART.] :

“The place is too narrow for me;

make room for me to dwell.”

And you will say in your heart:

“Who has begotten these for me?

I was barren and did not bear,

exiled and captive.

And who raised these?

I was abandoned and alone.

And these—[Note: In Hebrew it is written אֵיפֹה, *epho*, which taken together means “where”; but when divided into two words, namely אֵ, *e*, and פֹה, *pho*, it likewise means “where here.” Therefore, whether you call the word compound or read it separately, as we have already noted, Jerome’s interpretation is excellent. We have restored it here according to the copies of the Canon of Hebrew Truth and all the ancient manuscript codices. MART.] where were they?”

Thus says the Lord God:

[Col. 0829A] Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations,

and I will raise my sign to the peoples.

They will bring your sons in their arms,

and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will be your foster fathers,

and queens your nursing mothers.

With faces lowered to the earth,

they will worship you,

and lick the dust of your feet.

And you will know that I am the Lord,

and that those who await him

will not be ashamed.

Can spoil be taken from the strong,

or can what has been captured by the mighty

be rescued?

For thus says the Lord:

Indeed, the captivity of the strong will be taken away,

and what has been seized from the mighty

will be rescued.

I myself will judge those who judged you,

and I myself will save your children.

I will feed your enemies with their own flesh,

and they will become drunk with their own blood

as with new wine.

[Col. 0829B] And all flesh will know

that I am the Lord,

your Savior

and your redeemer,
the Mighty One of Jacob.

[Cap. L.] Thus says the Lord:

“Where is this bill of your mother’s divorce,

by which I dismissed her?

Or who is my creditor,

to whom I sold you?

Behold, you were sold because of your iniquities,

and because of your crimes

I dismissed your mother.

For I came,

and there was no man;

I called,

and there was no one who answered.

Has my hand become shortened

and small,

so that I cannot redeem?

Or is there no strength in me to deliver?

Behold, at my rebuke

I will make the sea desolate;

I will turn rivers into dry land.

The fish will rot for lack of water,

and they will die of thirst.

I will clothe the heavens with darkness,

and I will make sackcloth their covering.”

[Col. 0829C] The Lord has given me a learned tongue,

so that I may know how to sustain the weary

with a word.

He awakens morning by morning;

morning by morning he awakens my ear,

so that I may hear like a teacher.

The Lord God opened my ear,

but I did not resist;

I did not turn back.

I gave my body to those who struck me,

and my cheeks to those who tore out my hair.

I did not turn my face away

from those who reproached me

and spat upon me.

The Lord God is my helper.

Therefore I was not ashamed.

Therefore I set my face

like the hardest stone,

and I know that I shall not be put to shame.

He is near who justifies me.

Who will oppose me?

Let us stand together.

Who is my adversary?

Let him approach me.

[Col. 0829D] Behold, the Lord God is my helper.

Who is he who will condemn me?

Behold, they will all be worn out like a garment;

the moth will consume them.

Who among you fears the Lord,

hearing the voice of his servant?

Let him who walks in darkness

and has no light

hope in the name of the Lord

and rely upon his God.

Behold, all of you who kindle a fire,

who gird yourselves with flames,

walk in the light of your fire

and in the flames that you have kindled.

This has come upon you from my hand;

you shall lie down in sorrows.

[Col. 0830A] [Cap. LI.] Hear me, you who pursue what is just

and seek the Lord.

Pay attention to the rock

from which you were hewn,

and to the hollow of the pit

from which you were cut.

Look to Abraham your father

and to Sarah who bore you.

For I called him when he was one,

and I blessed him

and multiplied him.

Therefore the Lord will console Zion,

and he will console all its ruins.

He will make its wilderness like delights

and its solitude like the garden of the Lord.

Joy and gladness will be found in it,

thanksgiving

and the voice of praise.

Pay attention to me, my people,

and hear me, my tribe.

For the law will go forth from me,

and my judgment will rest as a light

for the peoples.

My righteous one is near;

my Savior has gone forth.

[Col. 0830B] And my arms will judge the peoples.

The islands will await me,

and they will hope in my arm.

Lift up your eyes to heaven,

and look down beneath the earth.

For the heavens will melt like smoke,

and the earth will be worn out like a garment,

and its inhabitants will perish in the same way.

But my salvation will be forever,

and my righteousness will not fail.

Hear me, you who know what is just,

a people who have my law in their hearts.

Do not fear the reproach of men,

and do not be afraid of their blasphemies.

For as a garment is consumed by the worm,

so they will be consumed;

and as wool is devoured by the moth,

so they will be devoured.

But my salvation will be forever,

and my righteousness

throughout all generations.

Arise, arise;

clothe yourself with strength,

O arm of the Lord.

Arise as in former days,

as in the generations of ancient times.

Were you not the one who struck down the proud,

who wounded the dragon?

Were you not the one who dried up the sea,

the water of the mighty abyss,

who made the depths of the sea a road

for the redeemed to cross?

And now those redeemed by the Lord

will return.

They will come to Zion with praise,

and everlasting joy will be upon their heads.

They will possess joy and gladness;

sorrow and groaning will flee.

I, I myself will console you.

Who are you that you should fear

a mortal man

and a son of man,

who withers like grass?

And you have forgotten the Lord your maker,

who stretched out the heavens

and founded the earth.

[Col. 0830D] And you have continually feared all day long

the face of the fury of the one who oppressed you

and prepared himself to destroy you.

Where now is the fury of the oppressor?

Quickly he will come,

the one who advances to open,

and he will not kill to utter destruction,

nor will his bread fail.

But I am the Lord your God,

who stirs up the sea,

and its waves swell.

The Lord of hosts is my name.

I have placed my words in your mouth,

and in the shadow of my hand

I have protected you,

to plant the heavens

and found the earth,

and to say to Zion:

[Col. 0831A] “You are my people.”

Rise up, rise up;

arise, Jerusalem,

you who have drunk from the hand of the Lord

the cup of his wrath.

You have drunk the dregs

of the cup of stupor,

and you have drunk to the lees.

There is no one to sustain her

among all the sons whom she bore;

there is no one to grasp her hand

among all the sons whom she raised.

Two things have befallen you.

Who will grieve for you?

Desolation and destruction,

famine and sword.

Who will console you?

Your sons have been cast down;

they have lain asleep at the head of every road,

like a [Note: The scribes of the Canon and many other manuscript codices supplied the general name, namely, “like a snared wild beast.” Saint Jerome observes, however, in Book XIV of his Commentaries that, instead of the “half-cooked beta” rendered by the Septuagint, all the other interpreters translated “an oryx captured and snared.” This animal is called in Hebrew תּוֹא, *tho*, a kind of beast born in the wilderness and counted among the clean animals in Leviticus and Deuteronomy. For it, the Septuagint, supposing a Syriac word, read [lacuna] *Thoreth*, which is called “beta.” MART.] snared oryx,

full of the indignation of the Lord,

with the rebuke of your God.

[Col. 0831B] Therefore hear this,

poor little one,

and drunk, but not with wine.

Thus says your Lord,

the Lord,

and your God,

who will fight [Alt.: fought] for his people:

Behold, I have taken from your hand

the cup of stupor,

the bottom of the cup of my indignation.

You shall no longer add

to drinking it.

And I will put it into the hand

of those who humbled you,

who said to your soul:

“Bend down,

so that we may pass over you.”

And you made your body like the ground,

and like a road for passersby.

[Cap. LII.] Arise, arise;

clothe yourself with your strength,

O Zion.

Clothe yourself with the garments of your glory,

Jerusalem,

holy city.

For the uncircumcised and the unclean

shall no longer continue to pass through you.

[Col. 0831C] Shake yourself free from the dust;

arise,

sit up,

Jerusalem.

Loose the bonds of your neck,

captive daughter of Zion.

For thus says the Lord:

“You were sold without payment,

and you shall be redeemed without silver.”

For thus says the Lord God:

“My people went down into Egypt

at the beginning,

to dwell there as a settler;

and Assyria oppressed him

without cause.

And what is this to me now,

says the Lord,

that my people has been taken away for nothing?

Its rulers act unjustly,

says the Lord,

and my name is continually blasphemed

all day long.

Therefore my people will know my name

on that day,

for I am the one who was speaking.

Behold, I am here.”

How beautiful upon the mountains

are the feet of the one who announces

and proclaims peace,

who announces good things

and proclaims salvation,

who says to Zion:

“Your God will reign!”

The voice of your watchmen:

they have raised their voice;

together they will praise,

[Col. 0832A] for they will see eye to eye

when the Lord restores Zion.

Rejoice and praise together,

desolate places of Jerusalem,

for the Lord has consoled his people;

he has redeemed Jerusalem.

The Lord has prepared his holy arm

before the eyes of all the nations,

and all the ends of the earth

will see the salvation of our God.

Depart, depart;

go out from there.

Do not touch what is polluted.

Go out from its midst;

purify yourselves,

you who carry the vessels of the Lord.

For you shall not go out in tumult,

nor shall you hasten in flight.

For the Lord will go before you,

and the God of Israel will gather you.

Behold, my servant will understand;

he will be exalted and lifted up,

and he will be very high.

[Col. 0832B] Just as many were astonished at you,

so his appearance will be without glory

among men,

and his form among the sons of men.

He will sprinkle many nations.

Because of him kings will shut their mouths,

for those to whom nothing had been told about him [Alt.: had not been told about him] will see,

and those who had not heard

will contemplate.

[Cap. LIII.] Who has believed our report,

and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?

And he will rise up before him like a shoot,

and like a root from thirsty ground.

He has no appearance or beauty,

and we saw him,

but there was no aspect to him,

and we desired him.

Despised and last among men,

a man of sorrows

and acquainted with weakness,

like one whose face is hidden

and despised,

and so we did not esteem him.

[Col. 0832C] Truly, he himself bore our infirmities,

and he himself carried our pains [Alt.: “he carried our pains”; *ipse* is omitted].

And we considered him like a leper,

struck by God

and humbled.

But he was wounded because of our iniquities;

he was crushed because of our crimes.

The discipline of our peace was upon him,

and by his bruise we were healed.

We all, like sheep, have gone astray;

each one has turned to his own way.

And the Lord placed upon him

the iniquity of us all.

He was offered because he himself willed it,

and he did not open his mouth.

Like a sheep he will be led to slaughter,

and like a lamb before its shearer

he will be silent,

and he will not open his mouth.

[Col. 0832D] From distress and judgment

he was taken away.

Who will declare his generation?

For he was cut off from the land of the living.
because of the transgression of my people [Note: [Col. 0831D] This is how the copies of the Canon of the Hebrew Truth read, although in the Carcassonian manuscript an unskilled corrector [Col. 0832D] erased the final letter of the word *percussit*. The very ancient book called the *Comes of Saint Jerome*, or manuscript lectionary, likewise retains this reading; its author drew all parts of the Old Testament from the edition of Jerome prepared according to the Hebrew codices, as its preface attests. Other manuscript copies of the Holy Scriptures agree with our Vulgate, which reads in the first person, “I struck him.” It should be noted, however, that in Corbeiensis manuscript no. 12 the first hand wrote *percussit eos* (“he struck them”), later changed to *percussit eum* (“he struck him”); conversely, the Royal codex no. 3563, as corrected, reads *percussit eos*, whereas it had previously read *percussi eum* (“I struck him”). Moreover, in the printed books of Saint Jerome’s Commentaries, as well as in the older and better manuscripts, we read *percussit eos* according to the Hebrew words *naga lamo*, which some learned men understand as though it were *nega lo*, that is, “a blow to him,” or “he struck him,” instead of “he struck them.” On *lamo* for *lo*, see the sacred critics on this passage of Isaiah. MART.] he struck him.

And he will give the wicked for his burial,

[Col. 0833A] and the rich man for his death:

because he committed no iniquity,

nor was there deceit in his mouth.

And the Lord desired to crush him in weakness:

If he makes his life an offering for sin,

he will see a long-lived offspring,

and the will of the Lord will prosper in his hand.

Because his soul has labored [Al. *will have labored*],

he will see and be satisfied:

by his knowledge the righteous one himself, my servant, will justify [Note: [Col. 0833D] Several manuscript codices, together with the copies of the Canon, read in the accusative case, *servos meos multos* (“my many servants”), which can be understood from the Hebrew. For if it is read *audi* or *abdi*, it means “my servant”; but if *avadai* [Col. 0834D] or *abadai*, it signifies “my servants.” MART.] many [Al. *my many servants*],

and he himself will bear their iniquities.

Therefore I will allot many to him;

and he will divide the spoils of the strong,

because he delivered his soul to death,

and was reckoned among criminals:

And he himself bore the sin of many,

and pleaded for transgressors [Note: [Col. 0834D] The Carcassonian Canon adds here, “so that they might not perish,” which is superfluous and is reported by no translator; but it was taken from the lectionaries, for the *Comes of Saint Jerome* has this addition: “so that they might not perish: says the almighty Lord.” MART.].

### Chapter LIV

Sing praise, barren woman who do not bear:

break forth in singing,

[Col. 0833B] and neigh, you who did not bear:

for the children of the deserted woman are many,

more than those of her who had a husband, says the Lord.

Enlarge the place of your tent,

and stretch out the skins of your dwellings; do not

spare:

lengthen your cords,

and strengthen your pegs.

For you will penetrate to the right and to the left:

and your offspring will inherit the nations,

and will inhabit deserted cities.

Do not fear, for you will not be put to shame, nor will you blush:

for you will not be disgraced,

because you will forget the shame of your youth,

and will remember the reproach of your widowhood no more.

For he who made you will rule over you;

the Lord of hosts is his name:

[Col. 0833C] and your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel,

will be called the God of all the earth.

For as a woman abandoned and grieving in spirit,

the Lord has called you,

and as a wife rejected from youth, your God has said.

For a brief moment I abandoned you,

but with great compassion I will gather you.

In a moment of indignation I hid my face

from you for a little while,

but with everlasting mercy I have had compassion on you:

your redeemer, the Lord, has said.

As in the days of Noah, this is to me,

to whom I swore that I would not again bring the waters of Noah

over the earth:

so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you,

nor rebuke you.

For the mountains will be shaken, and the hills will tremble:

but my mercy will not depart from you,

and my covenant of peace will not be moved:

[Col. 0833D] said your compassionate Lord:

Poor little woman, tossed by the storm, without any

[Al. omits *any*] consolation.

Behold, I will set your stones in order,

and lay your foundations in sapphires,

[Col. 0834A] and I will make your battlements of jasper;

and your gates of carved stones,

and all your borders of precious stones:

All your children taught by the Lord;

and great will be the peace of your children:

And you will be founded in righteousness:

withdraw far from slander, for you will not fear;

and from terror, for it will not approach you.

Behold, a sojourner will come who was not with me,

and your former alien will be joined to you.

Behold, I created the smith who blows on the coals in the fire,

and brings forth a vessel for his work,

and I created the destroyer to lay waste.

Every vessel, and everything fashioned against you, will not prosper:

and you will judge every tongue that resists you in judgment.

This is the inheritance of the servants of the Lord,

and their righteousness is with me, says the Lord.

### Chapter LV

All you who thirst, come to the waters:

[Col. 0834B] and you who have no silver [Al. *money*], hurry,

buy, and eat:

Come, buy without silver,

and without any exchange, wine and milk.

Why do you weigh out silver for what is not bread,

and your labor for what does not satisfy?

Listen, listening to me, and eat what is good,

and your soul will delight in abundance.

Incline your ear and come to me:

listen, and your soul will live,

And I will make for you [Al. *with you*] an everlasting covenant,

the faithful mercies of David [Note: [Col. 0834D] Through the error of copyists, the manuscripts and the Canon of the Hebrew Truth read *David fidelis* (“faithful David”); but in the Hebrew text and among the interpreters of the Septuagint the number is plural, that is, “faithful mercies,” or “faithful acts,” and not singular “faithful.” MART.].

Behold, I have given him as a witness to the peoples,

as a leader and instructor to the nations.

Behold, you will call a nation that you did not know,

and nations that did not know you will run to you,

because of the Lord your God,

[Col. 0834C] and the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.

Seek the Lord while he can be found; call upon

him while he is near.

Let the wicked abandon his way,

and the unrighteous man his thoughts,

And let him return [Al. *turn back*] to the Lord, and he will have mercy on him,

and to our God, for he is abundant in forgiveness.

For my thoughts are not your thoughts,

nor are your ways my ways, says the Lord.

For as the heavens are raised above the earth,

so are my ways raised above your ways,

and my thoughts above your thoughts.

And just as rain and snow descend from heaven,

and do not return there again [Note: [Col. 0834D] In the Commentary on the Hebrew text, Saint Jerome more correctly reads this in the future tense: “it will return.”],

but water the earth and soak it,

and make it sprout,

and give seed to the sower,

and bread to the eater:

[Col. 0834D] so will my word be that goes forth from my mouth:

it will not return to me empty,

but it will do whatever I desired,

and will prosper in the things for which I sent it.

For you will go forth in joy, and will be led in peace;

[Col. 0835A] the mountains and hills will sing praise before you,

and all the trees of the region will clap their hands.

In place of the saltwort, the fir will rise,

and in place of the nettle, the myrtle will grow;

And the Lord will be named as an everlasting sign,

which will not be taken away.

### Chapter LVI

Thus says the Lord:

Keep judgment, and practice righteousness:

for my salvation is near, that it may come,

and my righteousness, that it may be revealed.

Blessed is the man who does this,

and the son of man who grasps it:

who keeps the sabbath, so as not to profane it,

who keeps his hands from doing any evil.

And let not the son of the foreigner who clings to the Lord say,

saying:

“The Lord will separate me from his people,”

And let not the eunuch say:

“Behold, I am a dry tree.”

For thus says the Lord to the eunuchs:

[Col. 0835B] Those who keep my sabbaths and choose what I desired,

and hold fast my covenant:

I will give them a place in my house and within my walls,

and a name better than sons and daughters:

I will give them an everlasting name,

which will not perish.

And the sons of the foreigner who cling to the Lord, to worship

him,

and to love his name, so that they may be his servants:

everyone who keeps the sabbath, so as not to profane it,

and holds fast my covenant:

I will bring them to my holy mountain,

and I will gladden them in my house of prayer;

their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be pleasing to me

upon my altar:

for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.

The Lord God says, who gathers the dispersed of Israel:

I will still gather others to him, together with those already gathered.

[Col. 0835C] All the beasts of the field, come to devour,

all the beasts of the forest.

His watchmen are blind;

all of them have no knowledge:

all of them are mute dogs, unable to bark,

seeing empty things,

sleeping, and loving dreams.

And the dogs are utterly shameless

and do not know satiety:

the shepherds themselves have no understanding:

all have turned to their own way,

each one to his own greed,

from the highest to the last.

Come, let us take wine,

and let us fill ourselves with drunkenness:

And as it is today, so also tomorrow,

and much more.

### Chapter LVII

The righteous man perishes,

and no one considers it in his heart,

[Col. 0835D] and men of mercy are gathered away,

because there is no one who understands:

for the righteous man has been gathered away from the face of evil.

Let peace come;

let him who walked [Al. *walks*]

in his own uprightness rest in his bed.

But you, draw near here, sons of the sorceress,

offspring of the adulterer and the prostitute.

Over whom did you mock?

Over whom did you open wide your mouth and thrust out your tongue?

Are you not wicked children, lying offspring?

[Col. 0836A] You who find comfort in gods beneath every leafy tree,

sacrificing little children in the torrents, beneath overhanging rocks?

Among the fathers of the torrent is your portion;

this is your lot:

and to them you poured out a libation,

you offered sacrifice.

Surely over these things I will not be indignant?

Upon a high and lofty mountain you placed your bed,

and there you went up to sacrifice victims.

And behind the door and behind the doorpost you placed your memorial,

because beside me you uncovered yourself and received the adulterer:

You enlarged your bed and made a covenant with them [Note: [Col. 0835D] Closer to the Hebrew, the holy Father omits *foedus* (“covenant”) in the Commentary. More correctly, in the same place, together with that archetype, he reads *regi* (“for a king”) shortly afterward, instead of *regio* (“royal”), as in the Hebrew.].

you loved their bed with an open hand.

And you adorned yourself with royal ointment,

and multiplied your perfumes.

[Col. 0836B] You sent your messengers far away,

and humbled yourself even to the underworld.

You wearied yourself with the multitude of your ways:

you did not say, “I will rest.”

You found life for your hand;

therefore you did not ask [Al. adds *me*],

Whom did you anxiously fear, that you lied,

and did not remember me,

nor consider it in your heart?

Because I was silent, and as though not seeing,

you forgot me.

I will announce your righteousness,

and your works will not profit you.

When you cry out, let your gathered companions deliver you;

but the wind will carry them all away;

a breath will take them away.

But he who puts his trust in me will inherit the earth,

and possess my holy mountain.

And I will say:

[Col. 0836C] “Make a way,

prepare a road,

turn aside from the path,

remove the stumbling blocks from the way of my people.”

For thus says the High and Lofty One who inhabits eternity:

and whose holy name dwells in the high and holy place,

and with the contrite and humble in spirit:

to revive the spirit of the humble,

and to revive the heart of the contrite.

For I will not bind forever,

nor will I be angry to the end:

For the spirit will go forth from my presence,

and I will make breath.

Because of the iniquity of his greed I was angry,

and I struck him:

I hid [Note: [Col. 0835D] The words “my face from you” are scarcely likely to have proceeded from Jerome’s hand. Not only does he omit them entirely when he explains this passage in the Commentary [Col. 0836D], but in the exposition attached there he also clearly teaches that they are merely understood from the context. Certainly they are not in the Hebrew, which has only *abscondi*, “I hid”; and the other versions after the Septuagint, which contain them, appear to have taken them from the parallel passage Deuteronomy 31:17 or 32:20. MART.] my face from you,

and was indignant:

[Col. 0836D] And he went about wandering [Al. *walked grieving*] in the way of

his heart.

I have seen his ways and healed him,

and led him back and restored consolations to him,

and to those who mourn with him.

I created the fruit of the lips: peace,

peace to him who is far and to him who is near, says the Lord,

and I healed him.

But the wicked are like a turbulent sea that cannot rest,

[Col. 0837A] and its waves overflow into trampling and

mud.

“There is no peace,” said my God [Al. omits *my*],

for the wicked.

### Chapter LVIII

Cry out; do not cease;

raise your voice like a trumpet,

and announce to my people their transgressions,

and to the house of Jacob their sins.

For they seek me from day to day,

and desire to know my ways:

like a nation that had practiced righteousness,

and had not abandoned the judgment of its God.

They ask me for judgments of righteousness;

they desire to draw near to God.

“Why have we fasted, and you have not looked upon us?

We have humbled our soul, and you have not known?”

Behold, on the day of your fast your will is found [Note: [Col. 0837D] The word “your” is not added in the Hebrew, nor is it known to the Ambrosian codex, which we used in revising Jerome’s Commentaries. In those Commentaries it is also more correctly read in the future tense, “will be found,” rather than “is found.” In Hebrew there is *…*.],

and you demand payment from all your debtors [Al. *demanded payment*].

Behold, you fast for disputes and contentions,

and strike wickedly with the fist.

Do not fast as you have done to this day,

[Col. 0837B] so that your cry may be heard on high.

Is this the kind of fast that I chose,

for a man to afflict his soul for a day?

Is it to bend his head like a reed,

and to spread out sackcloth and ashes?

Will you call this a fast,

and a day acceptable to the Lord?

Is not this rather the fast that I chose?

loose the bonds of wickedness,

untie the burdens that oppress:

set free those who are broken,

and break every burden.

Break your bread for the hungry,

And bring the poor and homeless into your house [Note: [Col. 0837D] We have deleted, in accordance with the manuscripts, the pronoun *tuam* (“your”), since it is scarcely credible that it was added here by Jerome, who states in his exposition of this passage that the Hebrew simply has *in domum*, “into a house.” He observes that the deeper meaning is that, even if you do not have your own house, you should bring them into a little lodging which you either rent or possess by favor. The added word is found in the Septuagint, which Jerome’s version certainly rejects. MART.];

When you see the naked, cover him,

and do not despise your own flesh [Note: [Col. 0838D] From this point through the words “if you remove,” Saint Augustine’s copy marks four verses; but in the Corbeiensis manuscript there are six divisions, separated by members. The sentences themselves, contained in these two columns, seem to require an equal number. Perhaps Saint Augustine was attending to two cola, which often comprise only four verses, or clauses, within themselves.].

Then your light will break forth like the morning,

and your healing will rise quickly [Al. *soon*],

and your righteousness will go before your face,

[Col. 0837C] and the glory of the Lord will gather you.

Then you will call, and the Lord will hear [Note: [Col. 0838D] The word *te* (“you”) is known neither to the Hebrew text nor to the holy Interpreter in the Commentary.] you;

you will cry out, and he will say: “Here I am.”

If you remove the chain from your midst,

and cease to extend the finger,

and to speak what is unprofitable.

When you pour out your soul for the hungry,

and satisfy the afflicted soul,

[Al. adds *Then*] your light will rise in the darkness,

and your darkness will be like midday.

And the Lord will give you rest always,

and has filled your soul with splendors,

and will deliver your bones,

And you will be like a watered garden,

and like a spring of waters whose waters will not fail.

And the ancient ruins will be built up in you:

you will raise the foundations of generation after generation:

and [Note: [Col. 0838D] In the Commentary the holy Father reads beforehand: “And he will be called in you a builder.” The Hebrew has *…*.] you will be called a builder of hedges,

turning [Al. *converting*] paths into rest.

[Col. 0837D] If you turn your foot away from the sabbath,

from doing your will on my holy day,

And call the sabbath delightful,

and the holy day of the Lord glorious:

[Col. 0838A] And glorify it by not following your own ways,

and by not finding your own will, so as

to speak a word;

Then you will delight in the Lord,

and I will lift you above the heights of the earth,

and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father.

For the mouth of the Lord has spoken.

### Chapter LIX

Behold, the hand of the Lord is not shortened,

so that it cannot save,

nor is his ear burdened, so that it cannot hear:

But your iniquities have separated between you and

your God,

and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he would not hear.

For your hands are polluted with blood,

and your fingers with iniquity;

your lips have spoken lies,

and your tongue utters iniquity.

There is no one who invokes righteousness,

nor is there anyone who judges truthfully:

[Col. 0838B] but they trust in nothingness,

and speak vanities:

They have conceived labor,

and given birth to iniquity.

They have broken the eggs of vipers,

and woven spiders’ webs:

Whoever eats of their eggs will die,

and what has been hatched will burst forth as a basilisk.

Their webs will not become clothing,

nor will they cover themselves with their works:

their works are useless works,

and the work of iniquity is in their hands.

Their feet run toward evil,

and hasten to shed innocent blood.

Their thoughts are useless thoughts:

desolation and destruction are in their ways.

They have not known the way of peace,

and there is no judgment in their footsteps.

Their paths have been made crooked for them:

[Col. 0838C] everyone who treads upon it [Al. *them*] does not know peace.

Therefore judgment has been far removed from us,

and righteousness will not reach us:

We awaited light, and behold, darkness;

brightness, and we walked in darkness.

We groped like the blind against a wall,

and as though without eyes we felt our way:

We stumbled at midday as though in darkness,

in gloomy places [Al. *dark places*] as though dead.

We will all growl like bears,

and like doves we will moan meditatively.

We awaited judgment, and it is not [Al. *will not be*];

salvation, and it has been far from us:

For our iniquities have multiplied before you,

and our sins have answered us.

For our crimes are with us,

and we have known our iniquities:

to sin and lie against the Lord,

And we have turned away, so as not to go behind the back of our God [Al.

*our Lord*],

[Col. 0838D] to speak slander, and we have conceived transgression,

and spoken words of deceit from the heart.

And judgment has turned backward,

[Col. 0839A] and righteousness has stood far away:

For truth has fallen in the street,

and equity could not enter.

And truth has become forgotten,

and he who withdrew from evil was exposed to plunder:

And the Lord saw,

and it was evil in his eyes,

that there was no judgment.

And he saw that there was no man,

and he was perplexed,

because there was no one to intervene;

And his own arm saved him,

and his own righteousness strengthened him.

He put on righteousness as a breastplate,

and a helmet [Al. *the helmet*] of salvation on his head;

He put on garments of vengeance,

and was covered as with a cloak of zeal.

As for vengeance, as for repayment of indignation against his enemies

and recompense for his adversaries,

[Col. 0839B] he will repay the islands.

And those from the west will fear the name of the Lord,

and those from the rising of the sun his glory:

When he comes like a violent river,

which the spirit of the Lord drives:

And the redeemer will come to Zion,

and to those who return from iniquity in Jacob, says

the Lord.

This is my covenant with them, says the Lord:

My spirit, which is in you,

and my words, which I have placed in your mouth,

will not depart from your mouth,

nor from the mouth of your offspring’s offspring, says the Lord,

from now and forever.

### Chapter LX

Rise, shine, [Note: [Col. 0839D] In printed editions and several more recent manuscripts the name “Jerusalem” has been added; but it is absent from the Canon of the Hebrew Truth. Concerning this word Saint Jerome says in Book XVII of the Commentary: “Moreover, the name Jerusalem and of the nations, which is placed here by the Septuagint, is not found in the Hebrew, and must be marked beforehand with an obelus,” etc. MART.] for your light

has come,

and the glory of the Lord has risen over you.

For behold, darkness will cover the earth,

and gloom the peoples;

[Col. 0839C] but over you the Lord will rise,

and his glory will be seen in you.

And nations will walk in your light,

and kings in the splendor of your rising.

Lift your eyes around and see:

all these have been gathered [Al. omits *have been gathered*], they have come to you:

your sons will come from far away,

and your daughters will suck [Note: [Col. 0839D] Through the error of scribes, the corruption arose that instead of *sugent* (“will suck”) this passage was written *surgent* (“will rise”)—*in latere surgent*. But skilled correctors restored in some older manuscripts what had been written by the first hand, namely *sugent*. Consult Jerome’s Commentaries on this passage. MART. —Three manuscript codices of the Scriptures praised by Victorius have *lac* (“milk”) instead of *in latere*, a reading which he himself supports from the lower context at verse 16, “you will suck the milk of the nations, and you will be nursed at the breast of kings,” and which Saint Jerome’s own Commentary also supports more strongly. The Hebrew text and all the other books oppose it. In any case, both the manuscripts mentioned and the more accurate Latin editions correctly have *sugent* instead of *surgent*, which is found in the Vulgate.] at your side.

Then you will see and overflow with abundance,

and your heart will wonder and be enlarged,

when the multitude of the sea has been turned toward you,

and the strength of the nations has come to you.

An inundation of camels will cover you,

the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah;

all those from Sheba will come,

bearing gold and frankincense,

and proclaiming praise to the Lord.

Every flock of Kedar will be gathered to you,

the rams of Nebaioth will serve you;

[Col. 0839D] they will be offered upon my pleasing altar,

and I will glorify the house of my majesty.

Who are these who fly like clouds,

and like doves to their windows?

For the islands will wait for me [Al. *wait for*],

[Col. 0840A] and the ships of the sea at the beginning,

so that I may bring your sons from far away;

their silver and their gold with them,

for the name of the Lord your God and the Holy One of Israel,

because he has glorified you.

And the sons of foreigners will build your walls,

and their kings will serve you;

for in my indignation I struck you,

and in my reconciliation I had mercy on you.

And your gates will be open continually:

day and night they will not be closed,

so that the strength of the nations may be brought to you,

and their kings led in.

For the nation and kingdom that will not serve you will perish,

and the nations will be laid waste into desolation.

The glory of Lebanon will come to you,

the fir, the boxwood, and the pine together,

to adorn the place of my sanctuary;

and I will glorify the place of my feet.

[Col. 0840B] And the bent sons of those who humbled you will come to you,

and all who slandered you will worship the traces

of your feet,

and they will call you the city of the Lord,

Zion of the Holy One of Israel:

because you were abandoned and hated,

and there was no one who passed through you [Al. *who might pass through*],

I will make you the pride of the ages,

a joy from generation to generation:

And you will suck the milk of the nations,

and you will be nursed at the breast of kings:

And you will know that I am the Lord who saves you,

and your strong redeemer, the God of Jacob.

In place of bronze I will bring gold,

and in place of iron I will bring silver,

and in place of wood, bronze,

and in place of stones, iron:

And I will appoint peace as your visitation,

[Col. 0840C] and your overseers [Al. adds *in*] as righteousness.

Iniquity will no longer be heard in your land,

desolation and destruction within your borders,

And salvation will occupy your walls,

and praise your harbors.

The sun will no longer be your light by day,

nor will the brightness of the moon illuminate you:

But the Lord will be your everlasting light,

and your God your glory.

Your sun will no longer set,

and your moon will not diminish:

For the Lord will be your everlasting light,

and the days of your mourning will be completed.

But all your people will be righteous;

they will inherit the land forever,

the shoot of my planting,

the work of my hands, for glorification.

The least will become a thousand,

and the smallest a most powerful nation:

I, the Lord,

[Col. 0840D] will suddenly accomplish this in its time.

### Chapter LXI

The spirit of the Lord [Al. adds *of God*] is upon me,

because the Lord has anointed me;

he sent me to announce good news to the meek,

[Col. 0841A] to heal the brokenhearted,

and to proclaim release to captives,

and opening to those who are imprisoned:

to proclaim [Al. *and announce*] the acceptable year of the Lord,

and the day of vengeance of our God:

to comfort all who mourn:

to place upon the mourners of Zion,

and to give them a crown instead of ashes,

the oil of joy instead of mourning,

a garment of praise instead of a spirit of sorrow:

And they will be called mighty ones of righteousness,

the planting of the Lord for glorification.

And they will build the ancient ruins,

and raise up the old devastations,

And they will restore the deserted cities,

laid waste from generation to generation.

And foreigners will stand and pasture your flocks;

and the sons of foreigners

will be your farmers and vinedressers.

But you will be called priests of the Lord:

[Col. 0841B] you will be called ministers of our God:

you will eat the strength of the nations,

and will glory in their glory.

Instead of your double shame and disgrace,

they will praise their portion:

therefore in their land they will possess double,

and everlasting joy will be theirs.

For I am the Lord, who loves judgment,

and hates robbery in a burnt offering:

And I will give their work in truth,

and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.

And their offspring will be known among the nations,

and their descendants in the midst of the peoples:

all who see them will recognize them,

because they are the offspring whom the Lord has blessed.

Rejoicing, I will rejoice in the Lord,

and my soul will exult [Al. *exulted*] in my God:

For he has clothed me with garments of salvation,

[Col. 0841C] and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness,

like a bridegroom adorned with a crown,

and like a bride adorned with her ornaments.

For just as the earth brings forth its shoot,

and just as a garden makes its seed sprout,

so the Lord God will make righteousness and praise sprout

before all the nations.

### Chapter LXII

For Zion’s sake I will not be silent,

and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest,

until her righteous one goes forth like a brightness,

and her savior is kindled like a lamp.

And the nations will see your righteous one,

and all kings your illustrious one:

And you will be called by a new name,

which the mouth of the Lord will name [Al. *has named*].

And you will be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord,

and a diadem of royalty in the hand of your God.

You will no longer be called “Forsaken,”

and your land will no longer be called “Desolate”:

but you will be called “My Will Is in Her,”

[Col. 0841D] and your land, “Inhabited” [Al. *Settled*]. [Note: [Col. 0841] Instead of *Inhabitata* (“Inhabited”), the Canon of Saint-Germain and the Anicensis Colbertine manuscript corruptly read *inhabitabitur* (“will be inhabited”). MART.]

For the Lord has been pleased with you,

and your land will be inhabited.

For a young man will dwell with a virgin,

and your sons will dwell in you.

And as a bridegroom rejoices over a bride,

so your God will rejoice over you.

Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen;

all day and all night they will never be silent:

You who remember the Lord, do not be silent,

and do not give him silence,

until he establishes,

and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

[Col. 0842A] The Lord has sworn by his right hand,

and by the arm of his strength:

“If I give your grain any longer as food to your enemies,

and if foreigners drink your wine for which you labored.

For those who gather it will eat it,

and will praise the Lord;

and those who carry it together

will drink in my holy courts.”

Pass through, pass through the gates,

prepare the way for the people:

make the road level,

choose the stones,

and raise a sign for the peoples.

Behold, the Lord has made hearing heard to the ends of the earth;

say to the daughter of Zion:

“Behold, your Savior comes;

behold, his reward is with him,

and his work before him.”

And they will call them “Holy People,” redeemed [Al. *redeemed, singular*]

[Col. 0842B] by the Lord.

But you will be called “Sought-After City,”

and not forsaken.

### Chapter LXIII

Who is this who comes from Edom,

with garments dyed from Bozrah?

This one is beautiful in his robe,

walking in the abundance of his strength.

“I am the one who speaks righteousness,

and I am a defender for saving.”

Why, then, is your garment red,

and your clothing like that of those who tread in the winepress?

I have trodden the winepress alone,

and there is no man from the nations with me:

I trod them in my fury,

and trampled them in my anger:

and their blood was sprinkled upon my garments,

and I stained all my clothing.

For the day of vengeance was in my heart,

[Col. 0842C] and the year of my redemption has come.

I looked around, and there was no helper;

I sought, and there was no one to assist:

And my own arm saved me,

and my indignation itself helped me.

And I trampled the peoples in my fury,

and made them drunk in my indignation,

and brought down their strength to the earth.

I will remember the mercies of the Lord,

the praise of the Lord for all that the Lord has repaid us,

and for the abundance of good things bestowed upon the house of Israel,

which he granted them according to his mercy,

and according to the abundance of his compassion.

And he said:

“Nevertheless, they are my people, sons who do not deny”;

and he became their savior.

In all their distress he was not distressed,

[Col. 0842D] and the angel of his presence saved them:

in his love and in his mercy he himself redeemed them,

and carried them and lifted them all the days of the age.

But they provoked him to anger,

and afflicted the spirit of his holy one:

and he became their enemy,

and himself fought against them.

And he remembered the days of old—Moses, his people:

“Where is the one who brought them out of the sea with the shepherds

of his flock?

Where is the one who placed in their midst the spirit of his holy one?

[Col. 0843A] He who led Moses by the right hand with the arm of his majesty,

who divided the waters before them to make for himself an everlasting name;

who led [Al. *drove*] them through the abysses, like

a horse in the desert that does not stumble;

like an animal descending in the plain.

The spirit of the Lord was his guide:

so you led your people,

to make for yourself a glorious name.

Look down from heaven, and see from the dwelling place of your holiness

and your glory:

Where are your zeal and your strength?

The abundance of your compassion and your mercies

toward me

have restrained themselves.

For you are our father,

though Abraham did not know us,

and Israel did not recognize us:

[Col. 0843B] You, Lord, are our father,

our redeemer; your name is from eternity.

Why have you made us wander, Lord, from [Al. *in*] your ways?

You have hardened our heart, so that we would not fear you?

Turn back for the sake of your servants,

the tribes of your inheritance.

They have possessed your holy people as though it were nothing;

our enemies have trampled your sanctuary.

We have become as at the beginning,

when you did not rule over us,

and your name was not invoked over us.

### Chapter LXIV

If only you would tear the heavens and descend:

the mountains would melt before your face.

As in the burning of fire they would melt,

the waters would burn with fire,

so that your name might become known to your enemies;

[Col. 0843C] nations would be troubled before your face.

When you do marvelous things, we will not endure them;

you descended, and before your face the mountains melted.

From eternity they have not heard,

nor perceived with their ears:

no eye has seen, O God, besides you,

what you have prepared for those who await you.

You met the one rejoicing and practicing righteousness;

in your ways they will remember you.

Behold, you were angry, and we sinned;

we were always in them, and we will be saved.

And we all became like the unclean,

and all our righteousness like a menstrual cloth:

and we all fell like a leaf,

and our iniquities carried us away like the wind:

There is no one who invokes your name,

who rises up and takes hold of you:

You hid your face from us,

[Col. 0843D] and crushed us in the hand of our iniquity [Note: [Col. 0843] The pronoun “our” is added neither in the Hebrew nor in the Commentary, where the holy Father himself reads the passage without it.].

And now, Lord, you are our father,

but we are clay;

and you are our maker,

and we are all the work of your hands.

Do not be angry, Lord, beyond measure,

and do not remember our iniquity forever.

Behold, look:

we are all your people.

The city of your holy one has become deserted;

Zion has become a desert;

Jerusalem has been laid waste.

The house of our sanctuary and of our glory,

where our fathers praised you,

has become a burning of fire,

[Col. 0844A] and all our desirable things have been turned into ruins.

Will you restrain yourself over these things, Lord?

Will you be silent and afflict us exceedingly?

### Chapter LXV

Those who previously did not ask have sought me;

those who did not seek me have found me.

I said: “Here I am,

here I am,” to a nation that did not invoke

my name.

I stretched out my hands all day to an unbelieving people,

who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts.

A people who continually provoke me to anger before my face,

who sacrifice in gardens,

and offer sacrifice upon bricks:

who dwell in tombs,

and sleep in the shrines of idols.

Who eat swine’s flesh,

and have unclean broth in their vessels.

Who say: “Withdraw from me,

[Col. 0844B] do not come near me, for you are unclean”:

These will be smoke in my anger,

a burning fire all day.

Behold, it is written before me; I will not be silent,

but I will repay and requite into their bosom your iniquities,
and the iniquities of your fathers together, says the Lord.

Who sacrificed upon the mountains

and reproached me upon the hills:

I will repay their former deed into their bosom.

Thus says the Lord:

Just as, when a grape-cluster is found, it is said,

“Do not destroy it, for there is a blessing in it,”

so I will act for the sake of my servants,

so that I may not destroy the whole.

And I will bring forth offspring from Jacob,

and from Judah one who shall possess my mountains;

and my chosen ones shall inherit it,

[Col. 0844C] and my servants shall dwell there.

And the plains shall become sheepfolds,

and the valley of Achor a resting-place for cattle,

for my people who have forsaken me.

But you who have forsaken the Lord,

who have forgotten my holy mountain,

who set a table for Fortune and pour libations upon it,

I will number you for the sword,

and all of you shall fall in the slaughter:

because I called, and you did not answer;

I spoke, and you did not hear;

and you did what was evil in my sight

[Alternative: “but you did”],

and chose what I did not desire.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

Behold, my servants shall eat,

but you shall hunger;

behold, my servants shall drink,

but you shall thirst;

behold, my servants shall rejoice,

but you shall be put to shame;

[Col. 0844D] behold, my servants shall praise out of the exultation of their heart,

but you shall cry out because of the anguish of your heart,

and because of the crushing of your spirit you shall howl.

And you shall leave your name as a curse for my chosen ones;

and the Lord God shall put you to death,

but he shall call his servants by another name.

Whoever is blessed upon the earth

shall be blessed in God. Amen.

And whoever swears upon the earth

shall swear by God. Amen.

For the former troubles have been given over to oblivion,

and because they are hidden from my eyes.

For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth;

and the former things shall not be remembered,

[Col. 0845A] nor shall they rise upon the heart.

But you shall rejoice and exult forever,

in the things that I create;

for behold, I create Jerusalem for exultation,

and its people for joy.

And I will exult in Jerusalem,

and rejoice in my people;

and the sound of weeping and the sound of crying shall no longer be heard in it.

[Note: In Hebrew the following word is feminine, meaning “in her”; thus the holy father reads it more correctly in his Commentary.]

There shall no longer be there [Alternative omits “there”] an infant of days,

or an old man who does not complete his days;

for the child shall die at a hundred years,

and the sinner who is a hundred years old shall be accursed.

And they shall build houses and inhabit them;

and they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

They shall not build, and another inhabit;

they shall not plant, and another eat.

For as the days of a tree shall be the days of my people,

and the works of their hands shall grow old.

[Note: Another sequence of words, and apparently a more harmonious one, is found in the Commentaries: “My chosen ones shall grow old. They shall not labor,” etc. The sense is also truer according to the Hebrew.]

My chosen ones shall not labor in vain,

[Col. 0845B] nor shall they bear children in distress;

for they are the offspring of those blessed by the Lord,

and their descendants are with them.

And it shall come to pass that before they call, I will answer;

while they are still speaking, I will hear them [Alternative: “I will answer”].

The wolf and the lamb shall feed together;

the lion and the ox shall eat straw;

and dust shall be the serpent’s bread.

They shall not harm, nor shall they kill, on all my holy mountain,

says the Lord.

[Cap. LXVI.] Thus says the Lord:

“Heaven is my throne,

but the earth is the footstool of my feet.

What is this house that you will build for me?

And what is this place of my rest?

My hand made all these things,

and all these things came to be,” says the Lord.

“But upon whom shall I look, except upon the poor and the contrite in spirit,

[Col. 0845C] and the one who trembles at my words?

Whoever sacrifices an ox is like one who kills a man;

whoever slaughters a beast is like one who dashes out a dog’s brains;

whoever offers an offering is like one who offers swine’s blood;

whoever remembers incense is like one who blesses an idol.

They have chosen all these things in their own ways,

and their soul has delighted in their abominations.

Therefore I also will choose their mockeries,

and I will bring upon them the things they feared;

because I called, and there was no one who answered;

I spoke, and they did not hear;

and they did what was evil in my sight,

[Col. 0846A] and did what I did not desire.

[Note: In the Commentary the holy interpreter more correctly reads “they chose.”]

Hear the word of the Lord,

you who tremble at his word.

Your brothers who hate you

and cast you out because of my name have said:

“Let the Lord be glorified,

and we shall see in your joy”—

but they themselves shall be put to shame.

[Note: Here too the reading of the Commentaries is truer: “roar” instead of “of the people,” in agreement with the Hebrew.]

A sound from the city,

a sound from the temple,

a sound of the Lord rendering retribution to his enemies.

Before she was in labor, she gave birth;

before labor came upon her, she brought forth a male child.

Who has ever heard such a thing?

And who has seen anything like this?

Will the earth give birth in one day?

Or will a nation be brought forth at once,

[Note: Although all the books, as well as the reading of Jerome’s own Commentaries, have “at once,” I nevertheless think that “once” should be written here in place of “at once.” For in Hebrew it is *ahad*, “once,” and in Greek *eisapax*, which means “once.” Finally, the fact that this was written in the old Latin translation is attested by the holy Father himself elsewhere in his Commentaries on Jeremiah, chapter 31, where he quotes this passage from the Vulgate of his time: “For a nation has been born once.” Nor is it reasonable to suppose that he would have departed without cause from the Hebrew text and the reading received in the other books. On the contrary, in the very similar Latin wording, copyists could easily have mistaken *simul* (“at once”) for *semel* (“once”), and this is most probably what happened.]

because Zion has been in labor and has given birth to her children?

Shall I, who cause others to give birth,

myself not give birth? says the Lord.

[Col. 0846B] Shall I, who grant generation to others,

be barren? says the Lord your God.

Rejoice with Jerusalem,

and exult in her, all you who love her;

rejoice with her in joy, all you who mourn over her,

so that you may suck and be filled from the breast of her consolations;

so that you may milk and overflow with delights from all her glory.

For thus says the Lord:

Behold, I will turn toward her like a river of peace,

and like an overflowing torrent, the glory of the nations,

which you shall suck.

You shall be carried upon the breasts,

and they shall caress you upon their knees.

As a mother caresses someone,

so I will console you,

and in Jerusalem you shall be consoled.

[Col. 0846C] You shall see, and your heart shall rejoice,

and your bones shall flourish like grass.

And the hand of the Lord shall be known to his servants,

and he shall be indignant against his enemies.

For behold, the Lord shall come in fire,

and his chariots like a whirlwind,

to render his fury in indignation,

and his rebuke in a flame of fire.

For the Lord shall judge in fire

[Alternative: “shall be judged”]

and with his sword all flesh,

and those slain by the Lord shall be multiplied.

Those who sanctified themselves

and considered themselves clean in the gardens after one within—

[Note: This kind of genuine reading is preserved by the Canon of Hebrew Truth and by the sacred text in all corrected manuscript books of the Commentaries of Saint Jerome. We have found many manuscript copies corrupted through the ignorance of scribes or the rashness of correctors, who, removing the Interpreter’s word, substituted *janua* (“door”) on their own behalf for *unam* (“one”). In the Corbie manuscript no. 12, we read *unam* in the sacred text, and opposite it in the margin, *janua*. The modern Hebrew has undergone some alteration here: it has *ahad* instead of *ahath*, as the Masoretic note on this passage observes. Moreover, interpreters understand the word “pool” or “tree” to be supplied, so that the sense is: “those who sanctify themselves after one tree, which is in the middle of the gardens”; or “after one,” that is, after a notable and principal pool situated in a particular place in the middle of the garden. Symmachus and Theodotion interpreted this passage thus, according to Jerome: “Those who sanctify and cleanse themselves in the gardens, one after another, among those who eat swine’s flesh,” etc. The Syriac Interpreter expressed the same thing, saying *hhad bathar hhad*, that is, “one after another,” or “one after one.” The Chaldean has the same or a closely related sense: “crowd after crowd.” MART. —Formerly the Vulgate had “after a door,” a reading to which some manuscripts also agree, and which seems to have been occasioned both by the Septuagint, who translated “in the vestibules” (*en tois prothyrois*), and by the verse of the preceding chapter, 58:8, where Isaiah reproaches them for placing their idol behind doors: “Behind the door and the doorpost you have set your memorial.” Nevertheless, there is no doubt from the Hebrew text that the printed reading is the true one, and Saint Jerome also proves it in his Commentary. What is written there in Hebrew as *ahad*, the learned interpreters of the Critics explain as *ehat* or *ehatem*, that is, “one.”]

[Col. 0847A] those who ate swine’s flesh, and abomination,

and the mouse—

they shall all be consumed together, says the Lord.

But I am coming, in view of their works and thoughts, to gather all nations and tongues;

and they shall come and see my glory.

And I will set a sign among them,

and I will send from them those who have been saved to the nations overseas,

to Africa and Lydia,

[Note: Here too a scribal error has persisted: in the Canon and in other manuscript copies they wrote *tenentes* (“holding”) instead of *tendentes* (“stretching”), through an easy and, I think, involuntary slip, since it is entirely contrary to Jerome’s exposition. They call the Lydians “Lydos”; their colonists, the Etruscans, who are now called Tuscans, were formerly highly skilled in shooting arrows and are now described as “stretching the bow.” In Hebrew one reads *masche ceseth*, which, apart from the Septuagint, all translated similarly as “stretching the bow”; but the Septuagint used *mesoch*, interpreting a noun as a verb. MART.]

to Italy and Greece,

to distant islands, to those who have not heard of me

and have not seen my glory.

And they shall announce my glory among the nations

[Alternative: “in the nations”]

and shall bring all your brothers from all the nations as a gift to the Lord,

upon horses and in chariots,

and in litters,

[Col. 0848A] and on mules and in carts,

to my holy mountain, Jerusalem, says the Lord;

just as the children of Israel bring offerings in a clean vessel

into the house of the Lord.

And I will take some of them as priests and Levites, says the Lord.

For just as the new heavens and the new earth

which I make stand before me, says the Lord,

so shall your offspring and your name stand.

And it shall be month after month,

and sabbath after sabbath.

All flesh shall come to worship before my presence, says the Lord.

And they shall go out and see the corpses of the men

who transgressed against me.

Their worm shall not die,

and their fire shall not be extinguished;

and they shall be, to the satisfaction of the sight, for all flesh.

The prophet Isaiah ends here.

[Col. 0847]

[THE BOOK OF JEREMIAH.]

JEROME’S PROLOGUE TO JEREMIAH

[Col. 0847C] The prophet Jeremiah, to whom this prologue is written, appears indeed in language to be more rustic than Isaiah, Hosea, and certain other prophets among the Hebrews, but he is their equal in meaning, since he prophesied by the same Spirit. Moreover, the simplicity of his expression derives from the place in which he was born. For he was an Anathothite,

[Note: In the Commentary on chapter 23:9 he says: “Certainly I think no one is holier than Jeremiah, who, as a virgin, prophet, and one sanctified in the womb, prefigures the Lord the Savior by his very name.” Yet the Chaldean Paraphrast assigns him sons in chapter 37:12. The holy Father also again calls Jeremiah an evangelical man in the Prologue to his Commentaries.]

who is to this day a small village three miles distant from Jerusalem; a priest descended from priests, and sanctified in his mother’s womb, dedicating by his virginity an evangelical man to the Church of Christ. He began to prophesy as a boy, and he saw the captivity of the city and of Judah not only in spirit but also with the eyes of the flesh. By then the Assyrians had transferred the ten tribes of Israel into Media; by then colonies of nations possessed their lands. Therefore he prophesied only concerning Judah and Benjamin, and he lamented the ruins of his city in a fourfold alphabet, which we have rendered according to metrical measure and in verses.

[Note: Jerome rendered the fourfold alphabet of Jeremiah’s Lamentations according to metrical measure because he preserved the sequence of the Hebrew letters and the number of verses in his Latin translation. We too carefully observe this distinction of verses—the alphabets and divisions—in the present edition of the Canon; the divisions into members that follow will make the matter clear. MART.]

Furthermore, we have corrected the order of the Visions, which among the Greeks and Latins was altogether confused, restoring it to its original form. But we omitted the book of Baruch, his secretary,

[Note: He says the same in the prologue to the Commentaries: “But the little book of Baruch, which is commonly joined to the edition of the Septuagint and is not found among the Hebrews, and the pseudepigraphal letter of Jeremiah, I have by no means judged worthy of discussion.”]

which is neither read nor found among the Hebrews; and the pseudepigraphal letter of Jeremiah, which is joined to the common edition of the Septuagint, I did not consider worth discussing. In place of all these things we await curses from our rivals, to whom I must answer in each of my works.

[Col. 0849A] And I endure this because you compel me.

Otherwise, to lessen the evil, it would have been better to put an end to their fury by my silence than, by writing something new every day, to provoke the madness of the envious.

THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET JEREMIAH BEGINS

[Col. 0849]

[Col. 0849A] [Cap. I.] The words of Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth,

in the land of Benjamin.

The word of the Lord came to him in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah,

in the thirteenth year of his reign.

And it came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah,

until the completion of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah,

until the deportation of Jerusalem, in the fifth month.

[Col. 0849B] And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you;

and before you came forth from the womb, I sanctified you,

and I appointed you a prophet to the nations.

And I said:

[Note: In Hebrew it is written *ha ha ha*, three times, according to Jerome’s pronunciation, since he read the aleph and he as vowel letters represented by *a*. Thus the Canon of Hebrew Truth retains *A, a, a*. Other manuscript copies of the Bible read *ha ha ha* or *ah ah ah*. MART. —The Hebrew word is written once as *ah*, a word that can be pronounced with three vowel letters. Nevertheless, the Palatine manuscript, like others in Martianay’s possession, reads *ah*; perhaps this is more correct, for it is the interjection of one complaining.]

“A, a, a, Lord God!

Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am a child.”

And the Lord said to me:

Do not say, “I am a child,”

for you shall go to all to whom I send you,

and you shall speak whatever I command you.

Do not fear their presence,

for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.

And the Lord stretched out his hand and touched my mouth,

and the Lord said to me:

Behold, I have put my words in your mouth.

Behold [Alternative adds “I”], today I have appointed you over nations and kingdoms,

to uproot and to demolish,

[Col. 0849C] and to destroy and to scatter,

and to build and to plant.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

What do you see, Jeremiah?

And I said:

I see a watchful rod.

And the Lord said to me:

You have seen well,

for I will watch over my word

to carry it out.

And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying:

What do you see?

And I said:

I see a boiling pot,

and its face is toward the north.

And the Lord said to me:

From the north evil shall be opened

[Alternative: “evils shall be opened”]

against all the inhabitants of the land.

For behold, I will summon all the families of the kingdoms of the north, says the Lord;

[Col. 0849D] and they shall come and each shall set up his throne

at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem,

and against all its surrounding walls,

and against all the cities of Judah.

And I will pronounce my judgments against them for all their wickedness,

because they have forsaken me,

and have poured libations to foreign gods,

and have worshiped the work of their hands.

Therefore gird up your loins,

[Col. 0850A] and arise and speak to them all that I command you.

Do not be afraid before them;

for I will not make you fear their faces.

For behold, today I have made you a fortified city,

and an iron pillar,

and a bronze wall,

against all the land,

against the kings of Judah,

its princes and its priests,

and the people of the land.

[Col. 0850B] And they shall fight against you,

but they shall not prevail,

for I am with you, says the Lord,

to deliver you.

[Cap. II.] And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Go and cry in the ears of Jerusalem, saying:

Thus says the Lord:

I remember you, showing compassion for your youth,

and the love of your betrothal,

when you followed me in the wilderness,

in a land that is not sown.

Israel was holy to the Lord,

the firstfruits of his harvest.

All who devour him shall offend

[Alternative: “shall offend” in the future];

evil shall come upon them, says the Lord.

Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob,

and all the families of the house of Israel.

Thus says the Lord:

What iniquity did your fathers find in me,

[Col. 0850C] that they went far from me,

and walked after vanity,

and became vain?

And they did not say:

“Where is the Lord,

who brought us up from the land of Egypt,

who led us through the wilderness,

through an uninhabited and trackless land,

through a land of thirst and the image of death,

through a land in which no man walked,

nor did any human being dwell?”

And I brought you into the land of Carmel,

so that you might eat its fruit and its best produce

[Alternative: “its good produce”].

But you entered and defiled my land,

and made my inheritance an abomination.

The priests did not say, “Where is the Lord?”

Those who held the law did not know me

[Alternative: “my law”];

[Col. 0850D] the shepherds transgressed against me,

and the prophets prophesied by Baal,

and followed idols.

Therefore I will still contend with you in judgment, says the Lord,

and I will dispute with your children.

Cross over to the islands of Kittim and see;

send to Kedar and consider carefully;

and see whether anything like this has happened,

[Col. 0851A] whether a nation has changed its gods—

and yet they are not gods.

But my people has exchanged its glory for an idol.

Be appalled, O heavens, at this,

and let its gates be utterly desolate, says the Lord.

For my people has committed two evils:

They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water,

and have dug cisterns for themselves,

broken cisterns

that cannot hold water.

Is Israel a slave or a household servant?

Why, then, has he become plunder?

Lions roared over him

and raised their voices;

they made his land a desolation.

His cities were burned,

and there is no one who dwells in them.

The sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes have ravished you to the crown of your head.

[Col. 0851B] Has this not happened to you

because you forsook the Lord your God

at the time when he was leading you on the way?

And now what do you want on the road to Egypt,

to drink turbid water

[Alternative: “the water of the Sihor”]?

And what have you to do with the road of the Assyrians,

to drink the water of the river?

Your wickedness shall accuse you,

and your apostasy shall rebuke you.

Know and see that it is evil and bitter

for you to have forsaken the Lord your God,

and that the fear of me is not in you,

says the Lord God of hosts.

From long ago you broke my yoke,

you tore my bonds,

and said, “I will not serve.”

For upon every high hill

and under every leafy tree

[Col. 0851C] you lay down as a prostitute.

Yet I planted you as a choice vine,

all of it true seed.

How, then, have you been turned for me into a corrupt,

foreign vine?

Even if you wash yourself with natron

and multiply the herb *borith* for yourself,

you are stained by your iniquity before me, says the Lord God.

How can you say, “I am not defiled;

I have not gone [Alternative: “departed”] after the Baals”?"

See your ways in the valley;

know what you have done.

A swift runner unfolding his ways;

a wild donkey accustomed to the wilderness,

in the desire of its soul it drew in the wind of its passion.

No one can turn it away.

All who seek it will not grow weary;

in its menstruation they will find it.

[Col. 0851D] Keep your foot from nakedness,

[Col. 0852A] and your throat from thirst.

And you said:

“I have despaired;

I will by no means do it.

For I have loved strangers,

and I will walk after them.”

As a thief is put to shame when he is caught,

so the house of Israel has been put to shame—

they and their kings,

their princes, priests, and prophets—

saying to a piece of wood, “You are my father,”

and to a stone, “You gave me birth.”

They turned their backs to me,

and not their faces.

And in the time of their affliction they will say:

“Arise and deliver us.”

Where are your gods,

which you made for yourself?

Let them arise and deliver you

in the time of your affliction.

For according to the number of your cities

were your gods, Judah.

[Col. 0852B] Why do you wish to contend with me in judgment?

You have all forsaken me, says the Lord.

In vain

[Alternative: “without cause”]

I struck your children;

they did not accept discipline.

Your sword devoured your prophets,

like a destroying lion your generation.

See the word of the Lord:

Have I become a wilderness for Israel,

or a land of late harvest?

Why, then, did my people say,
