“We have withdrawn; we will no longer come to you”?

Will a virgin forget her ornament,

or a bride the band around her breast?

But my people has forgotten me for innumerable days.

Why do you strive to show your way to be good

in order to seek love,

when you have even taught your ways your wickedness,

and the blood of the souls of the poor and innocent has been found on your wings?

[Col. 0852C] I did not find them in pits,

but in all the things I have mentioned above.

And you said:

“I am without sin and innocent;

therefore let your fury turn away from me.”

Behold, I will contend with you in judgment

because you have said, “I have not sinned.”

How utterly vile you have become,

repeating your ways!

And you shall be put to shame by Egypt,

just as you were put to shame by Assyria.

For you shall also go out from there,

and your hands shall be upon your head,

because the Lord has shattered your confidence,

and you shall have no success in it.

[Cap. III.] It is commonly said:

“If a man divorces his wife,

and she departs from him and marries another man,

will he return to her again?

Will she not be polluted and defiled,

that woman?”

[Note: In the manuscript text of his Commentaries Jerome reads: “Will that woman not be polluted and defiled?” Later, explaining this, he warns the reader in these words: “When he says, ‘And will that woman be defiled?’ where in Hebrew we read ‘the land,’ he has left an example and speaks more explicitly of the land of Israel, which is compared to an adulterous woman. Accordingly, Jerome interpreted the Hebrew words *haarets hahi* not according to their simple sense, but according to the prophetic example and comparison.” MART.]

But you have fornicated with many lovers;

nevertheless, return to me,

[Note: The addition immediately supplied by the Vulgate book, “and I will receive you,” is found neither in the Hebrew text nor in the better Latin manuscripts that preserve Jerome’s version. Nevertheless, if the matter is judged from Jerome’s testimonies, the opposite conclusion plainly seems necessary: namely, that this was once the genuine sense of the Hebrew text, but that through the injury of time it later fell out of other books and finally from the archetype itself. For in Letter 122 to Rusticus, section 2, he says quite clearly: “It is written according to the Hebrew truth, though it is not found in the Greek and Latin copies: ‘And you have forsaken me; nevertheless, return, AND I WILL RECEIVE YOU,’ says the Lord.” No less plainly he says in the Commentary itself on this passage: “In the Hebrew, even after fornication, he receives the penitent and urges her to return to him; but in the Septuagint he does not summon her to repentance, but reproves the shamelessness of the prostitute, who dares to return to her husband after adultery.” Clearly, the Greek *kai anakampteis* should not be rendered, as it commonly is, “return,” in the manner of one inviting, but, as though reproving, “nevertheless you will return”—that is, “you dare to return.” It is therefore all the more remarkable that the holy Father reports this about the Hebrew exemplar of his own time, from which the Greek copy differed so greatly both in the reduction of the words and in sense. But that his testimony may be beyond all objection, this very fact proves it to me: the addition did not flow into the Latin copies from the Septuagint, which entirely lack it and express the passage in precisely the opposite sense; therefore it seems able to have derived only from the Hebrew.]

says the Lord.

[Col. 0852D] Lift up your eyes straight ahead

[Col. 0853A] and see where you have not lain prostrate.

You sat by the roads, waiting for them like a robber in the wilderness;

and you polluted the land with your fornications

[Alternative: “wicked deeds”]

and with your wickedness.

Therefore the drops of rain were withheld,

and the late rain did not come.

You have acquired the forehead of a prostitute;

you did not wish to be ashamed.

At least from now on call me, “My father”;

you are the guide of my virginity.

Will you be angry forever,

or will you persist to the end?

Behold, you have spoken and done evil,

and you were able.

And the Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah:

Have you seen what apostate Israel has done?

She went away for herself upon every high mountain,

and under every leafy tree,

and fornicated there.

And I said, when she had done all these things:

“Return to me.”

But she did not return.

And her treacherous sister Judah saw that,

because apostate Israel had committed adultery,

I had sent her away

and given her a certificate of divorce.

Yet her treacherous sister Judah did not fear;

she went away and herself also fornicated.

And by the ease of her fornication she polluted the land;

and she committed adultery with stone and wood.

And in all these things her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with her whole heart,

but in deceit, says the Lord.

And the Lord said to me:

Apostate Israel has justified her soul

in comparison with treacherous Judah.

Go and cry out these words toward the north,

and say:

Return, apostate Israel, says the Lord,

and I will not turn my face from you,

for I am holy, says the Lord,

and I will not be angry forever.

Nevertheless, know your iniquity,

because you have transgressed against the Lord your God;

you have scattered your ways among strangers under every leafy tree,

and you have not heard my voice, says the Lord.

Return [Alternative adds “to me”], returning children,

says the Lord,

for I am your husband.

And I will take one of you from a city,

and two from a clan,

and I will bring you into Zion.

And I will give you shepherds according to my heart,

and they shall feed you with knowledge and instruction.

And when you have multiplied and increased in the land

in those days, says the Lord,

they shall no longer say, “The ark of the covenant of the Lord.”

[Col. 0853D] Nor shall it rise upon the heart,

nor shall they remember it,

nor shall it be visited,

nor shall it be made again.

At that time they shall call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord,

and all the nations shall gather to it in the name of the Lord, in Jerusalem,

and they shall not walk after the perversity of their most wicked heart.

[Col. 0854A] In those days the house of Judah shall go to the house of Israel,

and they shall come together from the land of the north

to the land that I gave to your fathers.

But I said:

How shall I place you among sons

[Alternative: “to sons”]

and give you a desirable land,

a splendid inheritance of the armies of the nations?

And I said:

“You shall call me ‘Father,’

and you shall not cease to follow me.”

But just as a woman despises her lover,

so the house of Israel has despised me, says the Lord.

A voice was heard on the roads,

weeping and wailing of the children of Israel,

because they made their way wicked,

and forgot the Lord their God.

Return, returning children,

and I will heal your apostasies.

Behold, we do not come to you,

for you are the Lord our God.

[Col. 0854B] Truly the hills were deceitful,

the multitude of the mountains.

Truly in the Lord our God is Israel’s salvation.

Shame has devoured the labor of our fathers

from our youth,

their flocks and their herds,

their sons and their daughters.

We shall sleep in our shame,

and our disgrace shall cover us,

because we have sinned against the Lord our God,

we and our fathers,

from our youth to this day,

and we have not heard the voice of the Lord our God.

[Cap. IV.] If you return [Alternative: “you will return”], Israel,

[Note: Thus read both copies of the Canon and all manuscript copies of the Bible except one recent copy, which reads “you will return.” The word “you will return” is also written in the Commentaries; but it makes no difference. Let each choose whichever he wishes, since the sense suffers no harm. MART.]

says the Lord,

return to me.

If you remove your stumbling-blocks from my presence,

you shall not be moved.

And you shall swear:

“The Lord lives,” in truth, in judgment,

[Col. 0854C] and in righteousness.

And the nations shall bless him,

and shall praise him.

For thus says the Lord to the man of Judah and Jerusalem:

Break up new ground for yourselves,

and do not sow upon thorns.

Circumcise yourselves for the Lord,

and remove the foreskins of your hearts,

men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem,

lest my indignation go forth like fire,

and burn, with no one to extinguish it,

because of the evil of your thoughts.

Announce in Judah,

and make it heard in Jerusalem.

Speak and sound the trumpet in the land.

Cry out loudly;

say, “Gather yourselves,

and let us enter the fortified cities.”

Raise the standard in Zion.

Strengthen yourselves; do not stand still,

[Col. 0854D] for I am bringing evil from the north

and great destruction.

A lion has risen from its lair,

and the destroyer of the nations has lifted himself up.

He has gone out from his place

to make your land a desolation

[Alternative: “a wilderness”].

[Col. 0855A] Your cities shall be laid waste,

remaining without an inhabitant.

For this gird yourselves with sackcloth,

mourn and howl,

because the anger of the fury of the Lord has not turned away from us.

And on that day, says the Lord,

the heart of the king shall perish,

and the heart of the princes.

The priests shall be stupefied,

and the prophets shall be terrified.

And I said:

“Alas, alas, alas, Lord God!

Have you indeed deceived this people and Jerusalem,

saying, ‘There shall be peace for you’?

And behold, the sword has reached to the soul.”

At that time it shall be said to this people and to Jerusalem:

A scorching wind on the roads,

which are the roads of the daughter

[Alternative: “son”]

of my people in the wilderness,

not for winnowing and not for [Alternative: omits “for”] cleansing.

A spirit full of these things shall come to me,

[Col. 0855B] and now I will speak my judgments against them.

Behold, like a cloud he shall ascend,

and like a storm are his chariots.

His horses are swifter than eagles.

Woe to us, for we have been laid waste!

Wash your heart from wickedness, Jerusalem,

so that you may be saved.

How long shall harmful thoughts remain within you?

For the voice of one proclaiming from Dan

and making an idol known from Mount Ephraim:

Tell the nations:

[Note: I wonder what the reason was that “tell the nations” is read in the Canon and the other manuscripts as “hasten the nations,” especially since in the printed and manuscript books of his Commentaries Jerome reads “tell the nations.” MART.]

Behold, it has been heard in Jerusalem:

watchmen are coming from a distant land

and raising [Alternative: “have raised”] their voice against the cities of Judah.

They have become like guardians of fields around it,

because it provoked me to anger, says the Lord.

Your ways and your thoughts have done these things to you.

This is your wickedness,

because it is bitter,

because [Alternative omits “because”] it has touched your heart.

My belly, my belly—I am in pain!

The senses of my heart are troubled within me.

I will not be silent,

for my soul has heard the sound of the trumpet,

the cry of battle.

Destruction upon destruction is summoned,

and the whole land has been laid waste.

Suddenly my tents have been laid waste;

in an instant, my curtains.

How long shall I see the one fleeing,

and hear the sound of the trumpet?

For my foolish people has not known me.

They are senseless children and without understanding.

They are wise to do evil,

but they do not know how to do good.

I looked at the earth,

and behold, it was empty and nothing;

and at the heavens,

and there was no light in them.

[Col. 0855D] I saw the mountains,

and behold, they were shaking;

and all the hills were trembling.

I looked,

and there was no human being,

and every bird of heaven had departed.

I looked,

and behold, Carmel was a desert;

and all its cities were destroyed

before the Lord,

and before the face of his furious anger.

For thus says the Lord:

The whole land shall be desolate,

yet I will not bring it to complete destruction.

The land shall mourn,

and the heavens above shall grieve,

because I have spoken [Alternative: “I am”];

[Col. 0856A] I have thought,

and I have not repented,

nor have I turned back from it.

At the sound of the horseman and the archer, every city flees;

they enter the steep places and climb the rocks:

All the cities are abandoned,

and no one dwells in them.

But you, once devastated, what will you do?

when you clothe yourself in scarlet,

when you adorn yourself with a golden necklace,

and paint your eyes with antimony—will you adorn yourself in vain?

Your lovers have despised you;

they will seek your life.

For I heard a sound like that of a woman in labor,

anguish like that of a woman giving birth:

The voice of the daughter of Zion [Note: [Col. 0855D] This is read less correctly in the Commentary, between “those dying” [Col. 0856D] and “stretching out,” etc.] dying and stretching out

her hands:

“Woe is me, for my life has failed because of the slain!”

[Col. 0856B] [Chapter V] Go around the roads of Jerusalem,

and look, and examine,

and search in her squares,

to see whether you can find a man practicing justice and seeking faithfulness:

and I will be merciful to him.

And even if they say, “As the Lord lives,”

they will swear falsely by this as well.

Lord, your eyes look for faithfulness:

you struck them, and they did not grieve;

you consumed them, and they refused to accept discipline;

They hardened their faces more than rock,

and they were unwilling to return.

But I said:

“Perhaps they are poor and foolish,

unaware of the way of the Lord, the judgment of their God.

I will therefore go to the great

and speak to them:

for they know the way of the Lord, the judgment of their God.”

[Col. 0856C] And behold, these had broken the yoke even more completely,

and had torn the bonds.

Therefore the lion from the forest struck them,

the wolf at evening ravaged them,

the leopard kept watch over their cities:

Everyone who goes out from them will be captured;

for their transgressions have multiplied,

their apostasies have grown strong.

How can I be merciful to you concerning this?

Your sons have forsaken me,

and swear by those who are not gods:

I satisfied them, and they committed adultery,

and they wantoned in the house of a prostitute.

They became lustful and spirited stallions [Note: [Col. 0856D] In the Commentary, “toward women” is added, and at the end of the verse, “to me,” from the Septuagint; for these words do not sound in the Hebrew original.],

each neighing after his neighbor’s wife.

Shall I not punish them for these things? says the Lord.

Or shall my soul not avenge itself on such a nation?

Go up upon its walls and destroy,

but do not bring it to complete ruin:

Remove its branches,

for they are not the Lord’s.

For the house of Israel has acted utterly treacherously against me,

and the house of Judah, says the Lord.

They denied the Lord and said:

“He is not the one” [Alternative: “they did not speak”]:

“Evil will not come upon us,

and we shall not see sword or famine.

The prophets have become wind,

and no answer was in them:

so these things will happen to them.”

[Col. 0857A] Thus says the Lord, the God of hosts:

Because you have spoken this word:

behold, I make my words fire in your mouth,

and this people wood, and it will devour

them.

Behold, I am bringing upon you a nation from afar,

house of Israel, says the Lord—

a strong nation, an ancient nation,

a nation whose language you will not know,

nor understand what it says.

Its quiver is like an open grave;

all of them are mighty men.

And it will consume your harvest and your bread;

it will devour your sons and your daughters;

it will consume your flocks and your herds;

it will consume your vine and your fig tree;

and it will crush your fortified cities, in which you place

your trust, with the sword.

Nevertheless, in those days, says the Lord,

I will not bring you to complete ruin.

[Col. 0857B] And if you say, “Why has the Lord our God

done all these things to us?”

you shall say to them:

“As you forsook me and served a foreign god in your land,

so you shall serve foreigners in a land that is not yours.”

Announce this to the house of Jacob,

and make it heard in Judah, saying:

Hear this, foolish people, who have no heart:

you have eyes, but do not see;

you have ears, but do not hear.

Will you not fear me, says the Lord,

and tremble before me?

I set the sand as a boundary for the sea,

an eternal ordinance that it cannot pass:

They are stirred up, but cannot prevail;

its waves surge, but cannot cross it.

[Col. 0857C] But this people has an unbelieving and rebellious heart;

they have turned aside and gone away.

They have not said in their heart:

“Let us fear the Lord our God,

who gives us the early and late rain

in its season,

who preserves for us the fullness of the annual harvest.”

Your iniquities [Note: [Col. 0857D] All the manuscript copies of the biblical books have the first person instead of the second, namely, “our iniquities”; and this is clearly a copyists’ error, as can easily be proved from what follows. MART.] have turned these things aside,

and your sins have withheld good from you.

For wicked men have been found among my people, lying in wait

like bird-catchers,

setting traps and snares to catch men.

Like a cage full of birds,

so their houses are full of deceit;

therefore they have become great and rich.

They have grown fat and sleek,

[Col. 0857D] and have passed beyond my words in the worst manner.

They did not judge the case [Note: [Col. 0857D] The word “widow,” which is found here in the copies of the Canon and in certain other manuscript copies, is absent from the Hebrew text; nor is it represented in Saint Augustine’s *Speculum*, and Saint Jerome’s Commentaries do not mention this word. I think it was taken up or added through the error of scribes; for this is clearly demonstrated by certain copies of the sacred Scriptures, in which we find the aforementioned word added by a later hand. MART.],

they did not uphold the case of the orphan,

and they did not judge the cause of the poor.

Shall I not punish them for these things? says the Lord.

Or shall my soul not avenge itself on such a nation?

Astonishment and wonders have occurred in the land:

The prophets prophesied lies,

and the priests applauded with their hands.

And my people loved such things:

[Col. 0858A] what, then, will happen at its end?

[Chapter VI] Strengthen yourselves, sons of Benjamin, in the midst

of Jerusalem,

and blow the trumpet in Tekoa,

and raise a banner over Beth-haccerem:

for evil has looked out from the north,

and great destruction.

I have compared the daughter of Zion to a beautiful and delicate woman.

Shepherds will come to her, and their flocks;

they will pitch tents around her;

each one will pasture those who are

under his hand.

Prepare war against her:

arise, and let us go up at midday.

Woe to us, for the day has declined,

because the evening shadows have lengthened.

Arise, and let us go up by night,

and let us destroy her houses.

For thus says the Lord of hosts:

Cut down her wood,

[Col. 0858B] and cast up a siege rampart around Jerusalem:

This is the city of visitation;

all kinds of oppression are in its midst.

As a cistern keeps its water cool,

so she has kept her wickedness cool:

Iniquity and devastation will be heard in her;

before me there is continually weakness and plague.

Be instructed, Jerusalem,

lest my soul depart from you,

lest I make you desolate,

an uninhabited land.

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

They will gather the remnants of Israel as far as the grape cluster,

as in a vineyard:

Turn your hand, like a grape-gatherer, toward the basket.

To whom shall I speak?

and whom shall I warn, so that he may hear?

Behold, their ears are uncircumcised,

[Col. 0858C] and they cannot hear:

Behold, the word of the Lord has become a reproach to them,

and they will not receive it.

Therefore I am full of the fury of the Lord;

I am weary of enduring.

Pour it out upon the child outside,

and likewise upon the assembly of young men:

For man and woman shall be captured,

the old man together with the one full of days.

And their houses shall pass to others,

their fields and wives alike:

for I will stretch out my hand over the inhabitants of the land,

says the Lord.

For from the least to the greatest, all pursue greed,

and from prophet to priest, all practice deceit.

[Col. 0858D] And they treated the wound of the daughter of my people shamefully, saying:

“Peace, peace,”

when there was no peace.

They were ashamed,

because they committed abomination;

yet they were not ashamed of their shame,

and did not know how to blush.

Therefore they will fall among those who fall;

at the time of their visitation they will collapse, says the Lord.

[Col. 0859A] Thus says the Lord:

Stand upon the roads and look,

and ask about the ancient paths, which is the good way,

and walk in it;

and you will find rest for your souls.

But they said, “We will not walk in it.”

And I appointed watchmen over you:

“Listen to the sound of the trumpet.”

But they said, “We will not listen.”

Therefore hear, nations, and know, O congregation,

what I will do to them.

Hear, O earth:

Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people,

the fruit of their thoughts,

because they did not listen to my words,

and rejected my law.

Why do you bring me frankincense from Sheba,

and fragrant reed from a distant land?

Your burnt offerings are not acceptable,

and your sacrifices have not pleased me.

[Col. 0859B] Therefore thus says the Lord:

Behold, I am bringing ruins upon this people,

and fathers and sons will fall among them together;

neighbor and friend will perish.

Thus says the Lord:

Behold, a people is coming from the land of the north,

and a great nation will arise from the ends of the earth.

It will take up bow and shield;

it is cruel and will not show mercy.

Its voice will roar like the sea;

they will mount horses,

prepared like a man for battle,

against you, daughter of Zion.

We have heard its report;

our hands have grown weak;

distress has seized us,

pains like those of a woman in labor.

Do not go out into the fields,

and do not walk on the road,

[Col. 0859C] for the enemy’s sword is terror all around.

Daughter of my people, gird yourself with sackcloth,

and sprinkle yourself with ashes;

make mourning for yourself as for an only child,

bitter lamentation,

for the destroyer will suddenly come upon us.

I have appointed you as a strong tester among my people,

and you shall know and test their way.

All these are princes who turn aside,

who walk deceitfully;

bronze and iron:

they are all corrupt.

The bellows have failed,

the lead has been consumed by the fire;

the smelter has smelted in vain,

for their wickednesses have not been consumed.

Call them rejected silver,

for the Lord has rejected them.

[Chapter VII] The word that came to Jeremiah

from the Lord, saying:

[Col. 0859D] Stand at the gate of the house of the Lord,

and proclaim this word there, and say:

Hear the word of the Lord, all Judah,

you who enter through these gates

to worship the Lord.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Make your ways and your practices good,

and I will dwell with you in this place.

Do not trust in lying [Alternative: “false”] words,

saying:

“The temple of the Lord,

the temple of the Lord,

the temple of the Lord is this.”

For if you truly make your ways and your practices straight;

if you execute judgment between a man and his neighbor;

if you do not oppress the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow;

[Col. 0860A] if you do not shed innocent blood in this place;

and if you do not go after foreign gods to your own harm—

I will dwell with you in this place,

in the land that I gave to your fathers from age to age

and forever.

Behold, you trust yourselves in lying words,

which will not profit you:

stealing,

murdering,

committing adultery,

swearing falsely,

offering libations to the Baals,

and going after foreign gods whom you do not know.

Then you come and stand before me in this house,

in which my name has been invoked,

and you say:

“We have been delivered,”

because we have committed all these abominations.

Has this house, in which my name has been invoked,

therefore become a den of thieves in your eyes?

[Col. 0860B] I, even I, am he;

I have seen it, says the Lord.

Go to my place in Shiloh,

where my name dwelt at the beginning,

and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people

Israel.

And now, because you have done all these works, says the Lord,

and I spoke to you, rising early and speaking, but you did not listen;

and I called you,

but you did not answer;

I will do to this house, in which my name has been invoked,

and in which you trust,

and to the place that I gave to you and your fathers,

as I did to Shiloh.

And I will cast you away from my presence,

as I cast away all your brothers,

the whole offspring of Ephraim.

[Col. 0860C] Therefore you shall not pray for this people,

nor take up praise and prayer on their behalf,

and do not oppose me,

for I will not hear you.

Do you not see what these people are doing in the cities of Judah and

in the streets of Jerusalem?

The sons gather wood,

the fathers kindle the fire,

and the women mix fat,

to make cakes for the queen of heaven,

and pour out libations to foreign gods,

and provoke me to anger.

Are they provoking me to anger? says the Lord.

Are they not rather provoking themselves to the shame of their faces?

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

Behold, my fury and my indignation are being poured out [Alternative:

“have been poured out”] upon this place,

upon men and beasts,

and upon the trees of the countryside,

[Col. 0860D] and upon the crops of the land;

it will burn, and will not be extinguished.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices,

and eat meat.

For I did not speak with your fathers,

nor command them, on the day when I brought

them out of the land of Egypt,

concerning burnt offerings and sacrifices.

But this word I commanded them, saying:

“Listen to my voice, and I will be your God,

and you shall be my people;

and walk in every way that I have commanded you,

so that it may go well with you.”

But they did not listen, nor incline their ear;

instead they went according to their own desires

and the perversity of their evil heart;

and they became backward and not forward,

[Col. 0861A] from the day when their fathers came out of the land of Egypt to this day.

And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early day

after day and sending them.

But they did not listen to me, nor incline their ear;

instead they stiffened their neck [Alternative: “their neck” added],

and acted worse than their fathers.

And you shall speak all these words to them, but they will not listen to you;

and you shall call them, but they will not answer you.

And you shall say to them:

“This is the nation that did not listen to the voice of the Lord its God,

nor received correction.

Faithfulness has perished,

and has been removed from their mouth.”

Cut off your hair and throw it away,

and take up a lamentation on the heights;

for the Lord has rejected and abandoned the generation

of his fury,

[Col. 0861B] because the sons of Judah did evil in my eyes,

says the Lord.

They placed their offenses in the house in which my name has been invoked,

to defile it;

and they built the high places of Topheth, which is in the valley

of the son of Hinnom,

to burn their sons and daughters with fire—something

I did not command, nor did it enter my heart.

Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

when it will no longer be called Topheth, or the valley of the son

of Hinnom,

but the valley of slaughter.

And they will bury [Alternative: “be buried”] in Topheth,

because there will be no room.

And the corpses of this people will be food for the birds

of the sky and the beasts of the earth,

and there will be no one to drive them away.

And I will silence from the cities of Judah and from the streets of

[Col. 0861C] Jerusalem the voice of joy and the voice of gladness,

the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride,

for the land will become desolate.

[Chapter VIII] At that time, says the Lord,

they will bring out the bones of the kings of Judah and the bones of its princes,

and the bones of the priests,

and the bones of the prophets,

and the bones of those who lived in Jerusalem, from their tombs.

And they will spread them out before the sun and the moon,

and all the host of heaven, which they loved,

and served,

and followed,

and sought,

and worshiped.

They will not be gathered up or buried;

they will be dung upon the face of the earth.

And they will choose death rather than life,

[Note: [Col. 0861D] Saint Augustine recognizes the following nine verses in the *Speculum*, and determined that there are exactly that many up to the words “How do you say,” etc. From this you can see how far from the truth certain recent writers are when they rashly teach that the individual verses, which they very often call the authorities of ecclesiastical writers, contained six continuous words. [Col. 0862D] The prophets’ verses as written now prove the contrary; and the same is demonstrated even more clearly below from the works of Job, David, and Solomon, which are found written στιχηρῶς (*stichērōs*, in verse form) in both copies of the Canon of Hebrew truth. MART.] all who remain of this evil kindred,

in all the places that remain, to which

[Col. 0861D] I have driven them, says the Lord of hosts.

And you shall say to them:

Thus says the Lord:

Does one who falls [Alternative: “will fall”] not rise again?

and does one who has turned away not return?

Why, then, has this people in Jerusalem turned away

with a persistent rebellion?

They have grasped deceit,

and have refused to return.

I paid attention and listened:

no one speaks what is good;

[Col. 0862A] there is no one who repents of his sin,

saying:

“What have I done?”

All have turned to their own course,

like a horse rushing into battle.

The kite in the sky knows its season;

the turtledove,

the swallow,

and the stork

observe the time of their coming;

but my people

do not know the judgment of the Lord.

How can you say, “We are wise,

and the law of the Lord is with us”?

Truly, the lying pen of the scribes has worked deceit.

The wise have been put to shame,

terrified and captured;

for they have rejected the word of the Lord,

and there is no wisdom in them.

[Col. 0862B] Therefore I will give their wives to foreigners,

their fields to heirs;

for from the least to the greatest they all pursue greed

[Alternative: “are devoted to greed”];

from prophet to priest they all practice falsehood.

And they treated the wound of the daughter of my people shamefully, saying:

“Peace, peace,”

when there was no peace.

They were ashamed,

because they committed abomination;

yet they were not ashamed of their shame,

and did not know how to blush.

Therefore they will fall among those who fall;

at the time of their visitation they will collapse, says the Lord.

Gathering, I will gather them, says the Lord:

There are no grapes on the vines,

[Col. 0862C] and there are no figs on the fig tree;

the leaf has fallen,

and I have given them what has passed away.

Why are we sitting?

Come together, and let us enter the fortified city,

and let us be silent there;

for the Lord our God has made us silent,

and has given us water of gall to drink.

For we have sinned against the Lord.

We waited for peace,

but there was no good;

a time of healing,

and behold, terror.

From Dan the snorting of his horses has been heard;

at the sound of the neighing of his warhorses the whole land

was shaken.

And they came and devoured the land and its fullness,

the city and its inhabitants.

For behold, I am sending among you basilisk-serpents for which [Col. 0862D] there is no charm,

and they will bite you, says the Lord.

My pain is upon pain;

my heart within me mourns.

Behold, the voice of the cry of the daughter of my people from a distant land:

“Is the Lord not in Zion,

or is her king not in her?”

Why, then, did they provoke me to anger with

their carved images,

with foreign vanities?

[Col. 0863A] The harvest has passed,

the summer has ended,

and we have not been saved.

Because of the wound of the daughter of my people I am wounded and

sorrowful;

astonishment has seized me.

Is there no balm in Gilead,

or is there no physician there?

Why, then, has the wound of the daughter of my people not been bound up?

[Chapter IX] Who will give water to my head,

and a fountain of tears to my eyes?

Then I will weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people.

Who will give me a lodging for travelers in the wilderness,

so that I may leave my people and depart from them?

For all are adulterers,

a gathering of transgressors.

And they have stretched out their tongue like a bow of deceit

and not of truth.

They have grown strong in the land,

[Col. 0863B] for they have gone from evil to evil,

and have not known me, says the Lord.

Let each one guard himself from his neighbor,

and let no one trust in any brother;

for every brother utterly supplants [Alternative: “with treachery will supplant”],

and every friend walks deceitfully.

And each man mocks his brother,

and they do not speak the truth.

For they have taught their tongue to speak lies;

they have labored to act wickedly.

Your dwelling is in the midst of an idol;

through deceit they refused to know me, says the Lord.

Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts:

Behold, I will smelt them and test them;

for what else shall I do because of the daughter of my people?

Their tongue is a wounding arrow;

it has spoken deceit.

With his mouth he speaks peace with his friend,

[Col. 0863C] but secretly he sets an ambush for him.

Shall I not punish them for these things? says the Lord.

Or shall my soul not avenge itself on such a nation?

Upon the mountains I will take up weeping and lamentation,

and upon the beautiful places of the wilderness, mourning,

because they have been burned, since there is no passerby;

and they have not heard the voice of the one who possesses them.

From the bird of the sky to the cattle,

they have migrated and gone away.

And I will make Jerusalem heaps of sand,

and lairs of dragons;

and I will make the cities of Judah desolate,

because there is no inhabitant.

Who is the wise man who understands this,

and to whom the word of the Lord’s mouth comes, so that he may announce

it?

Why has the land perished and been burned [Alternative:

“is burned”] like a wilderness,

[Col. 0863D] because there is no one who passes through it?

And the Lord said:

Because they forsook my law, which I gave them,

and did not listen to my voice, nor walk in it;

but they followed the perversity of their heart,

and the Baals,

which [Alternative: “whom”] they learned from their fathers.

Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Behold, I will feed [Note: [Col. 0863D] Saint Jerome placed this more precisely according to the Hebrew exemplar in the Commentary: “I will feed this people.” The Hebrew likewise has [Hebrew term not reproduced in the supplied text].] this people with wormwood,

and I will give them water of gall to drink.

And I will scatter them among nations whom neither they nor their fathers knew,

[Col. 0864A] and I will send the sword after them until they are consumed.

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

Consider,

and summon the mourning women, and let them come;

and send for those who are skilled,

and let them hurry.

Let them hasten and take up lamentation over us;

let our eyes pour forth tears,

and let our eyelids flow with waters.

For the voice of lamentation has been heard from Zion:

“How we have been devastated and greatly confounded!

For we have forsaken the land,

because our dwellings have been thrown down.”

Therefore hear, women, the word of the Lord,

and let your ears receive the word of his mouth.

Teach your daughters lamentation,

and each one her neighbor a dirge.

For death has climbed through our windows;

it has entered our houses,

to destroy the children outside,

[Col. 0864B] and the young men in the streets.

Speak:

Thus says the Lord:

The corpse of a man will fall like dung upon

the face of the land,

and like grass behind the reaper,

and there will be no one to gather it.

Thus says the Lord:

Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom,

nor the strong man glory in his strength,

nor the rich man glory in his riches;

but let the one who glories glory in this:

to understand and know me,

that I am the Lord who practices mercy, judgment, and righteousness in

the earth.

For these things please me [Note: [Col. 0863D] Read here in Saint Augustine’s *Speculum*, “and after thirteen” [Col. 0864D] verses, not “after sixteen.” MART.], says the Lord.

Behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

when I will punish everyone who is circumcised in the foreskin,

[Col. 0864C] Egypt,

and Judah,

and Edom,

and the sons of Ammon,

and Moab,

and all those who have their hair cut short,

who dwell in the wilderness.

For all the nations have foreskins,

but the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.

[Chapter X] Hear the word

that the Lord has spoken concerning you, house of Israel.

Thus says the Lord:

Do not depart according to the ways of the nations,

and do not fear the signs of heaven, which the nations fear;

for the laws of the peoples are vain.

For a tree is cut from the forest,

the work of the craftsman’s hands with an axe.

He decorates it with silver and gold;

he fastens it with nails and hammers,

so that it will not come apart.

[Col. 0864D] They are fashioned in the likeness of a palm tree,

but they will not speak.

They are carried and lifted,

because they cannot walk.

Therefore do not fear them,

for they can do neither evil nor good.

There is none like you, Lord;

you are great, and your name is great in might.

Who will not fear you, O king of the nations?

For this is your glory.

Among all the wise men of the nations,

and in all their kingdoms, there is none like you.

Together [Note: [Col. 0864D] In the Commentary: “Fools and wise men.” See what is noted there.] they will be proved foolish and senseless;

[Col. 0865A] their doctrine of vanities is wood.

Silver beaten thin is brought from Tarshish,

and gold from Uphaz;

the work of the craftsman and the hands of the goldsmith.

Hyacinth and purple are their clothing.

All these are the work of artisans.

But the Lord God is true;

he is the living God and everlasting King.

At his indignation the earth will be shaken,

and the nations will not endure his threat.

Thus, then, you shall say to them:

The gods who did not make the heavens and the earth

shall perish from the earth and from what is under the heavens.

He who made the earth by his power,

prepared the world by his wisdom,

and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.

At his voice he gives a multitude of waters in the heavens,

and raises clouds from the ends of the earth.

He makes lightning for the rain,

and brings forth the wind from his treasuries.

[Col. 0865B] Every man has become foolish through knowledge [Alternative: “through his knowledge”];

every craftsman has been put to shame by his carved image,

for what he cast is false,

and there is no spirit in them.

They are vanity, a work worthy of ridicule;

at the time of their visitation they will perish.

The portion of Jacob is not like these,

for he is the one who formed all things;

and Israel is the rod of his inheritance.

The Lord of hosts is his name.

Gather your shame from the earth,

you who dwell under siege.

For thus says the Lord:

Behold, I will cast far away the inhabitants of the land at this time,

and I will afflict them so that they will be found [Note: [Col. 0865D] In all the manuscripts and in the Canon the negative particle is added, so that the reading is “so that they will not be found.” But Saint Jerome himself, in Book II of his Commentary on Jeremiah, teaches that it should be read without this negation. “Thus,” he says, “I will cause them to be besieged, and thus I will trouble and hem them in, so that all will be found in the city and will be unable to escape the evil.” MART.].

Woe is me because of my wound,

my grievous plague.

[Col. 0865C] But I said:

“Surely this is my sickness,

and I will bear it.”

My tent has been devastated;

all my cords have been broken;

my sons have gone away from me, and are no more.

There is no one who will extend my tent any further,

and raise up my tent-curtains.

For the shepherds have acted foolishly,

and have not sought the Lord;

therefore they have not understood,

and their whole flock has been scattered.

Behold, the sound of a report is coming,

and a great commotion from the land of the north,

to make the cities of Judah [Alternative: “in Judah”] desolate,

and a dwelling place of dragons.

I know, Lord, that a man’s way is not his own,

nor is it within a man to walk and direct his steps.

Correct me, Lord,

yet with judgment, and not in your anger,

lest you reduce me to nothing.

[Col. 0865D] Pour out your indignation upon the nations that have not known you,

and upon the provinces that have not invoked your name,

because they have devoured Jacob and consumed him,

and destroyed him [Alternative: “his place”],

and laid waste his glory.

[Chapter XI] The word that came from the Lord to

Jeremiah, saying:

Hear the words of this covenant,

and speak to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

[Col. 0866A] And you shall say to them:

Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel:

Cursed is the man who does not listen to the words of this covenant,

which I commanded your fathers on the day when I brought

them out of the land of Egypt,

from the iron furnace, saying:

“Listen to my voice, and do all that I command you,

and you shall be my people, and I will be your

God,

so that I may establish the oath that I swore to your fathers,

to give them a land flowing with milk and honey,

as it is this day.”

And I answered and said:

“Amen, Lord.”

And the Lord said to me:

Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah

and outside Jerusalem, saying:

Hear the words of this covenant, and do them,

[Col. 0866B] for I solemnly warned your fathers,

on the day when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, until

this day.

Rising early, I solemnly warned them,

and said:

“Listen to my voice.”

But they did not listen, nor incline their ear;

instead each one went in the perversity of his evil heart.

And I brought upon them all the words of this covenant,

which I commanded them to do,

but they did not do them.

And the Lord said to me:

A conspiracy has been found among the men of Judah

and among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They have returned to the former iniquities of their fathers,

who refused to hear my words.

And these too have gone after foreign gods,

to serve them.

[Col. 0866C] The house of Israel and the house of Judah have made my covenant void,

which I made with their fathers.

Therefore thus says the Lord:

Behold, I am bringing evils upon them

from which they will not be able to escape;

and they will cry out to me, but I will not hear them.

And the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go

and cry out to the gods to whom they pour out libations,

but they will not save them in the time of their affliction.

For according to the number of your cities were your gods,

O Judah;

and according to the number of the streets of Jerusalem you have set up

altars of shame,

altars for offering libations to the Baals.

Therefore you shall not pray for this people,

nor take up praise and prayer on their behalf,

for I will not hear them at the time of their cry to me,

at the time of their affliction.

[Col. 0866D] What is my beloved doing in my house,

since she has committed many crimes?

Will holy flesh remove from you your wickednesses

in which you exulted?

An olive tree, luxuriant,

beautiful,

fruitful,

splendid—

the Lord called your name.

At the sound of the word, a great fire blazed in it,

and its thickets were burned.

And the Lord of hosts, who planted you, spoke evil against you

[Col. 0867A] because of the evils of the house of Israel and the house of Judah,

which they committed to provoke me,

offering libations to the Baals.

But you, Lord, showed me, and I came to know.

Then [Note: [Col. 0867D] Less correctly read in the Commentary: “You” instead of “Then,” which is in the Hebrew.] you showed me their designs.

And I was like a gentle lamb being led to

the sacrifice,

and I did not know that they had devised plots against me, [Note: [Col. 0867D] Neither does the Hebrew text add “saying,” nor did the holy Father place this word in the Commentary.]

saying:

“Let us put wood into his bread,

and let us cut him off [Alternative: “crush him”] from the land of the living,

so that his name may no longer be remembered.”

But you, Lord of hosts, who judge justly

and test the kidneys and hearts,

let me see your vengeance upon them,

for to you I have revealed my cause.

Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the men of Anathoth,

who seek your life and say:

“Do not prophesy in the name of the Lord,

so that you may not die by our hands.”

Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts:

Behold, I will punish them.

The young men will die by the sword,

their sons and their daughters will die of famine,

and none of them will be left.

For I will bring evil upon the men of Anathoth,

the year of their visitation.

[Chapter XII] You are indeed righteous, Lord,

if I dispute with you;

yet I will speak just judgments to you:

Why does the way of the wicked prosper?

Why is it well with all who transgress and act wickedly?

You planted them, and they took root;

they advance, and produce fruit.

You are near their mouths,

but far from their kidneys.

And you, Lord, know me;

you have seen me and tested my heart before you.

Gather them like a flock for sacrifice,

and sanctify them for the day of slaughter.

How long will the land mourn,

and all the grass of the region wither,

because of the wickedness of those who dwell in it?

The animal and the bird have been consumed,

because they said:

“He will not see our end.”

If you have grown weary running with foot soldiers,

how will you contend with horses?

And when you are secure in a land of peace [Alternative: “If you trust in a land of peace”],

what will you do in the pride of the Jordan?

For even your brothers and the house of your father,

even they have fought against you,

and have cried out after you with a full voice.

Do not believe them when they speak good things to you.

I have left my house,

I have abandoned my inheritance,

[Col. 0867D] I have given my beloved life into the hand of its enemies.

My inheritance has become for me like a lion in the forest;

it has raised its voice against me;

therefore I have hated it.

Is my inheritance for me like a many-colored bird?

Is it like a bird dyed all over?

Come, gather yourselves, all the beasts of the earth;

hasten to devour.

Many shepherds have destroyed my vineyard;

they have trampled my portion;

they have made my desirable portion a desolate wilderness.

[Col. 0868A] They have made it a wasteland,

and it has mourned over me.

The whole land has been utterly desolated,

because there is no one who considers in his heart.

The destroyers have come upon all the paths of the wilderness,

for the sword of the Lord will devour from one end of the land to the other;

there is no peace for any flesh.

They sowed wheat and reaped thorns;

they received an inheritance, but it will not benefit them.

Be ashamed of your fruits,

because of the anger of the Lord’s fury.

Thus says the Lord against all my most wicked neighbors,

who touch the inheritance that I distributed to my people Israel:

Behold, I will uproot them from their land,

and I will uproot the house of Judah from their midst.

And when I have uprooted them, I will turn and have mercy on them;

[Col. 0868B] and I will restore them, each man to his inheritance [Alt. “in his inheritance”], and each man to his land.

And it shall be: if, having been instructed, they learn the ways of my people, so that they swear by my name, “The Lord lives,” just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, they shall be built up in the midst of my people.

But if they will not listen, I will utterly uproot and destroy that nation, says the Lord.

### Chapter XIII

Thus says the Lord to me:

“Go and acquire for yourself a linen loincloth, and put it around your loins, but do not bring it into water.”

And I acquired the loincloth according to the word of the Lord, and put it around my loins.

And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying:

“Take the loincloth that you acquired, which is around your loins, and, rising, go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in a hole in the rock.”

And I went and hid it in the Euphrates, as the Lord had commanded me.

And after many days the Lord said to me:

“Rise, go to the Euphrates, and take from there the loincloth that I commanded you to hide there.”

And I went to the Euphrates, dug, and took the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it. And behold, the loincloth had rotted, so that it was fit for no use.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Thus says the Lord:

“So will I cause the great pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem to rot: this most wicked people, who refuse to hear my words and walk in the perversity of their heart [Alt. adds: ‘of their most wicked heart’]. They have gone after foreign gods, to serve and worship them; and they shall be like this loincloth, which is fit for no use.

“For just as a loincloth clings to a man’s loins, so I attached to myself the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah, says the Lord, so that they might be my people, my name, my praise, and my glory; but they did not listen.

“Therefore you shall speak this word to them:

[Col. 0869A] Thus says the Lord God of Israel:

‘Every wineskin shall be filled with wine.’

And they will say to you:

‘Do we not know that every wineskin shall be filled [Alt. ‘is to be filled’] with wine?’

And you shall say to them:

Thus says the Lord:

“Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, and the kings who sit from the line of David upon his throne, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, with drunkenness. And I will scatter them, each man from his brother, and fathers and sons alike, says the Lord. I will not spare, nor grant pardon, nor have mercy, so as not to destroy them.

“Hear and perceive with your ears. Do not exalt yourselves, for the Lord has spoken. Give glory to the Lord your God before it grows dark, and before your feet stumble against the dark mountains. You will await light, but he will turn it into the shadow of death and darkness.

“But if you will not hear this, my soul shall weep in secret [Alt. ‘your soul shall weep in secret’] because of pride. It shall weep bitterly [Alt. adds: ‘Jerusalem shall weep bitterly’], and my eye shall shed a tear, because the Lord’s flock has been captured.

“Say to the king and to the queen:

‘Humble yourselves; sit down, for the crown of your glory has descended from your head.’

“The cities of the South are shut, and there is no one to open them. All Judah [Alt. ‘Judea’] has been carried away in complete exile.

“Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock that was given to you, your renowned sheep? What will you say when he visits you? For you yourself taught them against you, and instructed them for your own ruin [Alt. ‘you teach them against yourself, and instruct them for your own ruin’].

“Will not pains seize you, like a woman in labor?

“But if you say in your heart, ‘Why have these things happened to me?’—because of the multitude of your iniquity your shameful parts have been exposed; your soles have been defiled.

“If an Ethiopian can change his skin, or a leopard its spots, then you too will be able to do good, once you have learned evil.

“And I will scatter them like stubble carried by the wind in the desert.

[Col. 0869D] “This is your lot and the measure of your portion from me, says the Lord, because you have forgotten me and trusted in falsehood.

“Therefore I have also uncovered your thighs [Alt. ‘your hindparts’] before your face, and your disgrace, your adulteries, your neighing, and the wickedness of your prostitution have appeared.

“Upon the hills in the countryside I saw your abominations.

“Woe to you, Jerusalem; you shall not be cleansed after me. How long still?”

### Chapter XIV

The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning the words about the drought:

Judah mourned, and its gates collapsed, and they were darkened upon the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem rose up.

The elders sent their younger men for water. They came to draw it, but found no water; they carried their vessels back empty. They were ashamed and afflicted, and covered their heads.

Because of the devastation of the land, because rain did not come upon the land, the farmers were ashamed and covered their heads.

For even the doe in the field gave birth and abandoned [it], because there was no grass.

And the wild asses stood on the rocks; they drew in the wind like dragons. Their eyes failed, because there was no grass.

If our iniquities testify against us, act for the sake of your name, O Lord, for our apostasies are many; we have sinned against you.

O Hope of Israel, its savior in the time of trouble:

Why will you be like a sojourner in the land, and like a traveler turning aside to stay for the night?

Why will you be like a wandering man, like [Alt. ‘or’] a strong man who cannot save?

But you are among us, O Lord, and your name has been invoked over us; do not abandon us.

Thus says the Lord to this people, who loved to move their feet and did not rest, and who did not please the Lord:

“Now he will remember their iniquities and visit their sins.”

And the Lord said to me:

“Do not pray for the good of this people.

“When they fast, I will not hear their prayers. And if they offer burnt offerings and sacrifices, I will not accept them, for I will consume them by sword, famine, and pestilence.”

[Col. 0870C] And I said:

“Ah, ah, ah, Lord God! The prophets say to them, ‘You shall not see the sword, and famine shall not be among you, but he will give you true peace in this place.’”

And the Lord said to me:

“The prophets prophesy falsely in my name. I did not send them, nor command them, nor speak to them. They prophesy to you a false vision, divination, fraud [Alt. ‘a fraudulent thing’], and the deceit of their own heart.

“Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name, whom I did not send, saying, ‘Sword and famine shall not be in this land’: By sword and famine those prophets shall be consumed, and the people to whom they prophesy shall be cast out in the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and sword, and there shall be no one to bury them—them, their wives, their sons, and their daughters—and I will pour out their own wickedness upon them.

“And you shall say this word to them:

‘Let my eyes shed tears night and day, and let them not be silent, for the virgin daughter of my people has been crushed with a great crushing, with a very grievous wound.

‘If I go out into the fields, behold, those slain by the sword; and if I enter the city, behold, those weakened by famine. For both prophet and priest have gone to a land they did not know.’

“Have you utterly rejected Judah? Or has your soul abhorred Zion? Why then have you struck us, so that there is no healing?

“We hoped for peace, but there is no good; and for a time of healing, but behold, confusion.

“We acknowledge our wickedness, O Lord, the iniquities of our fathers, because we have sinned against you.

“Do not give us over to reproach for the sake of your name, and do not dishonor the throne of your glory. Remember; do not annul your covenant with us.

“Are there among the idols of the nations any who bring rain? Or can the heavens give showers? Are you not the Lord our God, whom [Alt. ‘O Lord God, whom,’ etc.] we have awaited? For you made all these things.”

### Chapter XV

And the Lord said to me:

“Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my soul would not be toward this people. Cast them out from my presence, and let them go forth.

“And if they say to you, ‘Where shall we go?’ you shall say to them:

Thus says the Lord:

‘Those destined for death—to death;

and those destined for the sword—to the sword;

and those destined for famine—to famine;

and those destined for captivity—to captivity.’

“And I will visit them with four kinds of punishment, says the Lord: the sword for slaughter, dogs for tearing apart, and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth for devouring and scattering.

“And I will make them a terror to all the kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for all that he did in Jerusalem.

“For who will have mercy on you, Jerusalem? Or who will grieve for you? Or who will go to plead for your peace?

“You have abandoned me, says the Lord; you have gone backward. Therefore I will stretch out my hand against you and destroy you. I have grown weary of pleading.

“And I will scatter them with a winnowing fork at the gates of the land. I have slain and destroyed [Alt. ‘ruined’] my people, yet they have not turned back from their ways.

“Her widows have become more numerous to me than the sand of the sea. I brought upon the mother of the young man a destroyer at midday; I suddenly sent terror upon the cities.

“She who gave birth to seven has grown weak; her soul has failed. Her sun has set while it was still day; she has been put to shame and disgraced. And I will give what remains of them to the sword before their enemies, says the Lord.”

Woe is me, my mother, for you have borne me, a man of strife, a man of discord throughout the whole earth. I have neither lent at interest, nor has anyone lent to me; everyone curses me.

The Lord says:

“If your remnant is not for good,

if I do not meet you in the time of affliction,

and in the time of trouble [Note: [Col. 0871] The Commentary adds, ‘and distress’: closer to the Hebrew [Hebrew term omitted in source].]

against the enemy.

“Can iron be joined to iron from the north, and bronze?

I will give your wealth and your treasures for plunder, without payment, because of all your sins and in all your borders.

And I will bring your enemies from a land you do not know, because a fire has been kindled in my fury; it shall burn against you.

You know, O Lord; remember me and visit me, and protect me from those who persecute me. Do not take me away in your patience; know that I have endured reproach for your sake.

Your words were found, and I consumed them, and your word became joy and gladness to my heart, for your name was invoked over me, O Lord God of hosts.

I did not sit in the assembly of those who mock, nor did I rejoice because of your hand. I sat alone, because you filled me with denunciation [Alt. ‘bitterness’].

Why has my pain become perpetual, and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? It has become for me like deceitful waters that cannot be trusted.

Therefore thus says the Lord:

“If you return, I will restore you, and you shall stand before my face. And if you separate the precious from the worthless, you shall be as my mouth. They shall return to you, but you shall not return to them.

“And I will make you to this people a strong bronze wall. They will fight against you, but they will not prevail, because I am with you to save you and deliver you [Alt. omits ‘you’], says the Lord. And I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked, and redeem you from the hand of the strong.”

### Chapter XVI

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Do not take a wife, and do not let there be sons or daughters for you in this place.

“For thus says the Lord concerning the sons and daughters who are born in this place, and concerning their mothers who bore them, and concerning their fathers from whose stock they were born in this land:

“They shall die of grievous diseases; they shall not be mourned or buried. They shall be dung upon the face of the earth, and they shall be consumed by sword and famine. Their corpses shall be food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth [Alt. ‘their corpses’].”

For thus says the Lord:

“Do not enter a house of feasting, nor go to mourn, nor console them, for I have taken away my peace from this people, says the Lord, mercy and compassion.

“And great and small shall die in this land. They shall not be buried or mourned; no one shall make cuts or shave the head for them. Nor shall they break bread among them in mourning, to console anyone over the dead; nor shall they give them the cup of drink to console them over their father or mother.

“And do not enter a house of feasting [Alt. ‘you shall not enter’], to sit with them and eat and drink, for thus says the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel:

‘Behold, I will remove from this place, before your eyes and in your days, the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.’

“And when you announce all these words to this people, and they say to you, ‘Why has the Lord spoken against us all this great evil? What is our iniquity, and what is our sin that we have committed against the Lord our God?’ you shall say to them:

‘Because your fathers abandoned me, says the Lord, and went after foreign gods, served them, and worshiped them; they abandoned me and did not keep my law.

‘But you have acted worse than your fathers. For behold, each one walks after the perversity of his evil heart, so as not to listen to me.

‘Therefore I will cast you out of this land into a land that you and your fathers do not know, and there you shall serve foreign gods day and night, who will not give you rest.

‘Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when it shall no longer be said, “The Lord lives, who brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt,” but, “The Lord lives, who brought the children of Israel out of the land of the north and from all the lands to which he had driven them.” And I will restore them to their land, which I gave to their fathers.

‘Behold, I will send many fishers, says the Lord, and they shall fish for them. And after this I will send them many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain, and from every hill, and from the caves of the rocks.

‘For my eyes are upon all their ways; they are not hidden from my face, and their iniquity has not been concealed from my eyes.

‘And I will repay their first offenses doubly, and their sins, because they have polluted my land with the carcasses of their idols and filled my inheritance with their abominations.’

O Lord, my strength and my stronghold, and my refuge in the day of trouble: to you the nations shall come from the ends of the earth and say:

“Truly our fathers possessed falsehood, vanity that did not profit them.

“Can a man make gods for himself? Yet they are not gods.”

Therefore, behold, I will show them this time; I will show them my hand and my power, and they shall know that my name is the Lord.

### Chapter XVII

The sin of Judah is written with an iron stylus, with a diamond point, engraved upon the tablet of their heart and upon the horns of their altars.

When their sons remember their altars, their sacred groves, and their leafy trees upon the high mountains, sacrificing in the countryside, I will give your strength and all your treasures for plunder, and your high places because of your sins throughout all your borders.

[Col. 0874A] And you shall be left alone, separated from your inheritance, which I gave you; and I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, because you have kindled a fire in my fury; it shall burn forever.

Thus says the Lord:

“Cursed is the man who trusts in man, and makes flesh his arm, while his heart turns away from the Lord.

“He shall be like a tamarisk in the desert, and shall not see good when it comes; he shall dwell in dryness in the wilderness, in a salty and uninhabited land.

“Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his confidence [Alt. ‘hope’].

“He shall be like a tree transplanted [Alt. ‘that has been transplanted’] beside waters, sending its roots toward moisture; he shall not fear when heat comes.

“His leaf shall be green, and in the time of drought he shall not be anxious, nor shall he ever cease to bear fruit.

“The heart of all is devious and inscrutable; who can know it?

“I, the Lord, search the heart and test the kidneys; I give to each according to his way and according to the fruit of his devices.

“Like a partridge that broods over what it did not hatch, so is one who makes riches, but not by justice. In the middle of his days he will abandon them, and at his end he will be a fool.

“A throne of glory, exalted from the beginning, the place of our sanctification.

“O Hope of Israel, Lord: all who abandon you shall be put to shame; those who turn away [Note: [Col. 0873] In Hebrew there is only [Hebrew word(s) omitted in source], without ‘from you’; Saint Jerome does not acknowledge these words in the Commentary either.] from you shall be written in the earth, because they have abandoned the Lord, the fountain of living waters.

[Col. 0874C] Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved, for you are my praise.

Behold, they say to me: “Where is the word of the Lord? Let it come.”

But I have not been troubled, following you as shepherd, and I have not desired the day of man. You know. What came forth from my lips was upright in your sight.

Do not be a terror to me [Alt. omits “be”]; you are my hope in the day of affliction.

Let those who persecute me be put to shame, but let me not be put to shame; let them be afraid, but let me not be afraid. Bring upon them the day of affliction, and crush them with double destruction.

Thus says the Lord to me:

“Go and stand at the gate of the sons of the people, through which the kings of Judah enter and depart, and at all the gates of Jerusalem, and say to them:

‘Hear the word of the Lord, kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem who enter through these gates.

‘Thus says the Lord:

Guard your lives, and do not carry burdens on the Sabbath day, nor bring them through the gates of Jerusalem.

‘Do not carry loads out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do not do any work. Sanctify the Sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.’

“But they did not listen or incline their ear; they hardened their neck, so as not to hear me and not to accept discipline.

“And it shall be: if you listen to me, says the Lord, so that you do not bring burdens through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, and if you sanctify the Sabbath day so that you do no work on it, kings and princes sitting upon the throne of David shall enter through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their princes, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and this city shall be inhabited forever.

“And they shall come from the cities of Judah and from the surroundings of Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the lowlands, from the hill country, and from the South, bringing burnt offerings, sacrifices, offerings, and incense, and bringing an offering into the house of the Lord.

“But if you will not listen to me, to sanctify the Sabbath day, and not to carry a burden or bring it through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall devour the houses of Jerusalem, and it shall not be extinguished.”

### Chapter XVIII

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:

“Rise and go down to the potter’s house, and there you shall hear my words.”

And I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was making a work upon the wheel.

And the vessel that he was making from clay with his hands was spoiled. Then he turned and made it into another vessel, as it seemed good in his eyes to make.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Just as this potter does, can I not also do to you, house of Israel?” says the Lord.

“Behold, like clay in the hand of the potter, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.

“Suddenly I will speak against a nation and against a kingdom, to uproot, destroy, and annihilate it.

“If that nation repents of its evil, against which I have spoken, I too will repent of the evil that I had thought to do to it.

“And suddenly I will speak concerning a nation and a kingdom, to build and plant it.

“If it does evil in my sight, so that it does not hear my voice, I will repent of the good that I had spoken of doing to it.

“Now therefore say to the man of Judah and to the inhabitants [Alt. ‘inhabitant’] of Jerusalem:

‘Thus says the Lord:

Behold, I am devising evil against you, and planning a plan against you. Let each one return from his evil way, and direct your ways and your purposes.’

“But they said: ‘We have despaired. For we shall follow our own plans, and each of us shall carry out the perversity of his evil heart.’

“Therefore thus says the Lord:

‘Ask among the nations: Who has heard such terrible things as the virgin Israel has committed so excessively?

‘Will the snow of Lebanon ever fail from the rock of the field? Or can the cold, gushing waters that flow down ever be torn away?

‘For my people have forgotten me, offering libations in vain, and causing them to stumble from their ways, from the ancient paths, so that they walk on paths by an untrodden road, to make their land a desolation and an everlasting hissing.

[Col. 0876A] ‘Everyone who passes through it will be astonished and will shake his head.

‘Like a scorching wind I will scatter them before the enemy; I will show them my back and not my face on the day of their destruction.’

And they said:

“Come, let us devise plans against Jeremiah. For the law shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue [Alt. adds: ‘with the tongue’], and let us pay no attention to all his words.”

Attend, O Lord, to me, and hear the voice of my adversaries.

Is evil repaid for good, because they dug a pit for my soul? Remember that I stood in your presence, speaking good on their behalf and turning your indignation away from them.

Therefore give their sons over to famine, and deliver them into the hands of the sword. Let their wives be childless and widows, and let their men be killed by death; let their young men be pierced by the sword in battle.

Let a cry be heard from their houses, for you will suddenly bring a raider upon them, because they dug a pit to capture me and hid snares for my feet.

But you, O Lord, know all their counsel against me for death. Do not be merciful toward their iniquity, and do not erase their sin from your sight. Let them fall before you; deal with them in the time of your fury.

### Chapter XIX

Thus says the Lord:

“Go and take a clay flask from the potter, from the elders of the people and the elders of the priests, and go out to the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is beside the entrance of the Potsherd Gate.

“And you shall proclaim there the words that I will speak to you, and say:

‘Hear the word of the Lord, kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem.

‘Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Behold, I will bring affliction upon this place, so that everyone who hears of it will have his ears tingle.

‘Because they abandoned me and made this place foreign, and poured libations [Alt. ‘will pour libations’] there to foreign gods whom neither they, nor their fathers, nor the kings of Judah knew; and they filled this place with the blood of the innocent.

‘And they built the high places of the Baals, to burn their sons with fire as a burnt offering to the Baals—things that I neither commanded nor spoke, nor did they enter my heart.

[Col. 0876D] ‘Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when this place shall no longer be called Topheth and the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

‘And I will destroy the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem in this place, and overthrow them by the sword before their enemies and by the hand of those who seek their lives.

‘And I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth. And I will make this city an object of astonishment and a hissing. Everyone who passes through it will be astonished and will hiss over all its wounds.

‘And I will feed them the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and each one shall eat the flesh of his neighbor during the siege and in the distress in which their enemies and those who seek their lives confine them.’

“And you shall break the flask before the eyes of the men who go with you, and say to them:

‘Thus says the Lord of hosts:

So will I break this people and this city, as a potter’s vessel is broken and cannot be restored again. And they shall be buried in Topheth, because there is no other place for burial.

‘Thus will I do to this place, says the Lord, and to its inhabitants, and I will make this city like Topheth.

‘And the houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah shall be unclean like the place of Topheth—all the houses on whose roofs they sacrificed to all the host of heaven and poured libations to foreign gods.’”

Jeremiah then came from Topheth, where the Lord had sent him to prophesy, and stood in the court of the house of the Lord and said to all the people:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

“Behold, I will bring upon this city and upon all its cities every evil that I have spoken against it, because they have hardened their neck so as not to hear my words.”

### Chapter XX

And Phassur son of Emmer, the priest who had been appointed chief in the house of the Lord, heard Jeremiah prophesying these words.

And Phassur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks that were at the upper Gate of Benjamin, in the house of the Lord.

When the next day dawned, Phassur brought Jeremiah out of the stocks.

And Jeremiah said to him:

[Col. 0877C] “The Lord has not called your name Phassur, but Terror on Every Side.

“For thus says the Lord:

‘Behold, I will make you a terror to yourself [Alt. omits “to yourself”] and to all your friends. They shall fall by the sword of their enemies, and your eyes shall see it. And I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall lead them to Babylon and strike them with the sword.

‘And I will give all the wealth of this city, all its labor, every price, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah into the hand of their enemies [Note: [Col. 0877D] Martianus read “my enemies” incorrectly, contrary to the other books, especially the Hebrew [Hebrew term omitted in source].]. They shall plunder them, take them, and lead them to Babylon.

‘But you, Phassur, and all the inhabitants of your house, shall go into captivity. You shall enter Babylon and die there, and there you and all your friends shall be buried, because you prophesied falsehood to them.’”

You seduced me, O Lord, and I was seduced; you were stronger than I and prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all day long; everyone mocks me.

For whenever I speak, I cry out, proclaiming violence and announcing devastation. And the word of the Lord has become for me reproach and ridicule all day long.

And I said:

“I will not remember him, nor speak any longer in his name.”

But [Alt. “For”] it became in my heart like a seething fire, shut up in my bones, and I grew weary, unable to endure it.

For I heard the insults of many and terror on every side:

“Denounce him, and let us denounce him,” from all the men who had been at peace with me and watched my side, in case he might somehow be deceived and we might prevail against him and take our revenge on him.

But the Lord is with me like a mighty warrior. Therefore those who persecute me shall fall and be weak. They shall be greatly put to shame [Alt. “Let them be greatly put to shame”], because they have not understood the everlasting reproach that shall never be erased.

But you, O Lord of hosts, tester of the righteous, who see the kidneys and the heart, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have revealed my cause.

Sing to the Lord; praise the Lord, for he has delivered the soul of the poor from the hand of evildoers [Alt. “the worst of evildoers”].

Cursed be the day on which I was born; may the day on which my mother bore me not be blessed.

Cursed be the man who announced to my father, saying, “A male child [Alt. ‘son’] has been born to you,” and made him rejoice as though with joy.

May that man be like the cities that the Lord overthrew and did not repent. May he hear a cry in the morning and a wailing at midday, because he did not kill me from the womb, so that my mother might have been my tomb, and her womb an eternal conception.

Why did I come forth from the womb, to see labor and sorrow, and for my days to be consumed in confusion?

### Chapter XXI

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord when King Zedekiah sent to him Phassur son of Melchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest, saying:

“Inquire of the Lord for us, because Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is warring against us. Perhaps the Lord will act toward us according to all his wonders, and he will withdraw from us.”

And Jeremiah said to them:

“Thus you shall say to Zedekiah:

‘Thus says the Lord God of Israel:

Behold, I will turn back the weapons of war that are in your hands, with which you fight against the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who besiege you around the walls, and I will gather them in the middle of this city.

‘And I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand, a strong arm, fury, indignation, and great anger.

‘And I will strike the inhabitants of this city; men and beasts shall die by a great pestilence.

‘And after this, says the Lord, I will give Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants, his people, and those who remain in this city from pestilence, sword, and famine, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of those who seek their lives.

‘And he shall strike them with the edge of the sword, and he shall not bend, nor spare, nor have mercy [Note: [Col. 0878D] The San-Germain Canon and other manuscript codices read “and he shall not be moved,” etc. [Col. 0879D] The Palatine and other manuscripts cited by Martianus likewise read “he shall not be moved,” instead of “he shall not bend.” The Hebrew has more, literally, “he shall not feel compassion for them.”].’

“And to this people you shall say:

‘Thus says the Lord:
