Behold, I set before you the way of life and the way of death. Whoever remains in this city shall die by sword, famine, and pestilence; but whoever goes out and defects to the Chaldeans who besiege you shall live, and his life shall be to him like spoil.

‘For I have set my face against this city for evil and not for good, says the Lord. It shall be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire.’

“And to the house of the king of Judah:

‘Hear the word of the Lord, house of David.

‘Thus says the Lord:

Execute judgment in the morning, and deliver the oppressed from the hand of the calumniator, lest my indignation go forth like fire and be kindled, with no one to extinguish it, because of the wickedness of your deeds.

‘Behold, I am against you, inhabitant of the solid and level valley, says the Lord, you who say, “Who will strike us? And who will enter our houses?”

‘And I will visit you according to the fruit of your deeds, says the Lord, and I will kindle a fire in its forest, and it shall devour everything around it.’”

### Chapter XXII

Thus says the Lord:

“Go down to the house of the king of Judah, speak this word there, and say:

‘Hear the word of the Lord, king of Judah, who sits upon the throne of David—you, your servants, and your people who enter through these gates.

‘Thus says the Lord:

Practice judgment and righteousness, and deliver the oppressed from the hand of the calumniator.

‘Do not wrongfully afflict or oppress the resident alien, the orphan, or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.

‘For if you truly do this word, kings sitting from the line of David upon his throne shall enter through the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their servants and their people.

‘But if you will not hear these words, I swear by myself, says the Lord, that this house shall become a desolation [Alt. “through myself”].

‘For thus says the Lord concerning the house of the king of Judah:

Gilead, you are to me the head of Lebanon; I will surely make you a desolation, cities uninhabited.

‘And I will consecrate against you a destroyer, a man and his weapons; and they shall cut down your chosen cedars and cast them into the fire.’

“And many nations shall pass through this city, and each one shall say to his neighbor:

‘Why has the Lord acted thus toward this great city?’

“And they shall answer:

‘Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord their God, and worshiped foreign gods and served them.’

“Do not weep for the dead, nor mourn over him with lamentation [Note: [Col. 0879D] In the Commentary the holy Interpreter reads the order differently: ‘Nor mourn over him. Lament with weeping for him who departs,’ closer to the Hebrew text [Hebrew term omitted in source].].

[Col. 0880A] “Weep for him who departs, for he shall not return again, nor see the land of his birth.

“For thus says the Lord concerning Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah [Alt. ‘the king’], who reigned in place of Josiah his father, who went out from this place:

‘He shall not return here again, but in the place to which I have transported him, there he shall die, and he shall not see this land again.’

“Woe to him who builds his house in injustice and his upper chambers without justice, who oppresses his neighbor without cause and does not pay him his wages.

“He says, ‘I will build myself a spacious house and broad upper chambers.’ He opens windows for himself and makes cedar ceilings, and paints with vermilion.

“Will you reign because you contend with cedar?”

“Did your father not eat and drink, and at that time act with judgment and righteousness when it was well with him?

“He judged the cause of the poor and needy for their benefit. Was this not because he knew me? says the Lord.”

But your eyes and your heart are set on greed, on shedding innocent blood, on calumny, and on pursuing evil deeds.

Therefore thus says the Lord concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:

“They shall not lament him:

‘Woe, brother, and woe, sister’” [Note: Other copies of the Canon and all our manuscript codices read: “Woe, brother, and woe, brothers.” But the Hieronymian Commentaries on this passage plainly refute this error of the copyists. “What we have set down from the Hebrew,” says the holy Doctor, “is: ‘They shall not lament him, Woe, brother, and woe, sister’; this is not found in the Septuagint.” MART.],

nor shall they cry aloud for him:

“Woe, Lord,

and woe, illustrious one.”

He shall be buried with the burial of a donkey,

rotting and cast outside the gates of Jerusalem.

Go up to Lebanon and cry out,

and raise your voice in Bashan,

and cry out to those passing by,

for all your lovers have been crushed.

I spoke to you in your prosperity,

and you said, “I will not listen.”

This has been your way from your youth,

because you did not listen to my voice.

The wind will pasture all your shepherds,

and your lovers will go into captivity.

Then you will be ashamed

and blush because of all your wickedness—

you who sit in Lebanon

and nest among the cedars.

How you groaned when pains came upon you,

like the pains of a woman in labor!

“As I live,” says the Lord,

“if Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah,

were a signet ring on my right hand,

I would tear him away from there.

And I will deliver you into the hand of those seeking your life,

and into the hand of those whose face you fear,

and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

and into the hand of the Chaldeans.

And I will send you and your mother who bore you

into a foreign land, in which you were not born,

and there you shall die.

And into the land to which they themselves lift up their soul,

desiring to return,

there they shall not return.

Is this man Jeconiah a clay vessel, crushed,

a vessel devoid of all pleasure?

Why have he and his offspring been cast away,

and thrown into a land they did not know?

Land, land, land,

hear the word of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord:

Write down this man as childless,

a man who will not prosper in his days.

For none of his offspring shall be a man

who sits upon the throne of David

and exercises authority any longer in Judah.”

### Chapter XXIII

Woe to the shepherds who destroy and tear apart the flock of my pasture, says the Lord.

Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel to the shepherds who pasture my people:

“You have scattered my flock,

you have driven them away,

and you have not visited them” [Al. omits “them”].

“Behold, I will visit upon you the wickedness of your endeavors,” says the Lord.

“And I myself will gather the remnant of my flock from all the lands to which I drove them,

and I will bring them back to their pasturelands,

and they shall increase and multiply.

And I will raise up shepherds over them,

and they shall pasture them.

They shall no longer fear or be terrified,

and none shall be missing from their number,” says the Lord.

“Behold, days are coming,” says the Lord,

“and I will raise up for David a righteous Branch.

He shall reign as king and act wisely,

and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land.

In those days Judah shall be saved,

and Israel shall dwell securely.

And this is the name by which they shall call him:

‘The Lord is our righteousness.’

Therefore, behold, days are coming,” says the Lord,

“when they shall no longer say:

‘As the Lord lives, who brought the children of Israel up from the land of Egypt.’

Rather:

‘As the Lord lives, who brought up and led back the offspring of the house of Israel from the land of the north,

and from all the lands to which I had driven them.’”

### To the Prophets

My heart is broken within me;

all my bones tremble.

I have become like a drunken man,

like a man overcome with wine,

because of the Lord

and because of the presence of his holy words.

For the land is full of adulterers;

because of the curse the land mourns;

the pastures of the wilderness have dried up.

Their course has become evil,

and their strength is unlike.

For both prophet and priest are polluted,

and in my house I found their wickedness [Al. “their evils”],

says the Lord.

Therefore their way shall be like slippery ground in darkness;

they shall be driven onward,

and they shall fall upon it.

For I will bring evils upon them,

the year of their visitation,

says the Lord.

And among the prophets of Samaria I saw folly:

they prophesied by Baal

and deceived my people Israel.

And among the prophets of Jerusalem I saw the likeness of adulterers [Al. “adultery”],

and a path of falsehood.

They strengthened the hands of evildoers,

so that no one would turn from his wickedness.

They have all become for me like Sodom,

and its inhabitants like Gomorrah [Note: Supply the little word “as” (*ut*), or “like” (*quasi*), as the holy Father himself has it in his Commentary. The Hebrew likewise has the corresponding expression.].

Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts concerning the prophets:

“Behold, I will feed them wormwood,

and give them gall to drink.

For from the prophets of Jerusalem

pollution has gone out over the whole land.”

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Do not listen to the words of the prophets

who prophesy to you and deceive you.

They speak the vision of their own heart,

not from the mouth of the Lord.

They say to those who blaspheme me,

‘The Lord has said: Peace shall be yours.’

And to everyone who walks in the perversity of his heart they say,

‘No evil shall come upon you.’

For who has stood in the council of the Lord,

and seen and heard his word?

Who has considered his word

and heard it?

Behold, the whirlwind of the Lord’s indignation shall go forth,

and a storm breaking forth shall come upon the head of the wicked.

The Lord’s anger shall not turn back

until he has acted,

and until he has fulfilled the thought of his heart.

In the last days

you shall understand his purpose.

I did not send the prophets,

yet they ran.

I did not speak to them,

yet they prophesied.

If they had stood in my council

and had made my words known to my people,

I would certainly have turned them from their evil way

and from their most wicked thoughts.

Am I a God nearby,” says the Lord,

“and not a God far away?

If a man hides himself in secret places,

shall I not see him?” says the Lord.

“Do I not fill heaven and earth?” says the Lord.

I have heard what the prophets said,

who prophesied falsely in my name and said,

‘I dreamed,

I dreamed.’

How long shall this be in the heart of the prophets

who prophesy falsehood

and prophesy the deceit of their own heart?

They intend to make my people forget my name

because of their dreams, which each one recounts to his neighbor,

just as their fathers forgot my name because of Baal.

Let the prophet who has a dream

recount the dream.

And let the one who has my word

speak my word truthfully.

What has straw in common with grain?” says the Lord.

“Are not my words like fire?” says the Lord,

“and like a hammer smashing a rock?

Therefore, behold, I am against the prophets,” says the Lord,

“who steal my words, each one from his neighbor.

Behold, I am against the prophets,” says the Lord,

“who use their tongues and say, ‘The Lord says.’

Behold, I am against the prophets of lying dreams,” says the Lord,

“who recounted it [Al. ‘recount it’]

and led my people astray with their lie [Al. ‘lead my people astray with their lies’] and their marvels,

although I did not send them

or command them.

They have been of no benefit at all to this people,” says the Lord.

And if this people, or a prophet, or a priest asks you, saying,

“What is the burden of the Lord [Al. ‘of God’]?”

you shall say to them:

“Why do you ask about a burden?” [Note: The commonly circulated books read: “You are the burden.” The Hebrew has literally: “What burden?”]

“For I will cast you away,” says the Lord.

And the prophet, and the priest, and the people who say,

“The burden of the Lord,”

I will visit that man and his house.

Thus shall each one say to his neighbor [Al. “friend”]

and to his brother:

“What has the Lord answered?”

and:

“What has the Lord spoken?”

And “the burden of the Lord” shall no longer be remembered,

for each one’s own word shall be his burden.

And you have perverted [Al. “pervert”] the words of the living God,

the Lord of hosts, our God.

Thus you shall say to the prophet:

“What has the Lord answered you?”

and:

“What has the Lord spoken?”

But if you say, “The burden of the Lord,”

therefore thus says the Lord:

“Because you have said this word, ‘The burden of the Lord,’

and I sent to you saying, ‘Do not say, “The burden of the Lord,”’

therefore, behold, I will take you up as a burden

and abandon you [Al. “cast you away”],

and the city that I gave you and your fathers,

away from my presence.

And I will give you over to everlasting disgrace

and eternal shame,

which shall never be erased from memory.”

### Chapter XXIV

The Lord showed me,

and behold, two baskets full of figs

set before the temple of the Lord,

after Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

had carried away Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah,

and his officials, and the craftsman, and the smith,

from Jerusalem and brought them to Babylon.

One basket had exceedingly good figs,

such as figs are at the beginning of the season.

And one basket had exceedingly bad figs,

which could not be eaten,

because they were bad.

And the Lord said to me:

“What do you see, Jeremiah?”

And I said:

“Figs—good figs, very good;

and bad figs, very bad,

which cannot be eaten,

because they are bad.”

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Thus says the Lord God of Israel:

“As these figs are good,

so I will regard the exiles of Judah

whom I sent away from this place into the land of the Chaldeans,

for good.

And I will set my eyes upon them for good [Al. “to do good”],

and I will bring them back to this land.

And I will build them up and not tear them down;

and I will plant them and not uproot them.

And I will give them a heart to know me,

that I am the Lord.

And they shall be my people,

and I shall be their God,

for they shall return to me with their whole heart.

And as for the very bad figs,

which cannot be eaten

because they are bad,

thus says the Lord:

so will I make Zedekiah king of Judah,

and his officials,

and the remnant of Jerusalem who remained in this city,

and those who dwell in the land of Egypt.

And I will make them a source of agitation and affliction

to all the kingdoms of the earth,

a disgrace, a parable, a proverb,

and a curse in all the places to which I drove them.

And I will send among them sword, famine, and pestilence,

until they are consumed from the land that I gave to them and to their fathers.”

### Chapter XXV

The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah

in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah—

that is, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—

which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah

and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying:

From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah,

to this day—

this is the twenty-third year—

the word of the Lord has come to me,

and I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking,

but you did not listen.

And the Lord sent to you all his servants, the prophets,

rising early and sending them,

but you did not listen,

nor did you incline your ears to hear.

He said [Al. “I said”]:

“Return, each one from his evil way

and from your most wicked thoughts,

and you shall dwell in the land that the Lord gave to you

and to your fathers,

from age to age and forever.

And do not go after foreign gods

to serve and worship them.

Do not provoke me to anger by the works of your hands,

and I will not afflict you.”

But you did not listen to me, says the Lord,

so as to provoke me to anger by the works of your hands,

for your own harm.

Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Because you did not listen to my words,

behold, I will send for and take all the families of the north,” says the Lord,

“and Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, my servant” [Note: The Canon of Saint-Germain, together with the Corbie manuscript no. 12, reads “to Nebuchadnezzar,” in accordance with the Hebrew, which has the preposition *el*, that is, “to.” We have by no means followed this reading, both because it is found written by a second hand in the manuscripts just mentioned, and especially because Saint Jerome does not recognize it in his Commentaries. MART.].

“And I will bring them against this land and against its inhabitants,

and against all the nations surrounding it.

And I will destroy them,

and make them an object of astonishment and hissing,

and everlasting desolations.

And I will destroy from them the voice of joy

and the voice of gladness,

the voice of bridegroom

and the voice of bride,

the sound of the mill,

and the light of the lamp.

And this whole land [Al. “their land”] shall become a desolation

and an object of astonishment.

And all these nations shall serve the king of Babylon

seventy years.

And when the seventy years have been completed,

I will visit upon the king of Babylon and upon that nation,” says the Lord,

their iniquity,

and upon the land of the Chaldeans,

and I will make it everlasting desolations.

And I will bring upon that land all my words

that I have spoken against it,

everything written in this book,

whatever Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.

For they served them,

although they were many nations and great kings.

And I will repay them according to their works

and according to the deeds of their hands.

For thus says the Lord of hosts [Al. omits “of hosts”], the God of Israel [Al. adds “to me”]:

“Take from my hand this cup of the wine of fury,

and you shall give all the nations to which I send you to drink from it.

And they shall drink,

and be shaken [Al. “drunk”],

and become insane because of the sword

that I will send among them.”

And I took the cup from the hand of the Lord

and gave all the nations to drink

to which the Lord sent me:

Jerusalem and the cities of Judah,

and its kings and its princes,

to make them a desolation,

an object of astonishment,

a hissing,

and a curse,

as it is this day;

Pharaoh, king of Egypt,

and his servants,

and his princes,

and all his people,

and all the peoples generally;

all the kings of the land of Ausitis,

and all the kings of the land of the Philistines,

and Ashkelon,

and Gaza,

and Ekron,

and the remnant of Ashdod;

Edom,

Moab,

and the children of Ammon;

all the kings of Tyre,

and all the kings of Sidon;

and the kings of the land of the islands beyond the sea [Note: The Hebrew text does not have “of the land”; nor does the holy Father insert this word in his Commentary.];

and Dedan,

and Tema [Note: The copies of the Canon and the manuscript codices of the Bibles have “Teman”; the Syriac interpreter also supports this reading, in which we read *Thaimno*. The Vulgate and the present-day Hebrew read “Thama.” MART. — Martianaeus falsely substituted “Teman” from several manuscripts, failing to notice that Tema is different from Teman. The former is a region of Palestine in the eastern part, that is, Arabia Deserta; the latter is the celebrated city of Idumea in Arabia Petraea toward the north, as is clear both from other testimonies of Scripture and from Jeremiah himself below, chapter XLIX, 7: “Concerning Edom. Thus says the Lord of hosts: Is there no longer wisdom in Teman?” Moreover, both the Hebrew text and nearly all the books here have “Tema,” or “Thema,” not “Teman.”],

and Buz,

and all who cut their hair at the temples;

all the kings of Arabia,

and all the kings of the west who dwell in the desert;

all the kings of Zimri,

all the kings of Elam,

all the kings of the Medes,

and all the kings of the north, near and far,

each one against his brother,

and all the kingdoms of the earth

that are upon its face.

And the king of Sheshach shall drink after them.

And you shall say to them:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

“Drink and become drunk;

vomit and fall,

and do not rise [Al. “and do not get up”]

from before the sword

that I will send among you [Al. “into you”].”

And when they refuse to take the cup from your hand

to drink,

you shall say to them:

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

“You shall certainly drink.

For behold, in the city over which my name has been invoked,

I am beginning to afflict,

and shall you be like the innocent and the exempt?

You shall not be exempt.

For I am summoning the sword

against all the inhabitants of the earth,”

says the Lord of hosts.

And you shall prophesy all these words against them,

and say to them:

“The Lord will roar from on high,

and from his holy dwelling he will utter his voice.

He will roar over his splendor.

A shout like that of those treading grapes

will be raised against all the inhabitants of the earth.

The sound has reached to the ends of the earth,

for the Lord has a judgment with the nations.

He himself is judged with all flesh.

I have handed the wicked over to the sword,”

says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Behold, affliction shall go forth from nation to nation,

and a great whirlwind shall go forth

from the farthest parts of the earth.

And on that day the slain of the Lord shall be

from one end of the earth to the other.

They shall not be mourned,

nor gathered,

nor buried;

they shall lie as dung upon the face of the earth.

Howl, shepherds, and cry out;

sprinkle yourselves with ashes, leaders of the flock.

For your days have been completed,

so that you may be slaughtered,

and your dispersions.

And you shall fall like precious vessels.

Flight shall perish from the shepherds,

and safety from the leaders of the flock.

The sound of the shepherds’ cry

and the howl of the leaders of the flock,

for the Lord has devastated their pasture.

The peaceful pastures have fallen silent

before the face of the Lord’s anger and fury.

He has abandoned his shelter like a lion,

for their land has become a desolation

before the face of the anger of the dove [Note: The causal particle “for” is absent from copies of the Canon of the Hebrew truth and from the manuscript codices of the sacred Bibles, nor does Saint Jerome acknowledge it while expounding this verse in his Commentaries—although it is read in the text of those Commentaries, in the Latin Vulgate, and in the Hebrew volumes. MART.],

and before the face of the anger of the Lord’s fury.”

### Chapter XXVI

At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah,

king of Judah,

this word came from the Lord, saying:

Thus says the Lord:

“Stand in the court of the house of the Lord,

and speak to all the cities of Judah,

from which they come to worship in the house of the Lord,

all the words that I have commanded you to speak to them.

Do not withdraw a word,

in case they listen

and each one turns from his evil way,

and I relent of the evil that I am considering doing to them

because of the wickedness of their endeavors.”

And you shall say to them:

Thus says the Lord:

“If you will not listen to me,

to walk in my law that I gave you,

to hear the words of my servants the prophets,

whom I sent to you, rising early and sending them,

but you did not listen,

I will make this house like Shiloh,

and I will give this city as a curse to all the nations of the earth.”

And the priests, and the prophets, and all the people

heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the Lord.

And when Jeremiah had finished speaking all that the Lord had commanded him to speak to all the people,

the priests, and the prophets, and all the people seized him, saying:

“He shall surely die” [Al. “Let him die”].

“Why did he prophesy in the name of the Lord, saying:

‘This house shall be like Shiloh,

and this city shall be desolated,

because there is no inhabitant’?”

And all the people gathered against Jeremiah

in the house of the Lord.

And the officials of Judah heard these words,

and they went up from the king’s house to the house of the Lord,

and sat at the entrance of the new gate of the house [Al. omits “of the house”] of the Lord.

And the priests and the prophets spoke to the officials

and to all the people, saying:

“This man deserves the sentence of death,

because he has prophesied against this city,

as you have heard with your ears.”

And Jeremiah said to all the officials

and to all the people, saying:

“The Lord sent me to prophesy against this house

and against this city

all the words that you have heard.

Now therefore make your ways and your deeds good,

and listen to the voice of the Lord your God.

Then the Lord will relent of the evil

that he has spoken against you.

But as for me, behold, I am in your hands.

Do with me what is good and right in your eyes.

Nevertheless, know and understand

that if you kill me,

you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves,

and upon this city,

and upon its inhabitants.

For in truth the Lord sent me to you

to speak all these words in your ears.”

And the officials and all the people said

to the priests and the prophets:

“This man does not deserve the sentence of death,

for he has spoken to us

in the name of the Lord our God.”

Then men from the elders of the land rose

and said to the whole assembly of the people:

Micah of Moresheth was a prophet

in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah,

and he said to all the people of Judah:

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Zion shall be plowed like a field,

and Jerusalem shall become a heap of stones,

and the mountain of the house

a wooded height.”

Did Hezekiah, king of Judah,

and all Judah,

condemn him to death?

Did they not fear the Lord

and entreat the face of the Lord?

And did the Lord not relent of the evil

that he had spoken against them?

But we are committing great evil

against our own lives.

There was also a man prophesying in the name of the Lord,

Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim.

He prophesied against this city

and against this land,

in accordance with all the words of Jeremiah.

And King Jehoiakim, and all the mighty men,

and his officials heard these words,

and the king sought to kill him.

And Uriah heard,

and was afraid,

and fled and entered Egypt.

And King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt,

Elnathan son of Achbor,

and men with him,

to Egypt.

And they brought Uriah out of Egypt

and brought him to King Jehoiakim.

And he struck him with the sword

and cast his corpse into the tombs of the common people.

Nevertheless [Al. “But”], the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah,

so that he was not handed over to the hands of the people

and they did not kill him.

### Chapter XXVII

At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah,

king of Judah,

this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:

Thus says the Lord to me:

“Make yourself bonds and chains,

and put them on your neck.

And send them to the king of Edom,

to the king of Moab,

to the king of the children of Ammon,

to the king of Tyre,

and to the king of Sidon,

by the hand of the messengers

who have come to Jerusalem

to Zedekiah, king of Judah.

And command them to speak to their lords:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Thus you shall say to your lords:

I made the earth,

and human beings,

and the animals that are upon the face of the earth,

by my great strength

and my outstretched arm.

And I gave it to the one who was pleasing in my eyes.

And now, therefore, I have given all these lands

into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

my servant.

Moreover, I have given him the beasts of the field

to serve him.

And all nations shall serve him,

and his son,

and his grandson,

until the time of his land and of him comes.

And many nations and great kings shall serve him.

But the nation and kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

and whoever will not bend his neck beneath the yoke of the king of Babylon,

I will visit that nation with sword, famine, and pestilence,” says the Lord,

“until I consume them by his hand.

Therefore do not listen to your prophets,

your diviners,

your dreamers,

your augurs,

or your sorcerers,

who say to you,

‘You shall not serve the king of Babylon.’

For they prophesy falsehood to you,

to remove you far from your land,

and to drive you out,

and for you to perish.

But the nation that subjects its neck to the yoke of the king of Babylon

and serves him,

I will leave in its land,” says the Lord,

“and it shall till it

and dwell in it.”

And I spoke to Zedekiah, king of Judah,

according to all these words, saying:

“Submit your necks to the yoke of the king of Babylon,

and serve him and his people,

and you shall live.

Why should you die—you and your people—

by sword, famine, and pestilence,

as the Lord has spoken concerning the nation

that will not serve the king of Babylon?

Do not listen to the words of the prophets

who say to you,

‘You shall not serve the king of Babylon’ [Al. “Do not serve the king of Babylon”],

for they speak falsehood to you.

For I did not send them,” says the Lord,

“and they prophesy falsely in my name,

so that they may drive you out

and you may perish—

both you and the prophets who prophesy to you.”

And I spoke to the priests

and to this people, saying:

Thus says the Lord:

“Do not listen to the words of your prophets

who prophesy to you, saying:

‘Behold, the vessels of the Lord will quickly be brought back from Babylon.’

For they prophesy falsehood to you.

Therefore do not listen to them,

but serve the king of Babylon,

so that you may live.

Why should this city be given over to desolation?

And if they are prophets,

and the word of the Lord is with them,

let them meet with the Lord of hosts,

so that the vessels that had been left

in the house of the Lord,

and in the house of the king of Judah,

and in Jerusalem,

may not go to Babylon.

For thus says the Lord of hosts concerning the pillars,

and the sea,

and the bases,

and the remaining vessels

that were left in this city,

which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

did not take

when he carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah,

from Jerusalem to Babylon,

together with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel,

concerning the vessels left

in the house of the Lord,

and in the house of the king of Judah,

and in Jerusalem:

They shall be carried to Babylon,

and there they shall remain

until the day of their visitation,” says the Lord.

“And I will bring them back

and restore them to this place.”

### Chapter XXVIII

And it came to pass in that year,

at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah,

in the fourth year,

in the fifth month,

that the prophet Hananiah son of Azur from Gibeon

spoke to me in the house of the Lord,

in the presence of the priests

and all the people, saying:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

“I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.

Within two years of days

I will bring back to this place all the vessels

of the house [Al. omits “of the house”] of the Lord

that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

took [Al. “carried away”] from this place

and brought to Babylon.

And Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah,

and all the exiles of Judah

who entered Babylon,

I will bring back to this place,” says the Lord,

“for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.”

And the prophet Jeremiah spoke to the prophet Hananiah

in the presence of the priests

and in the presence of all the people

who were standing in the house of the Lord.

And the prophet Jeremiah said:

“Amen!

May the Lord do so.

May the Lord raise up your words

that you have prophesied,

so that the vessels may be brought back

to the house of the Lord,

and all the exiles from Babylon [Al. “of Babylon”]

to this place.

Nevertheless, hear this word

that I speak in your ears

and in the ears of all the people:

The prophets who were before me

and before you from the beginning,

and who prophesied over many lands

and great kingdoms,

spoke of war,

affliction,

and famine.

The prophet who prophesied peace—

when his word comes,

the prophet will be known

as one whom the Lord truly sent.”

And the prophet Hananiah took the chain

from the neck of the prophet Jeremiah

and broke it.

And Hananiah spoke in the presence of all the people, saying:

Thus says the Lord:

“So I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

after two years of days,

from the neck of all the nations.”

And the prophet Jeremiah went his way [Al. omits “the prophet”].

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah

after the prophet Hananiah had broken the chain

from the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, saying:

“Go and say to Hananiah:

Thus says the Lord:

You have broken wooden chains,

but you shall make iron chains in their place [Al. “bars”].

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

I have placed an iron yoke upon the neck

of all these nations,

so that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

and they shall serve him.

Moreover, I have given him the beasts of the earth.”

And the prophet Jeremiah said to the prophet Hananiah:

“Hear, Hananiah:

The Lord did not send you,

and you have made this people trust in a lie.

Therefore thus says the Lord:

Behold, I will send you away from the face of the earth.

This year you shall die,

for you have spoken against the Lord.”

And the prophet Hananiah died in that year,

in the seventh month.

### Chapter XXIX

And these are the words of the book

that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem

to the remnant of the elders of the exile,

and to the priests,

and to the prophets,

and to all the people

whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away

from Jerusalem to Babylon:

after Jeconiah the king had gone out,

and the lady,

and the eunuchs,

and the officials of Judah and Jerusalem,

and the craftsman and the smith from Jerusalem [Al. “the craftsmen from Jerusalem”];

by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan

and Gemariah son of Hilkiah,

whom Zedekiah, king of Judah,

sent to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

to Babylon, saying:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel,

to all the exiles

whom I carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon:

“Build houses and dwell in them.

Plant gardens

and eat their fruit.

Take wives

and beget sons and daughters.

Give wives to your sons,

and give your daughters to husbands,

so that they may bear sons and daughters.

Increase there [Al. omits “there”],

and do not become few in number.

And seek the peace of the city

to which I caused you to migrate [Al. “carried you away”],

and pray to the Lord for it,

for in its peace there shall be peace for you.”

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

“Do not let your prophets

who are among you,

or your diviners,

deceive you.

And do not pay attention to your dreams

that you dream.

For they prophesy falsely to you in my name,

and I did not send them,” says the Lord.

For thus says the Lord:

“When the seventy years in Babylon begin to be completed,

I will visit you [Note: Martianaeus incorrectly reads: “I will raise up over my word,” etc., omitting the pronoun “you,” which we have supplied both from other books and on the authority of the Hebrew text.],

and I will raise up over you my good word

to bring you back to this place.

For I know the thoughts

that I think concerning you,” says the Lord—

“thoughts of peace and not of affliction,

to give you an end and patience.

And you will call upon me

and go,

and you will pray to me,

and I will hear you.

You will seek me

and find me,

when you seek me with your whole heart.

And I will be found by you,” says the Lord,

“and I will restore your captivity,

and gather you from all the nations

and from all the places to which I drove you,” says the Lord.

“And I will bring you back from the place

to which I caused you to migrate,

because you said,

‘The Lord has raised up prophets for us in Babylon.’

For thus says the Lord concerning the king

who sits upon the throne of David,

and concerning all the people

who dwell in this city,

and concerning your brothers

who did not go out with you into exile:

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Behold, I will send among them sword,

famine,

and pestilence,

and I will make them like bad figs

that cannot be eaten,

because they are exceedingly bad.

And I will pursue them

with sword,

famine,

and pestilence.

And I will make them a source of agitation

to all the kingdoms of the earth,

a curse,

an object of astonishment,

a hissing,

and a disgrace to all the nations

to which I drove them [Al. “shall drive them”],

because they did not listen to my words,” says the Lord,

which I sent to them through my servants the prophets,

rising early and sending them.

“And you did not listen,” says the Lord.

Therefore hear the word of the Lord,

all you exiles

whom I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel,

concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah

and concerning Zedekiah son of Maaseiah,

who prophesy falsely to you in my name:

“Behold, I will deliver them into the hand

of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

and he shall strike them before your eyes.

And a curse shall be taken from them

for all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylon,

saying:

‘May the Lord make you like Zedekiah

and like Ahab,

whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire,

because they committed folly in Israel,

committed adultery with the wives of their friends,

and spoke a word falsely in my name,

which I did not command them.

I am judge and witness,’ says the Lord.”

And to Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall say:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

“Because you sent letters in your own name

to all the people who are in Jerusalem,

and to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest,

and to all the priests, saying:

‘The Lord has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest,

so that you may be overseer in the house of the Lord

over every madman and prophet,

to put him in the stocks and in prison.

And now, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah the Anathothite,

who prophesies to you?

For he sent to us in Babylon, saying:

“It will be a long time.

Build houses and dwell in them.

Plant gardens

and eat their fruit.”’

So the priest Zephaniah read this letter

in the ears of the prophet Jeremiah.

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:

“Send to all the exiles, saying:

Thus says the Lord concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite:

Because Shemaiah prophesied to you,

although I did not send him,

and made you trust in a lie,

therefore thus says the Lord:

Behold, I will visit upon Shemaiah the Nehelamite

and upon his offspring.

He shall have no man sitting

in the midst of this people,

and he shall not see the good

that I will do for my people,” says the Lord,
because he has spoken treachery against the Lord.

**[Chapter XXX]** This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:

Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel:

“Write for yourself in a book all the words that I have spoken to you.

For behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I shall restore the fortunes of my people [Alternative: in the land] Israel and Judah, says the Lord;

and I shall bring them back to the land that I gave to their fathers,

and they shall possess it.”

[Col. 0892B] These are the words that the Lord spoke concerning Israel and Judah:

For thus says the Lord:

“We have heard a voice of terror,

fear, and there is no peace.

Ask and see whether a male gives birth. Why, then, have I seen every man’s hand upon his loins, like a woman in labor [Alternative: giving birth],

and why have all faces turned yellow?

Alas! For that day is great,

and there is none like it:

it is a time of distress for Jacob,

but he shall be saved from it.

And it shall come to pass on that day, says the Lord of hosts,

that I shall break his yoke from your neck,

and I shall burst your bonds,

and foreigners shall no longer rule over him.

But they shall serve the Lord their God,

and David their king, whom I shall raise up for them.

[Col. 0892C] Therefore do not fear, my servant Jacob, says the Lord,

and do not be dismayed, Israel;

for behold, I shall save you from a distant land,

and your offspring from the land of their captivity.

Jacob shall return and be at rest,

and shall abound in all good things,

and there shall be none whom he fears.

For I am with you, says the Lord, to save you.

For I shall bring an end to all the nations among which I scattered you;

but I shall not bring an end to you.

Rather, I shall chastise you with judgment,

so that you may not appear innocent in your own eyes.

For thus says the Lord:

Your fracture is incurable,

your wound is most grievous.

There is no one to judge your case, for binding it;

there is no benefit from remedies for you.

All your lovers have forgotten you,

and they will not seek you.

[Col. 0892D] For I have struck you with the wound of an enemy,

with cruel chastisement;

because of the multitude of your iniquity,

your sins have become harsh.

Why do you cry out over your fracture?

Your pain is incurable.

Because of the multitude of your iniquity

and the harshness of your sins,

I have done these things to you.

Therefore all who devour you shall be devoured,

and all your enemies shall be led into captivity.

Those who lay you waste shall be laid waste,

and I shall give all your plunderers as plunder.

For I shall close your wound with a scar,

and I shall heal you of your injuries, says the Lord.

For they have called you “the outcast,” Zion:

“She is the one for whom no one seeks.”

Thus says the Lord:

“Behold, I shall restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob,

[Col. 0893A] and I shall have mercy on his dwellings [Alternative: their dwellings];

the city shall be rebuilt upon its height,

and the temple shall be founded according to its order.

Praise shall go forth from them,

and the voice of those who rejoice.

I shall multiply them, and they shall not be diminished;

I shall glorify them, and they shall not be weakened.

Their children shall be as at the beginning,

and their assembly shall endure before me.

I shall punish all who afflict him.

Their leader shall come from among them,

and their ruler shall be brought forth from their midst.

I shall draw him near, and he shall approach me.

For who is this who has set his heart to draw near to me? says the Lord.

And you shall be my people,

and I shall be your God.

Behold, the storm of the Lord,

an anger going forth,

a sweeping tempest;

it shall rest upon the head of the wicked.

The Lord shall not turn back the wrath of his indignation

until he has acted and fulfilled the intention of his heart.

[Col. 0893B] In the latter days you shall understand these things.

**[Chapter XXXI]** At that time, says the Lord,

I shall be God to all the thoughts of Israel,

and they shall be my people.

Thus says the Lord:

The people that survived the sword found grace in the wilderness;

Israel shall go to its rest.

The Lord appeared to me from afar.

And I have loved you with everlasting love;

therefore I have drawn you, taking pity on you.

Again I shall build you,

and you shall be built, virgin Israel.

Again you shall adorn yourself with your timbrels,

and you shall go forth in the chorus of those who dance.

Again you shall plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria.

Those who plant shall plant [Note: See the Commentaries, and what we note concerning this passage.],

and until the time comes they shall not gather the grapes.

For there shall be a day when the watchmen cry out on Mount

[Col. 0893C] Ephraim:

“Rise, and let us go up to Zion,

to the Lord our God.”

For thus says the Lord:

“Rejoice with gladness, Jacob,

and neigh against the head of the nations.

Proclaim, sing, and say:

‘Save, O Lord, your people,

the remnant of Israel.’

Behold, I shall bring them from the land of the north,

and I shall gather them from the ends of the earth.

Among them shall be the blind and the lame,

the pregnant woman and the woman in labor together—

a great assembly [Alternative: a great church] of those returning here.

They shall come with weeping,

and with prayers I shall lead them [Alternative: in mercy I shall bring them back].

I shall bring them by streams of water,

on a straight road in which they shall not stumble.

For I have become a father to Israel,

[Col. 0893D] and Ephraim is my firstborn.

Hear the word of the Lord, O nations,

and proclaim it in the distant islands, and say:

‘He who scattered Israel will gather him,

and he will guard him as a shepherd guards his flock.’

For the Lord has redeemed Jacob [Alternative: redeemed],

and he has delivered him [Alternative: delivered him] from the hand of one stronger than he.

They shall come and praise on Mount Zion,

and they shall stream toward the good things of the Lord—

toward grain, wine, and oil,

and the offspring of sheep and cattle.

Their soul shall be like a watered garden,

and they shall hunger no longer.

Then the virgin shall rejoice in the dance,

young men and old men together.

I shall turn their mourning into joy,

I shall console them,

and I shall gladden them after their sorrow.

I shall intoxicate the soul of the priests with abundance,

and my people shall be filled with my goods, says the Lord.”

Thus says the Lord:

“A voice was heard on the heights:

lamentation,

weeping and mourning—

Rachel weeping for her children

and refusing [Alternative: she refused] to be comforted over them [Alternative: over her children],

because they are no more.”

Thus says the Lord:

“Let your voice cease from weeping

and your eyes from tears,

for there is a reward for your work, says the Lord.

They shall return from the land of the enemy,

and there is [Alternative: there shall be] hope for your latter days, says the Lord,

and the children shall return to their own borders.”

Hearing, I heard Ephraim in exile:

“You chastised me,

and I was instructed,

like an untamed young bull.

Convert me, and I shall be converted,

for you are the Lord my God.

For after you converted me, I repented,

and after you showed me [Alternative: I came to know],

I struck my thigh.

I was ashamed and humiliated,

because I bore the disgrace of my youth.

Is Ephraim a son precious to me?

Is he a beloved child?

For from the time I spoke of him,

I shall still remember him [Alternative: remembering him].

Therefore my inward parts are troubled over him;

I shall surely have compassion on him, says the Lord.”

Set up a watchtower for yourself;

place bitter things before yourself.

Direct your heart onto the straight road

on which you walked.

Return, virgin Israel;

return to these cities of yours.

[Col. 0894C] How long will you dissolve in pleasures,

wandering daughter?

For the Lord has created a new thing upon the earth:

a woman shall encompass a man.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

“Again this word shall be spoken in the land of Judah

and in its cities,

when I restore their fortunes:

‘May the Lord bless you,

beauty of righteousness,

holy mountain.’

And Judah and all its cities shall dwell in it together,

farmers and those driving flocks.

For I have intoxicated the weary soul,

and I have filled every hungry soul.

Therefore I awoke as if from sleep [Alternative: I awakened],

and I saw,

and my sleep was sweet to me.

Behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

when I shall sow the house of Israel

and the house of Judah with the seed of a man

[Col. 0894D] and with the seed of cattle.

And just as I watched over them

to uproot, demolish, destroy, annihilate, and afflict,

so I shall watch over them

to build and plant, says the Lord.

In those days they shall no longer say:

‘The fathers ate a sour grape,

and the children’s teeth were set on edge’ [Alternative: shall be set on edge].

Rather, each person shall die for his own iniquity.

Every person who eats the sour grape—

his own teeth shall be set on edge.

Behold, days shall come [Alternative: are coming], says the Lord,

when I shall make a new covenant with the house of Israel

and with the house of Judah.

[Col. 0895A] It shall not be like the covenant that I made with your fathers, [Note: This is how the copies of the Canon and all the manuscript codices of the sacred Bible that we examined read. The Commentaries of St. Jerome, both printed and manuscript, likewise consistently retain the second-person pronoun. Modern Hebrew, however, has [Hebrew word], *avetham*, that is, “their fathers”; but in the course of time the letter Kaph appears to have been omitted from the second-person plural suffix, since Jerome found in his copy [Hebrew word], *avitechem*, that is, “your fathers.” MART.]

on the day when I took them by the hand

to lead them out of the land of Egypt—

the covenant that they made void,

while I ruled over them, says the Lord.

But this shall be the covenant that I shall make with the house of Israel

after those days, says the Lord:

I shall place my law within them,

and I shall write it upon their heart.

I shall be their God,

and they shall be my people.

They shall no longer teach one another,

each person his neighbor,

and each person his brother, saying:

‘Know the Lord.’

For all shall know me,

from the least of them to the greatest, says the Lord,

because I shall be merciful toward their iniquity,

and I shall remember their sin no more.

[Col. 0895B] Thus says the Lord,

who gives the sun for light by day,

the order of the moon and stars for light by night,

who stirs up the sea,

and its waves roar.

The Lord of hosts is his name.

If these ordinances should fail before me, says the Lord,

then the offspring of Israel also shall fail,

so that it shall no longer be a nation before me forever.

Thus says the Lord:

If the heavens above can be measured,

and the foundations of the earth below searched out,

then I too shall reject all the offspring of Israel

because of everything they have done, says the Lord.

Behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

when the city shall be built for the Lord,

from the tower of Hananel

to the Corner Gate.

The measuring line shall go out farther before it,

over the hill of Gareb;

it shall go around Goah,

and the entire Valley of the Corpses [Alternative: ruins]

and of the ashes,

[Col. 0895C] and the whole region of death,

as far as the torrent of Kidron

and as far as the corner of the eastern Horse Gate—

the holy place of the Lord.

It shall not be uprooted

and shall not be destroyed again forever.”

**[Chapter XXXII]** The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord

in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah—

that is, the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar—

when the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem,

and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the court of the prison

that was in the house of the king of Judah.

For Zedekiah king of Judah had confined him, saying:

“Why do you prophesy, saying:

‘Thus says the Lord:

Behold, I shall give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon,

and he shall capture it?

And Zedekiah king of Judah shall not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans,

[Col. 0895D] but shall be handed over into the hand of the king of Babylon.

His mouth shall speak with his mouth,

and his eyes shall see his eyes.

He shall lead Zedekiah to Babylon,

and there he shall remain until I visit him, says the Lord.

But if you fight against the Chaldeans,

you shall have no success.’”

And Jeremiah said:

The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Behold, Hanamel son of Shallum, your cousin, shall come [Alternative: has come] to you, saying:

[Col. 0896A] ‘Buy for yourself my field that is in Anathoth,

for you have the right of redemption by kinship to buy it [Alternative: the purchase].’”

And Hanamel, the son of my uncle, came to me,

according to the word of the Lord,

at the entrance of the prison,

and said to me:

“Take possession of my field that is in Anathoth,

in the land of Benjamin,

for the inheritance belongs to you,

and you are the near relative entitled to possess it.”

I understood that this was the word of the Lord.

And I bought the field from Hanamel,

the son of my uncle,

which is in Anathoth.

I weighed out for him seven staters of silver

and ten pieces of silver.

I wrote it in a book,

sealed it,

called in witnesses,

and weighed out the silver on the scales.

I took the sealed deed of purchase,

the stipulations and valid agreements [Note: The Canon of Saint-Germain reads at this point: “sealed with a valid stipulation, and sealed on the outside.”],

and the seals on the outside.

[Col. 0896B] And I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah,

in the presence of Hanamel my cousin

and in the presence of the witnesses who were recorded in the deed of purchase,

and in the presence of all the Jews who were sitting in the court of the prison.

And I charged Baruch in their presence, saying:

“Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Take these documents,

this deed of purchase, the sealed one,

and this deed, which is open,

and place them in an earthen vessel,

so that they may endure for many days.

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Houses, fields, and vineyards shall again be possessed in this land.”

And I prayed to the Lord

after I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, saying:

“Ah, ah, ah, Lord God!

[Col. 0896C] Behold, you made heaven and earth

by your great power

and by your outstretched arm.

No word is difficult for you.

You show mercy to thousands,

and repay the iniquity of the fathers

into the bosom of their children after them.

Most mighty,

great,

powerful—

the Lord of hosts is your name.

Great in counsel

and incomprehensible in thought,

whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the children of Adam,

to repay each person according to his ways

and according to the fruit of his devices [Alternative: their devices].

You who performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt

until this day,

and in Israel and among humankind,

and made yourself a name,

as it is today.

You led your people Israel out of the land of Egypt

with signs and wonders,

with a mighty hand,

an outstretched arm,

[Col. 0896D] and great terror.

You gave them this land,

which you swore to their fathers to give them—

a land flowing with milk and honey.

They entered and possessed it,

but they did not obey your voice,

and they did not walk in your law.

They did not do any of the things that you commanded them to do,

and all these evils befell them.

Behold, siegeworks have been built against the city

to capture it,

and the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans,

who are fighting against it because of the sword,

famine,

and pestilence.

Whatever you have spoken has happened,

as you yourself see.

Yet you say to me, Lord God:

‘Buy the field with silver,

and call in witnesses’—

while the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans?”

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:

“Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh.

Can any word be difficult for me?

Therefore thus says the Lord:

Behold, I shall give this city into the hands of the Chaldeans

[Col. 0897B] and into the hands of the king of Babylon,

and he shall capture it.

And the Chaldeans shall come [Note: Saint Jerome himself is better heard discussing this reading in his Commentary: “Aquila translated what is written as ‘they shall come’ more accurately as εἰσελεύσονται, that is, ‘they shall enter the city.’ For they were not absent, so that they might come, since they had surrounded Jerusalem: ‘At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem.’ And afterward: ‘Behold, siegeworks have been built against the city, to capture it, and the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans.’ How, then, shall those who were present come? But those who were besieging the city, he says, shall enter it, capture it, set it on fire, and burn it to the ground. For the Hebrew word, because of its ambiguity, means both ‘they shall come’ and ‘they shall enter.’”] fighting against this city,

and they shall burn it with fire

and consume it.

They shall burn the houses on whose roofs they sacrificed to Baal

and poured libations to foreign gods

to provoke me.

For the children of Israel and the children of Judah

have continually done evil in my sight

from their youth.

The children of Israel

have provoked me continually until this day

by the work of their hands, says the Lord.

For this city has been an object of my fury and indignation,

from the day they built it until this day,

when it shall be removed [Alternative: is removed] from my sight.

Because of the wickedness of the children of Israel

and the children of Judah,

which they committed to provoke me—

they and their kings,

their princes,

their priests,

their prophets,

the men of Judah,

and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They turned their backs to me

and not their faces.

Though I taught them at dawn

and instructed them,

they would not listen

or accept discipline.

They placed their idols in the house

on which my name was invoked,

to defile it.

They built high places for Baal,

which are in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom,

to initiate their sons and daughters for Molech—

something that I did not command them,

nor did it enter my heart that they should do this abomination

and lead Judah into sin.

And now, because of these things,

thus says the Lord God of Israel concerning this city,

of which you say that it shall be handed over [Alternative: may be handed over]

[Col. 0897D] into the hand of the king of Babylon,

by the sword,

famine,

and pestilence:

Behold, I shall gather them from all the lands

to which I drove them

in my fury,

my anger,

and great indignation.

I shall bring them back to this place,

and I shall make them dwell securely.

They shall be my people,

and I shall be their God.

[Col. 0898A] I shall give them one heart

and one way,

so that they may fear me all their days,

for their good

and for the good of their children after them.

I shall make an everlasting covenant with them,

and I shall not cease doing good to them.

I shall place my fear in their heart,

so that they may not depart from me.

I shall rejoice over them

when I do good to them,

and I shall plant them in this land in truth,

with all my heart

and with all my soul.

For thus says the Lord:

Just as I brought upon this people all this great evil,

so I shall bring upon them all the good

that I am promising them.

Fields shall again be bought in this land,

of which you say that it is desolate,

because neither human nor animal remains,

and it has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans.

Fields shall be bought with money,

and deeds shall be written in a book,

and the seal shall be impressed [Alternative: the seal],

and a witness shall be called in,

in the land of Benjamin,

in the environs of Jerusalem,

in the cities of Judah,

in the mountain cities,

in the lowland cities,

and in the cities that are toward the south.

For I shall restore their fortunes, says the Lord.”

**[Chapter XXXIII]** And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah a second time,

while he was still confined in the court of the prison,

saying:

Thus says the Lord,

who will make it

and form it

and prepare it—

the Lord is his name.

“Call to me, and I shall answer you,

and I shall announce to you great and secure things

that you do not know.

For thus says the Lord God of Israel concerning the houses of this city

[Col. 0898C] and concerning the houses of the king of Judah,

which have been destroyed,

and concerning the fortifications

and the sword of those who are coming to fight against the Chaldeans

and to fill them with the corpses of human beings—

those whom I struck in my fury and indignation,

hiding my face from this city

because of all their wickedness:

Behold, I shall close their wound with a scar,

bring them health,

and heal them.

I shall reveal to them a prayer for peace and truth.

I shall restore the fortunes of Judah

and the fortunes of Jerusalem,

and I shall build them as at the beginning.

I shall cleanse them from all their iniquity

in which they sinned against me,

and I shall be merciful toward all their iniquities

in which they transgressed against me

and despised me.

It shall be for me a name,

a joy,

a praise,

and an exultation among all the nations of the earth

[Col. 0898D] that hear all the good things

that I shall do for them.

They shall fear and be troubled

because of all the good things

and all the peace that I shall make for them.”

Thus says the Lord:

“Again there shall be heard in this place,

which you say is desolate

because there is neither human being nor animal,

[Col. 0899A] in the cities of Judah

and outside Jerusalem,

which are desolate without human being,

without inhabitant,

and without livestock,

the voice of joy

and the voice of gladness,

the voice of the bridegroom

and the voice of the bride,

the voice of those saying:

‘Give thanks to the Lord of hosts,

for the Lord is good,

for his mercy is everlasting’;

and the voice of those bringing offerings of vows into the house of the Lord.

For I shall restore the fortunes of the land

as at the beginning, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

Again there shall be in this desolate place,

without human being

and without animal,

and in all its cities,

a dwelling place of shepherds lying down with their flocks.

In the mountain cities,

in the lowland cities,

and in the cities toward the south,

[Col. 0899B] in the land of Benjamin,

in the environs of Jerusalem,

and in the cities of Judah,

flocks shall again pass under the hand of the one who counts them,

says the Lord.

Behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

when I shall raise up the good word

that I spoke concerning the house of Israel

and concerning the house of Judah.

In those days and at that time

I shall cause a righteous branch to sprout for David,

and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land.

In those days Judah shall be saved,

and Jerusalem shall dwell securely.

And this is what shall call her:

The Lord is our righteous one [Note: Thus read both Canons of the Hebrew truth—the Garcassonian, and our Saint-Germain Canon, which retain the genuine and original reading of Jerome. For in Hebrew it is written, וְזֶה אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָא לַיהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ, *ve-zeh asher yiqra la-YHWH tsidqenu*, or, as it is read today, וְזֶה אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָא לָהּ יְהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ, *ve-zeh asher yiqra lah YHWH tsidqenu*, which some interpret: “And this is what shall call her, ‘The Lord is our righteousness.’” The Chaldean and Syriac have: “And this is the name by which they shall call her.” Our Vulgate agrees with this reading. Refer here to what is written above in chapter XXIV, 6, although there is some difference between the two passages of the prophet, as will be clear at once to the reader. MART.].

For thus says the Lord:

A man shall not be cut off from David

who sits upon the throne of the house of Israel.

And from the priests and Levites

a man shall not be cut off from before me

who offers burnt offerings,

burns sacrifices,

and slaughters victims

all the days.”

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:

Thus says the Lord:

“If my covenant with day and my covenant with night

can be annulled,

so that day and night do not occur at their appointed time,

then my covenant with David my servant can also be annulled,

so that he has no son who reigns upon his throne,

and likewise with the Levites and priests who minister to me.

Just as the stars of heaven cannot be numbered

and the sand of the sea cannot be measured,

so I shall multiply the offspring of David my servant

and the Levites who minister to me.”

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:

“Have you not seen what this people has spoken, saying:

‘The two families that the Lord had chosen have been rejected,

and they have despised my people,

because it is no longer a nation before them’?”

Thus says the Lord:

“If I have not established my covenant with day and night,

and the ordinances of heaven and earth,

then indeed I shall also reject the offspring of Jacob

and David my servant,

so that I will not take from his offspring rulers over the offspring of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

For I shall restore their fortunes,

and I shall have mercy on them.”

**[Chapter XXXIV]** The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord

when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon,

and all his army,

and all the kingdoms of the earth that were under the power of his hand,

and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem

and against all its cities,

saying:

Thus says the Lord God of Israel:

“Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah,

and say to him:

Thus says the Lord:

Behold, I shall give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon,

and he shall burn it with fire.

You shall not escape from his hand,

[Col. 0900B] but you shall be captured by seizure

and handed over into his hand.

Your eyes shall see the eyes of the king of Babylon,

and his mouth shall speak with your mouth,

and you shall enter Babylon.

Nevertheless, hear the word of the Lord,

Zedekiah king of Judah.

Thus says the Lord concerning you:

You shall not die by the sword,

but you shall die in peace.

And just as they burned your fathers,

the former kings who were before you,

so they shall burn you.

And ‘Alas, lord!’ they shall mourn for you,

for I have spoken the word, says the Lord.”

And Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words

to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem.

The army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem

and against all the cities of Judah that remained—

against Lachish and Azekah.

For these were the fortified cities

that remained among the cities of Judah.

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord

after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem,

proclaiming that each person should release his male slave

and each person his female slave,

a Hebrew man and a Hebrew woman,

free,

and that they should by no means rule over them—

that is, over a Judean and his brother.

All the princes and all the people who had entered into the covenant

heard that each person should release his male slave

and each person his female slave free,

and no longer rule over them [Alternative: the word “over” is absent].

They heard and released them.

But afterward they turned back

and took back their male slaves

and their female slaves,

whom they had released as free,

[Col. 0900D] and subjugated them as male and female servants.

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:

Thus says the Lord God of Israel:

“I made a covenant with your fathers

on the day when I led them out of the land of Egypt,

from the house of slavery,

saying:

‘When seven years have been completed,

each person shall release his Hebrew brother

who has been sold to him

and has served you for six years,

and you shall release him from your service as a free man.’

But your fathers did not listen to me,

nor did they incline their ear.

Today you turned back

and did what is right in my eyes,

proclaiming freedom each person to his neighbor.

You entered into a covenant in my presence,

in the house over which my name was invoked.

But you turned back

and profaned my name.

Each of you brought back his male slave

and each his female slave,

whom you had released to be free

and under their own authority,

and you subjugated them

so that they would be your male and female slaves.

Therefore thus says the Lord:

You did not listen to me

by proclaiming freedom each person to his brother

and each person to his neighbor.

Behold [Note: The copies of the Canon, together with several manuscript codices, do not read the pronoun “to you,” but have this wording: “Behold, I proclaim freedom.” The Hebrew, however, has לכם, *lakhem*, that is, “to you.” MART.], I proclaim freedom to you, says the Lord,

to the sword,

to pestilence,

and to famine.

I shall make you a source of terror to all the kingdoms of the earth.

I shall give the men who transgress my covenant

and have not observed the words of the covenant

to which they consented in my presence—

the calf that they cut in two

and passed between its pieces:

the princes of Judah,

the princes of Jerusalem,

the eunuchs,

the priests,

and all the people of the land

who passed between the pieces of the calf.

I shall give them into the hand of their enemies

and into the hand of those who seek their lives.

Their corpses shall be food

for the birds of heaven

and the beasts of the earth.

And Zedekiah king of Judah

and his princes

I shall give into the hand of their enemies,

into the hand of those who seek their lives,

and into the hand of the armies of the king of Babylon

that have withdrawn from you.

Behold, I command it, says the Lord,

and I shall bring them back to this city.

They shall fight against it,

capture it,

and burn it with fire.

I shall make the cities of Judah desolate,

because there is no inhabitant.”

**[Chapter XXXV]** The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord

in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah,

king of Judah,

saying:

“Go to the house of the Rechabites

and speak to them.

Bring them into the house of the Lord,

into one of the treasury chambers,

and give them wine to drink.”

So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah,

his brothers,

all his sons,

and the entire house of the Rechabites.

[Col. 0901D] I brought them into the house of the Lord,

to the treasury of the sons of Hanan,

son of Igdaliah, a man of God,

which was beside the treasury of the princes,

above the treasury of Maaseiah son of Shallum,

who was guardian of the vestibule.

I placed bowls full of wine

and cups before the sons of the house of the Rechabites,

and I said to them:

“Drink wine.”

They answered:

“We shall not drink wine.

For Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying:

‘You shall not drink wine,

neither you nor your sons,

forever.

[Col. 0902A] You shall not build a house,

you shall not sow seed,

you shall not plant vineyards,

nor shall you possess them.

Rather, you shall dwell in tents

all your days,

so that you may live many days

upon the face of the land

in which you dwell as resident foreigners.’

Thus we obeyed the voice of Jonadab son of Rechab, our father,

in everything that he commanded us,

so that we did not drink wine

all our days—

we,

our wives,

our sons,

and our daughters.

We did not build houses to dwell in,

nor did we possess a vineyard,

a field,

or seed.

Rather, we dwelt in tents

and obeyed according to everything

that Jonadab our father commanded us.

But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against our land,

we said:

‘Come, let us enter Jerusalem

because of the army of the Chaldeans

and because of the army of Syria.’

And we remained in Jerusalem.”

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

“Go and say to the men of Judah

and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem:

‘Will you not accept discipline,

so as to obey my words?’ says the Lord.

The words of Jonadab son of Rechab prevailed,

for he commanded his sons not to drink wine,

and they have not drunk it until this day,

because they obeyed their father’s command.

But I have spoken to you,

rising early and speaking,

and you have not obeyed me.

I sent to you all my servants the prophets,

rising early,

sending them,

and saying:

[Col. 0902C] ‘Turn back, each of you, from your most evil way,

and make your practices good.

Do not follow foreign gods,

and do not worship them.

Then you shall dwell in the land

that I gave to you and to your fathers.’

But you did not incline your ear,

and you did not listen to me.”

Thus the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab

established the command of their father,

which he had commanded them,

but this people did not obey me.

Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

“Behold, I shall bring upon Judah

and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem

all the affliction that I have spoken against them,

because I spoke to them

and they did not listen.

I called them,

and they did not answer me.”

But to the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

“Because you obeyed the command of Jonadab your father,

and kept all his commandments,

and did everything that he commanded you,

therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

A man from the line of Jonadab son of Rechab

shall never be absent,

standing in my presence all the days.”

**[Chapter XXXVI]** In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah,

king of Judah,

this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:

“Take a scroll of a book,

and write in it all the words that I have spoken to you

against Israel,

Judah,

and all the nations,

from the day when I spoke to you,

from the days of Josiah until this day.

[Col. 0903A] Perhaps, when the house of Judah hears all the evils

that I am considering doing to them,

each person may turn back from his most evil way,

and I shall be merciful toward their iniquity

and their sin.”

Jeremiah therefore called Baruch son of Neriah,

and Baruch wrote from Jeremiah’s mouth

all the words of the Lord

that he had spoken to him,

in the scroll of the book.

And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying:

“I am confined,

and I cannot enter the house of the Lord.

Therefore you go,

and read from the scroll in which you wrote from my mouth

the words of the Lord,

in the hearing of the people in the house of the Lord,

on the day of fasting.

Moreover, in the hearing of all Judah

who come from their cities,

you shall read to them.

Perhaps their prayer may fall before the Lord,

and each person may turn back from his most evil way,

[Col. 0903B] for great are the fury and indignation

that the Lord has spoken against this people.”

And Baruch son of Neriah did according to everything

that Jeremiah the prophet had commanded him,

reading the words of the Lord from the scroll

in the house of the Lord.

Now in the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah,

king of Judah,

in the ninth month,

they proclaimed a fast before the Lord

for all the people in Jerusalem

and for all the multitude

that had gathered from the cities of Judah in Jerusalem.

And Baruch read from the scroll the words of Jeremiah

in the house of the Lord,

in the treasury of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe,

in the upper vestibule,

at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the Lord,

in the hearing of all the people.

When Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan

heard all the words of the Lord from the book,

he went down to the king’s house,

to the treasury of the scribe.

And behold, all the princes were sitting there:

Elishama the scribe,

Delaiah son of Shemaiah,

Elnathan son of Achbor,

Gemariah son of Shaphan,

Zedekiah son of Hananiah,

and all the princes.

And Michaiah reported to them all the words that he had heard, when Baruch was reading from the scroll in the hearing of the people.

So all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying:

“Take in your hand the scroll from which you read in the hearing of the people, and come.”

So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.

And they said to him:

[Col. 0903D] “Sit down and read this in our hearing.”

And Baruch read in their hearing.

When they had heard all the words, each one was astonished, looking at his neighbor, and they said to Baruch:

“We must report all these words to the king.”

And they questioned him, saying:

“Tell us how you wrote all these words from his mouth.”

Baruch said to them:

“He was speaking from his mouth, as though reading all these words to me, and I was writing them in the scroll with ink.”

And the officials said to Baruch:

“Go, and hide—you and Jeremiah—and let no one know where you are.”

And they went in to the king in the court.

[Col. 0904A] They deposited the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and reported all the words in the hearing of the king.

Then the king sent Jehudi to take the scroll. He took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe and read it in the hearing of the king and of all the officials who were standing around the king.

Now the king was sitting in the winter house, in the ninth month, and a brazier full of burning coals had been placed before him.

When Jehudi had read three or four columns, he cut it with the scribe’s knife and threw it into the fire that was on the brazier, until the entire scroll was consumed by the fire that was on the brazier.

Yet neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words were afraid, nor did they tear their garments.

Nevertheless Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, but he did not listen to them.

[Col. 0904B] And the king commanded Jeremiel son of Ammelech, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the Lord hid them.

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah [Al. adds: “the prophet”], after the king had burned the scroll and the words that Baruch had written from Jeremiah’s mouth, saying:

“Take another scroll again and write in it all the former words that were in the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

“And to Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say:

‘Thus says the Lord:

You burned that scroll, saying:

“Why did you write in it, announcing:

[Col. 0904C] The king of Babylon will surely come, and he will devastate this land, and make man and beast cease from it”?

Therefore thus says the Lord against Jehoiakim king of Judah:

He shall have no one sitting upon the throne of David, and his corpse shall be thrown out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.

I will punish him, his offspring, and his servants for their iniquities. I will bring upon them, upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah, all the calamity that I spoke against them, and they did not listen.’”

Jeremiah then took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe. He wrote in it from Jeremiah’s mouth all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many more words than before were added to them.

[Col. 0904D] [Chapter XXXVII.] King Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned in place of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had appointed king in the land of Judah.

But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land obeyed the words of the Lord that he had spoken through Jeremiah the prophet.

King Zedekiah sent Jucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying:

“Pray to the Lord our God for us.”

Jeremiah was moving freely among the people, for they had not put him in prison custody.

Now Pharaoh’s army had come out of Egypt. When the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard this report, they withdrew from Jerusalem.

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, [Col. 0905A] saying:

“Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel:

Thus you shall say to the king of Judah, who sent you to me to inquire:

Behold, Pharaoh’s army, which has come out to your aid, will return to its own land, to Egypt.
