Then the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city; they will capture it and burn it with fire [Al. reads: “destroy it”].

Thus says the Lord:

Do not deceive yourselves, saying:

‘The Chaldeans will go away from us and withdraw.’

For they will not go away.

Even if you were to strike the entire army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and some wounded men were left among them, each one would rise from his tent and burn this city with fire.”

[Col. 0905B] When the Chaldean army had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh’s army, Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin and to divide the inheritance there in the presence of the citizens.

When he had reached the Benjamin Gate, a gatekeeper on duty there, named Jeriah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah, seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying:

“You are deserting to the Chaldeans.”

Jeremiah replied:

“It is false; I am not deserting to the Chaldeans.”

But he did not listen to him. Jeriah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.

Therefore the officials were angry with Jeremiah, beat him, and sent him into the prison that was in the house of Jonathan the scribe.

[Col. 0905C] For he was in charge of the prison.

So Jeremiah entered the house of the pit and into the dungeon, and Jeremiah remained there many days.

Then King Zedekiah sent for him and brought him out. He questioned him secretly in his house and said:

“Is there a word from the Lord?”

Jeremiah said, “There is,” and added:

“You will be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.”

And Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah:

“What have I done wrong against you, your servants, or your people, that you have put me into the house of imprisonment?

“Where are your prophets who prophesied to you and said:

‘The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land’?

“Now therefore, please listen, my lord the king. May my supplication find favor before you, and do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there.”

[Col. 0905D] So King Zedekiah commanded that Jeremiah be confined in the court of the prison and that a round loaf of bread be given him daily, except for the stew, until all the bread in the city had been consumed.

And Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.

[Chapter XXXVIII.] Now Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people, saying:

“Thus says the Lord:

Whoever remains in this city [Col. 0906A] shall die by the sword, famine, and pestilence.

But whoever goes over to the Chaldeans shall live, and his life shall be preserved and he shall remain alive.

“Thus says the Lord:

This city shall surely be delivered into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he shall capture it.”

And the officials said to the king:

“Let this man, we beg you, be put to death, for he is deliberately weakening the hands of the fighting men who remain in this city and the hands of all the people by speaking to them according to these words:

‘Surely this man is not seeking the welfare of this people, but their harm.’”

King Zedekiah said:

“Behold, he is in your hands, for the king can deny you nothing.”

So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah son of Amelech, which was in the court of the prison.

[Col. 0906B] And they lowered Jeremiah [Note: [Col. 0905D] Other copies of the Vulgate read: “They lowered Jeremiah with ropes into the cistern, in which there was no water, etc.,” farther from the Hebrew.]

with ropes. There was no water in the cistern, but mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mire.

Now Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, a eunuch who was in the king’s house, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. At that time the king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate.

Ebed-melech went out from the king’s house and spoke to the king, saying:

“My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done against Jeremiah the prophet, casting him into the cistern so that he may die there of hunger, for there is no longer any bread in the city.”

So the king commanded Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, saying:

“Take with you from here thirty men and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies.”

[Col. 0906C] So Ebed-melech took the men with him, entered the king’s house beneath the storeroom, took from there old rags and worn-out things that had rotted, and lowered them to Jeremiah in the cistern by ropes.

And Ebed-melech the Ethiopian said to Jeremiah:

“Place these old rags and these torn and rotten things under the armpits of your hands, and [Note: [Col. 0906D] Other copies read “above,” contrary to the Hebrew] beneath the ropes.”

Jeremiah did so.

Then they drew Jeremiah up with the ropes and brought him out of the cistern.

Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.

And King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah and brought him to himself at the third entrance, which was in the house of the Lord.

And the king said to Jeremiah:

“I am asking you about a matter; do not hide anything from me.”

[Col. 0906D] Jeremiah said to Zedekiah:

“If I tell you, will you not surely kill me? And if I give you counsel, you will not listen to me.”

So King Zedekiah swore secretly to Jeremiah, saying:

“As the Lord lives, who made this life for us, I will not kill you, nor will I deliver you into the hand of these men who seek your life.”

And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah:

“Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

If you go out and surrender to the officials of the king of Babylon, your life shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; you and your house shall be safe.

But if you do not go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, this city shall be delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire; and you shall not escape from their hand.”

[Col. 0907A] King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah:

“I am anxious because of the Jews who have deserted to the Chaldeans, lest I be delivered into their hands and they mock me.”

Jeremiah replied:

“They will not deliver you. Please listen to the voice of the Lord that I am speaking to you, and it will go well with you, and your life shall live.

“But if you refuse to go out, this is the word that the Lord has shown me:

Behold, all the women who remain in the house of the king of Judah shall be brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon. And they themselves shall say:

‘Your peaceful friends have deceived you and prevailed against you; they have plunged your feet into mud and slippery ground, and they have withdrawn from you.’

“And all your wives and your sons shall be brought out to the Chaldeans. You shall not escape their hands, but you shall be seized in the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn this city with fire.”

[Col. 0907B] So Zedekiah said to Jeremiah:

“Let no one know these words, and you shall not die.

“But if the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say:

‘Tell us what you said to the king; do not hide it from us, and we will not kill you. And what did the king say to you?’

—you shall say to them:

‘I laid my supplication before the king, that he should not order me to be taken back to the house of Jonathan, lest I die there.’”

Then all the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him.

He spoke to them according to all the words that the king had commanded him, and they ceased questioning him, for nothing had been heard.

Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison until the day Jerusalem was captured.

And it happened that Jerusalem was captured.

[Chapter XXXIX.] In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

But in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, the city was breached.

All the officials of the king of Babylon entered and sat at the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsekim, Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer, Rab-mag, and all the remaining officials of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the fighting men saw them, they fled.

[Col. 0907D] They went out of the city at night by way of the king’s garden and through the gate that was between the two walls, and they went out toward the road of the wilderness.

The army of the Chaldeans pursued them and seized Zedekiah in the plain of the wilderness near Jericho. They brought him, captured, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah, which is in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgments against him.

The king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah at Riblah before his eyes, and the king of Babylon killed all the nobles of Judah.

He also put out Zedekiah’s eyes and bound him in fetters, to be taken to Babylon.

[Col. 0908A] The Chaldeans burned the king’s house and the houses of the common people with fire, and they demolished the wall of Jerusalem.

As for the rest of the people who remained in the city, and the deserters who had deserted to him, and the remainder of the common people who were left, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, deported them to Babylon.

But Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left some of the poor people who possessed absolutely nothing in the land of Judah, and on that day he gave them vineyards and cisterns.

Now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had commanded Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, concerning Jeremiah, saying:

“Take him, keep your eyes on him, and do him no harm; but do with him as he wishes.”

So Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, and Nebushazban, Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer, Sarsekim, Rab-mag, and all the nobles of the king of Babylon sent for Jeremiah and took him from the court of the prison.

[Col. 0908B] They entrusted him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, so that he might enter a house and live among the people.

The word of the Lord had come to Jeremiah when he was confined in the court of the prison, saying:

“Go and say to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian:

‘Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Behold, I am bringing my words against this city for harm and not for good, and they shall be before your eyes on that day.

“But I will deliver you on that day,’ says the Lord, ‘and you shall not be handed over to the men whom you fear.

“For I will surely rescue you, and you shall not fall by the sword; your life shall be given to you as a prize, because you trusted in me,’ says the Lord.”

[Col. 0908C] [Chapter XL.] The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had released him from Ramah, when he had taken him bound in chains among all those who were being deported from Jerusalem and Judah and led away to Babylon.

The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him:

“The Lord your God pronounced this evil against this place, and the Lord has brought it about and done as he said, because you sinned against the Lord and did not listen to his voice; therefore this thing has happened to you.

“Now, behold, today I release you from the chains that are on your hands.

“If it pleases you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will keep my eyes on you.

“But if it displeases you to come with me to Babylon, stay here. Behold, the whole land is before you; wherever you choose and wherever it pleases you to go, go there.

[Col. 0908D] “Do not come with me, but live with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon appointed over the cities of Judah.

“Live with him among the people, or go wherever it pleases you to go.”

The captain of the guard also gave him provisions and gifts, and released him.

Jeremiah came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and lived with him among the people who had been left in the land.

When all the army officials who had been scattered through the regions, they and their companions, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land,

[Col. 0909A] and that he had entrusted to him men, women, and children, and some of the poor of the land who had not been deported to Babylon,

they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ophai, who were from Netophah, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite—they and their men.

Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore to them and to their companions, saying:

“Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

“Behold, I am living at Mizpah, to answer the command of the Chaldeans who are sent to us. But you, gather wine, grain, and oil, store them in your vessels, and remain in your cities that you possess.”

[Col. 0909B] Moreover, all the Jews who were in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom, and in all the regions, when they heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah,

and that he had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan,

all the Jews, I say, returned from all the places to which they had fled, and they came into the land of Judah to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they gathered an exceedingly large amount of wine and grain.

Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officials who had been scattered through the regions came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and said to him:

“Know that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to strike you down.”

But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Johanan son of Kareah spoke privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah, saying:

[Col. 0909C] “I will go and strike down Ishmael son of Nethaniah without anyone knowing, lest he kill you, and all the Jews who have gathered around you be scattered, and the remnant of Judah perish.”

Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah:

“Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsely about Ishmael.”

[Chapter XLI.] In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of royal descent, came with the king’s nobles and ten men with him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and they ate bread together there at Mizpah.

Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him rose up and struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword, and killed him—the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.

Ishmael also struck down all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, as well as the Chaldeans who were found there and the fighting men.

[Col. 0909D] On the second day after he had killed Gedaliah, when no one yet knew it, eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria, with shaven beards, torn garments, and covered with dirt. They had offerings and incense in their hands, to bring them to the house of the Lord.

Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, walking and weeping as he went. When he met them, he said to them:

“Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.”

[Col. 0910A] When they had come into the middle of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, he and the men who were with him, killed them beside the middle of the cistern.

Ten men were found among them who said to Ishmael:

“Do not kill us, for we have treasures in the field—wheat, barley, oil, and honey.”

So he stopped and did not kill them with their brothers.

The cistern into which Ishmael had thrown all the corpses of the men whom he had struck down because of Gedaliah is the one that King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with those who had been killed.

Ishmael took captive all the remainder of the people who were in Mizpah—the king’s daughters and all the people who remained in Mizpah,

[Col. 0910B] whom Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.

Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them and departed to cross over to the Ammonites.

Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officials who were with him heard of all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.

They took all their men and set out to fight against Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They found him by the great waters at Gibeon.

When all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officials who were with him, they rejoiced.

All the people whom Ishmael had taken captive turned back at Mizpah and returned to Johanan son of Kareah.

[Col. 0910C] But Ishmael son of Nethaniah fled with eight men from before Johanan and went to the Ammonites.

Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officials who were with him took all the rest of the common people whom he had brought back from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after he had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam: the fighting men, the women, the children, and the eunuchs whom he had brought back from Gibeon.

They went and settled as temporary residents at Chimham, which is near Bethlehem, in order to go on and enter Egypt, away from the Chaldeans.

For they feared them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land of Judah.

[Chapter XLII.] All the army officials, Johanan son of Kareah, and Jaazaniah son of Hoshaiah, together with all the rest of the people, from the least to the greatest, approached and said to Jeremiah the prophet:

“May our supplication come before you, and pray to the Lord your God for us, for all this remnant.

“For we have been left, few out of many, as your eyes see us.

“May the Lord your God announce to us the way by which we should go and the word that we should do.”

Jeremiah the prophet said to them:

“I have heard. Behold, I am praying to the Lord your God according to your words. Whatever word he answers me, I will declare to you; I will hide nothing from you.”

[Col. 0911A] They said to Jeremiah:

“May the Lord be a true and faithful witness among us: if we do not act according to every word with which the Lord your God sends you to us, so shall we act.

“Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may be well with us when we obey the voice of the Lord our God.”

When the ten days had been completed, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.

He summoned Johanan son of Kareah, all the army officials who were with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.

And he said to them:

“Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to present your supplications before him:

If you remain quietly in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, for I have relented concerning the evil that I did to you.

[Col. 0911B] “Do not fear the king of Babylon, whom you fear in terror; do not be afraid of him, says the Lord, for I am with you, to save you and deliver you from his hand.

“I will grant you mercies and have mercy on you, and I will make you dwell in your own land.

“But if you say:

‘We will not dwell in this land, and we will not listen to the voice of the Lord our God,’ saying:

‘No, but we will go to the land of Egypt, where we shall not see war, hear the sound of the trumpet, or suffer hunger, and there we shall dwell’—

therefore now hear the word of the Lord, remnant of Judah.

[Col. 0911C] “Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

If you set your faces to enter Egypt, and you enter in order to dwell there, the sword that you fear shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine about which you are anxious shall cling to you in Egypt, and there you shall die.

“All the men who set their faces to enter Egypt and [Al. adds: “to”] dwell there shall die by the sword, famine, and pestilence. None of them shall remain or escape from the evil that I will bring upon them.

“For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

As my anger and my wrath were poured out upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath shall be poured out upon you when you enter Egypt, and you shall become an oath, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach. You shall never again see this place.

[Col. 0911D] “The word of the Lord concerning you, remnant of Judah: Do not enter Egypt. Know with certainty that I have solemnly warned you today, for you have deceived yourselves.

“For you sent me to the Lord our God, saying:

‘Pray to the Lord our God for us, and according to everything that the Lord our God tells you, announce it to us, and we will do it.’

“I have announced it to you today, and you have not listened to the voice of the Lord your God concerning anything for which he sent me to you.

[Col. 0912A] “Now therefore know with certainty that you shall die by sword, famine, and pestilence in the place where you wished to enter in order to dwell there.”

[Chapter XLIII.] When Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of the Lord their God, for which the Lord their God had sent him to them—all these words—

Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men spoke to Jeremiah, saying:

“You are speaking a lie. The Lord our God did not send you, saying:

‘Do not enter Egypt in order to dwell there.’

Rather, Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us, in order to deliver us into the hands of the Chaldeans, to kill us and deport us to Babylon.”

Johanan son of Kareah, all the army officials, and all the people did not obey the voice of the Lord, to remain in the land of Judah.

[Col. 0912B] Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officials took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations to which they had previously been scattered, in order to dwell in the land of Judah:

men, women, children, the king’s daughters, and every person whom Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, together with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.

They entered the land of Egypt because they did not obey the voice of the Lord, and they reached as far as Tahpanhes.

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah at Tahpanhes, saying:

“Take large stones in your hand and hide them in the crypt beneath the brick wall at the entrance of Pharaoh’s house at Tahpanhes, in the sight of the Jewish men.

[Col. 0912C] “And say to them:

‘Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Behold, I will send for and bring Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will set his throne upon these stones that I have hidden, and he will establish his seat upon them.

“‘He will come and strike the land of Egypt:

Those destined for death—to death;

those destined for captivity—to captivity;

and those destined for the sword—to the sword.

“‘He will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt and burn them, and he will take them captive.

“‘He will wrap the land of Egypt around himself as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and he will depart from there in peace.

“‘He will break the statues of the house of the sun that are in the land of Egypt, and he will burn the temples of the gods of Egypt with fire.’”

[Chapter XLIV.] The word that came through Jeremiah concerning all the Jews who were living in the land of Egypt, who lived at Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and in the land of Pathros, saying:

“Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

You have seen all this evil that I brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah. Behold, they are desolate today, and there is no inhabitant in them,

because of the wickedness that they committed, provoking me to anger by going to sacrifice and worship foreign gods whom neither they, nor you, nor your fathers knew.

[Col. 0913A] I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying:

‘Do not do this abominable thing, which I hate.’

But they did not listen or incline their ear to turn from their evils and not sacrifice to foreign gods.

So my indignation and my anger were poured out, and they burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. They became a desolation and a wasteland, as they are this day.

“Now therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Why are you doing this great evil [Al. adds: “this”] against your own lives, so that man and woman, child and nursing infant, may perish from the midst of Judah, leaving you no remnant,

[Col. 0913B] provoking me by the works of your hands, sacrificing to foreign gods in the land of Egypt, into which you have entered to dwell there, so that you may perish and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?

“Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers, the evils of the kings of Judah, the evils of his wives, your own evils, and the evils of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and in the regions of Jerusalem?

“They have not been cleansed to this day. They have not feared, nor have they walked in the law of the Lord, in my statutes, which I gave before you and before your fathers.

“Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Behold, I will set my face against you for harm, and I will destroy all Judah.

[Col. 0913C] I will take the remnant of Judah who have set their faces to enter the land of Egypt and dwell there, and all of them shall be consumed in the land of Egypt.

They shall fall by the sword and famine; from the least to the greatest, they shall be consumed. They shall die by the sword and famine, and they shall become an oath, a portent, a curse, and a reproach.

“I will punish the inhabitants of the land of Egypt as I punished Jerusalem, by sword, famine, and pestilence.

“There shall be no one who escapes or remains from the remnant of the Jews who go to reside in the land of Egypt and return to the land of Judah, to which they lift up their lives in order to return and dwell there. They shall not return, except those who escape.”

[Col. 0913D] All the men who knew that their wives were sacrificing to foreign gods, and all the women—a great assembly—and all the people who lived in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying:

“As for the word that you have spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to you.

“Rather, we will certainly do every word that comes out of our mouth, to sacrifice to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, as we and our fathers, our kings, and our officials did in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem.

[Col. 0914A] “We were filled with bread, and it went well with us; we saw no evil.

“But from the time when we ceased sacrificing to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything, and we have been consumed by sword and famine.

“And when we sacrifice to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, is it without our husbands that we make cakes for her, to worship her and pour out drink offerings to her?”

Jeremiah said to all the people, against the men, against the women, and against all the common people who had answered him, saying:

“Did the sacrifices that you offered in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—you and your fathers, your kings and your officials, and the people of the land—not come to the Lord’s remembrance, and did it not rise upon his heart?

[Col. 0914B] “The Lord could no longer bear it because of the evil of your practices and because of the abominations that you committed.

“Your land became a desolation, an astonishment, and a curse, because there is no inhabitant, as it is this day.

“Because you sacrificed to idols, sinned against the Lord, did not listen to the voice of the Lord, and did not walk in his law, statutes, and testimonies, therefore these evils have happened to you, as it is this day.”

Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women:

“Hear the word of the Lord, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled with your hands, saying:

[Col. 0914C] ‘Let us fulfill our vows that we have vowed, to sacrifice to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.’

“You have fulfilled your vows and carried them out in deed.

“Therefore hear the word of the Lord, all Judah who live in the land of Egypt:

Behold, I have sworn by my great name, says the Lord, that my name shall no longer be called from the mouth of any Jewish man, saying:

‘As the Lord God lives,’ throughout the entire land of Egypt.

“Behold, I will watch over them for harm and not for good, and all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by sword and famine, until they are completely consumed.

“And those who escape the sword shall return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah—few men.

[Col. 0914D] All the remnant of Judah who have entered the land of Egypt to dwell there shall know whose word will stand, mine or theirs.

“And this shall be a sign for you, says the Lord, that I will punish you in this place, so that you may know that my words will surely be fulfilled against you for harm.

“Thus says the Lord:

Behold, I will deliver Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, just as I delivered Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy and the one who sought his life.”

[Chapter XLV.] The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he had written these words in a book from Jeremiah’s mouth, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:

[Col. 0915A] “Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning you, Baruch:

You said:

‘Woe is me, miserable man, for the Lord has added sorrow to my pain.

I have grown weary with my groaning, and I have found no rest.’”

[Note: [Col. 0915D] Other books read, “Thus says the Lord: You shall say to him.”] You shall say to him:

Thus says the Lord:

Behold, those whom I built, I destroy;

and those whom I planted, I uproot,

and this whole land.

And you, do you seek great things for yourself?

Do not seek them.

For behold, I am bringing evil upon all flesh,

says the Lord;

but I will give you your life as your spoil,

in every place wherever you may go.

[Chap. XLVI.] The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations, concerning Egypt,

[Col. 0915B] against the army of Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt,

which was beside the Euphrates River at Carchemish,

which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, struck down,

in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah.

Prepare shield and buckler,

and advance to battle.

Harness the horses, and mount the riders;

stand in helmets;

polish the spears;

put on the breastplates.

What then? I saw them terrified and turning their backs,

their warriors slain.

They fled in haste and did not look back;

terror on every side, says the Lord.

Let not the swift flee,

nor let the warrior think he can save himself.

To the north, beside the Euphrates River,

they were defeated,

and they fell.

[Col. 0915C] Who is this that rises like a river,

whose waters surge like the currents of rivers?

Egypt will rise like a river,

and like rivers its waters will surge,

and it will say:

“Rising, I will cover the land;

I will destroy the city and its inhabitants.”

Mount the horses and exult in the chariots,

and let the warriors advance:

Ethiopia and the Libyans carrying shields,

and the Lydians grasping and shooting arrows.

That day belongs to the Lord God of hosts,

the day of vengeance,

when he takes revenge on his enemies.

The sword shall devour and be satisfied;

it shall drink its fill of their blood.

For there is a sacrifice for the Lord [Al. adds: God] of hosts

in the land of the north beside the Euphrates River.

Go up to Gilead

[Col. 0915D] and take balm, virgin daughter of Egypt.

In vain you multiply medicines;

there will be no healing for you.

The nations have heard of your disgrace,

and your wailing has filled the land;

for warrior has collided with warrior,

and both have fallen together.

The word that the Lord spoke to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the matter that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, would come [Al. comes]

and strike the land of Egypt.

Announce it in Egypt,

and make it heard in Migdol;

let it resound in Memphis,

and say it in Tahpanhes:

Stand and prepare yourself,

[Col. 0916A] for the sword shall devour those who are around you.

Why has your strong man rotted away?

He did not stand, because the Lord overthrew him.

He multiplied those who fell;

one man fell beside another.

And they shall say:

“Rise, and let us return to our people

and to the land of our birth,

away from the sword of the dove.”

Call Pharaoh king of Egypt,
“Time has brought tumult.”

“As I live,” says the king,

whose name is the Lord of hosts,

“as Tabor is among the mountains,

and as Carmel is by the sea, so shall he come.”

Prepare for yourself the baggage of exile,

inhabitant, daughter of Egypt;

for Memphis shall become a wilderness,

and it shall be deserted and uninhabitable.

Egypt is a beautiful and graceful heifer;
a goader from the north shall come upon her.

Her mercenaries also, who were in her midst,

have turned like fattened calves,

and they fled together and could not stand,

because the day of their slaughter has come upon them,

the time of their visitation.

Her voice shall resound like bronze,

for they shall hurry with the army,

and they shall come with axes against her,

like men cutting wood.

They have cut down her forest, says the Lord,

which cannot be counted.

They have become more numerous than locusts,

and there is no number to them.

The daughter of Egypt is confounded

and given into the hand of the northern people.

The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, said:

Behold, I will visit the tumult of Alexandria,

and Pharaoh, and Egypt,

[Col. 0916C] and its gods,

and its kings,

and Pharaoh, and those who trust in him.

And I will give them into the hand of those who seek their lives,

and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

and into the hand of his servants.

After this it shall be inhabited as in former days, says the Lord.

But you, my servant Jacob, do not fear,

and do not be terrified, Israel;

for behold, I will save you from afar,

and your offspring from the land of its captivity [Al. your captivity].

Jacob shall return, and shall rest and prosper,

and there shall be no one to terrify him.

But you, my servant Jacob, do not fear, says the Lord,

for I am with you;

for I will consume all the nations to which I have driven you.

But I will not consume you;

I will chastise you with justice,

and I will not spare you as though you were innocent.

[Col. 0916D] [Chap. XLVII.] The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines,

before Pharaoh struck Gaza:

Thus says the Lord:

Behold, waters are rising from the north,

and they shall become like an inundating torrent;

they shall cover the land and its fullness,

the city and its inhabitants.

The men shall cry out,

and all the inhabitants of the land shall wail,

at the noise of the pomp of its weapons and its warriors,

at the shaking of its chariots

and the multitude of its wheels.

The fathers did not look back toward their children,

with hands hanging limp,

because of the coming of the day

on which all the Philistines shall be devastated,

and Tyre and Sidon shall be destroyed

[Col. 0917A] together with all their remaining auxiliaries.

For the Lord has devastated the Philistines,

the remnant of the island of Cappadocia.

Baldness has come upon Gaza;

Ashkelon has fallen silent,

and the remnants of their valley.

How long will you cut yourself down?

O sword of the Lord, how long will you not rest?

Enter your sheath;

cool yourself and be silent.

How shall it rest,

when the Lord has commanded it against Ashkelon

and against its maritime regions,

and there has appointed it for that place?

TO MOAB.

[Chap. XLVIII.] Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Woe to Nebo, for it has been devastated and confounded.

Kiriathaim has been captured;

the stronghold is confounded and trembles.

[Col. 0917B] There is no longer exultation in Moab.

They have plotted evil against Heshbon:

“Come, and let us destroy it from being a nation.”

Therefore you shall be silent;

you shall keep silent,

and the sword shall follow you.

The sound of a cry from Horonaim:

devastation and great destruction.

Moab has been destroyed.

Announce the cry to its little ones.

For by the ascent of Luhith,

weeping, she shall ascend in tears;

because on the descent of Horonaim

the enemies have heard the cry of destruction.

Flee; save your lives,

and you shall be like a tamarisk in the desert.

Because you trusted in fortifications

and in your treasures,

you also shall be captured.

And Chemosh shall go into exile,

his priests and his princes together.

[Col. 0917C] And the destroyer shall come upon every city,

and no city shall be saved.

The valley shall perish,

and the plains shall be destroyed,

because the Lord has said:

“Give a flower to Moab,

for it shall go out flowering.”

Its cities shall become deserted

and uninhabitable.

Cursed is he who does the work of the Lord deceitfully,

[Note: [Col. 0917D] The copyists of the Hebrew Canon version added on their own another adverb, namely *desidiose* (“slothfully”); it is also found written above the line in a later hand in the Corbie manuscript, no. 12. But the Royal manuscript and the Colbertine manuscript of Aniane have the pure sacred text without such an addition. MART.]

and cursed is he who withholds his sword from blood.

Moab was fertile from its youth,

and it rested upon its dregs.

It was not poured from vessel to vessel,

and it did not go into exile.

Therefore its taste remained in it,

and its odor was not changed.

Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

when I shall send him arrangers, those who lay out jars;
they shall lay him low,

empty his vessels,

and shatter their jars.

[Col. 0917D] And Moab shall be confounded because of Chemosh,

as the house of Israel was confounded because of Bethel,

in which it had trusted.

How can you say:

“We are warriors,

and men strong for battle”?

Moab has been devastated,

and its cities have gone up [Al. have been cut down],

and its chosen young men have descended to slaughter,

[Col. 0918A] says the king, whose name is the Lord of hosts.

The destruction of Moab is near;

its evil is coming very swiftly.

Console him, all who are around him,

and all who know his name, say:

“How the strong rod has been broken,

the glorious staff!”

Descend from glory,

and sit in thirst,

inhabitant, daughter of Dibon;

for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you

and has destroyed your fortifications.

Stand by the road and look,

inhabitant of Aroer.

Ask the fugitive,

and the one who has escaped [Al. him who has escaped], saying:

“What has happened?”

Moab is confounded,

because it has been defeated.

Wail and cry out;

announce it in the Arnon,

for Moab has been devastated.

And judgment has come upon the plain,

upon Holon,

and upon Jahzah,

and upon Mephaath,

and upon Dibon,

[Col. 0918B] and upon Nebo,

and upon the house of Diblathaim,

and upon Kiriathaim,

and upon Beth-gamul,

and upon Beth-meon,

and upon Kerioth,

and upon Bozrah,

and upon all the cities of the land of Moab,

those far away and those nearby.

The horn of Moab has been cut off,

and its arm has been broken, says the Lord.

Make him drunk,

because he has risen up against the Lord.

Moab shall clap his hand in his own vomit,

and he himself shall become a laughingstock.

For Israel was a laughingstock to you,

as though you had found him among thieves.

Therefore, because of your words

that you spoke against him,

you shall be led away captive.

Leave the cities and dwell in the rock,

inhabitants of Moab;

[Col. 0918C] and be like a dove nesting

at the summit of a cleft.

We have heard of the pride of Moab:

he is exceedingly proud—

of his loftiness,

his arrogance,

his pride,

and the haughtiness of his heart.

I know, says the Lord, his boastfulness;

but his strength is not according to it,

nor has he attempted to do what he was capable of doing.

Therefore I shall wail over Moab,

and I shall cry out over all Moab,

for the men of the clay wall, lamenting.

I shall weep for you with the mourning of Jazer,

vineyard of Sibmah.

Your branches have crossed the sea;

they have reached as far as the sea of Jazer.

The destroyer has rushed upon your harvest

and your vintage.

Joy and exultation have been taken away

from Carmel and from the land of Moab,

and I have removed wine from the winepresses.

The treaders of grapes shall no longer sing

the customary vintage song.

From the cry of Heshbon to Elealeh and Jahaz,

they have raised their voice.

From Zoar to Horonaim,

[Note: [Col. 0917D] The copies of the Hebrew Canon and all manuscripts, except one—the Colbertine manuscript of Aniane—read *vitulam conternantem*, “a terrified heifer,” in the accusative. The latter retains the ablative with our Latin Vulgate, so that the sense is: “from Zoar, a terrified heifer, to Horonaim.” For this is the name and designation of Zoar, not of Horonaim, Isaiah, chapter XV. Nevertheless, Pagninus’s Latin translation, called the interlinear translation, has the same accusative reading, *vitulam conternantem*, which is not without probability. MART.]

a trampling heifer.

The waters of Nimrim shall also become exceedingly bad.

And I shall remove from Moab, says the Lord,

the one who offers upon the high places

and sacrifices to its gods.

Therefore my heart shall resound for Moab

like a flute,

[Col. 0919A] and my heart shall make the sound of flutes

for the men of the clay wall.

For he has done more than he could;

therefore they have perished.

Every head shall be bald,

and every beard shall be shaved.

There shall be binding on all hands,

and sackcloth on every back.

On all the roofs of Moab

and in its streets there shall be nothing but mourning,

because I have broken Moab like a useless vessel, says the Lord.

How has it been defeated,

and how have they wailed?

How has Moab bowed its neck,

and how has it been confounded?

Moab shall become a laughingstock

and an example to all who are around it.

Thus says the Lord:

Behold, like an eagle it shall fly,

and shall spread its wings over Moab.

Kerioth has been captured,

and the fortifications have been seized.

[Col. 0919B] And the heart of Moab’s warriors shall be

on that day like the heart of a woman in labor.

Moab shall cease to be a people,

because it has gloried against the Lord.

Terror, pit, and snare are upon you,

inhabitant of Moab, says the Lord.

Whoever flees from the face of terror

shall fall into the pit,

and whoever climbs out of the pit

shall be caught in the snare.

For I shall bring upon Moab the year of their visitation,

says the Lord.

In the shade of Heshbon

those fleeing from the snare have stood.

[Note: [Col. 0919D] In Hebrew it is written, which means “from strength,” namely, from the strength of enemies; or, as the Septuagint has it, ἀπὸ δουνὰμεως, “from strength.” But the holy Father may have taken the middle letters as one, either through a hurried glance or because he found it thus written in his Hebrew exemplar, which is interpreted “truly, from the snare.”]

For fire has gone out from Heshbon,

and flame from the midst of Sihon,

and it shall devour the portion of Moab

and the crown of the sons of tumult.

Woe to you, Moab;

you have perished, people of Chemosh.

For your sons have been captured,

and your daughters have gone into captivity.

[Col. 0919C] And I shall restore the captivity of Moab

in the latter days, says the Lord.

Thus far the judgments of Moab.

TO THE SONS OF AMMON.

[Chap. XLIX.] Thus says the Lord:

Are there not sons for Israel?

Or does he have no heir?

Why, then, has Milcom possessed Gad as an inheritance,

and has his people dwelt in his cities?

Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

when I shall make the war cry heard

over Rabbah of the sons of Ammon,

and it shall be scattered into a mound.

Her daughters shall be burned with fire,

and Israel shall possess those who possessed him, says the Lord.

Wail, Heshbon,

for Ai has been devastated.

Cry out, daughters of Rabbah;

gird yourselves with sackcloth.

[Col. 0919D] Mourn and go around the hedges,

for Milcom shall go into captivity,

his priests and his princes together.

Why do you glory in the valleys?

Your valley has flowed away,

delicate daughter,

you who trusted in your treasures

and said:

“Who will come against me?”

Behold, I shall bring terror upon you, says the Lord God of hosts,

from all those who are around you.

You shall be scattered, each one away from his own sight,

and there shall be no one to gather the fugitives.

After this I shall restore the captives of the sons of Ammon,

says the Lord.

TO EDOM.

[Col. 0920A]

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

Is there no longer wisdom in Teman?

Counsel has perished from the sons;

their wisdom has become useless.

Flee, turn your backs, descend into the chasm,

inhabitants of Dedan,

for I have brought the destruction of Esau upon him,

the time of his visitation.

If grape-gatherers had come upon you,

they would have left no gleaning.

If thieves had come by night,

they would have taken only what was enough for them.

But I have uncovered Esau;

I have revealed his hidden things,

and he shall not be able to conceal himself.

His offspring, his brothers, and his neighbors

have been devastated,

and he shall be no more.

Leave your orphans;

[Col. 0920B] I shall keep them alive,

and your widows shall hope in me.

For thus says the Lord:

Behold, those who had no judgment

to drink the cup

shall surely drink.

And you—as though innocent—shall you be left?

You shall not be innocent;

you shall surely drink.

For by myself I have sworn, says the Lord,

that Bozrah shall become a desolation,

a reproach,

a desert,

and a curse,

and all its cities shall become everlasting desolations.

I have heard a report from the Lord,

and a messenger has been sent to the nations:

“Gather yourselves and come against her,

and let us rise up for battle.”

For behold, I have made you small among the nations,

despised among human beings.

Your arrogance has deceived you,

and the pride of your heart—

you who dwell in the clefts of the rock

and strive to grasp the height of the hill.

Though you raise your nest high like an eagle,

from there I shall bring you down, says the Lord.

And Edom shall become a desert.

Everyone who passes through it shall be astonished

and shall hiss over all its wounds.

As Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors were overthrown,

says the Lord,

no man shall dwell there,

and no son of man shall sojourn in it.

Behold, like a lion it shall rise

from the pride of the Jordan

against the strong beauty.

For I shall suddenly make him run against her.

And who is the chosen one

whom I shall appoint over her?

For who is like me?

Who shall withstand me?

And who is this shepherd

who can resist my face?

[Col. 0920D] Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord,

which he has formed concerning Edom,

and his thoughts that he has thought

concerning the inhabitants of Teman:

Surely the little ones of the flock shall cast them down;

surely their dwelling shall be destroyed with them.

At the sound of their ruin

the earth was shaken;

the sound of its cry was heard at the Red Sea.

Behold, like an eagle he shall rise and fly away,

and spread his wings over Bozrah.

And the heart of Edom’s warriors shall be

on that day like the heart of a woman in labor.

TO DAMASCUS.

Hamath and Arpad are confounded,

[Col. 0921A] because they have heard a very evil report.

They are troubled on the sea;

because of anxiety I could not rest.

Damascus has been dissolved and turned to flight;

trembling seized her.

Distress and pains have taken hold of her,

like a woman in labor.

How have they abandoned the praised city,

the city of joy?

Therefore her young men shall fall in her streets,

and all the men of war shall be silent on that day,

says the Lord of hosts.

And I shall kindle a fire on the wall of Damascus,

and it shall devour the walls of Ben-hadad.

[Note: [Col. 0921] Only the Canon of the Church of Carcassonne preserves the true reading here, namely “Ben-hadad.” All the other manuscript codices corruptly read “Ben-hadab.” MART.]

TO KEDAR AND TO THE KINGDOMS OF HAZOR,

which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, struck.

Thus says the Lord:

Rise and go up to Kedar,

and devastate the sons of the East.

[Col. 0921B] They shall seize their tents and their flocks,

their skins and all their vessels,

and they shall take their camels for themselves.

They shall call terror against them on every side.

Flee, depart quickly;

sit in the depths,

you who dwell in Hazor, says the Lord.

For Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

has formed a plan against you

and conceived designs against you.

Rise and go up against a nation at ease

and dwelling in confidence, says the Lord.

They have neither doors nor bars;

they dwell alone.

And their camels shall become booty,

and the multitude of their cattle plunder.

I shall scatter those who are shorn in the hair

to every wind,

and from every border of theirs

I shall bring destruction upon them,

[Col. 0921C] says the Lord.

And Hazor shall become a dwelling of dragons,

a desert forever.

No man shall remain there,

and no son of man shall dwell in it.

The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet

against Elam,

at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah,

saying:

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

Behold, I shall break the bow of Elam

and the sum of their strength.

And I shall bring upon Elam four winds

from the four quarters of heaven,

and I shall scatter them into all these winds.

There shall be no nation

to which the fugitives of Elam do not come.

And I shall make Elam tremble before its enemies

and in the sight of those who seek its life.

And I shall bring evil upon them,

the anger of my wrath, says the Lord,

[Col. 0921D] and I shall send the sword after them

until I consume them.

And I shall set my throne in Elam,

and I shall destroy kings and princes from there,

says the Lord.

But in the latter days

I shall restore the captives of Elam.

[Chap. L.] The word that the Lord spoke concerning Babylon

and concerning the land of the Chaldeans,

by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.

Announce it among the nations,

and make it heard.

Raise a banner;

proclaim it and do not conceal it.

Say:

Babylon has been captured;

Bel is confounded;

[Col. 0922A] Merodach has been defeated;

its carved images are confounded;

its idols have been overcome.

For a nation from the north has come up against her,

which shall make her land a wilderness.

There shall be no one dwelling in it,

from human being to beast,

and they have moved and departed.

In those days and at that time, says the Lord,

the sons of Israel shall come,

they and the sons of Judah together.

Walking and weeping,

they shall hurry and seek the Lord their God.

In Zion they shall ask the way,

with their faces turned toward it.

They shall come and join themselves to the Lord

in an everlasting covenant

that shall not be erased by any forgetfulness.

My people has become a lost flock.

Their shepherds led them astray

and made them wander on the mountains.

[Col. 0922B] They passed from mountain to hill;

they forgot their resting place.

All who found them devoured them,

and their enemies said:

“We have not sinned.”

Because they sinned against the Lord,

the dwelling of righteousness,

and against the Lord,

the hope of their ancestors.

Depart from the midst of Babylon,

and go out from the land of the Chaldeans.

Be like young goats before the flocks.

For behold, I am raising up

and bringing against Babylon

an assembly of great nations

from the land of the north.

They shall prepare themselves against her,

and from there she shall be captured.

Her arrow, like that of a mighty man who kills,

shall not return empty.

And Chaldea shall become plunder.

All who devastate her shall be filled, says the Lord.

Because you exult and speak great things,

plundering my inheritance,

[Col. 0922C] because you have leapt about like a calf over grass

and bellowed like bulls,

your mother is exceedingly confounded,

she who bore you has been leveled with the dust.

Behold, she shall be the last among the nations,

a desert,

impassable,

and dry.

Because of the anger of the Lord she shall not be inhabited,

but shall be reduced entirely to desolation.

Everyone who passes through Babylon shall be astonished

and shall hiss over all her wounds.

Prepare yourselves against Babylon all around,

all who bend the bow.

Fight against her.

Do not spare the arrows,

for she has sinned against the Lord.

Cry out against her on every side.

She has given her hand everywhere;

her foundations have fallen;

her walls have been destroyed,

[Col. 0922D] because it is the vengeance of the Lord.

Take vengeance upon her.

As she has done,

so do to her.

Destroy the sower from Babylon

and him who holds the sickle at harvest time.

Before the sword of the dove,

each one shall turn back to his own people,

and each shall flee to his own land.

Israel was a scattered flock;

lions drove him away.

The first to devour him was the king of Assyria;

this last one stripped his bones,

Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.

Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts,

the God of Israel:

[Col. 0923A] Behold, I shall visit the king of Babylon

and his land,

as I visited the king of Assyria.

And I shall bring Israel back to his pasture,

and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan,

and his soul shall be satisfied

on Mount Ephraim and Gilead.

In those days and at that time, says the Lord,

the iniquity of Israel shall be sought,

and there shall be none,

and the sin of Judah,

and it shall not be found.

For I shall be merciful to those whom I leave behind.

Go up against the land of those who rule,

and visit its inhabitants.

Destroy and kill what remains behind them,

says the Lord,

and do according to all that I have commanded you.

The sound of war in the land,

and great destruction.

How the hammer of the whole earth

has been broken and crushed!

How Babylon has become a desolation

among the nations!

[Col. 0923B] I have ensnared you,

and you have been captured, Babylon,

and you did not know it.

You have been found and seized,

because you provoked the Lord.

The Lord has opened his treasury

and brought out the vessels of his wrath,

for this is the work of the Lord God of hosts

in the land of the Chaldeans.

Come against her from the ends of the earth.

Open, so that those who trample her may come out.

Take the stones from the road

and pile them up,

and destroy her.

Let nothing remain.

Disperse all her warriors;

let them descend to slaughter.

Woe to them,

for their day has come,

the time of their visitation.

The sound of those fleeing

and of those who escaped from the land of Babylon,

[Col. 0923C] to announce in Zion the vengeance

of the Lord our God,

the vengeance of his temple.

Announce it in Babylon to the many,

to all who bend the bow.

Take your stand against her all around,

and let no one escape.

Repay her according to her work.

According to all that she has done,

do the same to her,

for she has risen up against the Lord,

against the Holy One of Israel.

Therefore her young men shall fall in her streets,

and all her warriors shall be silent on that day,

says the Lord.

Behold, I am against you, arrogant one,

says the Lord God of hosts,

for your day has come,

the time of your visitation.

The arrogant one shall fall and collapse,

and there shall be no one to raise him up.

And I shall kindle a fire in his cities,

[Col. 0923D] and it shall devour everything around him.

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

The sons of Israel and the sons of Judah

are suffering oppression together.

All who captured them hold them fast;

they are unwilling to release them.

Their redeemer is strong;

the Lord of hosts is his name.

In judgment he shall defend their cause,

to terrify the land

and to shake the inhabitants of Babylon.

[Col. 0924A] A sword against the Chaldeans, says the Lord,

and against the inhabitants of Babylon,

and against her princes,

and against her wise men.

A sword against her diviners,

who shall become fools.

A sword against her warriors,

who shall be terrified.

A sword against her horses

and against her chariots,

and against all the populace that is in her midst;

and they shall become like women.

A sword against her treasures,

and they shall be plundered.

Drought shall be upon her waters,

and they shall dry up,

because it is a land of carved images,

and they glory in monstrous things.

Therefore dragons shall dwell with [Note: [Col. 0923D] Some older books, as well as the Complutensian Bible and that of Sixtus V, read *fatuus*, “fools,” instead of *faunis*, “fauns”; others read *sicariis*, “assassins,” instead of *ficariis*, “fig-fauns.” There is a parallel passage in Isaiah, chapter XIII, verse 21, where the holy Interpreter says in his Commentary: “Incubi, or satyrs, or certain wild men, whom some call *fatui ficarii*, or they understand kinds of demons.” See what we have noted on the Life of Saint Paul the Hermit, vol. II, col. 7, note on the chapter. The reading printed here is the one adopted after the correction of Clement VIII.]

fig-fauns,

and ostriches shall dwell in it.

It shall no longer be inhabited forever,

nor shall it be rebuilt from generation to generation.

As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah

and their neighboring cities, says the Lord,

no man shall dwell there,

and no son of man shall sojourn in it.

[Col. 0924B] Behold, a people is coming from the north,

and a great nation,

and many kings shall rise from the ends of the earth.

They shall grasp bow and shield.

They are cruel and merciless.

Their voice shall resound;

they shall mount horses,

like a man prepared for battle

against you, daughter of Babylon.

The king of Babylon heard their report,

and his hands were loosened.

Anguish seized him,

pain like that of a woman in labor.

Behold, like a lion he shall rise

from the pride of the Jordan

against the strong beauty,

for I shall suddenly make him run against her.

And who is the chosen one

whom I shall appoint over her?

For who is like me?

Who shall withstand me?

And who is this shepherd

who can resist my face?

[Col. 0924C] Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord,

which he has conceived in his mind against Babylon,

and the thoughts that he has thought

concerning the land of the Chaldeans:

Surely the little ones of the flocks shall cast them down;

surely their dwelling shall be destroyed with them.

At the sound of Babylon’s captivity

the earth was shaken,

and a cry was heard among the nations.

[Chap. LI.] Thus says the Lord:

Behold, I shall raise up against Babylon

and against its inhabitants

those who have lifted up their heart against me
like a pestilential wind.

And I shall send winnowers against Babylon,

and they shall winnow her

and devastate her land,

for they have come upon her from every side

on the day of her affliction.

Let not the archer who bends his bow bend it,

and let not the armored man ascend.

[Col. 0924D] Do not spare her young men;

destroy all her army.

And the slain shall fall in the land of the Chaldeans,

and the wounded in her regions.

For Israel and Judah have not been widowed

by their God,

the Lord of hosts.

But their land is filled with guilt

against the Holy One of Israel.

Flee from the midst of Babylon,

and let each one save his life.

Do not be silent concerning her iniquity,

[Col. 0925A] for it is the time of vengeance for the Lord [Al. “from the Lord”];

he himself shall repay her in kind.

Babylon is a golden cup in the hand of the Lord,

making the whole earth drunk.

The nations drank of her wine,

and therefore they were shaken.

Suddenly Babylon has fallen

and been crushed.

Wail over her;

take balm for her pain,

if perhaps she may be healed.

We have healed Babylon,

but she was not healed.

Let us abandon her,

and let each one go to his own land,

for her judgment has reached the heavens

and has been lifted up to the clouds.

The Lord has brought forth our acts of justice.

Come, and let us recount in Zion

the work of the Lord our God.

Sharpen the arrows;

[Col. 0925B] fill the quivers.

The Lord has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes,

and his purpose is against Babylon,

to destroy her,

for it is the vengeance of the Lord,

the vengeance of his temple.

Raise a banner on the walls of Babylon;

strengthen the guard.

Raise up watchmen;

prepare ambushes.

For the Lord has conceived it

and has done all that he spoke

against the inhabitants of Babylon.

You who dwell upon many waters,

rich in treasures,

your end has come,

the measure of your cutting off.

The Lord of hosts has sworn by his own life:

I shall fill you with men like a locust,

and a vintage song shall be sung over you.

He who made the earth by his strength,

prepared the world by his wisdom,

[Col. 0925C] and by his understanding stretched out the heavens—

when he gives forth his voice,

the waters in heaven multiply.

He raises clouds from the end of the earth;

he makes lightning for the rain,

and brings the wind out of his treasuries.

Every human being has become foolish through knowledge;

every metalworker is confounded by the carved image,

because his casting is false [Al. “their casting is false”],

and there is no spirit in them.

They are vain works,

worthy of laughter;

at the time of their visitation they shall perish.

Jacob’s portion is not like these,

for he who made all things is himself,

and Israel is the scepter of his inheritance.

The Lord of hosts is his name.

You shatter weapons for me,

and I shall shatter nations through you,

and I shall destroy kingdoms through you.

[Col. 0925D] I shall shatter horse and rider through you;

I shall shatter chariot and rider through you;

I shall shatter man and woman through you;

I shall shatter old man and child through you;

I shall shatter young man and virgin through you;

I shall shatter shepherd and flock through you;

I shall shatter farmer and draft animals through you.

And I shall shatter governors and magistrates.

And I shall repay Babylon

and all the inhabitants of Chaldea

for all the evil they did in Zion,

before your eyes, says the Lord.

Behold, I am against you,

mountain of destruction, says the Lord,

which corrupts the whole earth.

And I shall stretch out my hand against you,

and roll you down from the rocks.

And I shall make you a mountain of burning.

They shall not take from you a stone for a corner

or a stone for foundations,

[Col. 0926A] but you shall be a perpetual ruin, says the Lord.

Raise a banner in the land;

sound the trumpet among the nations.

Consecrate nations against her.

Announce against her to the kings of Ararat,

Minni, and Ashkenaz.

Muster against her Tapsar;

bring up the horse like a bristling locust.

Consecrate nations against her,

the kings of Media,

its governors,

and all its magistrates,

and the whole land under its dominion.

The earth shall shake and tremble,

for the Lord’s plan against Babylon shall awaken,

to make the land of Babylon

a desert and uninhabitable.

The warriors of Babylon have ceased from battle;

they have remained in the strongholds.

Their strength has been devoured,

and they have become like women.

[Col. 0926B] Her tents have been set on fire;

her bars have been broken.

Runner shall meet runner,

and messenger shall meet messenger,

to announce to the king of Babylon

that his city has been captured

from end to end.

The fords have been seized,

the marshes have been burned with fire,

and the warriors have been thrown into confusion.

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor;
it is the time of her threshing.

A little longer,

and the time of her harvest shall come.

He has devoured me;

Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,

has swallowed me.

He has made me like an empty vessel;

he has swallowed me like a dragon.

He has filled his belly with my delicacies,

and he has expelled me.

[Col. 0926C] “The violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon,”

says the dwelling of Zion.

“And my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea,”

says Jerusalem.

Therefore thus says the Lord:

Behold, I shall judge your case

and avenge your vengeance,

and I shall make her sea a desert,

and dry up her spring.

And Babylon shall become heaps,

a dwelling of dragons,

an astonishment,

and a hissing,

because there is no inhabitant.

Together the lions shall roar,

and they shall shake their manes

like lion cubs.

In their heat I shall prepare their drink,

and I shall make them drunk

so that they may grow drowsy

and sleep an everlasting sleep,

and not rise,

says the Lord.

[Col. 0926D] I shall bring them down like lambs to the slaughter,

and like rams with young goats.

How has Sheshach been captured,

and the glory of the whole earth seized?

How Babylon has become an astonishment

among the nations!

The sea has risen over Babylon;

she has been covered by the multitude of its waves.

Her cities have become an astonishment,

an uninhabitable and deserted land,

a land in which no one dwells,

nor does a son of man pass through it.

And I shall visit Bel in Babylon,

and cast out from his mouth what he had swallowed.

The nations shall no longer flow toward him,

for the wall of Babylon also shall fall.

Go out from the midst of her, my people,

so that each one may save his life

from the anger of the Lord’s wrath.

[Col. 0927A] And lest your heart grow faint

and you fear the report

that shall be heard in the land,

a report shall come in one year,

and after that year another report,

and iniquity in the land,

and ruler against ruler.

Therefore, behold, days are coming,

and I shall visit the carved images of Babylon.

All her land shall be confounded,

and all her slain shall fall in her midst.

And the heavens and the earth

and all that is in them

shall rejoice over Babylon,

for destroyers shall come against her from the north,

says the Lord.

And just as Babylon caused those slain in

Israel

to fall,

so those slain throughout the whole earth shall fall because of Babylon.

You who have fled the sword,

come, do not stand still:

remember the Lord from afar,

and let Jerusalem rise upon your hearts.

[Col. 0927B] We are confounded, because we have heard reproach;

shame has covered our faces,

because foreigners have come upon the sanctity of the house

of the Lord.

Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

and I shall punish her idols,

and throughout all her land the wounded shall bellow.

Though Babylon should ascend to heaven and establish her

stronghold in the heights,

from me her devastators shall come, says the Lord.

A voice of outcry from Babylon,

and great ruin from the land of the Chaldeans.

For the Lord has devastated Babylon,

and destroyed from her the great voice.

And her waves shall roar like many waters;

their voice has given forth a sound.

For a plunderer has come upon her—that is, upon Babylon—

and her strong men have been seized.

And their bow has withered,

[Col. 0927C] because the Lord is a mighty avenger;

he will repay with retribution.

And I shall make drunk her princes and her wise men,

her governors, her magistrates, and her strong men.

And they shall sleep an everlasting sleep

and shall not awake, says the King—

the Lord of hosts is his name.

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

The broad wall of Babylon shall be utterly undermined,

and her lofty gates shall be burned with fire;

the labor of the peoples shall be for nothing,

and the nations’ works shall become fire and perish.

The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah,

son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah,

when he was going with Zedekiah king of Babylon,

in the fourth year [Note: [Col. 0927D] Martianaeus notes that the Syriac reads “in the eleventh year,” which is of no concern here. For the fourth year agrees well with the Hebrew text.] of his reign.

Now Seraiah was chief officer of the prophecy.

And Jeremiah wrote in one book all the evil that was to come

upon Babylon—

all these words that are written against Babylon.

[Col. 0927D] And Jeremiah said to Seraiah:

“When you come to Babylon, see and read all these words,

and say:

‘Lord, you have spoken against this place in order to destroy it,

so that no one may dwell in it, from human being to cattle,

and so that it may be an everlasting desolation.

And when you have finished reading this book, you shall bind a stone to it

and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates, and say:

“Thus shall Babylon be submerged,

and shall not rise again from the face of the affliction that I am bringing

upon her;

and she shall be dissolved.”’

[Col. 0928A] Thus far the words of Jeremiah.

## Chapter LII

Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah. He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to everything that Jehoiakim had done. For the anger of the Lord was against Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them away from his presence; and Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

Now in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, he and all his army, came against Jerusalem. They besieged it and built siegeworks against it all around. And the city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

In the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, [Col. 0928B] famine prevailed in the city, and there was no food for the people of the land. Then the city was breached, and all the fighting men fled from the city. They went out by night by way of the gate between the two walls, which leads toward the king’s garden—while the Chaldeans were surrounding the city—and they went by the road leading to the wilderness.

But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king, and they seized Zedekiah in the wilderness near Jericho; and all his retinue scattered from him. When they had captured the king, they brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, which is in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgments upon him.

The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; he also killed all the princes of Judah at Riblah. He put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with fetters, and [Col. 0928C] the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and placed him in the prison house until the day of his death.

In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month—which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, the commander of the army who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem. And he burned the house of the Lord, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem; and he burned every large house with fire.

The entire army of the Chaldeans that was with the commander of the army demolished all the wall around Jerusalem. As for the poor among the people and the rest of the common people who remained in the city, and the fugitives who had defected to the king of Babylon, and the remainder of the multitude, Nebuzaradan, the commander of the army, deported them.

But from the poor of the land Nebuzaradan, [Col. 0928D] the commander of the army, left some as vinedressers and [Al. omits “as”] farmers.

The Chaldeans also broke up the bronze pillars that were in the house of the Lord, the stands, and the bronze Sea that was in the house of the Lord, and they carried all their bronze to Babylon. They took the pots, the shovels, the lyres, the bowls, the little mortars, and all the bronze vessels used in the service; also the basins, the censers, the jugs, the bowls, the lampstands, the mortars, and the cups. Whatever was of gold, the commander of the army took as gold; whatever was of silver, as silver.

He took the two pillars, the one Sea, and the twelve bronze calves that were beneath the stands, which King Solomon had made in the house of the Lord. There was no weighing the bronze of all these vessels.

As for the pillars: the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, and a cord of twelve cubits went around it; its thickness was four fingers, and it was hollow inside. There were bronze capitals upon both of them. The height of one capital was five cubits, with latticework and pomegranates upon the crown all around, all of bronze. The second pillar was likewise furnished with pomegranates.

There were ninety-six hanging pomegranates, and all the pomegranates surrounding the latticework numbered one hundred.

The commander of the army took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three keepers of the vestibule. From the city he took one eunuch who was in charge of the fighting men, and seven men of those who saw the king’s face, who were found in the city; also the chief scribe of the army, who tested recruits, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.

Nebuzaradan, the commander of the army, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah. The king of Babylon struck them and killed [Col. 0930A] them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. And Judah was deported from its land.

This is the people whom Nebuchadnezzar deported: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Judeans; in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, from Jerusalem, eight hundred and thirty-two persons; in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan, the commander of the army, deported seven hundred and forty-five Judeans. Thus all the persons numbered four thousand six hundred.

Now in the thirty-seventh year of the deportation of Jehoiakim king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in that year of his reign, raised up the head of Jehoiakim king of Judah and brought him out of the prison house. He spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him [Col. 0930B] in Babylon. He changed his prison garments, and Jehoiachin always ate bread before him [Note: [Col. 0929B] After this final chapter of Jeremiah’s prophecy, the book of Baruch is found transcribed, contrary to Jerome’s intention, in both copies of the Canon of the Hebrew Truth. The following annotation is prefixed by the person who rashly introduced this portion of the Old Edition from the Septuagint into the new edition prepared according to the Hebrew codices: “This book, which is entitled by the name of Baruch, is not found in the Hebrew Canon, but only in the Vulgate edition; likewise the letter of Jeremiah the prophet.” [Col. 0929C] [Col. 0930B] “For the information of readers, these things are written here because they indicate much concerning Christ and the last times. It should be noted, however, that in the Carcassonne Canon these words are written in the middle of the page in the manner of a title, whereas in our San-Germain Canon the same words appear in the margin, and indeed in very small letters, like the other critical marginal scholia of the same book. MART.] all the days of his life. And his food was continually supplied to him by the king of Babylon, a fixed portion for each day, throughout all the days of his life, until the day of his death.

[Note: [Col. 0929C] The copies of the Canon of the Hebrew Truth, like many manuscripts of the sacred Scriptures, entitle the book of Jeremiah’s Lamentations in this way: “Here begins the Lamentation of the same author, which is entitled Qinoth, with the completion of the Hebrew letters.” They then append the preface found among the Septuagint interpreters and in the Latin Vulgate; but the older manuscripts of Jerome’s version contain nothing except what is read in the Hebrew text. Hence in the Royal Codex—which ought rightly to be accepted as a third copy of the Canon of the Hebrew Truth—and in the excellent Colbertino-Anician manuscript, there are absolutely none of these additions. The Corbie manuscript no. 2, written in the time of Charlemagne, struck out all the lines of the preface with obeli, thus making clear that these additions are foreign to Jerome’s version and were borrowed from the Greek interpretation of the Seventy Elders. Let the reader remember that the Lamentations are written in meters and arranged alphabetically, as Saint Jerome testifies in these words: “You have,” he says, “in the Lamentations of Jeremiah four alphabets, of which the first two are written almost in Sapphic meter, because a heroic comma concludes three verses joined together, which begin with one and the same letter. The third alphabet is written in trimeter, and each group of three verses begins with three letters, the same letters in each group. The fourth alphabet resembles the first and second.” Consult the letter to Paula of Rome and our Prolegomena, where a discussion of the meters of the Hebrews is undertaken. MART. — The Palatine manuscript, like other codices cited by Martianaeus, has this inscription: “Here begins the Lamentation of the same author, which is entitled Qinoth, with the completion of the Hebrew letters.” It also places before the book that preface, or summary, which begins: “And it happened after Israel had been led into captivity,” etc.; these words were received from the Septuagint interpretation into the Latin Vulgate edition. But nowhere are they found in Hebrew, Chaldean, or Syriac—or, what is most important, in the older and better manuscripts of Jerome’s version.] HERE BEGIN THE QINOTH, THAT IS, THE LAMENTATIONS OF JEREMIAH THE PROPHET.

[Col. 0929]

[Col. 0929C] [Aleph.] How the city full of people sits alone;

she has become like a widow,

the mistress of the nations;

the princess of the provinces has become tributary.

[Col. 0930C] Weeping, she wept through the night,

and her tears are upon her cheeks.

There is no one to comfort her among all her beloved;

[Col. 0931A] all her friends have despised her

and have become her enemies.

[Gimel.] Judah has migrated because of affliction

and the multitude of her servitude.

She dwells among the nations

and finds no rest.

All her pursuers have overtaken her

among the distressing places.

[Daleth.] The roads of Zion mourn,

because there are none who come to the solemn assembly.

All her gates are destroyed;

her priests groan;

her virgins are disheveled,

and she herself is oppressed with bitterness.

[He.] Her enemies have become her leaders;

her foes have grown rich,

because the Lord has spoken against her

on account of the multitude of her iniquities.

Her little ones have been led into captivity

before the face of the oppressor.

[Vav.] And all her beauty has departed

from the daughter of Zion.

[Col. 0931B] Her princes have become like rams

that find no pasture,

and they have gone away without strength

before the face of the pursuer.

[Zain.] Jerusalem remembered the days of her affliction

and the transgression of all her desirable things

that she had possessed from ancient days,

when her people fell into the hand of the enemy

and there was no helper.

The enemies saw her

and mocked her Sabbaths.

[Heth.] Jerusalem sinned grievously;

therefore she has become unstable.
