All who honored her have despised her,

because they saw her shame.

She herself groans

and turns backward.

[Teth.] Her uncleanness is upon her feet,

and she has not remembered her end.

She has been brought down violently,

with no one to comfort her.

“See, Lord, my affliction,

for the enemy has magnified himself.”

[Jod.] The enemy stretched out his hand

toward all her desirable things,

for she saw nations entering her sanctuary,

concerning whom you had commanded

that they should not enter your assembly.

[Chaph.] All her people groan

and seek bread.

They gave their precious things for food,

to revive their life.

“See, Lord, and consider,

for I have become despised.”

[Lamed.] O all you who pass along the way,

pay attention and see

whether there is any sorrow like my sorrow.

For he has harvested me,

as the Lord spoke,

on the day of his furious anger.

[Mem.] From on high he sent fire into my bones

and disciplined me.

He spread a net for my feet

and turned me backward.

He made me desolate,

exhausted with mourning all day long.

[Nun.] The yoke of my iniquities has kept watch.

They have been bound together by his hand

and laid upon my neck.

My strength has failed.

The Lord has given me into a hand

from which I cannot rise.

[Samech.] The Lord has removed all my mighty ones

from my midst.

He summoned a time against me

to crush my chosen men.

The Lord has trodden the winepress

for the virgin daughter of Judah.

[Ain.] Therefore I weep,

and my eye pours out waters,

because the comforter who restores my life

has been removed far from me.

My sons have become lost,

because the enemy has prevailed.

[Col. 0932A] [Phe.] Zion stretches out her hands;

there is no one to comfort her.

The Lord commanded against Jacob,

all around him,

that his enemies should be his enemies.

Jerusalem has become among them

like a woman defiled by menstruation.

[Sade.] The Lord is righteous,

for I provoked his mouth to anger.

Hear, I beg you, all peoples,

and see my sorrow.

My virgins and my young men

have gone into captivity.

[Coph.] I called my friends,

but they deceived me.

My priests and my elders

perished in the city,

because they sought food for themselves

to revive their lives.

[Res.] See, Lord, that I am afflicted;

my belly is troubled.

My heart is overturned within me,

because I am filled with bitterness.

[Col. 0932B] Outside, the sword kills,

and inside there is death like it.

[Sin.] They heard that I was groaning,

and there was no one to comfort me.

All my enemies heard of my evil;

they rejoiced,

because you did it.

You have brought the day of consolation,

and they shall become like me.

[Thav.] Let all their evil come before you,

and harvest them

as you harvested me

because of all my iniquities.

For my groans are many,

and my heart is mourning.

## Chapter II

[Aleph.] How the Lord in his fury

has covered the daughter of Zion with darkness.

He has cast down from heaven to earth

the glory of Israel,

and he has not remembered his footstool

on the day of his anger.

[Beth.] The Lord has thrown down

and has not spared

all the beautiful things of Jacob.

In his fury he has destroyed

the fortifications of the daughter of Judah,

and cast them to the ground.

He has polluted the kingdom

and its princes.

[Col. 0932C] [Gimel.] In the anger of his fury

he has broken every horn of Israel.

He has drawn back his right hand

from before the enemy,

and has kindled against Jacob

a consuming flame of fire all around.

[Daleth.] He has bent his bow like an enemy;

he has steadied his right hand like a foe.

He has killed everything beautiful to behold

in the tent of the daughter of Zion.

He has poured out his indignation like fire.

[He.] The Lord has become like an enemy.

He has cast down Israel;

he has cast down all its walls.

He has scattered its fortifications

and filled the daughter of Judah

with humiliation and humiliation.

[Vav.] He has scattered his tent like a garden;

he has demolished his tabernacle.

The Lord has given over to oblivion

the festival and Sabbath in Zion,

[Col. 0932D] and in the indignation of his fury

he has treated king and priest with contempt.

[Zain.] The Lord has rejected his altar;

he has cursed his sanctuary.

He has delivered the walls of its towers

into the hand of the enemy.

They raised a cry in the house of the Lord

as on the day of a solemn assembly.

[Heth.] The Lord planned to destroy

the wall of the daughter of Zion.

He stretched out his measuring line

and did not withdraw his hand from destruction.

The outer wall mourned,

and the wall likewise was destroyed.

[Theth.] Her gates have been driven into the ground.

He has destroyed and crushed her bars.

Her king and her princes are among the nations.

There is no law,

and her prophets have not found a vision

from the Lord.

[Col. 0933A] [Jod.] The elders of the daughter of Zion

sit on the ground and are silent.

They have sprinkled dust upon their heads

and girded themselves with sackcloth.

The virgins of Jerusalem

have cast their heads to the ground.

[Chaph.] My eyes have failed through tears;

my inward parts are troubled.

My liver has been poured out upon the ground

over the destruction of the daughter of my people,

when child and suckling fainted

in the streets of the town.

[Lamed.] They said to their mothers,

“Where are grain and wine?”

when they fainted like the wounded

in the streets of the city,

when they were breathing out their souls

in their mothers’ bosoms.

[Mem.] To what shall I compare you?

Or to what shall I liken you,

daughter of Jerusalem?

To what shall I make you equal,

and comfort you,

virgin daughter of Zion?

For your destruction is great like the sea;

who will heal you?

[Nun.] Your prophets saw false and foolish things for you,

and they did not uncover your iniquity

to provoke you to repentance.

Instead, they saw false burdens for you

and expulsions.

[Samech.] All who passed along the way

clapped their hands over you.

They hissed

and shook their heads

over the daughter of Jerusalem:

“Is this the city,” they said,

“of perfect beauty,

the joy of the whole earth?”

[Phe] [Note: [Col. 0933D] A learned man before our time observed that in the second, third, and fourth chapters of the Lamentations the order of the letters Phe and Ain is reversed. For among the Hebrews Ain normally precedes and Phe follows; here the opposite occurs, so that Phe precedes and Ain follows. The ancient scribes, and other writers unskilled in the Hebrew language, not understanding this, attempted to restore everything to the order of the first alphabet, sometimes striking out the letter Ain or omitting it from the alphabetic sequence. Some codices, however, follow the correct order, as it appears in the Hebrew. MART. — Critics inquire why Jeremiah placed the letter Phe before Ain in this chapter and the two following chapters, in reversed order, although in the first chapter he consistently observed the rule of the Hebrew alphabet. For us, after Martianaeus, it is enough to have warned the reader here that in most books this is the rashness of ancient scribes, who, while restoring the familiar alphabetical order, completely overturn the sense, despite the opposing sequence of the context.] All your enemies have opened their mouths against you.

They hissed and gnashed their teeth,

and said:

“We shall devour her.

This is the day we awaited;

we have found it,

we have seen it.”

[Col. 0933C] [Ain.] The Lord has done what he planned;

he has fulfilled his word,

which he commanded from ancient days.

He has destroyed and has not spared.

He has made the enemy rejoice over you

and exalted the horn of your foes.

[Sade.] Their heart cried out to the Lord

over the walls of the daughter of Zion.

“Pour out tears like a torrent,

by day and by night.

Give yourself no rest,

and let the pupil of your eye not be silent.”

[Coph.] Rise up, praise in the night,

at the beginning of the watches.

Pour out your heart like water

before the sight of the Lord.

Lift your hands to him

for the life of your little ones,

who have fainted from hunger

at the head of every street.

[Col. 0933D] [Res.] See, Lord, and consider

whom you have harvested in this way.

Will women then eat their own fruit,

children the measure of a palm?

Will priest and prophet be killed

in the sanctuary of the Lord?

[Col. 0934A] [Sin.] Boy and old man lie on the ground outside.

My virgins and my young men

have fallen by the sword.

You killed them on the day of your fury;

you struck them and showed no mercy.

[Thau.] You summoned, as for a solemn day,

those who would terrify me from every side.

On the day of the Lord’s fury

there was no escapee or survivor

of those whom I raised and nurtured.

My enemy consumed them.

## Chapter III

[Aleph.] I am the man who sees my poverty

under the rod of his indignation.

He led me

and brought me into darkness

and not into light.

Against me alone he turned and turned his hand

all day long.

[Beth.] He has aged my skin and my flesh;

he has crushed my bones.

He built around me

and surrounded me with gall and hardship.

[Col. 0934B] He placed me in darkness

like those long dead.

[Gimel.] He built a wall against me

so that I could not escape.

He made my fetter heavy.

And when I cried out and pleaded,

he shut out my prayer.

He enclosed my ways with hewn stones;

he overturned my paths.

[Daleth.] He became for me a bear lying in wait,

a lion in hiding.

He overturned my paths

and broke me.

He made me desolate.

He bent his bow

and set me like a target for the arrow.

[He.] He shot into my kidneys

the daughters of his quiver.

I became a mockery to all my people,

their song all day long.

He filled me with bitterness;

he inebriated me with wormwood.

[Col. 0934C] [Vav.] He broke my teeth with gravel;

he fed me ashes.

My soul has been driven away from peace;

I have forgotten good things.

And I said:

“My end has perished,

and my hope from the Lord.”

[Zain.] Remember my poverty and my transgression,

the wormwood and the gall.

My soul will remember continually,

and it will waste away within me.

Recalling this in my heart,

therefore I shall hope.

[Heth.] It is because of the Lord’s mercies

that we have not been consumed,

because his compassions have not failed.

They are new every morning;

great is your faithfulness.

“The Lord is my portion,”

my soul has said;

therefore I shall wait for him.

[Teth.] The Lord is good to those who hope in him,

to the soul that seeks him.

It is good to await silently

the salvation of God.

It is good for a man

to bear the yoke from his youth.

[Col. 0934D] [Jod.] He will sit alone

and keep silent,

because he has lifted it upon himself.

He will place his mouth in the dust;

perhaps there is hope.

He will offer his cheek to the one who strikes him;

he will be filled with reproaches.

[Chaph.] For the Lord will not reject forever.

[Col. 0935A] For if he has cast off,

he will also have mercy

according to the multitude of his mercies.

For he has not humbled from his heart

or cast off the children of men.

[Lamed.] To crush beneath his feet

all the prisoners of the earth.

To turn aside the judgment of a man

before the face of the Most High.

To pervert a man in his judgment—

the Lord has not approved.

[Mem.] Who is this who said that something should happen

when the Lord did not command it?

Do not evil and good proceed

from the mouth of the Most High?

Why should a living man complain,

a man for his sins?

[Nun.] Let us examine our ways,

and seek,

and return to the Lord.

Let us lift our hearts with our hands

to the Lord in the heavens.

We have acted wickedly

and provoked him to anger;

[Col. 0935B] therefore you are implacable.

[Samech.] You have covered us in fury

and struck us.

You have killed

and have not spared.

You have set a cloud before yourself

so that prayer may not pass through.

You have made me an object of eradication

and rejection

in the midst of the peoples.

[Phe.] All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.

Terror and the snare have become our prophecy,

and destruction.

My eye pours out streams of water

over the destruction of the daughter of my people.

[Ain.] My eye is afflicted

and does not keep silent,

because there is no rest,

until the Lord looks down

and sees from the heavens.

My eye has plundered my soul

among all the daughters of my city.

[Sade.] My enemies hunted me like a bird,

without cause.

[Col. 0935C] My life fell into a pit,

and they placed a stone over me.

The waters flooded over my head;

I said:

“I am lost.”

[Coph.] I called upon your name, Lord,

from the deepest pit.

You heard my voice.

Do not turn your ear away

from my sighing and cries.

You drew near on the day when I called upon you;

you said:

“Do not fear.”

[Res.] You judged, Lord,

the cause of my soul,

redeemer of my life.

You saw, Lord,

their wickedness against me;

judge my judgment.

You saw all their fury,

all their thoughts against me.

[Sin.] You heard their reproach, Lord,

all their thoughts against me,

the lips of those rising up against me,

and their meditations against me all day long.

[Col. 0935D] See their sitting down

and their rising up;

I am their song.

[Thav.] You shall repay them,

Lord,

according to the works of their hands.

You shall give them the shield of your heart [Note: [Col. 0935D] The Hebrew has a word that properly means “your curse”; it appears, however, that Saint Jerome read in his copy a word differing from it by the transposition of one little letter, which truly signifies labor, hardship, and similar things.]—

your labor.

You shall pursue them in fury

and destroy them beneath the heavens,

Lord.

## Chapter IV

[Aleph.] How the gold has become dim,

the finest color has changed,

the stones of the sanctuary have been scattered

at the head of every street.

[Beth.] The sons of Zion, glorious

and clothed in finest gold—

how they have been counted as earthen vessels,

[Col. 0936A] the work of the potter’s hands.

[Gimel.] Even the monsters (lamiae)

have exposed the breast;

they have suckled their young.

The daughter of my people is cruel,

like an ostrich in the wilderness.

[Daleth.] The tongue of the suckling

clings to his palate in thirst.

The little children ask for bread,

and there is no one to break it for them.

Those who ate delicacies

have perished in the streets.

Those who were nourished in scarlet

have embraced dung.

[Vav.] The iniquity of the daughter of my people

has become greater than the sin of Sodom,

which was overturned in an instant,

and no hands seized her.

[Zain.] Her Nazirites were whiter than snow,

brighter than milk,

redder than ancient ivory,

more beautiful than sapphire.

[Col. 0936B] [Heth.] Their faces have become blacker than coals,

and they are not recognized in the streets.

Their skin clings to their bones;

it has withered

and become like wood.

[Teth.] It was better for those killed by the sword

than for those killed by hunger,

because these wasted away,

consumed by the barrenness of the land.

[Jod.] The hands of compassionate women

have cooked their own children.

They became their food

in the destruction of the daughter of my people.

[Chaph.] The Lord has completed his fury;

he has poured out the anger of his indignation.

He has kindled a fire in Zion

and devoured its foundations.

[Lamed.] The kings of the earth

and all the inhabitants of the world

did not believe

that an enemy and foe would enter

through the gates of Jerusalem.

[Col. 0936C] [Mem.] Because of the sins of her prophets

and the iniquities of her priests,

who poured out the blood of the righteous

in her midst.

[Nun.] The blind wandered in the streets;

they were defiled with blood.

When they could not do otherwise,

they clutched their garments.

[Samech.] “Depart, you defiled ones!” they cried to them.

“Depart, go away, do not touch!”

For they quarreled

and, being agitated, said among the nations:

“He shall no longer dwell among them.”

[Phe.] The face of the Lord divided them;

he will no longer look upon them.

They did not respect the faces of the priests,

nor did they spare the elders.

[Ain.] While we still stood,

our eyes failed,

looking toward our vain help,

when we watched attentively for a nation

that could not save.

[Col. 0936D] [Sade.] Our footsteps slipped

on the paths of our streets.

Our end drew near.

Our days were completed,

for our end came.

[Coph.] Our pursuers were swifter

than the eagles of heaven.

They pursued us over the mountains;

they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.

[Res.] The breath of our mouth,

Christ the Lord,

was captured in our sins.

Of him we said:

“In your shadow

we shall live among the nations.”

[Sin.] Rejoice and be glad,

daughter of Edom,

who dwell in the land of Uz.

The cup will come to you also.

[Col. 0937A] You shall become drunk

and shall be stripped naked.

[Thau.] Your iniquity is completed,

daughter of Zion;

he will no longer deport you.

He has punished your iniquity,

daughter of Edom;

he has uncovered your sins.

HERE BEGINS [Note: [Col. 0937B] Saint Jerome mentions Jeremiah’s Prayer in the Prologue to the Scriptures prefixed to the Books of Kings, proving that there are twenty-two letters among the Hebrews from the twenty-two divisions counted in this same prayer. The Greek numerals that we use in the present edition are likewise found written in the copies of the Canon of the Hebrew Truth. MART. — Learned men have thought that Saint Jerome also said in his prologue to the Books of Kings that this Prayer of Jeremiah was composed in acrostic order, structured after the manner of the Lamentations, where he says: “Jeremiah’s Lamentations and his Prayer are woven in an alphabet of the same number.” But since this work was written differently—that is, by the author without regard to alphabetical order—they accuse the holy Doctor of error. Yet Saint Jerome does not say, as they claim, that the Prayer itself is arranged in alphabetical order, as are the chapters of the Lamentations; rather, he says that it is contained in twenty-two verses, corresponding in number to the letters of the alphabet, and that it is included in an alphabet of the same number as the Lamentations. The latter, however, have the additional feature that, according to the sequence of the letters, either individual verses or pairs of verses begin with them in order. In that passage he had proposed only to demonstrate that there are twenty-two Hebrew letters, a fact he showed truly and learnedly by other examples and by this very Lamentation and Prayer of Jeremiah. Moreover, it is so certain that he understood only the Lamentations to have been composed by that acrostic art that whenever he speaks elsewhere on the subject, he praises only Jeremiah’s four alphabets in different meters; by this designation he indicates that only the four chapters of the Lamentations have that form. See Letters 53 to Paulinus and 30 to Paula, no. 3. The Greek letters placed beside the individual verses have been retained from an ancient manuscript after Martianaeus, since they indicate the number, not the initial letter of the archetype.] THE PRAYER OF JEREMIAH THE PROPHET.

## Chapter V

Remember, Lord, what has happened to us;

look and see our reproach.

Our inheritance has been turned over to foreigners,

our houses to strangers.

We have become orphans without a father;

our mothers are like widows.

We drank our own water for money;

we bought our own wood at a price.

[Col. 0937B] We were threatened at our necks;

the weary were given no rest.

We gave our hand to Egypt

and to the Assyrians

in order to be filled with bread.

Our fathers sinned and are no more,

and we have borne their iniquities.

Servants have ruled over us;

there was no one to redeem us from their hand.

[Col. 0938A] At the risk of our lives

we brought in our bread,

away from the sword in the wilderness.

Our skin, like an oven,

has been scorched by the blasts of famine.

Women were humbled in Zion,

and virgins in the cities of Judah.

Princes were hanged by the hand;

the faces of elders were not respected.

They abused young men shamefully,

and boys fell upon the wood.

The elders failed at the gates,

and the young men from the chorus of singers.

The joy of our heart has failed;

our dance has turned into mourning.

The crown has fallen from our head.

Woe to us,

because we have sinned.

Therefore our heart has become sorrowful;

for this reason our eyes have grown dark.

Because of Mount Zion,

which has perished,

foxes walk upon it.

[Col. 0938B] But you, Lord,

remain forever;

your throne from generation to generation.

Why will you forget us forever?

Will you abandon us for the length of our days?

Restore us to yourself, Lord,

and we shall be restored.

Renew our days

as at the beginning.

But by casting us off

you have utterly rejected us;

you have been exceedingly angry with us

[Note: [Col. 0938C] In the Palatine manuscript the copyist adds: “Jeremiah has four hundred and fifty-four verses.”].

[Col. 0937] Jeremiah the prophet ends here.

[Col. 0937]

# THE BOOK OF EZEKIEL

## JEROME’S PREFACE TO EZEKIEL
[Col. 0937D] The prophet Ezekiel was led captive into Babylon together with Jehoiachin, king of Judah. There he prophesied to those who had been taken captive with him, as they repented of having voluntarily surrendered themselves to the enemies contrary to Jeremiah’s prophecy, while they still saw the city of Jerusalem standing, although Jeremiah had foretold that it would fall. In the thirtieth year of his age [Note: [Col. 0937D] The holy Father himself denies this very point in the commentary, at the very beginning, saying: “The thirtieth year is not, as most suppose, spoken of the prophet’s age.” Then [Col. 0938D] he himself prefers the interpretation that is closer to the truth: that the thirtieth year should be reckoned from the renewal under Josiah of the covenant of the Jews with God, when Ezekiel had already spent five years in captivity.] and the fifth year of the captivity, he began to speak to his fellow captives. At the same time, although later, he prophesied here in Chaldea, while Jeremiah did so in Judaea [Col. 0938D]. His language is neither sufficiently eloquent nor particularly rustic, but is moderately balanced between the two. He too was a priest, as was Jeremiah; the beginnings and the end of his book are shrouded in great obscurities. Yet his Vulgate edition also differs little from the Hebrew. Hence I am sufficiently amazed at what reason there could have been for the same translators, if we have them as translators throughout all the books, to have rendered the same things alike in some books and differently in others. Read, therefore, this book also according to our translation, [Col. 0939A] because, being written in cola and commata, it gives readers a clearer meaning. But if my friends mock this work also, tell them that no one compels them [Col. 0940A] to write [Note: [Col. 0939A] Here again the later critic’s hand has altered the Palatine manuscript, reading “so that they may read what I have written” instead of “so that they may write.” The printed reading, however, agrees perfectly with Jerome’s intention. Moreover, the excellent Greek writer Pamphilus the martyr, in his *Apology for Origen*, says that sophists who revile and other abusive writers were called by the Greeks φαγολοίδοροι.] But I fear that what is expressed more forcefully in Greek may happen to them, so that they will be called [Note: [Col. 0939A] All manuscript codices preserve this Greek word. Although it is read somewhat corruptly in some copies, it could easily have been restored by anyone not wholly unfamiliar with the Greek language. Yet the interpreters’ confusion and fluctuation over this same word are remarkable. In ancient manuscript copies this threefold Latin interpretation is supplied: φαγολοίδοροι, which among us is “eaters of seneciae”; that is, “eaters of seneciae,” or “eaters of senedae.” What seneciae or senedae may be, however, we are entirely ignorant, since these words mean nothing either in Greek or in Latin. Marianus therefore rightly taught that one should read “eaters of mockeries” (*manducantes sannas*), not “eaters of seneciae” or “those who delight in abuse.” The same Marianus adds that Jerome took this expression from Demosthenes: in the speech *On the Crown*, Demosthenes calls Aeschines, his opponent, ἰαμβόφαγος, because he consumed and gorged himself on abuse by reviling others. If this is so, why did Jerome not say: “But I fear that what is expressed more forcefully in Greek may happen to them, so that they will be called ἰαμβόφαγοι”? The word ἰαμβόφαγοι was readily available. Why, then, was it necessary to resort to another Greek compound, when ἰαμβόφαγοι and φαγολοίδοροι have the same meaning? I would more readily believe that Jerome expressed a manner of speech belonging to the Syrians. For it is customary among the Syrians to call the Devil, the craftsman of every slander, *ocel-kartso*, that is, “the eater of accusation”; this word corresponds equally to the Greek expression φαγολοίδορος, both in meaning and in the form of its composition. MART. — This is the reading of all the manuscripts we have seen, although it is often written somewhat more corruptly in Latin letters as *fagolidari*. Erasmus had not conjectured very successfully that it should be read φιλολοίδοροι, since both the script of the ancient books rejects this and the interpretation appended to that word, “eaters of mockeries,” even if we grant to Clericus, who rashly maintains it, that it was not added by Jerome but by some copyist or learned reader, is nevertheless clear evidence that it was written in this way long ago: φαγολοίδοροι. For it is derived not from φίλος, “loving,” but from φάγος, “eating.” Nor do we deny that this compound conflicts with the common analogy of the Greek language and that good writers do not customarily place the word φάγος first, whereas it is plainly postponed in hundreds of examples. Yet, as Martianaeus had almost conjectured before us, Jerome seems deliberately to have used nearly the very word by which the Syrians among whom he lived called the father of slanders—and, preeminently, the slanderer—the devil. They call him [Greek term absent in the supplied text], which means “eating mockeries” or “devouring accusations,” from [Greek term absent in the supplied text], meaning “to eat,” and [Greek term absent in the supplied text], meaning “slander.” We nevertheless do not think that Jerome himself translated that name from the Greek in this way; rather, we think he retained it in a form fashioned by the immigrant Greek-speaking populace of Syria, from whom the Syrians received almost countless words. Clericus is therefore excessively fastidious when, in investigating a word that was used by the common people and coined in a later age, on foreign soil, and under the influence of another language, he demands the elegance of the original Greek and grammatical analogy. Similar examples, and by no means few, can be found in glossaries, and no one has dared to reject them, as he judges in this case, as if they were the σφάλματα—“mistakes”—of uneducated people.] φαγολοίδοροι, that is, “eaters of mockeries.”

# THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET EZEKIEL BEGINS.

[Col. 0939]

[Col. 0939C] [Chapter I.] And it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, when I was in the midst of the captives beside the river Chobar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.

On the fifth day of the month,

that is, the fifth year of the deportation of King Jehoiachin,

the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel son of Buzi,

the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans, beside

the river Chobar;

and the hand of the Lord came upon him there.

And I saw, and behold, a storm wind was coming from the north;

and a great cloud, with fire enveloping it, and brightness

around it:

and from its midst, as it were, the appearance of amber—that is,

from the midst of the fire—

And [Note: [Col. 0939D] This passage is corrupt in the copies of the Hebrew Canon of Truth and in all the other manuscripts where it reads, “and from the midst of them the likeness of four living creatures.” How contrary this is to Saint Jerome’s interpretations, you may see in Book I of his *Commentary on Ezekiel*. The Colbertinus Aniciensis manuscript and the ancient Saint-Germain manuscript no. 3 retain the pure reading, but by a second hand. MART.] in its midst was the likeness of four living creatures;

and this was their appearance: they had the likeness of a human being.

And each had four faces,

and each had four wings.

[Col. 0939D] Their feet were straight feet,

[Col. 0940C] and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf’s foot,

and they sparkled like the appearance of glowing bronze.

Human hands were beneath their wings on their four sides;

and they had faces and wings on their four sides.

Their wings were joined one to another.

They did not turn back as they went;

but each walked straight forward.

As for the likeness of their faces:

each of the four had a human face and a lion’s face on its right;

each of the four had the face of an ox on its left,

and each of the four had the face of an eagle [Al. adds: “above”].

Their faces and their wings were extended upward;

two wings of each were joined to one another,

and two covered their bodies;

and each walked straight forward [Al.

“went”].

Wherever the impulse of the spirit was, they went;

they did not turn back as they walked.

[Col. 0940D] And the likeness of the living creatures: their appearance was like burning coals of fire,

and like the appearance of lamps.

This was a vision moving about in the midst of the living creatures:

the brightness of fire,

and lightning coming forth from the fire.

The living creatures went and returned,

like the appearance of flashing lightning.

And as I looked at the living creatures,

behold, one wheel appeared upon the earth beside the living creatures,

with [At. “having”] four faces.

The appearance of the wheels and their workmanship

was like the appearance of the sea;

and all four had one likeness;

and their appearance and workmanship

were as though one wheel were within another wheel.

They went in their four directions,

and they did not turn back as they went.

The wheels were tall,

and their height and appearance were fearful;

[Col. 0941B] and their entire bodies were full of eyes all around,

all four of them.

And when the living creatures went,

the wheels beside them went at the same time;

and when the living creatures rose from the earth,

the wheels rose at the same time.

Wherever the spirit went,

the spirit went there, and the wheels were likewise lifted,

following it.

For the spirit of life

was in the wheels.

When the creatures went, the wheels went;

when the creatures stood, the wheels stood;

and when they were lifted from the earth, the wheels were likewise lifted,

following them,

because the spirit of life was in the wheels.

And above the heads of the living creatures was the likeness of a firmament,

like the appearance of a terrifying crystal,

spread out above their heads.

[Col. 0941C] And beneath the firmament their wings were straight, one toward

the other;

each covered its body with two wings,

and the other was covered in the same way.

And I heard the sound of their wings, like the sound of many waters,

like the sound of the Most High God;

when they moved, there was a sound like that of a multitude,

like the sound of an army.

And when they stood,

their wings were lowered.

For when there was a voice above the firmament that was

over their heads,

they stood and lowered their wings.

And above the firmament that was over their heads

was something like the appearance of a sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne;

and above the likeness of the throne

was a likeness resembling the appearance of a human being above it.

And I saw something like the appearance of amber,

like the appearance of fire within it, all around;

from his loins and upward,

and from his loins downward,

I saw something like the appearance of shining fire all around,

like the appearance of a rainbow when it is in a cloud on a rainy day.

This was the appearance of the surrounding brightness.

[Chapter II.] This was the vision of the likeness of the glory of the Lord.

And I saw, and I fell upon my face,

and I heard the voice of one speaking.

And he said to me:

“Son of man,

stand upon your feet, and I will speak with you” [Al. “to you”].

And the spirit entered into me after he had spoken

[Col. 0942A] to me,

and set me upon my feet;

and I heard him speaking to me and saying:

“Son of man,

I am sending you to the children of Israel, to apostate nations that have withdrawn from me.

They and their fathers have transgressed my covenant

to this very day.

And the children are shameless in face and stubborn in heart;

to them I am sending you.

And you shall say to them:

‘Thus says the Lord God.’

Perhaps they themselves will listen, and perhaps they will cease,

for they are a provoking house;

and they shall know that a prophet has been among them.

You therefore, son of man, do not fear them,

and do not be afraid of their words,

for they are unbelieving and rebellious toward you,

and you dwell among scorpions.

Do not fear their words,

[Col. 0942B] and do not be terrified by their faces,

for they are a provoking house.

Therefore you shall speak my words to them, perhaps they will listen

and cease,

for they are provocateurs.

But you, son of man, hear whatever I speak

to you,

and do not be provoking, as the provoking house

is.

Open your mouth and eat whatever I give

you.”

And I saw, and behold, a hand was extended toward me, in which was a rolled-up book;

and he spread it out before me. It was written inside and outside,

and written upon it were lamentations, a song,

and woe.

[Chapter III.] And he said to me:

“Son of man,

[Col. 0942C] whatever you find, eat.

Eat this scroll,

and go and speak to the children of Israel.”

And I opened my mouth,

and he fed me that scroll.

And he said to me:

“Son of man,

your belly shall eat,

and your innermost parts shall be filled with this scroll that

I give you.”

And I ate it,

and it became in my mouth like sweet honey.

And he said to me:

“Son of man,

go [Note: [Col. 0941] In the commentary: “Go, and enter the house,” etc., more closely corresponding to the Hebrew.] to the house of Israel,

and speak my words to them.

For you are not sent to a people of deep speech and an unknown

[Al. “difficult”] language, to the house

of Israel;

nor to many peoples of deep speech and an

[Col. 0942D] unknown language whose words you could not understand;

Behold, I have made your face stronger than their faces,

And he said to me:

[Col. 0943A] “Son of man,

take into your heart all my words that I speak

[Col. 0943B] And I came to the exiles, to the mound of new grain,

but I shall require his blood from your hand.

And you shall turn your face toward the siege of Jerusalem,

And you, take wheat, barley,

[Col. 0944C] beans, lentils, millet, and spelt.

And he said to me:

[Col. 0944D] so that, when bread and water fail,

[Col. 0945C] and I myself shall execute judgments in your midst before the eyes

of the nations.

And I shall do in you what I have not done, and what I shall not do again,

because of all your abominations.

Therefore fathers shall eat their sons in your midst, and sons shall eat

their fathers;

and I shall execute judgments upon you,

and scatter all your survivors toward every

wind.

Therefore, as I live,

says the Lord God,

surely because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your offenses

and with all your abominations,

I too shall shatter you [Al. adds “you”];

my eye shall not spare, and I shall not have pity.

One third of you shall die by pestilence

and be consumed by famine in your midst;

one third of you shall fall by the sword around you;

[Col. 0945D] and I shall scatter the remaining third toward every wind,

and I shall unsheathe a sword after them.

And I shall complete my fury,

and make my indignation rest upon them,

and I shall be comforted.

And they shall know that I, the Lord, have spoken in my zeal,

when I have fulfilled my indignation against them.

And I shall make you a wilderness and a reproach to the nations

that are around you,

in the sight of everyone who passes by.

And you shall be a reproach and a blasphemy,

an example and an astonishment among the nations that are around

you,

when I execute judgments against you in fury, indignation,

and furious rebukes.

I, the Lord, have spoken.

When I send against them the deadly arrows of famine [Note: [Col. 0945D] At this point the copies of the Canon add the word “beasts,” so that the sense is: “When I send against them the arrows of famine, wicked beasts”; this has been taken from the following verse, where, after the calamity of famine, the most wicked beasts are mentioned. MART.],

which will be fatal,

and which I shall send to destroy you,

and gather famine against you,

and break for you [Al. omits “for you”] the staff of bread,

and send famine against you,

and the most wicked beasts, unto destruction,

then pestilence and blood shall pass through you,

and I shall bring the sword against you.

I, the Lord, have spoken.”

[Chapter VI.] And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel,

[Col. 0946B] and prophesy against them, and say:

Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God.

Thus says the Lord God to the mountains and hills,

to the cliffs and valleys:

Behold, I shall bring a sword against you,

and destroy your high places.

And I shall demolish your altars,

and your idols shall be shattered;

and I shall cast your slain before your idols.

And I shall place the corpses of the children of Israel before your idols,

and scatter your bones around your altars,

throughout all your dwelling places.

The cities shall become desolate,

and the high places shall be demolished and destroyed.

Your altars shall perish and be shattered,

your idols shall cease,

your shrines shall be crushed,

and your works shall be wiped out.

[Col. 0946C] And the slain shall fall in your midst,

and you shall know that I am the Lord.

And I shall leave among you those who escape the sword among

the nations,

when I scatter you throughout the lands.

And your survivors shall remember me among the nations to which they

were led captive,

because I crushed their adulterous heart, which had departed from

me,

and their adulterous eyes, which followed their idols.

And they shall be displeased with themselves because of the evils they had done,

because of all their abominations.

And they shall know that I am the Lord; I have not spoken in vain,

that I would bring this evil upon them.

Thus says the Lord God:

Strike your hand [Al. “with your hand”],

stamp your foot, and say:

‘Alas!’ [Note: [Col. 0945D] The same copies repeat the word “Alas” three times at this point [Col. 0946D], although other manuscript codices read “Alas” only once, in accordance with Jerome in his commentaries. Since similar expressions frequently occur in the prophets, the repeated “Alas” could easily have been transferred here from Jeremiah or from chapter nine of this book. MART.] concerning all the abominations and evils of the house

of Israel,

[Col. 0946D] for they are about to fall by sword, famine, and pestilence.

The one who is far away shall die by pestilence;

the one who is near shall fall by the sword;

and the one who remains and is surrounded [Al. “besieged”]

shall die of famine.

And I shall complete my indignation against them.

And you shall know that I am the Lord,

when your slain are in the midst of your idols,

around your altars,

on every high hill,

[Col. 0947A] and on all the summits of the mountains,

and beneath every leafy tree,

and beneath every spreading oak,

[Note: [Col. 0947D] In both copies of the Canon we read *lucum* (“grove”), not *locum* (“place”): “a leafy tree” is the same as a grove, and thus the Canon gives a sufficiently suitable sense, although the Hebrew has “place.” MART. — *Lucum* is erroneous in place of *locum* in the manuscripts praised by Martianus, whereas the Hebrew very clearly has [Hebrew term omitted in the supplied text]. Critics may have been emboldened to this rashness by these words from Jerome’s exposition: “on the high hills, among the very altars of idols, and groves,” which are called “leafy trees.”] at the place where they burned fragrant incense to all their idols.

And I shall stretch out my hand against them,

and make the land desolate and empty,

from the wilderness of Deblatha,

throughout all their dwelling places;

and they shall know that I am the Lord.”

[Chapter VII.] And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“And you, son of man,

thus says the Lord God to the land of Israel:

The end has come;

the end has come upon the four regions [Al. “wings”] of the land.

Now the end is upon you,

and I shall send my fury against you.

And I shall judge you according to your ways,

and bring all your abominations against you.

[Col. 0947B] My eye shall not spare you, and I shall not have pity,

but I shall place your ways upon you,

and your abominations shall be in your midst;

and you shall know that I am the Lord.

Thus says the Lord God:

One affliction;

behold, affliction is coming.

The end has come;

the end has come;

it has awakened against you;

behold, it has come.

The destruction has come upon you, inhabitant of the land;

the time has come, the day of slaughter is near,

and not the glory of the mountains.

Now I shall shortly pour out my wrath upon you,

and complete [Al. “repeat”] my fury against you.

And I shall judge you according to your ways,

and impose upon you all your crimes [Al. “all your abominations”].

[Col. 0947C] My eye shall not spare, nor shall I have pity,

but I shall impose your ways upon you,

and your abominations shall be in your midst;

and you shall know that I am the Lord who strikes.

Behold the day; behold, it has come.

The destruction has gone forth [Note: [Col. 0948D] As we said, here too Jerome appears to have written *contractio* (“contraction”) instead of *contritio* (“destruction”); this is especially clear from the context of his exposition, where he interprets it as “the day has been contracted and shortened,” etc. Martianaeus, although we do not know on whose authority, changes the word to *confractio* (“breaking”); nor does he inform the reader of his new reading.],

the rod has blossomed,

pride has budded;

iniquity has risen upon the rod of wickedness.

It is not from them, nor from the people, nor from their noise,

and there shall be no rest among them.

The time has come; the day has drawn near.

Let the buyer not rejoice,

and let the seller not mourn,

for wrath is upon all its people.

For the seller shall not return to what he sold,

and their life is still among the living.

[Col. 0947D] For the vision concerning all its multitude shall not return,

and no one in the iniquity of his life shall grow strong.

[Col. 0948A] Blow the trumpet; let everyone prepare,

but there is no one who goes to battle,

for my wrath is upon its entire people [Al. “whole multitude”].

The sword is outside, and pestilence and famine within.

The one who is in the field shall die by the sword,

and the one who is in the city shall be devoured by pestilence and famine.

And those who flee from them shall be saved,

and they shall be on the mountains like doves of the valleys,

all of them trembling,

each one in his iniquity.

All hands shall grow weak,

and all knees shall flow with water.

And they shall gird themselves with sackcloth,

and dread shall cover them,

and confusion shall be on every face,

and baldness on all their heads [Al. omits “their”].

They shall cast their silver outside,

and their gold shall be like refuse.

[Col. 0948B] Their silver and their gold

shall not be able to save them on the day of the Lord’s fury.

They shall not satisfy their souls,

and their bellies shall not be filled,

because the stumbling-block of their iniquity has come about.

They made the ornament of their necklaces into pride,

and made from it images of their abominations and

their idols.

Therefore I gave it to them as an impurity.

And I shall give it into the hands of foreigners for plundering,

and to the wicked of the land as spoil,

and they shall defile it.

And I shall turn my face away from them,

and they shall violate my secret place.

Those sent in shall enter it,

and they shall defile it.

Make a chain,

for the land is full of the judgment of blood,

[Col. 0948C] and the city is full of iniquity.

And I shall bring the worst of the nations,

and they shall possess their houses.

And I shall make the pride of the mighty cease,

and they shall possess their sanctuaries.

When distress comes, they shall seek peace,

and there shall be none.

Confusion shall come upon confusion,

and report upon report.

And they shall seek a vision from the prophet,

and the law shall perish from the priest,

and counsel from the elders.

The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed in sorrow,

and the hands of the people of the land shall be troubled.

I shall deal with them according to their way,

and judge them according to their judgments;

and they shall know that I am the Lord.”

[Chapter VIII.] And it came to pass in the sixth year, in the sixth

month, on the fifth day of the month,

that I was sitting in my house,

[Col. 0948D] and the elders of Judah were sitting before me,

and there the hand of the Lord God fell upon me.

[Col. 0949A] And I saw, and behold, something like the appearance of

fire: from the appearance of his loins downward there was fire,

and from his loins upward

something like the appearance of brightness,

like the appearance of amber.

And the likeness of a hand was extended and seized me by a lock of the hair of my head,

and the spirit lifted me between earth and heaven.

And it brought me to Jerusalem in a vision of God,

to the inner gate that faced north,

where the idol of jealousy had been set up to provoke

jealousy.

And behold, there was the glory of the God of Israel,

according to the vision that I had seen in the plain.

And he said to me:

“Son of man,

lift your eyes toward the way of the north.”

And I lifted my eyes toward the way of the north,

[Col. 0949B] and behold, to the north of the altar gate

was the idol of jealousy at the entrance.

And he said to me:

“Son of man,

do you suppose that you see what these people are doing—the great abominations

that the house of Israel commits here, so that I may withdraw far from

my sanctuary?

And you shall still turn and see greater abominations.”

And he brought me to the entrance of the court,

and I saw, and behold, a single opening in the wall.

And he said to me:

“Son of man, dig through the wall.”

And when I had dug through the wall,

behold, a single door appeared.

And he said to me:

“Enter and see the most wicked abominations that

these people commit here.”

And I entered and saw,

[Col. 0949C] and behold, every likeness of creeping things and animals,

an abomination,

and all the idols of the house of Israel were depicted upon the wall

all around.

And seventy men from the elders of the house of Israel,

with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among those who stood

before the paintings.

And each had a censer in his hand,

and a cloud of smoke rose from the incense.

And he said to me:

“Surely you see, son of man, what the elders of the house of Israel

are doing in darkness,

each one in the hidden chamber of his own room.

For they say:

‘The Lord does not see us;

the Lord has abandoned the land.’”

And he said to me:

“Still turn and you shall see greater abominations

than these people commit.”

And he brought me through the entrance of the gate of the house of the Lord,

[Col. 0949D] which faced north;

and behold, women were sitting there mourning for Adonis.

And he said to me:

“Surely you have seen, son of man.

Still turn and you shall see greater abominations

than these.”

And he brought me into the inner court of the house of the Lord,

and behold, at the entrance of the temple of the Lord, between the vestibule and

the altar, there were about twenty-five men,

with their backs toward the temple of the Lord and their faces

toward the east;

and they were worshiping toward the rising of the sun.

And he said to me:

“Surely you have seen, son of man.

Is this a small thing for the house of Judah,

that they should commit these abominations that they have committed here,

filling the land with iniquity and turning to

provoke me?

And behold, they are applying the branch to their noses.

Therefore I too shall act in fury.

My eye shall not spare, nor shall I have pity.

And when they cry out in a loud voice into my ears,

I shall not hear them.”

[Chapter IX.] And he cried out in my ears with a loud voice, saying:

“The visitations of the city have drawn near,

and each man has the instrument of slaughter in his hand.

And behold, six men were coming from the way of the upper gate,

which faces north,

and each had the instrument of destruction in his hand.

And there was one man in their midst, clothed in linen,

with a writer’s inkwell at his waist.

And they entered,

and stood beside the bronze altar.

And the glory of the Lord [Al. “God”] of Israel was taken up from the

cherub,

[Col. 0950B] which was above it, to the threshold of the house:

And he called the man who was clothed in linen and had the writer’s inkwell at his waist.

And the Lord said to him:

“Pass through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and mark a tau on the foreheads of the men who groan and grieve over all the abominations that are committed in its midst.”

And to the others he said in my hearing:

“Pass through the city after him and strike. Let your eye not spare, and do not show pity. Kill old man, young man, virgin, child, and women, to complete destruction. But do not touch anyone on whom you see the tau, and begin from my sanctuary.”

So they began with the elderly men who were before the front of the house.

[Col. 0950C] And he said to them:

“Defile the house and fill the courts with the slain; go out!”

And they went out and struck those who were in the city.

When the slaughter was completed, I alone remained; I fell on my face and cried out:

“Alas, alas, alas [Al. once: alas], Lord God! Will you then destroy all the remnant of Israel, pouring out your fury upon Jerusalem?”

And he said to me:

“The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great, and the land is filled with blood, and the city is filled with apostasy. For they said:

‘The Lord has abandoned the land, and the Lord does not see.’

[Col. 0950D] Therefore my eye also will not spare, nor will I show pity; I will repay their way upon their own heads.”

And behold, the man who was clothed in linen, who had the inkwell on his back [Al. at his waist], answered and said:

“I have done as you commanded me.”

**[Chapter X]** And I saw, and behold, upon the firmament that was above the heads of the cherubim there appeared something like a sapphire stone, like the appearance of the likeness of a throne, above them.

And he said to the man who was clothed in linen:

“Enter among the wheels beneath the cherubim, fill your hand with burning coals from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.”

And he entered before my eyes. The cherubim were standing on the right side of the house when the man entered,

[Col. 0951A] and the cloud filled the inner court.

And the glory of the Lord rose from above the cherub to the threshold of the house; the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the radiance of the glory of the Lord.

And the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty speaking.

And when he commanded the man who was clothed in linen, saying:

“Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubim,”

he entered and stood beside the wheel.

And one cherub stretched out his hand from between the cherubim toward the fire that was between the cherubim; he took it and placed it in the hands of the man who was clothed in linen, and he took it and went out.

And there appeared in the cherubim the likeness of a human hand beneath their wings.

[Col. 0951B] And I saw, and behold, four wheels beside the cherubim: one wheel beside one cherub, and another wheel beside another cherub.

The appearance of the wheels was like the appearance of a chrysolite stone.

And their appearance was one likeness in all four, as though one wheel were within another wheel.

And when they moved, they went in the four directions; as they went, they did not turn back. Rather, toward whichever place the first one inclined to go, the others followed, and they did not turn.

And their whole bodies, their necks, their hands, their wings, and their wheel-rims were full of eyes all around the four wheels.

And he called these wheels “the whirling ones,” as I heard.

Each of the four had four faces: one face was the face of a cherub;

[Col. 0951C] the second face was the face of a man; the third was the face of a lion; and the fourth was the face of an eagle.

And the cherubim rose up [Al. the cherubim were raised up]. This is the living creature that I had seen beside the river Chebar.

And when the cherubim moved, the wheels also went alongside them [Al. eos]. When the cherubim raised their wings to be lifted from the earth, the wheels did not remain behind, but were likewise beside them.

When they stood, the wheels stood; and when they were raised, the wheels were raised with them.

For the spirit of life was in them.

And the glory of the Lord went out from the threshold of the temple and stood over the cherubim.

And when the cherubim raised their wings, they were lifted up from the earth before me; and as they went out, the wheels also followed them.

[Col. 0951D] And they stood at the entrance of the eastern gate of the house of the Lord, and the glory of the God of Israel was over them.

This is the living creature that I saw beneath the God of Israel beside the river Chebar, and I understood that they were cherubim.

There were four, each with four faces and each with four wings; and beneath their wings was the likeness of a human hand.

The likeness of their faces was the same faces that I had seen beside the river Chebar; their appearance and the movement of each one were such that each proceeded straight ahead.

**[Chapter XI]** And the spirit lifted me up and brought me to the eastern gate of the house of the Lord, which faces the sunrise.

And behold, at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men. And I saw among them Jezaniah son of Azur and Pheltiah son of Benaiah, princes of the people.

[Col. 0952A] And he said to me:

“Son of man, these are the men who devise iniquity and deliberate an evil plan in this city, saying:

‘Are not houses built long ago? This is the cooking pot, and we are the meat.’

Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man.”

And the spirit of the Lord fell upon me and said to me:

“Speak:

Thus says the Lord:

So you have spoken, house of Israel, and I know the thoughts of your heart. You have killed many in this city and filled its streets with the slain.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

Your slain whom you have placed in its midst—they are the meat,

[Col. 0952B] and it is the cooking pot; but I will bring you out from its midst.

You feared the sword, and I will bring the sword upon you, says the Lord God.

I will cast you out from its midst and give you into the hand of enemies, and I will execute judgments among you.

You shall fall by the sword. I will judge you at the borders of Israel, and you shall know that I am the Lord.

This city shall not be a cooking pot for you, nor shall you be the meat in its midst; at the borders of Israel I will judge you.

And you shall know that I am the Lord, because you did not walk in my commandments and did not observe my judgments, but acted according to the judgments of the nations around you.”

[Col. 0952C] And it happened that, while I was prophesying, Pheltiah son of Benaiah died.

And I fell on my face and cried out with a loud voice:

“Alas, alas, alas, Lord God! Are you bringing the remnant of Israel to an end?”

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, your brothers, your brothers, your close relatives, and the whole house of Israel, all of them, are those to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said:

‘Keep far from the Lord; the land has been given to us as a possession.’

Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because I have sent them far away among the nations and scattered them throughout the lands, I will be for them a small sanctuary in the lands to which they have come [Al. may come].

Therefore speak:

[Col. 0952D] Thus says the Lord God:

I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the lands among which you have been scattered, and I will give you the soil of Israel.

And they shall enter there and remove from it all its offenses and all its abominations [Al. “its” omitted].

And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them.

I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,

so that they may walk in my commandments, observe my judgments, and perform them; so that they may be my people, and I may be their God.

But as for those whose heart follows after their offenses and abominations, I will bring their way upon their own heads,”

says the Lord God.

And the cherubim raised their wings, and the wheels with them; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them.

And the glory of the Lord rose from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain that is east of the city.

And the spirit lifted me up and brought me to Chaldea, to the exiles, in a vision, by the spirit of God; and the vision that I had seen was lifted away from me.

And I spoke to the exiles all the words of the Lord that he had shown me.

**[Chapter XII]** And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, you dwell in the midst of a provoking house, which has eyes to see but does not see, and ears to hear but does not hear, because it is a provoking house.

Therefore, son of man, prepare for yourself the baggage of an exile, and you shall go into exile by day before their eyes.

You shall go into exile from your place to another place in their sight, if perhaps they will look, because they are a provoking house.

And you shall bring out your baggage by day before their eyes, like the baggage of one going into exile; but you yourself shall go out in the evening before them, as an exile goes out.

In their sight, dig through the wall for yourself, and go out through it.

In their sight you shall be carried on shoulders; you shall be brought out in darkness. You shall cover your face and shall not see the ground, because I have made you a portent for the house of Israel.”

So I did as he had commanded me. I brought out my baggage by day, like the baggage of an exile; and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hand. I went out in darkness and was carried on shoulders in their sight.

[Col. 0953C] And the word of the Lord came to me in the morning, saying:

“Son of man, surely the house of Israel, that provoking house, has said to you:

‘What are you doing?’

Say to them:

Thus says the Lord God:

This burden concerns the prince who is in Jerusalem and the whole house of Israel that is in their midst.

Say: I am your portent. As I have done, so shall it be done to them: they shall go into exile and captivity.

The prince who is in their midst shall be carried on shoulders and shall go out in darkness. They shall dig through the wall to bring him out; his face shall be covered so that he does not see the ground with his eyes.

And I will spread my net over him, and he shall be caught in my snare.

And I will bring him to Babylon, to the land of the Chaldeans; but he shall not see it, and there he shall die.

And all who are around him, his guard and his troops, I will scatter to every wind, and I will unsheathe the sword after them.

And they shall know that I am the Lord when I scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.

And I will leave a few men among them, spared from sword, famine, and pestilence, so that they may recount all their abominations among the nations to which they shall go; and they shall know that I am the Lord.”

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, eat your bread in agitation, and drink your water in haste and sorrow [Al. ‘but’ omitted].

And you shall say to the people of the land:

Thus says the Lord God to those who dwell in Jerusalem, in the land of Israel:

‘They shall eat their bread in anxiety and drink their water in desolation, so that the land may be desolated of its multitude, because of the iniquity of all who dwell in it.

And the cities that are now inhabited shall be desolate, and the land shall be deserted; and you shall know that I am the Lord.’”

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, what is this proverb that you have in the land of Israel, saying:

‘The days will be prolonged, and every vision will come to nothing’?

Therefore say to them:

Thus says the Lord God:

I will put an end to this proverb, and it shall no longer be spoken as a common saying in Israel.

And say to them that the days and every word of the vision have drawn near.

For there shall no longer be any futile vision, nor ambiguous divination in the midst of the house of Israel.

For I, the Lord, will speak whatever word I speak, and it shall happen; it shall no longer be delayed.

But in your days, provoking house, I will speak the word and perform it,”

says the Lord God.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, behold, the house of Israel says:

‘The vision that he sees concerns many days, and he prophesies for distant times.’

Therefore say to them:

Thus says the Lord God:

None of my words shall be delayed any longer. The word that I speak shall be fulfilled,”

says the Lord God.

**[Chapter XIII]** And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who prophesy, and say to those who prophesy from their own hearts:

‘Hear the word of the Lord.’

Thus says the Lord God:

Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit and see nothing.

Your prophets, Israel, have become [Al. shall be] like foxes in the deserts.

You did not go up to the breach, nor did you build a wall for the house of Israel, so that you might stand in battle on the day of the Lord.

They see vanity and divine falsehood, saying, ‘The Lord says,’ when the Lord has not sent them; yet they persist in confirming the word.

Have you not seen a futile vision and spoken a lying divination, saying, ‘The Lord says,’ when I have not spoken?

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

Because you have spoken vanity and seen falsehood, therefore behold, I am against you,”

says the Lord God.

“And my hand shall be against the prophets who see vanity and divine falsehood. They shall not be in the council of my people, nor shall they be inscribed in the register of the house of Israel, nor shall they enter the land of Israel; and you shall know that I am the Lord God.

Because they have deceived my people, saying, ‘Peace,’ when there is no peace; while he was building a wall, they were plastering it with mud without straw.

[Col. 0955A] Say to those who plaster without tempering it that it shall fall. For there will be a flooding rain, and I will cause very large stones to descend upon it, and a storm wind will scatter it.

Behold, the wall has fallen. Will it not be said to you, ‘Where is the plaster with which you plastered it?’

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

I will release a tempestuous wind in my indignation, and there shall be a flooding rain in my fury, and great stones in anger for complete destruction.

And I will destroy the wall that you plastered without tempering it, and I will level it to the ground, and its foundation shall be exposed.

It shall fall and be consumed in its midst, and you shall know that I am the Lord.

And I will complete my indignation against the wall and against those who plaster it without tempering it, and I will say to you:

‘There is no wall, and there are none who plaster it’—

the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem and see a vision of peace for it, when there is no peace,”

says the Lord God.

“And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy from their own hearts. Prophesy against them and say:

Thus says the Lord God:

Woe to those who sew cushions under every elbow of the arm and make pillows beneath the head of people of every age, to capture souls.

When they captured the souls of my people, they made their souls live.

And they profaned me before my people for a handful of barley and a piece of bread, to kill souls that do not die and to make alive souls that do not live, by lying to my people who believe lies.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I am against your cushions, with which you capture flying souls, and I will tear them from your arms. I will release the souls that you capture, souls to fly away.

And I will tear apart your pillows, and I will rescue my people from your hand. They shall no longer be in your hands as prey, and you shall know that I am the Lord.

Because you have falsely grieved the heart of the righteous, whom I did not cause grief, and strengthened the hands of the wicked so that he would not turn from his evil way and live.

Therefore you shall no longer see vanity or divine divinations, and I will rescue my people from your hand; and you shall know that I am the Lord.”

**[Chapter XIV]** And the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, these men have placed their filth in their hearts and set the stumbling-block of their iniquity before their faces. Should I be consulted by them?

Therefore speak to them and say:

Thus says the Lord God:

Any man of the house of Israel who places his filth in his heart and sets the stumbling-block of his iniquity before his face [Al. adds: ‘for him’], and comes to the prophet, asking him to inquire of me:

[Note: [Col. 0955D] This brief passage, “asking me through him,” has been retained here from the old Latin version, apparently by Jerome himself. For in his commentary he also reads it first from the Hebrew as “asking him through me,” and then from the Septuagint as “that he may inquire of him in me.” Yet in this place it is found neither in the Hebrew nor, as far as I know, in any Greek manuscript of the Septuagint. It does occur once in both texts below, in its proper place, at verse 7: in the Hebrew, לדרוש אותו בי, “to inquire of him in me,” and likewise in the Greek, τοῦ ἐπερωτῆσαι αὐτὸν ἐν ἐμοὶ, “to inquire of him in me.” Jerome again renders it there somewhat differently, “that he may inquire through him of me.” The reason, therefore, why he inserts the same sentence here as well, although the original books unanimously omit it, is simply that he found it in the old Latin Vulgate; and, because of a preconceived opinion, he thought this version of the prophet sufficiently conformed to the Hebrew text, as he himself declares in the preface.]

I, the Lord, will answer him through the multitude of his impurities, so that the house of Israel may be caught in its own heart, by which they have departed from me through all their idols.

Therefore say to the house of Israel:

Thus says the Lord God:

Turn and withdraw from your idols, and turn your faces away from all your abominations.

For any man of the house of Israel, and of the resident aliens who reside in Israel, if he has become estranged from me, has placed his idols in his heart, has set the stumbling-block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to the prophet to inquire of me through him—

I, the Lord, will answer him through myself.

I will set my face against that man and make him an example and a proverb, and I will cut him off from the midst of my people; and you shall know that I am the Lord.

And if the prophet is led astray and speaks a word, I, the Lord, have led that prophet astray. I will stretch out my hand against him and wipe him out from the midst of my people Israel.

And they shall bear their iniquity. As the iniquity of the one who inquires is, so shall be the iniquity of the prophet,

[Col. 0956C] so that the house of Israel may no longer stray from me [Al. “no longer” omitted] and may not be defiled by all its transgressions.

Rather, they shall be my people, and I shall be their God,

says the Lord of hosts.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, when a land sins against me by committing a transgression, I will stretch out my hand over it [Al. ‘my hand’ omitted] and break its staff of bread. I will send famine upon it and destroy man and beast from it.

And if these three men were in its midst—Noah, Daniel, and Job—they would deliver their own souls by their righteousness,”

says the Lord of hosts.

“But if I also brought the most savage beasts upon the land to devastate it, and it became impassable because no one could pass through it on account of the beasts, and these three men were in it—

as I live, says the Lord God, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters; they alone would be delivered, but the land would be desolated.

Or if I brought the sword upon that land and said to the sword, ‘Pass through the land,’ and destroyed man and beast from it, and these three men were in its midst—

as I live, says the Lord God, they would not deliver sons or daughters; they alone would be delivered.

And if I also sent pestilence upon that land and poured out my indignation upon it in blood, to cut off from it man and beast, and Noah, Daniel, and Job were in its midst—

as I live, says the Lord God, they would deliver neither son nor daughter; they would deliver their own souls by their righteousness.

For thus says the Lord God:

Even if I send my four most severe judgments—sword, famine, evil beasts, and pestilence—against Jerusalem, to destroy from it man and beast,

[Col. 0957B] nevertheless a remnant shall be left in it, consisting of those who bring out sons and daughters.

Behold, they shall come out to you, and you shall see their way of life and their deeds, and you shall be comforted concerning the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, concerning all that I have brought upon it.

And they shall comfort you when you see their way of life and their deeds, and you shall know that I have not acted without cause in everything that I have done in it,”

says the Lord God.

**[Chapter XV]** And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, what will happen [Note: [Col. 0957D] The printed editions read, ‘what will happen to the wood of the vine’; however, the copies of the Canon and all manuscript codices read ‘wood of the vine,’ without any preposition. The Commentaries of Saint Jerome agree with this reading. MART.] to the wood of the vine [Al. ‘of the wood of the vine’] among all the woods of the forest, among the trees of the woodland?

Will a piece of wood be taken from it to make some work, or will a peg be fashioned from it on which to hang any vessel?

Behold, it has been given to the fire as fuel; the fire has consumed both its ends, and its middle has been reduced to ashes. Will it be useful for any work?

Even when it was whole, it was not suitable for work; how much less, when the fire has devoured and burned it, will anything made from it be useful?

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

As the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I gave to the fire to consume, so I have handed over [Al. will hand over] the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

And I will set my face against them. They shall go out from the fire, and the fire shall consume them.

And you shall know that I am the Lord, when I set my face against them and make the land impassable and desolate, because they have been transgressors,”

says the Lord God.

**[Chapter XVI]** And [Note: [Col. 0958D] Saint Jerome himself notes in Book IV of his Commentary on Ezekiel that the prophecy of this sixteenth chapter extends for nearly two hundred verses.] the word of the Lord came to me,

[Col. 0957D] saying:

“Son of man, make Jerusalem aware of her abominations, and say:

Thus says the Lord God to Jerusalem:

Your root and your origin are from the land of Canaan; your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite.

And when you were born, on the day of your birth, your navel was not cut, nor were you washed in water for purification, nor rubbed with salt, nor wrapped in swaddling clothes.

[Col. 0958A] No eye looked upon you with pity, to do any one of these things for you, out of compassion for you; rather, you were thrown upon the face of the earth in the rejection of your life, on the day you were born.

And as I passed by you, I saw you being trampled in your blood. And I said to you when you were in your blood: ‘Live.’ I said to you, I repeat: ‘Live in your blood.’

I made you numerous like a plant of the field; you multiplied, grew great, and entered into maturity. Your breasts became firm, your hair grew, but you were naked and full of shame.

And I passed by you and saw you, and behold, your time was the time of lovers.

And I spread my cloak over you and covered your nakedness. I swore an oath to you and entered into a covenant with you,

says the Lord God, and you became mine.

And I washed you with water and cleansed your blood from you, and anointed you with oil.

And I clothed you in embroidered garments and shod you with violet-colored leather; I girded you with fine linen and clothed you in delicate fabrics.

And I adorned you with ornaments, put bracelets on your hands, and a necklace around your neck.

And I put a pendant on your mouth, rings in your ears, and a crown of beauty on your head.

And you were adorned with gold and silver, clothed in fine linen, embroidered cloth, and many colors. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil; you became exceedingly beautiful and advanced to royal dignity.

And your name went out among the nations because of your beauty,

[Col. 0958C] for you were perfect in the beauty that I had placed upon you,

says the Lord God.

But trusting in your beauty, you played the prostitute, and you prostituted your name to every passerby, so that you became his.

And taking some of your garments, you made for yourself high places sewn together here and there, and you prostituted yourself upon them, as had never happened and never shall.

And you took the vessels of your adornment, made of my gold and my silver, which I had given you, and made for yourself male images, and prostituted yourself with them.

And you took your multicolored garments and covered them; you placed my oil and my incense before them.

And my bread, which I had given you—the fine flour, the oil, and the honey with which I had fed you—you placed before them as a pleasing aroma; and so it happened,

says the Lord God.

And you took your sons and daughters, whom you had borne to me, and sacrificed them to be devoured.

Was your prostitution a small matter?

You sacrificed my sons and gave them over, consecrating them to these idols.

And after all your abominations and your acts of prostitution, you did not remember the days of your youth,

[Col. 0959A] when you were naked and full of shame, trampled in your blood.

And it happened after all your wickedness—woe, woe to you, says the Lord God—that you built yourself a brothel and made yourself a place of prostitution in every square.

At every crossroads you built a sign of your prostitution, and you made your beauty abominable.

You spread your legs to every passerby and multiplied your acts of prostitution.

And you prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors, men of great flesh, and multiplied your prostitution in order to provoke me.

Behold, I will stretch out my hand against you [Al. “I stretched out”] and remove your rights, and I will give you over to the souls of the daughters of the Philistines who hate you, who are ashamed of your wicked way.

[Col. 0959B] And you prostituted yourself with the sons of Assyria, because you were not yet satisfied; and after prostituting yourself, you were still not satisfied.

And you multiplied your prostitution in the land of Canaan with the Chaldeans, and even then you were not satisfied.

With what shall I cleanse your heart,

says the Lord God,

when you do all these deeds of a prostitute and a shameless woman?

For you built your brothel at the head of every road and made your high place in every square; you did not become like a prostitute who increases the price out of disdain,

but like an adulterous woman who brings in strangers in place of her husband.

All prostitutes receive payment, but you gave payments to all your lovers and bribed them to come to you from every side to prostitute themselves with you.

[Col. 0959C] And it came about in you contrary to the custom of women in your acts of prostitution, and after you there shall be no prostitution.

For in that you gave payments and did not receive payments, the opposite happened in you.

Therefore, prostitute, hear the word of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord God:

Because your bronze has been poured out and your shame has been exposed in your acts of prostitution with your lovers and with all the idols of your abominations, in the blood of your sons whom you gave to them—

behold, I will gather all your lovers with whom you have mingled, and all those whom you loved, together with all those whom you hated.

I will gather them against you from every side and uncover your shame before them, and they shall see all your disgrace.

And I will judge you with the judgments of adulteresses and of those who shed blood, and I will give you over to bloodshed in fury and jealousy.

And I will give you into their hands, and they shall destroy your brothel and demolish your place of prostitution.

And they shall strip you of your garments and take away the vessels of your adornment, and leave you naked and full of shame.

And they shall bring a mob against you,

[Col. 0960A] stone you with stones, and slaughter you with their swords.

And they shall burn your houses with fire and execute judgments against you before the eyes of many women.

You shall cease from prostitution, and you shall no longer give payments.

And my indignation against you shall rest; my jealousy shall be taken away from you, and I shall be quiet and no longer angry.

Because you did not remember the days of your youth and provoked me in all these things,

therefore I too have brought your ways upon your head,”

says the Lord God.

“And I did not act according to your crimes in all your abominations.

Behold, everyone who commonly tells a proverb will apply this proverb to you, saying:

‘Like the mother, so is her daughter.’
