[Col. 0960B] You are the daughter of your mother, who rejected her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who rejected their husbands and their children.

Your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.

And your elder sister was Samaria, she and her daughters, who dwell to your left.

And your younger sister, who dwells to your right, was Sodom and her daughters.

Yet you did not walk in their ways, nor did you do even a little less according to their crimes; you became almost more criminal than they in all your ways.

As I live, says the Lord God, Sodom your sister and her daughters did not do what you and your daughters have done.

Behold, this was the iniquity of Sodom your sister: pride, fullness of bread, abundance, and leisure for her and her daughters; but they did not extend a hand to the needy and poor.

And they became arrogant and committed abominations before me, and I removed them, as I saw fit.

[Note: [Col. 0959D] Thus the Hebrew and the Canon of Saint-Germain read. All the other manuscript codices, together with the printed books, retain the second person, “you saw.” Either reading produces a true and appropriate sense. “I saw” should be referred to God, who removed the cities of Sodom and Samaria as it seemed right to him and as it pleased him. “You saw,” however, refers to the Jewish people, because they themselves witnessed the overthrow of the cities mentioned above. [Col. 0960D] The Vulgate, together with several manuscripts, has “you saw,” in disagreement with the Hebrew.]

And Samaria did not commit half of your sins; rather, you surpassed them in your crimes and justified your sisters by all your abominations that you committed.

Therefore you also bear your shame, because you surpassed your sisters by your sins, acting more wickedly than they; for they have been justified by comparison with you.

Therefore you too be ashamed and bear your disgrace, you who have justified your sisters.

And I will restore them, restoring Sodom and her daughters, and restoring Samaria and her daughters; and I will restore your return in their midst, so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all that you did while comforting them.



And your sister Sodom and her daughters shall return to their former state, and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former state, and you and your daughters shall return to your former state.

[Col. 0961A] Yet Sodom your sister was not heard from your mouth in the day of your pride, before your wickedness was revealed,

as at this time, when you are a reproach to the daughters of Syria and all the daughters of the Philistines around you, who surround you on every side.

You have borne your crime and your disgrace,

says the Lord God.

For thus says the Lord God:

I will deal with you as you dealt with the oath, to make the covenant void.

But I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth and raise up for you an everlasting covenant.

And you shall remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your sisters, those older than you [Al. with you] together with those younger than you.

And I will give them to you as daughters, but not by your covenant.

[Col. 0961B] And I will raise up my covenant with you [Al. “for you”], and you shall know that I am the Lord, so that you may remember and be ashamed and no longer dare open your mouth because of your shame, when I have been reconciled to you for all that you have done,

says the Lord God.”

**[Chapter XVII]** And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, propose a riddle and tell a parable to the house of Israel, and say:

Thus says the Lord God:

A great eagle, with large wings, long pinions, full of feathers and varied plumage, came to Lebanon and took the marrow of the cedar.

It plucked off the highest of its branches and carried it to the land of Canaan; it placed it in the city of merchants.

And it took some of the seed of the land and placed it in the ground as seed, so that it might establish its root over abundant waters; it placed it on the surface.

And when it had sprouted, it grew into a spreading vine of low stature, with its branches turned toward the eagle, while its roots were beneath it.

So it became a vine, produced branches, and sent out shoots.

And there was another great eagle, with large wings and many feathers.

And behold, this vine, as though sending its roots toward it, stretched its branches toward it, so that the eagle might water it from the beds of its planting.

It was planted in good soil beside abundant waters [Al. “he planted it”], so that it might produce foliage and bear fruit and become a great vine.

Say:

Thus says the Lord God:

Will it prosper?

Will he not tear out its roots and strip off its fruit, dry up all its budding branches, and make it wither?

And not by a great arm or by a numerous people will he uproot it from its roots?

Behold, it has been planted; will it prosper?

Will it not wither when the scorching wind touches it, and dry up in the beds of its growth?”

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Say to the provoking house:

‘Do you not know what these things mean?’

Say:

Behold, the king of Babylon comes to Jerusalem and will take its king and its princes and bring them to himself in Babylon.

And he will take some of the royal offspring and make a covenant with him, and receive an oath from him.

He will also take the strong men of the land, so that the kingdom may be humble and not exalt itself, but may keep his covenant and observe it.

But the one who turned away from him sent messengers to Egypt,

</source continues>
that he might furnish it with horses and a numerous people.

Will he prosper, or will he achieve deliverance, who has done these things? And will he who has broken the covenant escape?

As I live, says the Lord God: in the place of the king who made him king, whose oath he invalidated and whose covenant with him he broke, in the midst of Babylon he shall die.

[Col. 0962B] Nor will Pharaoh, with a great army or a numerous people, engage him in battle, by casting up a ramp and constructing siegeworks, in order to destroy many lives.

For he had despised the oath in order to break the covenant; and behold, he had given his hand. After doing all these things, he shall not escape.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

As I live, because he despised the oath that he rejected and violated the covenant, I will place it upon his head.

I will spread my net over him, and he shall be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon, and there I will judge him for the violation by which he despised me.

And all his fugitives, together with his entire army, shall fall by the sword; but those who remain shall be scattered to every wind. And you shall know that I, the Lord, have spoken.

[Col. 0962C] Thus says the Lord God:

I myself will take from the marrow of the lofty cedar and plant it; from the top of its branches I will pluck a tender shoot and plant it upon a high and prominent mountain.

On the lofty mountain of Israel I will plant it, and it will send forth a shoot and produce fruit, and it will become a great cedar. Under it all the birds will dwell, and every winged creature will nest beneath the shade of its foliage.

And all the trees of the region shall know that I, the Lord, have humbled the lofty tree and exalted [Alternative: raised] the lowly tree; I have dried up the green tree and made the dry tree sprout leaves. I, the Lord, have spoken and acted.

[Col. 0962D] **[Chapter XVIII]** And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“What is this proverb that you turn into a parable among yourselves in the land of Israel, saying:

‘The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children’s teeth are set on edge’ [Alternative: ‘were set on edge’]?

“As I live, says the Lord God, this proverb shall no longer be a proverb for you in Israel.

“Behold, all souls are mine: just as the soul of the father is mine, so also the soul of the son is mine. The soul that sins—it shall die.

“And if a man is righteous and practices judgment and righteousness; if he has not eaten upon the mountains, nor lifted his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel; if he has not violated his neighbor’s wife, nor approached a menstruating woman; if he has not grieved anyone; if he has returned the debtor’s pledge, taken nothing by force; if he has given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with clothing; if he has not lent at interest or taken more; if he has turned his hand away from iniquity and rendered true judgment between one man and another; if he has walked in my commandments and kept my ordinances, in order to act faithfully—he is righteous; he shall surely live, says the Lord God.

“But if he has begotten a son who is a robber and sheds blood, and does one of these things—while not doing all these things, but eating upon the mountains and defiling his neighbor’s wife; if he grieves the needy and poor, commits robberies, does not return the pledge, lifts his eyes to idols and commits abomination; if he lends at interest and takes more—will he live? He shall not live. Because he has done all these detestable things, he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him.

“But if he has begotten a son who sees all the sins of his father that he committed, and is afraid and does not act similarly [Alternative: ‘in a similar manner’; literally, ‘similarly to them’]; who has not eaten upon the mountains, nor lifted his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel; who has not violated his neighbor’s wife; who has not grieved anyone, has not retained a pledge, and has not committed robbery; who has given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with clothing; who has turned his hand away from injuring the poor; who has not taken interest or increase; who has practiced my ordinances and walked in my commandments—he shall not die for his father’s iniquity, but shall surely live.

“His father, because he slandered and used violence against his brother, and did evil among his people—behold, he is dead in his iniquity.

“And you say: ‘Why has the son not borne the father’s iniquity?’ Clearly, because the son practiced judgment and righteousness, kept all my commandments, and acted according to them—he shall surely live.

“And the soul that sins—it shall die. A son shall not bear the father’s iniquity, and a father shall not bear the son’s iniquity. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.

“But if the wicked person repents of all his sins that he has committed, and keeps all my commandments and practices judgment and righteousness, he shall surely live; he shall not die. None of all his iniquities that he has committed shall be remembered; because of the righteousness that he has practiced, he shall live.

“Is my desire the death of the wicked, says the Lord God, and not rather that he turn from his ways and live?

“But if the righteous person turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity according to all the abominations that the wicked habitually commits, shall he live? None of all his righteous deeds that he had done shall be remembered [Alternative: ‘shall be in remembrance’]. In the violation by which he violated the covenant and in the sin that he committed—in these he shall die.

“And you said: ‘The way of the Lord is not fair.’

“Therefore hear, house of Israel: Is my way not fair, and are not your ways rather crooked?

“For when the righteous person turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, he shall die because of them; for the injustice that he has committed, he shall die.

“And when the wicked person turns away from his wickedness that he has committed and practices judgment and righteousness, he shall preserve his life.

“For when he considers and turns away from all his iniquities that he has committed, he shall surely live and shall not die.

“And the children of Israel say: ‘The way of the Lord is not fair.’

“Are my ways not fair, house of Israel, and are not your ways rather crooked?

“Therefore I will judge each of you according to your ways, house of Israel, says the Lord God.

“Turn and repent of all your iniquities, and iniquity shall not become your ruin.

[Col. 0964C] “Cast away from yourselves all your violations by which you have violated the covenant, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, house of Israel?

“For I do not desire the death of the one who dies, says the Lord God. Return and live.”

**[Chapter XIX]** And you [Note: [Col. 0963D] In copies of the Canon, “And you, son of man,” a reading retained by the Syriac and Arabic. The Hebrew, however, the Commentaries of Saint Jerome, and three very ancient manuscript codices of the sacred Scriptures read nothing further [Col. 0964D] than what is presented here. MART.], take up a lament over the princes of Israel and say:

“Why did your mother, a lioness, lie down among lions and raise her cubs in the midst of young lions?

“And she brought up one of her cubs; he became a lion and learned to seize prey and devour human beings.

“And the nations heard about him, and they seized him—not without wounding him—and brought him in chains to the land of Egypt.

“When she saw that she had become weak and that her expectation had perished, she took one of her cubs and made him a lion.

[Col. 0964D] “He moved among lions and became a lion; he learned to seize prey and devour human beings. He learned to make widows and to turn their cities into a desert. The land and its fullness became desolate at the sound of his roaring.

“And nations gathered against him from every side, from the provinces, and they spread their net over him; he was caught in their wounds.

“And they put him in a cage [Note: The Palatine manuscript and others in Martianay’s possession read, more closely following the Hebrew, ‘in a cage in chains, and they brought him,’ and so forth.], and in chains they brought him to the king of Babylon.

[Col. 0965A] “They put him in prison, so that his voice might no longer be heard upon the mountains of Israel.

“Your mother was like a vine, planted by the waters in your blood; its fruit and its branches grew from abundant waters.

“And strong rods grew from it, fit for the scepters of rulers; its stature rose among the branches, and it saw its height amid the multitude of its tendrils.

“But it was uprooted in anger and thrown to the ground, and the scorching wind dried up its fruit. Its rods of strength withered and dried up; fire consumed it.

“And now it has been transplanted into the desert, into a dry and thirsty land.

“And fire went out from the rod of its branches and consumed its fruit. It had no strong rod, no scepter [Note: The San-Germain Canon and the Corbie manuscript, in the first hand, read ‘a scepter of rulers.’] for rulers.

“It is a lament, and it shall be a lament.”

**[Chapter XX]** And it came to pass in the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, that men came from the elders of Israel to inquire of the Lord, and they sat before me.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and say to them:

“Thus says the Lord God: Have you come to inquire of me? As I live, says the Lord God, I will not answer you.

“If you judge them—if you judge, son of man—show them the abominations of their fathers [Alternative: ‘of themselves’].

“And say to them:

[Col. 0965C] “Thus says the Lord God:

“On the day when I chose Israel, I lifted my hand in favor of the offspring of the house of Jacob, and I revealed myself to them in the land of Egypt. I lifted my hand in their favor, saying: ‘I am the Lord your God.’

“On that day I lifted my hand in their favor, to bring them out of the land of Egypt into the land that I had provided for them, flowing with milk and honey; it is excellent among all lands.

“And I said to them: ‘Let each person cast away the offenses of his eyes, and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.’

“But they provoked me and refused to listen to me. Each person did not cast away the abominations of his eyes, nor did they abandon the idols of Egypt. And I said that I would pour out my indignation upon them and complete my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt.

“But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned before the nations in whose midst they were, and among whom I had revealed myself to them in order to bring them out of the land of Egypt.

“So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the desert.

“And I gave them my commandments and showed them my ordinances, which, if a person does them, he shall live by them.

“Moreover, I gave them my Sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, so that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them.

“But the house of Israel provoked me in the desert; they did not walk in my commandments,

[Col. 0966A] and they rejected my ordinances, which, if a person does them, he shall live by them; and they greatly profaned my Sabbaths.

“So I said that I would pour out my fury upon them in the desert and consume them.

“But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned before the nations from whose sight I had brought them out.

“Therefore I also lifted my hand against them in the desert, not to bring them [Alternative: ‘lead them out’] into the land that I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, the choicest of all lands, because they rejected my ordinances, did not walk in my commandments, and profaned my Sabbaths. For their heart went after idols.

“Yet my eye spared them, so that I would not kill them; I did not consume them in the desert.

“Then I said to their children in the wilderness: ‘Do not walk in the commandments of your fathers, nor keep their ordinances, nor defile yourselves with their idols.

“‘I am the Lord your God. Walk in my commandments, keep my ordinances and perform them. Sanctify my Sabbaths, so that they may be a sign between me and you, and so that you may know [Alternative: ‘it may be known’] that I am the Lord your God.’

“But the children provoked me; they did not walk in my commandments, nor did they keep my ordinances in order to perform them—although when a person performs them, he shall live by them—and they profaned my Sabbaths.

“So I threatened to pour out my fury upon them and complete my anger against them in the desert. But I turned my hand away,

[Col. 0966C] and acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned before the nations from whose sight I had brought them out.

“Again I lifted my hand against them in the wilderness, to scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands, because they had not performed my ordinances, had rejected my commandments, profaned my Sabbaths, and kept their eyes fixed upon the idols of their fathers.

“So I also gave them commandments that were not good and ordinances by which they would not live.

“And I defiled them through their gifts, when they offered every firstborn, everything that opens the womb, because of their transgressions; and they shall know that I am the Lord.

“Therefore speak to the house of Israel, son of man, and say to them:

“Thus says the Lord God: Even in this your fathers again blasphemed me when they rejected me with contempt.

“And when I had brought them into the land over which I had lifted my hand, intending to give it to them, they saw every high hill and every leafy tree, and there they sacrificed their victims. There they presented the provocation of their offering, there they placed the fragrance of their pleasing sacrifice, and there they poured out their libations [Alternative: add ‘there’].

“And I said to them: ‘What is this high place to which you are entering?’ And its name was called ‘High Place’ to this day.

“Therefore say to the house of Israel:

“Thus says the Lord God: Surely you defile yourselves in the way of your fathers and commit fornication after their offenses.

[Col. 0967A] “And in the offering of your gifts, when you lead your children through the fire, you defile yourselves with all your idols to this day.

“And shall I answer you, house of Israel? As I live, says the Lord God, I will not answer you.

“Nor shall the thought of your mind come to pass, when you say: ‘We shall be like the nations and like the families of the lands, serving wood and stone.’

“As I live, says the Lord God, I will reign over you with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and poured-out fury.

“I will lead you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands in which you have been scattered. With a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and poured-out fury I will reign over you.

“And I will bring you into the desert of the peoples, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face.

“Just as I entered into judgment with your fathers in the desert of the land of Egypt, so I will judge you, says the Lord God.

“And I will subject you to my scepter and bring you into the bonds of the covenant.

“I will select from among you the transgressors and the wicked, and I will bring them out from the land of their sojourn; but they shall not enter the land of Israel. And you shall know that I am the Lord.

“And you, house of Israel—thus says the Lord God—each of you, go after your idols and serve them. But if even in this you will not listen to me, and you continue to profane my holy name through your gifts and your idols:

“On my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord God, there the entire house of Israel shall serve me;

[Col. 0967C] all of them, I say, in the land in which they shall please me. There I will seek your firstfruits and the beginning of your tithes, together with all your holy offerings.

“I will receive you as a pleasing fragrance when I bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands into which you have been scattered, and I will be sanctified in you before the nations.

“And you shall know that I am the Lord when I bring you into the land of Israel, into the land for which I lifted my hand, intending to give it to your fathers.

“And there you shall remember your ways and all your crimes by which you defiled yourselves, and you shall be displeased with yourselves in your own sight because of all your evil deeds that you committed.

“And you shall know that I am the Lord when I deal well with you for the sake of my name, and not according to your evil ways or your worst crimes, house of Israel, says the Lord God.”

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, set your face toward the way of the south, and drip your words toward the south, and prophesy against the forest of the southern country.

“And say to the southern forest: ‘Hear the word of the Lord:

“‘Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am going to kindle a fire in you, and I will consume in you every green tree and every dry tree. The blazing flame shall not be extinguished, and every face from south to north shall be burned by it.

“‘And all flesh shall see that I, the Lord, have kindled it; it shall not be extinguished.’”

[Col. 0968A] And I said:

“Ah, ah, Lord God! They are saying of me: ‘Does he not speak in parables?’”

**[Chapter XXI]** And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem, drip your words toward the sanctuaries, and prophesy against the soil of Israel.

“And say to the land of Israel:

“Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, and I will draw my sword from its sheath and kill in you the righteous and the wicked.

“But because you have killed the righteous and the wicked within you, therefore my sword shall go out from its sheath against all flesh from south to north, so that all flesh may know that I, the Lord, have drawn my sword from its sheath; it shall not return.

[Col. 0968B] “And you, son of man, groan with breaking in your loins, and groan in bitterness before them.

“And when they say to you, ‘Why are you groaning?’ you shall say: ‘Because of the report—for it is coming.’

“And every heart shall melt, all hands shall go limp, every spirit shall fail, and water shall run down every knee.

“Behold, it is coming, and it shall happen, says the Lord God” [Alternative: omit “God”].

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, prophesy and say:

“Thus says the Lord God:

“Speak:

“‘A sword, a sword is sharpened and polished.

[Col. 0968C] “It is sharpened to slaughter victims; it is polished to flash.

“‘You who move the scepter of my son, you have cut down every tree.

“And I gave it to be polished, so that it might be held in the hand. This is a sharpened sword, and this is a polished sword, to be in the hand of the slayer.

“Cry out and howl, son of man, because this has happened to my people, to all the leaders of Israel who had fled. They have been delivered over to the sword together with my people. Therefore strike your thigh, for it has been tested; and this is so when it overturns the scepter and it shall no longer exist, says the Lord God.

“You, therefore, son of man, prophesy and strike hand against hand, and let the sword be doubled and tripled—the sword of the slain.

“This is the sword of the great slaughter, which makes them stunned, causes their hearts to waste away, and multiplies ruins.

[Col. 0968D] “I have appointed at all their gates the confusion of the sharp and polished sword, prepared to flash and armed for slaughter.

“Sharpen yourself; go to the right or to the left, wherever the desire of your face directs you.

“Indeed, I too will strike hand against hand and satisfy my indignation. I, the Lord, have spoken.”

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“And you, son of man, mark out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to come. From one land both shall issue, and by hand he shall cast a lot; at the head of the road to the city he shall cast it.

“Mark out a road for the sword to come against Rabbah of the Ammonites and against Judah, and against [Alternative: ‘and against’] fortified Jerusalem.

[Col. 0969A] “For the king of Babylon stood at the fork, at the head of the two roads, seeking an omen, mixing arrows. He questioned the idols and consulted the entrails.

“At his right hand the divination was made for Jerusalem: to set up battering rams, to open the mouth for slaughter, to raise the voice in a howl, to set up battering rams against the gates, to heap up a ramp, and to build fortifications.

“And it will be like consulting an oracle in vain in their eyes, and like imitating the repose of Sabbaths. But he will remember iniquity for the purpose of capture.

“Therefore thus says the Lord God:

“Because you have remembered your iniquity and exposed your violations, and your sins have appeared in all your thoughts—because, I say, you have remembered them, you shall be seized by the hand.

“But you, profane and wicked prince of Israel, whose day has come at the appointed time of iniquity:

“Thus says the Lord God:

“Remove the turban; take off the crown. Is this not the thing that has raised up the lowly and humbled the lofty?

“I will make it iniquity, iniquity, iniquity; and this has not yet happened until he comes [Alternative: ‘until it happens and he comes’] to whom judgment belongs, and I shall hand it over to him.

“And you, son of man, prophesy and say:

“Thus says the Lord God concerning the children of Ammon, and concerning their reproach; and say:

“‘Sword, sword, draw yourself for slaughter; polish yourself, so that you may kill and flash,

[Col. 0969C] while they regarded you as futile and divined lies [Note: In this place the sacred text of the San-Germain Canon has the following scholion sewn into it: ‘It is not the divination of demons, but the judgment of God, who has given an end to perfected wickedness. From this saying comes: “It is not ours to divine.”’ MART.],

“to place you upon the necks of the wounded wicked, whose day has come at the appointed time of iniquity.

“Return to your sheath, in the place where you were created. In the land of your birth I will judge you, and I will pour out my indignation upon you.

“In the fire of my fury I will blow upon you, and I will deliver you into the hands of foolish men [Alternative: ‘stupid men’] and craftsmen of destruction [Alternative: ‘corruption’].

“You shall be food for fire; your blood shall be in the midst of the land; you shall be handed over to oblivion. For I, the Lord, have spoken.”

**[Chapter XXII]** And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“And you, son of man, will you judge—will you judge—the city of bloodshed?

[Col. 0969D] And you shall show it all its abominations and say:

“Thus says the Lord God:

“City that sheds blood in its midst, so that its time may come, and that has made idols against itself, so that it might be defiled:

“You have sinned through your blood that you have shed, and you have been defiled through your idols that you have made.

“You have brought your days near and brought on the time of your years. Therefore I have given you as a reproach to the nations and as a mockery to all lands.

[Col. 0970A] “Those nearby and those far from you shall triumph over you—filthy, infamous, great in destruction.

“Behold, the princes of Israel, each relying on his own arm, have been within you for the shedding of blood.

“They dishonored father and mother within you; they oppressed the resident alien in your midst; they grieved the orphan and the widow among you.

“You despised my sanctuaries [Alternative: ‘you despised’; alternative: ‘you polluted’], and you profaned my Sabbaths.

“Slanderers were within you, for the shedding of blood; they ate upon the mountains within you and committed wickedness in your midst.

“They uncovered the nakedness of their father within you; they humbled the impurity of a menstruating woman within you.

“Each man committed abomination with his neighbor’s wife; the father-in-law defiled his daughter-in-law disgracefully; the brother oppressed his sister, his father’s daughter, within you.

“They accepted gifts among you for the shedding of blood. You took interest and increase, and you greedily oppressed your neighbors; and you forgot me, says the Lord God.

“Behold, I have clapped my hands over your greed that you have practiced and over the blood that has been shed in your midst.

“Will your heart endure, or will your hands prevail, in the days that I will bring upon you? I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will act.

“I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you throughout the lands, and I will remove your impurity from you.

“And I will take possession of you in the sight of the nations, and you shall know that I am the Lord.”

[Col. 0970C] And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me. All these—copper, tin, iron, lead—are in the midst of the furnace; they have become silver dross.

“Therefore thus says the Lord God:

“Because you have all become dross, behold, I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem, as one gathers silver, copper, iron, tin, and lead into the midst of a furnace, in order to kindle a fire in it for melting.

“Thus I will gather you in my fury and in my anger, and I will rest; and I will melt you.

“I will gather you and kindle you in the fire of my fury, and you shall be melted in its midst.

[Col. 0970D] “As silver is melted in the midst of a furnace, so you shall be in its midst; and you shall know that I am the Lord when I have poured out my indignation upon you.”

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, say to it:

“You are an unclean land, not rained upon in the day of fury.

“The conspiracy of its prophets is in its midst, like a roaring lion that seizes prey. They devoured lives, took wealth and payment, and multiplied its widows in its midst.

[Col. 0971A] “Its priests despised my law and polluted my sanctuaries. They made no distinction between holy and profane; they did not discern between polluted and clean; they turned their eyes away from my Sabbaths, and I was profaned in their midst.

“Its princes were in its midst like wolves seizing prey, to shed blood, destroy lives, and greedily pursue profits.

“But its prophets plastered them without restraint, seeing vain things and divining lies for them, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord God,’ when the Lord had not spoken.

“The people of the land practiced oppression and committed robbery. They afflicted the needy and poor and oppressed the resident alien with slander, without justice.

“And I sought among them a man who would set up a hedge and stand opposed before me on behalf of the land, so that I would not destroy it; but I found none.

“So I poured out my indignation upon them; I consumed them in the fire of my wrath. I returned their way upon their own head, says the Lord God.”

**[Chapter XXIII]** And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother, and they committed fornication in Egypt; they committed fornication in their youth.

“There their breasts were pressed, and the breasts of their maidenhood were handled.

“Their names were Oholah, the elder, and Oholibah, her sister;

[Col. 0971C] and I took them, and they bore sons and daughters. Their names were Samaria—Oholah—and Jerusalem—Oholibah.

“Oholah committed fornication against me and became infatuated with her lovers, the Assyrians who approached her [Alternative: add ‘her’], dressed in violet, princes and officials, young men of desire, all of them horsemen and riders.

“And she bestowed her fornications upon all the chosen sons of Assyria, and with all those with whom she had become infatuated she defiled herself through their impurities.

“Moreover, she did not abandon her fornications, which she had practiced in Egypt; for they had lain with her in her youth, and they had handled the breasts of her maidenhood and poured out their fornication upon her.

[Col. 0971D] “Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the sons of Assyria, after whom she had lusted.

“They uncovered her shame; they took her sons and daughters, and they killed her herself with the sword. And she became notorious among women, and they executed judgments upon her.

“When her sister Oholibah saw this, she became even more infatuated with lust than she. And she shamelessly offered her fornication after her sister’s fornication to the sons of Assyria, to the leaders and officials who came to her, dressed in varied clothing, horsemen riding horses, all of them young men of exceptional beauty.

“And I saw that the way of both of them was defiled.

“And she increased her fornications:

[Col. 0972A] when she saw men portrayed upon the wall, images of Chaldeans depicted in colors, girded about the loins with belts, with dyed turbans upon their heads, the appearance of commanders—all of them resembling the sons of Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans in which they were born—

“she became infatuated with them through the desire of her eyes and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.

“When the sons of Babylon came to her, to the bed of her breasts, they defiled her with their acts of fornication; she was defiled by them, and her soul was filled with them.

“She exposed her fornications and uncovered her shame, and my soul withdrew from her, just as my soul had withdrawn from her sister.

“For she multiplied her fornications,

[Col. 0972B] remembering the days of her youth, when she committed fornication in the land of Egypt.

“And she became infatuated with lust for their intercourse, whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys and whose emission is like the emission of horses.

“And you revisited the wickedness of your youth, when your breasts were pressed in Egypt and the breasts of your maidenhood were handled.

“Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord God:

“Behold, I will stir up against you all your lovers, of whom your soul was satisfied, and I will gather them around you:

“the sons of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, nobles, tyrants, and princes; all the sons of Assyria, young men of exceptional beauty, all the leaders and officials, princes of princes, and renowned horsemen.

“And they shall come against you equipped with chariot and wheel, a multitude of peoples. They shall arm themselves against you on every side with breastplate, shield, and helmet.

[Col. 0972C] “And I will set judgment before them [Alternative: omit ‘before them’], and they shall judge you by their judgments.

“And I will set my jealousy against you, which they will exercise against you in fury. They shall cut off your nose and your ears, and what remains of you they shall cut down with the sword.

“They themselves shall seize your sons and daughters, and your remnant shall be devoured by fire.

“They shall strip you of your clothing and take away the vessels of your glory.

“And I will remove your wickedness from you, and your fornication from the land of Egypt. You shall not lift your eyes toward them, and you shall no longer remember Egypt.

“For thus says the Lord God:

“Behold, I will deliver you into the hands of those whom you hate, into the hands of those of whom your soul was satisfied.

“And they shall deal with you in hatred; they shall take away all your labors and leave you naked and full of shame.

“And the shame of your fornications, your wickedness and your fornications, shall be exposed.

“They have done these things to you because you committed fornication after the nations among whom you were defiled by their idols.

“You walked in the way of your sister, and I will place her cup in your hand.

“Thus says the Lord God:

“You shall drink the deep and broad cup of your sister. You shall become an object of derision and mockery, for it is very capacious.

“You shall be filled with drunkenness and grief, with a cup of mourning and sadness, the cup of your sister Samaria.

“And you shall drink it and drain it to the dregs,

[Col. 0973A] and you shall devour its fragments, and tear your breasts; for I have spoken, says the Lord God” [Alternative: omit “God”].

“Therefore thus says the Lord God:

“Because you have forgotten me and cast me behind your body, you too shall bear your wickedness and your fornications.”

And the Lord said to me:

“Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah and announce their wickedness to them?

“For they have committed adultery, and blood is upon their hands, and they have committed fornication with their idols.

“Moreover, they offered their sons, whom they had borne for me, to them as food.

“But they also did this to me: they polluted my sanctuary on that day,

[Col. 0973B] and they profaned my Sabbaths.

“When they sacrificed their sons to their idols and entered my sanctuary on that day to pollute it, they did these things even within my house.

“They sent to men coming from far away, to whom they had sent a messenger [Note: In the Canon manuscripts and in the Colbertine, Anician, and Corbie no. 1 manuscripts, we read ‘messengers.’ Saint Jerome has the same reading in his exposition of this passage. [Col. 0974D] See Book VII of the Commentary. MART.].

“And behold, they came; you washed yourself for them and painted your eyes with antimony [Note: The word ‘with antimony’ is found neither in the Hebrew nor in the Holy Father’s commentary.], and you adorned yourself with feminine ornaments.

“You sat upon a very beautiful bed, and a table was arranged before it; you placed my incense and my oil upon it.

“And the sound of an exultant multitude was in it; and among the men who were brought in from the multitude of people and who came from the desert, they placed bracelets upon their hands and beautiful crowns upon their heads.

[Col. 0973C] “And I said to her who was worn out by adulteries: ‘Now this woman too will commit fornication in her fornication.’

“And they entered her as one enters a prostitute. Thus they entered Oholah and Oholibah, wicked women.

“Therefore these men [Alternative: omit ‘these men’] are righteous; they shall judge them with the judgment of adulteresses and with the judgment of women who shed blood.

“For they are adulteresses, and blood is upon their hands.

“For thus says the Lord God:

“Bring up a multitude against them and hand them over to tumult and plunder.

“And they shall be stoned with the stones of the peoples and pierced with their swords. They shall kill their sons and daughters, and burn their houses with fire.

“And I will remove wickedness from the land, and all women shall learn not to act according to their wickedness.

[Col. 0973D] “And they shall place your wickedness upon you, and you shall bear the sins of your idols; and you shall know that I am the Lord God.”

**[Chapter XXIV]** And the word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, saying:

“Son of man, write down for yourself the name of this day, on which the king of Babylon established himself against Jerusalem, on this very day.

“And speak by way of a proverb to the rebellious house a parable, and say to them:

[Col. 0974A] “Thus says the Lord God:

“Set the pot.

Put it, I say, and pour water into it.

Pile its pieces into it, every good piece, thigh and shoulder, choice meat and pieces full of bone.

Take the fattest of the flock, and also arrange a pile of bones beneath it. Let its boiling become fierce, and let its bones be thoroughly cooked in its midst.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

Woe to the city of bloodshed, the pot whose rust is in it and whose rust has not gone out of it. Bring it out piece by piece; no lot has fallen upon it.

For its blood is in its midst; she poured it upon the clearest rock and did not pour it upon the ground, so that it might be covered with dust. [Col. 0974B]

That I might bring my indignation upon it and take vengeance in retribution, I set its blood upon the clearest rock, so that it might not be covered.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

Woe to the city of bloodshed, whose great pyre I shall make.

Heap up the bones that I shall burn in the fire. The flesh shall be consumed, the whole composition shall be boiled, and the bones shall be charred.

Set it also upon the coals empty, so that it may grow hot and its bronze may melt; let its uncleanness be liquefied in its midst [the variant omits “its”], and let its rust be consumed.

It has been sweated over with great labor, yet its excessive rust has not gone out, not even through the fire. [Col. 0974C]

Your filth is accursed: because I wished to cleanse you, but you were not cleansed from your impurities. Nor will you be cleansed beforehand, until I cause my indignation to rest upon you.

I, the Lord, have spoken. It has come, and I shall act; I shall not pass over it, nor spare, nor be appeased. According to your ways and according to your devices I shall judge you [the variant: “I have judged you”], says the Lord.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, behold, I am taking away from you the object dear to your eyes by a plague; but you shall not mourn, nor shall you weep, and your tears shall not flow.

Groan in silence; you shall not perform the mourning of the dead. Let your crown remain bound upon you, [Col. 0974D] and your sandals shall be on your feet. You shall not veil your face with a covering, nor eat the food of mourners.

So I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening. In the morning he did as he had commanded me [the variant: “and I did”].

And the people said to me:

“Will you not tell us what these things mean that you are doing?”

And I said to them:

“The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

‘Speak to the house of Israel:

Thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I am profaning my sanctuary, the pride of your dominion, the object dear to your eyes, and that upon which your soul trembles. Your sons and your daughters whom you have left behind shall fall by the sword. [Col. 0975A]

And you shall do as I have done: you shall not veil your faces with a covering, and you shall not eat the food of mourners.

You shall have your crowns upon your heads and your sandals upon your feet. You shall not mourn or weep, but you shall waste away in your iniquities, and each one shall groan toward his brother.

Ezekiel shall be a sign for you. According to everything he has done, so shall you do when this comes; and you shall know that I am the Lord God.’

And you, son of man, behold, on the day when I take away from them their strength, [Col. 0975B] the joy of their dignity, the desire of their eyes, and that upon which their souls rest—their sons and daughters—

on that day a fugitive shall come to you to report it to you. On that day your mouth shall be opened together with that of the fugitive; you shall speak and no longer remain silent. You shall be a sign to them, and they shall know that I am the Lord.”

## Chapter XXV

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, set your face against the sons of Ammon, and prophesy concerning them.

And you shall say to the sons of Ammon:

“Hear the word of the Lord God.

Thus says the Lord God:

Because you said, ‘Aha, aha!’ over my sanctuary, because it has been profaned; over the land of Israel, because it has been desolated; and over the house of Judah, because they have gone into captivity— [Col. 0975C]

therefore I shall give you to the sons of the East as a possession. They shall establish their sheepfolds in you and set up their tents in you; they shall eat your produce, and they shall drink your milk [the variant omits “your”].

I shall make Rabbah a dwelling-place for camels and the sons of Ammon a resting-place for flocks; and you shall know that I am the Lord.

For thus says the Lord God:

Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet, and rejoiced with all your heart over the land of Israel, therefore behold, I shall stretch out my hand against you and give you as plunder to the nations. I shall cut you off from the peoples, destroy you from the lands, and annihilate you; and you shall know that I am the Lord.”

Thus says the Lord God:

Because Moab and Seir said, “Behold, the house of Judah is like all the nations,” therefore behold, I shall open the shoulder of Moab—from its cities, I say, from its cities and from its borders—the renowned land of Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim, [Col. 0975D] and I shall give it to the sons of the East, together with the sons of Ammon, as a possession,

so that the sons of Ammon may no longer be remembered among the nations. And I shall execute judgments upon Moab, and they shall know that I am the Lord.

Thus says the Lord God:

Because Edom took vengeance, seeking retribution for itself against the sons of Judah, and sinned by transgressing and demanded vengeance against them,

therefore thus says the Lord God:

I shall stretch out my hand against Edom and remove from it human being and beast. I shall make it desolate from the south, and those who are in Dedan [the variant: “those who are absent”] shall fall by the sword.

I shall execute my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel. They shall act in Edom according to my anger and my fury, and they shall know my vengeance [the variant: “my indignation”], says the Lord God. [Col. 0976A]

Thus says the Lord God:

Because the Philistines acted in vengeance and took revenge with all their heart, killing and perpetuating ancient hostilities,

therefore thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I shall stretch out my hand against the Philistines and destroy the destroyers; I shall annihilate the remnant of the coastal region.

I shall execute great acts of vengeance upon them, reproving them in fury; and they shall know that I am the Lord when I have taken my vengeance upon them.

## Chapter XXVI

And it came to pass in the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, because Tyre said concerning Jerusalem, “Aha! The gates of the peoples are broken; she has turned toward me; I shall be filled, for she has been desolated,”

therefore thus says the Lord God: [Col. 0976C]

“Behold, I am against you, Tyre. I shall bring up against you many nations, as the sea brings up its waves.

They shall destroy the walls of Tyre and demolish its towers. I shall scrape away its dust from it and make it a clearest rock.

It shall be a drying-place for nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken,” says the Lord God. “And it shall become plunder for the nations.

Its daughter-towns in the countryside shall be killed by the sword, and they shall know that I am the Lord.

For thus says the Lord God [the variant omits “God”]:

Behold, I shall bring against Tyre Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, from the north, king of kings, with horses, chariots, cavalry, and a great assembly and multitude.

He shall kill your daughter-towns in the countryside with the sword. He shall surround you with fortifications, pile up a siege ramp around you, [Col. 0976D] and raise a shield against you.

And he shall set up siege-engines [Note: Because ancient scribes did not understand the word *vineas*, “siege-engines,” they changed it in several manuscripts to *lineas*, “lines.” A *vinea* is a military device beneath which besiegers fight more safely to undermine the walls of a city. MART.] and adjust battering-rams against your walls, and he shall destroy your towers with his weapons.

The dust raised by his horses shall cover you in an inundation. Your walls shall shake at the sound of cavalry, wheels, and chariots, when he enters your gates as one enters a breached city.

With the hooves of his horses he shall trample all your streets. He shall strike your people with the sword, and your noble statues shall fall to the ground. [Col. 0977A]

They shall plunder your wealth and seize your merchandise. They shall demolish your walls and overthrow your splendid houses. Your stones, your timber, and your dust they shall cast into the midst of the waters.

I shall put an end to the multitude of your songs, and the sound of your lyres shall no longer be heard.

I shall make you a clearest rock; you shall be a drying-place for nets. You shall never again be rebuilt, for I have spoken,” says the Lord God.

Thus says the Lord God to Tyre:

“Will not the islands be shaken at the sound of your ruin and the groaning of your slain, when those killed have fallen in your midst?

All the princes of the sea shall descend from their thrones. [Col. 0977B] They shall remove their robes, strip off their embroidered garments, and clothe themselves with terror. They shall sit upon the ground and, stunned, gaze in astonishment at your sudden downfall.

They shall take up a lament over you and say to you:

‘How you have perished, you who dwell upon the sea, renowned city, which was strong upon the sea with your inhabitants, whom all feared!

Now the ships shall be terrified on the day of your dread, and the islands in the sea shall be troubled, because no one goes out from you.

For thus says the Lord God [the variant omits “God”]:

When I make you a desolate city, like cities that are not inhabited, and bring the abyss up over you, and many waters cover you, [Col. 0977C]

and drag you down with those who descend into the pit, to the everlasting people, and place you in the land below, like ancient desolations, with those who are brought down into the pit, so that you may not be inhabited;

and when I bestow glory in the land of the living,

I shall reduce you to nothing, and you shall not exist. You shall be sought, but you shall not be found again forever,’” says the Lord God.

## Chapter XXVII

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

You, therefore, son of man, take up a lament over Tyre.

And say to Tyre, which dwells at the entrance of the sea, the merchant of the peoples toward many islands:

Thus says the Lord God:

“O Tyre, you have said, ‘I am perfect in beauty and situated in the heart of the sea.’

Your neighbors, who built you up, filled out your beauty [Note: The Hebrew has a term that properly means “your builders.” If pointed differently, it can be rendered quite suitably as “your sons,” which is the reading preferred by the Septuagint, υἱοί σου, “your sons.” Jerome, who translated it as “neighbors,” is said to have wished to preserve both readings; but how they understand this, I do not see. For even if we somehow compare sons with neighbors, that term is extraordinarily far removed from anything connected with building. I believe this to be the old Latin reading that the Holy Father judged worth retaining. The celebrated Greek manuscript of the Paris Jesuits, cited by Montfaucon in his *Hexapla*, also gives under an asterisk οἱ ὅμοροι, “those bordering on you,” or “neighbors.” MART.].

They built you with firs from Senir, with all the planking [Note: In Hebrew it is expressed by a single word meaning “double,” namely, boards. Jerome, not without learning, divided that word into two and read “boards of the sea,” without any alteration of the letters. MART.] of the sea.

They took cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.

They shaped oaks from Bashan into your oars. They made your benches for you of Indian ivory, and your deckhouses from the islands of Italy.

Embroidered fine linen from Egypt was woven for you as a sail, to be placed upon your mast.

Violet and purple from the islands of Elishah became your covering.

The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad [Hebrew: Arvad] were your rowers. Your wise men, Tyre, became your pilots.

The elders of Byblos and its wise men supplied sailors for the service of your varied equipment [Note: All the biblical manuscripts we examined, without exception, read this way. They differ only in the verb “supplied,” since many retain the corrupt reading “had.” In all the manuscript copies of St. Jerome’s *Commentary on Ezekiel* we likewise find: “The elders of Byblos and its wise men supplied sailors,” and so forth. It is astonishing that learned men were so mistaken here that, on account of the present Hebrew *ziqne gebal*, “the elders of Byblos,” they supposed that in the books of the Septuagint Βιβλίων, “of books,” was read through scribal error instead of Γιβλίων, “of Byblos”; and that the Gebalites now mentioned by the prophet were clever architects celebrated for building Solomon’s Temple. Scripture itself refutes this: in this passage the subject is sailors and ships, not buildings and architects. The Byblians, therefore, or Biblians, supplied Tyre with highly skilled sailors for caulking ships, as the literal Hebrew indicates; in French we say, *pour calfater les vaisseaux*. The Giblians are the same as the Biblians: among geographers, Gibel is the Phoenician city Gebala, also called Byblos or Byblus, now Giblet, according to Brochard. But why seek the aid of geographical lexicons? We have at hand St. Jerome’s book *On Hebrew Places*, where, listing names beginning with the letter B in the Books of Kings, he writes: “Byblos, a city of Phoenicia, which Ezekiel mentions; in Hebrew it is written GOBEL.” See also the scholia of the *Canon of Hebrew Truth*, Book I, *Malachim*, chapter V. MART.].

All the ships of the sea and their sailors were among your people of commerce.

Persians, Lydians, and Libyans were in your army, your warriors. They hung shield and helmet upon you for your adornment.

The sons of Arvad [Hebrew: Arvad] were with your army upon your walls all around. The Pygmies also, who were in your towers, hung their quivers upon your walls around; they completed your beauty. [Col. 0978C]

The Carthaginians were your merchants; because of the abundance of all your wealth, they filled your markets with silver, iron, tin, and lead.

Greece, Tubal, and Meshech were your traders. They brought slaves and bronze vessels for your people.

From the house of Togarmah they brought horses, horsemen, and mules to your marketplace.

The sons of Dedan were your merchants, and many islands were the commerce of your hand. They exchanged ivory tusks and ebony for your goods. [Col. 0979A]

Aram was your merchant because of the abundance of your works. They placed in your market precious stones [the variant: “a drop”], purple, embroidered cloth, fine linen, silk, and scarlet [Hebrew: *chad chod*; some manuscripts have this marginal note in the sacred text: “*chod chod*.” MART.].

Judah and the land of Israel were your traders in prime grain. They placed balsam, honey, oil, and resin in your markets.

Damascus was your merchant because of the multitude of your works, because of the abundance [the variant: “supply”] of your various riches, in rich wine and wool of the finest color.

Dan, Greece, and Mozal [Hebrew: Muzal] placed worked iron in your markets; stacte and calamus were among your merchandise.

Dedan was your trader in coverings for sitting. [Col. 0979B]

Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were merchants under your hand. Your merchants came to you with lambs, rams, and goats.

The merchants of Sheba and Raamah [Hebrew: Raamah] were your merchants. They brought every finest spice, precious stone [the variant: “most precious stone”], and gold, which they placed in your market.

Haran, Canneh, and Eden were your merchants; Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad were your sellers.

They were your merchants in every kind of merchandise: violet fabrics, embroidered cloths, and precious woven materials, wrapped and bound with cords. They also had cedar in their merchandise.

The ships of the sea were your leaders in your commerce; you were filled and exceedingly glorified in the heart of the sea.

Your rowers brought you into many waters; the south wind shattered you in the heart of the sea.

Your wealth, your treasures, and your varied equipment; your sailors and your pilots, who managed your furnishings and presided over your people; your warriors also who were in you, together with all your multitude that is in your midst—all shall fall into the heart of the sea on the day of your ruin.

At the sound of the cry of your pilots the fleets shall be shaken.

All who held the oar shall descend from their ships. The sailors and all the pilots of the sea shall stand upon the land. They shall wail over you with a loud voice and cry out bitterly.

They shall throw dust upon their heads and sprinkle themselves with ashes.

They shall shave themselves bald for you and gird themselves with sackcloth. [Col. 0979D]

They shall weep over you in the bitterness of their souls, with a most bitter lamentation.

They shall take up a mournful song over you and lament you:

“Who is like Tyre, which has been silenced in the midst of the sea?

At the departure of your merchandise from the sea you filled many peoples; through the abundance of your riches and your peoples you enriched the kings of the earth [the variant: “many kings”].

Now you have been shattered by the sea. In the depths of the waters your wealth and all your multitude that was in your midst have fallen.

All the inhabitants of the islands have been stunned because of you, and all their kings, struck by the storm, have changed countenance.

The merchants of the peoples [the variant: “of the nations”] have hissed at you. [Col. 0980A]

You have been reduced to nothing, and you shall not exist [the variant adds: “any longer”] forever.”

## Chapter XXVIII

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre:

Thus says the Lord God:

“Because your heart has been lifted up and you have said, ‘I am a god, and I sit [the variant: ‘I sat’] in the seat of a god, in the heart of the sea,’ though you are a human being and not a god, and you have made your heart like the heart of a god—

behold, you are wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you.

By your wisdom and understanding you made strength for yourself and acquired gold and silver in your treasuries.

By the abundance of your wisdom and your commerce you multiplied your strength for yourself, and your heart was lifted up because of your power. [Col. 0980B]

Therefore thus says the Lord God [the variant omits ‘God’]:

Because your heart has been lifted up like the heart of a god, therefore behold, I shall bring foreigners against you, the strongest of the nations. They shall draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and profane your splendor.

They shall kill and bring you down [the variant: ‘hand you over’], and you shall die the death of the slain in the heart of the sea.

Will you still say, ‘I am a god,’ in the presence of those killing you, though you are a human being and not a god, in the hand of those who kill you?

You shall die the death of the uncircumcised at the hand of foreigners, because I have spoken,” says the Lord God.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, raise a lament over the king of Tyre and say to him:

Thus says the Lord God:

“You were the seal of likeness, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.

You were in the delights of the paradise of God. Every precious stone was your covering: sardius, topaz, jasper, chrysolite, onyx, beryl, sapphire, carbuncle, and emerald.

Gold was the workmanship of your adornment, and your settings were prepared on the day when you were created.

You were an outstretched cherub, protecting, and I placed you upon the holy mountain of God; you walked in the midst of fiery stones.

You were perfect in your ways from the day of your creation, until iniquity was found in you.

Through the abundance of your commerce your inner parts were filled with iniquity, and you sinned. So I cast you out from the mountain of God and destroyed you, O protecting cherub, from the midst of the fiery stones.

Your heart was lifted up because of your beauty; [Col. 0980D]

you corrupted your wisdom because of your beauty [the variant: ‘your loveliness’]. I cast you to the ground; I set you before the faces of kings, so that they might look upon you.

By the multitude of your iniquities and the iniquity of your commerce you profaned your sanctuaries.

Therefore I shall bring forth fire from your midst; it shall devour you, and I shall turn you to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all who see you.

All who see you among the nations shall be astonished at you. You have become nothing, and you shall not exist forever.”

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, set your face against Sidon. [Col. 0981A]

Prophesy concerning her and say:

Thus says the Lord God:

“Behold, I am against you, Sidon, and I shall be glorified in your midst. They shall know that I am the Lord when I execute judgments in her and am sanctified in her.

I shall send pestilence and blood into her streets, and the slain shall fall in her midst by the sword on every side. They shall know that I am the Lord.

She shall no longer be a bitter stumbling-block to the house of Israel, or a thorn causing pain on every side to those who oppose them. And they shall know that I am the Lord God.

Thus says the Lord God:

When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they have been scattered, I shall be sanctified in them before the nations. [Col. 0981B]

They shall dwell in their own land, which I gave to my servant Jacob.

They shall dwell in it securely; they shall build houses and plant vineyards, and they shall dwell confidently when I have executed judgments upon all those who oppose them [the variant omits “them”] on every side.

And they shall know that I am the Lord their God.”

## Chapter XXIX

In the tenth year [Note: “In the tenth year.” This passage is highly complicated because of the diversity of readings. In the current Hebrew text we read: “In the tenth year, in the tenth, in the twelfth month.” In the Septuagint, however: “In the twelfth year, in the tenth month, on the first day of the month.” The Alexandrian manuscript has: “In the tenth year, in the eleventh month,” and so forth. St. Jerome, for his part, cites the text of this chapter in Book IX of his *Commentary on Ezekiel* as follows: “In the tenth year (or, according to the Septuagint, the twelfth), in the tenth month (or, according to the Hebrew, the twelfth), on the first (or, one) day of the month,” and so forth. Later, however, while explaining chapter thirty of the same prophet, he plainly confirms the truth of the Latin manuscripts in these words: “After the twenty-seventh year of the captivity of King Jehoiachin, he returns to the present time, when he had begun to prophesy against Egypt, that is, to the tenth year and the tenth month, the eleventh day of the month,” and so forth. These statements, unless I am mistaken, clearly prove that the genuine reading is the one represented by the Latin copies, while the other readings were confused and corrupted, as is readily apparent from their disagreement. MART.], in the tenth month, on the eleventh day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and prophesy concerning him and all Egypt.

Speak, and say:

Thus says the Lord God:

“Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh, king of Egypt, great dragon, lying in the midst of your rivers and saying, ‘My river belongs to me, and I made myself.’ [Col. 0981C]

I shall put a bridle in your jaws and fasten the fish of your rivers to your scales.

I shall drag you out from the midst of your rivers, and all the fish of your rivers shall cling to your scales.

I shall cast you into the desert, and all the fish of your river with you. You shall fall upon the face of the earth; you shall not be gathered up or collected.

I have given you to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky for food.

And all the inhabitants of Egypt shall know that I am the Lord, because you were a staff of reed to the house of Israel.

When they grasped you with the hand [the variant adds: ‘their hand’], you broke, and you tore their entire shoulder.

When they leaned upon you, you broke apart and threw all their loins out of joint.”

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

“Behold, I shall bring a sword against you and destroy from you human being and beast.

The land of Egypt shall become a desert and a desolation, and they shall know that I am the Lord, because you said, ‘My river belongs to me, and I made it.’ [Col. 0981D]

Therefore behold, I am against you and your rivers. I shall give the land of Egypt to desolation, laid waste by the sword, from the tower of Syene to the borders of Ethiopia.

No human foot shall pass through it, nor shall the foot of an animal travel through it; it shall not be inhabited for forty years.

I shall make the land of Egypt desolate in the midst of desolated lands, and its cities in the midst of overthrown cities.

They shall be desolate for forty years, and I shall scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.

For thus says the Lord God:

At the end of forty years I shall gather Egypt from the peoples among whom they had been scattered, and I shall restore the captivity of Egypt.

I shall settle them in the land of Pathros [Hebrew: Pathros], in the land of their origin. [Col. 0982B]

There they shall be a lowly kingdom. It shall be the lowliest among the kingdoms, and it shall no longer exalt itself over the nations. I shall diminish them, so that they may not rule over the nations.

Nor shall they any longer be a source of confidence to the house of Israel, teaching iniquity, so that Israel might flee and follow them. And they shall know that I am the Lord God.”

And it came to pass in the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, made his army perform great service against Tyre.

Every head was made bald, and every shoulder was rubbed bare; yet no payment was given to him or to his army from Tyre for the service with which he served me against it. [Col. 0982C]

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

“Behold, I shall give Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, the land of Egypt. He shall take its multitude, plunder its spoils, and seize its booty; and it shall be payment for his army.

And for the labor by which he served [the variant omits “for” and adds “me”] against it, I have given him the land of Egypt, because he labored for me,” says the Lord God.

On that day a horn shall sprout for the house [the variant: “house”] of Israel, and I shall give you an open mouth in their midst; and they shall know that I am the Lord.

## Chapter XXX

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, prophesy and say:

Thus says the Lord God: [Col. 0982D]

“Wail, ‘Alas, alas!’ for the day is near, and the day of the Lord approaches; it shall be a day of cloud, a time for the nations.

A sword shall come upon Egypt, and there shall be terror in Ethiopia, [Col. 0983A]

when the slain fall in Egypt, its multitude is removed, and its foundations are destroyed.

Ethiopia, Libya, the Lydians, all the remaining populace, Chub, and the sons of the covenant land shall fall by the sword with them.

Thus says the Lord God:

Those who support Egypt shall fall, and the pride of its dominion shall be destroyed. From the tower of Syene [Hebrew: Sevene] they shall fall by the sword in it,” says the Lord God of hosts [the Hebrew does not add “of hosts”; this title is nevertheless retained in Jerome’s commentary, with the other word, “God,” deleted. MART.].

They shall be scattered in the midst of desolated lands, and the cities shall be in the midst of deserted cities.

And they shall know that I am the Lord when I send fire upon Egypt and all its helpers are crushed.

On that day messengers shall go forth from me in ships to crush the confidence of Ethiopia; and there shall be terror among them on the day of Egypt, for it shall certainly come.

Thus says the Lord God:

I shall bring the multitude of Egypt to an end by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.

He and his people with him, the strongest of the nations, shall be brought to destroy the land. They shall draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with slain.

I shall make the channels of the rivers dry and give the land into the hand of wicked men. I shall lay waste the land and all that fills it by the hand of foreigners. I, the Lord, have spoken.

Thus says the Lord God:

I shall destroy the idols and put an end to the images in Memphis [Hebrew: Noph]. There shall no longer be a prince [Note: Copies of the *Canon* read “the prince of the land of Egypt.” In Jerome’s *Commentary*, “the prince in the land of Egypt.” MART.] from the land [the variant: “of the land”] of Egypt, and I shall bring terror upon the land of Egypt. [Col. 0983C]

I shall destroy the land of Pathros [Hebrew: Pathros], send fire upon Taphnis, and execute judgments in Alexandria [Note: Its former name was No. “We,” says Jerome, “have substituted Alexandria for No by anticipation, which in Greek is called πρόληψις … so that the passage might become clearer to the reader’s understanding.” See Book IX of the *Commentary on Ezekiel*. MART.].

I shall pour out my indignation upon Pelusium, the stronghold of Egypt, and destroy the multitude of Alexandria; I shall send fire upon Egypt.

Pelusium shall suffer like a woman in labor, Alexandria shall be scattered, and Memphis [Hebrew: Noph] shall suffer daily anguish.

The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis [Hebrew: Phibezeth] shall fall by the sword, and the women themselves shall be led into captivity.

In Taphnis the day shall grow dark when I break there the scepters of Egypt and its proud power comes to an end. A cloud shall cover it, and its daughters shall be led into captivity.

I shall execute judgments in Egypt, and they shall know that I am the Lord.” [Col. 0983D]

And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh day of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh, king of Egypt; and behold, it has not been wrapped so that it might be restored to health, bound up with bread, and bandaged [the variant: “mended”] with linen cloths, [Col. 0984A]

so that, once strength was restored, it might be able to hold a sword.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

“Behold, I am against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and I shall crush his strong but broken arm. I shall cast the sword from his hand.

I shall scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.

I shall strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and place my sword in his hand. I shall break the arms of Pharaoh, and he shall groan with the groaning of one slain before him.

I shall strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh shall fall.

And they shall know that I am the Lord when I place my sword in the hand of the king of Babylon and he stretches it out over the land of Egypt.

I shall scatter [the variant: ‘destroy’] Egypt among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands, [Col. 0984B] and they shall know that I am the Lord.”

## Chapter XXXI

And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, say to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to his people:

“To whom are you comparable in your greatness?

Behold, Assyria was like a cedar in Lebanon, beautiful in branches, leafy and forested, lofty in height, with its crown raised among dense foliage.

The waters nourished it, the abyss exalted it [the variant: ‘raised it’]. Its rivers flowed around its roots, and it sent out its channels to all the trees of the region.

Therefore its height was greater than that of all the trees of the region, its branches multiplied, and its boughs grew high because of the many waters. [Col. 0984C]

When it spread out its shade, all the birds of the sky made their nests in its branches, all the beasts of the forests gave birth beneath its foliage, and beneath its shadow dwelt an assembly of very many nations [the variant: ‘all nations’].

It was exceedingly beautiful in its greatness and in the spread of its branches, for its root was beside many waters.

The cedars in the paradise of God were not taller than it; the firs did not equal its crown, and the plane trees were not equal to its foliage. No tree in the paradise of God was like it or equal to its beauty.

For I had made it beautiful, with abundant and dense foliage, and all the trees of delight that were in the paradise of God envied it.

Therefore thus says the Lord God: [Col. 0984D]

Because it was exalted in height and raised its crown, green and dense, and its heart was lifted up in its height,

I gave it into the hand of the mightiest of the nations; he dealt fully with it. According to its wickedness I cast it out.

Foreigners and the most ruthless of the nations shall cut it down and throw it upon the mountains. [Col. 0985A] Its branches shall fall in all the valleys, and its boughs shall be broken upon all the ravines of the land.

All the peoples of the land shall withdraw from its shadow and abandon it.

Upon its ruin all the birds of the sky shall dwell, and all the beasts of the region shall be among its branches.

Therefore all the trees of the waters shall no longer exalt themselves in their height, nor set their crowns among thick and leafy growth, nor shall all that is watered by the waters stand in their height.

For all have been handed over to death, to the land below, in the midst of the sons of humankind, among those who descend into the pit.

Thus says the Lord God:

On the day when it descended to the underworld, I proclaimed mourning and covered it with the abyss. [Col. 0985B]

I restrained its rivers and checked the many waters.

Lebanon mourned over it [the variant: “was crushed”], and all the trees of the field were shaken.

At the sound of its downfall I shook the nations when I brought it down to the underworld with those who descended into the pit.

And in the nether land all the trees of delight, the finest and most splendid in Lebanon, all that was watered by the waters, were comforted.

For they too shall descend with it to the underworld, to those slain by the sword, and each one’s arm [Note: See what we observe in the commentary on this passage.] shall rest beneath its shadow in the midst of the nations.

To whom are you likened, O illustrious and lofty one, among

the trees of delight?

Behold, you have been brought down with the trees of delight to the farthest land:

in the midst of the uncircumcised you shall sleep,

with those who were slain by the sword:

[Col. 0985C] He is Pharaoh [Al. “Thus: Pharaoh”], and all his multitude,

says the Lord God.

[Chapter XXXII.] And it came to pass, in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man,

raise a lamentation over Pharaoh, king of Egypt,

and say to him:

You are like a lion among the nations,

and like a dragon that is in the sea:

You churned up the horn in your rivers,

and troubled the waters with your feet,

and fouled their rivers.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

I will spread my net over you among a multitude of many peoples,

and I will drag you out in my seine.

And I will throw you onto the land [Al. “the land upon you”],

I will cast you upon the face of the field:

And I will cause every bird of the heavens to settle upon you,

[Col. 0985D] and I will fill the beasts of the whole earth with you.

And I will lay your flesh upon the mountains,

and fill the hills with your corruption.

And I will water the land with the stench of your blood upon the mountains,

and the valleys shall be filled with you.

And when you have been extinguished, I will cover the heavens,

and make their stars dark;

I will cover the sun with a cloud,

and the moon shall not give its light.

[Col. 0986A] I will make all the lights of heaven mourn over you,

and I will bring darkness over your land, says the Lord God [Note: [Col. 0985D] The commonly circulated books add, “when your wounded have fallen in the midst of the land”; yet this is lacking in the Hebrew, Chaldean, and even the Septuagint, and finally in the better-quality Hieronymian manuscripts, both printed and manuscript. He seems to have looked back to the preceding chapter, XXX, verse 4, and added this passage to the Latin interpretation. [Col. 0986D] If it were present in Hebrew, it would have had to be written approximately in these words, [Hebrew text omitted in the supplied text], which differ very greatly from those of the immediately preceding clause, [Hebrew text omitted in the supplied text], so that, as we suspected, it may be considered merely another translation of the same Hebrew sentence, owing to a variant reading.].

And I will trouble the hearts of many peoples,

when I bring your destruction among the nations, into lands that you do not know.

And I will cause many peoples to be astonished at you;

and their kings shall fear you with exceedingly great terror,

when my sword begins to fly over their faces;

and suddenly each shall be stupefied for his own life

on the day of your ruin.

For thus says the Lord God:

The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon you;

with the swords of the mighty I will cast down your multitude:

all these nations are unconquerable;

and they shall ravage the pride of Egypt,

and its multitude shall be scattered.

And I will destroy all its livestock, which were beside

[Col. 0986B] very abundant waters:

and no longer shall a human foot trouble them,

nor shall the hoof of cattle disturb them.

Then I will make their waters exceedingly clear,
