and I will lead their rivers along like oil, says the Lord God:

When I make the land of Egypt desolate, it shall be deserted

by its fullness, when I strike all its inhabitants; and they shall know that I am

the Lord.

There is a lamentation, and they shall lament over it:

the daughters of the nations shall lament over Egypt,

and over its multitude they shall lament, says the Lord God.

And it came to pass in the twelfth year, on the fifteenth

day of the month,

that the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man,

sing a mournful song over the multitude of Egypt:

[Col. 0986C] And bring it down, itself and the daughters of mighty nations,

to the farthest land,

with those who go down to the pit.

Whom do you surpass in beauty?

Go down, and sleep with the uncircumcised.

In the midst of those slain by the sword they shall fall:

the sword has been given;

they have dragged her away, and all her peoples.

The mightiest of the mighty shall speak to her from the midst

of hell,

with those who went down with her helpers,

and slept uncircumcised, slain by the sword [Al. “with the uncircumcised and the slain”].

There is Assyria, and all her multitude,

around her are her graves;

all slain, and those who fell by the sword.

Their graves were set in the farthest parts of the pit,

and her multitude became all around her grave:

all slain, and fallen by the sword,

who once gave terror in the land of the living.

[Col. 0986D] There is Elam, and all her multitude around her grave [Al. “around his grave”]:

all these slain and fallen by the sword,

who went down uncircumcised to the farthest land,

who spread their terror in the land of the living,

and bore their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

In the midst of the slain they set her bed among all [Col. 0987A] her peoples;

around her is her grave:

all these uncircumcised and slain by the sword.

For they gave their terror in

the land of the living,

and bore their disgrace with those who go down to the pit:

in the midst of the slain they have been placed.

There are Meshech [Hebrew: Mesech], and Tubal, and all their multitude; around them are their graves:

all these uncircumcised, slain, and fallen

by the sword,

because they gave their terror in the land of the living.

And they shall not sleep with the mighty, who fell and were uncircumcised,

who went down to the underworld with their weapons,

and placed their swords beneath their heads,

and their iniquities were upon their bones:

because they had become the terror of the mighty in the land of the living.

[Col. 0987B] And you therefore shall be crushed in the midst of the uncircumcised,

and shall sleep with those slain by the sword.

There is Edom, and her kings,

all her leaders, who were given over with their army

to those slain by the sword;

and those who slept with the uncircumcised,

and with those who go down [Al. “went down”] to

the pit.

There are all the princes of the north, and all the hunters,

who were brought down with the slain, trembling and

confounded in their strength;

who slept uncircumcised with those slain by the sword,

and bore their confusion with those who

go down to the pit.

Pharaoh saw them,

and was comforted over all his multitude,

which was slain by the sword;

Pharaoh and all his army, says the Lord God:

because I gave my terror in the land of the living,

[Col. 0987C] and he slept in the midst of the uncircumcised with those slain by the sword,

Pharaoh and all his multitude, says the Lord God.

[Chapter XXXIII.] And the word of the Lord came to me,

saying:

Son of man, speak to the children of your people, and say

to them:

When I bring a sword upon a land,

and the people of the land take one man from among their last members,

and appoint him over themselves as a watchman,

and he sees the sword coming upon the land,

and blows the trumpet and announces it to the people:

whoever hears the sound of the trumpet

and does not take heed,

and the sword comes and takes him,

his blood shall be upon his own head.

He heard the sound of the trumpet and did not take heed;

his blood shall be upon him.

But if he had guarded himself,

[Col. 0987D] he would have saved his life.

But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not sound the trumpet,

and the people do not take heed,

and the sword comes and takes a life from among them,

that man indeed is seized in his iniquity,

but I will require his blood from the hand of the watchman.

And you, son of man,

I have appointed you as a watchman for the house of Israel:

when you hear a word from my mouth,

you shall announce it to them from me.

When I say to the wicked, “Wicked one, you shall surely die,”

and you have not spoken so that the wicked person may guard himself from his way,

that wicked person shall die in his iniquity,

[Col. 0988A] but I will require his blood from your hand.

But if, when you announce to the wicked person that he should turn back from his ways,

he does not turn back from his way,

he shall die in his iniquity;

but you have saved your life.

Therefore you, son of man, say to the house of Israel:

Thus you have spoken, saying:

“Our iniquities and our sins are upon us,

and in them we waste away;

how then can we live?”

Say to them:

“As I live,” says the Lord God,

“I do not desire the death of the wicked,

but that the wicked turn back from his way and live.

Turn back,

turn back from your exceedingly evil ways;

and why will you die, house of Israel?”

Therefore you, son of man, say to the children of your people:

The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him on whatever day

[Col. 0988B] he sins,

and the wickedness of the wicked shall not harm him on whatever

day he turns back from his wickedness.

And the righteous shall not be able to live by his righteousness

on whatever day he sins.

Even if I say to the righteous that he shall live,

and, trusting in his righteousness, he commits iniquity,

all his righteous deeds shall be consigned to oblivion,

and in the iniquity that he has committed, in that he shall die.

But if I say to the wicked, “You shall surely die,”

and he repents of his sin,

and does judgment and righteousness,

if that wicked person restores the pledge,

and returns what he has seized,

and walks in the commandments of life,

and does nothing unjust,

he shall surely live and shall not die.

All his sins that he has committed [Al. omits “his”]

[Col. 0988C] shall not be reckoned against him;

he has done judgment and righteousness; he shall surely live.

And the children of your people said:

“The way of the Lord is not balanced,”

while their own way is unjust.

For when the righteous turns away from his righteousness and commits

iniquities,

he shall die in them.

And when the wicked turns away from his wickedness and does

judgment and righteousness,

he shall live by them.

And you say:

“The way of the Lord is not straight.”

I will judge each of you according to his ways [Hebrew: “you”], house of Israel.

And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the tenth month [Al. adds “month”], on the fifth day of our exile,

that a man who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me, saying:

“The city has been destroyed.”

[Col. 0988D] Now the hand of the Lord had been upon me in the evening,

before the one who had escaped came;

and he opened my mouth until he came to me in the morning,

and when my mouth was opened, I was no longer silent.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man,

those who dwell in these ruins upon the soil of Israel,

speaking, say:

“Abraham was one,

and he possessed the land as an inheritance;

but we are many [Al. adds “we are”],

and the land has been given to us as a possession.”

Therefore say to them:

Thus says the Lord God:

[Note: [Col. 0987D] Here he refers to the distinguished testimony of the holy Father concerning the former division of the verses, from his Commentary on [Col. 0988D] this passage: “It should be known,” he says, “that eight verses, more or less, from the place that we have set down—‘You who eat blood and lift your eyes to your impurities’—up to the place where it is written, ‘Thus you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God’—are not found in the Septuagint. Indeed, exactly that many verses are numbered in this edition of ours [Col. 0990D] according to Jerome’s recension.”]

“You who eat blood,

and lift your eyes to your impurities,

[Col. 0989A] and shed blood:

shall you possess the land as an inheritance?

You have stood upon your swords,

you have committed abominations,

and each of you has defiled his neighbor’s wife;

and shall you possess the land as an inheritance?”

Say to them:

Thus says the Lord God:

“As I live, surely those who dwell in the ruins

shall fall by the sword;

and whoever is in the field

shall be given over to the beasts for devouring;

but those who are in the strongholds and in the caves

shall die by pestilence.

And I will make the land a desolation and a wilderness,

and its proud strength shall fail;

and the mountains of Israel shall be desolate,

because there is no one who passes through them.

And they shall know that I am the Lord,

when I have made the land [Al. adds “their land”] desolate

[Col. 0989B] and a wilderness,

because of all their abominations that they have committed.”

And you, son of man:

the children of your people who speak about you beside the walls,

and at the doors of the houses,

and say to one another, each man to his neighbor,

speaking:

“Come, and let us hear what word proceeds from

the Lord.”

And they come to you as though a people were entering,

and my people sit before you;

and they hear your words, but do not do them,

because they turn them into a song of their mouth,

while their heart follows their greed.

And you are to them like a musical song sung with a sweet and pleasing sound;

they hear your words, but do not do them.

And when what was foretold comes—for behold, it is coming—

[Col. 0989C] then they shall know that a prophet has been among them [Al. “in their midst”].

[Chapter XXXIV.] And the word of the Lord came to

me, saying:

Son of man,

prophesy concerning the shepherds of Israel;

prophesy, and say to the shepherds:

Thus says the Lord God:

Woe to the shepherds of Israel who fed themselves!

Are not flocks fed by shepherds?

You ate the milk,

you clothed yourselves with the wool,

and you slaughtered what was fat;

but you did not feed my flock.

You did not strengthen what was weak,

you did not heal what was sick,

you did not bind up what was broken [Al. “was”],

you did not bring back what was cast away,

you did not seek what was lost;

but you ruled over them with severity and with power.

[Col. 0989D] And my sheep were scattered because there was no shepherd,

and they became food for all the beasts

of the field, and were scattered.

My flocks wandered over all the mountains and over

every high hill;

and my flocks were scattered over the whole face of the earth,

and there was no one who sought them—

[Col. 0990A] there was, I say, no one who sought them.

Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord:

“As I live,” says the Lord God,

“because my flocks became [Note: [Col. 0990D] Manuscripts read, without that pronoun, ‘flocks for plunder.’ MART. The Palatine manuscript likewise omits the pronoun ‘my,’ which is nevertheless found in the original books.] prey,

and my sheep food for all the beasts

of the field,

because there was no shepherd,

nor did my shepherds seek my flock [Al. omits “my”],

but the shepherds fed themselves,

and did not feed my flocks,

therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I myself will require my flock from the shepherds,

from their hand,

and I will make them cease, so that they will no longer feed the flock [Al. adds “my”],

nor will the shepherds feed themselves any longer.

And I will deliver my flock from their mouth,

[Col. 0990B] and it shall no longer be food for them.

For thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I myself will seek my sheep,

and I will visit them.

As a shepherd visits his flock on the day when he is among his scattered sheep,

so I will visit my sheep and deliver them from all

the places in which they were scattered on the day of cloud

and darkness.

And I will bring them out from the peoples,

and gather them from the lands,

and bring them into their own land.

And I will feed them on the mountains of Israel,

by the streams, and in all the inhabited places of the land.

I will feed them in the most fertile pastures,

and on the high mountains of Israel their pastures shall be;

there they shall rest in green grasses,

and they shall feed on rich pastures upon the mountains

of Israel.

[Col. 0990C] I will feed my sheep,

and I myself will make them lie down,” says the Lord God.

What was lost I will seek,

what was cast away I will bring back,

what was broken I will bind up,

what was weak I will strengthen,

and what was fat and strong I will guard;

I will feed them with judgment.

But you, my flocks, thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I judge between sheep and sheep, between rams and

goats.

Was it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture?

Moreover, you trampled the remnants of your pastures beneath your feet.

And when you drank the purest water,

you muddied what remained with your feet.

And my sheep fed on what had been trampled by your feet,

and drank what your feet had muddied.

Therefore thus says the Lord God to them:

[Col. 0990D] Behold, I myself judge between the fat cattle and the lean:

because you pushed with your sides and shoulders,

and butted with your horns all the weak

cattle,

until they were scattered outside,

I will save my flock, and it shall no longer be prey,

and I will judge between sheep and sheep.

And I will raise up over them one shepherd who shall feed them,

my servant David;

[Col. 0991A] he shall feed them, and he himself shall be their shepherd.

And I, the Lord, shall be their God; and my servant

David shall be prince in their midst;

I, the Lord, have spoken.

And I will make a covenant of peace with them,

and I will make the evil beasts cease from the land;

and those who dwell [Al. “dwelt”] in the wilderness shall sleep securely

in the forests.

And I will make them, and the places around my hill, a blessing;

and I will bring rain in its season:

there shall be rains of blessing.

And the tree of the field shall give its fruit,

and the land shall yield its growth,

and they shall be in their land without fear;

and they shall know that I am the Lord,

when I have broken the chains of their yoke

and delivered them from the hand of those who ruled over them.

And they shall no longer be prey to the nations,

nor shall the beasts of the earth devour them;

but they shall dwell securely, without any terror.

[Col. 0991B] And I will raise up for them a renowned shoot,

and they shall no longer be diminished by famine in the land,

nor shall they bear the reproaches of the nations any longer.

And they shall know that I, the Lord their God, am with them,

and that they are my people, the house of Israel, says the Lord

God.

But you, my flocks, the flocks [Al. “flock”] of my pasture,

are human beings;

and I am the Lord your God, says the Lord God.

[Chapter XXXV.] And the word of the Lord came to me,

saying:

Son of man,

set your face against Mount Seir,

and prophesy against it, and say to it:

Thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir,

and I will stretch out my hand over you,

and make you desolate and deserted.

I will demolish your cities,

[Col. 0991C] and you shall be desolate;

you shall know that I am the Lord.

Because you have been an everlasting enemy,

and have delivered the children of Israel into the power of the sword at the time of their affliction,

at the time of their final iniquity,

therefore, as I live, says the Lord God,

I will hand you over to blood, and blood shall pursue you;

and because you hate blood, blood shall pursue you.

And I will make Mount Seir desolate and deserted,

and remove from it one who goes and one who returns.

And I will fill its mountains with its slain;

on your hills, in your valleys, and in your ravines,

those slain by the sword shall fall.

I will hand you over to everlasting desolations,

and your cities shall not be inhabited;

and you shall know that I am the Lord God [Al. omits “God”].

Because you said, “The two nations and the two lands shall be mine,

[Col. 0991D] and I shall possess them as an inheritance,”

when the Lord was there,

therefore, as I live, says the Lord God,

I will act according to your anger and according to your jealousy,

which you exercised in hatred against them;

and I will make myself known through them when I judge you [Al. “to you, when I judge you”].

And you shall know that I am the Lord [Al. “I am the Lord”]. I have heard

all your reproaches that you uttered against

the mountains of Israel, saying:

“They have been given to us as desolate places, for us to devour.”

And you rose up against me with your mouth,

and spoke insulting words against me;

I heard.

Thus says the Lord God:

While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you a desolation.

As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel,

[Col. 0992A] because it had been scattered,

so I will do to you:

You shall be desolated, Mount Seir, and all Edom;

and they shall know that I am the Lord.

[Chapter XXXVI.] But you, son of man, prophesy concerning the mountains of Israel, and say:

Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord:

Thus says the Lord God:

Because the enemy said concerning you:

“Hurrah! The everlasting heights have been given to us as an inheritance [Al. “possession”].”

Therefore prophesy, and say:

Thus says the Lord God:

Because you have been desolate and trampled on every side,

and have become an inheritance for the remnant of the nations,

and have come upon the lips of tongues, and a reproach

of the peoples [Al. “to the peoples”],

therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord

God:

[Col. 0992B] Thus says the Lord God to the mountains and hills, ravines and valleys, and desolate places, and ruined walls,

and abandoned cities,

which have been depopulated and mocked by the remnant

of the nations around them.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

Because I have spoken in the fire of my jealousy concerning the remnant

of the nations, and concerning all Edom,

who assigned my land to themselves as an inheritance,

with joy, with all their heart, and with their soul,

and cast it out in order to ravage it,

therefore prophesy over the soil of Israel,

and say to the mountains and hills, ridges and valleys:

Thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I have spoken in my jealousy and in my fury,

because you have borne the disgrace of the nations.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

I have raised my hand,

so that the nations around you themselves may bear their disgrace.

But you, mountains of Israel, put forth your branches,

and yield your fruit to my people Israel,

for it is near that it should come.

For behold, I am coming to you, and I will turn toward you,

and you shall be plowed, and you shall receive seed.

And I will multiply human beings upon you, the whole house of Israel;

and the cities shall be inhabited, and the ruins restored.

And I will fill you with human beings and cattle;

and they shall multiply and increase.

And I will make you inhabited as at the beginning,

and bestow greater benefits upon you than you had

at the beginning;

and you shall know that I am the Lord.

And I will bring human beings upon you, my people

Israel,

and they shall possess you as an inheritance.

[Col. 0992D] And you shall be their inheritance [Al. “possession”],

and you shall no longer continue to be without them.

Thus says the Lord God:

Because they say of you:

“You devour human beings and strangle your people,”

therefore you shall no longer devour human beings,

nor shall you ever again kill your people, says the Lord

God.

And I will no longer make the disgrace of the nations heard in you,

and you shall not bear the reproach of the peoples at all,

nor shall you lose your people any longer, says the Lord

God.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man,

the house of Israel dwelt upon its soil,

and defiled it by its ways and by its practices;

their way before me became like the uncleanness of a menstruating woman.

[Col. 0993A] And I poured out my indignation upon them because of the blood that they had shed upon the land,

and because they had defiled it with their idols.

And I scattered them among the nations,

and they were dispersed through the lands;

according to their ways and their inventions I judged them.

And they entered among the nations to which they had gone,

and profaned my holy name,

when it was said of them, “This is the people of the Lord,

and they have gone out from his land.”

And I spared my holy name,

which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations to which

they had gone.

Therefore say to the house of Israel:

Thus says the Lord God:

It is not for your sake that I will act, house of Israel,

but for the sake of my holy name, which you profaned

among the nations to which you entered.

And I will sanctify my great name, which has been profaned [Col. 0993B] among the nations,

which you profaned in their midst,

so that the nations may know [Al. omits “the nations”] that I am the Lord, says the Lord of hosts,

when I have been sanctified in you before their eyes.

For I will take you from the nations,

and gather you [Al. omits “you”] from all

the lands,

and bring you into your own land.

And I will pour clean water over you,

and you shall be cleansed from all your impurities,

and I will cleanse you from all your idols.

And I will give you a new heart,

and put a new spirit within you.

And I will take away the stony heart from your flesh,

and give you a heart of flesh.

And I will put my spirit within you,

and cause you to walk in my commandments,

and to observe my judgments and perform them [Al. adds “them”].

And you shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers,

and you shall be my people,

and I will be your God.

And I will save you from all your impurities,

and I will call for grain and multiply it,

and I will not impose [Note: [Col. 0993D] The Canon of Saint-Germain reads, “I will not impose upon you.” The Colbertinus-Aniciensis codex reads, “I will not impose upon you.” MART.] famine upon you.

And I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the produce of the field,

so that you shall no longer bear the reproach of famine among the nations.

And you shall remember your exceedingly evil ways

and your practices that were not good;

and your iniquities and your crimes shall be displeasing to you.

It is not for your sake that I will act, says the Lord God; let it be known to you:

Be ashamed and confounded because of your ways, house of Israel.

Thus says the Lord God:

On the day when I cleanse you from all your iniquities,

[Col. 0993D] and cause the cities to be inhabited, and restore the ruins,

and the deserted land has been cultivated—

the land that had formerly been desolate in the sight of every passerby—

they shall say:

“That uncultivated land has become like a garden of delight;

and the deserted, abandoned, and demolished cities

have been fortified and inhabited.”

And whatever nations remain around you shall know

that I, the Lord, have built what was destroyed and planted

what was uncultivated.

I, the Lord, have spoken, and I have acted.

Thus says the Lord God:

[Col. 0994A] In this also the house of Israel shall seek me, that I may act in [Al. omits “in”] them:

I will multiply them like a human flock, like a holy flock,

like the flock of Jerusalem during its festivals.

Thus the deserted cities shall be filled with human flocks,

and they shall know that I am the Lord.

[Chapter XXXVII.] The hand of the Lord came upon me,

and he brought me out in the spirit of the Lord

and set me down in the midst of a plain that was full

of bones.

And he led me around among them in a circle;

and behold, they were very many upon the face of the plain,

and exceedingly dry.

And he said to me:

Son of man,

do you suppose that these bones will live?

And I said:

Lord God, you know.

[Col. 0994B] And he said to me:

Prophesy concerning these bones, and say to them:

Dry bones, hear the word of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord God to these bones:

Behold, I will bring spirit into you, and you shall live.

And I will place sinews upon you,

and cause flesh to grow over you,

and stretch skin over you.

And I will give you spirit, and you shall live,

and you shall know that I am the Lord.

And I prophesied as he had commanded me;

and as I prophesied, there was a sound,

and behold, a commotion.

And the bones came together,

each one to its joint.

And I saw, and behold, sinews and flesh came upon them,

and skin was stretched over them from above,

but they had no spirit.

And he said to me:

[Col. 0994C] Prophesy to the spirit;

prophesy, son of man,

and say to the spirit:

Thus says the Lord God:

Come from the four winds, O spirit,

and breathe upon these slain, that they may live again.

And I prophesied as he had commanded me,

and the spirit entered them, and they lived;

and they stood upon their feet, an exceedingly great army.

And he said to me:

Son of man,

all these bones are the house of Israel.

They themselves say: “Our bones have dried up,

and our hope has perished,

and we have been cut off.”

Therefore prophesy, and say to them:

Thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I will open your graves,

and bring you out from your tombs, my people,

[Col. 0994D] and bring you into the land of Israel.

And you shall know that I am the Lord,

when I open your graves,

and bring you out from your tombs, my people.

And I will give my spirit within you, and you shall live,

and I will cause you to rest upon your own soil;

and you shall know that I am the Lord who has spoken and acted,

says the Lord God.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

And you, son of man, take one piece of wood

and write upon it:

“For Judah and for the children of Israel [Note: [Col. 0994D] Many manuscripts read, not “his associates,” but “for his associates” in the dative. MART.] associated with him” [Al. “to his associates”].

And take another piece of wood,

and write upon it:

[Col. 0995A] “For Joseph [Note: [Col. 0995D] Thus the copies of the Canon read, together with all the manuscript codices of the sacred Scriptures. The printed editions retain the dative: “on the wood of Ephraim and of the whole house of Israel.” MART. The Palatine manuscript, as also those cited by Martianaeus, has the same reading. The holy Father likewise has in his Commentary, “the wood of Ephraim and the whole house of Israel.” The Greek has the accusative case; the Latin Vulgate editions prefer the dative.]—the wood of Ephraim and of the whole house of Israel,

and of his associates.”

And join them, one to the other, into one piece of wood for yourself,

and they shall become one in your hand.

But when the children of your people speak to you, saying:

“Will you not tell us what you intend by these things?”

you shall say to them:

Thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I will take the wood of Joseph, which is in the hand

of Ephraim,

and the tribes of Israel that are joined to him,

and I will place them together with the wood of Judah,

and make them one piece of wood;

and they shall be one in his hand.

The pieces of wood on which you have written shall be in your hand,

before their eyes.

And you shall say to them:

Thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the nations

[Col. 0995B] to which they went,

and gather them from every side,

and bring them to their own soil.

And I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains

of Israel,

and one king shall rule over all of them.

And they shall no longer be two nations,

nor shall they be divided into two kingdoms any longer.

And they shall no longer defile themselves with their idols,

their abominations, or any of their iniquities.

And I will save them from all their dwelling places in which they sinned,

and I will cleanse them.

And they shall be my people,

and I will be their God.

And my servant David shall be king over them,

and there shall be one shepherd over all of them.

They shall walk in my judgments,

and observe my commandments and perform them.

And they shall dwell upon the land that I gave to my servant

[Col. 0995C] Jacob,

in which your fathers dwelt.

And they themselves and their children,

and their children’s children, shall dwell upon it forever.

And David my servant shall be their prince forever.

And I will make a covenant of peace with them;

it shall be an everlasting covenant for them.

And I will establish them, and multiply them,

and set my sanctification in their midst forever.

And my tabernacle shall be among them,

and I will be their God,

and they shall be my people.

And the nations shall know that I am the Lord who sanctifies

Israel,

when my sanctification is in their midst forever.

[Chapter XXXVIII.] And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man,

[Col. 0995D] set your face against Gog, the land of Magog,

the prince of the chief of Meshech [Hebrew: Mesech] and Tubal,

and prophesy concerning him, and say to him:

Thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I am against you, Gog,

the prince of the chief of Meshech [Hebrew: Mesech] and Tubal.

And I will turn you around, and put a bit in your jaws,

and bring you out, and your whole army,

[Col. 0996A] horses and horsemen, all clothed in breastplates,

a great multitude, grasping spear and shield and sword;

Persians, Ethiopians, and Libyans with them,

all bearing shields and helmets.

Gomer and all his armies,

the house of Togarmah, the sides of the north,

and all its strength, and many peoples with you.

Prepare yourself, and equip yourself,

you and all your multitude that has been gathered

to you;

and be a command to them.

After many days you shall be visited;

in the latter years you shall come to a land that has recovered from the sword,

and has been gathered from many peoples to the mountains of Israel,

which had continually been desolate.

It was brought out from the peoples,

and they shall all dwell in it securely.

[Col. 0996B] Rising up like a storm, you shall come,

and like a cloud,

to cover the land—you and all your armies,

and many peoples with you.

Thus says the Lord God:

On that day thoughts shall rise into your heart,

and you shall devise an exceedingly evil plan,

and say:

“I will go up against a land without walls;

I will come against those at rest who dwell securely.

All these dwell without walls;

they have no bars or gates,

so that you may seize spoil and take plunder,

to lay your hand upon those who had been desolate and afterward restored,

and upon the people gathered from the nations,

who have begun to possess and to be [Note: [Col. 0995D] Some books read, “inhabitants of Jerusalem, the navel of the earth.” Martianaeus found in some of his copies, “an inhabitant of Jerusalem, the navel of the earth.” The Hebrew is [Hebrew text omitted in the supplied text], “inhabitants upon Mount Tabor.” The rest is well known: Jerusalem was regarded by the ancients as the center of the earth; hence Ezekiel above, chapter V: “This is Jerusalem: I have placed her in the midst of the nations.”] inhabitants of the navel

of the earth.”

[Col. 0996C] Sheba, Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish,

and all its young lions shall say to you:

“Have you come to take spoil?

Behold, you have gathered your multitude to seize plunder,

to carry away silver and gold,

to take away equipment and wealth,

and to seize countless booty.”

Therefore prophesy, son of man,

and say to Gog:

Thus says the Lord God:

“Will you not know on that day, when my people Israel

dwells securely?

And you shall come from your place, from the farthest parts of the north,

you and many peoples with you,

all riding horses,

a great assembly and a powerful army.

And you shall go up against my people Israel like a cloud,

to cover the land.

You shall be in the latter days,

[Col. 0996D] and I will bring you against my land,

so that the nations may know [Al. adds “all”] me,

when I have been sanctified in you before their eyes,

O Gog.

Thus says the Lord God:

You are the one of whom I spoke in former days,

by the hand of my servants, the prophets of Israel,

[Col. 0997A] who prophesied in those days and times [Al. “in those days and at those times”],

that I would bring you against them.

And it shall come to pass on that day, on the day when Gog comes upon the land

of Israel, says the Lord God,

that my indignation shall rise in my fury.

And in my jealousy,

in the fire of my wrath, I have spoken.

For on that day there shall be a great commotion over the land

of Israel;

and the fish of the sea, and the birds of the heavens,

and the beasts of the field shall tremble before me.
and every creeping thing that moves upon the ground,

and all human beings who are upon the face of the earth:

And the mountains shall be overturned, and the hedges shall fall,

and every wall shall collapse to the ground.

And I will summon against him, upon all my mountains, the sword,

says the Lord God:

each man’s sword shall be directed against his brother.

And I will judge him with pestilence and bloodshed,

[Col. 0997B] and with a torrential rain and immense hailstones:

I will rain fire and brimstone upon him and upon his army,

and upon the many peoples who are with him.

And I will magnify myself and sanctify myself,

and I shall make myself known in the eyes of many nations,

and they shall know that I am the Lord.

### Chapter XXXIX

But you, son of man, prophesy

against Gog, and say:

Thus says the Lord God:

Behold, I am against you, Gog,

prince and chief of Mosoch and Thubal:

And I will turn you about, and lead you out [Al. lead you back],

and cause you to come up from the far north,

and bring you upon the mountains of Israel.

And I will strike your bow from your left hand,

and cast your arrows from your right hand [Al. and I will cast you down].

Upon the mountains of Israel you shall fall, you and all your armies,

[Col. 0997C] and your peoples [Al. omits “your”] who are with you:

I have given you to the beasts, to the birds, to every winged creature,

and to the beasts of the earth, for devouring.

Upon the face of the field you shall fall,

for I have spoken, says the Lord God.

And I will send fire upon Magog,

and upon those who dwell securely in the islands,

and they shall know that I am the Lord.

And I will make my holy name known in the midst of my people Israel,

and I will no longer profane my holy name,

and the nations shall know that I am the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.

Behold, it is coming and it has happened, says the Lord God [Al. omits “God”];

this is the day of which I have spoken.

And the inhabitants shall go out from the cities [Al. towns] of Israel,

and shall kindle and burn the weapons:

shield and spears, bow and arrows,

hand-staves and lances,

[Col. 0997D] and they shall burn them with fire for seven years.

And they shall not carry wood from the regions,

nor cut it from the forests,

because they shall burn the weapons with fire;

and they shall plunder those by whom they had been plundered,

and they shall despoil their despoilers, says the Lord God.

And it shall come to pass on that day:

I will give Gog a named burial place in Israel,

the valley of the travelers, east of the sea,

which shall cause passers-by to be astonished:

and there they shall bury Gog

and all his multitude,

and the valley shall be called “the Valley of the Multitude of Gog.”

And the house of Israel shall bury them,

in order to cleanse the land for seven months.

And all the people of the land shall bury them,

and the day on which I was glorified shall be named for them,

says the Lord God.

[Col. 0998A] And they shall appoint men continually to inspect the land,

to bury and search out those who remained

upon the face of the earth,

in order to cleanse it.

After seven months they shall begin to search,

and they shall go about traversing the land.

And when they see a human bone, they shall set up a marker beside it,

until the buriers bury it in the Valley of the Multitude of Gog.

And the name of the city shall be Amona,

and they shall cleanse the land.

But you, son of man,

thus says the Lord God:

Say to every bird and to all winged creatures,

and to all the beasts of the field:

Gather together, hurry, assemble from every side for my sacrifice,

which I am offering [Al. have offered] for you,

a great sacrifice upon the mountain of Israel,

[Col. 0998B] so that you may eat flesh and drink blood.

You shall eat the flesh of mighty men,

and drink the blood of the princes of the earth:

of rams, lambs, and goats, and bulls,

of fattened animals, and of every fat creature.

And you shall eat fat until you are satisfied,

and drink blood until you are drunk,

from the sacrifice which I will offer [Al. have offered] for you.

And you shall be satisfied at my table with horse and

with the mighty rider,

and with every warrior, says the Lord God.

And I will set my glory among the nations,

and all the nations shall see my judgment, which I have executed,

and my hand, which I have laid upon them.

And the house of Israel shall know that I am the Lord their God,

[Col. 0998C] from that day and thereafter.

And the nations shall know [Al. adds “all”] that the house of Israel was taken captive in its iniquity [Al. because of its iniquities],

because they abandoned me, and I hid my face from them,

and delivered them into the hands of their enemies,

and they all fell by the sword.

I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and their crime,

and I hid my face from them.

Therefore, thus says the Lord God:

Now I will restore the captivity of Jacob,

and I will have mercy on all the house [Al. on the whole house] of Israel,

and I will be zealous for my holy name.

And they shall bear their shame,

and all their transgression by which they transgressed against me,

when they dwell securely in their own land, fearing no one.

[Col. 0998D] And when I have brought them back from the peoples,

and gathered them from the lands of their enemies,

and have been sanctified in them in the eyes of very many nations,

they shall know that I am the Lord their God,

because [Al. when] I carried them away among the nations,

and gathered them upon their own land,

and will leave none of them there.

And I will no longer hide my face from them,

because I have poured out my spirit upon the whole house of Israel,

says the Lord God.

### Chapter XL

In the twenty-fifth year of our exile,

at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month,

in the fourteenth year after the city was struck,

on that very day the hand of the Lord came upon me,

and he brought me there.

[Col. 0999A] In the visions of God he brought me into the land of Israel,

and set me upon a very high mountain;

upon it there was something like a city-building, sloping toward the south.

And he brought me there,

and behold, there was a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze,

with a linen cord in his hand

and a measuring reed in his hand.

He was standing at the gate,

and that same man spoke to me:

Son of man,

see with your eyes and hear with your ears,

and set your heart upon everything that I shall show you,

for you have been brought here so that they may be shown to you.

Declare everything that you see to the house of Israel.

And behold, an outer wall surrounded the house on every side,

and in the man’s hand was a measuring reed six cubits long,

including a handbreadth.

[Col. 0999B] And he measured the width of the building with one reed,

and its height also with one reed.

And he came to the gate that faced toward the eastern road,

and went up its steps.

And he measured the threshold of the gate: one reed in width,

that is, one threshold, one reed in width;

and one chamber, one reed in length

and one reed in width;

and between the chambers, five cubits;

and the threshold of the gate beside the inner vestibule of the gate,

one reed.

And he measured the vestibule of the gate: eight cubits,

and its front: two cubits.

The vestibule of the gate was on the inside.

Now the chambers of the gate facing the eastern road were three on one side

and three on the other;

all three had the same measurement,

and the fronts on both sides had the same measurement.

[Col. 0999C] And he measured the width of the gate’s threshold: ten cubits,

and the length of the gate: thirteen cubits.

And the border before the chambers was one cubit,

and the border at each end was one cubit;

the chambers were six cubits on each side.

And he measured the gate from the roof of one chamber to the roof opposite it:

its width was twenty-five cubits,

with doorway facing doorway.

And he made fronts extending for sixty cubits,

and in front of the gate was the court on every side, all around.

And before the face of the gate, which reached as far as the face of the inner gate vestibule,

there were fifty cubits.

And there were slanting windows in the chambers

and in their fronts, which were within the gate all around.

Likewise, there were windows in the vestibules all around on the inside,

[Col. 0999D] and before the fronts were palm-tree designs.

And he led me into the outer court,

and behold, there were chambers

and a pavement laid with stone throughout the court all around:

thirty chambers around the pavement.

And the pavement in front of the gates,

along the length of the gates, was lower.

And he measured the width from the front of the lower gate

to the front of the inner court on the outside:

one hundred cubits, toward the east and toward the north.

He also measured the gate that faced the northern road

of the outer court,

measuring both its length and its width.

Its chambers were three on one side and three on the other,

and its front and its vestibule were according to the measurement of the former gate:

its length was fifty cubits,

[Col. 1000A] and its width twenty-five cubits.

Its windows, its vestibule, and its carvings were according to the measurement of the gate that faced east.

It had seven steps by which one went up,

and a vestibule before it.

And the gate of the inner court was opposite the northern gate

and the eastern one,

and he measured from gate to gate: one hundred cubits.

And he led me to the southern road,

and behold, there was a gate that faced south.

And he measured its front and its vestibule

according to the preceding measurements.

And its windows and vestibules all around were like the other windows:

its length was fifty cubits

and its width twenty-five cubits [Al. “in which the length was fifty cubits and the width twenty-five, apart from the cubits”].

[Col. 1000B] It was approached by seven steps,

and there was a vestibule before its doors.

There were carved palm trees, one on one side and one on the other,

on its front.

And the gate of the inner court was on the southern road,

and he measured from gate to gate along the southern road: one hundred cubits.

And he brought me into the inner court by the southern gate,

and measured the gate according to the preceding measurements.

Its chamber, its front, and its vestibule

had the same measurements;

and its windows and its vestibule all around

were fifty cubits long

and twenty-five cubits wide.

And the vestibule was twenty-five cubits long

and five cubits wide.

And its vestibule opened toward the outer court,

[Col. 1000C] with its palm trees on the front,

and there were eight steps [Al. adds “of it”] by which one went up to it [Al. toward it].

And he brought me into the inner court by the eastern road,

and measured the gate according to the preceding measurements.

Its chamber, its front, and its vestibule were as above;

and its windows and its vestibules all around

were fifty cubits long

and twenty-five cubits wide.

And its vestibule—that is, toward the outer court—

had carved palm trees on its front, on both sides,

and it was approached by eight steps.

And he brought me to the gate that faced north,

and measured it according to the preceding measurements:

its chamber, its front,

[Col. 1000D] and its vestibule,

and its windows all around,

were fifty cubits long

and twenty-five cubits wide.

And its vestibule faced the outer court,

and there was palm-tree carving on its front, on both sides,

and it was approached by eight steps.

And beside each chamber there was a doorway in the fronts [Al. doors] of the gates;

there they washed the burnt offering.

And in the vestibule of the gate there were two tables on one side

and two tables on the other,

on which the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering were slaughtered.

And on the outer side, as one goes up to the doorway of the gate that leads northward, there were two tables;

and on the other side, before the vestibule of the gate, two tables.

Four tables on one side and four tables on the other:

[Col. 1001A] there were eight tables beside the gate, upon which they slaughtered.

And there were four tables for the burnt offering, constructed of squared stones,

one and a half cubits long,

one and a half cubits wide,

and one cubit high.

Upon them they placed [Al. shall place] the vessels in which the burnt offering and the sacrifice were slaughtered.

And their rims were one handbreadth, turned inward all around;

upon the tables were the flesh of the offering.

And outside the inner gate

were chambers for the singers in the inner court,

which was beside the gate facing north.

Their fronts faced toward the southern road,

one being beside the eastern gate that faced toward the northern road.

And he said to me:

This is the chamber that faces the southern road;

[Col. 1001B] it shall belong [Al. omits “it shall belong”] to the priests who keep watch over the temple.

The chamber that faces the northern road shall belong to the priests

who keep watch over the service of the altar.

These are the sons of Zadok,

who, from among the sons of Levi, approach the Lord to minister to him.

And he measured the court: one hundred cubits long

and one hundred cubits wide, square,

with the altar before the temple.

And he brought me into the vestibule of the temple,

and measured the vestibule: five cubits on one side

and five cubits on the other,

and the width of the doorway: three cubits on one side

and three cubits on the other.

The length of the vestibule was twenty cubits,

[Col. 1001C] and its width eleven cubits,

and it was approached by eight steps [Note: [Col. 1001C] In the Hebrew, instead of this number, there is a relative pronoun, “which.” Since the Septuagint interpreters rendered this as δέκα, “ten,” it is clear that they read it in place of [unreadable Hebrew text in the supplied source]; and this seems finally to be the genuine reading. But Jerome, following Symmachus, interprets it as “eight,” while in another respect Aquila’s second edition and Theodotion, who translate “eleven,” indicate that they read it in different ways; and the obvious emendation of the Hebrew codex does not allow the matter to be regarded as settled.]

And there were columns on the fronts [Al. “of them”],

one on one side and one on the other.

### Chapter XLI

And he brought me into the temple,

and measured the fronts: six cubits wide on one side

and six cubits wide on the other,

the width of the tabernacle.

And the width of the doorway was ten cubits,

and the sides of the doorway were five cubits on one side

and five cubits on the other.

And he measured its length: forty cubits,

[Col. 1002A] and its width: twenty cubits.

And entering inside, he measured the front of the doorway: two cubits,

and the doorway: six cubits,

and the width of the doorway: seven cubits.

And he measured its length: twenty cubits,

and its width: twenty cubits, before the face of the temple.

And he said to me:

This is the Holy of Holies.

And he measured the wall of the house: six cubits,

and the width of the side-chamber: four cubits all around

the house.

The side chambers were side by side, thirty-three twice over,

and there were projections that entered through the wall of the house

into the side chambers all around,

so that they might support them and not touch the wall of the temple.

And there was a circular passage, rising upward by a spiral staircase,

and leading around to the upper story of the temple.

[Col. 1002B] Therefore the temple was broader in its upper parts,

and thus one ascended from the lower levels to the upper levels

toward the middle.

And I saw that the house had height all around,

with the side chambers founded at a distance measured by a reed of six cubits.

And the width of the outer wall of the side chamber was five cubits,

and there was an inner space within the side chambers of the house.

And between the chambers there was a width of twenty cubits

all around the house on every side,

and a doorway of the side chamber toward the place of prayer:

one doorway toward the northern road,

and one doorway toward the southern road.

And the width of the place of prayer was five cubits all around.

And the building that was set apart and faced the road toward the sea

was seventy cubits wide.

[Col. 1002C] The wall of the building was five cubits wide all around,

and its length was ninety cubits.

And he measured the house: its length was one hundred cubits;

and the building that was set apart, together with its walls,

was also one hundred cubits long.

And the width before the face of the house,

and of the building that was set apart opposite it toward the east,

was one hundred cubits.

And he measured the length of the building opposite the face

of the structure that was set apart behind it:

“ecthetas” [Note: [Col. 1001D] The ancient Regius manuscript of the Bible reads EKTHETAS; the Colbertinus Aniciensis manuscript, no. 157, has haecthetas, with diphthong and aspiration, as do two manuscripts of Saint-Germain, nos. 3 and 16. Copies of the Canon have ecthetas, hecthetas, or et zethas. Two more recent biblical manuscripts of Saint-Germain, our nos. 5 and 164, read “and thecas.” In the sacred text of Saint Jerome’s Commentary on Ezekiel, we find this Greek word written in Greek in the very ancient Corbie manuscript, copied in Lombard letters: ἐκθέτας “on both sides ... and ἐκθέτας around,” and so forth. The exposition itself in the same Commentary agrees entirely with this reading: “Ecthetas,” Jerome says, “at Rome they call solaria—projecting platforms from the walls of upper rooms—or maeniana, after the person who first invented them; some Greeks call them ἐξώστρας.” I found the same word written in this way in three other manuscript copies of the Commentary: one at Colbert, another at the Abbey of Cluny, and a third at the monastery of Saint-Cygirannus. Therefore certain German scholars are unjustly criticized by Marianus Victorius when he says of Reuchlin and others: “But they not only failed to recognize the word; they even perversely fabricated the Greek expression ἐκθέτας from their own brains,” and so forth. They did not fabricate from their own brains what was read in that form eight hundred years ago in the more accurate books of Saint Jerome. Rather, Marianus himself was misled by the similarity between the Hebrew readings [illegible in the supplied source], rendered “athicim” and “athicia,” and the word “ethecas,” which he thought should be substituted here, supposing that Hebrew words had been retained by Jerome at this point. In any case, ἔκθεμα among the Greeks is a board or display set out before the eyes of passers-by, by which something is signified or explained. Therefore ἔκθεται signifies exposed places, or maeniana, which in French we call balcons, “balconies.” MART. — We have said elsewhere, and more than once, especially in Letter 106 to Sunnia and Fretela, no. 63, concerning ecthetas, which, according to Jerome’s own testimony, were called at Rome solaria or maeniana, after the person who first invented them. There is scarcely any doubt that this word derives from the Hebrew name [illegible in the supplied source], either athikim or athikiah, although the correct form in Latin manuscripts is not ethecas, as Victorius maintained, but ecthetas. As for what interpreters commonly say—that the meaning of the word can be assigned only by conjecture, and that the meaning handed down by Jerome is incompatible with the fact that in the following chapter he interprets the same word as “porticoes”—this can easily, I think, be explained and reconciled if one understands that the term refers to the projections placed upon porticoes: projecting or roofed porticoes in which one may bask in the sun. Saint Isidore likewise records, in Book XV, chapter 3 of the Etymologies, citing an ancient grammarian: “Maeniana, that is, ecthetas, are structures built upon porticoes.”]

on both sides one hundred cubits,

[Col. 1003A] together with the inner temple and the vestibules of the court.

Thresholds, slanting windows, and ecthetas all around,

on three sides, opposite each threshold,

and wood was laid around the entire circuit.

The ground extended up to the windows,

and the windows were closed above the doors.

And up to the inner house,

and outside along the entire wall, inside and out,

everything was according to the measurement.

And there were carved cherubim and palm trees,

with a palm tree between one cherub and another.

And each cherub had two faces:

the face of a man beside the palm tree on one side,

and the face of a lion beside the palm tree on the other side,

depicted throughout the entire house all around.

From the ground up to the upper parts of the gate,

cherubim and carved palm trees were upon the wall of the temple.

The threshold was square,

[Col. 1003B] and the face of the sanctuary faced directly toward the opposite face.

The wooden altar was three cubits high,

and its length was two cubits.

And it had its corners, its length,

and its wooden walls.

And he said to me:

This is the table that stands before the Lord.

And there were two doors in the temple and in the sanctuary.

And in the two doors, on each side, there were two folding leaves,

for there were two doors on each side of the doorways.

And cherubim and carved palm trees were engraved upon the doors of the temple,

as they were also depicted upon the walls.

For this reason the timbers were thicker on the outer front of the vestibule,

above which were slanting windows,

and the likeness of palm trees on either side upon the shoulders of the vestibule,

[Col. 1003C] corresponding to the sides of the house and the width of the walls.

### Chapter XLII

And he led me into the outer court by the road leading north,

and brought me into the chamber that was opposite the structure set apart,

and opposite the building facing north.

Along its length there was a northern doorway one hundred cubits long,

and it was fifty cubits wide,

opposite the twenty cubits of the inner court

and opposite the stone-laid pavement of the outer court,

where one portico was joined to a three-storied portico.

And before the chambers there was a walkway ten cubits wide,

facing inward, with a road one cubit wide.

And their doors were toward the north.

The chambers on the upper levels were narrower,

because they supported the porticoes that projected from them,

from the lower and middle levels of the building.

For they were three-storied and had no columns,

as the columns of the courts did.

Therefore they projected from the lower and middle levels,

fifty cubits above the ground.

And the outer surrounding wall corresponded to the chambers

that were on the road of the outer court before the chambers,

[Col. 1003D] [Col. 1004A] and its length was fifty cubits.

For the length of the chambers of the outer court was fifty cubits,

and the length before the face of the temple was one hundred cubits.

And beneath these chambers there was an entrance

from the east, by which those entering them came from the outer court.

The width of the surrounding wall of the court,

which was opposite the eastern road,

faced the building that was set apart,

and the chambers were before the building.

And there was a road before them,

like the chambers that were on the northern road.

Their length and their width were the same,

as were all their entrances, their forms, and their doors.

Like the doors of the chambers that were on the road

[Col. 1004B] facing south,

there was a door at the head of the road,

which lay before the vestibule of the structure set apart,

for those entering by the eastern road.

And he said to me:

The northern chambers and the southern chambers,

which are before the structure set apart,

are the holy chambers.

In them the priests who approach the Lord in the Holy of Holies eat.

There they shall place the Holy of Holies,

and the offerings for sin and for guilt,

for the place is holy.

But when the priests have entered,

they shall not go out from the holy place into the outer court.

There they shall put away the garments in which they minister,

because they are holy.

They shall put on other garments,

[Col. 1004C] and thus go out to the people.

And when he had completed measuring the inner house,

he led me out by the gate that faced the eastern road,

and measured it all around.

And he measured eastward with the measuring reed:

five hundred reeds with the measuring reed, all around.

And he measured northward:

five hundred reeds with the measuring reed, all around.

And toward the south

he measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed,

all around.

And toward the west

he measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.

On the four sides he measured it [Al. omits “it”],

its wall all around,

[Col. 1004D] five hundred cubits long

and five hundred cubits wide,

separating the sanctuary from the place of the common people.

### Chapter XLIII

And he led me to the gate that faced the eastern road.

And behold, the glory of the God of Israel was entering by the eastern road.

[Col. 1005A] And there was a sound like the sound of many waters,

and the earth shone with his majesty.

And I saw a vision like the appearance that I had seen

when he came to destroy the city,

and an appearance like the one I had seen beside the river Chebar.

And I fell upon my face.

And the majesty of the Lord entered the temple

by the gate that faced east.

And the spirit lifted me

and brought me into the inner court,

and behold, the house was filled with the glory of the Lord.

And I heard him speaking to me from the house,

and the man who stood beside me said to me:

Son of man,

this is the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet,

where I dwell in the midst of the children of Israel forever.

And the house of Israel shall no longer profane my holy name,

[Col. 1005B] they and their kings,

with their fornications,

with the ruins of their kings and with their high places.

They set their threshold beside my threshold,

and their doorposts beside my doorposts,

and there was a wall between me and them.

And they profaned my holy name by the abominations that they committed;

therefore I consumed them in my anger.

Now, then, let them put their fornication far away from me,

and the ruins of their kings away from me,

and I will dwell in their midst forever.

But you, son of man, show the house of Israel the temple,

so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities

and measure its construction,

and be ashamed of everything they have done:

the form of the house and its construction,

its exits and entrances,

and its entire plan,

[Col. 1005C] all its ordinances and its entire order [Al. omits “its”],

and show them all its laws,

and write them before their eyes,

so that they may observe all its plans [Al. distributions]

and its ordinances,

and carry them out.

This is the law of the house upon the summit of the mountain:

all its boundary all around is the Holy of Holies [Al. shall be the Holy of Holies].

This, then, is the law of the house.

These are the measurements of the altar,

in the most exact cubit, which had a cubit and a handbreadth.

Its hollow was one cubit,

and its width was one cubit,

and its rim extended all around to the edge,

one handbreadth [Al. one handbreadth wide].

This also was the trench of the altar.

From the hollow of the ground to the lower ledge,

two cubits,

and its width one cubit.

[Col. 1005D] From [Note: [Col. 1005] The manuscript codices have the word order reversed: “and from the greater ledge to the smaller ledge.” MART.] the lower ledge to the greater ledge,

four cubits,

and its width one cubit.

The Ariel itself was four cubits,

and from the Ariel upward were four horns.

And the Ariel was twelve cubits long

by twelve cubits wide,

square, with equal sides.

And the ledge was fourteen cubits long

by fourteen cubits wide at its four corners.

And its rim was half a cubit all around,

and its hollow was one cubit all around,

and its steps faced east.

[Col. 1006A] And he said to me:

Son of man,

thus says the Lord God:

These are the rites of the altar, on whatever day it is built,

so that burnt offerings may be offered upon it

and blood poured out.

And you shall give them to the priests and Levites who are of the seed of Zadok,

who approach me, says the Lord God,

so that they may offer me a bull from the herd for sin.

And taking some of its blood,

you shall place it upon its four horns,

and upon the four corners of the ledge,

and upon the rim all around.

And you shall cleanse it and make atonement for it.

And you shall take the bull that was offered for sin,

and burn it in the designated place of the house outside the sanctuary.

And on the second day you shall offer an unblemished male goat [Col. 1006B] for sin,

and they shall make atonement for the altar as they made atonement with the bull.

And when you have completed making atonement for it,

you shall offer an unblemished bull from the herd

and an unblemished ram from the flock.

And you shall offer them before the Lord,

and the priests shall throw salt upon them,

and offer them as a burnt offering to the Lord.

For seven days you shall offer a male goat for sin each day,

and they shall offer an unblemished bull from the herd

and an unblemished ram from the flock.

For seven days they shall make atonement for the altar and cleanse it,

and they shall fill its hand.

When the days have been completed,

on the eighth day and thereafter,

the priests shall perform your burnt offerings upon the altar,

and the offerings presented for peace.

And I shall be reconciled to you, says the Lord God.

### Chapter XLIV

And he turned me toward the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary,

which faced east,

and it was closed.

And the Lord said to me:

This gate shall be closed.

It shall not be opened,

and no man shall pass through it,

because the Lord God of Israel has entered through it.

It shall therefore be closed to the prince.

The prince himself shall sit in it,

to eat bread before the Lord.

He shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate,

and he shall go out by way of it.

And he brought me by way of the northern gate

before the house,

and I saw, and behold, the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord.

And I fell upon my face.

And the Lord said to me:

Son of man, set your heart

[Col. 1006D] and see with your eyes,

and hear with your ears everything that I speak to you

concerning all the ceremonies of the house of the Lord

and all its laws.

And set your heart upon the ways of the temple

at all the exits of the sanctuary.

And say to the house of Israel, which provokes me:

Thus says the Lord God:

Let all your crimes suffice you, house of Israel,

because you bring in foreign sons, uncircumcised in heart

and uncircumcised in flesh,

to be in my sanctuary and to profane my house.

And you offer my bread, the fat, and the blood,

[Col. 1007A] and you dissolve [Al. “dissolved”] my covenant in all your crimes.

And you did not keep the ordinances of my sanctuary,

and you appointed for yourselves guardians of my observances

in my sanctuary.

Thus says the Lord God:

No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh,

shall enter my sanctuary,

nor any foreign son who is among the children of Israel.

But the Levites also, who departed far from me in the error of the children of Israel,

and went astray from me after their idols,

and bore [Al. “shall bear”] their iniquity,

shall be [Al. “who were”] gatekeepers in my sanctuary

and doorkeepers of the house,

and ministers of the house.

They shall slaughter [Al. “they slaughtered”] the burnt offerings

and the sacrifices of the people,

[Col. 1007B] and they shall stand before them to minister to them

[Al. “they stood before them to minister on their behalf”].

Because they ministered to them [Al. “on their behalf”] before their idols,

and became for the house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity,

therefore I lifted up my hand against them, says the Lord God,

and they shall bear [Al. “they bore”] their iniquity.

And they shall not approach me to serve me as priests,

nor shall they come near any of my sanctuary,

near the Holy of Holies.

But they shall bear their shame

and the crimes they committed.

And I will make them doorkeepers of the house

in all its service

and in everything that shall be done [Al. “is done”] in it.

But the priests and Levites, the sons of Zadok,

who kept the ordinances of my sanctuary

[Col. 1007C] when the children of Israel went astray from me,

shall approach me to minister to me.

And they shall stand before me

to offer me the fat and the blood, says the Lord God.

They shall enter my sanctuary,

and they shall approach my table to minister to me,

and they shall keep my ordinances.

And when they enter the gates of the inner court,

they shall be clothed in linen garments.

Nothing woolen shall come upon them

when they minister at the gates of the inner court and within.

They shall have linen bands upon their heads,

and linen undergarments upon their loins,

and they shall not gird themselves in anything that causes sweat.

And when they go out to the outer court among the people,

they shall remove the garments in which they ministered,

[Col. 1007D] and put them away in the chamber of the sanctuary,

and put on other garments,

so that they do not sanctify the people with their garments.

They shall not shave their heads,

nor let their hair grow long,

but they shall trim their heads closely.

No priest shall drink wine

when he is about to enter the inner court.

And they shall not take a widow or a divorced woman as wives,

but virgins from the seed of the house of Israel.

They may also take a widow who was widowed by a priest.

And they shall teach my people what is holy

and what is profane,

[Col. 1008A] and show them the difference between clean and unclean.

And when there is a dispute,

they shall stand in my judgments and judge.

They shall keep my laws and my ordinances at all my appointed festivals,

and they shall sanctify my Sabbaths.

And they shall not enter in to a dead person,

lest they be defiled,

except for a father and mother,

and son and daughter,

and brother and sister

who has not had another husband [Note: [Col. 1007D] The word “another” is found neither in the Hebrew nor recognized by Jerome in his Commentary. See what we have noted there.]

with whom they may become defiled.

And after he has been cleansed,

seven days shall be counted for him.

And on the day of his entering the sanctuary, into the inner court,

to minister to me in the sanctuary,

he shall offer for his sin, says the Lord God [Al. “to the Lord God”].

They shall have no inheritance,

[Col. 1008B] for I am their inheritance.

You shall give them no possession in Israel, for I am their possession.

And they themselves shall eat the victim offered for sin and for guilt,

and every vow in Israel shall belong to them.

And the firstfruits of all the firstborn;

and all the offerings from everything that is offered

shall belong to the priests.

And you shall give the firstfruits of your food to the priest,

so that he may lay up a blessing for your house [Alt. his house].

The priests shall not eat any carcass,

or anything torn by a beast, whether of birds or livestock.

[Chapter XLV.] And when you begin to divide the land

by lot [Alt. as a possession],

you shall set apart an offering for the Lord, sanctified from the land,

twenty-five thousand in length

and ten thousand in width.

[Col. 1008C] It shall be holy throughout its entire boundary on every side.

And from every side there shall be a sanctified area,

five hundred by five hundred,

four-sided on every side,

with fifty cubits of open land around it.

And according to this measure you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand

and a width of ten thousand.

Within it shall be the temple and the Holy of Holies.

The sanctified portion of the land shall belong to the priests, ministers

of the Sanctuary, who draw near to minister to the Lord.

It shall be a place for houses for them and for the Sanctuary of holiness.

The twenty-five thousand in length

and the ten thousand in width shall belong to the Levites who [Alt.

But the Levites who] minister in the house.

They shall possess twenty chambers.

And you shall give the city’s possession five

[Col. 1008D] thousand in width

and twenty-five thousand in length,

corresponding to the separation of the Sanctuary,

for the whole house of Israel.

For the prince also, on this side and on that, there shall be a portion beside the separation of the Sanctuary

and beside the city’s possession,

opposite the front of the Sanctuary’s separation

and opposite the front of the city’s possession:

from the seaward side to the sea,

and from the eastern side to the east.

[Note: [Col. 1008D] Instead of *longitudinis autem* (“but of the length”), we read *longitudinem autem* (“but the length”) in all the manuscripts. MART.]

But the length along each portion

shall extend from the western boundary to the eastern boundary.

[Col. 1009A] His possession in Israel shall be land [Alt. of the land];

and the princes shall no longer despoil my people,

but shall give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.

Thus says the Lord God:

Let it be enough for you, princes of Israel.

Put an end to violence and plunder,

and practice judgment and righteousness.

Remove your boundaries from my people, says the Lord God.

You shall have a just balance, a just ephah, and a just bath.

The ephah and the bath shall be equal and of one measure,

so that the bath contains one-tenth of a kor,

and the ephah one-tenth of a kor.

According to the measure of the kor shall their weighing be equal.

The shekel shall contain twenty obols.

Twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels shall make a mina [Alt. make].

[Col. 1009B] And these are the firstfruits that you shall take:

a sixth part of an ephah from a kor of wheat,

and a sixth part of an ephah from a kor of barley.

The measure of oil—the bath of oil—is one-tenth of a kor;

ten baths make a kor,

because ten baths fill a kor.

And one ram from a flock of two hundred,

from those that nourish [Alt. nourish] Israel,

shall be offered as a sacrifice, a burnt offering, and a peace offering,

to make atonement for them, says the Lord God.

All the people of the land shall be bound to provide these firstfruits

for the prince in Israel.

The burnt offerings, sacrifices,

and drink offerings at the festivals, at the new moons, and

on the Sabbaths,

at all the festivals of the house of Israel,

shall be the prince’s responsibility.

He shall offer the sin offering, the burnt offering,

and the peace offerings,

to make atonement for the house of Israel.

[Col. 1009C] Thus says the Lord God:

In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take an unblemished bull from the herd,

and you shall make atonement for the Sanctuary.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering

and put it on the doorposts of the house,

on the four corners of the ledge of the altar,

and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.

You shall do likewise on the seventh day of the month for everyone

who has sinned through ignorance [Alt. who shall have sinned through ignorance]

and has been deceived by error,

and you shall make atonement [Alt. you shall make atonement] for the house.

In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month,

you shall have the feast of Passover.

For seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten [Alt. they shall eat].

On that day the prince shall offer for himself and for all the people of the land

a bull as a sin offering.

And during the seven days of the feast he shall offer as a burnt offering

to the Lord seven bulls

[Col. 1009D] and seven unblemished rams each day for seven

days,

and a male goat as a sin offering each day.

He shall make a grain offering of an ephah for each bull

and an ephah for each ram,

and a hin of oil for each ephah.

In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the feast,

he shall do the same for seven days as described above,

both for the sin offering and for the burnt offering,

and for the grain offering and the oil.

[Chapter XLVI.] Thus says the Lord God:

The gate of the inner court facing east shall be closed

during the six working days,

but on the Sabbath it shall be opened,

and it shall also be opened on the day of the new moon.

The prince shall enter by way of the vestibule of the outer gate and stand at the threshold of the gate.

[Col. 1010A] The priests shall offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings.

He shall worship at the threshold of the gate and then go out;

but the gate shall not be closed until evening.

The people of the land shall worship at the entrance of that gate

on the Sabbaths

and on the new moons before the Lord.

The burnt offering that the prince shall offer to the Lord shall be this:

on the Sabbath, six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram.

His grain offering shall be an ephah for the ram;

for [Alt. *for* is omitted] the lambs, the grain offering shall be whatever his hand can provide,

and a hin of oil for each ephah.

On the day of the new moon, he shall offer an unblemished bull from the herd,

and there shall be six lambs and unblemished rams.

He shall make a grain offering of an ephah for the bull

and an ephah for the ram.

For [Alt. *For* is omitted] the lambs, it shall be according to what his hand

[Col. 1010B] can provide,

and a hin of oil for each ephah.

When the prince is about to enter,

he shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate

and go out by the same way.

When the people of the land enter before the Lord at the festivals,

whoever enters through the northern gate to worship

shall go out by way of the southern gate.

Whoever enters by way of the southern gate

shall go out by way of the northern gate.

He shall not return by way of the gate through which he entered,

but shall go out opposite it.

The prince shall enter in their midst when they enter,

and he shall go out with them when they go out.

At the market-days and at the festivals there shall be a grain offering

of an ephah for the bull

[Col. 1010C] and an ephah for the ram.

For the lambs, the grain offering shall be according to what his hand

can provide,

and a hin of oil for each ephah.

When the prince offers a freewill burnt offering or voluntary peace offerings to the Lord,

the gate facing east shall be opened for him.

He shall offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings

as is done on the Sabbath,

and he shall go out; the gate shall be closed after he has gone out.

He shall offer an unblemished lamb of the same year [Alt. a year-old lamb]

as a burnt offering to the Lord every day.

He shall offer it continually in the morning.

He shall make a grain offering over it, according to [*cata*; Alt. *cata* is omitted], morning by morning,

a sixth part of an ephah,

and a third part of a hin of oil, to mix it [Alt. and] with the fine flour.

A grain offering to the Lord,

a perpetual and continual offering.

He shall offer [Alt. You shall offer] the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil

[Col. 1010D] according to [*cata*; Alt. *cata* is omitted], morning by morning,

as a perpetual burnt offering.

Thus says the Lord God:

If the prince gives a gift to one of his sons,

it shall be his sons’ inheritance;

they shall possess it as an inheritance.

But if he gives a bequest from his inheritance to one of his servants,

it shall belong to that servant until the year of release,

and [Alt. but] it shall return to the prince.

His inheritance, however, shall belong to his sons.

The prince shall not take any of the people’s inheritance by force,

or any part of their possession.

Rather, from his own possession he shall give an inheritance to his sons,

so that my people may not be scattered, each one from his possession.

And he brought me through the entrance that was beside the gate

[Col. 1011A] to the storerooms of the Sanctuary for the priests,

which faced north.

There was [Alt. behold, there was] a place extending westward.

And he said to me:

This is the place where the priests shall cook the guilt offering

and the sin offering,

where they shall cook the sacrifice,

so that they do not carry it out into the outer court

and sanctify the people.

And he brought me out into the outer court

and led me around the four corners of the court.

And behold, there was a small court in the corner of the court,

a small court at each corner of the court.

In the four corners of the court were small courts arranged,

forty cubits long

and thirty wide.

All four had one measurement.

There was a wall surrounding the four small courts,

and kitchens had been constructed beneath the porticoes all around.

[Col. 1011B] And he said to me:

This is the house of the kitchens,

where the ministers of the house of the Lord [Alt. *of the Lord* is omitted]

shall cook the sacrifices of the people.

[Chapter XLVII.] And he turned [Alt. I turned] me toward the gate of the house,

and behold, water was coming out from beneath the threshold of the house

toward the east.

For the front of the house faced east,

and the waters descended along the right side of the temple,

south of the altar.

And he brought me out by way of the northern gate

and led me around toward the outer gate,

the way facing east.

And behold, waters were flowing from the right side.

When the man went out eastward with a measuring cord in his hand,

he measured a thousand cubits.

[Col. 1011C] And he led me through the water, up to the ankles.

Again he measured a thousand,

and led me through the water, up to the knees.

And he measured a thousand

and led me through the water, up to the loins.

And he measured a thousand,

and there was a torrent that I could not cross,

because the waters of the deep torrent had risen

and could not be forded.

And he said to me:

Surely you have seen this, son of man.

And he brought me out
