and turned me toward the bank of the torrent.

When I had turned,

behold, there were very many trees on the bank of the torrent, on both sides.

And he said to me:

These waters that flow out toward the eastern sand-hills

[Col. 1011D] and descend toward the plain of the wilderness

shall enter the sea and flow out,

and the waters shall be healed.

Every living creature that moves, wherever the torrent comes,

shall live.

There shall be very many fish when these waters reach there;

they shall be healed, and everything to which the torrent comes

shall live.

Fishermen shall stand beside it.

From Engaddi to Engallim there shall be a place for drying nets.

Its fish will be of very many kinds,

[Col. 1012A] like the fish of the great sea, exceedingly numerous.

But its shores and marshes shall not be healed;

they shall be given over to salt.

On both banks of the torrent, on either side,

every kind of fruit-bearing tree shall grow.

Its leaf shall not fall,

and its fruit shall not fail.

Each month it shall produce firstfruits,

because its waters flow out from the Sanctuary.

Its fruit shall be for food,

and its leaves for medicine.

Thus says the Lord God:

This is the boundary within which you shall possess the land among the twelve tribes of Israel,

because Joseph has a double portion.

You shall possess it equally, each one like his brother,

the land over which I raised my hand to give it to your fathers.

This land shall fall to you as a possession.

[Col. 1012B] This is the boundary of the land:

on the northern side, from the Great Sea by way of [Note: [Col. 1011D] Here the manuscript codices corruptly read *Bethalon*; then, in the first verse of the following chapter, the same name is written *Ethlon* and *Aethelon* in those same books. MART.] Ethalon,

as one comes to Sadada,

Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the boundary of Damascus

and the border of Hamath,

the house of [Note: [Col. 1012D] It may perhaps be more correctly read in the Commentary of the holy Doctor as *the court of Thicon*. The Hebrew likewise has [the Hebrew term is not reproduced in the supplied text].] Atthicon,

which is beside the boundary of Hauran.

The boundary shall run from the sea to the court of Enon,

the boundary of Damascus,

and from the north toward the north, with the boundary of Hamath.

This is the northern side [Alt. *but* is omitted].

The eastern side shall be from the middle of Hauran,

and from the middle of Damascus,

and from the middle of Gilead,

and from the middle of the land of Israel.

The Jordan shall mark the boundary as far as the eastern sea.

You shall also measure the eastern side.

The southern side shall be toward the south,

from Tamar as far as the waters of Meribah at Kadesh,

and [Alt. Kadesh also is] the torrent as far as the Great Sea.

[Col. 1012C] This is the southern side, toward the south [Alt. *this is*].

The western side shall be the Great Sea,

from the boundary straight ahead until one comes to Hamath.

This is the western side.

You shall divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel

and assign it to yourselves as an inheritance,

and also to the resident aliens who have joined you,

who have fathered children among you.

They shall be to you like native Israelites;

with you they shall divide the inheritance in the midst of the tribes

of Israel.

In whichever tribe the resident alien resides,

there you shall give him his possession, says the Lord God.

[Chapter XLVIII.] And these are the names of the tribes, from the northern boundaries,

along the way of Ethalon,

toward Hamath,

the court of Enon, the boundary of Damascus, toward the north,

beside Hamath.

Its eastern side [Alt. *from the eastern side*] shall be the sea:

one portion for Dan.

And beside the boundary [Alt. *from the boundary*] of Dan,

from the eastern side to the western side,

one portion for Asher.

And beside the boundary of Asher,

from the eastern side to the western side,

one portion for Naphtali.

And beside the boundary of Naphtali,

from the eastern side to the western side,

one portion for Manasseh.

And beside the boundary of Manasseh,

from the eastern side to the western side,

one portion for Ephraim.

[Col. 1013A] And beside the boundary of Ephraim,

from the eastern side to the western side,

one portion for Reuben.

And beside the boundary of Reuben,

from the eastern side to the western side,

one portion for Judah.

And beside the boundary of Judah,

from the eastern side to the western side,

there shall be the offering that you shall set apart,

twenty-five thousand in width and in length,

corresponding to the individual portions from the eastern side to the western side.

The Sanctuary shall be in its midst.

The offering that you shall set apart for the Lord

shall be twenty-five thousand in length

and ten thousand in width.

This shall be the offering of the Sanctuary for the priests:

toward the north, twenty-five thousand in length;

toward the sea, ten thousand in width;

also toward the east, ten thousand in width;

and toward the south, twenty-five thousand in length.

[Col. 1013B] The Sanctuary of the Lord shall be in its midst.

The Sanctuary shall belong to the priests, the sons of Zadok,

who kept my ordinances

and did not go astray when the Israelites went astray,

as the Levites also went astray.

The offering from the offering of the land shall be theirs,

a Holy of Holies,

beside the boundary of the Levites.

The Levites likewise shall have a portion beside the priests’ boundary,

twenty-five thousand in length

and ten thousand in width.

The whole length shall be twenty-five thousand,

and the width ten thousand.

They shall not sell any of it,

nor exchange it,

nor shall the offering of the land be transferred,

because it has been sanctified to the Lord.

The remaining five thousand in width

by twenty-five thousand

shall be common land for the city, for habitation and open land.

[Col. 1013C] The city shall be in its midst.

And these shall be its measurements:

on the northern side, four thousand five hundred;

on the southern side, four thousand five hundred;

on the eastern side, four thousand five hundred;

and on the western side, four thousand five hundred.

The open land belonging to the city shall be two hundred fifty toward the north,

two hundred fifty toward the south,

two hundred fifty toward the east,

and two hundred fifty toward the sea.

The remaining length, corresponding to the offering of the Sanctuary,

ten thousand toward the east

and ten thousand toward the west,

[Col. 1013D] shall be like the offering of the Sanctuary.

Its produce shall be for bread [Alt. food for those],

who serve the city.

Those who serve the city

shall come from all the tribes of Israel.

The entire offering, twenty-five thousand

by twenty-five thousand, square,

shall be set apart as the offering of the Sanctuary

[Col. 1014A] and as the possession of the city.

The remainder shall belong to the prince,

on every side of the offering of the Sanctuary

and of the possession of the city,

opposite the twenty-five-thousand portion of the offering,

as far as the eastern boundary.

Likewise toward the sea [Alt. *from the sea*],

opposite the twenty-five thousand,

as far as the boundary of the sea,

it shall belong to the prince’s portions.

The offering of the Sanctuary

and the Sanctuary of the temple shall be in its midst.

The possession of the Levites and the possession

of the city shall be in the midst of the prince’s portions.

It shall lie between the boundary of Judah and the boundary of Benjamin,

and shall belong to the prince.

And for the remaining tribes:

from the eastern side to the western side,

one portion for Benjamin.

[Col. 1014B] Opposite the boundary of Benjamin,

from the eastern side to the western side,

one portion for Simeon.

And beside the boundary of Simeon,

from the eastern side to the western side,

one portion for Issachar.

And beside the boundary of Issachar,

from the eastern side to the western side,

one portion for Zebulun.

And beside the boundary of Zebulun,

from the eastern side to the side of the sea,

one portion for Gad.

And beside the boundary of Gad, toward the southern side, to the south,

the end shall extend from Tamar to the waters of Meribah at Kadesh,

with the inheritance opposite the Great Sea.

This is the land that you shall assign [Alt. measure] by lot to the tribes of Israel,

and these are their divisions, says the Lord God.

[Col. 1014C] And these are the exits of the city:

on the northern side, you shall measure four thousand five hundred.

The gates of the city shall bear the names [Alt. *from the people*]

of the tribes of Israel.

There shall be three gates on the north:

one gate of Reuben,

one gate of Judah,

one gate of Levi.

On the eastern side, four thousand five hundred,

and three gates:

one gate of Joseph,

one gate of Benjamin,

one gate of Dan.

On the southern side, you shall measure four thousand five hundred,

and three gates:

one gate of Simeon,

one gate of Issachar,

[Col. 1014D] one gate of Zebulun.

On the western side, four thousand five hundred,

and its three gates:

one gate of Gad,

one gate of Asher,

one gate of Naphtali.

Its circumference shall be eighteen thousand.

And the name of the city from that day shall be: “The Lord is there.”

[Col. 1013] Here ends the book of the prophet Ezekiel.

[Col. 1013]

[THE TWELVE BOOKS OF THE PROPHETS.]

PREFACE OF ST. JEROME TO THE TWELVE PROPHETS

[Col. 1013D] The order of the twelve prophets among the Hebrews is not the same as it is among us [Alt. *is*]. [Note: That is, in the Greek exemplars, to whose exact rule the Latin Vulgate translation was made: Amos is second, Micah third, Joel fourth, Obadiah fifth, and Jonah sixth; in listing the rest, they agree with the Hebrew. See the preface to the Commentary on Joel.]

Therefore, according to what is read there, they have also been arranged here.

Hosea is concise and speaks, as it were, in brief statements.

Joel is clear at the beginning, but more obscure at the end.

And up to Malachi, each has his own distinctive character [Note: These words, “each has his own distinctive character,” seem to us to have been misplaced, and to belong at the end of the sentence. They believe that the meaning would certainly be much more polished and clearer there.]

—Malachi, whom the Hebrews maintain was Ezra the scribe and teacher of the Law.

And because it would take too long to discuss everyone now,

I wish only to inform you of this, Paula and Eustochium:

that the twelve prophets constitute one book;

that Hosea was contemporary [Greek: *σύγχρονον*] with Isaiah;

and that Malachi lived in the time of Haggai and Zechariah.

Where the time is not stated in the title,

they prophesied under those kings under whom those who have titles before them also prophesied.

THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET HOSEA BEGINS

[Col. 1015]

[Col. 1015B] [Chapter I.] [Note: [Col. 1015D] Martianus found in both copies of the Canon of Hebrew Truth the following annotation: Among the Hebrews there are two opinions concerning these four verses placed at the beginning. Most say that Ezra the scribe supplied such a title in all the prophets, so that, once each prophet’s name had been written above it, one could know whose prophecy followed. This Ezra is the one who is described as the last of the prophets under the name Malachi. Others say that the titles were supplied by the prophets themselves through the Holy Spirit, just as the rest was written. Many learned men of more recent times have embraced this opinion, especially for these reasons: first, it cannot at all be proved that Hosea prophesied for so long under these kings; second, it is not credible that he would have inscribed his prophecies under the names of the kings of Judah, under whose rule he did not live; finally, these four verses seem easily to be the heading of the whole work of the twelve prophets, whereas what follows—“The beginning of the Lord’s speaking in Hosea”—is properly the beginning of Hosea’s individual prophecy. Consult the sacred critics, if you wish.]

The word of the Lord that came to Hosea son of Beeri,

in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings

of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king

of Israel.

The beginning of the Lord’s speaking through Hosea:

And the Lord said to Hosea:

Go, take for yourself a wife of fornication,

and make for yourself children of fornication,

because the land will surely commit fornication, turning away from the Lord.

And he went and took Gomer, daughter of Diblaim.

She conceived and bore him a son.

And the Lord said to him:

Call his name Jezreel,

because in a little while

I shall visit the bloodshed of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu,

and I shall bring the kingdom of the house of Israel to an end.

And on that day I shall break the bow of Israel in the valley

of Jezreel.

And she conceived again and bore a daughter.

And he said to her:

[Col. 1015C] Call her name “Without Mercy,”

because I will no longer continue to have mercy on the house of Israel,

but I will utterly forget them.

But I will have mercy on the house of Judah,

and I will save them by the Lord their God.

I will not save them by bow, or sword,

or war, or horses, or horsemen.

And she weaned her, the one who was “Without Mercy.”

And she conceived and bore a son.

And he said:

Call his name “Not My People,”

because you are not my people,

and I will not be yours.

And the number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea,

which cannot be measured

and cannot be counted.

And it shall be in the place where it was said to them,

“You are not my people,”

that it shall be said to them,

“Children of the living God.”

[Col. 1015D] And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall gather together,

[Col. 1016B] and they shall appoint one head for themselves,

and they shall come up from the land,

because great is the day of Jezreel.

[Chapter II.] Say to your brothers, “My People,”

and to your sister, “She Has Obtained Mercy.”

Bring charges against your mother, bring charges,

because she is not my wife,

and I am not her husband.

Let her remove her fornications from her face

and her adulteries from between her breasts,

lest I strip her naked

and set her as she was on the day of her birth.

I will make her like a wilderness

and set her like an impassable land,

and I will kill her with thirst.

I will not have mercy on her children,

because they are children of fornication.

For their mother has committed fornication;

she who conceived them has been disgraced.

For she said:

“I will go after my lovers,

who give me my bread and my water,

[Col. 1016C] my wool and my flax,

my oil and my drink.”

Therefore, behold, I will hedge your way with thorns

and wall it in with a barrier,

and she shall not find her paths.

She will pursue her lovers but will not overtake them;

she will seek them but will not find them.

And she will say:

“I will go and return to my first husband,

because it was better for me then than now.”

But she did not know that I gave her grain and wine and oil,

and that I multiplied silver for her, and gold,

which they used for Baal.

Therefore I will turn [Alt. return]

and take back my grain in its season and my wine in its season,

and I will reclaim my wool and my flax,

which covered her shame.

And now I will expose her folly in the sight of her lovers,

[Col. 1016D] [Col. 1017A] and no man will rescue her from my hand.

I will put an end to all her joy,

her festival, her new moon,

her Sabbath,

and all her appointed feasts.

I will destroy her vine and her fig tree,

of which she said, “These are my wages,

which my lovers gave me.”

And I will make [Note: [Col. 1017D] The corrected San-Germanus Canon reads in this way; other manuscripts have the feminine form: “I will make her into a forest, and the wild beast of the field will devour her,” and so forth. MART.] them [Alt. her] into a forest,

and the wild beast of the field shall devour it [Alt. her].

I will visit upon her the days of the Baals,

when she burned incense to them,

adorned herself with her earring and her necklace,

and went after her lovers,

while she forgot me,

says the Lord.

Therefore, behold, I will allure her

and lead her into the wilderness,

and I will speak to her heart.

And I will give her vineyards from that place,

and the valley of Achor as a door of hope.

[Col. 1017B] And there she shall sing as in the days of her youth,

and as in the days when she came up from the land of Egypt.

And on that day, says the Lord,

she will call me “My Husband,”

and she will no longer call me [Note: [Col. 1017D] In all the manuscripts we read *Baalim* instead of *Baali*. The scribes corrupted it through ignorance of the Hebrew language. *Baali* means “my lord,” or “my husband,” that is, “the one who has me”; *Baalim*, however, is the name of the demons. MART.] “My Baal.”

I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth,

and she shall no longer remember their name.

And on that day I will make a covenant for them

with the wild beast of the field,

with the birds of heaven,

and with the creeping things of the earth.

I will break bow, sword, and war from the land,

and I will make them lie down securely.

I will betroth you to me forever.

I will betroth you to me in righteousness and judgment,

in mercy and compassion.

I will betroth you to me in faithfulness,

and you shall know that I am the Lord.

And on that day:

“I will answer,” says the Lord.

“I will answer the heavens,

[Col. 1017C] and they shall answer the earth.

And the earth shall answer the grain,

the wine, and the oil,

and these shall answer Jezreel.

And I will sow her for myself in the land,

and I will have mercy on her who was ‘Without Mercy.’

And I will say to ‘Not My People,’ ‘You are my people,’

and he shall say, ‘You are my God.’”

[Chapter III.] And the Lord said to me:

Go again and love a woman who is loved by a friend

and is an adulteress,

as the Lord loves the children of Israel,

while they turn to foreign gods

and love raisin cakes.

And I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver,

a kor of barley,

and half a kor of barley.

And I said to her:

You shall wait for me many days.

You shall not commit fornication,

and you shall not belong to a man.

And I too shall wait for you.

For the children of Israel shall sit many days without a king

[Col. 1017D] and without a prince,

without sacrifice and without [Note: [Col. 1017D] Jerome, very learnedly, read in his Hebrew exemplar, instead of the reading now current, a word almost identical in form and sound [the Hebrew terms are not reproduced in the supplied text]. The first means “altar,” indicating, in the prophet’s view and in the context of the entire prophecy, that the Hebrews would long and greatly lack this and the other instruments of true religion. The other means “image” or “statue,” by which idolatrous worship is signified. It is scarcely reasonable that the Prophet should threaten the people with the abandonment of false gods as though it were some very serious kind of calamity. Moreover, the Septuagint before Jerome had read the passage in the same way as he did when they translated it as *θυσιαστηρίου* (“of the altar”).]

an altar,

without an ephod,

and without teraphim.

After this the children of Israel shall return

and seek the Lord their God

and David their king.

They shall fear the Lord and his goodness

in the latter days.

[Chapter IV.] Hear the word of the Lord, children of Israel,

for the Lord has a lawsuit with the inhabitants of the land.

There is no truth,

no mercy,

and no knowledge of God in the land.

Cursing, lying, murder, theft,

and adultery have overflowed,

and bloodshed has touched bloodshed.

Therefore the land shall mourn,

and everyone who lives in it shall grow weak,

together with the beasts of the field

and the birds of heaven.

Even the fish of the sea shall be gathered together.

Nevertheless, let no one judge,

and let no one accuse another.

For your people are like those

who contend with the priest.

You will stumble today,

and the prophet also with you;

by night I have silenced your mother.

[Col. 1018B] My people have been silenced

because they have had no knowledge.

Because you rejected knowledge,

I will reject you [Alt. *and I too*],

so that you shall not serve as my priest.

And because you have forgotten the law of your God,

I too will forget your children.

The more numerous they became,

the more they sinned against me.

I will change their glory into disgrace.

They consume the sin of my people,

and they lift up their souls toward their iniquity.

And it shall be: like people, like priest.

I will visit his ways upon him,

and I will repay him for his thoughts.

They shall eat,

but shall not be satisfied.

They have committed fornication,

but have not ceased,

[Col. 1018C] because they abandoned the Lord by failing to keep watch.

Fornication, wine, and drunkenness take away the heart.

My people consulted their wooden image,

and their staff announced things to them.

For a spirit of fornication has deceived them,

and they have committed fornication against their God.

They sacrificed on the mountaintops

and burned incense on the hills,

beneath the oak, the poplar, and the terebinth,

because its shade was good.

Therefore your daughters shall commit fornication,

and your daughters-in-law shall commit adultery.

I will not visit your daughters when they commit fornication,

nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery.

For they themselves consort with prostitutes,

and sacrifice with effeminate men,

and a people without understanding shall be beaten.

[Col. 1018D] If you commit fornication, Israel,

let Judah at least not offend.

Do not enter Gilgal,

and do not go up to Beth-Aven,

and do not swear, “As the Lord lives.”

[Col. 1019A] For Israel has turned aside like a wanton heifer.

Now the Lord will pasture them like a lamb in an open place.

Ephraim is joined to idols.

Leave him.

Their banquet has been separated;

they have committed fornication utterly.

They have loved bringing disgrace upon their protectors.

A spirit has bound her with its wings [Alt. with her wings],

and they shall be put to shame because of their sacrifices.

[Chapter V.] Hear this, priests.

Pay attention, house of Israel.

Listen, house of the king [Alt. *with your ears*].

For judgment is against you,

because you have become a snare to the watchtower

and a net spread over Tabor.

You have turned sacrifices aside into the depths,

and I am the instructor [Note: [Col. 1019D] Several manuscripts retain from the Septuagint “of all of you,” instead of “of all of them.” MART.] of all of them [Alt. of you].

I know Ephraim,

[Col. 1019B] and Israel is not hidden from me.

For now Ephraim has committed fornication,

and Israel has been defiled.

They will not direct their thoughts toward returning to their God,

because a spirit of fornication is among them,

and they have not known the Lord.

The arrogance of Israel will answer against him to his face.

Israel and Ephraim shall fall in their iniquity,

and Judah shall also fall with them.

With their flocks and herds they will go to seek the Lord,

but they will not find him.

He has been taken away from them.

They have acted treacherously against the Lord,

because they have fathered foreign children.

Now the month [Note: [Col. 1019D] Here the scribes of the books inserted not what they found but what they understood. The Carcassonne Canon reads: “Now Memphis shall devour them with their fathers.” In our San-Germanus manuscript: “the month with its associates.” The Colbertinus-Aniciensis codex reads: “the harvest with its fathers”; our manuscript no. 16 has: “the month with its fathers.” The Royal manuscript is entirely sound. MART. —The Palatine manuscript, like another cited by Martianus, reads *harvest*, though incorrectly. As for what the holy Father wonders at in the Commentary—why the Septuagint translated the word as “rust,” namely *erysibē*, which is called *hasil* in Hebrew—I think it happened because they took the middle letter of the word for another letter, which differs from it only slightly, and then read the third letter as another. They thus read a form meaning rust or corrosion, as in Ezekiel 27:6 and elsewhere, where they themselves so interpret it. Conversely, the reading of the other word could neither be made nor maintained at all.] with its portions.

Blow the horn in Gibeah,

the trumpet in Ramah.

Cry aloud in Beth-Aven.

Behind you, Benjamin.

Ephraim shall be desolate on the day of punishment.

Among the tribes of Israel I have shown faithfulness.

The princes of Judah have become like those who move a boundary marker.

I will pour out my wrath upon them like water.

Ephraim suffers oppression,

broken by judgment,

because he began to follow filth.

And I am like a moth to Ephraim,

and like decay to the house of Judah.

Ephraim saw his sickness,

and Judah his bond.

Ephraim went to Assyria

and sent to the avenging king.

But he will not be able to heal you,

nor will he be able to release the bond from you.

For I am like a lioness to Ephraim,

and like a young lion to the house of Judah.

I—I will seize and go away.

I will carry off,

and there is no one who can rescue.

[Col. 1019D] I will go and return to my place

until you fail

and seek my face.

[Col. 1020A] [Chapter VI.] In their affliction they will rise early to come to me.

“Come, let us return to the Lord,

for he has seized us, and he will heal us.

He will strike us, and he will bind us up.

He will revive us after two days.

On the third day he will raise us up,

and we shall live in his presence.

We shall know;

we shall pursue knowledge of the Lord.

His going forth is prepared like the dawn,

and he will come to us like the early rain,

and the latter rain upon the earth.”

What shall I do with you, Ephraim?

What shall I do with you, Judah?

Your mercy is like a morning cloud,

and like dew that passes away in the morning.

Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets;

I have slain them by the words of my mouth:

[Col. 1020B] and your judgments shall go forth like the light.

For I desired mercy [Alt. I desire it], and not sacrifice,

and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.

But they, like Adam, transgressed the covenant;

there they acted treacherously against me.

Gilead is a city of those who practice idolatry,

marked with blood.

And like the jaws of bandits, a company of priests,

on the road, murdering those who travel from Shechem:

for they have committed a crime.

In the house of Israel I saw a horrifying thing:

there were the fornications of Ephraim;

Israel was defiled.

But Judah too, set [Heb. “[Col. 1020D] Here the Author is mistaken in this and the following scholion, both of which Martianaeus brought forth from the Saint-Germain manuscript: for it is most clearly written in Hebrew, *pone*.] a harvest for yourself,

when I restore the captivity of my people.

[Chapter VII.] When I wished to heal Israel,

the iniquity of Ephraim and the wickedness of Samaria were revealed,

[Col. 1020C] because they practiced falsehood:

the thief entered, plundering,

and the bandit was outside.

And lest they say in their hearts that I have remembered all their wickedness,

now their inventions have surrounded them;

they have been made before my face.

In their wickedness they gladdened the king,

and in their falsehoods, the princes.

All are adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker:

the city rested for a little while from the mixing of the leaven,

until the whole was fermented.

Days [Note: [Col. 1020D] We restore *Days* in place of *Day*, which Martianaeus read, contrary to all the manuscripts and to the proper sense.] of our king began with the princes raging from wine;

he stretched out his hand with scoffers.

For they applied their heart like an oven while he lay in wait for them:

the one baking them slept all night;

in the morning he himself was kindled like a flame of fire.

They were all heated like an oven,

[Col. 1020D] and they devoured their judges.

All their kings fell;

there is none among them who calls to me.

[Col. 1021A] Ephraim himself mingled among the peoples:

Ephraim became a cake baked under the ashes, which is not turned.

Strangers consumed his strength, and he did not know it;

moreover, gray hairs were scattered upon him, and he did not know it.

And the pride of Israel will be humbled before his face;

yet they did not return to the Lord their God,

and they did not seek him amid all these things.

And Ephraim became like a dove, deceived and without understanding:

they called upon Egypt;

they went to the Assyrians.

And when they depart, I shall spread my net over them;

like a bird of the sky I shall bring them down;

I shall strike them according to the report of their assembly.

Woe to them, for they have withdrawn from me;

they shall be devastated, for they have acted treacherously against me.

Yet I redeemed them,

and they have spoken lies against me.

[Col. 1021B] They did not cry out to me in their heart,

but they wailed upon their beds;

they ruminated over grain and wine, and withdrew from me.

Yet I instructed them and strengthened their arms,

and they devised wickedness against me.

They returned so as to be without a yoke;

they became like a deceitful bow.

Their princes shall fall by the sword, because of the fury of their tongue.

This is their derision in the land of Egypt.

[Chapter VIII.] A trumpet is made in your throat, like an eagle over the house of the Lord,

because they have transgressed my covenant

and violated my law.

They will call upon me:

“My God, Israel knows you.”

Israel rejected the good;

the enemy shall pursue him.

They themselves reigned, but not from me;

[Col. 1021C] they established princes, and I did not know them.

They made idols for themselves from their silver and gold,

so that they might perish.

Your calf, Samaria, has been rejected;

my anger has burned against them [Note: [Col. 1021D] The manuscript has *in eis*, but corruptly, as is certainly established from Jerome’s commentaries. MART.].

How long will they be unable to be cleansed?

For it is from Israel;

the craftsman made it, and it is not God.

Indeed, the calf of Samaria shall be like a spider’s web.

For they will sow wind,

and reap a whirlwind.

A standing stalk: there is no sprout in it;

it will produce no flour.

And even if it does produce it,

strangers will consume it.

Israel has been devoured;

now it has become among the nations like an unclean vessel.

For they themselves went up to Assyria,

a wild ass alone by itself.

Ephraim gave gifts to lovers.

[Col. 1021D] But even when they hire nations for payment, now I shall gather them;

and they shall rest for a little while from the burden of the king and the princes.

For Ephraim multiplied altars for sinning;

the altars became for him occasions of guilt.

I shall write for him my many laws,

which have been regarded [Alt. thought] as something foreign.

They shall bring sacrifices [Note: [Col. 1021D] Many manuscripts read otherwise there: “Bring sacrifices, bring them; they shall sacrifice flesh,” and so forth. Nothing prevents this interpretation from being derived from the Hebrew text taken without vowel points, . This reading is preferred by the Saint-Germain canon, the Corbie manuscript no. 3, Saint-Germain nos. 2 and 10, and the Colbertinus Aniciensis in its first hand [Col. 1022D]. Others read as we have printed. MART.],

[Col. 1022A] they shall sacrifice flesh and eat it;

the Lord will not accept them.

Now he will remember their iniquity

and visit their sins.

They themselves will return to Egypt.

Israel forgot his maker and built shrines;

and Judah multiplied fortified cities.

I shall send fire upon his cities,

and it shall devour his houses.

[Chapter IX.] Do not rejoice, Israel;

do not exult like the peoples,

for you have prostituted yourself away from your God.

You have loved payment above all the threshing floors of grain.

The threshing floor and the winepress shall not feed them,

and the wine shall deceive them.

They shall not dwell in the land of the Lord.

Ephraim has returned to Egypt,

and in Assyria he has eaten what is unclean.

They shall not pour wine offerings to the Lord,

and they shall not please him.

[Col. 1022B] Their sacrifices shall be like the bread of mourners.

All who eat it will be defiled,

for their bread is for their own souls;

it shall not enter [Alt. they shall not enter] the house of the Lord.

What will you do on the solemn day,

on the day of the Lord’s festival?

For behold, they have departed because of devastation.

Egypt shall gather them,

Memphis shall bury them.

Their desirable silver shall be inherited by the nettle;

the thistle shall be in their tents.

The days of visitation have come;

the days of retribution have come.

Know this, Israel: the prophet is foolish,

the spiritual man is mad,

because of the multitude of your iniquity

and the multitude of your madness.

Ephraim’s watchman is with my God;

[Col. 1022C] the prophet has become a snare of ruin [Alt. *has become* is omitted] over all his ways;

madness is in the house of his God.

They have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gibeah.

He will remember their iniquity

and visit their sins.

Like grapes in the wilderness, I found Israel;

like the first fruit of the fig tree at its top,

I saw their fathers.

But they entered into Baal-Peor

and withdrew into shame,

and became abominable like the things they loved.

Ephraim flew away like a bird:

their glory from birth,

from the womb,

and from conception.

And even if they raise their children,

I shall make them childless among human beings.

Moreover, woe to them when I withdraw from them.

Ephraim, as I saw it, was Tyre, formed in beauty;

yet Ephraim shall bring out his children to the slayer.

[Col. 1022D] Give them, Lord.

What will you give them?

Give them a womb without children [Note: [Col. 1022D] The manuscripts of the Canon have a twofold Latin interpretation of the same Hebrew word: “Give them a barren womb without children,” and so forth. For “barren womb” and “womb without children” are synonyms. Martianaeus’s manuscripts improperly insert *barren*, a gloss belonging to the subsequent interpretation, “without children,” which alone is represented by the Hebrew word, .],

and dry breasts.

All their wickedness is at Gilgal,

for there I hated them.

Because of the wickedness of their inventions,

I shall drive them from my house.

I shall no longer love them.

[Col. 1023A] All their princes are departing.

Ephraim is struck;

their root is dried up.

They shall produce no fruit at all.

And even if they give birth,

I shall kill the beloved ones of their womb.

My God will reject them,

because they have not listened to him,

and they shall be wanderers among the nations.

[Chapter X.] Israel is a luxuriant vine;

its fruit was proportionate to it.

According to the abundance of its fruit,

it multiplied altars.

According to the fertility of its land,

it increased its idols.

Their heart was divided;

now they shall perish.

He himself will shatter their idols;

he will lay waste their altars.

For now they will say:

“We have no king,

for we do not fear the Lord.

And what can the king do for us?”

You speak words of an empty vision

and make a covenant;

judgment shall sprout like bitterness

upon the furrows of the field.

The inhabitants of Samaria worshiped the cows of Beth-Aven,

because its people mourned over it,

and its priests exulted over it because of its glory,

because its glory had departed from it.

Indeed, even he himself was carried away to Assyria

as a gift to the avenging king.

Ephraim shall be seized by shame,

and Israel shall be ashamed of his plan.

Samaria caused its king to pass away

like foam upon the face of the water.

The high places of the idol,

the sin of Israel,

shall be destroyed.

The nettle and the thorn shall rise upon their altars.

And they shall say to the mountains:

“Cover us!”

and to the hills:

“Fall upon us!”

From the days of Gibeah Israel sinned;

there they remained.

The battle at Gibeah against the children of iniquity

shall not overtake them.

According to my desire I shall chastise them.

Peoples shall gather against them

when they are chastised for their two iniquities [Alt. *over their two iniquities*].

Ephraim is a heifer trained to love threshing,

and I passed over the beauty of her neck.

I shall mount Ephraim;

Judah shall plow;

Jacob shall break up his furrows.

Sow for yourselves in righteousness,

[Col. 1024A] and reap in the mouth of mercy.

Break up for yourselves new ground.

But it is time to seek the Lord,

when he comes who will teach you righteousness.

You plowed wickedness;

you reaped iniquity.

You ate the fruit of falsehood,

because you trusted in your ways,

in the multitude of your warriors.

Tumult shall arise among your people,

and all your multitudes shall be devastated,

as Salmana was devastated by the house of him [Note: [Col. 1023C] The Saint-Germain canon adds the name Jerobaal: “as Salmana was devastated by the house of Jerobaal, who judged Baal,” and so forth. This could have been borrowed from the third book of Jerome’s Commentaries on Hosea, because there we read: “And he was devastated, as it is contained in the Hebrew, by ARBEL, signifying the same thing as Jerobaal, but in a shorter and more explicit expression.” MART. [Col. 1023D] —In place of “of him who judged Baal,” the Hebrew has only : in the Greek of the Seventy, only Ἱεροβαάλ. The Greeks likewise explain the name from its Hebrew etymology as “he who judged Baal,” as can be seen in Jerome’s own book of Names. It therefore seems that the Latin translator rendered “of him who judged Baal” from the reading of that version and from the widely known meaning of the name, although Martianaeus praises one Saint-Germain manuscript that has the closer Greek form, “by the house of Jerobaal.” This was indeed Gideon’s surname in Judges 6:32, and most interpreters after Jerome believe that the Prophet alludes to that story. I am, however, troubled by so great a difference between the Hebrew name and the reading of the Greeks . Moreover, in place of “judged,” Jerome consistently reads and explains “vindicated” in his Commentary.],

who judged Baal on the day of battle,

with mother dashed against children.

Thus Beth-el did to you,

because of the face of the wickedness of your evils.

[Chapter XI.] As morning passes,

the king of Israel has passed away.

For Israel was a child,

and I loved him;

and from Egypt I called my son.

[Col. 1024B] They called them;

so they went away from before them.

They sacrificed to the Baals,

and sacrificed to idols.

Yet I was like a nurse to Ephraim;

I carried them in my arms,

and they did not know that I healed them.

I shall draw them with the cords of Adam,

with the bonds of love.

And I shall be to them like one lifting the yoke above their jaws;

I bent down to him so that he might eat.

He shall not return to the land of Egypt,

and Assyria itself is his king,

because they refused to return.

The sword has begun in his cities;

it shall consume his chosen ones,

and devour their heads.

And my people shall hang upon my return.

[Col. 1024C] But the yoke shall be imposed upon them together,

and it shall not be removed.

How [Note: [Col. 1023D] This passage is notably corrupt in the manuscript copies. The Saint-Germain canon reads as follows: “How shall I give you up, Ephraim? Shall I defeat you, Israel?” The copy of the Church of Carcassonne: “How shall I give you up, Ephraim? Shall I defeat you, shall I protect you, Israel?” The Colbertinus Aniciensis manuscript had the word *shall I defeat*, which a later hand erased, as can be seen in the ancient Saint-Germain no. 3. Hence both now read as we have printed, following Jerome himself, because in book 3 of his Commentaries on Hosea he acknowledges that this is his own translation [Col. 1024D], although he later does not fully approve it: “In that passage,” he says, “where both we and the Seventy translated ‘I shall protect you, Israel,’ it is written in Hebrew *AMAGGENACH*, which Aquila translated ὅπλῳ κυκλώσω σε, that is, ‘I shall surround you with a shield.’ Since we thought this was to be understood favorably and meant protection, from Symmachus’s edition a contrary sense is imposed upon us, saying ἐκδώσω σε, that is, ‘I shall hand you over.’ From Theodotion’s translation likewise an unfavorable rather than favorable meaning is indicated: ἀφοπλίσω σε, which means ‘I shall disarm you’ and take away from you ὅπλον, that is, the shield with which I previously protected you. This sense also better suits the Lord when he threatens.” MART. —The holy Interpreter himself in his Commentary also serves as a guarantor: “In that passage,” he says, “where both we and the Seventy translated ‘I shall protect you, Israel,’ it is written in Hebrew *Ammagenach*, and so forth. Martianaeus, who also cites the entire passage, found *I shall defeat you* in other manuscripts instead of *I shall protect you*; in still others that same verb was joined to it.],

shall I give you up, Ephraim?

Shall I protect you, Israel?

How shall I give you up like Admah?

Shall I make you like Zeboiim?

My heart has been turned within me;

my compassion has been stirred together.

I shall not carry out the fury of my anger;

I shall not turn back to destroy Ephraim.

For I am God,

[Col. 1025A] and not a human being;

the Holy One in your midst,

and I shall not enter the city.

They shall follow the Lord;

he shall roar like a lion.

For he himself shall roar,

and the children of the sea shall fear.

And they shall fly away like a bird from Egypt,

and like a dove from the land of the Assyrians.

And I shall settle them in their houses, says the Lord.

Ephraim surrounded me with denial [Alt. *his denial*],

and the house of Israel with deceit.

But Judah descended as a witness with God,

and was faithful with the holy ones.

[Chapter XII.] Ephraim feeds on wind

and pursues the scorching wind.

All day he multiplies falsehood and devastation.

He made a covenant with the Assyrians,

and carried oil into Egypt.

[Col. 1025B] Therefore the Lord has a judgment with Judah,

and visitation upon Jacob.

According to his ways

and according to his inventions

he will repay him.

In the womb he supplanted his brother,

and in his strength he contended with the angel.

He prevailed over the angel

and was strengthened.

He wept

and pleaded with him.

At Beth-el he found him,

and there he spoke with us.

And the Lord God of hosts—

the Lord is his memorial.

But you shall return to your God.

Keep mercy and judgment,

and hope in your God always.

Canaan, in his hand is a deceitful balance;

he loved oppression.

And Ephraim said:

[Col. 1025C] “Nevertheless, I have become rich;

I have found an idol for myself.

All my labors

will not find in me the iniquity that I have committed.”

But I am the Lord your God [Alt. adds “who brought you out”] from the land of Egypt.

I shall still make you dwell in tents,

as in the days of the festival.

I spoke through the prophets,

and I multiplied visions;

and by the hand of the prophets I was represented.

If Gilead is an idol,

then [Alt. therefore] they were sacrificing oxen in vain at Gilgal.

Indeed, their altars are like heaps upon the furrows of the field.

Jacob fled to the region of Syria,

and Israel served for a wife,

and for a wife he kept watch.

But through a prophet the Lord brought Israel up from Egypt,

and through a prophet he was preserved.

Ephraim provoked me to anger with his bitterness,

and his blood shall come upon him;

his Lord shall repay him for his reproach.

[Chapter XIII.] When Ephraim spoke,

terror seized Israel.

He sinned in Baal,

and died.

And now they have added to sinning.

They made for themselves a molten image from their silver,

like the likeness of idols;

it is entirely the work of craftsmen.

To these they say:

“Sacrifice human beings, worshipping calves.” [Note: [Col. 1025D] Elsewhere the holy Father himself translates from the Hebrew differently. When quoting this passage of Hosea in his Commentary on Isaiah 57, he says: “As it is written in Hebrew, ‘Those who sacrifice human beings worship calves.’” And indeed the Hebrew reads literally: . Nevertheless, we do not deny that it admits other interpretations.].

Therefore they shall be like a morning cloud,

and like the morning dew that passes away,

like dust carried off by a whirlwind from the threshing floor,

and like smoke from the chimney.

But I am the Lord your God [Alt. adds “who brought you out”]

from the land of Egypt.

You shall know no God besides me,

and there is no savior except me.

I knew you in the wilderness,

in a land of desolation.

According to their pastures they were filled,

and when they were satisfied

they lifted up their heart

and forgot me.

And I shall be to them like a lioness,

[Col. 1026B] like a leopard on the road of the Assyrians.

I shall meet them like a bear robbed of her cubs,

and tear open the covering of their liver.

I shall consume them there like a lion;

the beast of the field shall rip them apart.

Your destruction, Israel;

your help is only in me.

Where is your king?

Let him save you now,

especially in all your cities,

and your judges of whom you said:

“Give me a king and princes.”

I shall give you a king in my fury,

and take him away in my indignation.

The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up;

his sin is hidden.

The pains of a woman in labor shall come upon him.

He is a son without understanding;

for now he shall not stand in the breaking forth of children.

From the hand of death I shall free them;

[Col. 1026C] from death I shall redeem them.

I shall be your death, O death;

I shall be your bite, O underworld.

Consolation is hidden from my eyes.

For he himself shall divide among the brothers.

The Lord shall bring a scorching wind,

rising from the wilderness.

It shall dry up his veins,

desolate his spring,

and he himself shall plunder the treasure of every desirable vessel.

[Chapter XIV.] Let Samaria perish,

because she has provoked her God to bitterness.

By the sword [Note: [Col. 1026D] The copies of the Canon read, “By the sword let them perish.” MART.] let them perish;

let their little ones be dashed to pieces,

and let their pregnant women be ripped open.

Return, Israel, to the Lord your God,

for you have fallen because of your iniquity.

Take words with you

and return to the Lord.

Say to him:

“Take away all iniquity;

receive what is good,

and we shall repay the calves of our lips.”

Assyria will not save us;

we shall not mount a horse;

nor shall we say any longer:

“Our gods are the works of our hands,”

for you will have mercy on the orphan who is in you.

I shall heal their contritions [Note: [Col. 1026D] In place of what the Hebrew text has, namely the word , meaning “their turning,” the holy Father seems to have read in his copy , which means “their fractures” or “their contritions.”],

I shall love them freely,

for my anger has turned away from them.

I shall be like dew.

[Col. 1027A] Israel shall sprout like a lily,

and his root shall break forth like Lebanon.

His branches shall go forth,

and his glory shall be like that of an olive tree,

and his fragrance like Lebanon [Note: [Col. 1027] Martianaeus read *pain* incorrectly; the Hebrew and all the other books contradict it, as does the proper sense.].

They shall return, sitting in his shade.

They shall live on grain

and sprout like a vine.

His memorial shall be like the wine of Lebanon.

[Col. 1028A] Ephraim, what have I henceforth to do with idols?

I shall hear him,

and I myself shall direct him like a green fir tree.

From me your fruit has been found.

Who is wise and will understand these things?

Who is discerning and will know them?

For the ways of the Lord are right,

and the righteous shall walk in them;

but transgressors shall fall in them.

[Col. 1027] Here ends the book of the prophet Hosea.

THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET JOEL BEGINS.

[Col. 1027B] [Chapter I.] The word of the Lord that came to Joel,

the son of Pethuel.

Hear this, elders,

and listen with your ears, all inhabitants of the land.

Has this happened in your days,

or in the days of your fathers?

Tell your children about it,

and your children to their children,

and their children to another generation.

The locust ate what the caterpillar left;

the grub ate what the locust left;

and the rust-insect ate what the grub left.

Awake, drunkards, and weep,

and howl, all you who drink wine with delight,

for it has perished from your mouth.

For a nation has come up over my land,

strong and innumerable.

Its teeth are like the teeth of a lion,

and its molars like those of a lion’s cub.

It made my vine a wilderness,

[Col. 1027C] and stripped the bark from my fig tree.

It laid it bare, utterly stripped it,

and cast it away.

Its branches have become white.

Mourn like a virgin girded with sackcloth

over the husband of her youth [Alt. *your youth*].

Sacrifice and libation have perished from the house of the Lord;

the priests, the ministers of the Lord, have mourned.

The region has been devastated;

the soil has mourned.

For the grain has been destroyed,

the wine has been confounded,

and the oil has languished.

The farmers are ashamed;

the vine-dressers howl over the wheat and barley,

because the harvest of the field has perished.

The vine is confounded,

and the fig tree has languished.

The pomegranate,

the palm,

the apple,

and all the trees of the field have dried up,

because joy has been confounded among the children of human beings.

[Col. 1027D] Gird yourselves and mourn, priests;

howl, ministers of the altar.

Enter and lie in sackcloth, ministers of my God,

for sacrifice and libation have perished from the house of your God.

Sanctify a fast,

call an assembly,

gather the elders,

all the inhabitants of the land,

into the house of your God,

and cry out to the Lord:

“Ah, ah, for the day!”

For the day of the Lord is near,

and it shall come like devastation from the Mighty One.

Have not provisions perished before your eyes [Alt. *our eyes*]

from the house of our God,

joy and exultation?

[Col. 1028B] The animals have rotted in their dung;

the granaries have been demolished,

the storehouses have been scattered,

because the grain has been confounded.

Why does the animal groan?

Why do the herds of cattle bellow?

For they have no pasture.

Moreover, the flocks of sheep have perished.

To you, Lord, I shall cry,

for fire has consumed the beautiful places of the wilderness,

and flame has set fire to all the trees of the region.

Even the beasts of the field,

like a thirsty plain longing for rain,

looked up to you,

for the springs of water have dried up,

and fire has devoured the beautiful places of the wilderness.

[Chapter II.] Blow the trumpet in Zion,

howl on my holy mountain.

Let all the inhabitants of the land be disturbed,

[Col. 1028C] for the day of the Lord is coming,

for the day of darkness and gloom is near,

a day of cloud and tempest.

Like morning spread over the mountains,

a numerous and strong people.

There has never been anything like it from the beginning,

nor shall there be after it

through the years of generation and generation.

Before its face is a consuming fire,

and behind it a flame burning.

The land before it is like a garden of delight,

and behind it a desolate wilderness;

there is no one who can escape it.

Their appearance is like the appearance of horses,

and like horsemen so they shall run.

They shall leap over the tops of the mountains

like the sound of chariots,

like the sound of a flame of fire devouring stubble,

like a strong people prepared for battle.

[Col. 1028D] Before them peoples shall be tortured;

all faces shall be turned into a cooking pot.

Like mighty men they shall run;

like warriors they shall climb [Alt. *they climbed*] the wall.

A man [Alt. *men*] shall walk [Alt. *walk*] in his ways,

and they shall not turn aside from their paths.

Each one shall not crowd his brother;

each shall walk in his own path.

They shall also fall through the windows,

and they shall not be demolished.

They shall enter the city;

they shall run upon the wall.

They shall climb into the houses;

[Col. 1029A] through the windows they shall enter like a thief.

Before them the earth trembled;

the heavens were shaken.

The sun and moon were darkened,

and the stars withdrew their radiance.

And the Lord gave his voice before the face of his army,

for his camps are exceedingly numerous,

for they are mighty and carry out his word.

For the day of the Lord is great

and exceedingly terrible.

Who will endure it?

Now therefore, says the Lord:

Return to me with all your heart,

with fasting,

with weeping,

and with mourning.

Tear your hearts,

and not your garments,

and return to the Lord your God.

For he is gracious and merciful,

patient [Note: [Col. 1029D] The Palatine manuscripts, which we used in revising the Commentaries, prefer in the text “and rich in mercy and to be entreated.” Martianaeus likewise found “to be entreated” in one or another manuscript instead of “abounding.” The Hebrew word properly means “repentant.”]

and rich in mercy,

and abounding [Note: [Col. 1029D] In the Saint-Germain copy of the Hebrew truth [i.e. the Hebrew text], the text reads “abounding,” and in the margin as a variant reading, “to be entreated” [Col. 1030D]. But in the context of the Carcassonne Canon it reads “to be entreated,” without any marginal variant. MART.] in regard to evil.

Who knows whether he may turn and forgive,

and leave behind him a blessing,

a sacrifice and libation

[Col. 1029B] for the Lord your God [Alt. *our God*]?

Blow the trumpet in Zion,

sanctify a fast,

call an assembly,

gather the people,

sanctify the congregation,

assemble the elders,

gather the little ones and those nursing at the breast.

Let the bridegroom go forth from his chamber,

and the bride from her bridal room.

Between the vestibule and the altar

the priests, the ministers of the Lord, shall weep

and say:

“Spare, Lord, spare [Alt. *the second ‘spare’ is omitted*] your people,

and do not give your inheritance over to reproach,

so that nations may rule over them.

Why should they say among the peoples:

‘Where is their God?’”

[Col. 1029C] The Lord was jealous for his land

and spared his people.

And the Lord answered

and said to his people:

“Behold, I shall send you grain,

wine,

and oil,

and you shall be filled with it.

I shall no longer make you a reproach among the nations.

And I shall drive far from you the one who is from the north.

I shall expel him into a pathless and desolate land,

his face toward the eastern sea,

and his rear toward the western sea.

His stench shall rise,

and his decay shall rise,

because he has acted arrogantly [Alt. *he who has acted arrogantly*].”

Do not fear, land;

exult and rejoice,

for the Lord has acted magnificently.

Do not fear, animals of the region,

for the beautiful places of the wilderness have sprouted,

[Col. 1029D] for the tree has borne its fruit,

the fig tree and the vine have given their strength.

And you, children of Zion,

exult and rejoice in the Lord your God,

for he has given you a teacher of righteousness,

and he will bring down upon you the early and latter rain,

as at the beginning [Alt. *as* is omitted].

The threshing floors shall be filled with grain,

and the winepresses shall overflow with wine and oil.

And I shall restore to you the years

[Col. 1030A] that the locust, the grub, the rust-insect, and the caterpillar consumed,

my great army, which I sent against you.

You shall eat, eating until you are satisfied,

and you shall praise the name of the Lord [Alt. *the Lord* is omitted], your God,

who has done wonders with you [Alt. *with us*].

My people shall not be confounded forever.

And you shall know that I am in the midst of Israel,

and I am the Lord your God,

and there is no other.

My people shall not be confounded forever.

And it shall be after these things:

I shall pour out my spirit upon all flesh.

Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy;

your elders shall dream dreams,

and your young men shall see visions.

Moreover, upon my male servants and female servants [Note: [Col. 1030D] Some manuscripts, including the Palatine manuscripts, add “my,” which pronoun the Hebrew omits both here and with the word “servants.”]

in those days I shall pour out my spirit.

And I shall give signs in heaven

[Col. 1030B] and on earth:

blood,

fire,

and vapor of smoke.

The sun shall be turned into darkness,

and the moon into blood,

before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes.

And it shall be:

everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord

shall be saved.

For in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be salvation,

as the Lord has said,

and among the survivors whom the Lord shall call.

[Chapter III.] For behold, in those days and at that time,

when I restore the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,

I shall gather all the nations

and lead them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat.

And there I shall enter into judgment with them

over my people and my inheritance, Israel,

[Col. 1030C] whom they scattered among the nations

and divided my land.

They cast lots over my people;

they gave a boy to a prostitute,

and sold a girl for wine,

so that they might drink.

But what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon,

and every territory of the Philistines?

Will you repay me with vengeance?

And if you take vengeance against me,

I shall quickly and swiftly return your recompense upon your head.

For you took my silver and gold [Alt. adds *my*],

and brought my desirable and most beautiful things

into your shrines.

You sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem

to the sons of the Greeks,

so that you might remove them far from their borders.

Behold, I shall raise them up from the place where you sold them,

[Col. 1030D] and I shall turn your recompense upon your head.

And I shall sell your sons and your daughters

into the hands of the sons of Judah,

and they shall sell them to the Sabeans,

a distant nation,

for the Lord has spoken.

Proclaim this among the nations,

sanctify war,

rouse the strong.

Let all the men of war draw near;

let them go up.

[Col. 1031A] Beat your plowshares into swords,

and your pruning hooks into spears.

Let the weak man say:

“I am strong.”

Break forth and come,

all nations from the surrounding regions,

and gather yourselves together.

There the Lord shall cause your strong men to fall.

Let the nations arise

and go up into the valley of Jehoshaphat,

for there I shall sit

to judge all the nations around.

Send out sickles,

for the harvest has ripened.

Come and descend,

for the winepress is full;

the winepresses overflow,

for their wickedness has multiplied.

Peoples, peoples, in the valley of slaughter,

for the day of the Lord is near

in the valley of slaughter.

The sun and moon were darkened,

and the stars withdrew their radiance.

And the Lord shall roar from Zion,

and from Jerusalem he shall give his voice.

[Col. 1031B] And the heavens and the earth shall be shaken.

[Col. 1032A] And the Lord is the hope of his people

and the strength of the children of Israel.

And you shall know that I am the Lord your God,

dwelling in Zion, on my holy mountain.

And Jerusalem shall be holy,

and strangers shall no longer pass through it.

And it shall be on that day:

the mountains shall drip sweetness,

and the hills shall flow with milk,

and waters shall flow through all the streams of Judah.

And a spring shall go forth from the house of the Lord

and water the torrent of thorns.

Egypt shall become a desolation,

and Idumea a desert of destruction,

because they acted wickedly against the children of Judah

and shed innocent blood in their land.

But Judah shall be inhabited forever,

and Jerusalem from generation to generation.

And I shall cleanse their blood,

which I had not cleansed [Alt. *whom I had not cleansed*].

[Col. 1032B] And the Lord shall dwell in Zion.

[Col. 1031] Here ends the book of the prophet Joel.

THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET AMOS BEGINS.

[Col. 1031B] [Chapter I.] The words of Amos,

who was among the pastoral keepers of Tekoa [Note: [Col. 1031D] Jerome asserts that he translated this from the Hebrew in book 1 of his Commentaries on Amos, and we find it written in this way in all the manuscript copies of the Canon and of the sacred Scriptures. The printed editions read “among the shepherds.” But Jerome should be heard on this matter: “In that passage,” he says, “where the Seventy translated *in accarim*, Theodotion placed the Hebrew word *NOCEDIM*, which Aquila translated ἐν ποιμανοτρόφοις, that is, ‘among pastoral keepers.’ Symmachus and the fifth edition have ἐν τοῖς προιμέσιν, that is, ‘among shepherds.’ And I think that here too they were deceived because of the similarity of the letters DALETH and RES, although at the beginning of the name the letter NUN leaves no excuse for the error. I have not yet found *Accarim* to be Hebrew.” MART.],

which he saw concerning Israel

in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah,

and in the days of Jeroboam, son of Joash, king of Israel,

two years before the earthquake.

And he said:

The Lord shall roar from Zion,

and from Jerusalem he shall give his voice.

And the beautiful places of the shepherds shall mourn,

[Col. 1031C] and the summit of Carmel shall dry up.

Thus says the Lord:

For three crimes of Damascus,

and for four I shall not turn him back,

because they threshed Gilead

with iron threshing sledges.

And I shall send fire upon the house of Hazael,

and it shall devour the houses of Ben-hadad.

And I shall break the bar of Damascus,

and destroy the inhabitant from the plain of the idol,

and the one holding the scepter from the house of delight.

And the people of Syria shall be transferred to Cyrene,

says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord:

For three crimes of Gaza,

and for four I shall not turn him back,

because they deported a complete captivity

to confine it in Idumea.

And I shall send fire upon the wall of Gaza,

and it shall devour its houses.

And I shall destroy the inhabitant from Azotus,

[Col. 1031D] and the one holding the scepter from Ashkelon.

And I shall turn my hand against Accaron,

and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish,

says the Lord God [Alt. *God* is omitted].

Thus says the Lord:

For three crimes of Tyre,

and for four I shall not turn him back,

because they confined a complete captivity

</source>
[Col. 1032B] Idumaea,

and they did not remember the covenant of brothers.

And I will send fire upon the wall of Tyre,

and it shall devour its houses.

Thus says the Lord:

For three crimes of Edom, and for four, I will not revoke it:

because he pursued his brother with the sword,

and violated his compassion,

and maintained his anger beyond measure,

and preserved his indignation to the end.

I will send fire upon Teman,

and it shall devour the houses of Bozrah.

Thus says the Lord:

For three crimes of the sons of Ammon,

and for four, I will not revoke it:

because he ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead

in order to enlarge his territory.

And I will kindle fire upon the wall of Rabbah,

and it shall devour its houses amid wailing on the day of battle,

and amid the whirlwind on the day of upheaval.

And Milcom shall go into captivity,

he and his princes together, says the Lord.

[Chapter II]

Thus says the Lord:

For three crimes of Moab, and for four, I will not revoke it:

because he burned the bones of the king of Edom completely to ashes.

And I will send fire upon Moab,

and it shall devour the houses of Kerioth.

And Moab shall die amid a tumult,

and amid the blast of the trumpet.

And I will destroy the judge from its midst,

and I will kill all its princes with him, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord:

For three crimes of Judah, and for four, I will not revoke it:

because he rejected the law of the Lord,

and did not keep his commandments.

For their idols deceived them,

after which their fathers had gone.

And I will send fire upon Judah,

and it shall devour the houses of Jerusalem.

Thus says the Lord:

For three crimes of Israel, and for four, I will not revoke it:

because he sold the righteous for silver [Alternative: without “for”],

and the poor for a pair of sandals.

They crush the heads of the poor into the dust of the earth,

and turn aside the way of the humble.

A son and his father went to the same girl [Alternative: entered],

to profane [Alternative: pollute] my holy name.

And upon garments taken in pledge they reclined beside every altar,

and they drank the wine of the condemned in the house of their god.

Yet I destroyed the Amorite from before them,

whose height was like the height of cedars,

and he himself was strong like an oak.

And [Note: [Col. 1033] Martianaeus had wrongly read *continui*, contrary to the testimony of all the books and to the sequence of the sacred text.] I crushed his fruit above,

and his roots below.

I am the one who brought you up from the land of Egypt,

and led you in the wilderness for forty years,

so that you might possess the land of the Amorite.

And I raised up prophets from among your sons,

and Nazirites from among your young men.

Is this not so, sons of Israel? says the Lord.

Yet you gave the Nazirites wine to drink,

and commanded the prophets, saying:

“Do not prophesy.”

Behold, I will creak beneath you,

as a wagon creaks when loaded with hay.

And flight shall perish from the swift,

and the strong man shall not retain his strength,

and the mighty shall not save his life.

The archer shall not stand,

and the swift-footed man shall not save himself.

The rider of a horse shall not save his life.

And the courageous man among the mighty

shall flee naked on that day, says the Lord.

[Chapter III]

Hear this word that the Lord has spoken concerning you, sons of Israel,

concerning the whole kindred whom I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying:

“You alone have I known among all the kindreds of the earth;

therefore I will visit all your iniquities upon you.”

Will two walk together

unless they have agreed?

Will the lion roar in the forest

unless it has prey?

Will a lion’s cub give forth its voice from its den

unless it has seized something?

Will a bird fall into a snare on the ground

without a bird-catcher?

Will the snare be taken up from the ground

before it has caught something?

If the trumpet sounds in a city,

will the people not be afraid?

If there is evil in a city,

has the Lord not done it [Alternative: does not the Lord do it]?

For the Lord God does nothing

unless he has revealed his secret to his servants the prophets.

The lion has roared; who will not fear?

The Lord God has spoken; who will not prophesy?

Make it heard in the houses of Ashdod,

and in the houses of the land of Egypt, and say:

“Gather upon the mountains of Samaria,

and see the many insanities in its midst,

and those suffering oppression within its chambers.”

And they did not know how to do what is right, says the Lord,

storing up iniquity and plunder in their houses.

Therefore thus says the Lord God:

The land shall be troubled and surrounded,

and your strength shall be taken away from you,

and your houses shall be plundered.

Thus says the Lord:

Just as a shepherd rescues from the mouth of a lion two legs,

or the tip of an ear,

so shall the sons of Israel be rescued,

those who dwell in Samaria on the edge of a couch,

and in Damascus on a bed.

Hear, and testify against the house of Jacob,

says the Lord God of hosts:

For on the day when I begin to visit Israel’s transgressions,

I will visit them also upon the altars of Bethel.

And the horns of the altar shall be cut off,

and they shall fall to the ground.

And I will strike the winter house together with the summer house.

And the ivory houses shall perish,

and the many houses shall be destroyed, says the Lord.

[Chapter IV]

Hear this word, fat cows,

you who are on the mountain of Samaria,

who oppress the needy and crush the poor,

who say to your masters, “Bring us something, and we will drink.”

The Lord God has sworn by his holiness:

Behold, days are coming upon you,

and they shall lift you up on poles,

and your remnants in boiling pots.

And you shall go out through the breaches,

each one directly opposite the other,

and you shall be cast toward Harmon, says the Lord.

Come to Bethel, and act impiously;

to Gilgal, and multiply transgression.

And bring your sacrifices in the morning,

your tithes every three days.

And sacrifice praise from what has been leavened [Alternative: from leaven],

and proclaim freewill offerings, and announce them;

for this is what you desired, sons of Israel, says the Lord God.

Therefore I also gave you numbness of teeth in all your cities,

and lack of bread in all your places.

Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.

I also withheld rain from you,

when there were still three months before the harvest.

And I rained upon one city,

but did not rain upon another city.

One part was watered,

but the other part [Alternative: one part], upon which I did not rain,

dried up.

And two or three cities came to one city to drink water,

but they were not satisfied.

Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.

I struck you with scorching wind and mildew,

the multitude of your gardens and your vineyards.

The locust devoured your olive groves and your fig trees.

Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.

I sent death among you by the way of Egypt.

I killed your young men with the sword,

even to the captivity of your horses.

And I caused the stench of your camps to rise into your nostrils.

Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.

I overthrew you,

as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah,

and you became like a brand snatched from the fire.

Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.

Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel.

And after I have done this to you,

prepare to meet your God, Israel.

For behold, he forms the mountains,

and creates the wind,

and announces his word to a human being,

making the morning mist,

and walking upon the heights of the earth.

The Lord God of hosts is his name.

[Chapter V]

Hear this word that I raise over you as a lament,

house of Israel.

The virgin Israel has fallen;

she shall not rise again.

She has been cast upon her own land;

there is no one to raise her up.

For thus says the Lord God:

The city from which a thousand went out

shall have a hundred left in it;

and from which a hundred went out,

ten shall be left in it,

in the house of Israel.

For thus says the Lord to the house of Israel:

Seek me, and you shall live.

And do not seek Bethel,

and do not enter Gilgal,

and do not cross over to Beersheba [Alternative: do not cross over].

For Gilgal shall surely go into captivity,

and Bethel shall become useless.

Seek the Lord, and live,

lest he burn like fire upon the house of Joseph,

and it devour,

with no one to extinguish Bethel.

You who turn judgment into wormwood,

and abandon righteousness on the earth,

the one who makes Arcturus and Orion,

who turns darkness into morning,

and changes day into night,

who summons the waters of the sea,

and pours them out over the face of the earth—

the Lord is his name.

He smiles destruction upon the strong,

and brings devastation upon the mighty.

They hated the one who rebuked at the gate,

and abhorred the one who spoke with integrity.

Therefore, because you plundered the poor,

and took a choice portion from him,

you shall build houses of hewn stone,

but you shall not dwell in them.

You shall plant delightful vineyards,

but you shall not drink their wine.

For I know your many crimes

and your mighty sins:

enemies of the righteous, taking bribes,

and oppressing the poor at the gate.

Therefore the prudent person will keep silent at that time,

for it is an evil time.

Seek the good, and not evil, so that you may live.

Then the Lord God of hosts will be with you,

as you have said.

Hate evil and love good,

and establish judgment at the gate.

Perhaps the Lord God of hosts will have mercy

on the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore thus says the Lord God of hosts, the Sovereign:

In all the squares there shall be lamentation,

and in every place outside it shall be said, “Alas! Alas!”

They shall call the farmer to mourning,

and those skilled in lamentation to wailing.

And in all the vineyards there shall be lamentation,

because I shall pass through your midst, says the Lord.

Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord!

Why do you desire it?

The day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.

It is as when a man flees from the face of a lion,

and a bear meets him.

He enters the house,

leans his hand against the wall,

and a serpent bites him.

Is not the day of the Lord darkness, and not light,

gloom, and no brightness in it?

I hate and reject your festivals,

and I will not accept the fragrance of your assemblies.

Even if you offer me burnt offerings and your gifts,

I will not accept them,

and I will not look upon the offerings of your fattened animals.

Take away from me the tumult of your songs,

and I will not hear the music of your lyres.

And judgment shall be revealed like water,

and righteousness like a mighty torrent.

Did you offer me sacrifices and offerings

for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?

And you carried the tent of your Moloch,

and the image of your idols,

the star of your god,

which you made for yourselves.

And I will make you migrate beyond Damascus, says the Lord;

the Lord God of hosts is his name.

[Chapter VI]

Woe to you who are wealthy in Zion,

and trust in Mount Samaria,

leaders of the foremost peoples,

entering the house of Israel ceremoniously.

Cross over to Calneh and see,

and go from there to great Hamath.

Then descend to Gath of the Philistines,

and to the best of these kingdoms.

Are their boundaries broader than your boundary?

You who set yourselves apart for the evil day,

and draw near to a throne of iniquity.

You who sleep on ivory beds,

and live wantonly upon your couches,

who eat lambs from the flock,

and calves from the midst of the herd,

who sing to the sound of the psaltery,

who think they have instruments of song like David,

who drink wine from bowls,

and anoint yourselves with the finest ointment,

yet suffer nothing over the ruin of Joseph.

Therefore now they shall migrate at the head of those being carried away,

and the company of the wanton shall be removed.

The Lord God has sworn by his own life,

says the Lord God of hosts:

I detest the pride of Jacob,

and I hate his houses,

and I will hand over the city together with its inhabitants.

And if ten men remain in one house,

even they shall die.

And his relative shall take him

and burn him,

in order to carry the bones out of the house.

And he shall say to the one in the innermost part of the house,

“Is anyone still with you?”

And he shall answer,

“It is finished.”

And he shall say,

“Be silent, and do not remember the name of the Lord.”

For behold, the Lord will command,

and he will strike the great house with ruins,

and the small house with breaches.

Can horses run upon rocks,

or can one plow with buffaloes,

since you have turned judgment into bitterness,

and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood?

You who rejoice in what is nothing,

who say:

“Have we not acquired horns for ourselves by our own strength?”

For behold, I will raise up against you, house of Israel, a nation,

says the Lord God of hosts,

and they shall crush you from the entrance of Hamath

to the torrent of the wilderness.

[Chapter VII]

This is what the Lord God showed me:

behold, a maker of locusts at the beginning of the growth of the late rain.

And behold, the late growth after the king’s shearing.

[Note: [Col. 1035D–1038D] All the manuscript codices read not “the shearing of the king,” but “the shearer of the flock.” In the present Hebrew text it is written *gizze hammelech*, “the king’s shearing,” whereas Jerome read it in the singular as *gozi ammelech*, “the shearer of the king.” See Book III of the Commentaries in the manuscript books, since in many places they differ from the corruption of the printed editions and from the vowel-points of the Masoretes. — Martianaeus. Jerome appears to have preferred, in the Commentary, after “the late growth,” “the king’s shearer,” or “the king’s shearing.” In the Cistercian manuscript we found: “the late growth after the shearer,” or “the king’s shearing.” But what Martianaeus found in all his copies, *flock* for *king*, is plainly an error of scribes or of a somewhat too audacious critic.]

And it happened:

when it had finished consuming the grass of the land, I said:

“Lord God, be gracious, I beg you.

Who will raise up Jacob,

for he is small?”

The Lord had mercy concerning this.

“It shall not happen,” said the Lord.

This is what the Lord God showed me:

behold, the Lord God was calling judgment by fire,

and it devoured the great abyss,

and consumed a portion at the same time.

And I said:

“Lord God, cease, I beg you.

Who will raise up Jacob,

for he is small?”

The Lord had mercy concerning this.

“This too shall not happen,” said the Lord God.

This is what he showed me:

behold, the Lord was standing upon a plastered wall,

and in his hand was a builder’s trowel.

And the Lord said to me:

“What do you see, Amos?”

And I said:

“A builder’s trowel.”

And the Lord said:

“Behold, I will place a trowel in the midst of my people Israel.

I will no longer pass over him.”

And the high places of the idol shall be demolished,

and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be desolated.

And I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.

And Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent to Jeroboam, king of Israel, saying:

“Amos has rebelled against you in the midst of the house of Israel.

The land cannot bear all his words.”

For thus says Amos:

“Jeroboam shall die by the sword,

and Israel shall migrate into captivity from its land.”

And Amaziah said to Amos:

“You who see, go away!

Flee to the land of Judah,

and eat bread there,

and prophesy there.

But do not continue to prophesy at Bethel,

for it is the king’s sanctuary,

and it is the house of the kingdom.”

And Amos answered and said to Amaziah:

“I am not a prophet,

and I am not a prophet’s son.

I am a herdsman [Alternative: shepherd],

one who pinches or tends sycamores.

And the Lord took me when I was following the flock,

and the Lord said to me [some copies omit “the Lord”]:

‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’

And now hear the word of the Lord.

You say:

‘You shall not prophesy against Israel,

and you shall not drip words against the house of the idol.’

Therefore thus says the Lord:

Your wife shall fornicate in the city,

and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword.

Your land shall be measured with a measuring line.

And you shall die in an unclean land,

and Israel shall migrate into captivity from its land.”

[Chapter VIII]

This is what the Lord God showed me:

behold, a hook for summer fruit.

And he said:

“What do you see, Amos?”

And I said:
