“A hook for summer fruit.”

And the Lord said to me:

“The end has come upon my people Israel.

I will no longer pass by them.”

And the doorposts of the temple shall creak on that day, says the Lord God.

Many shall die.

In every place silence shall be cast down.

Hear this, you who crush the poor,

and cause the needy of the land to fail,

saying:

“When will the month pass,

so that we may sell our goods,

and the Sabbath,

so that we may open the grain,

in order to make the measure smaller,

increase the shekel,

and falsify the scales,

so that we may acquire the needy for silver

and the poor for a pair of sandals,

and sell the sweepings of grain?”

The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob [Alternative: by the pride of Jacob]:

“If I ever forget all their works to the end!”

Will the earth not be shaken because of this,

and will every inhabitant of it not mourn?

And will it not rise up like a river in its entirety,

be cast out,

and flow away like the river of Egypt?

And it shall be on that day, says the Lord God [some copies omit “God”]:

the sun shall set at midday,

and I will make the earth dark on the day of light.

And I will turn your festivals into mourning,

and all your songs into lamentation.

And I will bring sackcloth upon every back,

and baldness upon every head.

And I will make it like the mourning for an only child,

and its end like a bitter day.

Behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

when I will send famine upon the land—

not a famine of bread,

nor a thirst for water,

but of hearing the word of the Lord.

And they shall be moved from sea to sea,

and from north to east.

They shall wander about seeking the word of the Lord,

but they shall not find it.

On that day the beautiful virgins shall fail,

and the young men shall faint from thirst.

Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria,

and say:

“As your god lives, Dan,

and as the way of Beersheba lives”—

they shall fall,

and shall not rise again.

[Chapter IX]

I saw the Lord standing upon the altar,

and he said:

“Strike the doorpost,

and let the lintels be shaken.

For avarice is at the head of them all,

and I will kill their remnant with the sword.

There shall be no escape for those who flee,

and none of those who escape shall be saved.

If they descend as far as the underworld,

from there my hand shall bring them out.

And if they ascend to heaven,

from there I shall drag them down.

And if they hide at the summit of Carmel,

from there I shall search them out and take them away.

And if they conceal themselves from my eyes in the depths of the sea,

there I shall command the serpent,

and it shall bite them.

And if they go into captivity before their enemies,

there I shall command the sword,

and it shall kill them.

And I will set my eyes upon them for evil,

and not for good.”

And the Lord God of hosts touches the earth,

and it melts.

And all who dwell in it shall mourn.

And it shall rise up like a river in its entirety,

and flow away like the river of Egypt.

He builds his ascent in heaven,

and establishes his bundle upon the earth.

He summons the waters of the sea,

and pours them out over the face of the earth.

The Lord is his name.

Are you not like the sons of the Ethiopians to me,

sons of Israel? says the Lord.

Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt,

and the Philistines from Cappadocia,

and the Syrians from Cyrene?

Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom,

and I will crush it from the face of the earth.

Nevertheless, in crushing,

I will not utterly crush the house of Jacob,

says the Lord.

For behold, I will command,

and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations,

as grain is shaken in a sieve.

[Note: [Col. 1039A] The word “grain” is found neither in Jerome’s Commentary nor truly in the Hebrew text, but only “as it is shaken in a sieve”; the Septuagint likewise have no more.]

And not a pebble shall fall upon the earth.

All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword,

those who say:

“Evil shall not draw near,

and it shall not come upon us.”

On that day I will raise up the fallen tent of David.

And I will rebuild its breaches,

and restore what had collapsed.

And I will rebuild it as in ancient days,

so that they may possess the remnant of Edom

and all the nations upon whom my name has been invoked,

says the Lord who does these things.

Behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

when the plowman shall overtake the reaper,

and the one who treads grapes shall overtake the one who sows seed.

And the mountains shall drip sweetness,

and all the hills shall be cultivated.

I will turn the captivity of my people Israel.

And they shall build the desolated cities,

and inhabit them.

And they shall plant vineyards,

and drink their wine.

And they shall make gardens,

and eat their fruits.

And I will plant them upon their own soil,

and I will no longer uproot them from their land,

which I gave them, says the Lord your God.

[Col. 1039] The book of the prophet Amos ends.

# THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET OBADIAH BEGINS

[Col. 1039B] [Chapter I]

The vision of Obadiah.

Thus says the Lord God concerning Edom:

“We have heard a report from the Lord,

and he has sent a messenger among the nations:

‘Rise,

and let us rise against him for battle.’”

Behold, I have made you small among the nations.

You are exceedingly despised.

The pride of your heart has lifted you up,

you who dwell in the clefts of the rocks [Alternative: of the rock],

who exalt his throne [Alternative: your throne],

who say in your heart:

“Who will bring me down to the ground?”

If you are exalted like an eagle,

and if you set your nest among the stars,

from there I will bring you down, says the Lord.

If thieves had entered upon you,

if robbers by night,

how would you have kept silent?

Would they not have stolen enough for themselves?

If grape-gatherers had entered upon you,

would they not at least have left you some clusters? [Alternative: would they not have left you clusters?]

How thoroughly Esau has been searched!

How his hidden things have been investigated!

They have sent you away to the border.

All the men of your covenant have mocked you.

The men of your peace have prevailed against you.

Those who eat with you have set an ambush beneath you.

There is no wisdom in him.

Will I not on that day, says the Lord,

destroy the wise from Edom,

and prudence from Mount Esau?

And your mighty men shall fear from the south,

so that the man from Mount Esau may perish.

Because of the slaughter

and because of the violence against your brother Jacob,

shame shall cover you,

and you shall perish forever.

On the day when you stood opposed [Note: The printed books, and Jerome himself in the Commentary, add “him”; yet the pronoun is not present in the Hebrew],

when foreigners captured his army,

and strangers entered his gates,

and cast lots over Jerusalem,

you too were like one of them.

You shall not look with contempt upon the day of your brother,

on the day of his exile.

You shall not rejoice over the sons of Judah

on the day of their destruction,

and you shall not enlarge your mouth

on the day of distress.

You shall not enter the gate of my people

on the day of their ruin.

You shall not even look with contempt upon his calamity

on the day of his devastation.

And you shall not go out against his army

on the day of his devastation.

You shall not stand at the exits

to kill those who escape,

and you shall not shut up his survivors

on the day of tribulation.

For the day of the Lord is near upon all the nations.

As you have done,

so shall it be done to you.

Your retribution shall be turned back upon your own head.

For just as you drank upon my holy mountain [Alternative: you drank],

so shall all the nations drink continually.

And they shall drink and swallow,

and they shall be as though they did not exist.

But upon Mount Zion there shall be deliverance,

and it shall be holy.

And the house of Jacob shall possess those who had possessed them.

And the house of Jacob shall be fire,

and the house of Joseph a flame,

and the house of Esau stubble.

And they shall kindle them,

and devour them,

and there shall be no remnant of the house of Esau,

because the Lord has spoken.

And those in the south shall inherit Mount Esau,

and those in the lowlands the land of the Philistines.

And they shall possess the region of Ephraim

and the region of Samaria,

and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.

And the exiles of this army [Alternative: his army] of the sons of Israel

shall possess all the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath.

And the exiles of Jerusalem,

which is in Bosphorus,

shall possess the cities of the south.

And saviors shall ascend Mount Zion

to judge Mount Esau,

and the kingdom shall belong to the Lord.

[Col. 1041] The book of the prophet Obadiah ends.

# THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET JONAH BEGINS

[Col. 1041A] [Chapter I]

And the word of the Lord came to Jonah,

son of Amittai, saying:

“Rise, go to Nineveh, the great city,

and preach in it,

for its wickedness has risen before me.”

And Jonah rose

to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord.

And he went down to Joppa,

and found a ship going to Tarshish.

And he paid its fare,

and went down into it

to go with them to Tarshish,

away from the presence of the Lord.

But the Lord sent a great wind upon the sea,

and a great storm arose on the sea,

and the ship was in danger of being broken apart.

And the sailors were afraid,

and the men cried out to their gods.

And they threw the cargo that was in the ship into the sea,

so that it might be lightened for them.

But Jonah had gone down into the inner part of the ship,

and was sleeping in a deep sleep.

And the helmsman approached him and said:

“Why are you sunk in sleep?

Rise, call upon your god.

Perhaps God will take thought for us,

and we shall not perish.”

And each man said to his companion:

“Come, and let us cast lots,

and let us learn on whose account this evil has come upon us” [Alternative: has happened to us].

And they cast lots,

and the lot fell upon Jonah.

And they said to him:

“Tell us on whose account this evil has come upon us.

What is your work?

What is your land,

and where are you going?

Or from what people are you?”

And he said to them:

“I am a Hebrew,

and I fear the Lord God of heaven,

who made the sea and the dry land.”

And the men were exceedingly afraid,

and they said to him:

“Why have you done this?”

For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the Lord,

because he had told them.

And they said to him:

“What shall we do with you,

so that the sea may cease from us?”

For the sea was growing increasingly stormy.

And he said to them:

“Take me and throw me into the sea,

and the sea will cease from you.

For I know that on my account

this great storm has come upon you.”

And the men rowed to return to the dry land,

but they could not,

because the sea was growing increasingly stormy against them.

And they cried out to the Lord and said:

“We beg you, Lord,

do not let us perish because of this man’s life,

and do not lay innocent blood upon us.

For you, Lord,

have done as you willed.”

And they took Jonah

and threw him into the sea,

and the sea ceased from its raging.

And the men feared the Lord with great fear,

and they sacrificed sacrifices to the Lord,

and made vows.

[Col. 1042A] [Chapter II]

And the Lord prepared a great fish

to swallow Jonah.

And Jonah was in the belly of the fish

for three days and three nights.

And Jonah prayed to the Lord his God

from the belly of the fish.

And he said:

“I cried out from my distress to the Lord,

and he answered me.

From the belly of the underworld I cried out,

and you heard my voice.

You cast me into the depths,

into the heart of the sea,

and the flood surrounded me.

All your whirlpools and your waves

passed over me.

And I said:

‘I have been cast away from the sight of your eyes.’

Yet again I shall see your holy temple.

The waters surrounded me,

even to my life [Alternative: even my life].

The abyss encircled me;

the deep covered my head.

I descended to the ends of the mountains.

The bars of the earth closed me in forever.

But you shall raise my life from corruption,

Lord my God.

When my soul was fainting within me,

I remembered the Lord,

so that my prayer might come to you,

to your holy temple.

Those who keep worthless vanities

abandon their own mercy.

But I will sacrifice to you with a voice of praise.

Whatever I have vowed,

I will repay for salvation to the Lord.’”

And the Lord spoke to the fish,

and it vomited Jonah onto the dry land.

[Chapter III]

And the word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time, saying:

“Rise and go to Nineveh, the great city,

and preach in it the preaching that I speak to you.”

And Jonah rose and went to Nineveh

according to the word of the Lord.

Now Nineveh was a great city,

a journey of three days.

[Note: [Col. 1041D–1042D] The holy Translator himself reads in his Commentary, with the added word “of God,” “a great city of God,” following the Hebrew; this is an idiom of that language when it commends the size and excellence of something.]

And Jonah began to enter the city,

a journey of one day,

and he cried out and said:

“Yet forty days,

and Nineveh shall be overthrown.”

And the men of Nineveh believed in God.

And they proclaimed a fast,

and clothed themselves in sackcloth,

from the greatest to the least.

And the word reached the king of Nineveh.

And he rose from his throne,

and cast off his garment from himself,

and clothed himself in sackcloth,

and sat in ashes.

And he proclaimed and said in Nineveh,

by decree of the king and his nobles:

“Let neither human beings nor animals,

neither cattle nor sheep,

taste anything.

Let them not feed,

and let them not drink water.

And let human beings and animals be covered with sackcloth,

and let them cry out to God [Alternative: the Lord] with all their strength.

Let each person turn from his evil way,

and from the iniquity that is in their hands.

Who knows whether God may turn and forgive,

and turn back from the fury of his anger,

so that we may not perish?”

And God saw their works,

that they had turned from their evil way.

And God had mercy concerning the evil

that he had said he would do to them,

and he did not do it.

[Chapter IV]

And Jonah was deeply distressed,

and he became angry.

And he prayed to the Lord and said:

“I beg you, Lord,

was this not my word

while I was still in my own land?

Therefore I hastened to flee to Tarshish.

For I know that you are a gracious and merciful God,

patient and abounding in compassion,

and forgiving in regard to evil.

And now, Lord, I beg you,

take my life from me,

for death is better for me than life.”

And the Lord said:

“Are you right to be angry?”

And Jonah went out from the city,

and sat opposite the city toward the east.

And he made himself a shelter there,

and sat beneath it in the shade,

until he might see what would happen to the city.

And the Lord God prepared an ivy plant,

[Note: [Col. 1043B–1044B] Recall the holy Translator in the Commentary, where, discussing this rendering of his own, he says: “We followed the older translators, who likewise rendered it ‘ivy,’ which is called κισσός (*kissos*) in Greek; for they had no other word to use.” See also what we have noted at this passage.]

and it grew up over Jonah’s head

to be a shade over his head

and protect him

(for he had been laboring),

and Jonah rejoiced over the ivy plant with great joy.

And God prepared a worm at the rising of dawn on the following day,

and it struck the ivy,

and it withered.

And when the sun had risen,

the Lord commanded a hot and burning wind.

And the sun struck Jonah’s head,

and he was faint with heat.

And he asked for his life,

that he might die,

and said:

“Death is better for me than life.”

And the Lord said to Jonah:

“Are you right to be angry over the ivy?”

And he said:

“I am right to be angry,

even unto death.”

And the Lord said:

“You grieve over the ivy,

for which you did not labor,

and which you did not make grow,

which came into being in one night

and perished in one night.

And should I not spare Nineveh,

the great city,

in which there are more than one hundred and twenty thousand human beings

who do not know the difference between their right hand and their left,

and many animals?”

[Col. 1043] The book of the prophet Jonah ends.

# THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET MICAH BEGINS

[Col. 1043C] [Chapter I]

The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite

in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah,

kings of Judah,

which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

Hear, all peoples,

and let the earth and its fullness attend.

And let the Lord God be a witness against you,

the Lord from his holy temple.

For behold, the Lord is coming out from his place [Alternative: shall come out],

and he shall descend,

and tread upon the heights of the earth.

And the mountains beneath him shall melt,

and the valleys shall be split

like wax before fire,

like waters pouring down a precipice.

All this is because of the crime of Jacob,

and because of the sins of the house of Israel.

What is the crime of Jacob?

Is it not Samaria?

And what are the high places of Judah?

Is it not Jerusalem?

And I will make Samaria like a heap of stones in a field

when a vineyard is planted.

And I will drag its stones down into the valley,

and I will uncover its foundations.

And all its carved images shall be shattered,

and all its wages shall be burned with fire,

and I will set all its idols to destruction.

For they were gathered from the wages of a prostitute,

and they shall return to the wages of a prostitute.

Because of this I will mourn and howl.

I will go stripped and naked.

I will make mourning like that of dragons,

and lamentation like that of ostriches.

For her wound is incurable,

because it has come as far as Judah.

It has touched the gate of my people,

as far as Jerusalem.

Do not announce it in Gath.

Do not weep with tears.

In the house of Dust,

sprinkle yourselves with dust.

And cross over for yourselves,

you inhabitants of Beautiful [Alternative: Saphir],

in shame and disgrace.

The inhabitant of the Exit [Alternative: Sennan]

has not gone out.

The mourning of the neighboring house [Alternative: Asel]

shall receive from you,

the house that stood by itself.

For the inhabitant of Bitterness [Alternative: Maroth]

has grown weak for good,

because evil has descended from the Lord

upon the gate of Jerusalem.

The tumult of the chariot is stupefying

for the inhabitant of Lachish.

She is the beginning of sin for the daughter of Zion,

because the crimes of Israel have been found in you.

Therefore he shall send messengers

over the inheritance of Gath,

houses of deceit [Alternative: a house of deceit]

for the deception of the kings of Israel.

I shall yet bring an heir to you,

you who dwell in Mareshah.

The glory of Israel shall come as far as Adullam.

Shave your head and cut your hair

for the children of your delights.

Enlarge your baldness like an eagle,

because they have been led away captive from you.

[Chapter II]

Woe to those who devise what is useless,

and work evil upon their beds.

In the morning light they carry it out,

because their hand is against God.

They coveted fields,

and seized them by force.

*The supplied source ends here, in an incomplete sentence.*
[Col. 1045A] and they seized the houses:

And they oppressed a man and his house,

a man and his inheritance.

Therefore thus says the Lord:

Behold, I am devising evil against this family,

from which you shall not withdraw your necks, nor walk proudly,

for the time is exceedingly evil.

On that day a proverb shall be taken up against you,

and a song shall be sung with sweetness, saying:

“We have been utterly devastated by devastation;

the portion of my people has been exchanged.

How will he withdraw from me, when he returns,

the one who divides our regions?”

For this reason you shall have no one casting the measuring line by lot

in the assembly of the Lord.

Do not speak, speaking thus:

“Dripping shall not come upon these;

confusion shall not overtake them.”

The house of Jacob says:

[Col. 1045B] “Has the spirit of the Lord been shortened,

or are such his thoughts?

Are not my words good toward him who walks rightly?”

But, on the contrary, my people have risen up as an enemy:

you strip off the cloak from their garments;

and you have turned those who were passing by simply and peaceably

into war.

You have driven the women of my people out of the house of their delights;

from their little ones you have taken away my praise forever.

Rise and go,

for you have no rest here:

because of its uncleanness it shall be corrupted with the worst corruption.

Would that I were not a man having the spirit,

and that I spoke rather a lie:

“I shall drip upon you wine and drunkenness”—

and this shall be upon the people upon whom it drips.

Gathering, I shall gather you wholly, Jacob;

I shall bring together the remnant of Israel into one;

I shall place him together like a flock in a fold,

like a herd in the midst of its enclosures;

they shall resound with the multitude of people.

For the one opening the way shall go up before them:

they shall divide, pass through the gate, and go out by it;

and their king shall pass before them,

and the Lord at their head [Al. heads].

[Cap. III.] And I said: Hear, princes of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel:

Is it not yours to know judgment,

you who hate what is good and love what is evil?

You who violently strip their skin from them

and their flesh from their bones;

who have eaten the flesh of my people,

stripped their skin from them,

[Col. 1045D] broken their bones, and cut them up as for a kettle,

and as flesh in the midst of a pot.

Then they will cry out to the Lord, and he will not hear them;

and he will hide his face from them at that time,

just as they acted wickedly in their devices.

Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead my people astray,

who bite with their teeth and proclaim peace;

and if anyone gives nothing into their mouths,

they sanctify war against him.

Therefore night shall be vision for you,

and darkness divination for you:

the sun shall set upon the prophets,

and the day shall grow dark over them.

Those who see visions shall be ashamed,

and the diviners shall be confounded;

they shall all cover their faces,

because there is no answer from God.

[Col. 1046A] Yet I am filled with strength by the spirit of the Lord,

with judgment and might,

to declare to Jacob his transgression

and to Israel his sin.

Hear this, princes of the house of Jacob and judges of the house of Israel,

you who abhor judgment and pervert everything that is right;

you who build Zion with blood

and Jerusalem with iniquity.

Her princes judged for gifts,

her priests taught for payment,

and her prophets divined for money.

And they rested upon the Lord, saying:

“Is not the Lord in our midst?

Evil will not come upon us.”

Therefore, because of you, Zion shall be plowed like a field;

Jerusalem shall become like a heap of stones,

and the mountain of the Temple like the high places of forests.

[Cap. IV.] And it shall come to pass:

[Col. 1046B] In the last days the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared at the summit of the mountains,

and shall be exalted above the hills;

and peoples shall flow toward it.

And many nations shall hasten and say:

“Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord

and to the house of the God of Jacob;

and he will teach us his ways,

and we shall walk in his paths.”

For from Zion the law shall go forth,

and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

And he shall judge among many peoples,

and shall rebuke strong nations even at a distance.

And they shall beat their swords into plowshares

and their spears into pruning hooks.

Nation shall not take up the sword against nation,

nor shall they learn war any longer.

And each man shall sit beneath his vine and beneath his fig tree,

[Col. 1046C] and there shall be no one who terrifies [Al. frightens],

for the mouth of the Lord of hosts has spoken.

For all peoples shall walk, each in the name of his god;

but we shall walk in the name of the Lord our God

forever and beyond.

On that day, says the Lord, I shall gather the lame;

I shall assemble the one whom I had driven away,

and the one whom I had afflicted.

And I shall place the lame among the remnant,

and the one who had been wearied among a strong nation.

And the Lord shall reign over them on Mount Zion,

from this time forth and forever.

And you, tower of the flock, misty daughter of Zion, to you it shall come,

and the former dominion shall come,

the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.

Now why are you contracted with grief?

Is there no king for you,

or has your counselor perished,

[Col. 1046D] because pain has seized you like a woman in labor?

Suffer and struggle, daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor,

for now you shall go out from the city and dwell in the countryside,

and you shall come as far as Babylon.

There you shall be delivered;

there the Lord shall redeem you from the hand of your enemies.

And now many nations have gathered against you,

who say: “Let her be stoned,”

and “Let our eye gaze upon Zion.”

But they did not know the thoughts of the Lord,

nor did they understand his counsel,

for he has gathered them like hay on the threshing floor.

Rise and thresh, daughter of Zion,

for I shall make your horn iron

and your hoofs bronze.

And you shall crush many peoples,

[Col. 1047A] and [Note: [Col. 1047D] It is remarkable that all the Latin books prefer the second person, “you will slay,” and the Greeks ἀναθήσεις (“you will devote”), whereas in Hebrew it is nevertheless in the first person: “I will slay,” or, more accurately, “I will devote under a ban.”] I shall devote their plunder under a ban to the Lord,

and their strength for the Lord of the whole earth.

[Cap. V.] Now you shall be devastated, daughter of the robber;

they have laid siege against us.

With a rod they shall strike the cheek of the judge of Israel.

And you, Bethlehem Ephrata, you are little among the thousands of Judah;

from you there shall go forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel,

whose going forth is from the beginning,

from the days of eternity.

Therefore he will give them up until the time when she who is in labor gives birth;

and the remnant of his brothers [Note: Although the holy Father himself reads it thus in the Commentary, he seems to have preferred another rendering of Symmachus: “And they shall return,” he says, or, as Symmachus translated more accurately, “they shall dwell.” For the Hebrew verb *yāshūbū* signifies both things. “They shall dwell, however, in the Church of the Lord,” and so forth.] shall return to the children

of Israel.

And he shall stand and feed them in the strength of the Lord,

in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God.

And they shall return,

for now he shall be magnified as far as the ends of the earth.

And this man shall be peace.

When the Assyrian comes into our land

and treads upon our houses,

[Col. 1047B] we shall raise up against him seven shepherds

and eight principal men.

And they shall pasture the land of Assyria with the sword,

and the land of Nimrod with his spears.

And he shall deliver us from Assyria when he comes into our land,

and when he treads within our borders.

And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many peoples,

like dew from the Lord

and like drops upon the grass,

which does not await a man

and does not wait for the sons of men.

And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the nations,

in the midst of many peoples,

like a lion among the beasts of the forests,

and like a young lion among flocks of sheep,

which, when it passes through, tramples and seizes,

has no one who can rescue.

Your hand shall be exalted over your enemies,

and all your enemies shall perish.

[Col. 1047C] And it shall come to pass on that day, says the Lord:

I shall remove your horses from your midst

and destroy your chariots.

I shall destroy the cities of your land

and demolish all your fortifications.

I shall remove sorceries from your hand,

and there shall be no divinations in you.

I shall cause your carved images and your statues

to perish from your midst,

and you shall no longer worship the works of your hands.

I shall uproot your sacred groves from your midst

and crush your cities.

And in anger and indignation I shall execute vengeance

upon all the nations that have not listened.

[Cap. VI.] Hear what the Lord says:

Rise, contend in judgment against the mountains,

and let the hills hear your voice.

Let the mountains hear the judgment of the Lord,

and the strong foundations of the earth.

[Col. 1047D] For the Lord’s judgment is with his people,

and he shall be judged with Israel.

My people, what have I done to you,

and in what have I wearied you?

[Col. 1048A] Answer me.

For I brought you up from the land of Egypt,

and from the house of [Note: The Canon of St. Germain and manuscript no. 3 read “and from the house of servitude,” which St. Jerome also retains in the Commentaries.] slavery I delivered you.

And I sent Moses before your face,

and Aaron and Miriam.

My people, remember, I ask, what Balak the king of Moab devised

[Note: Other books add “against you,” as the holy Father himself also reads it in the Commentary. These words are derived from the Greek *katà sou* (κατὰ σοῦ, “against you”), for which there is nothing corresponding in the Hebrew.] ,

and what Balaam son of Beor answered him,

from Shittim to Gilgal,

so that you might know the righteous acts of the Lord.

What worthy offering shall I make to the Lord?

Shall I bend my knee before God Most High?

Shall I offer him burnt offerings

and yearling calves?

Can the Lord be appeased with thousands of rams,

or with many thousands of fat goats?

Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression,

the fruit of my womb for the sin of my soul?

I will show you, O man, what is good

[Col. 1048B] and what the Lord seeks from you:

namely, to do judgment,

to love mercy,

and to walk carefully with your God.

The voice of the Lord cries out to the city,

and salvation shall be for those who fear your name.

Hear, O tribes,

and who will approve it?

There is still fire in the house of the wicked,

the treasure of iniquity [Al. wickedness],

and a measure diminished and filled with wrath.

Shall I justify an impious balance

and deceitful weights in the bag?

Her rich men are filled with iniquity,

her inhabitants speak lies in her,

and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.

Therefore I too began to strike you with destruction

because of your sins.

You shall eat, but you shall not be satisfied;

and your humiliation shall be in your midst.

[Col. 1048C] You shall seize, but you shall not save;

and those whom you save I shall give to the sword.

You shall sow, but you shall not reap;

you shall tread the olive, but you shall not anoint yourself with oil;

and you shall make new wine, but you shall not drink wine.

You have kept the statutes of Omri

and every work of the house of Ahab.

You have walked in their counsels,

so that I might make you a desolation,

and its inhabitants a hissing,

and you shall bear the reproach of my people.

[Cap. VII.] Woe is me, for I have become like one gathering in autumn the clusters of the vintage:

there is no bunch to eat;

my soul has desired early figs.

[Note: The Canon of the Church of Carcassonne reads “unripe figs.” In the text of the Commentaries, however, we read “first figs,” and then in the explanations, “unripe figs.” “In vain,” says Jerome in his exposition, “I wished … to seek the last clusters, and, since there is no bunch to eat, at least to take as food unripe figs, which the Hebrews call *BECCORA*, that is, large figs.”]

The holy man has perished from the earth,

and there is no upright person among human beings.

All lie in wait for blood;

each man hunts his brother for death.

[Col. 1048D] They call the evil of their hands good.

The prince asks, and the judge is ready to repay;

the great man has spoken the desire of his soul,

and they have disturbed it.

[Col. 1049A] The best among them is like a thornbush,

and the upright like a thorn from a hedge.

The day of your watchmen,

your visitation,

has come;

now their devastation will be.

Do not believe a friend,

and do not trust a leader.

From the woman who sleeps at your breast,

guard the doors of your mouth.

For the son insults the father;

the daughter rises against her mother;

the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;

a man’s enemies are those of his own household.

But I shall look to the Lord;

I shall await God my Savior;

my God will hear me.

Do not rejoice over me, my enemy,

because I have fallen;

I shall rise when I sit in darkness;

the Lord is my light.

I shall bear the wrath of the Lord,

because I have sinned against him,

until he judges my cause

and executes my judgment.

[Col. 1049B] He will bring me out into the light;

I shall see his righteousness.

And my enemy shall look,

and she shall be covered with shame,

she who says to me:

“Where is the Lord your God?”

My eyes shall look upon her [Al. omits “upon”];

now she shall be trampled like the mud of the streets.

A day for rebuilding your walls;

on that day the law shall be far removed.

On that day, and as far as you, he shall come from Assyria,

and as far as the fortified cities;

[Col. 1050A] and from the fortified cities to the river,

and from sea to sea,

and from mountain to mountain.

And the land shall become desolate

because of its inhabitants

and because of the fruit of their thoughts.

Feed your people with your rod,

the flock of your inheritance,

those dwelling alone in the forest,

in the midst of Carmel.

They shall pasture in Bashan and Gilead

as in the days of old.

As in the days of your coming out from the land of Egypt,

I shall show him wonders.

The nations shall see

and shall be ashamed of all their might.

They shall place their hand over their mouth;

their ears shall be deaf.

They shall lick the dust like a serpent;

like reptiles of the earth they shall be driven from their houses.

They shall fear the Lord our God [Note: Instead of “they shall fear the Lord our God,” four manuscripts—that is, both copies of the Hebrew Canon, together with two Colbertine manuscripts, one from Anicy and another no. 75—read “they shall desire the Lord our God.” This reading is in no way supported by the Commentaries of St. Jerome, nor by the Hebrew volumes.] [Vulg. “they shall dread”],

[Col. 1050B] and they shall fear you.

Who is a God like you,

who takes away iniquity

and passes over the sin of the remnant of your inheritance?

He will not continue to retain his anger,

because he delights in mercy.

He will return and have mercy on us;

he will cast away our iniquities

and hurl all our sins into the depths of the sea.

You will give truth [Al. add. “in”] to Jacob,

mercy to Abraham,

[Note: Jerome himself prefers in the Commentary: “which you swore.”] which you swore to our fathers from days of old.

[Col. 1049] Here ends the book of the prophet Micah.

HERE BEGINS THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET NAHUM.

[Col. 1049C] [Cap. I.] The oracle of Nineveh.

The book of the vision of Nahum the Elcesite.

God is jealous and the Lord takes vengeance;

the Lord takes vengeance and possesses wrath.

The Lord takes vengeance on his enemies

and is angry with his adversaries.

The Lord is patient and great in strength,

and, though cleansing, he will not declare the guilty innocent.

The Lord’s way is in storm and whirlwind,

and clouds are the dust of his feet.

He rebukes the sea and dries it up,

and leads all the rivers into the desert.

Bashan and Carmel have languished,

and the blossom of Lebanon has faded.

The mountains have been shaken by him,

and the hills have been laid waste.

The earth trembled before his face,

the world and all who dwell in it.

Who can stand before his indignation?

Who can withstand the heat of his anger?

[Col. 1049D] His indignation is poured out like fire,

and the rocks are dissolved by him.

The Lord is good,

and he strengthens in the day of tribulation;

he knows those who hope in him.

And in an overflowing flood

he will bring the place to its end,

and darkness will pursue his enemies.

What are you devising against the Lord?

He himself will bring it to an end;

tribulation will not rise a second time.

For just as thorns embrace one another,

so are their banquet and those drinking together;

they shall be consumed like stubble full of dryness.

From you there went forth one devising evil against the Lord,

plotting treachery in his mind.

Thus says the Lord:

Though they should be complete,

and though they should be so numerous,

even so they shall be shorn,

and he shall pass away.

I have afflicted you,

but I shall not afflict you again.

And now I shall break his rod from your back

and tear apart your bonds.

And the Lord will command concerning [Al. against] you:

no more shall anything be sown from your name.

From the house of your God I shall destroy the carved image and the cast image;

I shall make your tomb,

because you have been dishonored.

Behold, upon the mountains are the feet of one bringing good news

and proclaiming peace.

Celebrate your festivals, Judah,

and fulfill your vows,

for Belial shall no longer continue to pass through you;

he has been utterly destroyed.

[Cap. II.] The one who scatters has gone up before you,

[Col. 1050D] the one who guards the siege [Al. “guarding before your face”].

Observe the way,

strengthen your loins,

fortify your strength greatly.

For the Lord has restored the pride of Jacob,

as the pride of Israel [Al. “For just as the Lord restored the pride of Jacob, so he will restore the pride of Israel”],

because devastators have ravaged them

and corrupted their branches.

[Col. 1051A] His warriors’ shield is fiery;

the men of the army are clothed in scarlet.

The reins of the chariots are fiery on the day of his preparation,

and [Note: It seems that the holy Translator read, instead of what the Hebrew text now has, the word [Hebrew word omitted in supplied text], “and fir trees,” a form not greatly different in writing but far more fitting and learned in sense, namely [Hebrew word omitted in supplied text], “and horsemen,” or “and drivers,” that is, “and those who drive horses.” It is clear from the context that the reading of the archetype makes the meaning somewhat obscure and appears to have been corrupted through the carelessness of scribes and the decay of long time. The Seventy also allowed themselves to substitute another reading, or at least read it differently from the present text, since they translated, *kai hoi hippēs* (καὶ οἱ ἱππεῖς), “and the horsemen.” This is certainly a suitable translation, and one to which Jerome seems to have come closest and conformed himself.] the charioteers are asleep.

They are thrown into confusion on the roads;

the chariots collide in the streets.

Their appearance is like lamps,

like flashing lightning racing about.

He remembers his warriors;

they stumble along their paths.

They hasten up its walls,

and the shelter is prepared.

The gates of the rivers are opened,

and the temple is thrown down to its foundations.

The soldier is led away captive,

and her maidservants moan like doves,

murmuring in their hearts.

And Nineveh is like a pool of water;

but they have fled.

“Stand, stand!”

but there is no one who returns.

Plunder silver, plunder gold;

there is no end to the wealth of all the desirable vessels.

She is scattered, torn apart, and ripped to pieces;

the heart melts,

the knees give way,

weakness seizes all the loins,

and the faces of them all are like the blackness of a pot.

Where is the lions’ den,

and the pasture of the young lions,

to which the lion went to enter,

the young lion,

with no one to frighten it?

The lion seized enough for his cubs

and killed for his lionesses;

he filled his caves with prey

and his lair with plunder.

Behold, I am against you, says the Lord of hosts,

and I will burn your chariots to smoke,

and the sword shall devour your young lions [Al. cubs].

[Col. 1051C] I shall exterminate your prey from the earth,

and the voice of your messengers shall no longer be heard.

[Cap. III.] Woe to the city of blood,

wholly full of deceit and plunder;

plunder shall not depart from you.

The sound of the whip,

the sound of the rushing wheel,

the neighing horse,

the heated chariot,

the mounted horseman,

the flashing sword,

the gleaming spear,

the multitude of slain,

the grievous ruin.

There is no end of corpses,

and they fall upon their bodies.

Because of the multitude of the fornications of the beautiful and charming prostitute,

who possessed sorceries,

who sold nations through her fornications

and families through her sorceries,

behold, I am against you, says the Lord of hosts,

and I will uncover your shame before your face,

and I will show the nations your nakedness,

[Col. 1052A] and your disgrace to kingdoms.

I will cast abominations upon you,

I will cover you with insults,

and I will set you up as an example.

And it shall be:

everyone who sees you will recoil from you

and will say:

“Devastated is Nineveh.

Who will shake his head over you?

From where shall I seek a comforter for you?”

Are you better than [Al. “Amon than”] Alexandria

of the peoples,

which dwells among the rivers,

with waters all around it,

whose wealth is the sea,

whose walls are waters?

Ethiopia was its strength,

and Egypt,

and there was no end.

Africa and Libya were your help.

Yet she herself has been led away into exile [Al. “is being led into exile”],

into captivity.

Her little ones were dashed to pieces [Al. “will be dashed”]

at the head of every road,

and they cast lots [Al. “will cast lots”] over her nobles;

[Col. 1052B] all her princes were fastened [Al. “will be afflicted”] in fetters.

And you too shall become drunk,

and you shall be despised;

you too shall seek help from the enemy.

All your fortifications are like a fig tree with its first fruits.

If they are shaken,

they will fall into the mouth of the eater.

Behold, your people are women in your midst.

The gates of your land shall be opened wide to your enemies;

fire shall devour your bars.

Draw water for yourself because of the siege;

build your fortifications.

Enter into the mud and tread it,

kneading the brick.

There the fire shall consume you;

you shall perish by the sword;

the locust shall devour you.

Gather yourself [Al. add. “therefore”] like a locust;

multiply yourself like a grasshopper.

[Col. 1052C] You have made your merchants more numerous than the stars of heaven.

The locust spread its wings and flew away.

Your guards are like locusts,

and [Note: The Hebrew instead has [word omitted in supplied text], “satraps.” Jerome substituted a similar-sounding word, either because his eye moved quickly or because he found it written thus in his copy. For he read [Hebrew word omitted in supplied text], “your little ones,” instead of [Hebrew word omitted in supplied text], “your satraps.” *Thaphsar* is the name of an Assyrian rank, from which the Greeks fashioned their *satraps*. ] your little ones are like locusts upon locusts,

which settle in the hedges on the day of cold.

The sun rose,

and they flew away,

and no one knows the place where they had been.

Your shepherds have slumbered, king of Assyria;

your princes shall be buried.

Your people have hidden in the mountains [Al. “scattered … upon the mountains”],

and there is no one who gathers them.

Your destruction is not obscure;

your wound is exceedingly grievous.

All who heard the report about you

clapped their hands over you,

for upon whom has your wickedness not continually passed?

[Col. 1051] Here ends the book of the prophet Nahum.

HERE BEGINS THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET HABAKKUK.

[Col. 1053]

[Col. 1053A] [Cap. I.] The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet saw.

How long, O Lord, shall I cry out,

and you will not hear?

Shall I shout to you under violence,

and you will not save?

Why have you shown me iniquity and toil [Al. pain],

to see plunder and injustice against me?

Judgment has come to be,

and contradiction has grown stronger.

Therefore the law is torn apart,

and judgment does not reach the end,

because the impious prevails over the just;

therefore perverse judgment goes forth.

Look among the nations and see;

wonder and be astonished,

for a work has been done in your days

that no one will believe when it is told.

For behold, I shall raise up the Chaldeans,

a bitter and swift nation,

walking across the breadth of the earth

to possess dwellings not its own.

[Col. 1053B] It is terrible and dreadful;

its judgment and its burden will go forth from itself.

Its horses are swifter than leopards

and faster than evening wolves.

Its horsemen spread out;

indeed, its horsemen come from afar.

They fly like an eagle hastening to devour.

They all come for plunder;

their faces are like a burning wind,

and they gather captives like sand.

He himself will triumph over kings,

and tyrants will be a laughingstock to him.

He will laugh at every fortress,

heap up earthworks,

and capture it.

Then his spirit will change,

he will pass on and fall;

this is the strength of his god.

Are you not from the beginning, O Lord my God,

[Note: Martianaeus had mistakenly read *tui*, “of you,” instead of *tua*, “your.”]

my Holy One,

and we shall not die?

[Col. 1053C] O Lord, you appointed him for judgment

and established him, the strong one,

to correct him.

Your eyes are pure, so that you cannot see evil,

and you cannot [Al. “are not able to”] look upon iniquity.

Why do you look upon those who act wickedly

and remain silent while the impious devours one more righteous than himself?

You make human beings like the fish of the sea,

like a creeping thing that has no ruler.

He lifted them all up on a hook,

drew them into his net,

and gathered them into his dragnet.

Because of this he will rejoice and exult.

Therefore he will sacrifice to his net

and offer incense to his dragnet,

because through them his portion has grown fat

and his food has become choice.

Therefore he spreads his net

and does not cease [Al. “does not stop”] continually slaughtering nations.

[Cap. II.] I will stand at my watch,

[Col. 1053D] and set my step upon the fortification.

I will keep watch to see what he will say to me,

and what I shall answer to the one who reproves me.

And the Lord answered me and said:

[Col. 1054A] Write the vision

and make it clear upon tablets,

so that the one who reads it may run.

For the vision is still for a distant time,

and it will appear at the end,

and it will not lie.

If it delays, wait for it,

for it will surely come;

it will not be late.

Behold, the unbelieving one,

his soul is not upright within him;

but the just shall live by his faith.

And just as wine deceives the drinker,

so shall the proud man be;

he shall not be adorned.

He has enlarged his soul like the underworld;

he himself is like death,

and he is not satisfied.

He gathers all nations to himself

and collects all peoples to himself.

Will not all these take up a proverb against him

and a speech of riddles against him,

and will it be said:

“Woe to him who multiplies what is not his!”

How long will he heap dense mud against himself?

Will not those who bite you suddenly rise up,

[Col. 1054B] and those who tear you apart awaken?

You will become their spoil.

Because you plundered many nations,

all who remain of the peoples shall plunder you,

because of human blood

and because of the iniquity of the land,

the city,

and all who dwell in it.

Woe to him who gathers evil greed for his house,

to set his nest on high

and thinks he can escape from the hand of evil.

You have devised shame for your house;

you have cut down many peoples,

and your soul has sinned.

For the stone from the wall will cry out,

and the wood between the joints of the buildings

will answer:

“Woe to him who builds a city with blood

and prepares a town in iniquity.”

Are not these things from the Lord of hosts?

For peoples will labor amid much fire,

and nations will toil in vain and grow weary.

For the earth shall be filled

so that they may know the glory of the Lord,

as waters cover the sea.

Woe to him who gives his friend drink,

sending him his gall

and making him drunk,

so that he may look upon his nakedness.

You are filled with disgrace instead of glory.

You too, drink and become senseless.

The cup of the Lord’s right hand shall surround you,

and vomiting of disgrace shall be upon your glory.

For the iniquity of Lebanon shall cover you,

and the destruction of animals [Al. beasts]

shall terrify them

because of the blood of human beings,

the iniquity of the land and the city,

and all who dwell in it.

What profit is there in a carved image,

because its maker has carved it,

a cast image and a false likeness?

For its maker has trusted in what he fashioned

[Col. 1054D] to make mute idols.

Woe to him who says to wood:

“Awake!”

and to a silent stone:

“Rise!”

Can it itself teach?

[Col. 1055A] Behold, it is covered with gold and silver,

and there is no spirit at all within its entrails.

But the Lord is in his holy temple.

Let all the earth be silent before him.

PRAYER OF HABAKKUK [Note: The Palatine manuscript reads “for the ignorant”; certain others read “for ignorances.” Rabanus also notes that the Seventy read “with a song” instead of “for ignorances.” “But it is better,” he says, “according to the Hebrew truth, to read: ‘The prayer of Habakkuk the prophet for ignorances.’” St. Jerome himself reads this way in the Commentary, and more clearly at the end of the first Dialogue against the Pelagians: “The prophet Habakkuk gives this title to his song: ‘The prayer of Habakkuk the prophet for ignorances.’ The Hebrew word [omitted in supplied text], which corresponds to it, the interpreters admit that they do not know precisely what it signifies. It can, however, quite suitably be derived from [an omitted Hebrew root], which means ‘to err,’ ‘to wander,’ or even ‘to slip through ignorance.’ Hence [an omitted Hebrew term] is called a wandering, or errant, song, one that is varied and mixed; its plural number here is [an omitted Hebrew form].] FOR IGNORANCES.

[Cap. III.] O Lord, I heard your report,

and I was afraid.

O Lord, your work—

in the midst of the years revive it.

In the midst of the years make it known.

When you are angry,

you will remember mercy.

God will come from the south,

and the Holy One from Mount Paran. [Note: The Canon of St. Germain retains here, in the Prayer of Habakkuk, the *diapsalma* of the Seventy interpreters. The Canon of Carcassonne, together with the other manuscript copies of the sacred Scriptures, always has *Semper*. St. Jerome says that the *diapsalma*, which is called *Selah* in Hebrew, is discussed more fully in the Psalter. See the same holy Doctor’s Commentaries on this passage and his letters to Marcella. MART. —The Palatine manuscript, together with the Vulgate books, omits this first occurrence and the one that follows immediately. Yet we do not think, as some claim, that Jerome neglected the word as useless.] ALWAYS.

His glory covered the heavens,

and the earth is full of his praise.

[Col. 1055B] His brightness shall be like the light.

Horns are in his hands.

There his strength is hidden.

Death shall go before his face,

and the devil shall go forth before his feet.

He stood and measured the earth.

He looked and dissolved the nations,

and the everlasting mountains were crushed.

The hills of the world bowed down

before the paths of his eternity.

Because of iniquity I saw the tents of Ethiopia;

the skins of the land of Midian will tremble.

Were you angry, O Lord, with the rivers,

or was your fury against the rivers,

or your indignation against the sea?

For you will mount your horses,

and your chariots are salvation.

Raising it up, you will surely raise your bow,

the oaths you spoke to the tribes. ALWAYS.

[Col. 1056A] You will split the rivers of the earth.

The mountains saw you and writhed;

the torrent of waters passed by.

The abyss gave its voice;

the height lifted up its hands.

The sun and moon stood in their dwelling.

At the light of your arrows they will go forth;

at the brightness of your flashing spear.

In fury you will trample the earth;

in anger you will stupefy the nations.

You went forth for the salvation of your people,

for salvation with your Anointed One.

You struck the head from the house of the impious;

you stripped the foundation as far as the neck. ALWAYS.

You cursed his scepters,

the head of his warriors,

who came like a whirlwind to scatter me.

Their exultation

was like that of one who devours the poor in secret.

You made a way in the sea for your horses,

[Col. 1056B] in the mud of many waters.

I heard,

and my belly was troubled.

At the sound [Al. “from the sound”]

my lips trembled.

Let rottenness enter my bones,

and let it seethe beneath me,

so that I may rest in the day of tribulation [Note: The Palatine manuscript and Jerome himself in the Commentary add here the pronoun “my,” which the Hebrew text omits.],

so that I may go up to our armed people.

For the fig tree shall not blossom,

and there shall be no fruit on the vines.

The work of the olive shall fail,

and the fields shall yield no food.

The flock shall be cut off from the fold,

and there shall be no herd in the stalls.

But I shall rejoice in the Lord

and exult in God my Jesus.

God the Lord is my strength,

and he will set my feet like those of deer.

And as victor he will lead me over my high places,

while I sing in psalms.

[Col. 1055] Here ends the book of the prophet Habakkuk.

HERE BEGINS THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET ZEPHANIAH.

[Col. 1055D] [Cap. I.] The word of the Lord that came to Zephaniah,

son of Cushi,

son of Gedaliah [Note: We find “Amasiah” written instead of “Amariah” through the scribes’ error in both copies of the Canon. MART.],

son of Amariah,

son of Hezekiah,

in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.

Gathering, I shall gather everything from the face of the earth,

says the Lord.

I shall gather human beings and animals;

I shall gather the birds of heaven

and the fish of the sea.

The ruins of the impious shall be,

and I shall destroy human beings from the face of the earth,

says the Lord.

I shall stretch out my hand over Judah

and over all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

I shall destroy from this place the remnants of Baal

and the names of the temple servants together with the priests.

I shall destroy those who worship upon the roofs

the host of heaven,

those who worship and swear by the Lord

and swear by Milcom.

And I shall destroy those who turn away from following the Lord

and those who have not sought the Lord

nor investigated him.

[Col. 1057A] Be silent before the face of the Lord God,

for the day of the Lord is near;

the Lord has prepared a sacrifice

and sanctified his invited ones.

And it shall come to pass:

On the day of the Lord’s sacrifice

I shall visit the princes,

the sons of the king,

and all who are clothed in foreign clothing.

I shall visit everyone who enters arrogantly

upon the threshold on that day,

those who fill the house of the Lord their God

with iniquity and deceit.

And it shall come to pass on that day, says the Lord:

a voice of outcry from the Fish Gate,

and a howling from the Second Quarter,
and great devastation from the hills.

Howl, inhabitants of Pilae;  
the whole people of Canaan has fallen silent,  
all those wrapped in silver have perished.

And at that time:

I will search Jerusalem with lamps;  
and I will visit those men who are settled upon their dregs, who say in their hearts:

“The Lord will do neither good nor evil.”

And their wealth shall become plunder,  
and their houses a desolation:

They shall build houses, but shall not inhabit them;  
they shall plant vineyards, but shall not drink their wine.

Near is the great day of the Lord,  
near, and exceedingly swift:

The sound of the day of the Lord is bitter;  
the mighty man shall be afflicted there.

A day of wrath is that day,  
a day of tribulation and distress,  
a day of calamity and misery,  
a day of darkness and gloom,  
a day of cloud and storm;  
a day of trumpet and battle-cry against fortified cities  
and against the lofty corners.

I will afflict human beings,  
and they shall walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the Lord:

Their blood shall be poured out like soil,  
and their bodies like dung.

But neither their silver nor their gold  
will be able to save them [Note: [Col. 1057D] The copies of the Canon add the words “in the day of the wrath of the fury of the Lord,” but this is superfluous. MART.] on the day of the Lord’s fury.

In the fire of his jealousy the whole earth shall be consumed,  
for he will make a swift end  
of all the inhabitants of the earth.

[Chapter II.] Gather together and assemble, nation not worthy of love,  
before the decree brings forth—like passing dust—the appointed day,  
before the anger of the Lord’s fury comes upon you,  
before the day of the Lord’s fury comes upon you [Alternative: wrath of indignation].

Seek the Lord, all you meek of the earth,  
who have practiced judgment;  
seek righteousness, seek meekness:  
perhaps you may be hidden on the day of the Lord’s fury.

For Gaza shall be destroyed,  
and Ashkelon shall become a desolation;  
Ashdod shall be driven out at noon,  
and Ekron shall be uprooted.

Woe to you who inhabit the seacoast, nation of the lost!  
The word of the Lord is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines.

[Col. 1058A] “I will destroy you, so that there will be no inhabitant.”

And the seacoast shall become a resting-place for shepherds  
and sheepfolds.

And the seacoast shall belong to the remnant of the house of Judah;  
there they shall pasture;  
in the houses of Ashkelon they shall lie down in the evening.

For the Lord their God will visit them  
and turn back their captivity.

I have heard the reproach of Moab  
and the blasphemies of the Ammonites,  
with which they reproached my people  
and magnified themselves against their borders.

Therefore, as I live, says the Lord [Alternative: God] of hosts,  
the God of Israel:  
Moab shall become like Sodom,  
and the Ammonites like Gomorrah;  
a dryness of thorns and heaps of salt,  
and a desolation forever.

The remnant of my people shall plunder them,  
and the survivors of my nation shall possess them.

This shall happen to them because of their pride,  
because they blasphemed and magnified themselves  
against the people of the Lord of hosts.

The Lord will be terrifying against them,  
and he will weaken all the gods of the earth;  
and men shall worship him, each from his place,  
all the islands of the nations.

You also, Ethiopians,  
shall be slain by my sword.

He will stretch out his hand toward the north  
and destroy Assyria;  
he will make the splendid one a desolation,  
a pathless place, and like a desert.

Flocks shall lie down in its midst,  
all the beasts of the nations;  
the pelican and the hedgehog shall lodge in its thresholds;  
the voice of one singing in the window,  
a raven on the lintel,  
because I will weaken its strength.

This is the glorious city,  
dwelling in security,  
which said in its heart: “I am,  
and there is no other besides me.”

How has it become a desolation,  
a resting-place for beasts?

Everyone who passes through it shall hiss  
and wag his hand.

[Chapter III.] [Note: [Col. 1057D] No one with even a little knowledge of Hebrew will doubt that, instead of what is written in the archetype as [Hebrew reading omitted in the supplied text], and is called “conspicuous,” or “famous and illustrious,” Jerome read—with one letter fewer—[Hebrew reading omitted in the supplied text], or [Hebrew reading omitted in the supplied text], meaning “provocative,” “contumacious,” or “exasperating,” and perhaps giving a better sense. I would further ascribe this to his supreme learning and mastery of Hebrew; for none of the earlier Greek translators, certainly not the Septuagint, who translate ἐπιφανής (“conspicuous”), provided him with guidance for correcting the reading of the Hebrew text.] Woe to the provocative, redeemed city,  
the dove.

She did not hear the voice  
and did not accept correction;  
she did not trust in the Lord,  
she did not draw near to her God.

Her princes in her midst  
are roaring lions;  
her judges are evening wolves,  
leaving nothing for the morning.

Her prophets are reckless men,  
faithless men;  
her priests have polluted the holy place  
and acted unjustly against the law.

The righteous Lord in her midst will do no injustice;  
morning by morning he brings his judgment to light,  
and it is not concealed.

But the unjust man has not known shame.

“I have destroyed nations,  
and their corners have been scattered;  
I have made their roads desolate,  
so that there is no one who passes by;  
their cities have been laid waste,  
with no man remaining,  
and no inhabitant.

“I said: ‘Nevertheless, you will fear me;  
you will accept correction’;  
and her dwelling would not perish  
because of all the things for which I had visited her.

“Yet, rising early,  
they corrupted all their thoughts.

“Therefore wait for me,” says the Lord,  
“on the day of my rising in the future,  
for my judgment is to gather nations  
and assemble kingdoms,  
to pour out upon them [Alternative: upon her] my indignation,  
all the anger of my fury.

“For in the fire of my jealousy  
the whole earth shall be consumed.

“For then I will restore to the peoples a chosen lip,  
so that all may call upon the name [Alternative: the name] of the Lord  
and serve him with one shoulder.

“From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia  
my suppliants, the children of my dispersed ones,  
shall bring me an offering.

“On that day you shall not be ashamed  
of all your deeds by which you transgressed against me,  
for then I will remove from your midst  
those who boast proudly,  
and you shall no longer continue to exalt yourself  
on my holy mountain.

“I will leave in your midst  
a poor and needy people,  
and they shall hope in the name of the Lord.

“The remnant of Israel shall do no injustice,  
nor speak falsehood,  
and a deceitful tongue shall not be found in their mouth.

[Col. 1060A] “For they themselves shall pasture and lie down,  
and there will be no one to terrify them.

“Praise, daughter of Zion”  
[Note: [Col. 1059B] The Vulgate has, “Rejoice, Israel”; but in Hebrew it is plural, “Rejoice.” One manuscript in Martianus has, “Rejoice, you.”] “Rejoice, Israel;  
be glad and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem.

“The Lord has removed your judgment;  
he has turned away your enemies.

“The Lord, the King of Israel, is in your midst;  
you shall fear evil no longer.

“On that day it shall be said to Jerusalem: ‘Do not fear’;  
and to Zion: ‘Let not your hands grow slack.’

“The Lord your God is in your midst, the mighty one;  
he himself will save.  
He will rejoice over you with gladness;  
he will be silent [Note: [Col. 1059B] Three manuscript copies read, “in your love.” The published sacred text also retains the second-person pronoun in the Hieronymian Commentaries; yet this cannot stand with the exposition of St. Doctor himself, where he says: “And he will do these things in his love, not because of your merit, but because of his mercy.” MART.] in his love [Alternative: your love];  
he will exult over you with praise.

“I will gather the trifles—those who had withdrawn from the law—  
because they were from you,  
so that you may no longer bear reproach concerning them.

“Behold, I will kill all who afflicted you  
at that time;  
I will save the lame  
and gather the one who had been expelled.

“I will make them a praise and a name  
throughout the whole land of their shame.

“At that time, when I bring you,  
and at the time when I gather you,  
I will give you a name and a praise  
among all the peoples of the earth,  
when I turn back your captivity  
before your eyes,” says the Lord.

[Col. 1059] Here ends the book of the prophet Zephaniah.

THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET HAGGAI BEGINS.

[Col. 1059C] [Chapter I.] In the second year of King Darius,  
in the sixth month, on the first day of the month,

the word of the Lord came through the prophet Haggai  
to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah,  
and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest,  
saying:

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

This people says:  
“The time has not yet come  
for the house of the Lord to be built.”

And the word of the Lord came through the prophet Haggai, saying:

Is it time for you to dwell in paneled houses,  
while this house lies desolate?

And now thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Set your hearts upon your ways.

“You have sown much, but brought in little;  
you have eaten, but have not been satisfied;  
you have drunk, but have not become drunk;  
you have clothed yourselves, but have not been warmed;  
and whoever gathered wages  
put them into a pierced purse.

“Thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Set your hearts upon your ways.

“Go up to the mountain, bring wood, and build the house;  
then it will be acceptable to me,  
and I will be glorified,” says the Lord.

“You looked for more, and behold, it became less;  
you brought it into the house, and I blew it away.

“Why?” says the Lord of hosts.  
“Because my house is desolate,  
while each of you hastens to his own house.

“Therefore the heavens over you have been shut,  
so that they give no dew,  
and the earth has been shut [Alternative: withheld its produce],  
so that it gives no yield.

“I called for drought [Note: [Col. 1059D] St. Jerome himself should be heard here in the Commentary: “In place of drought,” he says, “the Septuagint translated ῥομφαίαν, that is, ‘sword’; but in the Hebrew I found three letters written, ḥeth, resh, beth. If we read it as ḥāreb, it means ‘sword’; if as ʿōreb, καῦσων, ‘burning heat,’ which we translated as ‘drought,’ although it may better be rendered ‘burning wind.’ And indeed, since the subject is the earth and the barrenness of the fields, it seems to me that a burning wind rather than a sword is intended in the present passage,” and so forth.] upon the earth and upon the mountains,  
and upon the grain, the wine, and the oil,  
and upon whatever the soil produces,  
and upon human beings and animals,  
and upon all the labor of hands.”

[Col. 1060D] And Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel,  
and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest,  
and all the remnant of the people  
heard the voice of the Lord [Alternative: the Lord is omitted] their God  
and the words of the prophet Haggai,  
just as the Lord their God had sent him to them;  
and the people feared before the Lord.

And Haggai, the messenger of the Lord,  
one of the messengers of the Lord,  
said to the people:

“I am with you,” says the Lord.

And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah,  
and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest,  
and the spirit of all the remnant of the entire people;  
and they entered  
and carried out the work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God.

[Chapter II.] On the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month,  
in the second year of King Darius.

In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month,  
the word of the Lord came through the prophet Haggai, saying:

[Col. 1061B] Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah,  
and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest,  
and to the remnant of the people, saying:

“Who is there among you who remains  
who saw this house in its former glory?  
And what do you see now?  
Is it not, in your eyes, as though it were nothing?

“And now be strong, Zerubbabel,” says the Lord;  
“and be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, high priest;  
and be strong, all you people of the land,” says the Lord of hosts.

“And act, for I am with you,” says the Lord of hosts,  
“according to the word that I covenanted with you  
when you came out of the land of Egypt;  
and my spirit shall be in your midst.  
Do not fear.

“For thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Yet a little while,  
and I will shake heaven and earth,  
the sea and the dry land.

“And I will shake all the nations,  
and the desired one of all the nations shall come;  
and I will fill this house with glory,” says the Lord of hosts.

“Mine is the silver, and mine is the gold,” says the Lord of hosts.

“Great shall be the glory of this last house,  
greater than that of the first,” says the Lord of hosts;  
“and in this place I will give peace,” says the Lord of hosts.

On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month,  
in the second year of King Darius [Note: [Col. 1061] The Hebrew text does not add “king,” a word that St. Jerome himself also does not know here in the Commentaries.],  
the word of the Lord came to the prophet Haggai, saying:

[Col. 1062A] Thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Ask the priests about the law, saying:

‘If a man carries sanctified flesh in the fold of his garment,  
and with its edge touches bread, or stew, or wine, or oil, or any food,  
will it become sanctified?’”

The priests answered and said: “No.”

And Haggai said:

“If one who is defiled in soul touches any of these,  
will it become unclean?”

And the priests answered and said: “It will become unclean.”

And Haggai answered and said:

“So is this people, and so is this nation before my face,” says the Lord;  
“and so is every work of their hands;  
and everything that they offer there  
shall be unclean.

“And now set your hearts from this day onward,  
before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the Lord.

“When you approached a heap of twenty measures,  
there were ten;  
when you entered the winepress to draw out fifty jars,  
there were twenty.

“I struck you with burning wind, mildew, and hail—  
all the work of your hands—  
yet there was none among you who returned to me,” says the Lord.

“Set your hearts from this day and into the future,  
from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month.

“From the day on which the foundations of the temple of the Lord were laid,  
set your hearts upon it.

“Is the seed already in the sprout?  
And has neither the vine, nor the fig tree, nor the pomegranate,  
nor the olive tree yet blossomed?

“From this day I will bless.”

And the word of the Lord came a second time to Haggai  
on the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying:

Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying:

“I will shake heaven and earth.  
I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms,  
and destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations.  
I will overthrow the chariot and its rider;  
the horses and their riders shall descend,  
each man by the sword of his brother.

“On that day,” says the Lord of hosts,  
“I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, my servant,” says the Lord,  
“and I will make you like a signet ring,  
for I have chosen you,” says the Lord of hosts.

[Col. 1061] Here ends the book of the prophet Haggai.

THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET ZECHARIAH BEGINS.

[Col. 1061D] [Chapter I.] In the eighth month,  
in the second year of Darius,  
the word of the Lord came to Zechariah son of Berechiah,  
son of Iddo [Alternative: son], the prophet, saying:

The Lord was exceedingly angry with your fathers.

And you shall say to them:

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Return to me,” says the Lord of hosts,  
“and I will return to you,” says the Lord of hosts.

Do not be like your fathers,  
to whom the former prophets cried, saying:

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

“Return from your evil ways  
and from your worst thoughts.”

But they did not listen, nor pay attention to me, says the Lord.

[Col. 1063A] Where are your fathers?  
And do the prophets live forever?

Yet my words and my statutes,  
which I commanded my servants the prophets,  
did they not overtake your fathers?  
And they turned and said:

“As the Lord of hosts planned to do to us  
according to our ways  
and according to our deeds,  
so he did to us.”

On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, Shebat,  
in the second year of Darius,  
the word of the Lord came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:

I saw by night, and behold, a man riding upon a red horse;  
and he was standing among the myrtles  
that were in the deep ravine;  
and behind him were red, mottled, and white horses.

And I said:

“What are these, my lord?”

[Col. 1063B] And the angel who was speaking with me said:

“I will show you what these are.”

And the man who stood among the myrtles answered and said:

“These are those whom the Lord sent  
to patrol the earth.”

And they answered the angel of the Lord  
who stood among the myrtles  
and said:

“We have patrolled the earth,  
and behold, the whole earth is inhabited and at rest.”

And the angel of the Lord answered and said:

“Lord of hosts, how long will you not have mercy  
on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah,  
with which you have been angry?  
This is the seventieth year.”

And the Lord answered the angel  
who spoke with me with good words,  
words of consolation.

And the angel who spoke with me said:

“Cry out, saying:

“Thus says the Lord of hosts:

‘I have been zealous for Jerusalem and Zion  
with great zeal.

‘And with great anger I am angry  
against the wealthy nations,  
because I was angry only a little,  
but they helped toward evil.

‘Therefore thus says the Lord:

‘I will return to Jerusalem with mercies;  
my house shall be built in her,’ says the Lord of hosts,  
‘and the measuring line shall be stretched over Jerusalem.’

“Cry out again, saying:

“Thus says the Lord of hosts:

‘My cities shall yet overflow with good things;  
and the Lord shall yet console Zion,  
and shall yet choose Jerusalem.’”

And I lifted my eyes and saw,  
and behold, four horns.

And I said to the angel who spoke with me:

“What are these?”

And he said to me:

“These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”

And the Lord showed me four craftsmen.

And I said:

“What have these come to do?”

And he said:

“These are the horns that scattered Judah,  
each man separately,  
and none of them lifted his head.

“These have come to frighten them,  
to cast down the horns of the nations  
that raised a horn against the land of Judah  
to scatter it.”

[Chapter II.] And I lifted my eyes and saw,  
and behold, a man,  
with a measuring line in his hand.

And I said:

“Where are you going?”

And he said to me:

“To measure Jerusalem,  
and to see how great its width is  
and how great its length is.”

And behold, the angel who spoke with me was going out,  
and another angel was going out to meet him.

And he said to him:

“Run, speak to that young man, saying:

“‘Jerusalem shall be inhabited without walls,  
because of the multitude of people and animals within her.

“‘And I will be to her,’ says the Lord,  
‘a wall of fire all around,  
and I will be her glory in the midst of her.’

“‘Ho, ho! Flee from the land of the north,’  
[Note: [Col. 1063D] After these words, another clause is found added in copies of the Canon of the Hebrew truth: “From the four winds of heaven I will gather you.” We found it placed in the text in the first hand of the manuscript of Saint-Germain; but in the Carcassonne manuscript it is above the text and in a second hand. MART.] says the Lord,

[Col. 1064B] ‘for I have scattered you toward the four winds of heaven,’  
says the Lord.

“‘O Zion,  
flee [Alternative: rise], you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon.

“‘For thus says the Lord of hosts:

“‘After the glory he sent me to the nations  
that plundered you;  
for whoever touches you  
touches the pupil of my eye [Note: [Col. 1064D] Both the Hebrew text and St. Jerome himself, more closely following it in the Commentary, have “the pupil of his eye.”].

“‘For behold, I raise my hand against them,  
and they shall become plunder  
for those who served them;  
and you shall know that the Lord of hosts  
has sent me.

“‘Sing praise and rejoice, daughter of Zion,  
for behold, I am coming  
and I will dwell in your midst,’  
says the Lord.

“‘And many nations shall join themselves to the Lord  
on that day,  
and they shall be my people.

[Col. 1064C] “‘And I will dwell in your midst,  
and you shall know that the Lord of hosts  
has sent me to you.

“‘And the Lord shall possess Judah as his portion  
in the sanctified land,  
and he shall yet choose Jerusalem.

“‘Let all flesh be silent before the Lord,  
for he has risen from your holy dwelling.’”

[Chapter III.] And the Lord showed me Joshua [Alternative: the Lord is omitted], the high priest, standing before the angel of the Lord;  
and Satan was standing at his right hand  
to oppose him.

And the Lord said to Satan:

“May the Lord rebuke you, Satan;  
may the Lord who chose Jerusalem rebuke you.  
Is this not a brand plucked from the fire?”

And Joshua was clothed in filthy garments  
and stood before the angel.

And he answered and said to those standing before him:

“Remove the filthy garments from him.”

[Col. 1064D] And he said to him:

“Behold, I have taken away your iniquity from you  
and clothed you in festal garments.”

And he said:

“Put a clean turban upon his head.”

And they put a clean turban upon his head  
and clothed him in garments;  
and the angel of the Lord was standing there.

And the angel of the Lord charged Joshua, saying:

Thus says the Lord of hosts:

“If you walk in my ways  
and keep my watch,  
you also shall judge my house  
and guard my courts,  
and I will give you access among those  
who now stand here.

“Hear, Joshua, high priest,  
you and your companions who dwell before you,  
for they are men who are portents.

“For behold, I am bringing my servant, the Branch.

“For behold, the stone that I have set before Joshua:  
upon one stone are seven eyes.

“Behold, I will engrave its engraving,” says the Lord of hosts,  
“and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.

“On that day,” says the Lord of hosts,  
“each man shall call his neighbor  
under the vine and under the fig tree.”

[Chapter IV.] And the angel who spoke with me returned  
and awakened me,  
like a man who is awakened from his sleep.

[Col. 1065B] And he said to me:

“What do you see?”

And I said:

“I saw, and behold, a wholly golden lampstand,  
with its lamp upon its top,  
and its seven lamps upon it;  
[Note: [Col. 1065D] St. Jerome himself seems to read more correctly in the Commentary “seven and seven receptacles”: “Seven and seven receptacles,” and so forth. For this is precisely how it stands in the Hebrew manuscript, “seven and seven receptacles,” and so forth. Perhaps, following the form of the Greek version, where it occurs only once—καὶ ἑπτὰ ἐπαρυστρίδες—it was likewise placed only once here.]  
and seven receptacles for the lamps  
that were upon its top.

“And two olive trees were beside it,  
one on the right of the lamp  
and one on its left.”

And I answered and said to the angel  
who spoke with me:

“What are these, my lord?”

And the angel who spoke with me answered  
and said to me:

“Do you not know what these are?”
